Title: My son is graduating from junior high school this year and wants to study computer science. Which computer school in Dalian is good? Please give suggestions based on personal experience. Content: This relates to my child's future and also to the school's reputation. Please answer truthfully. The heart of parents everywhere, I will be very grateful. The heart of parents everywhere, I really sympathize with you. I am about to graduate from university now. Although I can't help you with choosing a computer school, I can share some of my experience. It's really not good to study computer science right after junior high graduation. The computer industry talent market is saturated; even university graduates have poor employment prospects. Also, the computer field rarely needs technical workers. I suggest studying something like mechanical control, as it will be easier to find a job later and save you worry. Secondly, it's best not to let him live alone outside; living in a dormitory is not good. Your son probably doesn't like studying much, since he didn't go to high school. Since he's learning a skill, if he leaves home and has no supervision, it will be even worse... Children need guidance. He probably just loves playing on the computer; I play too. But the important thing is to make sure he doesn't skip school. At the very least, even if he doesn't study for exams, he might still absorb something. He should also do the practical work himself. Don't you agree? You could buy him a computer to use at home, don't let him run outside. If he plays on the computer and doesn't study, he'll still learn some computer knowledge, which is better than going out and getting into fights, right? Haha, maybe this sounds harsh, but if the child is disobedient, this might be the only way. If he is obedient, he should repeat a year, test into high school, and then go to university. You need to believe in him; hard work can make up for everything. It's still better not to study computer science; it can be a hobby. Teenagers shouldn't have excessive contact with computers, as it can easily affect their future prospects.

Title: Doctor Taking Kickbacks Secretly Filmed, Difficult to Investigate Without Witnesses Content: Recently, a reader claiming to be a "social supervisor of conduct in the health system" used covert methods to film a scene in the surgical outpatient clinic of Luhe Hospital in Tongzhou. The footage shows a doctor accepting a stack of cash from a man. The doctor involved admitted to having taken money from a man claiming to be a pharmaceutical representative but said he returned it quickly. He also stated that the incident was a frame-up by colleagues. Recording: Doctor Accepts Stack of Cash "I am an ordinary social conduct supervisor in the health system. Out of a sense of responsibility to society, I conducted an undercover investigation into the phenomenon of individual doctors at Tongzhou Luhe Hospital accepting drug kickbacks (with on-site computer disc images) and have reported this phenomenon to the relevant authorities, but received no response. Therefore, I am providing this clue to your newspaper, hoping your newspaper can investigate and report on this matter with a fair, pragmatic, and responsible attitude." On December 8, our newspaper received a letter containing the above content and an attached disc. The disc contained a video recording of an incident in a consultation room. A man sat in the patient's seat, first handing the doctor a drug information leaflet, then a business card. After a brief exchange, the man pulled out several hundred-yuan bills. The doctor initially declined, but the man placed the money on the table. After the man left the room, the doctor put the money into his wallet. The entire video lasted about two minutes, and the doctor's face was clearly visible. The letter writer did not reveal their name or contact information, only stating that the footage was taken in the surgical outpatient clinic of Tongzhou Luhe Hospital. Explanation: Money Returned Immediately After Receipt Yesterday afternoon, in the surgical consultation room shown in the video, the reporter contacted the doctor in the footage. His name is Yin Lianhu, 40 years old. The hospital's "Expert Profile" states that Yin Lianhu is the chief physician of the hospital's neurosurgery department, holds a medical doctorate from Shandong University, is one of the country's first Gamma Knife experts, and has participated in the successful completion of over 3,000 surgeries of various difficulties. The contract shown by Yin Lianhu to the reporter indicates that he previously worked at Shandong Provincial Hospital. On March 1st of this year, the hospital recruited him as a talent and hired him to work in neurosurgery at Luhe Hospital. Yin Lianhu said he was already aware of the secret filming. In the middle of last month, the hospital's disciplinary inspection commission had approached him twice to understand the situation, and he had provided a detailed explanation. He recalled that the filmed event occurred in October, but he could not remember the exact date. It happened during his outpatient clinic hours, likely on a Monday morning. The man in the video did claim to be a "medical representative." After entering, the man handed over materials and gave a brief introduction. Yin Lianhu stated that he often encounters such medical representatives during outpatient clinics and intended to simply brush him off. However, the man looked troubled and said, "It's tough for everyone, please take care of me," before pulling out two to three hundred yuan and placing it on the table. Yin Lianhu said he declined, but the man left quickly. "I really shouldn't have put the money in my wallet, but everyone makes mistakes!" Yin Lianhu expressed. He emphasized that after putting the money away, he spoke to the next patient, then quickly came to his senses, thinking, "Why should I take his (the medical representative's) money?" He then rushed out and caught up with the man at the hospital lobby entrance, where he forced the money back into the man's hand. However, this part of the story was not recorded in the video. Speculation: Possibly a Setup to Frame Him Yin Lianhu said his greatest wish now is to find the man who gave him the money, "I can confront him face-to-face to clarify the facts." But Yin Lianhu stated he has been unable to locate the man. Two months have passed, and the man has never contacted him again. Yin Lianhu said he regrets not taking it seriously initially. After the man left, "I quickly forgot about it, and the business card he gave me was thrown away somewhere." He even said he couldn't remember which pharmaceutical company the man represented, "I encounter far too many people like this!" Yin Lianhu suggested the man might not have been a "medical representative" at all, and the whole incident was an act staged by someone close to him to frame him. He believes the video was specifically targeted at him personally. This is because almost all departments in the hospital received a letter in July titled "Why is Yin Lianhu from the Surgery Department so 'Arrogant'?" which contained sharp attacks against him. Yin Lianhu said he does not have the authority to decide which drugs the hospital purchases. Pharmaceutical representatives would only give him money hoping for kickbacks when he prescribes drugs. However, the man in the video was meeting him for the first time. Why would he give money directly? "What benefit could I bring him? Why hasn't he contacted me again?" Yin Lianhu also expressed self-blame for the incident, "I thought it was only two or three hundred yuan," so he didn't take it seriously. He added that he never accepts red envelopes from patients, which can often amount to thousands of yuan. Yin Lianhu was unwilling to discuss whether doctors in the hospital accept drug kickbacks. The only certainty is that pharmaceutical representatives come and go very frequently. "Only the individual knows if they take money." Hospital: Difficult to Punish the Doctor Involved Director Li of the hospital's disciplinary inspection commission confirmed that Yin Lianhu indeed does not have drug procurement authority. The hospital's drug procurement must first be discussed and decided by the Pharmacy Affairs Committee, followed by public tender. Doctors have no decision-making power over the hospital's drug purchases. If pharmaceutical companies want to give money to doctors, it can only be related to the doctors' prescription authority. That is, if the hospital stocks several drugs from different manufacturers with similar effects, the pharmaceutical representative hopes the doctor will prescribe their drug more often to increase sales. Ms. Song from the disciplinary inspection commission said Yin Lianhu is a very capable doctor at the hospital. Receiving such a disc was surprising, but the disc alone cannot serve as evidence for punishment. It would be best to find the pharmaceutical representative and the filmer to testify together. Currently, it cannot be confirmed that Yin Lianhu actually took the money, so the hospital is handling the matter cautiously and has not yet imposed any punishment. However, the investigation will continue. She stated that even if the fact of taking money is established, the hospital would impose penalties, such as fining Yin Lianhu and issuing a批评通报, but demotion or dismissal is unlikely. "After all, being a doctor is a highly technical profession, and it's not appropriate to punish too severely over a few hundred yuan." It is understood that Tongzhou Luhe Hospital has a history of over a hundred years and is currently the largest medical institution in Tongzhou District. Reporter's Investigation: Frequent Visits by Pharmaceutical Representatives at Luhe Hospital The morning before last, the reporter visited Tongzhou Luhe Hospital. A notice was posted at the hospital entrance prohibiting pharmaceutical representatives from entering consultation rooms and administrative departments. However, according to taxi drivers at the entrance, many pharmaceutical representatives enter daily. Having been there long enough, they can spot them at a glance: "The men all carry black square bags, the women carry small shoulder bags." On the desks in several surgical consultation rooms on the first floor of the hospital, scattered glossy drug brochures were found, including for injections and medications. While the reporter was looking at these brochures in an unoccupied consultation room, a male patient waiting for the doctor smiled and asked, "Are you selling drugs?" The man said he often encounters doctors receiving pharmaceutical representatives when he comes for appointments. He mentioned he had previously tried to sell a health product to doctors. According to him, doctors receive kickbacks based on drug sales volume. Drugs are categorized into three types: medical insurance drugs, publicly funded drugs, and self-paid drugs. Generally, doctors do not accept self-paid drugs, making them very difficult to promote. A doctor at the hospital who wished to remain anonymous said it is common for pharmaceutical representatives to visit outpatient clinics, but added, "The hospital manages it very strictly." The doctor also admitted that since the hospital has never penalized a doctor for taking kickbacks from pharmaceutical representatives, he is unclear what the punishment would entail. According to Ms. Song from the disciplinary inspection commission, operability is a major difficulty in managing the prohibition of pharmaceutical representatives entering the hospital, as they are hard to distinguish from ordinary patients by appearance. Despite posted notices, it is impossible to prevent them from entering. She said the hospital has received similar reports before, but due to the difficulty of obtaining evidence, it has been impossible to prove the existence of kickbacks. "We can only rely on the integrity of the pharmaceutical representatives and doctors themselves for self-restraint." She mentioned the hospital publicly praises doctors who proactively hand over kickbacks given by pharmaceutical representatives. Director Li of the disciplinary inspection commission said doctors also value this kind of spiritual reward. In the first half of this year, one doctor turned in 500 yuan. Doctors Taking Kickbacks Could Be Dismissed On April 22, the Ministry of Health issued the "Opinions on Strengthening the Construction of Conduct in the Health Industry," proposing "Eight Prohibitions" for medical personnel. These include prohibiting medical personnel from accepting kickbacks, commissions, and other improper benefits offered by manufacturers or sales personnel of medical devices, drugs, reagents, etc., under any name or form. It stipulates that medical personnel violating these provisions shall be subject to penalties by their employing unit based on the severity, including通报批评, disqualification from annual evaluation or professional title assessment for that year, suspension of appointment, waiting for reassignment, or even dismissal. For licensed physicians, the health administrative department at or above the county level shall, according to Article 37 of the Licensed Physician Law, impose penalties based on severity, including warnings, orders to suspend practice, or even revocation of their practice certificate. If a crime is constituted, the case shall be transferred to judicial authorities for criminal liability. (By Zhang Jie) The Beijing News

Title: I want to ask, my husband is helping his cousin get a loan, and I need to sign. Should I sign? Content: Normally it's a credit loan, not using your house as collateral. You've only been married for 3 months, so the house probably hasn't been mortgaged for long. This situation is very difficult. Actually, I think it's better if you don't sign. Why? Your husband works for his cousin, meaning his economic lifeline is in the cousin's hands. If the cousin asks for a favor, your husband would find it hard to refuse. But with favors like this, there's a fear it could become a bottomless pit. Today it's a 300,000 loan to expand the business, tomorrow an additional 300,000, the day after another 300,000. It becomes very tricky. Moreover, these loans are often interest-first, principal-later. When it matures, you can't easily refuse a renewal because most likely the cousin won't have saved 300,000 to settle it; it will just be a bridge loan renewal. It means unless the cousin strikes it rich, this debt could be endless. Your husband finds it hard to refuse because they're like brothers, and he works for him. But you can. You're the newcomer. You can act like you don't understand social obligations, play the 'bad guy' role, letting your husband show that he tried his best for this matter, but you just won't facilitate it. Of course, there's another scenario: if your husband is genuinely willing and not feeling pressured, then facilitating them is fine. But such things shouldn't happen repeatedly. For business, needing money can be a bottomless pit: when times are good, you need to expand; when times are bad, you need to sustain—both require spending money.

Title: Why did housing prices drop so much during the pandemic? Content: The reasons for this phenomenon are multifaceted. Specifically, they include three aspects: sluggish demand is the root cause of the price drop, reduced income is the direct cause of the price drop, and the lagging effect of economic recovery on housing prices. 1. The fundamental reason for the drop in housing prices lies in sluggish demand. Essentially, the weakness in housing prices is directly related to reduced demand. When demand for buying houses is strong, prices remain stable and continuously rise. When demand is sluggish, prices fall accordingly, showing a certain degree of decline. This is the root cause of the housing price drop. 2. The direct cause of the housing price drop is the reduction in people's income. The immediate reason for the price drop is the decrease in people's income. Affected by the pandemic, many people's incomes have decreased to some extent compared to before, which has reduced their ability to buy houses. This situation directly leads to the drop in housing prices. Therefore, the direct cause of the price drop is the reduction in people's income. 3. The pulling effect of economic recovery on housing prices has a lag, so prices remain sluggish recently. There is a very close relationship between the economic situation and housing prices. Specifically, when the economy is doing well, housing prices can remain stable and rise. When the economy is poor, housing prices fall. However, the positive impact of economic recovery on housing prices has a certain lag and cannot directly drive price increases in the short term. This is the situation we are currently facing. Only after some time will the pulling effect of economic recovery on housing prices become evident, gradually restoring and increasing prices.

Title: When the A-share market reaches a certain point level, what are the differences in returns for different groups of people? Content: When the A-share market is at different point levels, the returns for different groups of people vary significantly. For long-term value investors, if they enter the market when the A-share market is at a relatively low point, their assets are likely to steadily appreciate as the market rises. For example, by investing in high-quality blue-chip stocks in undervalued market intervals and holding them long-term, they can reap substantial returns when the market recovers to a reasonable or even high level. Long-term investors who enter at high points may face short-term fluctuations, but as long as they hold stocks with sound fundamentals, they still have the opportunity to achieve steady asset growth over the long run. Short-term traders are more directly affected by the market level. During an A-share market rally, short-term traders who buy on the rise may profit quickly, but if they fail to sell in time at high points, they can quickly lose profits or even incur losses as the market falls. If they try to bottom-fish too early during a market decline, they may suffer larger losses if the market continues to drop. Some ultra-short-term traders who rely on technical analysis operate based on indicator signals at different market levels; if their judgments are accurate, they can gain from price differences in the short term, but misjudgments can lead to immediate losses. The situation for institutional investors is more complex. Large institutions, with their substantial capital, have the ability to gradually build positions when the A-share market is low and see their portfolio values increase as the market rises. They diversify investments to reduce risks; at different market levels, some assets may profit, while others may break even or incur small losses, but overall, reasonable allocation can help achieve certain return targets. Smaller institutions may be more flexible, precisely targeting certain hot sectors at appropriate market levels to capture阶段性收益, but they are also more susceptible to significant uncertainty due to rapid market changes. The return performance of ordinary retail investors varies widely at different A-share market levels. Some retail investors hesitate to enter at low points, missing opportunities; others blindly follow trends and buy at high points, becoming trapped when the market falls. Some lack professional knowledge and investment discipline, frequently trading at different market levels, often resulting in losses. However, experienced retail investors who can control risks adjust their positions reasonably based on market level changes, striving for better returns amid market fluctuations.

Title: What to do when the phone shows an unauthorized application? Content: There is a setting in the phone settings, check and see there is an option for you to choose application software access, open it and there is an automatic start, inside there is a first-time inquiry to confirm, see OK, what is unauthorized? If your phone has built-in permission management (usually in the phone's built-in security management software, permission management, and application settings these three places), go in and authorize directly. If it doesn't have this function, then root it. However, after rooting, most phones will no longer be under warranty, and you cannot directly upgrade the system online in the system settings.

Title: 【Counter-Terrorism Mini-Class】How to Prevent Explosive Terrorist Attacks in Crowded Places? Content: ↑ Click "Kaiping Public Security" above to follow us. If one day you find a suspicious explosive device in a crowded place like a shopping mall, do you know what you should do? The consequences of an explosive terrorist attack, once it occurs, would be unimaginable. Today, let's learn together how to prevent and respond to explosive terrorist attacks. Identifying Suspicious Explosives: Without touching the suspicious object, follow three steps: look, listen, and smell. 1. Look. Observe meticulously from the outside in, from near to far, from top to bottom, without missing anything, to identify and judge whether the suspicious item or part contains a hidden explosive device. 2. Listen. In a quiet environment, listen carefully for any unusual sounds. 3. Smell. Black powder contains sulfur, which emits a smell of rotten eggs (hydrogen sulfide). Homemade ammonium nitrate explosives have a distinct smell of ammonia water due to the decomposition of ammonium nitrate. Where might explosives be placed? 1. Landmark buildings. Inside or outside landmark buildings or nearby structures. 2. Major event venues. Places like large sports games, parades, performances, pilgrimages, exhibitions, etc. 3. Crowded places. Locations with relatively dense populations, such as stadiums, theaters, hotels, athlete villages, shopping malls, supermarkets, stations, airports, docks, schools, etc. 4. Public entertainment venues. Hotels, restaurants, bath centers, karaoke bars, and other places easy to hide in and accessible to miscellaneous people. 5. Other easily accessible places. Locations that are easy to approach and can achieve the purpose of the explosion, such as hospitals, parks, scenic spots, etc. 6. Various transportation vehicles. Cars, trains, subways, etc. 7. Other daily items. Inside luggage, packages, food, handbags, and various daily necessities. What to do if you find a suspicious explosive? Follow these points to effectively protect your safety: 1. Evacuate in an orderly manner and stay rational. Pay attention to the safety evacuation signs and indicators in the venue. 2. Do not be greedy for possessions. Any property is insignificant compared to life safety. 3. Act cautiously. Do not crowd together, do not gather to watch, go to a safe place first, then look for companions. 4. Report to the police promptly. Assist the public security organs in the investigation by objectively and detailedly describing what you saw. When facing an explosion threat, adhere to the 5-character mantra: 1. Believe, "Better to believe it exists than to believe it doesn't"; 2. Fast, evacuate quickly; 3. Detail, observe suspicious people, things, and events carefully; 4. Report, call the police quickly; 5. Record, use a camera, phone, etc., to record the "scene." Source: Guangdong Counter-Terrorism Editor: Liu Yiting First Review: Wei Ping Second Review: Lin Yan Third Review: Chen Yuqiang

Title: Guangdong Enjoy Life Critical Illness Insurance Policy Content: The Guangdong Enjoy Life new definition critical illness insurance launched by Pacific Life Insurance has attracted widespread attention. As a savings-type whole life critical illness insurance, it mainly provides coverage for minor illnesses and critical illnesses. It is particularly noteworthy that this policy offers an additional payout of 100% of the basic sum insured for three high-incidence diseases in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, demonstrating attention to regional specific needs. However, after an in-depth analysis of the Guangdong Enjoy Life insurance contract, we found several shortcomings. Firstly, the insurance waiting period is as long as 180 days, which is relatively long in the critical illness insurance market. For claims occurring during the waiting period that are not due to accidental injury, the insurance company does not assume liability; therefore, a longer waiting period means the insured actually receives coverage for a shorter period. This provision is slightly inferior compared to other products. Secondly, Guangdong Enjoy Life has age restrictions for additional critical illness payouts; an additional 50% of the basic sum insured is only paid if the critical illness is diagnosed before the age of 50. Compared to old definition critical illness insurance products that offer additional payouts for critical illnesses diagnosed before age 60 or even 80, its terms appear stricter. Furthermore, although Guangdong Enjoy Life's minor illness coverage includes 50 diseases and can be paid up to 5 times, each payout is only 20% of the basic sum insured. Currently, many critical illness insurance products on the market offer minor illness payout ratios as high as 45%; in comparison, Guangdong Enjoy Life's payout ratio seems relatively low. Considering the above factors comprehensively, the coverage of Guangdong Enjoy Life is not comprehensive enough, and combined with its price, the cost-effectiveness is relatively low. For consumers seeking high cost-effective critical illness insurance products, it may be necessary to further explore other options in the market.

Title: Influenza (flu) has been etiologically confirmed to be caused by influenza virus infection, while the common cold has variable causes. Besides invading cells of the upper respiratory tract, the influenza virus can also invade the digestive tract and other parts of the body, causing different clinical symptoms, which has also been pathologically verified. The self-limiting nature of a cold comes from the generation of specific antibodies in the body, taking about 5-7 days. Western medicine is not very effective at preventing the virus from invading cells; instead, traditional Chinese medicines that clear heat and detoxify have antimetabolic effects that can alleviate viral invasion. I personally recommend using antipyretic and analgesic drugs in the early stages of a cold to relieve symptoms, but a fever <38.5°C can promote the immune system and antibody production. A hot bath is also a method, so it's a matter of opinion. Title: My home is on the 2nd floor, why is the kitchen drain backing up even when not in use? Content: We live in a 7-story building, we are on the 2nd floor. The drain often gets clogged, it has clogged 3 times this month already. Every time, my floor is covered in water, it backs up even when not in use. So why doesn't the 1st floor clog or have backflow? Could it be that my own pipe is clogged? How can I block my own drain outlet? I can't afford to unclog it anymore, 3 times a month. The upstairs neighbors aren't careful, there's nothing I can do. Reasons: 1. There is a blockage. It's very likely there is a blockage further down the main sewage pipe. When sewage flow is obstructed, the wastewater will back up to the outlet closest to the blockage point. You can't handle this situation yourself, you can only call a drain cleaning company. 2. Main pipe blockage. If you live on the 2nd floor and sewage backs up into your home, it indicates a blockage in the pipe below the 2nd floor. This is a main pipe blockage, meaning the main drain from the 1st to 7th floor is blocked. The blockage is usually located between the drain manhole cover and the 90-degree bend under the 1st floor. That's why backflow often happens on the 2nd floor. 3. Poor hydraulic conditions. Residential drainage is generally gravity-fed. Wastewater from sanitary fixtures first goes into the vertical drain stack, then into the horizontal main drain, and finally into the outdoor inspection chamber. 4. Significant building settlement. During construction, the slope of the horizontal main drain usually meets standard grades, allowing wastewater flow velocity to reach self-cleaning speed. Some settlement due to the building's weight and foundation is normal initially. However, if design/construction didn't prioritize this and take measures, significant settlement can occur, crushing or pressuring the drain outlet pipe, reducing its slope or even creating a reverse slope, leading to poor drainage. Additional Information: Drain unclogging is generally categorized into several types: 1. Foreign object blockage solution: Accidental drops of objects or installation errors causing blockages. Usually resolved using a drain auger/snake or pipe replacement. 2. Scale/Sediment blockage solution: Over time, pipes can develop scale/sediment buildup, reducing the inner diameter and affecting flow. This requires high-pressure water jetting to clean the pipe walls and enlarge the diameter. This is the most common issue for kitchen drains. 3. Poor hydraulic conditions solution: This should be considered during the design phase, accounting for adverse factors. Drainpipe layout should meet optimal hydraulic conditions. Pay special attention to: connecting the vertical stack to the horizontal main using two 45-degree bends or a 90-degree bend with a radius不小于4 times the pipe diameter. Horizontal pipes should have straight connections, minimize bends. The diameter and slope of the horizontal main should be appropriately larger. Your kitchen drain probably has a P-trap (water seal). The water overflowing likely comes from the water trapped in the P-trap. When upstairs neighbors drain water, it flows down, compressing air in the pipe, increasing pressure in the main stack on lower floors. This pressure acts on the water in your P-trap, causing it to overflow. The 1st floor doesn't overflow probably because their branch line lacks a P-trap. It's recommended to contact the property management for an on-site inspection. Reasons why lower floors (e.g., 1st floor) don't have backflow: 1. Standard practice might make the 1st floor's drain independent. So a main line blockage doesn't affect the 1st floor. The blockage could be anywhere in the pipe leading downstairs from your unit. 2. If the lower floors' drains are not independent, then the 1st floor doesn't backflow because the blockage is between the 2nd and 1st floors. In either case, your unit becomes the outlet. Water from upstairs or your own use will flow back into your home. If you block your outlet in desperation, the backflow will likely happen on the 3rd floor. This situation involves a main pipe blockage, which is difficult to fix yourself. Call a drain cleaning company; you can usually find their numbers posted in the building. We had the exact same situation. It's because the 2nd floor has the main stack connection. When the main pipe clogs, water backs up into the 2nd floor. It's driving me crazy. The 1st floor has an independent drain line, so if the main pipe clogs, it directly floods the 2nd floor.

Title: So Angry I Have to Vent Content: Arrived at Shanghai Pudong Airport at 12:30 AM, wanted to take the night airport bus to Shanghai Hongqiao High-Speed Rail Station. Ended up getting lost right after exiting the gate. There were people constantly asking if I needed a taxi along the way, but since I was alone it wasn't cost-effective and I was a bit scared. I walked down the same road twice and still couldn't find the way. Then a guy came up and asked if I wanted a taxi. I said no. He asked what I wanted to take, I said the bus. He said the late-night buses at Pudong Airport had already stopped running. I said okay. He grabbed my suitcase and started walking. I said I didn't need a taxi, it wasn't cost-effective alone. He said he'd find someone to share the ride with me. He went around asking people if they were going to Hongqiao Airport. Eventually found two uncles who were reluctant. He talked to them for about twenty minutes and convinced them. The three of us followed him to his car in the parking lot. (At this point I meant to ask the price! But I checked DiDi myself and it showed 166 RMB. I thought splitting three ways would be 60-70 RMB per person max, which seemed reasonable, so I didn't ask.) After arriving at Hongqiao, when paying, he said a DiDi would cost 300 RMB, plus his 25 RMB parking fee at Pudong Airport, plus some other unspecified charges, and asked me for 190 RMB, and the two uncles for 190 RMB total. I said shouldn't it be per person? He said that wouldn't be fair: you alone take one car, they two take one car together, so it's half and half. The two uncles naturally thought he made sense, paid and left. In the middle of the night, I didn't dare argue further, paid and let it go. I would have been better off taking a taxi myself for 166 RMB. Getting back to Suzhou cost 250 RMB. Now I deeply feel like a 380 [fool] and Hongqiao High-Speed Rail Station wasn't even open – doesn't he know that since he picks up customers every day? [Crying emoji] Now I'm sitting on a stone pillar outside the station, my period flowing heavily, it's really awful, and there's not even a bathroom nearby. Advising everyone to always ask the price upfront, I was really such an idiot, but more importantly, stay safe.

Title: Why is your loan still being rejected despite continuous bank credit easing? Content: Based in Jining Zaozhuang, working in the loan assistance industry. Why are so many people still being rejected even though banks are easing credit? Banks aren't actually easing credit - the requirements remain the same, but everyone's credit records are worse than before. Each bank has different credit requirements: some focus heavily on debt, some pay attention to debt but emphasize credit inquiries more, some banks prefer customers with housing provident funds, some prefer individual businesses, and others prefer limited liability companies. Due to these different preferences, people unfamiliar with loans often apply and end up with a blacklisted credit record before even getting the loan approved.

Title: Professor Qu Limin from Beijing University of Chinese Medicine questions modern health check-ups, arguing that they are essentially a commercial activity that can lead to major losses over minor gains, turning minor illnesses into major ones that are difficult to cure. In today's society, health check-ups have become commonplace, with almost everyone participating in the hope of ensuring their health through these examinations. Many people, due to high work pressure and influenced by others' emphasis on the importance of check-ups, blindly follow the trend and sign up for various health check-up packages. During the check-up process, faced with numerous tests, people feel both anticipation and anxiety. After receiving their reports, many discover minor health issues, such as high blood lipids or liver function indicators nearing the upper limit, which often leads to anxiety. This prompts them to reflect on their lifestyle and consider adjusting their dietary habits. Similar situations are not uncommon; some people, upon discovering minor abnormalities, become overly worried, which negatively impacts their mental health. Professor Qu's viewpoint reminds everyone that while health check-ups can provide certain health information, they should not be the sole reliance. More importantly, maintaining health through a healthy lifestyle, keeping a positive mindset, and rationally dealing with check-up results can help avoid unnecessary panic.

Title: Is Archaeology a Good Major for Employment? Content: The field of archaeology is relatively narrow, but it is a highly specialized area. Graduates can choose to work as teachers or researchers in universities or research institutions, engaging in teaching and scientific research. Additionally, they can work in museums, auction houses, antique shops, or customs, involved in cultural relic preservation, antique appraisal, or auction-related work. Some graduates opt to pursue further studies, such as a master's degree or studying abroad, to enhance their academic level and prepare for the future. Through in-depth research and academic exchanges, they can strengthen their competitiveness and lay a solid foundation for career development. The employment rate for archaeology majors is relatively low. 61% of graduates find jobs before or immediately after graduation, while 38% find employment within one year after graduation. On a 10-point scale, the fresh graduate employment rate for this major is 6.20, indicating that its employment rate is moderately low compared to other majors. Nevertheless, the employment prospects for archaeology majors are not entirely bleak. By broadening employment fields, such as transitioning to cultural heritage protection, cultural industry development, or cultural tourism, graduates can find more career opportunities. It is worth noting that graduates in archaeology need to possess solid professional knowledge and skills, as well as good communication abilities and teamwork spirit, to stand out in the job market. Furthermore, with increasing public awareness of cultural heritage protection and the development of the tourism industry, the demand for archaeology graduates may rise in certain areas. Therefore, students should focus on cultivating interdisciplinary knowledge and practical skills during their studies to increase their competitiveness.

Title: Experiencing the Shockwaves of the Tibet Pandemic at the Source of the River in Yushu Content: Author: Aqiong Early August is the golden season on the high plateau at the source of the river—Yushu—a time of lush grass, singing birds, and brilliant colors. Yushu had just finished its traditional horse racing festival and cultural tourism festival. The festive atmosphere had not yet receded; local people, still wanting more, turned to the embrace of nature. Various groups—family groups, unit groups, groups of friends and relatives, classmate groups, retiree groups, etc.—streamed continuously towards the grasslands for outings, gatherings at resorts, all with the aim of enjoying the natural scenery and experiencing a pastoral, idyllic life. Every weekend, Batang grassland was filled with wisps of smoke from cooking fires, birds singing and flowers fragrant, cattle covering the hillsides—a picture of tranquil times, speaking volumes about the peaceful days of a prosperous nation and contented people. Planes at Batang Airport took off and landed, receiving and sending off guests from all directions. Tourists and self-driving caravans from various places shuttled through the streets and alleys of Yushu and its surrounding scenic spots. Yushu, since ancient times an unshakably important transportation hub, is the famous intersection of the Tang-Tibet Ancient Road and the Tea-Horse Road. Now, with the addition of National Highway 214, the summer in River Source Yushu seemed even busier and more lively. According to my annual seasonal plan, at this time, I had prepared my camping gear for food, lodging, and travel, intending to live in a tent and return home in early September. I had already been living on Batang grassland for about twenty days. This year, the weather was favorable—temperatures were higher, rainfall was less—suited for outdoor living. Thus, this year's camping life proceeded more smoothly and satisfactorily than in previous years. My tent was pitched on a flat grassy area beside National Highway 214, near the Baqu River. Bushes about a meter tall grew along the riverbank, like a fence, forming a natural barrier. Nearby were small herdsmen's villages, and on the surrounding cliffs and rocky mountains, there were many maroon-colored monastic retreats for practitioners in seclusion. From the villages came the occasional barking of domestic dogs and the deep, throaty 'mooing' calls between cows and their calves, closing the distance between this nomadic life and nature, making me feel as if I were a shepherdess belonging to one of the families. Tent resorts, one紧挨着another, set up various splendid tents to attract tourists. From day to night, came sounds of joyful singing and laughter, with Tibetan songs playing nonstop from sound systems. Stray dogs wandered in twos and threes, patrolling back and forth in front of the resorts and camping tents. After a few trips, they became familiar faces at the tent doors, and you inadvertently became their owner. I spent my days contentedly, savoring the time,陶醉于the beauty of blue skies, white clouds, and lush green grass. I welcomed the morning glow and bid farewell to the evening sunset, lingering in the interplay of light and shadow. At night, the bright lights of the airport contrasted with the darkness; the stars in the azure sky and all things seemed to fall into a quiet, peaceful atmosphere, with only the murmuring sound of the river, like a soft lullaby, accompanying people to sleep. On August 7th, breaking news pushed to my phone: Tibet, once considered a COVID-free pure land, had discovered four infected individuals in Pulan County, Ngari Prefecture. Epidemiological investigation showed the variant was Omicron BA.76, the first time discovered in China. Online attention and discussion began. As the pandemic in Tibet expanded, the situation became serious, raising people's alertness. The virus gradually spread to neighboring areas, also approaching River Source Yushu. As the saying goes, 'misfortune befalls the neighboring pond.' Various places began taking defensive measures. The Yushu local government sprang into action, treating it as a formidable enemy and implementing major measures; preliminary preventive measures were put in place. Unexpectedly, just six days later, after noon on August 14th, Yushu discovered its first positive COVID case. This news caused an uproar instantly. In a moment, the news spread like the wind throughout every corner of Yushu. People couldn't believe it. Since the pandemic began in 2019, although it had surged and receded for nearly three years, River Source Yushu had passed through safely time and again, so we always felt the virus was far from us. Suddenly, the virus had arrived. Everyone found it hard to accept at first. However, after the initial shock, people started taking precautions: wearing masks, avoiding crowds, not roaming around unnecessarily, buying staple foods. They were already consciously preparing for prevention and control. This was because China, having undergone the baptism of the Wuhan battle and the experience of dozens of local battles, had 'influenced by what one sees and hears' in River Source Yushu, which naturally adopted a relatively scientific set of combined prevention and control measures, waiting for the government's order to act in unison across the prefecture. On August 15th, measures including nucleic acid testing across the prefecture, close contact tracing, clinical treatment, traffic control, news media reporting, ensuring supply channels for daily necessities, and requesting external assistance were all implemented simultaneously. Social mobilization capacity was activated. Staff from sub-district offices, communities, volunteers, reallocation of medical resources, recall of retired medical personnel, recruitment of volunteers—all these tasks proceeded methodically, marking the beginning of the River Source Yushu battle and demonstrating the effectiveness of the local government's and various departments' mobilization and coordination capabilities. Faced with the sudden pandemic, we stranded tourists on Batang grassland did not frantically try to find a way home. Instead, together with the local herdsmen of Batang, we joined the anti-pandemic effort: not running around, maintaining personal protection, going for daily nucleic acid tests on time, following the township government's arrangements, trying not to cause obstructions, traveling over twenty kilometers to the government-designated supply point to purchase food, and solving difficulties ourselves. In the face of hardship, everyone helped each other, closing the distance between people. When food was running low, households with surplus would share some. Helping charge your phone, township government staff coming to inquire about your well-being, concerned calls from family and friends one after another—these touching small things were all spiritual comforts to get through the difficult times. Every day, I followed the pandemic developments in Yushu on my phone. Tiny Batang Township was mobilized within a day: resorts and small supermarkets ceased operations, grassroots Party organizations played their role, herdsmen Party members took the lead actively, organizing personnel to set up checkpoints at various intersections and bridgeheads, flying the national flag, pulling up yellow警戒线for guard duty. Village-level leaders arranged herdsmen patrol teams, using private cars to take turns patrolling and standing guard on National Highway 214, strictly prohibiting strangers from appearing on Batang grassland and preventing idle personnel from entering Yushu city proper, creating an atmosphere of being 'scared by every bush or tree.' Isn't this series of strict defensive measures a miniature version of the Chinese government's COVID-19 prevention and control model? China's prevention and control measures involve finding a small number of cases, quickly acting to block the virus's spread, and daily nucleic acid testing for all. Similarly, River Source Yushu pressed the pause button and adopted a static management mode. On September 2nd, through the efforts of the township government and coordination with the city government, nearly a hundred of us stranded on Batang grassland finally embarked on the journey home—seemingly far away yet close at hand. We were grateful that the government, despite its busy schedule, considered us, handled our case specially without a one-size-fits-all rejection, allowing us to bid farewell to the anticipated autumn chill and food-scarce camping life and return home even before the entire city was unsealed. After a dozen-minute drive into the city, the roads were empty, the entire city quiet. The formerly bustling streets were suddenly still. Traffic lights at intersections operated寂寞地as usual. Police cars and officers stood ready at the intersections. I felt like a triumphant returner without a welcome ceremony, victoriously returning home. The victor wasn't me, but the pandemic prevention and control workers. After returning, reflecting on the more than half month of pandemic prevention experienced on Batang grassland, I firmly believe that River Source Yushu will surely overcome the pandemic. From small things, one can see the larger picture. From a small village like Batang, one can see the entire China's determination not to 'lie flat' in pandemic prevention, and see the measures of not coexisting with the virus. Whenever a local outbreak occurs, China's prevention and control measures are to quickly block the virus's spread. To achieve this requires the combination of many elements for effective联动and effective results. In the Batang Township government and its people, we see the capability of the Chinese government and the strength of China. One is the governance capacity of the Chinese government, the other is China's unique culture. The combination of the two is a powerful alliance, invincible and unconquerable. The organizational capacity of the Chinese government, the coordination ability from the central government to local governments, and from local governments to grassroots organizations and the masses is extraordinary. It achieves vertical and horizontal coordination, a nationwide chess game, everywhere demonstrating the superiority of the socialist system, which is unmatched by other countries. China's unique culture is the sense of responsibility that acknowledges 'when an avalanche occurs, no single snowflake is innocent'—the ordinary people who dare to take responsibility and face disasters head-on. They possess the sentiment that 'every man has a share of responsibility for the rise and fall of his country,' and there is also a high degree of altruism existing among ordinary Chinese people, which同样forms the backbone of Chinese culture. They weigh interests in matters of right and wrong, sacrificing some of their own convenience for the greater convenience of more people. It is this excellent culture of great pattern that nourishes the Chinese spirit, giving rise to the confidence of being united as one, making concerted efforts, and handling the pandemic battle adeptly. As the pandemic situation improves, River Source Yushu is expected to clear cases. May life return to normal soon. Eagerly looking forward to the early passing of the pandemic in Tibet, restoring its original sanctity and beauty. September 11, 2022, at my residence in Yushu.

Content Title: After a company is deregistered, is everything really settled? Release Date: 2025-01-14 14:30:34 Content Status: Review Completed Content Type: Multimedia Industry: Digital Employment_Talent Employment_- Author Name: Zhong Jiali Finance and Tax Q Owner Name: Zhong Jiali Finance and Tax Q Content Number Type: Personal Content Details: It's not that everything is settled once a company is deregistered. CERTIFICATE. Is it that after deregistering a problematic business license, everything is settled? Suppose the company is in debt. I go and deregister the company. Then I am no longer in debt. What are you thinking? That's wishful thinking. In situations like this, you cannot deregister. Unless, before a case is filed against you, your business license is gone. But they can choose not to sue the entity and instead sue you, the person who incurred the debt. It's different. Can a case still be filed? Let me give another example. A company in Heilongjiang evaded taxes. CERTIFICATE. They deregistered the company. The company was forced by the tax bureau to reinstate its tax registration. A company in Fuzhou was deregistered. But it was found to have income that was not declared. The tax bureau directly notified the company's legal representative to pay back taxes. Also, a gas station in Ziyang, Sichuan, because it issued false invoices. At this point, after issuing them, it deregistered the company. But it was eventually caught and fined over 7 million. Then someone asks, 'My company is already deregistered, where can they find me?' If you are suspected of issuing false invoices or tax evasion, for example, your company issued invoices. CERTIFICATE. The company that received your invoices will definitely trace it back. And this data of yours is not cleared from the tax bureau's inventory when you deregister. That is to say, it shows as deregistered, but the original invoicing data, tax data, everything is still archived in the system. It just means your status is deregistered, no longer operating. It doesn't mean your past messes are clean. CERTIFICATE. So if you deregister the company with loose ends or problems, there is still a possibility you will be investigated. It is absolutely not 'everything is settled'. Content Understanding Label: Non-serious Livelihood Content

Title: What does it mean when a laptop shows a 💻 blue screen upon startup? Content: There are many reasons for a blue screen. It could be due to incompatible external devices, or it could be a system issue. I suggest you first unplug any external devices, then reinstall the system, and try again. The main causes of a computer blue screen are: 1. Loose hardware leading to poor contact, such as memory and graphics card. 2. Incompatible drivers causing frequent blue screens, usually graphics card drivers. 3. The computer is infected with a virus. 4. The hard drive is damaged, or other hardware has issues.

Title: I just bought a new laptop, but 360 Antivirus shows it has been protected for 202 days. Content: 1. Some computer manufacturers pre-install certain software when preselling personal computers. Common examples include Windows, input methods, browsers, antivirus software, etc. 360 Antivirus calculates the days from the installation date, so it might show 254 days. 2. 360 Antivirus might have encountered an issue while reading the system time or read the computer time incorrectly. 3. It could be a used machine, but the probability is very low. Download 360 Hardware Master or Ludashi to check the hard drive's read/write count, which can help determine if it's a used machine.

Title: What Does a Stock Gap Down Mean? Content: A stock gap down means that the stock price opens lower than the lowest price of the previous trading day. A detailed explanation is as follows: A stock gap down refers to the opening price being lower than the lowest price of the previous trading day. This usually indicates that the selling pressure in the market is relatively strong, and investors have a more pessimistic outlook on the market prospects. This situation can be influenced by various factors, such as company performance, industry trends, and the macroeconomic environment. When a stock gaps down, investors need to pay close attention to relevant news and announcements to understand the specific reasons causing the stock price to fall. Furthermore, technical analysis is an important tool for judging stock trends. Analyzing technical indicators can help investors better grasp market dynamics and trends. It is worth noting that a gap down could also be part of a market adjustment. Investors need to remain calm, rationally analyze the market situation, and avoid blindly following the crowd or panic selling. Before making any investment decisions, investors should fully understand their own risk tolerance and investment objectives in order to make wise decisions. In summary, a stock gap down reflects an emotional reaction in the market, which may be the result of multiple factors working together. When facing this situation, investors should remain calm, rationally analyze the market conditions, and make decisions that align with their investment goals and risk tolerance.

Title: Building a Sports Power Province with Mountain Characteristics and Ethnic Features, Guizhou is Doing it This Way! Content: With the holding of the 11th Guizhou Provincial Games, after years of effort, Guizhou's public service level for fitness, covering urban and rural areas and benefiting all people, has continuously improved. The structure of competitive sports, both summer and winter events, has been continuously optimized. The integration of sports and education has deepened, the sports industry has accelerated its development, and the creation of a national sports tourism demonstration zone is steadily advancing. The construction of Guizhou as a sports power province with mountain and ethnic characteristics has achieved phased results. Recently, after consultation between the National Sports Administration and the Guizhou Provincial People's Government, the "Cooperation Agreement on Accelerating the High-Quality Development of Guizhou's Mountain Outdoor Characteristic Sports" was signed. The two parties will focus on the "14th Five-Year Plan for Sports Development" and the needs of Guizhou's high-quality economic and social development. By fully leveraging Guizhou's mountain resource advantages, collaborating closely, and forming synergy, they will jointly promote the high-quality development of Guizhou's mountain outdoor characteristic sports and the construction of the national sports tourism demonstration zone. They aim to build Guizhou into an internationally renowned, domestically first-class mountain tourism and outdoor sports tourism destination, promote the rapid and healthy development of Guizhou's sports undertakings and the sports industry, and contribute Guizhou's strength to the new journey of building a sports power. Leveraging Mountain Resource Advantages – Gaining Good Health in Beautiful Scenery Recently, Guizhou's "Beautiful Countryside" basketball tournament sparked widespread online discussion due to its lively atmosphere comparable to an NBA game, and was praised by Foreign Ministry spokesperson Zhao Lijian as having "pulled out all the stops on the atmosphere." In June 2021, the "Beautiful Countryside" basketball league, as a provincial-level independent IP event in Guizhou, attracted public attention immediately upon its launch, progressing from townships to county and district levels, then to prefectural and city levels, and finally to the provincial level. Along with the captivating games, Guizhou's beautiful rural landscapes, colorful cultural customs, and the people's spirit in pursuing a better and healthier life were also displayed to the world. Village-level competitions exhibit an international flair, and mass sports release new vitality, relying on years of Guizhou's implementation of the national fitness strategy, full efforts to promote the "Six Around" project for national fitness, and focus on building a higher-level public service system for national fitness. It is reported that during the "13th Five-Year Plan" period, Guizhou had already achieved full coverage of the "Rural Sports Project." Most townships and administrative villages have built a standard basketball court, equipped with a standard basketball hoop and two outdoor table tennis tables. In 2022, the selection event for the Tongren City marathon event of the "I Want to Go to the Provincial Games – Community Sports Games" was held on the Tongren Rural Revitalization Industrial Belt Marathon Smart Track. Compared to other marathons, this 43-kilometer professional marathon track connects the mountains, fields, rivers, and villages of Bijiang District and Jiangkou County in Tongren City. The scenery along the way allows participants not only to feel the joy brought by sports but also to feast their eyes during the intense competition. After more than a decade of development, Guizhou's mountain outdoor sports have not only accumulated numerous brand events but have also achieved significant results in the construction of mountain outdoor sports infrastructure. Facilities such as 100 ecological sports parks, 100 auto camping bases, thousands of miles of fitness green trails, and smart marathon tracks have strongly promoted the "15-minute" fitness circle, allowing the public to gain good health amidst beautiful scenery. According to statistics, by the end of 2021, Guizhou had established 1,457 sports social organizations at all levels, trained over 4,000 social sports instructors at various levels annually, built 45 national fitness activity centers, 5,628 national fitness activity stations (points), nearly 8,000 kilometers of fitness trails, cycling paths, and hiking trails, 15,478 indoor and outdoor public fitness facilities in urban streets, 16,437 farmer sports fitness projects in townships and administrative villages (communities). The per capita sports场地 area in the province reached 2.06 square meters, and the number of football fields reached 0.82 per 10,000 people. The number and scale of sports venues have significantly increased, their urban-rural distribution has become more balanced, and fitness events and activities accessible to the public have become increasingly rich. Leveraging Mountain Resource Advantages – Assisting in the Cultivation of Competitive Sports Talents On July 2, 19-year-old athlete Long Jianguo from Rongjiang, Guizhou, won a gold medal with a time of 5.23 seconds in the 2022 International Federation of Sport Climbing (IFSC) World Cup Sport Climbing competition, demonstrating "Chinese Speed" to the world. Since sport climbing joined the Olympic family, the national sport climbing training team has visited Guizhou multiple times for talent selection and training. In fact, Guizhou, with its unique natural, climatic, and geographical conditions, has always been a preferred location for the National Sports Administration's preparation for top-level competitions. "Guizhou is mostly mountainous, with interspersed hills and basins. The climate conditions and natural environment are comfortable and pleasant, with excellent training environment indicators, suitable for year-round outdoor training. Furthermore, there are training bases at different altitudes within the province, including plateau, sub-plateau, and low-altitude areas, allowing for alternating training within a short time," explained Gan Chunlong, Director of the Guizhou Provincial Sports Science Research Institute. Since the State Council Document No. 2 (2012) supported Guizhou in building a national ecological multi-gradient plateau sports training demonstration base, the province currently possesses the National Boxing Guizhou Sports Training Base – Qingzhen Sports Training Base, the National Canoe Sprint Guizhou Sports Training Base – Hongfeng Lake Water Sports Training Base, the National Canoe Slalom Qiandongnan Sports Training Base – Xiashi Slalom Training Base, as well as the Laowang Mountain Ecological Multi-gradient Sports Training Base, Liupanshui Yeyuhai Plateau Sports Training Base, Rongjiang Gymnastics Training Base, Weining Plateau Athletics Training Base, and others. These uniquely advantageous park-style sports training bases, along with good logistical support, attract a large number of national teams for training every year. In the 2021 Tokyo Olympics canoeing events, the Chinese team achieved excellent results: 1 gold, 2 silvers, 3 sixth places, and 2 eighth places. Prior to that, the national water sports team had undergone a 101-day winter training at the Laowang Mountain Ecological Multi-gradient Sports Training Base. At the 14th National Games mountain bike competition, Mi Jiujiang, an athlete from the Guizhou Wheel Trace Bicycle Sports Club, was the first to cross the finish line, creating history. The good results stem from continuous innovation in Guizhou sports. Title: Is laser therapy suitable for vulvar leukoplakia? Content: "Is laser therapy suitable for vulvar leukoplakia?" In outpatient clinics, patients with vulvar leukoplakia often ask this question. So today, let's discuss the effectiveness of laser therapy for vulvar leukoplakia. Is laser therapy suitable for vulvar leukoplakia? Laser treatment for vulvar leukoplakia uses the energy of high-frequency laser beams on the affected area, generating internal heat to kill diseased cells and achieve therapeutic goals. This therapy can temporarily relieve symptoms like itching and pain caused by vulvar leukoplakia, but it has certain drawbacks. High recurrence rate: Vulvar leukoplakia is a disease caused by nutritional disturbances in the basal layer cells of the vulva. While laser therapy can alleviate symptoms to some extent, it struggles to address the underlying cellular nutritional issues, treating the symptoms but not the root cause, leading to a high recurrence rate. Some patients may experience symptom recurrence or worsening after treatment. Variable efficacy: Clinically, some patients experience temporary symptom relief after laser therapy, while others see no effect. This is mainly due to significant differences in disease type, stage, and patient constitution among individuals with vulvar leukoplakia. Adverse reactions: Repeated laser treatments can cause skin damage, such as local skin fibrosis and aggravated mucosal injuries, leading to vulvar redness, swelling, dryness, burning pain, and worsening the condition. Is laser therapy suitable for vulvar leukoplakia? In summary, laser therapy has disadvantages including a high recurrence rate, variable efficacy, and potential adverse reactions. Therefore, patients with vulvar leukoplakia should cautiously choose laser therapy. How to treat vulvar leukoplakia comprehensively? Vulvar leukoplakia is a complex and stubborn chronic disease. To eliminate symptoms, completely eradicate the病灶 (lesion), and prevent recurrence after recovery, patients are advised to opt for Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) herbal treatments. TCM therapy involves classification by type and stage, and treatment based on syndrome differentiation. It can unblock obstructed blood vessels in the vulvar basal layer, thereby resolving cellular nutritional disturbances and repairing damaged cells. Simultaneously, combining internal and external medication eliminates various discomfort symptoms. This therapy involves no surgery or injections, causes no harm or side effects to the body, enhances physical constitution, and treats the disease from the inside out, promoting early recovery for patients. Kunming Liangfang Vulvar Leukoplakia Research Center is a diagnostic and treatment hospital for complex recurrent vulvar leukoplakia in Southwest China. It is also the "Vulvar Leukoplakia Joint Diagnosis and Treatment Center" established through a contract with the General Practice Medicine Collaboration Platform and led by Peking Union Medical College. Our hospital specializes in TCM diagnosis and treatment, has introduced multiple national patent technologies, and regularly invites authoritative experts from Beijing, Shanghai, Chengdu, and other regions for academic seminars and joint consultations, aiding scientific diagnosis and treatment and early recovery for vulvar leukoplakia patients in Southwest China.
