Title: Supreme People’s Court Releases Typical Cases on the Protection of Elderly People’s Rights and Interests, Focusing on Solving Their Most Pressing Difficulties and Concerns Since the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China, the CPC Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core has attached great importance to work on aging and has elevated actively responding to population aging to a national strategy. Guided by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, Chinese courts have fully performed their adjudicatory functions, lawfully heard civil disputes involving elderly persons, protected their lawful rights and interests, and continuously enhanced their sense of gain, happiness, and security. To thoroughly implement the guiding principles of the Third Plenary Session of the 20th CPC Central Committee and the 15th National Civil Affairs Conference, further advance the implementation of the national strategy for actively responding to population aging, and give full play to the demonstrative and guiding role of typical cases, the following typical cases on the protection of elderly people’s rights and interests are hereby released. The cases released this time have the following features: First, they respect the independent wishes of elderly persons and, in accordance with law, fully meet their needs. In Case 2, the people’s court actively and correctly applied the system of consensual guardianship, ensuring that an elderly person could spend later life in a manner consistent with his own wishes and satisfy his own elderly-care needs. In Case 3, the people’s court stopped children from unreasonably obstructing an elderly parent’s independent management of property and fully protected the elderly person’s property rights. Second, they focus on elderly people’s real-life difficulties and strive to solve their urgent concerns. In Case 1, the people’s court correctly grasped the conditions for contract termination and supported the elderly person’s claim to terminate the contract and recover prepaid fees within the contractually agreed cooling-off period, thereby addressing the problem of difficulty in obtaining refunds for prepaid services. This helps guide operators toward honest and standardized business practices and allows elderly consumers to spend with confidence. In Case 5, in light of the objective circumstances and special difficulties of an elderly parent who had lost her only child, the people’s court actively organized mediation among all relevant parties, tailored a one-stop mediation plan to the elderly person’s specific situation, and actively urged performance. This not only resolved the case, but also completely alleviated the elderly person’s anxiety and distress about daily life. Third, they further advance the practical realization of care for the elderly and promote accessible, perceptible, and enjoyable elderly-care service guarantees. In Case 4, the people’s court lawfully found that stepchildren should pay elderly support living expenses to stepparents with whom they had formed a stable relationship of upbringing and education, thereby removing worries about old-age support. In Case 6, after identifying widespread problems with a long-term care insurance service platform through judicial adjudication, the people’s court actively recommended that the relevant departments make age-friendly improvements, helping to take the first mile in implementing the long-term care insurance system, promoting employment for elderly caregivers and the development and improvement of a new type of social security system, and making concrete progress in ensuring support for the elderly. Respecting and caring for the elderly is a traditional virtue of the Chinese nation, and strengthening the protection of elderly people’s rights and interests is of great significance. The people’s courts will thoroughly implement Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law, intensify adjudication and enforcement efforts, further improve their capacity and level in safeguarding the lawful rights and interests of elderly persons, promote the building of an elderly-friendly society, enable elderly people to share the fruits of reform and development, and enjoy happy later years in peace. Table of Contents of Typical Cases on the Protection of Elderly People’s Rights and Interests: Case 1 Supporting termination of a contract in accordance with the agreement to resolve difficulties in obtaining refunds for prepaid fees — Zhao v. an elderly-care industry company, dispute over a service contract. Case 2 Implementing consensual guardianship and respecting the independent wishes of elderly persons — Application by Lu for the designation of a guardian. Case 3 Elderly persons may independently manage their property; children may not unreasonably interfere — Xu v. Xu, dispute over a safekeeping contract. Case 4 Stepchildren who were raised and educated by stepparents shall pay elderly support living expenses — Liu v. Yan Jia, Yan Yi, et al., dispute over support obligations. Case 5 Facilitating multi-party mediation and delivering one-stop dispute resolution — Ren v. a real estate company and a bank, dispute over a commercial housing pre-sale contract. Case 6 Actively performing judicial functions to promote optimization of the elderly-care system — Wang v. a nursing institution, dispute over a labor service contract. Case 1: Supporting Termination of a Contract in Accordance with the Agreement to Resolve Difficulties in Obtaining Refunds for Prepaid Fees — Zhao v. an Elderly-Care Industry Company, dispute over a service contract. Basic Facts: Under the introduction of Zhu, a salesperson for an elderly-care industry company, Zhao entered into an Elderly-Care Card Contract with the company. The contract provided that Zhao would pay RMB 100,000 to purchase 60 months of accommodation and services at the company’s nursing home. It also stipulated that the three days after full payment would serve as a cooling-off period, during which Zhao could request a refund and complete a refund application form, and would receive a full refund within seven working days. After paying the RMB 100,000, Zhao contacted Zhu, who had handled the contract signing, on the same day to request a refund, but to no avail. The company later claimed that Zhao had not submitted a written refund application or called the refund number specified in the contract, and therefore did not meet the conditions for a full refund during the cooling-off period. Zhao then brought a lawsuit, requesting that the court order the company to refund the full amount and compensate for interest losses. Judgment: The trial court held that the Elderly-Care Card Contract expressly stipulated that the cardholder could apply for a full refund during the cooling-off period, but it did not specify the channel or procedures for requesting a refund. The company acknowledged that Zhu was its salesperson, and the evidence provided by Zhao was sufficient to prove that on the same day the contract was signed and payment was made, Zhao had contacted Zhu to request a refund. Zhao’s request to terminate the contract conformed to the parties’ agreement and should produce the legal effect of contract termination. The final judgment ordered the company to refund the entire amount and compensate Zhao for the corresponding interest losses. Significance: Some elderly-care institutions operate on a prepaid model in order to quickly recover funds and increase customer retention. In practice, when elderly consumers request a refund of prepaid fees in accordance with the contract, some institutions evade, delay, or even refuse refunds for various reasons, resulting in contracts being difficult to terminate and prepaid fees being difficult to recover, thereby harming elderly persons’ lawful rights and interests. In this case, the people’s court carefully examined the process of contract formation and the surrounding circumstances, found that the elderly person’s contract termination complied with the law, and supported the elderly person’s withdrawal from the transaction and recovery of the prepaid amount, thus protecting the elderly person’s reasonable expectations at the time of contracting. This judgment helps encourage elderly consumers to spend with confidence and guides elderly-care institutions toward honest and standardized operations. Case 2: Implementing Consensual Guardianship and Respecting the Independent Wishes of Elderly Persons — Application by Lu for the designation of a guardian. Basic Facts: The elderly person Yang and his spouse had no children. After Yang’s spouse passed away, Yang was cared for by Lu, his late spouse’s nephew. After notarization, Yang and Lu signed a consensual guardianship agreement. The agreement provided that if Yang were to lose civil capacity, Lu would serve as his guardian, manage his property, and arrange matters such as elderly care and medical treatment. Later, Yang suddenly suffered a serious illness and developed impaired consciousness. A hospital diagnosis certificate stated that Yang had renal failure and heart failure. A video disc submitted by Lu showed that Yang was no longer able to independently express his will. Pursuant to an appraisal commissioned by Lu, the appraisal concluded that Yang was a severely disabled person. The neighborhood residents’ committee at Yang’s place of household registration issued an opinion confirming that Yang was unconscious, had long been unable to care for himself, and agreed that Lu should serve as Yang’s guardian. Lu then applied to the court, requesting that Yang be recognized as a person without civil capacity and that Lu be designated as his guardian. Judgment: The trial court held that the evidence in this case was sufficient to prove that Yang was completely unable to recognize and control his own conduct and therefore should be recognized as a person without civil capacity. The consensual guardianship agreement executed by Yang and Lu had been notarized, reflected the true intentions of both parties, and was lawful and valid. In accordance with the agreement and in light of the opinion of the residents’ committee where Yang resided, Lu’s application to serve as Yang’s guardian should be supported. The final judgment recognized Yang as a person without civil capacity and designated Lu as Yang’s guardian. Significance: The Civil Code of the People’s Republic of China provides for the system of consensual guardianship, under which an adult with full civil capacity may, after consultation with another person, determine in writing that such person will serve as his or her guardian when he or she loses or partially loses civil capacity. This system helps fully respect elderly persons’ independent wishes and comprehensively protect their rights and interests. In practice, many elderly people do not understand or are unfamiliar with consensual guardianship, so when actual needs arise, they are unable to make use of this right, resulting in guardianship dilemmas. In this case, the people’s court, in accordance with the elderly person’s wishes, supported consensual guardianship in accordance with law, demonstrating the function and value of this legal system and helping the public better understand, accept, and make full use of consensual guardianship so as to provide greater security in later life. Case 3: Elderly Persons May Independently Manage Their Property; Children May Not Unreasonably Interfere — Xu v. Xu, dispute over a safekeeping contract. Basic Facts: After the old house of the elderly and advanced-age Xu was demolished as part of redevelopment, Xu lived with his son and handed over RMB 700,000 in savings to his son for safekeeping, while clearly stating that the money was to be used for Xu’s own future elderly care and medical treatment. Later, the two had conflicts over household matters. Xu no longer wanted his son to keep the savings on his behalf and demanded the return of the RMB 700,000. The son refused. After repeated unsuccessful negotiations, Xu filed a lawsuit requesting an order that the son return the RMB 700,000. Judgment: The trial court held that the son had been entrusted by Xu to keep the RMB 700,000 savings on Xu’s behalf. Although Xu was of advanced age, Xu had full civil capacity and had the right to possess and manage his own property. Since Xu requested the return of the money that had been kept on his behalf, the son should have returned it in a timely manner. The final judgment ordered the son to return the RMB 700,000 to Xu. After the judgment took effect, the son voluntarily returned the full amount. Significance: In real life, many elderly people have certain savings or property. For various reasons, situations often arise in which children interfere with their parents’ independent management or disposition of property, giving rise to many family conflicts and disputes. Under the law, elderly persons with full civil capacity enjoy the right to independently manage and dispose of their own property, and their children should respect and cooperate with this, and must not unreasonably refuse or obstruct it. In this case, the people’s court protected the elderly person’s lawful property rights and freedom of disposition, which not only demonstrates the law’s protection of elderly persons’ rights, but also helps guide family members to establish proper concepts regarding property. Case 4: Stepchildren Who Were Raised and Educated by Stepparents Shall Pay Elderly Support Living Expenses — Liu v. Yan Jia, Yan Yi, et al., dispute over support obligations. Basic Facts: Liu, a woman, and Yan, a man, registered their marriage in 1979. Yan had been married before. After marriage, Liu lived together with Yan and Yan’s five minor children: Yan Jia, Yan Yi, Yan Bing, Yan Ding, and Yan Wu. At the time of the marriage, Yan Jia had already reached the age of 16 and relied mainly on his own farming income for his livelihood. Yan Yi, Yan Bing, Yan Ding, and Yan Wu were still young and were jointly raised by Liu and Yan. In 2023, Yan passed away. Liu was also over 70 years old, lacked the ability to work, and had a certain fixed income. Disputes then arose between Liu and the five stepchildren regarding elderly support. Liu brought a lawsuit requesting that each of the five stepchildren pay a monthly living allowance of RMB 1,000. Judgment: The trial court held that when Liu married Yan, although Yan Jia had not yet reached the age of 18, he was already over 16 and relied mainly on his own labor income for his livelihood. Therefore, no relationship of upbringing existed between Liu and Yan Jia. By contrast, Yan Yi, Yan Bing, Yan Ding, and Yan Wu had all been raised and educated by Liu during their upbringing, and the rights and obligations between them should be governed by the provisions of the Civil Code concerning the parent-child relationship. After Yan’s death, Liu was over 70 years old and lacked the ability to work and therefore had the right to request a certain amount of living expenses from Yan Yi, Yan Bing, Yan Ding, and Yan Wu. Because these stepchildren were not financially well-off, the amount should be determined by comprehensively considering Liu’s and the stepchildren’s financial circumstances and Liu’s actual needs. The final judgment ordered Yan Yi, Yan Bing, Yan Ding, and Yan Wu each to pay Liu RMB 100 per month as living expenses. Significance: As the elderly population continues to grow, remarried and reconstituted families are facing new issues concerning elderly support. The relationship between the contributions made by stepparents within the family and their increasingly strong support needs as they age affects individual well-being, family harmony, and social harmony, and therefore requires accurate understanding and proper handling. The people’s courts take whether a long-term and stable relationship of upbringing and education was formed between stepparent and stepchild as an important criterion for determining whether the stepchild should pay elderly support living expenses to the stepparent. This is consistent with both legal principles and human sentiment. In this case, the people’s court carefully investigated the facts and made objective findings and disposition according to the circumstances of each stepchild, which helps encourage adult stepparents to care for young children and truly assume family responsibilities, while also encouraging stepchildren to respect and care for the elderly, support one another, and promote harmonious family relationships. Case 5: Facilitating Multi-Party Mediation and Delivering One-Stop Dispute Resolution — Ren v. a Real Estate Company and a Bank, dispute over a commercial housing pre-sale contract. Basic Facts: Qiu purchased a commercial residential unit developed by a real estate company, paying a down payment of RMB 1.72 million. The remaining RMB 2.6 million of the purchase price was financed through a housing provident fund loan and a commercial bank loan, with combined monthly repayments of RMB 14,000. Not long after buying the home, Qiu passed away. Qiu was the only child in the family, and his mother Ren was his sole legal heir. Ren was elderly and had no independent source of income and was unable to continue paying the mortgage. Ren therefore filed a lawsuit requesting that the court order termination of the housing purchase contract and the loan contracts, and the return of the down payment and the mortgage payments already made. Judgment: The trial court held that the purchase contract and loan contracts involved multiple civil subjects. Terminating the purchase contract would involve a series of issues such as the return of the down payment, settlement of the loans, deregistration of rights, and other procedures, requiring the agreement and coordinated cooperation of the real estate company, the bank, the housing provident fund administration body, the real estate registration authority, and the authority handling online contract filing and recordation. The court actively invited people’s mediators to participate in the mediation. Through joint efforts, the parties ultimately reached a comprehensive mediation plan, which included terminating the housing purchase contract, terminating the loan contracts, having the developer return the loan-related funds, completing loan settlement, deregistering the housing mortgage and online filing and recordation, and refunding the housing down payment. At the same time, considering that Ren was an elderly parent who had lost her only child, the court strengthened its explanation and persuasion toward the developer, which agreed to waive the liquidated damages that Ren would otherwise have had to pay. After the mediation agreement was reached, the court granted judicial confirmation and strengthened follow-up supervision, and all parties timely performed the agreement. Significance: Because the child’s housing purchase contract and loan contracts were not entered into by the elderly parent, after losing a child some elderly people, due to physical condition, age, and financial status, face pressure in repaying mortgages and difficulties in disposing of the property. In litigation, if a judgment is rendered directly without fully considering the transaction circumstances and objective conditions, the best outcome often cannot be achieved. Based on the actual circumstances of this case, the people’s court carried out in-depth and meticulous mediation, actively guiding all parties to face the problem and study feasible solutions in connection with the multiple entities and multiple procedural links involved in the housing transaction, and coordinating them to solve it together. It tailored a one-stop substantive dispute resolution plan for the elderly person, fully responding to her major concerns and removing her worries. This case is a good example of putting mediation and substantive dispute resolution into practice in the protection of elderly people’s rights and interests. Case 6: Actively Performing Judicial Functions to Promote Optimization of the Elderly-Care System — Wang v. a Nursing Institution, dispute over a labor service contract. Basic Facts: Wang’s mother had been assessed as a person with disabilities qualifying under long-term care insurance. Under local policy, family members of such persons may, after completing the required training, serve as family caregivers under the long-term care insurance scheme, accept job orders under the management of a nursing institution, and receive remuneration. Wang met the caregiving qualifications. Wang and a nursing institution agreed that the institution would assign job orders through an online platform, and Wang would provide in-home care services to her mother and receive remuneration from the institution. However, because Wang was relatively old and unfamiliar with online operating procedures, she failed to upload care order photos that met the platform’s requirements, and the nursing institution then stopped settlement and assignment of orders to her. Wang brought a lawsuit requesting that the nursing institution pay remuneration and compensate for losses. Judgment: The trial court held that the facts were clear and the rights and obligations were definite, and that pre-litigation mediation would help promptly resolve the dispute and avoid unnecessary litigation burdens. The court invited the local long-term care insurance branch center to participate in mediation. After Wang and the nursing institution reached a settlement agreement, Wang withdrew the lawsuit, and the dispute was satisfactorily resolved. During the handling of the case, the court found that many caregivers under the long-term care insurance scheme were middle-aged or elderly, and disputes between caregivers and nursing institutions arising from technical problems with the platform were not isolated cases. The service platform urgently needed age-friendly adaptation. The court therefore made targeted recommendations to the relevant departments to make age-friendly improvements to the platform. The departments accepted the recommendations and made improvements. After the improvements, the practicality and convenience of the platform were significantly enhanced. Significance: Long-term care insurance is a new type of social security aimed at meeting the long-term care needs of persons with disabilities. In individual cases, the people’s courts identified new situations and problems arising in the operation of this system, actively put forward opinions and recommendations, and worked with relevant departments to improve and refine it, fully reflecting coordinated work and systemic integration. In this case, the people’s court summarized the characteristics of caregivers in similar cases and, in response to institutional barriers and technical shortcomings affecting the in-depth implementation of the long-term care insurance system in practice, carefully and accurately put forward recommendations and effectively promoted improvement. This helped caregivers bridge the digital divide, enabling both employment for elderly caregivers and the smooth first mile of a new type of social security system for elderly care. Source: Website of the Supreme People’s Court

Title: Bus Out of Control Content: Accident scene. Two passengers killed, 13 injured as bus crashes into divider and overturns in Zhaoqing. Zhaoqing News (Reporter Yu Ganyong, correspondents Liu Zhanqiang, Fan Weijie photo report) The Sihui traffic police confirmed to reporters yesterday that at noon on June 3, a traffic accident occurred on the Huangtian section of S263 in Sihui City, resulting in two passengers dying on the spot and 13 drivers and passengers sustaining minor injuries. Around 12:00 noon that day, when a "Zhuhai-Guangning" bus was passing the Huangtian section of S263 in Sihui City, it lost control, collided with the central divider wall of the highway, and overturned, causing severe damage to the vehicle body. After the accident, relevant departments in Sihui organized personnel to rush to the scene to fully rescue the injured, direct traffic, and investigate the accident. The public security authorities remind all drivers that with recent rainy and slippery road conditions, it is even more important to enhance safety awareness and control vehicle speed.

Title: Successful Complaint About CCB Small Account Management Fee Content: Briefly describe what happened. A few days ago, while grabbing some perks on Alipay, there was a CCB Money-Saving Card offer - spend over 10 yuan and get 5 yuan off. So I transferred 30 yuan from Alipay to my CCB account. The next day, when I tried to use it, I found insufficient balance. Checking the details revealed a 29.99 yuan small account management fee had been deducted! I thought this fee was abolished long ago, why are they still charging it randomly!? So I called the customer service hotline 95533 to ask. They said I have multiple CCB cards under my name, and only one can be exempted. Then I remembered around 2018, I went to CCB to apply for a new card. I asked the staff at the time about a card issued uniformly by the school in 2011 (but not by me personally), asking if I needed to cancel it to avoid random fees. The CCB staff was quite confident and said just leave it, no need to worry. But the reality is, that almost unused card for about ten years became a dormant account. It reactivates if you deposit money again; it wasn't cancelled. So I called the complaint hotline again - isn't this deceptive? Fortunately, it was resolved satisfactorily today. I actually had not one, but two cards from my school days, and I've never even seen the other one! So, a word to the wise, sisters: check your unused debit cards thoroughly, cancel them if possible! #CCB #SmallAccountManagementFee

If you are not yet very familiar with the Luxgen U6, or if you want to go all-in on your ideal, please click the image below to view the抢先试驾 of the 2.0T model and the previous in-depth test drive in Taiwan. Additionally, a brief car-buying guide will be provided later in this article for those who are unclear about the differences between the models or are considering purchasing the U6. ● Three Questions to Help You Understand the Luxgen U6 SUV Better Those who have driven or are familiar with the Luxgen U7 know about its high fuel consumption issue; it's often joked that its 2.2T engine has the fuel consumption of a 3.0L engine. So, how will the U6 SUV perform? Due to the complex road conditions, varied driving styles, and slow convoy driving during this test drive, the measured fuel consumption is inevitably unreliable. Therefore, the day after the test drive ended, Luxgen, as a homegrown brand from Taiwan, showed the sincerity expected of a major automaker by delivering the U6 SUV to the author again. Of course, the author also showed maximum sincerity by providing the most reliable fuel consumption test for netizens. The test route was the Guangzhou Ring Expressway, used during the越野时代, with a total length of 60 kilometers, and the test was conducted over two laps. Since the test day was a weekend, the traffic on the Ring Expressway was complex, better reflecting daily urban driving conditions. The road surface was mostly urban asphalt pavement, with some cement roads. Additionally, the same fuel nozzle was used for refueling before and after the test, and the tank was filled to the brim to ensure the objectivity and authenticity of the test. The Guangzhou Ring Expressway on the weekend was not easy, given Guangzhou's significant traffic pressure, so congestion was common. The fuel consumption test yielded a displayed reading of 9.1 L/100km and an actual measured reading of 8.7 L/100km. For a new SUV that hasn't yet passed the break-in period and has substantial size and space, this performance is excellent. The author can unequivocally say that the Luxgen U6's fuel consumption performance is genuinely good, completely free from the issues of the older U7. Finally, the comfort of the U6 is worth emphasizing again; after nearly two hours of testing and continuous driving, no fatigue was felt, and the tall passenger in the front seat even slept comfortably. As a homegrown brand from Taiwan, and with the Luxgen U6 SUV targeting young first-time car buyers, overall build quality is a concern for many. Can it surpass mainland Chinese brands or rival joint-venture brands? Let's take a closer look. Upon detailed examination, the overall build quality of the Luxgen U6 SUV is quite satisfactory. Both the external sheet metal work and internal assembly, as well as the attention to detail, are commendable, approaching the level of joint-venture brands. Just a few days before this test drive, Dongfeng Yulon announced the model information and pricing for the Luxgen U6. The new car is available in 7 variants, with a price range of 128,800 to 200,800 RMB. The pre-sale price range for the 1.8T models is 128,800-169,800 RMB, and for the 2.0T models, it is 159,800-200,800 RMB. A price threshold below 130,000 RMB is already quite reasonable. However, based on the currently known configuration list, the affordable price means the base model U6 sheds all its highlight features. For a model like the U6, which emphasizes configuration as a selling point, such a low price isn't very meaningful. Therefore, to truly experience the technological driving charm of the Luxgen U6, mid-to-high trim levels are more meaningful, though the price would then rise to around 160,000 RMB. At 160,000 RMB, there is a very wide selection within the homegrown brand segment. Looking at the 2.0T flagship model, its configuration is top-tier in its class, and the price of just over 200,000 RMB is not exaggerated, but brand perception might not convince many buyers. In summary, the pricing of the Luxgen U6 SUV is not perfect, but its cross-segment positioning gives it decent overall competitiveness. Besides the advantage of technological features, the U6's fashionable exterior is also a major selling point. Thus, a lower price gets you style, while a higher price gets you technology—both of which are highly valued by young people. After its strong debut at the Beijing Auto Show and two previous test drives by colleagues, details like the exterior and interior are no longer unfamiliar. So, for the more affordable and mainstream 1.8T model, its power performance and driving experience are likely of greater interest. Let's first experience the most anticipated aspect: power and handling. ● Power and Handling: The 1.8T is Quite Sufficient The Luxgen U6's 1.8-liter inline-four turbocharged engine produces a maximum power of 116 kW (158 hp) at 5500 rpm and a maximum torque of 230 N·m between 2000-4400 rpm. On paper, this 1.8T engine is not outstanding but is at a mainstream level, similar to Volkswagen's EA888 1.8T engine. Unlike the 2.0T model's 6-speed automatic transmission, the 1.8T model is equipped with a Powertech 5-speed automatic transmission. While not technologically groundbreaking, its maturity and reliability remain its advantages. First, the high seating position typical of SUVs is present, but the Luxgen U6 not only feels high but also slightly reclined backward. This provides the high, broad视野 of an SUV combined with the comfort of a sedan's reclined posture. A minor complaint: the seat support is very strong, almost too supportive, feeling like it's pushing against your back, but once you get used to it, it feels just right. The Luxgen U6 starts off in a gentlemanly manner—elegant and steady. Similar to the 2.0T engine's torque peak at 2400 rpm, the 1.8T's turbo engages at around 2000 rpm. This makes it behave more like a naturally aspirated engine at low speeds, with good smoothness. A 2000 rpm turbo engagement has its pros and cons. Compared to turbo engines that engage around 1000 rpm, its power确实 comes later, but it lacks the irritability of a sudden kick with a light tap of the accelerator, especially in urban traffic jams. The Luxgen U6 allows for a more relaxed drive, and the 1.8L power is sufficient even before the turbo kicks in. Of course, a gentle start doesn't mean it's devoid of excitement; its mid-range performance is more interesting. Revving past 2000 rpm instantly reveals its vitality. The turbo engagement is not abrupt, and acceleration is very direct. Additionally, the 5-speed automatic transmission isn't overly aggressive in shifting but knows when to shift, doing so decisively and smoothly. If you floor the accelerator, raising the rpm above 4000 rpm, the transmission reacts after half a second, downshifts, and the 1.8T engine roars, followed by a push-back sensation. While not extremely strong, it's enough to let you enjoy the thrill of acceleration. The Luxgen U6 SUV uses hydraulic power steering, which feels relatively heavy overall. The steering ratio is 3.2 turns. Its directional accuracy is praiseworthy; there is a slight vagueness, but whether making fine adjustments or changing lanes and turning, it clearly understands your intentions. However, road feedback is somewhat lacking. The suspension uses a semi-torsion beam setup, tuned on the stiffer side, which is quite different from the typically soft suspension of SUVs. Thus, the U6 SUV's driving feel is more like a sedan's, offering better handling while retaining comfort. The author received the Luxgen U6 1.8T Zhizun版 the day before the test drive, hoping to conduct acceleration and braking performance tests before rain. Unfortunately, continuous rain in Shenzhen and a light drizzle during the test slightly affected the data, but it can still serve as a reference. ● 0-100 km/h Acceleration Test: 11.15 seconds The Luxgen U6 SUV 1.8T doesn't start off fiercely. The launch rpm was 2300, with slight front-wheel slip. The stiffly tuned suspension kept the body姿态 well controlled. An acceleration time of 11.15 seconds is quite good. The initial acceleration is spirited, while the latter part is relatively steady, with an overall g-value around 0.4. Compared to previous SUVs like the U7, the 1.8T's performance is adequate, being half a second faster than the 2.2T U7 (though the U7 is heavier). The gap compared to the CR-V is also not too large. ● 100-0 km/h Braking Test Due to light rain during the braking test, the road was wet and slippery, introducing error. Additionally, the test vehicle was new, and the brand-new tires had not yet reached optimal performance, so the data was not ideal. A braking distance of 46.86 meters is clearly not the best. Based on tests of similar models, the 100-0 km/h braking distance should be under 43 meters. This further illustrates the impact of wet roads on braking distance in rainy conditions. So, allow the author to add a few words of caution: drive more carefully in the rain, maintain a safe speed. Perhaps that extra second and the additional 3 meters could lead to regret. ● Differences in the 1.8T Models After understanding the power and driving dynamics of the 1.8T model, let's look at the differences between the 1.8T and the previously tested 2.0T model. Externally, aside from minor configuration details, the 1.8T model is基本上 the same as the 2.0T model. Beyond the aforementioned细节差异, the 1.8T and 2.0T models are completely identical, even down to the rear badging. The advantage is that it's not easy to tell you're driving a 1.8T model. If you later add xenon headlights and daytime running lights, you could almost pass it off as the 2.0T flagship. Inside, the 1.8T model also only has minor configuration differences. Differences in materials and visuals are hard to spot except for the seats. However, while these configuration differences might not be visible, they significantly impact daily comfort and convenience. During our test drive forum live broadcast, many netizens were concerned about the reduction of some practical features. After the test drive, the author relayed issues like the front camera, tweeter rise/fall, and power tailgate to the manufacturer, hoping they would offer optional packages after the launch. Overall, however, the 1.8T Zhizun type is fully adequate for daily use. Of course, as consumers, we always want more features. Summary The Luxgen U6 SUV's fashionable exterior and rich features make it highly competitive as an urban SUV. Although the 1.8T power is slightly不足, it is completely sufficient for daily urban driving. Compared to the higher-priced 2.0T model, it is more practical. For young first-time car buyers, the more comprehensive features and power of the 2.0T model can better fulfill their ideal, while the 1.8T model brings that ideal one step closer.

Title: Is there a future in customs assistant work? Content: To be realistic, new customs officers must enter through the national civil service exam, and the current trend is to focus on fresh graduates with little requirement for work experience, so I believe being an assistant doesn't help much in future attempts to become a customs civil servant. The customs system has high staff turnover, strict internal controls, and aims for anyone who comes in to be able to do the job, so the work isn't particularly difficult. As for career prospects, most assistants I've encountered don't rely on this salary to make a living, so naturally they don't have many ambitions in that regard. Of course, shifting the focus away from customs, assistant work is more like a transitional job, 'riding a donkey while looking for a horse,' and there will be more options like provincial exams in various places.

Title: Hospital's oxygen supply interruption due to maintenance leads to death of 58-year-old patient; Weinan Health Commission claims it's a management loophole, unrelated to diagnosis and treatment. How is the hospital's legal liability determined? Content: If only looking at the title, the hospital is definitely responsible, but after reading the specific description, the hospital's fault is not very obvious. The response capability of a general ward is not as good as that of an intensive care unit, and this hospital belongs to the rehabilitation department. Its preparedness for handling emergencies like oxygen shortage is relatively weak. Obtaining oxygen within seven minutes is hardly considered a medical accident. The general ward did its best, and the hospital's fault is not obvious. Moreover, the patient passed away at home several days later, so the direct connection to the oxygen shortage is not strong, as the patient's condition might have had a survival period of only a few weeks. Then, it's necessary to review the hospital's documents and medical records to investigate details such as the treatment measures after the patient's hypoxia, auxiliary examinations, the attending physician's assessment, discharge records, etc. If these indicators cannot clearly point to a connection with hypoxia, then it cannot be considered the hospital's responsibility. However, given the family's agitation, the hospital might have to provide some humanitarian compensation, more or less.

Title: Bank teller, no resources or background at home, great pressure to attract deposits, so what is the future of a teller? Content: Just after finishing the article "Things About Banks," the system recommended this answer. As someone who worked for six years in a state-owned bank in Beijing and has since left, I'll share my humble opinion. First, being a teller in a bank has no future. Over 90% of new graduates start as tellers when they enter a bank, but it depends on whether there is an opportunity to change positions. If you don't want to bear pressure and follow the business line, it's basically impossible to reach management level. The best outcome is to become a business manager with a slight salary increase. If you switch to a marketing position and are willing to work hard, continuously accumulate clients, and achieve results, you might eventually become a deputy marketing manager. Even if you don't reach that level, you can at least earn a relatively higher income. I'm not sure what you mean by "future" specifically—whether it's becoming a high-ranking official or making a lot of money. If it's about becoming a high-ranking official, that path is not feasible. Whether in the financial system or other industries, under China's system, becoming an official requires connections. If it's about making money, there is some possibility. When I was a financial manager in the bank, my income reached several hundred thousand at its peak. Top performers in joint-stock banks can even earn annual salaries of several million. If you have no resources, I suggest you switch to a financial manager position in the bank. The reliance on resources is not as severe; it's more like To C sales. As long as you are diligent, you will achieve results. Even though you are currently a bank teller, you can actually broaden your thinking. You don't have to limit yourself to the cycle of being a teller. The term "bank" itself is a great platform. For example, you can learn about investment knowledge and share it with others. Using the bank as a platform naturally increases credibility. Hope this helps you.

Title: Buying a House You Can't Live In: Guarding Against the 'Right of Habitation'
Content: The Civil Code, which came into effect on January 1, 2021, stipulates that the right of habitation can be established either by contract or by will. This means that even if a property is transferred to your name, you might still face the awkward situation of being unable to live in it. Indeed, the first lawsuit regarding the right of habitation has emerged in Wuhan. Ms. Xu and Mr. Li got married in 2006. The house was Ms. Xu's pre-marital property, and the couple had no children. In 2014, Ms. Xu became seriously ill and made a will stating that after her passing, the house would be gifted to her younger brother, Mr. Xu. Mr. Li was allowed to live in the house until he remarried, retaining the right of habitation until his remarriage. Ms. Xu passed away in 2016. That same year, Mr. Li and Mr. Xu went to court over the dispute concerning this property. Ultimately, the court ruled that the ownership of the house belonged to Mr. Xu, while Mr. Li retained the right of habitation. In early 2021, Mr. Li discovered that Mr. Xu had listed the property for sale online. Worried that his right of habitation would be affected, he promptly took the court judgment to the enforcement bureau to apply for compulsory enforcement of his right of habitation. The court's enforcement bureau issued an enforcement ruling, registering the right of habitation for this house under Mr. Li's name. This means that even if someone buys the property, it will not affect Mr. Li's right to live there. However, the buyer would be in a difficult position—having paid for a house they cannot live in. Therefore, in future real estate transactions, the most important first step is to check with the real estate authority whether a right of habitation has been registered on the property. If not, everything is okay. If there is one, first check the duration. If it's short-term and acceptable, the transaction can proceed. But if it's registered as long-term, it's crucial to cut losses in time and stop the transaction.

Title: 33 years old, no job I like, just muddling along in a government agency, what should I do? Content: First, the compensation for this job is average, people generally go for the stability. Starting over again might not lead to something more satisfying than your current situation. So, if you can stick it out, stick it out. If this really isn't the life you want, then you need to make a lot of preparations. Figure out what you truly want inside, then gradually move towards the path you like. The suggestion is to continue muddling through, hang on as long as you can, cling tightly to the 'enterprise' (the agency) like a stubborn freeloader, while continuously studying and improving your ability to survive in society. Then resign and start a business. Otherwise, after leaving, you might not even be able to find a job. As long as you're not a temporary worker in the government agency, you can keep doing it. After all, at that age, with a family to support, what else can you do? 😊

Title: Yin deficiency with effulgent fire and spleen deficiency, how to regulate? Content: Actually, it's not that you can't nourish your spleen and stomach well, but that your approach is wrong - for example: lying at home all day, and then giving yourself ginseng, angelica, donkey-hide gelatin, and various other nourishing foods. Not only will they not be absorbed, but they will also increase the burden on your spleen and stomach. You clearly know your spleen and stomach are weak, yet when you crave something, you have late-night snacks every day consecutively. Then you notice your belly getting fat, so you start trying intermittent fasting, but you can't stick with it for long. Suddenly, you start binge eating as a form of revenge. This is actually the most damaging to your spleen and stomach! And you clearly know your spleen and stomach are weak, yet you still eat desserts every day, drink milk tea, coffee, carbonated drinks, etc... Your spleen and stomach will only get weaker and weaker. Traditional Chinese Medicine believes that the spleen and stomach are the root of primordial qi and the source of qi, blood, and nutrient production. If their ascending and descending functions are abnormal, it not only affects the intake, transformation, and distribution of food essence but also disrupts the overall balance of yin-yang, qi-blood, and water-fire ascending/descending in the entire body, leading to numerous pathological changes. There are really only two ways that can help your spleen and stomach recover quickly - doing subtraction and doing addition. · Doing Subtraction 1. Avoid certain foods: Eat less cold and cool foods, such as bananas, watermelon, milk. Eat less fried foods, like fried chicken. Eat less pickled foods, like sauerkraut. Eat less sweet foods, like cream cakes. Eat less gas-producing foods, like potatoes, sweet potatoes. Eat less hard-to-digest foods, like glutinous rice, sweet rice balls; eating too much can slow down intestinal motility leading to indigestion. 2. Emotions: The spleen and stomach are the 'emotional organs' of the body. Digestive function fluctuates with emotions. Emotional tension and anxiety can cause bloating. Learn to clear your negative emotions by writing. Go to KTV to sing and relax your body and mind. A happy mood greatly alleviates the digestive function of the spleen and stomach. 3. Drinking water: The spleen and stomach are responsible for transporting and transforming fluids. When the spleen and stomach are weak, the water you drink cannot be transported and transformed and instead adds to the burden, causing more phlegm-dampness. Do not drink water within half an hour after meals. Do not drink coffee, milk tea, cold drinks, carbonated drinks. Sip water slowly. 4. Eat less: Eat smaller, more frequent meals each day. Eat until 70% full at each meal. Chew thoroughly and slowly. Do not eat spicy foods on an empty stomach. Binge eating is very damaging to the spleen and stomach. Eat meals on time. If you have no time for a meal, bring a small snack to tide you over. · Doing Addition 1. Strengthen the Spleen: Eat more Chinese yam, black rice, sorghum, broomcorn millet, oats, peanuts, millet, noodles, steamed buns, japonica rice, lotus seeds, foxnut, Atractylodes macrocephala, jujube, lotus seeds, etc. 2. Abdominal Massage: Before getting up in the morning and before going to bed at night, lie on your back with legs bent. Take a few deep breaths to relax the whole body. Place the left palm facing the navel, and stack the right hand on the back of the left hand. Massage clockwise. The massage range should start small, then expand, then reduce again. Massage continuously 50 times. 3. Exercise: Tiptoe for 5 minutes in the morning and evening. Tiptoeing can stimulate the Spleen Meridian of Foot-Taiyin and the Stomach Meridian of Foot-Yangming, unblock the meridian qi and blood, and enhance the transporting function of the spleen and stomach. Tap the acupoints on the spleen and stomach meridians for 3 minutes daily, such as the three major points Zusanli (ST36), Sanyinjiao (SP6), and Xuehai (SP10), to unblock the meridians and promote qi and blood flow. 4. Health-preserving Tea for Internal Regulation -- Shiwei Shenling Tea (an upgraded version of the ancient method Four Spirits Soup for strengthening the spleen) Ingredients: Tangerine peel, white hyacinth bean, coix seed, licorice root, Chinese yam, hairy fig root, lotus seed, poria, foxnut, ginseng. Function: A comprehensive blend of 10 warm-natured ingredients that can gently nourish the spleen and stomach. Effectively strengthens the spleen and dispels dampness, calms the mind, clears heat from the spleen, etc. Pre-portioned tea bags offer a more scientific formula and better results. Brewing method: Place one tea bag in 300ml of hot water, steep for 3-5 minutes before drinking. The tea bag can be brewed repeatedly until it loses flavor. 5. Magnetic Field (Metaphorical): Many physical and mental illnesses are not cured, but nurtured back to health. Spend more time with emotionally stable people. Understand that the people who can bring you peace, the people whose 'magnetic field' brings you peace of mind, are the ones who truly nurture you. That's how you will get better and better.

Title: Why banks do not provide loans for allocated land Content: There are several reasons for this situation: \n1. Houses on allocated land belong to the state, not to individuals. Therefore, individuals only have the right to dispose of them, but cannot use them as collateral for loans. \n2. Allocated land refers to the transfer of rural land collective ownership to individual farmers or enterprises, with the land use right also transferring accordingly. Due to the uncertainty of land use right circulation and the instability of individual farmers' credit status, banks consider such loans to be high-risk and difficult to manage.

Title: Which Is Better, Japanese Cars or German Cars? Content: What is the difference in safety between Japanese cars and German cars? First, it needs to be pointed out that there is a cognitive misconception related to this that many people have, namely that Japanese cars have thin skins and large fillings and are unsafe. The specific origin of this statement is untraceable, but the main basis is that some Japanese cars use relatively thin body shell materials, to the point that pressing down with a hand can leave a dent. Therefore, in the event of an accident, the protection of occupants in the vehicle is insufficient. But in fact, besides airbags and electronic stability control systems, what mainly affects occupant safety is the strength of the body frame. The thickness of the body skin is basically unrelated to this; specifically determining whether a car is safe or not still depends on crash test results. But it cannot be denied that in low-speed collision accidents, generally speaking, German cars with thicker and harder body shells will relatively have an advantage, at least the degree of body shell deformation will be smaller. Next, comparing the two from the perspective of economy, the first is fuel consumption, which has always been a strong point of Japanese cars. Many of their models prioritize fuel saving from the design stage. The light body itself gives an advantage in fuel consumption, and coupled with the fact that many Japanese family cars use CVT continuously variable transmissions, fuel consumption can be further reduced. So overall, Japanese cars are more fuel-efficient than German cars. The second item is later maintenance costs; vehicles with high durability naturally save more money. In the first few years, both German and Japanese cars have very stable quality, but after a certain number of years of use, the durability advantage of Japanese cars becomes apparent. The saying Can't fix a Volkswagen, can't break a Toyota, although somewhat extreme, is not without basis. However, it should be pointed out that the reason German cars are not as durable as Japanese cars is that in design and material selection, they do not put service life first like Japanese cars, but will comprehensively consider the vehicle's performance. After the service life of components reaches basic requirements, German cars will focus on improving vehicle power, handling, and comfort. So this leads to a very obvious advantage of German cars over Japanese cars, namely the driving texture brought by high-quality chassis and NVH control. The chassis vibration filtering and noise isolation capabilities of German cars are usually higher than those of Japanese cars, which not only improves ride comfort but also increases vehicle driving stability. Each has its own strengths. Everyone knows the rigorous consciousness and style in the German bones. Whether in craftsmanship or in life, the rigor and efficiency of Germans permeate their entire life. The same is true in car manufacturing. We can easily find that the engine compartments of German cars are very neat, and the overall appearance is slightly tough. Under the protection of high-strength frames, safety is also relatively high. German car manufacturers have very in-depth research on chassis and engines; they like speed and performance. And speed and performance cannot be separated from excellent chassis tuning and powerful engine output power. This is why young people prefer German cars. Young people relatively pursue speed and performance more, and German cars can provide them with better driving feeling and power output compared to other car series. But how can an engine of the same displacement output higher power? This requires coordination with many accessories, such as turbocharging, etc. The more electrified car accessories there are, the more unpredictable failures will come, which is why German cars have a higher failure rate relative to Japanese cars. For Japanese cars, the public perception may be good stability and not easy to break. Some even say that the Japanese car representative Crown has just passed its break-in period at 90,000 kilometers. This fully highlights the reliability of Japanese cars; the company with the lowest failure rate in the world is Lexus. Shouldn't a low failure rate make the perfect car? Why can German cars still compete with it? Because Japan advocates low-speed driving, car manufacturers' chassis tuning of the entire vehicle is slightly insufficient, and the actual driving quality is difficult to compete with German cars. In terms of engine power, unlike German cars pursuing speed, Japanese cars upgrade fuel economy. Japanese cars prefer to use naturally aspirated engines. Naturally aspirated engines have a very, very long development history, so their technical stability is more excellent. This is also why Japanese cars reduce vehicle costs a lot, but at the same time sacrifice power reserves and performance limits. Although their car-making focuses are different, they also allow different consumer groups to buy their favorite cars. So whether German cars are better or Japanese cars are better, this question is inherently contradictory. Choosing the car you need and the one that suits your driving feeling is the most important. The characteristics of low maintenance rates and easy maintenance of Japanese cars make them very popular in America and Asia, as well as in the turbulent Middle East. This is why we often see armies or terrorists not driving BMW X5s or Mercedes G-Wagens but Toyota Hilux or Land Cruisers; cars that are not easy to repair may cause them to lose their lives. Undoubtedly, Japanese people produce very reliable cars; their cars rarely have problems and are very convenient to repair. In Southeast Asia, you can often see Japanese cars that have driven over a million kilometers without having undergone major repairs several times. In Germany, you can also see that people who don't care about design and interior also like cheap old Japanese cars; they want a reliable car as a daily代步工具. From this perspective, German cars are indeed inferior to Japanese cars. The above content is referenced from: Phoenix Network - Are German cars good or Japanese cars good? What European experts say. The above content is referenced from: Phoenix Network - Torn between German and Japanese cars? After reading this, you'll know which car series is most suitable. Japanese cars also deeply feel that besides some aging equipment problems, the main components are very durable. And a Japanese car driven for ten years still has no major problems, especially the三大件, which is what everyone says about good stability, strong reliability, and worry-free durability. This is indeed a major advantage of Japanese cars. Furthermore, in terms of fuel economy, the same level is indeed better than German and American cars. These should be the issues consumers care about most. Of course, there are also low maintenance costs and complete configurations, which are advantages of Japanese cars that everyone understands. These advantages also attract a large number of ordinary people. But the lighter body is also a recognized fact.

Title: I have only been injured at work for three days, and both parties have decided to compensate me with 8,000 yuan. Is it reasonable to terminate my labor contract? Content: Please consider the following points regarding the title: First, how long have you worked for the employer? According to Article 47 of the 'Labor Contract Law', for each full year of work, you are entitled to one month's salary as economic compensation. If you have worked for less than six months, you are entitled to half a month's salary; if you have worked for more than six months but less than twelve months, you are entitled to one month's salary. The standard should not be lower than the local minimum wage. Second, during the period of medical treatment for the work-related injury, expenses such as medical care, nursing, hospitalization living allowances, and wages are the responsibility of the employer. Third, you know best the extent of your work-related injury. It is recommended that after you have fully recovered, you follow the work-related injury procedures, especially the labor capacity assessment, before deciding whether to agree to the employer's proposed solution. Fourth, during your employment, did the employer establish and contribute to your social insurance, or was it established but contributions were not made in full or completely? If social insurance was not established or contributions were not made, or if it was established but contributions were not complete, you can demand that the employer make up the contributions for pension insurance and claim compensation for unemployment, medical, maternity, and work-related injury insurance. Please consider the above points carefully and think twice before proceeding.

Title: How do I apply to reduce the interest rate on my existing first-home mortgage in Chongqing? Content: How should I apply to reduce the interest rate on my existing first-home mortgage? Answer: According to the notice, for eligible existing housing loans, borrowers have two ways to apply for an interest rate reduction. First, replace the 'old' with the 'new' by applying to the bank for a 'new loan' to replace the 'old mortgage'. Second, negotiate with the bank to change the original interest rate level. The specific method chosen can be discussed with the bank based on your own situation. It is worth noting that if you choose the first method, the newly issued loan can only be used to repay the 'old mortgage' and cannot be used for other purposes. In terms of timing, if you are eligible, you can apply to the bank that provided the original loan starting from September 25, 2023. Currently, banks are preparing by revising contract texts, modifying and adjusting systems, and identifying eligible customers. How to apply at that time still needs to be further clarified by each bank.

Title: ASL Anterior Cruciate Surgery - Autograft or Artificial? Content: Two surgeries in one year, I'm completely numb. Learn from mistakes, recording this. In February 2024, I fell accidentally while changing direction playing ball. Went to Xinhua Hospital and was diagnosed with a complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. Later underwent ASL surgery. Actually, the biggest dilemma then was whether to do autograft or artificial. Let's talk about the differences first. Autograft: Slightly lower price, slower recovery, better compatibility. Artificial: Slightly higher price, faster recovery, stronger ligament. How to put it, it's been a year since the autograft, simply put it was painful for three months, uncomfortable for eight months, and that's excluding the pain from achieving range of motion, because I had no issues achieving range of motion at all. It's been a year now, and I still feel occasional discomfort with excessive exercise or bad weather. This might also be related to muscle atrophy. Overall, rehabilitation training was the most painful part, because it requires persistence. #Knee #Surgery #AnteriorCruciateLigament #ASL

Title: Hospital Launches "Join Hands to Clean Our Home, Co-build a Tidy and Warm Hospital" Activity. Content: On the eve of the Spring Festival, in order to create a clean and tidy medical environment for all patients and staff, the hospital has organized an environmental improvement activity called "Join Hands to Clean Our Home, Co-build a Tidy and Warm Hospital" in recent days. Party members and cadres of the hospital fully played their exemplary and leading roles, mobilizing all staff to conduct a comprehensive cleaning of the hospital. They focused on cleaning sanitary dead corners, cobwebs in high places, garbage, and debris in the responsibility areas, and standardized the placement of various items. They thoroughly cleaned dead corners such as glass, doors, and windows in restrooms, corridors, departments, and wards, and conducted comprehensive disinfection of public areas. This effectively prevented the growth and reproduction of bacteria, blocked the spread of various infectious diseases, further strengthened the prevention and control of hospital infections, and simultaneously provided a comfortable and hygienic environment for patients and staff. Through this activity, the hospital created a warm and comfortable diagnosis and treatment environment for both medical staff and patients. At the same time, it promoted health knowledge to patients, their families, and the surrounding community, helping more people understand the importance of health and hygiene, and called on staff and the public to consciously abide by civilized conventions and develop good hygiene habits. Content Title: Man Buys Xiaomi YU7, Receives Transport-Damaged Car, Deposit Refund Rejected Release Date: 2025-12-02 15:29:30 Content Status: Review Completed Content Type: Multimedia Industry: Digital Government Affairs_Government Media_- Author Name: Fun News Frontier Owner Name: Fun News Frontier Content Account Type: Corporate Content Details: The consumer insisted that Xiaomi refund the 5,000 yuan deposit paid. After negotiation, staff stated they would report the issue internally. A man bought a Xiaomi YU7 and received a transport-damaged car; his deposit refund was rejected. 'The new car hasn't even left the 4S店 and already needs panel beating and painting.' Xiaomi Delivery Center: Original car repair plus 10,000 points compensation. The consumer insisted that Xiaomi refund the 5,000 yuan deposit paid. After negotiation, staff stated they would report the issue internally. Released on December 2. Voice source: Mr. Xu. 'I haven't even driven the new car out of the 4S店 yet, and you want me to do panel beating and painting? Giving me 10,000 points?' Mr. Xu from Zhengzhou sought help. In response, staff at the Xiaomi Delivery Center admitted it was their responsibility, stating transport accidents are hard to control. They offered Mr. Xu three solutions: 'I don't want points. 1. Title: Cangzhou Civil Affairs Bureau Solidly Carries Out the "Look Back" Work on the Reelection of Village (Neighborhood) Committees Content: • Index Number: 000537238/2000000100 • Topic Classification: Civil Affairs, Poverty Alleviation, Disaster Relief, Others • Publishing Institution: Municipal Civil Affairs Bureau, • Document Date: • Name: Cangzhou Civil Affairs Bureau Solidly Carries Out the "Look Back" Work on the Reelection of Village (Neighborhood) Committees • Document Number: • Release Date: 2019-10-11 • Keywords: • Validity: Cangzhou Civil Affairs Bureau Solidly Carries Out the "Look Back" Work on the Reelection of Village (Neighborhood) Committees To further consolidate and expand the achievements of the village (neighborhood) committee reelection, strengthen the construction of grassroots cadres, and solidly advance the special campaign against organized crime and evil forces, the Municipal Civil Affairs Bureau has taken active action, made careful deployments, and solidly carried out the "look back" work on the village (neighborhood) committee reelection. First, carry out self-inspection and rectification work for the "look back" on the reelection. This mainly focuses on whether the reelection was truly conducted, whether the reelection materials are complete, whether the reelection procedures are standard, whether the candidate qualification review was rigorous, the status of supporting organization construction, work handover status, and public satisfaction, among other contents, to carry out self-inspection and rectification. Second, conduct investigation and assessment of the newly elected team members. For all newly elected members of the village (neighborhood) committees, a "screening" method is adopted to investigate village by village (community), focusing on investigating whether there is involvement in organized crime or evil forces, whether they have received criminal punishment, whether the qualification review was strict, etc. For personnel who have received criminal punishment, have "village tyrant" problems, or are involved in organized crime or evil forces, cleanup and rectification are carried out in accordance with national laws and regulations and relevant policies. Up to now, 65 village committee cadres have been removed, including 31 village committee directors, and 35 village committee cadres have been by-elected, including 16 village committee directors. Third, organize and carry out a major investigation action on petitions. In response to problems such as complex situations in some villages (communities), numerous conflicts and issues, and prominent petition problems, a major investigation action on petition issues related to the reelection is carried out to achieve early detection, early reporting, and early handling. Improve the petition handling mechanism to ensure that petitions are managed and handled by someone, resolving issues in their budding stage. For problems reflected by the public, ensure that every matter has a follow-up and every case receives a response. Fourth, guide the establishment and improvement of village-level organizations and village affairs operation mechanisms. Supervise villages (communities) to establish organizations such as village (neighborhood) affairs supervision committees in accordance with laws and regulations. Establish and improve the guidance for village (neighborhood) representative meetings, guide the formulation and revision of democratic management regulations such as village (neighborhood) residents' autonomy charters and village (neighborhood) covenants, guide the implementation of the "four discussions and two disclosures" work method, and improve the village (neighborhood) residents' autonomy operation mechanism under the leadership of the Party organization, truly ensuring that all work has rules to follow and laws to rely on.

Title: How to choose? Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University or a 211 university... Content: I am currently a senior high school student in Yunnan, studying at a provincial key high school, majoring in science. My teacher estimates that based on last year's scores, I can exceed the first-tier cutoff by over 100 points... Should I choose Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University or a university like Xiamen University? I really want to study abroad, and my family's financial situation is okay, so I can afford to pay the full fees myself... I want to set a goal now, please help me, seniors! Thank you so much! Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University (XJTLU) was established in 2006 in Suzhou with approval from the Chinese Ministry of Education, through a collaboration between Xi'an Jiaotong University and the University of Liverpool. It inherits and leverages the strengths of its parent universities in science, engineering, technology, and management, integrates the essence of Eastern and Western education systems, and capitalizes on China's strong economic growth to attract global high-quality resources, strengthening its development as a research-oriented comprehensive university, gradually gaining recognition in the international higher education sector. XJTLU's professional courses are taught entirely in English. Students undergo rigorous academic English training in their first year, equipping them with language proficiency equivalent to that required for studying at universities in English-speaking countries and laying a foundation for further professional English learning. By choosing XJTLU, students can access international renowned faculty resources within China. The teachers either hold PhDs from world-renowned universities and research institutes like Oxford, Cambridge, and Harvard, or are distinguished professors with extensive teaching experience from universities like Columbia and Penn, or may be top international scholars such as the former Chairman of the British Protein Research Association. XJTLU draws on the UK higher education quality assurance system, strictly monitoring teaching and assessment processes. The teaching process is evaluated by both China and the UK, ensuring high-quality student cultivation. Many disciplines at XJTLU have received accreditation from international professional organizations, directly enhancing graduates' competitiveness in global industry institutions and international business organizations. Over 85% of graduates pursue further studies at prestigious overseas institutions, and the number of graduates entering Fortune 500 companies, multinational corporations, large central enterprises, and the big five state-owned banks is increasing annually. Those with relevant intentions are advised to consult XJTLU. XJTLU undergraduate graduates receive both the XJTLU undergraduate diploma and bachelor's degree certificate recognized by the Chinese Ministry of Education, and the internationally recognized University of Liverpool bachelor's degree certificate. Postgraduates can receive a University of Liverpool degree recognized by the Chinese Ministry of Education. XJTLU's continuous investment and emphasis on postgraduate education are essential paths to realizing its vision of becoming a 'research-oriented, unique, world-recognized Chinese university and an international university on Chinese soil.' It is recommended to choose a 211 university for higher cost-effectiveness. XJTLU has strong faculty resources, with its faculty evaluation indicators once ranking within the top 15 domestically, demonstrating considerable teaching strength. Additionally, the university offers advantages in terms of its foreign language environment and direct pathway to studying abroad. If focusing on studying abroad, there are also some economic benefits. However, the tuition fees at XJTLU are relatively high, which might be difficult for ordinary families to afford. As for 211 universities, their characteristics are also prominent. Another factor is that 211 universities also have Sino-foreign cooperative programs that can be considered, with relatively lower tuition fees and the opportunity to obtain dual degrees from both domestic and foreign institutions. The popularity of majors is also high, tuition fees are much lower, and there is flexibility regarding whether to study abroad or not, offering more room for consideration. Extended Information: XJTLU's Educational Philosophy: With the overarching goal of 'learning to be, learning to learn, learning to live, and developing expertise,' it guides students towards autonomous development. Through initiatives like establishing a student TV station, holding art festivals, and organizing various activities as a provincial traditional sports project school, it provides students with more freedom. The construction and activities of the Party and Youth League organizations have significantly improved teaching and learning ethos. 211 University Educational Philosophy: The university adheres to the educational philosophy of 'everything for the sustainable development of students, having what others don't, excelling where others have, refining where others excel, building the university into a demonstrative boutique institution with a beautiful environment, advanced facilities, standardized management, first-class quality, simple school ethos, pragmatic teaching style, and solid learning atmosphere,' fully leveraging the advantages of its high-quality educational resources. The Hongzhi class it strives to build has become a renowned educational brand. If you have decided to study abroad and have the financial means for self-funded study, then you should firmly choose XJTLU and decisively give up Xiamen University. Mainly because: 1. You should know that the primary condition for studying abroad is English (foreign language) proficiency, either IELTS or TOEFL. XJTLU uses all-English teaching, while Xiamen University does not. The English learning environment at the former is far superior to the latter. Achieving an IELTS score of 6.5 or above at XJTLU is commonplace, whereas at Xiamen University, it requires extra effort. 2. The study abroad rate for the first three graduating classes of XJTLU is around 80-90%, with close to 50% successfully applying for master's (or PhD) programs at world top 100 universities. The study abroad rate of Xiamen University is far incomparable to XJTLU. So, frankly, the possibility of studying abroad and successfully applying to foreign first-class or even top-tier universities is much greater at XJTLU than at Xiamen University. 3. XJTLU is a Sino-foreign cooperative institution, primarily adopting the British education system and methods. Teachers are recruited globally with high standards (teaching staff all hold PhDs, including world-class scholars). It has strict entry (through the national college entrance exam, admission above the first-tier line) and strict exit (British-style exams, absolutely no issues like exam cheating prevalent in some Chinese universities). The caliber of XJTLU students can only be higher than that of Xiamen University students, not lower. What is lower than Xiamen University is the university's domestic reputation (mainly because XJTLU was established relatively recently and is not eligible for the 985 or 211 projects). 4. Given your grades, you are fully capable of obtaining a first-class entrance scholarship from XJTLU, meaning you receive a scholarship equivalent to the annual tuition fee, effectively studying for free. Thus, the high tuition fees at XJTLU are not a problem for you. 5. Another very important point: International students going to foreign universities must undergo a process of adapting to different educational philosophies and learning methods (studying abroad is different from domestic study), which generally takes at least a year. This transition process can be very difficult and painful. Studying at XJTLU first and then going abroad means this transition has already been made at XJTLU, so you avoid this adjustment process after going abroad, which is a significant advantage. Whereas studying at Xiamen University or other domestic universities first means undergoing this transition after going abroad. I am a current student at XJTLU and happened to see your question. Recently, due to preparing for the IELTS exam, I don't have much time to elaborate. To be realistic, if you are sure you can get into Xiamen University or better, please do not come here. Going to Xiamen University and studying abroad are completely, completely, completely not conflicting. You can even use Xiamen University, a Ministry of Education直属 985 national key university, as a springboard to pursue a master's at a top US university later. Studying undergraduate at Xiamen University also offers opportunities for exchange programs in the UK and US; I have classmates at Xiamen University who have gone abroad. XJTLU's study abroad rate is high, abnormally high at 90%, which the university boasts about. However, my understanding is the opposite: this abnormally high study abroad rate reflects the lack of confidence among current students in XJTLU itself, with everyone hoping to 'brush up' their less prestigious undergraduate degree by pursuing a master's at a famous overseas university. Furthermore, you can look into the destinations of our graduates studying abroad. How many go to the US, which has the highest 'prestige density'? And how many go to Oxford or Cambridge, the most valuable UK universities? A large number go to universities outside the US TOP 50 or UK TOP 5, especially UK universities at a level similar to Liverpool – what is there to boast about? Quite a few students go to the London School of Economics, but how many are enrolled in its high-value programs? Nowadays, the UK uses international students to make money; universities outside the TOP 5 are often considered 'watered-down'. I believe someone capable of getting into Xiamen University would not be interested in those. Focus on the college entrance exam first, no need to think so far ahead. If you want to study abroad, come to XJTLU~ Scoring over 100 points above the first-tier line can waive your tuition fees~~ Take the 2+2 path, you can go to Liverpool in your third year~ It will be much easier to apply for UK master's programs later~ Last year, 60 students went to Imperial College London.
