Title: Why Don't Chinese Public Hospitals Like to Advertise? Content: Author: 573 Searching on a search engine for 'Where is the best place to treat pancreatic cancer?', the first answer that pops up is from a certified doctor: 'Hard to treat, get surgery promptly.' Such a vague answer is like telling someone drowning and calling for help from the shore: 'Lifebuoys are important!' In fact, no matter what channel you use to search for similar questions, the answers you get are almost all ambiguous. Why? You can't make bricks without straw. At the source, public hospitals in China simply don't like to use advertising to attract patients, so patients can only rely on word-of-mouth and feel their way across the river. Public Hospitals That Don't Like to Advertise In China, private hospitals, with nearly 70% of the country's medical institutions, manage less than 15% of the patients, but their advertising coverage sweeps across the board, greatly overshadowing public hospitals. In terms of the number of advertisements, as far back as 2003, when private hospitals accounted for only 46% of the country's medical institutions, their number of advertising applications was still 9 times that of public institutions - and these public institutions were mainly ones with outsourced departments, with commercial promotion from regular top-tier (Grade 3A) hospitals being rare. Source: National Health Commission, edited by Toubao Institute However, what many people don't know is that public hospitals in China also had a history of advertising. In 2003, the Eye & ENT Hospital of Fudan University put up billboards at the South 1 and South 2 exits of Shanghai Railway Station, using the slogan 'Make the world more colorful' to welcome patients from afar. And 20 years ago, Ruijin Hospital affiliated with Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, Zhongshan Hospital affiliated with Fudan University, etc., also once promoted themselves at airports, subways, and upscale residential areas. So, it's not that public hospitals don't eat the 'advertising' meal, they just don't like it that much. Taking the present as an example, major public hospitals are using WeChat public accounts and APPs for self-promotion and branding. But are they really using these promotional channels well? It seems not; most public hospitals are just thinking in terms of 'being forced to compete intensely'. In terms of content, the front-page content of public hospitals' WeChat accounts is mostly about Party building meetings, free medical consultations, life-saving deeds, etc. – monotonous positive praises and legendary stories. Even case descriptions are filled with professional jargon. And in the more important mass media, the shadow of top hospitals is almost invisible; what the public is familiar with are instead some Putian-style hospitals. Outpatient Overload, Advertising is 'A Lot of Effort for Little Reward' It's important to know that 'public hospitals don't like to advertise' is not a universal rule. Also taking 'pancreatic cancer' as an example, if you search on Google for 'where to treat pancreatic cancer', the top results are respectively treatment introductions from the American Cancer Society, the UK's National Health Service (NHS), Mayo Clinic, and MD Anderson. Promotional videos for disease treatment from American non-profit university hospitals, such as Mayo Clinic and Massachusetts General Hospital, have long been ubiquitous on Google and YouTube; and the publicly-funded NHS in the UK even approved celebrities endorsing public hospitals in 2008. Non-profit or public hospitals in these countries and regions all engage in advertising or high-profile promotion, aiming to facilitate patient access to care. Road Trip, you know where to go Source: Mayo Clinic Ad So the question returns, why is it specifically public hospitals in our country that don't put effort into self-promotion? One problem everyone knows about is the already overloaded outpatient volume. According to the 2020 Statistical Bulletin on the Development of China's Health Undertakings, the outpatient volume of China's top-tier (Grade 3A) hospitals is already operating overloaded. Placing advertisements to attract patients seems to increase the hospital's operational burden. Overworked Chinese Doctors Source: 2020 Statistical Bulletin on the Development of China's Health Undertakings If we do a calculation, taking cardiology outpatient services in Shanghai and New York as an example, the fee for a cardiology outpatient visit in Shanghai is 25-500 RMB/person, while in New York City it is 195-510 USD/person (not counting insurance, international outpatient fees not included). Calculating for the hospital as a whole, from 2012 to 2018, outpatient revenue accounted for 32-33% of the total revenue of Chinese hospitals (of which registration fees were only 2%), showing an overall downward trend; while during the same period, outpatient revenue accounted for 40-48% of the total revenue of American hospitals, showing an overall upward trend. If in other countries, the economic benefits from outpatient labor can be equated with doctor income, then for most Chinese public hospitals, outpatient labor often means additional human resource costs without a significant increase in economic revenue. Clearly 'a lot of effort for little reward', this explains why domestic hospitals are unwilling to place advertisements and attract more patients. The Commercialization Paradox Another issue is that advertising seems to carry a 'commercialization' label, and for public hospitals, even a little bit of 'performance growth' is viewed by society as heresy. A few years ago, Wuchuan City People's Hospital in Guangdong hung a banner saying, 'Warmly congratulate our hospital for exceeding 40,000 inpatient admissions in 2012' – which drew criticism from netizens accusing the hospital doctors of being profit-driven and having lost medical ethics. Regarding this, some experts have suggested that, based on the public welfare nature of public hospitals and the特殊性 of receiving government funding (although some hospitals only have 5% of their income from government funding), public hospitals fundamentally cannot be marketized. If they were to engage in even a little bit of advertising to attract 'customers' like Putian-style hospitals, then public hospitals would more easily become the target of public criticism. Promotional information on the website of a Chinese top-tier (Grade 3A) hospital compared with that of a similar-level American university-affiliated hospital. Relatively speaking, the content promoted by Chinese hospitals is less connected to the daily lives of ordinary people. (Source: Hospital website screenshot) On this basis, the hospital's publicity departments are also relatively less dedicated. Overall, the focus of promotion for most public hospitals is on enhancing their reputation within the industry through various academic conferences, published papers and awards, surgical videos, etc. For public awareness outside the industry, they almost entirely rely on 'resting on their laurels'. The publicity departments of most hospitals also tend to operate their WeChat public accounts more as task completion rather than pursuing readership and effectiveness. The result is that the information released by the hospital's publicity department does not meet the needs of patients, lacking market awareness and a service attitude. These factors ultimately collectively lead to the weakness of the hospital's promotional channels and indifference to advertising and brand building. To Advertise or Not? The combined result of all these factors is that hospitals don't like to advertise, and patients have to continue 'the blind men touching the elephant'. Why 'the blind men touching the elephant'? Obviously, most patients rarely get to understand which department of which top-tier hospital is most suitable for treating their disease, let alone which department of which hospital is most expert in which specific disease area. In today's world where sub-specialties and disease specializations are increasingly refined, neither the National Health Commission's 'National Exam Report Card' nor Fudan University's Hospital Ranking can provide sufficiently detailed categorization. For example, the Fudan ranking has a full 40 specialties, but unfortunately, General Surgery alone has numerous sub-specialties like Basic Surgery (e.g., Peking Union Medical College Hospital), Liver Surgery, Biliary Surgery, Pancreatic Surgery, Colorectal Surgery, Gastrointestinal Surgery, and Thyroid & Breast Surgery, etc. And we all know that a single ranking can hardly provide sufficient advice for patients with specific diseases seeking medical care. Source: Fudan Ranking Official Website In such an environment, advertising is not just about pursuing performance improvement; it is also about hospital brand building and a form of patient service. For example, the total views on Mayo Clinic's YouTube channel exceed 2.2 billion, and one video about female reproduction reached 17 million views. The revenue brought by this video is not just the账面 income of 230,000 RMB; the power of science popularization and the attraction of patients to Mayo Clinic's reproductive medicine department are crucial. At the same time, if public hospitals do not occupy the various fronts of public opinion, they will be occupied by the 'enemy'. Although China's public medical units, constituting 50% of the total, handle over 90% of medical tasks and hold an unshakable position in the national medical system, patient healthcare-seeking behavior has already become fully marketized. Currently, the ones with the strongest promotional momentum are often the various Putian-style hospitals, especially those represented by certain Putian systems in urology, gynecology, and plastic surgery hospitals. If public hospitals still refuse large-scale self-promotion, they无形中 push vulnerable patients towards the well-packaged Putian-style hospitals, especially when the latter's official website development and the convenience of online guidance have already left public hospitals far behind. After all, the quality of promotional results can directly change patients' choices of where to seek medical care, affecting their trust in doctors and departments when they seek treatment, which is closely related to the hospital's economic benefits and social reputation. Outlook Finally, even brothers keep clear accounts; money is also a factor that cannot be avoided. Although the public welfare nature of public hospitals is beyond doubt, hospital performance should be put on the table: public hospitals also need to make money, and public hospital doctors also need to survive. Theoretically, by building the hospital's brand, increasing the strength of the hospital's 'external publicity', and encouraging doctors to build their personal brands, thereby guiding patients for efficient referrals and visits, increasing the hospital's surgical volume and outpatient volume, could be a way to promote hospital development. The orthopedic hospital ranked first in the US sets up huge billboards by the highway. Source: Author's photo Moreover, research shows that hospital mass media, APPs, and new media websites rank 2nd, 3rd, and 4th respectively among the most trusted ways for the public to seek medical care, indicating the significant impact of hospital promotion on patient healthcare choices. Through such promotion, specific disciplines within a hospital can highlight their characteristics and attract specific patients. Additionally, prefecture-level hospitals can even raise screening awareness in their regions through online, offline, and TV science popularization. Without deception or coercion, public hospitals' introduction and promotion of themselves can actually be considered a necessary medical service, and might even become a driving force for private hospitals to move towards standardized competition. (Supervised by: carollero, gyouza) Title image source: Tuchong Creativity References: [1]. He Sichang, Yang Changhao, Ying Jiachuan, Zhao Daren, Zhou Minghua, Jin Xiufang. Analysis of the changes in medical income of national tertiary public hospitals from 2012 to 2018 [J]. Chinese Health Quality Management, 2021, 28(03): 93-96. [2]. https://www.theguardian.com/society/2008/mar/20/nhs.health [3]. '2020 Statistical Bulletin on the Development of China's Health Undertakings' http://www.nhc.gov.cn/gui-huaxxs/s10743/202107/af8a9c98453c4d9593e07895ae0493c8.shtml [4]. 2017 Report on the Living Conditions of Chinese Doctors [5]. https://alyssacav.com/mayo-youknowwheretogo

Title: Which is more difficult, the English test for the college upgrade exam or CET-4? Content: Generally speaking, the difficulty of the English test for the college upgrade exam is not as high as CET-4. It is often explained that the difficulty of the upgrade exam's English is between Level 3 and Level 4, but this is not entirely accurate because the difficulty of the upgrade exam varies from province to province. Moreover, the content and format of the English test for the college upgrade exam are quite different from CET-4. The focus of CET-4 is on listening and reading. The four major sections of CET-4 are: Writing (15%), Listening Comprehension (35%), Reading Comprehension (35%), and Translation (15%). In contrast, most provinces do not test listening in the college upgrade exam. For example, the Shandong college upgrade English exam does not include listening. Instead, grammar and vocabulary account for a larger proportion in the upgrade exams of various provinces. In terms of difficulty, the English test for the college upgrade exam is less difficult than CET-4. The vocabulary requirement for the upgrade exam is about 3,500 words, while CET-4 requires about 4,500 words. The upgrade exam mainly tests the basic meanings and collocations of words, whereas CET-4 tests the multiple meanings of vocabulary in different contexts and involves more uncommon words. CET-4 places less emphasis on grammar, focusing instead on the application of the five skills: listening, speaking, reading, writing, and translation. It is highly comprehensive and can assess candidates' English proficiency more thoroughly, which is beneficial for future employment. The question types in the upgrade exam are more complex and detailed. Since most provinces do not test listening, the overall difficulty is lower. The upgrade exam places greater emphasis on reading, writing, translation skills, and grammar proficiency. In CET-4, grammar does not determine whether you pass but rather helps you achieve a higher score; however, in the upgrade exam, grammar can determine whether you reach the passing mark. Therefore, students preparing for the upgrade exam (especially those in their first or second year of college) must strengthen their grammar foundation if they want to score high in English. The college upgrade exam is a selective test that focuses more on students' basic English knowledge. CET-4 is a proficiency test that assesses whether students have reached a certain level. Don't assume that if you can't pass CET-4, the upgrade exam's English will be very difficult; nor should you think that if you pass CET-4, the upgrade exam's English will be easy. It can only be said that passing CET-4 is very helpful for preparing for the upgrade exam's English, as at least you will be ahead of many peers in terms of vocabulary.

Title: Is being 35 years old, working within the system but without a leadership position, considered a failure? Content: A netizen consulted: Is being 35 years old, working within the system but without a leadership position, considered a failure? My reply: Based on the many friends I know who work within the system, it is very normal to have no leadership position by age 35. A job within the system is essentially just a stable job. Regarding your question, I suggest considering the following aspects. 1. Many people apply for jobs within the system simply to obtain stable work. First, a very important point to tell you is that for many young people taking the civil service exam, when they initially take the exam, they never even consider what kind of leadership position they might hold in the future. Most people just hope to get a stable job. This is actually a very normal phenomenon because all stable jobs mean that turnover is relatively slow. When a leadership position becomes available, competition is very fierce. It's normal for dozens of people to compete for a single deputy section chief-level position. If you are not outstanding enough, you cannot get a leadership position. Especially among the young people taking the civil service exam, many have average educational backgrounds and average learning abilities. After starting work within the system, they simply treat it as a stable job and do not treat it as a career. Shouldn't these people work in ordinary operational positions their whole lives? 2. The vast majority of people working in public institutions have no leadership position. From the many friends I know working within the system, if you work in a public institution, most people will never hold any leadership position in their entire lives. This is because there simply aren't many leadership positions in public institutions, which is important to understand. For example, a public institution might have dozens of staff positions, but typically there are only three leadership positions allocated: one chief and two deputies. Among so many people, as long as someone occupies these three positions and doesn't vacate them, those below have no chance to become leaders. Another example is in the education system. If you are a teacher at a school, most people will never hold a leadership position in their lives; they will just be ordinary teachers. However, you can increase your salary by improving your professional title and technical grade, which does not affect your personal development. 3. For career development within the system, both ability and platform are very important. Based on my years of experience, I believe that for a young person to have good development within the system and reach important leadership positions, two factors are crucial. The first factor is the platform you are on, and the second factor is your ability level. The higher the platform of your unit, the better your future development space will be. For example, if you work at a county-level unit, which is a section chief-level unit, getting promoted to deputy section chief is very difficult. But if you work at a municipal unit, which is a department chief-level unit, getting promoted to section chief is very simple. Compared to a county town, the career ceiling is much higher. Another important factor is ability. The ability referred to here is comprehensive ability, not the ability for a specific operational task. Whether you can reach a leadership position depends on your comprehensive ability level and what significant achievements you can make. Don't focus on connections; capable people will eventually get to know many contacts. This article was originally created by Lingnan Tongtu. Welcome to consult through the homepage Q&A about the困惑 you face in life.

Title: Inaction by Property Management in a Residential Community in Zoucheng Content: On the evening of July 29 at 22:00, the Hongjing Yayuan residential community in Zoucheng experienced a power outage, which had not been restored by 16:00 on the afternoon of the 30th. Contact with State Grid revealed that it was not within their jurisdiction and required the property management to handle it. The property management was inactive, taking no emergency measures and not actively resolving the issue after the outage. It wasn't until around 7:00 on the morning of the 30th that repairs began. In such hot weather, it was impossible to rest properly at night. What about families with elderly and children! Can't we apply to switch to the unified national power grid? Handling Department: Zoucheng Municipal Government [2023-08-03 16:10:31] Reply as follows: Dear netizen, hello! Thank you for your trust and support. Your inquiry has been handled and replied by Gangshan Sub-district Office: Upon verification, due to recent heavy rainfall, a power outage occurred in the Hongjing Yayuan community around 21:43 on July 29 due to a substation trip. Around 22:10 that night, the property management's on-duty personnel immediately contacted the power supply department to restore power to the community. After the western section of the community was normally powered that night, it was discovered that the eastern section could not be powered when attempting to supply it. After investigation, it was determined that the cause was a fault in the high-voltage cable line from the western section's distribution room to the eastern section's distribution room. Staff immediately began detecting the specific fault point and carried out repair work. As this task is quite specialized, to resolve it quickly and ensure residents' normal power usage during the high-temperature weather, the property management company coordinated two external professional construction teams successively for inspection and repairs, and purchased cables to replace the high-voltage cable in the eastern section. Power was restored to the eastern section residents by 20:00 on the evening of July 30. We apologize for any inconvenience caused. Thank you for your inquiry, and we wish you a pleasant life. Source: Jining Online Inquiry Platform

Title: 【Thrilling】3-Year-Old Boy's Head Stuck in Guardrail, Body Hanging in Mid-Air; Yinchuan Elder Climbs Building Bare-Handed to Support Him for Half an Hour! Content: News Summary On the evening of July 4th, a 3-year-old child in Yanqingyuan Community climbed out of his 6th-floor window to play but accidentally got his head stuck between the guardrail bars, leaving his entire body dangling in mid-air in an extremely critical situation. At the crucial moment, an elderly man courageously climbed up to the 5th-floor balcony and supported the child with both hands until firefighters arrived and successfully rescued both of them. Afterwards, the elderly man left quietly. Now, the child's family just wants to find this brave and kind-hearted old man to thank him in person. Danger: 3-year-old child climbs out of the window, hanging on the guardrail. Ms. Kang lives in Yanqingyuan Community, managed by Yangeh Lake Committee. As her husband works outdoors year-round, she usually takes care of their 3-year-old son alone. Around 8:10 PM on July 4th, Ms. Kang needed to go out for an errand, so she asked her niece to look after the child. The little boy, having seen his mother lock the door every night, learned this skill. After his mother left, he locked the door himself. When Ms. Kang's niece arrived, she couldn't open the lock from the outside. Picture: The elderly man stands on the 5th-floor balcony, holding the frightened child. The little boy usually loves watching cartoons like Superman and Transformers and enjoys imitating various cool actions. After his mother left, he played by himself in the playroom. There is a sofa near the window in the playroom. The little boy stepped on the sofa and climbed onto the windowsill. Accidentally, his shoe fell down. He tried to retrieve it, but ended up flipping over outside the window. Fortunately, there was a guardrail outside the window. His head got stuck between two bars, but his body was left hanging in mid-air. The first to discover the danger was a neighbor on the third floor, who immediately called for help and quickly brought out a quilt from her home, spreading it on the cement ground directly below the child. Soon, residents active downstairs noticed the little boy. Some began calling the police and dialing 119 for rescue. Urgency: Elderly man fearlessly supports the child for half an hour; child rescued. When Ms. Kang heard her son was in danger, less than 5 minutes after she left home, she panicked, turned around, and rushed home. Before even reaching the building entrance, she saw her young son hanging from the guardrail of their 6th-floor balcony from a distance. Terrified, she burst into tears, crying and running upstairs. But the door was locked from the inside and couldn't be opened. Without a second thought, she planned to climb out of the 5th-floor corridor window to rescue the child. Picture: Residents downstairs reach out their hands, ready to catch the child at any moment. At that moment, an elderly man stopped her, saying, "You can't go. If the child sees you and reaches out, it will be dangerous. Let me go instead!" After saying this, the old man climbed out of the corridor window, moved step by step along the narrow ledge less than 20 cm wide on the exterior of the building, until he reached a stable position above the 5th-floor window guardrail. He reached out and firmly supported the child. By then, more and more residents gathered downstairs, anxiously watching the elderly man and the child. Community security also quickly arrived, splitting into two teams: one tried to pry open the door, while the other found space from a 5th-floor resident's window to protect the endangered elderly man and child. Soon after, firefighters arrived at the scene, along with a locksmith. Ms. Kang's door was finally opened. Firefighters worked from inside, cutting the guardrail and successfully pulling the child and the elderly man into the room. The entire process lasted about 32 minutes. Warmth: Son safe, she says she must find the lifesaver. Only when her son stood safely before her did Ms. Kang's heart settle. She hugged her son and couldn't hold back her tears. The elderly man who risked his life to support the child quietly got up to leave. The shocked Ms. Kang asked the old man to leave his name and contact information, but he waved his hand and declined, saying, "We're all from the same community. It's good that the child is safe." When the reporter met Ms. Kang today, her eyes were still red and swollen. The child's father rushed back overnight. They took the child to the hospital for a check-up; the child was physically fine. They are deeply grateful for the help from their neighbors, the police, and the firefighters. Of course, they are even more grateful to the old man. Due to the panic at the time, Ms. Kang didn't even remember what the old man looked like. "I only remember he wore gray pants, a blue top, had slightly yellowish skin, a square face, and looked very kind." Now, Ms. Kang's family just wants to find this kind-hearted old man to express their gratitude in person. "He saved our child's life. We must find him. We also hope residents who witnessed the incident can provide clues to help us fulfill our wish." Let's give a thumbs-up to the kind-hearted old man! Source: Ningxia News Network

Title: Residential Compound Fence Gets a "New Look", Enhancing Both Appearance and Safety! Content: "There were many damaged areas on this fence, posing safety hazards, and the outer protective path wasn't very good either. Now that it's repaired, I feel it's great. It's not only safer, but the environment is more beautiful, and our residents' sense of happiness has also improved!" Uncle Zhao is a long-term resident of Yangchun New Era Community in Haidian Street, having lived here for 18 years. Recently, the fence in Yangchun Guanghua Fengshuyuan residential compound got a "new look", giving the residents' living environment a "new face". It is understood that the compound's old fence, installed in 2000, had never been replaced. Long-term exposure to wind, sun, and rust meant the iron fence could potentially topple over in windy weather. Additionally, many concrete bases were broken and fallen, posing certain safety risks. "The community fence has been in use for over 20 years," said Sui Shucai, Secretary of the Yangchun New Era Community Party Committee. "It was built by the original developer during construction. Due to long-term exposure to wind and rain, rust and damage are quite severe. The property management would make timely repairs, but after all, it's been over 20 years, and some parts can no longer be welded." What troubled residents more was the numerous holes in the fence, making effective management impossible. People could enter and exit freely through the holes, and strangers often entered the compound, posing safety concerns that worried everyone. The residents' troubles are the top priority for the Community Party Committee. Since the beginning of this year, during household visits, the Yangchun New Era Community Party Committee learned about the residents' demands. To create a safe living environment and solve the residents' worries, the Community Party Committee, together with the property management office and resident representatives, conducted on-site inspections, widely collected public opinions, and held resident consultation meetings, deciding to put the fence replacement for Yangchun New Era Community on the agenda. "During daily work, some residents also mentioned to me their hope to repair and replace the fence," Sui Shucai told the reporter. The initial stage of the project was not smooth. The original developer could no longer be contacted, and the homeowners' committee had not been successfully re-elected since its term expired in 2012. Therefore, the possibility and feasibility of replacement by the developer or using public maintenance funds were extremely low and difficult. Consequently, after widely soliciting residents' opinions, the Community Party Committee summarized the fence replacement demand and reported it to the sub-district office. Understanding the public's need, the Haidian Street Party Working Committee always prioritized public demand, promptly held meetings to discuss, and finally decided to use the Party organization's service-to-the-masses funds to solve the financing problem for the fence replacement. "The urgent needs of the people are definitely the top priority for our Community Party Committee. We must put serving the people and doing practical things first, and improve the quality and effectiveness of our service to the people," Sui said. Less than a month after the replacement project started, the new stainless steel fence was completed. The new fence is made of painted aluminum art, in a purple-brown color, with a stylish and aesthetically pleasing appearance. This move not only resolved the long-standing safety hazards in Yangchun Guanghua Fengshuyuan compound but also built a "solid barrier" for the residents' living safety. People's livelihoods are no small matter, especially issues that endanger resident safety, which are the top priorities for the community to solve. The "Xiao Hai" members of Yangchun New Era Community will continue to promote the rapid implementation of the "Micro Practical Matters for People's Livelihoods" project, focusing on solving residents' minor, urgent, and difficult matters, and enhancing their sense of gain, happiness, and security. Haidian Media focuses on matters close to the people and serves their concerns, specially launching the "Xiao Hai Helps You" multimedia column for livelihood services. "Xiao Hai" is the collective name for the thousands of grassroots workers in Haidian District, the embodiment of serving the people, and a window for Haidian Media to follow urban governance through media. The "Xiao Hai Helps You" column airs every Tuesday and Friday after "Haidian News", and is simultaneously released on "Haidian News" newspaper, Haidian Net, the Palm Haidian mobile app, other district-level media platforms, and various online new media accounts. Title: Discussing Smart Property Management, Looking Forward to a New Chapter in Industry Development Content: From September 11 to 13, 2024, the "2024 5th Guangzhou International Smart Property Expo" was grandly held in Halls 5 and 6 of the Guangzhou Poly World Trade Expo Center, jointly organized by the Guangdong Property Management Industry Association, the Guangzhou Property Management Industry Association, and Guangzhou Xuyang International Exhibition Co., Ltd. As an annual event for the property management industry, this expo covered an exhibition area of 22,000 square meters. By integrating resources from the entire property industry chain, it gathered the most cutting-edge technological products and solutions in smart property management, smart communities, and smart cities. Concurrently, more than 10 high-end professional events were held, including the "3rd City Lights · Town-Wide Service Governance Exhibition," which showcased outstanding enterprise cases and member units participating in town-wide service governance and the "Hundreds, Thousands, and Tens of Thousands Project," promoting the high-quality development of urban services. The Qinghai Property Management Association (abbreviated as "Qinghai Property Association") participated as one of the co-organizers, actively engaging and showcasing the spirit of Qinghai's property management professionals. The Qinghai Property Association highly valued this participation opportunity, organizing a capable team with the aim of using the broad platform of the Guangzhou Expo to learn about new technologies and developments in the industry, absorb new ideas and concepts, and strengthen communication and cooperation with peers nationwide to jointly promote the innovative development of the property management industry. During the expo, the Qinghai Property Association conducted extensive and in-depth exchanges with property management associations, property companies, and related enterprises from various provinces and cities across China. Through mutual learning and complementing each other's strengths, they not only enhanced friendships and cooperation with peers but also laid a solid foundation for future in-depth collaboration in property management and urban services. Furthermore, the Qinghai Property Association actively participated in various high-end professional events held during the expo, including the main forum, sub-forums, and thematic seminars. By listening to the cutting-edge views and experience sharing of industry experts and enterprise representatives, the Qinghai Property Association further broadened its horizons and deepened its understanding of the development trends in the property management industry. Ding Qiuhua, President of the Qinghai Property Management Industry Association, stated: "We feel very honored to have organized Qinghai's property management enterprises to participate in this grand event. In the rapidly evolving property management industry, continuous learning and innovation are crucial. Therefore, we hope to continuously absorb cutting-edge wisdom and knowledge from the industry through this expo. We also hope that through in-depth exchanges and cooperation with peers from all over the country, we can jointly explore new models and methods for property management. Finally, we will apply what we have learned to practical work, striving to create a more harmonious, beautiful, and livable environment for the residents of Qinghai and contribute our part to the development of our cities and community construction." By participating in the 2024 5th Guangzhou International Smart Property Expo, the Qinghai Property Association not only gained rich industry information and cooperation opportunities but also further clarified its future development direction and priorities. Moving forward, the Qinghai Property Association will continue to adhere to its purpose of "serving members and promoting industry development," actively learn from advanced experiences and practices, continuously improve its service capabilities and standards, and contribute to the high-quality development of Qinghai's property management industry. Title: Shenzhen Content: > Shenzhen Tourism > Around Shenzhen > Shenzhen Surrounding Travel Guide > Zhuhai Famous Tourist Attractions Complete Guide Zhuhai Famous Tourist Attractions Complete Guide 2013-05-10 13:53 [I want to correct an error] Feisha Beach Attraction Introduction: Feisha Beach gets its name because it is a magical beach, featuring the rare "flying sand" spectacle and the unique tropical plant Langgu Tree. Besides bathing in the blue waves under the sun, you can also find many pleasures exploring nature here. Feisha Beach is located in the southeast of Gaolan Island in western Zhuhai and is rated as one of the Top Ten Scenic Spots of Zhuhai. The beach is about 600 meters long and 200 meters wide, with a vast hinterland, soft and bright sand, and excellent seawater quality. Embraced by green mountains and strange rocks on both sides, after summer rains when the sky clears, ethereal white mist lingers like a veil around the mountainsides. The beach is lush with plants, mostly subtropical species like Casuarina, Large-leaf Acacia, coconut trees, and Langgu. There are seven natural fine beaches around Feisha Beach: Dafeisha, Xisha Bay, Baisha Bay, Xieqian Bay, Sanlang Bay, Xizhen Bay, and Wenzhou Island, which have been developed into several characteristic bathing spots. Featured Landscape Flying Sand Spectacle The Flying Sand Spectacle is a huge sand belt where sand flies uphill against the slope, a rare and peculiar landscape in the South China Sea. It served as a natural coastal navigation marker on the ancient Maritime Silk Road. Langgu Tree Among the various subtropical tree species at Feisha Beach, the Langgu Tree is the most peculiar. They grow by the sea with strong vitality, bearing round fruits that are red with yellow, resembling pineapples, hence also called wild pineapples. Every midsummer, the branches are laden with fruits, creating a beautiful sight from afar. Mangrove Forest The "Peach Blossom Stream" to the right of Feisha Beach has a lush "mangrove forest," with about 5 different categories, estimated to be around 6 mu. With clear waters and green mountains, rare tree species, birds singing and flowers fragrant, and butterflies dancing in groups, it is a rare ecological protection area. Facilities Feisha Beach now has service facilities such as a shower room complex building, villas, and seafood restaurants. Here, you not only have things to see but also to play. Surfing, playing in the water, being a fisherman, beach camping, fishing, beach volleyball await you to show your skills. There are also thrilling sports like parasailing, water jet skiing, banana boats, and rubber boats, guaranteed to be exciting. You can also go scuba diving or visit the Feisha Beach Aquarium. Self-Service Guide: 1. Ticket Price: Peak season 38 yuan, off-season 28 yuan. 2. Transportation Guide: About a one-and-a-half-hour drive from Zhuhai. Take a minibus from the central Jida District (8 yuan per person) for about one hour to the Feisha Beach terminal station, then take a private motorcycle (can carry two people, 8 yuan per vehicle) and walk for half an hour on mountain roads to reach the beach. Alternatively, take bus 704 or 706 to the Jinshatan terminal station to reach Feisha Beach. 3. Title: A Boy in Zhangzhou Bitten by a Venomous Snake! If Bitten, These 7 Hospitals Can Save Lives Content: As temperatures gradually rise recently, snake activity has become more frequent, and snakebite incidents also occur from time to time. Recently, a 12-year-old boy in Zhangpu County was bitten by a bamboo viper. Fortunately, after timely treatment at Zhangpu County Hospital, he was discharged smoothly. Around 9 p.m. on the day of the incident, Congcong (pseudonym), who lives in Shiliu Town, Zhangpu County, went out to take out the trash. Due to poor visibility in the rain, he didn't notice a snake coiled at his doorstep. Subsequently, Congcong was accidentally bitten on his left foot. The wound was painful and swollen, and the top of his foot turned black and blue. After identification by family members, the snake was confirmed to be a venomous bamboo viper. The family urgently sent him to Zhangpu County Hospital for treatment. Upon admission, medical staff performed debridement and detoxification, administered antivenom serum injections, anti-infection measures, and other symptomatic treatments for Congcong. After three days of hospitalization, the pain in the patient's foot eased. The doctor stated that snake venom mainly includes neurotoxins, hemotoxins, and cytotoxins. The venom of the bamboo viper belongs to hemotoxins. This type of toxin primarily affects the human body's blood coagulation function. The doctor reminded that we have now entered the active period for snakes. Citizens engaging in outdoor activities must be extra careful and should not actively attack or disturb snakes. If accidentally bitten by a snake, remain calm and try to remember the snake's shape and color to help identify the type of snakebite. Go to the hospital as soon as possible for early administration of antivenom serum. It is understood that currently there are 7 hospitals in our city equipped with antivenom serum. If citizens are accidentally bitten by a snake, they can contact the nearest hospital to confirm the stock of antivenom serum and go to the hospital quickly for injection. The 7 hospitals equipped with antivenom serum and the types of antivenom serum stocked are as follows: Zhangzhou Municipal Hospital: Anti-Bungarus multicinctus (Many-banded Krait) Serum, Anti-Agkistrodon halys (Pallas's Pit Viper) Serum, Anti-Deinagkistrodon acutus (Sharp-nosed Pit Viper) Serum Contact Tel: 0596-2082582 Zhangzhou Zhengxing Hospital: Anti-Deinagkistrodon acutus (Sharp-nosed Pit Viper) Serum, Anti-Agkistrodon halys (Pallas's Pit Viper) Serum, Anti-Bungarus multicinctus (Many-banded Krait) Serum, Anti-Naja (Cobra) Serum Contact Tel: 0596-2052120 Zhao'an County General Hospital: Anti-Agkistrodon halys (Pallas's Pit Viper) Serum, Anti-Deinagkistrodon acutus (Sharp-nosed Pit Viper) Serum, Anti-Bungarus multicinctus (Many-banded Krait) Serum Contact Tel: 0596-3320120 Zhangpu County Hospital: Anti-Bungarus multicinctus (Many-banded Krait) Serum, Anti-Deinagkistrodon acutus (Sharp-nosed Pit Viper) Serum, Anti-Agkistrodon halys (Pallas's Pit Viper) Serum Contact Tel: 0596-3202034 / 0596-3202032 Yunxiao County Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine: Anti-Bungarus multicinctus (Many-banded Krait) Serum, Anti-Agkistrodon halys (Pallas's Pit Viper) Serum, Anti-Deinagkistrodon acutus (Sharp-nosed Pit Viper) Serum Contact Tel: 13607575389 Yunxiao County Hospital: Anti-Agkistrodon halys (Pallas's Pit Viper) Serum Contact Tel: 0596-6011107 No. 909 Hospital of the Joint Logistics Support Force: Anti-Agkistrodon halys (Pallas's Pit Viper) Serum, Anti-Bungarus multicinctus (Many-banded Krait) Serum, Anti-Deinagkistrodon acutus (Sharp-nosed Pit Viper) Serum Contact Tel: 0596-2975511 What should you do after being bitten by a snake? Step 1: Identify a Venomous Snake Bite Venomous snake bites typically have the following characteristics: Two or more deep fang marks; Intense pain at the bite site; Rapid swelling at the bite site; Skin may turn red or purple; In addition to typical fang marks and bleeding, symptoms like nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, sweating, and allergic reactions may occur. Step 2: First Aid Steps Stay Calm: Panic only accelerates the spread of venom in the body. Note the time of the bite, seek help, or call emergency services. Remember the snake's characteristics, or take a photo, which can help doctors assess the venom type and provide treatment. Handle the Injured Area: If conditions and environment permit, use an available item to tie a firm bandage about 10 centimeters above the wound. Loosen it for one or two minutes every 20 minutes to avoid necrosis due to prolonged restricted blood circulation. If resources are limited, immobilize the affected limb and apply local pressure to the injured area. Keep the injured area below the level of the heart to slow the flow of venom. Clean the Wound: Immediately use available clean water, saline, soapy water, etc., to rinse the wound and remove adherent venom. If fangs remain in the wound, remove them promptly. Avoid using alcohol or other chemicals for rinsing. After performing simple first aid, it is essential to go to a professional snakebite treatment hospital as soon as possible for early injection of antivenom serum and administration of tetanus antitoxin, along with professional treatments including disinfection, debridement, negative pressure suction, anti-infection, and anti-allergy measures. Source: Minnan Daily Editor: Hong Tingting

Content Title: Don't follow the car in front closely when driving through a crosswalk; safe driving is no joke Release Date: 2024-12-13 16:10:03 Content Status: Review completed Content Type: Multimedia Industry: Digital Government Affairs_Government Media_Government Media Author Name: Haiyue Talks Cars Owner Name: Haiyue Talks Cars Content Account Type: Enterprise Content Details: Learn safe driving by watching accidents. The white car did not slow down before approaching the crosswalk. It only braked sharply at the crosswalk. The yellow car following closely, due to the lack of a safe distance, naturally caused a rear-end collision. In terms of liability, it is definitely the fault of the following car. Ahead is the crosswalk. The white car should have slowed down in advance. And by tapping the brakes, it could remind the following car to maintain a safe distance. This makes it easier to avoid accidents. As for the yellow car, while driving at a considerable speed, following so closely is almost like driving blind. It did not observe in advance that there was a crosswalk ahead. Driving like this will lead to an accident sooner or later. The correct way for the yellow car to drive is to maintain a safe distance. And by using the offset method, allow itself to observe the road ahead of the car in front. This way, it can make predictions in advance and take measures early. Seeing far ahead allows for early prediction and early action. Did you remember? Content Understanding Tags: Non-serious civil content

Title: Why Doctors Don't Recommend Women to Get Eyebrow Tattooing Content: Why Doctors Don't Recommend Women to Get Eyebrow Tattooing Why doctors don't recommend women to get eyebrow tattooing. As the saying goes, everyone has a love for beauty; loving beauty is a natural instinct for girls. Naturally having dark, thick eyebrows is something every girl desires. Many women choose to draw their eyebrows to look better, but having to remove makeup every day is troublesome. Now that the medical aesthetics industry has developed, many women choose to get eyebrow tattooing directly. Let's look at why doctors don't recommend women to get eyebrow tattooing. Why doctors don't recommend women to get eyebrow tattooing 1. First, excessive heavy metal content in dyes, harming and irritating the skin. Many people get eyebrow tattoos, but few know that most eyebrow tattoo dyes are actually metal-based dyes. Furthermore, CCTV has reported that over half of the dyes used in Korean semi-permanent eyebrow tattoos have seriously exceeded heavy metal limits, including some Grade 1 carcinogens. These harmful substances enter the deeper layers of the skin through tattooing, particularly damaging the activity of underlying cells, affecting cell quality, and thus harming our skin. In mild cases, it can cause allergies; in severe cases, it can lead to skin diseases. Second, eyebrow tattoos can change color or fade. Since it's semi-permanent tattooing, some might ask how long 'semi-permanent' actually is. Tattoo artists often promise that the eyebrows will last 3 to 5 years, but in reality, many people's eyebrows start to fade and lighten after about a year, some even fading within six months, which looks very awkward. Besides fading, there's also the risk of color change. It's not hard to find women whose tattooed eyebrows have turned pink or bluish-green. This is because the tattoo artist's dye settles in the deeper layers, causing pigment deposition and color change. Moreover, this color change cannot be washed off or covered up. Repairing or re-tattooing would be very troublesome and costly, affecting not only appearance but also a person's self-confidence. Third, the hygiene of the tattooing environment and tools is not guaranteed. Strictly speaking, eyebrow tattooing is a form of pigmentation procedure that requires a sterile, disinfected environment and tools. However, most tattoo studios do not meet these standards, and tools are often not sterilized, leading to a high risk of infection. Fourth, the eyebrow shape can become outdated. Fashion changes too quickly. Once you have tattooed eyebrows, the shape is fixed and cannot keep up with trends. After all, different makeup styles might require different eyebrow styles; a single, fixed shape is too rigid. Furthermore, the shape designed by the tattoo artist might not suit your face shape. How can one have nice eyebrows without tattooing? The dangers of eyebrow tattooing are obvious. Actually, learning to draw eyebrows properly is a safer and healthier method. But for most women, drawing eyebrows is also a challenge. In fact, many women struggle to draw eyebrows well because they haven't chosen the right eyebrow pencil. Momo used to be bad at drawing eyebrows too, but since using the four-pronged eyebrow pencil recommended by Li Jiaqi, it has become much easier for her. Why doctors don't recommend women to get eyebrow tattooing 2 1. May cause disfigurement. Improper eyebrow tattooing might trigger diseases like lupus erythematosus. During tattooing, tiny wounds on the eyebrows can lead to pyogenic bacterial infections, potentially causing folliculitis, cellulitis, boils, septicemia, or even hepatitis B infection. If local inflammation reaches the dermis, it can lead to scar formation, or damage hair follicles, causing irregular eyebrow growth, or even disfigurement. 2. May lead to dysfunction of eye movement. The area around the eyes is densely packed with nerves and crucial points. Stimulation from plucking or tattooing eyebrows can affect vision or cause dysfunction in the muscles controlling eye movement, resulting in temporary or permanent damage that is hard to repair. A tattoo artist must understand the distribution of nerves and blood vessels around the eyes, which requires extensive medical experience and knowledge, not something easily mastered in a private studio. 3. May cause local infection. Due to inadequate disinfection by the tattoo artist before the procedure, failure to follow aseptic techniques, or improper aftercare, local infections can occur at the eyebrow site. Local infections are usually caused by several types of bacteria and typically manifest as pus, skin necrosis, etc. The safety of beauty products is crucial as it directly relates to physical health. If considering semi-permanent makeup, one should try to choose professional beauty institutions and be vigilant about product quality and safety. Additional information - Precautions for eyebrow tattooing: 1. Eyebrow tattooing is a cosmetic procedure. If it fails, it is often difficult to repair. Therefore, patients must go to正规 (formal/regular) cosmetic hospitals for this procedure. This ensures that experienced tattoo artists can design natural-looking eyebrows suitable for the patient's age and face shape, avoiding issues like asymmetrical eyebrows or incorrect color after tattooing. 2. Patients undergoing eyebrow tattooing should choose the dye color based on their individual skin and hair color. For younger women, a slightly darker dye can be chosen; older women should opt for a slightly lighter shade. 3. Patients should be aware of preoperative contraindications. Patients with inflammation or rashes on the eyebrows should avoid this procedure. Those with drug allergies or keloid tendencies should also avoid it. Why doctors don't recommend women to get eyebrow tattooing 3 Common precautions for eyebrow tattooing are as follows: 1. Avoid getting the treated area wet: After tattooing, the patient must not wet the tattooed area for 7 days to prevent infection. 2. Protect the wound: After tattooing, the patient will go through a scabbing phase (1-3 days) and a scab-shedding phase (5-7 days). During this time, apply a specialized tattoo repair ointment or erythromycin eye ointment to the area daily to protect the wound and prevent infection. Also, do not pick or peel off the scabs prematurely to avoid secondary injury. 3. Sun protection: After tattooing, patients need to avoid sun exposure and refrain from wearing makeup. 4. Dietary adjustments: After tattooing, patients should avoid spicy, stimulating foods, avoid tobacco and alcohol, and avoid fish and seafood. This period of dietary restrictions and avoiding不良刺激 (adverse stimuli) should last at least about one month. 5. Use professional products for care: After the scabs have completely fallen off, patients can use mild, non-irritating facial cleansers. They should also use gentle, non-irritating skincare products to avoid irritating the local skin and causing allergic reactions. 6. Avoid secondary tattooing or touch-ups during the color settling period: After natural scab shedding, there is a color settling period of about one month. Avoid secondary tattooing or touch-ups during this time. 7. Other aspects: Patients need to ensure normal nutrition daily to maintain normal metabolism. Endocrine stability requires patients to maintain a good mood, an optimistic attitude, and avoid overwork, keeping the body in a good state for faster recovery. Although eyebrow tattooing is a minor minimally invasive cosmetic procedure, the aforementioned daily habits and physical constitution can also affect the recovery speed and final outcome. Hazards of eyebrow tattooing: 1. The designed eyebrow shape may be uncoordinated, unsuitable for the patient's face shape, or the two eyebrows may be asymmetrical. 2. Poor choice of tattoo pigment color, often using dark black eyeliner ink mistakenly used for eyebrows, resulting in overly dark, bluish-black eyebrows. 3. Unscientific depth of pigment insertion into the skin, lacking artistry in the placement. 4. Poor handling of the eyebrow heads, making them too rigid, often seen as dark, round, or square-shaped eyebrow heads. 5. Uneven tattooing density, lacking a soft feel. 6. Damage to one's own skin. The skin is the body's first line of immune defense. Once the skin is damaged, pathogens can naturally invade the body, causing inflammation in mild cases and infection in severe cases. 7. Eyebrow embroidery必然使用 (inevitably uses) some cosmetics. Most of these chemical products contain heavy metals. If they enter through skin wounds, they can cause heavy metal infection in the body, which is more harmful than bacterial infections. 8. Eyebrow embroidery damages the eyebrows. Eyebrows are a natural barrier to prevent sweat and dust from entering the eyes. Reducing eyebrows can have certain negative effects on the eyes. Disadvantages of eyebrow tattooing: 1. The微小创面 (tiny wounds) left by tattooing are susceptible to pyogenic bacterial infection, which can lead to folliculitis, cellulitis, boils, and even septicemia, or hepatitis B infection. 2. If local inflammation invades the dermis, it can lead to scar formation or damage hair follicles, causing irregular eyebrow growth. 3. It can affect the functional movement of eye muscles, potentially causing temporary or permanent damage. 4. Tattooing is a form of traumatic skin pigmentation, implanting dye into the skin, which damages the original skin tissue and allows viruses and bacteria to enter. The above is some related knowledge about the disadvantages of eyebrow tattooing surgery. Everyone can get a general understanding. Because any surgery has certain disadvantages, for the sake of personal safety and postoperative results, it is recommended that everyone try to choose正规大型的医院 (formal, large hospitals) and have the surgery performed by experienced doctors. Professional doctors will use their superb skills to carefully perform each step of the surgery, minimizing the potential for disadvantages and achieving ideal results.

Title: Anti-theft lock bought on Taobao broke within half a year; consumer's communication with customer service for over a month yielded no results. Content: Recently, Mr. Xu, a resident of Gaojing Town, Baoshan District, sought help from the "Help You" column. He purchased a fingerprint anti-theft lock on Taobao. However, after less than half a year of use, the fingerprint recognition function of the lock completely "failed." But after more than a month, there was still no result. Caption: The merchant completely ignored Mr. Xu. Source/Photo provided by the interviewee. Mr. Xu said that on July 19 last year (2021), he purchased a "Mi Home Anti-theft Lock K2 Basic Model" for 1042 yuan from the "Mi Home Xiaomi Genuine Discount Store" on Taobao. On January 30 this year, Mr. Xu discovered that the fingerprint lock installed on his anti-theft door could not be opened at all. The lock showed no prompts or error codes. He and his family could only open the door using the spare key. "If I have to use the spare key to open the door, then what was the point of buying this anti-theft lock?" Mr. Xu recalled that when the problem occurred, he tried to communicate with the merchant multiple times, but the other party consistently refused to solve the problem and even ignored him. "Starting from February 7, I reported the situation to Taobao customer service many times, but even with their intervention, the problem still couldn't be resolved." After being delayed for over a month, Mr. Xu and his family still have to use the spare key every time they open the door, which is quite inconvenient. A reporter contacted the Taobao customer service hotline. A customer service representative stated that after an online check, consumer Mr. Xu did indeed complain about this issue in February this year. After the reporter described the general problem, the customer service said they would respond to consumer Mr. Xu within 24 hours. However, as of the time of writing, Taobao has still not provided any form of response to the consumer. Xinmin Evening News reporter Xu Chi, correspondent Zhou Bin.

Title: Market Warms Up, Public Fund Private Placements See Floating Gains Up to Over 200% Content: Currently, the private placement business, known as 'buying shares at a discount,' is gradually heating up, with public funds participating in subscriptions totaling nearly 2.6 billion yuan. As the market warms up, almost all private placement projects finalized within the year have floating gains, with the highest floating gain ratio even exceeding 200%. Some public fund institutions believe that the overall valuation of A-shares is currently at the historical median level. If the market faces a correction, the investment value of private placements may become more prominent. Low Discount Rates for Private Placements This Year Wind data shows that 21 public fund companies have participated in listed companies' private placements this year, with a total subscription amount of 2.591 billion yuan; last year, 17 public fund companies participated, with a total scale of approximately 2.921 billion yuan. Among them, E Fund Management participated with the highest amount, having invested a cumulative 1.162 billion yuan this year, with 28 products participating in private placements of 4 companies. For example, in early July, VeriSilicon Holdings Co., Ltd. announced that the E Fund SSE STAR Market 50 ETF invested 222 million yuan to subscribe to the company's private placement; in June, the E Fund CSI 300 ETF and E Fund Enhanced Return invested 214 million yuan and 110 million yuan, respectively, to participate in the private placement of AVIC Shenyang Aircraft Company. Besides E Fund, Penghua Fund, Zhuque Fund, and China Asset Management also participated in private placements with amounts exceeding 100 million yuan this year, at 193 million yuan, 172 million yuan, and 160 million yuan, respectively. Several funds under China Asset Management focused on private placement business, such as China Pan Yi One-Year Regular Open, China Pan Li One-Year Regular Open, China Pan Run Two-Year Regular Open, and China Pan Rui One-Year Regular Open, all participated in private placements of 9 individual stocks. Additionally, China Merchants Fund and Bosera Fund each participated in private placements with amounts exceeding 100 million yuan. Dai Jingxia, a senior analyst at Morningstar (China) Fund Research Center, believes that the active participation of public fund institutions in private placements is the result of the combined effect of supply and demand. 'On the supply side, policies such as the 'Six Rules on Mergers and Acquisitions' encourage listed companies to conduct supporting financing through mergers and acquisitions, driving the growth in the number of private placements for supporting fundraising; meanwhile, under the trend of economic restructuring and industrial upgrading, some high-growth industries have strong capital demand, promoting private placement financing for related enterprises. On the demand side, private placement issuers typically issue shares at a discount, providing public fund institutions with opportunities to obtain excess returns.' Caitong Fund analyzed that the biggest changes in the private placement market in the first half of 2025 are mainly two points: first, discounts are fewer, and public funds overall have high enthusiasm for bidding. Since February, there have been no cases of additional subscriptions, and overall discounts are somewhat less than in previous years, which may be related to the decent performance of the lifting of restrictions market in the first half; second, market participants are more diverse, with increasing participation from local state-owned assets. A fund observer believes that currently, 'new quality productive forces' are becoming a keyword for private placement investment. 'Looking at the overall situation of competitive bidding private placement proposal projects, from 2023 to 2025, the number and proportion of projects in industries related to new quality productive forces have shown an upward trend. At the same time, large-amount private placement projects have high 'new' content, mainly due to accelerated technological iteration in fields like new energy and new materials, requiring listed companies to need funds to support R&D and capacity expansion,' the person said. Public Funds Participating in Private Placements Generally See Floating Gains As the market warms up, private placement projects participated in by public funds this year have generally seen floating gains. On February 24 this year, Leshan Electric Power Co., Ltd. announced that it completed a 200 million yuan private placement project, with subscribers including 8 institutional investors and 1 individual investor, with a lock-up period of 6 months. The announcement showed that in this private placement, Caitong Fund, Nuode Fund, and China Asset Management were allocated 104 million yuan. According to the announcement, the cost price of this private placement project was 5.01 yuan per share. As Leshan Electric Power's stock price rose significantly in April, the public funds participating in the private placement also obtained substantial paper gains. As of July 5, Leshan Electric Power's stock price closed at 15.32 yuan per share, with the floating gain ratio of the private placement subscription reaching 205.79%. Based on disclosed information, China Pan Run Two-Year Regular Open under China Asset Management subscribed to Leshan Electric Power's private placement project with a cost of 8 million yuan for 1.5968 million shares. By the end of the first quarter, the holding value rose to 10.19 million yuan, and this stock also became the fund's seventh largest holding. As the market rose in the second quarter, this value has now exceeded 24 million yuan, but these private placement shares cannot be lifted until August 20 this year. Barring unforeseen circumstances, by the end of the second quarter, this stock may become the largest holding of China Pan Run Two-Year Regular Open. Additionally, the private placement amount of Jinghua New Materials in May was taken up by products under Xingquan Global Fund, such as Xingquan CSI 300 Index Enhanced and Xingquan CSI 800 Six-Month Hold Index Enhanced, with a current floating gain ratio of about 91%. Currently, private placement projects such as Northern Copper Industry and Dizal Pharmaceutical-U also have floating gain ratios exceeding 50%. It is worth mentioning that against the backdrop of普遍取得正收益 from 'discounted share purchases,' due to the weak performance of Imeik Technology Development Co., Ltd., its private placement project implemented in May currently has a floating loss ratio of about 14.28%, becoming the only private placement project still in a floating loss this year. Some analysts pointed out that private placements usually offer a certain issuance discount, but investors need to bear the liquidity risk of not being able to sell during the lock-up period. If the market overall declines during this period or the individual stock encounters specific negative factors, causing the stock price to fall more than the initial discount gain, it will lead to 'breaking issue price,' resulting in paper losses. Public funds, constrained by lock-up period rules, find it difficult to stop losses immediately even when seeing losses expand, which significantly increases the risk of private placement investment when market volatility intensifies. 'Small Amount, Quick' Private Placements May See a Boom Many institutions believe that, based on historical reviews, participating in private placements is an investment method worthy of long-term attention, especially when market sentiment is low, and one can appropriately actively watch for private placement investment opportunities. Looking ahead to the future of the private placement market, Caitong Fund believes attention can be paid from four aspects: First, from a valuation perspective, indices like the CSI 1000, which are of more concern to private placement participants, are currently at historical median levels, and the valuation of the Growth Enterprise Market is also relatively low; second, the marginal impact of factors such as tariffs on the market is weakening, and the expectation of Fed interest rate cuts may help improve liquidity, which is positive for the market; third, when the market experiences a significant correction, it might be a timing worth focusing on for allocation; fourth, pay attention to investment opportunities in private placement projects for supporting fundraising in mergers and acquisitions. Caitong Fund also stated that the 'small amount, quick' private placement mechanism may become very popular in the future. This mechanism allows listed companies to raise funds not exceeding 300 million yuan and within 20% of net assets through a simplified process, providing a channel for rapid financing for related enterprises with its efficient model. With continuous policy optimization and increasing market participation, 'small amount, quick' private placements are expected to become an important tool for promoting industrial upgrading, injecting stronger momentum into the high-quality development of the real economy. Speaking of promising sub-sectors, EMI Fund believes that, based on product investment strategies and continuous market tracking and risk assessment, investors can select relevant targets from two aspects: First, leading companies in key sub-sectors with deep value挖掘 and forward-looking judgment of景气度相结合, where technological barriers are continuously strengthened; second, high-quality companies where improvements in operational quality resonate with valuation repair, and which also possess long-term investment value.

Title: Couple argues in car on highway, wife gets off and walks in anger, police promptly rescue and eliminate safety hazard. Content: Impulse is the devil. Driving under emotional excitement can easily cause traffic accidents, especially on highways. When driving, it's essential to maintain a calm mindset; once emotions are involved, it becomes very dangerous both for others and oneself. Recently, Kaifeng highway traffic police encountered a couple arguing in their car over trivial matters, with the wife getting off and walking in anger. Fortunately, patrol officers promptly rescued her, eliminating the safety hazard. On the morning of November 28, 2022, at 10:05 AM, Officer Li Yajun from the Kaifeng Highway Traffic Police Brigade Border Law Enforcement Service Station, along with auxiliary police officers Yang Zhigang and Cai Huihui, patrolled to the 448-kilometer mark of the Rilan Highway icon. They discovered a woman walking alone on the highway. The police quickly got out of their vehicle, intercepted her on the spot, and persuaded her to leave the highway, proceeding to a nearby service area for questioning. Upon inquiry, it was learned that the woman and her husband were driving a large truck and had a dispute over trivial matters during the journey. In a fit of anger, the woman got out and started walking along the highway, intending to walk back to her hometown alone. Seeing this, the police immediately calmed the woman's emotions and contacted her husband. After the husband arrived at the scene, the police provided emotional counseling and criticism to the quarreling couple. Both recognized their mistakes, reconciled, and continued their journey. Kaifeng Traffic Police remind all drivers: when traveling, do not drive motor vehicles under emotional influence. Highways are enclosed, high-speed traffic environments. Pedestrians on highways not only seriously disrupt normal traffic order but also极易引发机动车与行人相撞的事故,潜伏着极大的交通事故安全隐患. (Kaifeng Traffic Police)
