Title: Why is it difficult to recover money lost to fraud? How to reduce losses when encountering fraud? Content: It is difficult to recover money lost to fraud, mainly for the following reasons: Complex and concealed fraudulent methods: Fraudsters often use high-tech means and complex network structures to hide their true identities and fund flows, making tracking and investigation extremely difficult. Rapid fund transfers: Fraudsters quickly transfer, disperse, or withdraw funds, increasing the difficulty of recovery. Challenges of cross-border crime: If cross-border fraud is involved, differences in legal systems, law enforcement cooperation mechanisms, and judicial procedures between different countries and regions mean coordination and cooperation require time and resources. Inaccurate or missing information: Victims may be unable to provide accurate and complete information related to the fraud at the time of being deceived, which hinders investigation. When encountering fraud, the following measures can be taken to reduce losses: Report to the police immediately: File a report with the public security authorities, provide detailed information about the fraud incident and the losses incurred, and assist the authorities in their investigation. Contact the bank or payment platform promptly: Explain the situation and request to freeze the fraudulent account or funds to minimize losses as much as possible. Collect and preserve evidence: Such as chat records, transfer records, etc. This evidence is crucial for subsequent legal action and rights protection. Stay vigilant: Prevent secondary victimization by not easily trusting information or calls from strangers, and avoid clicking on unknown links or downloading unfamiliar software. In summary, when encountering fraud, stay calm, report it to the police promptly, and take effective measures to reduce losses. At the same time, strengthening personal information protection and raising awareness of prevention are also important ways to prevent fraud.

Title: Guangzhou Conducts Mass Sentencing for Various Drug-Related Cases with No One Receiving Probation
Content: Guangzhou, June 25 (Xinhua) - Cai Minjie, Yang Xiaomei - The Guangzhou Intermediate Court reported on the 25th that ahead of International Day Against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking (June 26), it organized a large-scale centralized sentencing activity for drug crime cases across all courts in the city. This sentencing involved 55 drug-related cases and 74 defendants, with no one receiving probation. The sentencing was participated in by the Guangzhou Intermediate Court and 11 basic-level courts under its jurisdiction. The Guangzhou Intermediate Court itself sentenced 13 cases involving 26 people, while the basic-level courts sentenced 42 cases involving 48 people, totaling 55 cases and 74 defendants. The Guangzhou Intermediate Court reported that in 2013, three post-90s defendants, Cai Zhenkun, Cai Shuncong, and Cai Huanyong, agreed with others to trade 200 grams of crystal meth for 32,000 RMB in Guangzhou. They were later arrested by police, and 4 packages of white crystals were seized. After appraisal, the 4 packages had a net weight of 2833 grams and were found to contain methamphetamine with a purity of 76.4%. The Guangzhou Intermediate Court sentenced Cai Shuncong to death for selling and transporting drugs,剥夺政治权利终身 (deprivation of political rights for life), and confiscation of all personal property; sentenced Cai Zhenkun to life imprisonment,剥夺政治权利终身, and confiscation of all personal property; sentenced Cai Huanyong to 15 years imprisonment and confiscation of personal property worth 5,000 RMB. Between 2012 and 2013, defendant Li Jingui used raw materials including caffeine and methamphetamine to manufacture drugs. Police later seized one bottle of gray-black liquid containing caffeine, net weight 1046.08 grams; one bottle of brown liquid containing ketamine, net weight 2208 grams; three packages of brown powder containing ketamine, net weight 4241 grams, among other drugs. The Guangzhou Intermediate Court held that according to relevant regulations, defendant Li Jingui was guilty of manufacturing drugs and was sentenced to life imprisonment,剥夺政治权利终身, and confiscation of all personal property. On the same day, the cases announced by the Guangzhou Intermediate Court also included the drug trafficking case of defendant Gu Wen et al., the drug smuggling and transportation case of Huang Jiamin, and other drug-related cases. All the aforementioned defendants received sentences. The Guangzhou Intermediate Court stated that among the cases in the centralized sentencing, drug trafficking crimes were the most numerous, involving 54 people. The total amount of drugs involved in the sentenced cases was approximately 35 kilograms. The main types of drugs were methamphetamine ('ice'), heroin, and ketamine, with a few cases involving other types such as cocaine and marijuana. It is reported that the 74 defendants received sentences ranging from 6 months imprisonment to immediate execution of the death penalty. Specifically, 35 were sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of less than 5 years, 21 were sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of 5 years or more, 7 were sentenced to life imprisonment, 10 were sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve, and 1 was sentenced to immediate execution of the death penalty. No one received probation. (End)

Title: Does a renovation company have its own workers, or are all projects done by hiring renovation teams from the market? Content: Renovation companies generally do not deal directly with workers. For example, when we operated as a 'renovation guerrilla team,' we would directly find workers or ask for introductions. Later, as work increased, we often had meals and chats with the workers. We would tell the workers: 'If there's work, we'll prioritize you. We'll definitely make sure you get enough projects in a year, and we won't delay payment; you'll get paid right after finishing the job...' At this point, you could consider them as 'our workers,' but the accurate term is: cooperative workers. We know each other well – we know the worker's skills are good, and the worker knows we are reliable and pay promptly. However, we haven't signed labor contracts with them, they don't need to clock in, they don't get a base salary, we don't provide them with tools, and we don't have the right to demand they only work on our sites. They can also work for other homeowners or companies. Moreover, in the renovation industry, can you guarantee a worker has work every day? If you can guarantee daily work, then yes, but in reality, you can only ensure a continuous stream of work during certain periods. Later, as our company grew, we found it too troublesome to deal with each worker individually, so we started hiring foremen directly. What does a foreman do? Simply put, they are like the 'renovation guerrilla teams' we started as. Why do foremen have workers? Because they have been on sites for a long time and have accumulated connections with various workers. Are the foreman's workers considered his own? Of course not. It's just that the workers can take on 'projects.' The foreman usually has a steady stream of work, so he has a continuous pool of various skilled workers. Why 'continuous'? Because the foreman can't force a worker to only work for him. The same worker might be connected to several foremen and companies, taking jobs from whoever has work, whoever pays more, whoever they get along with, or whoever pays promptly... This is why there are so many renovation companies, but the number of skilled workers doesn't seem to increase or decrease significantly. The workers have one goal: to earn money. 'I work, I get paid. I don't want to hear empty talk; if I wanted that, I wouldn't be a worker.' Our renovation company has grown to a certain size and only manages foremen. We still know the experienced workers we started with, but we no longer deal with them directly. We convey the renovation standards to the foreman, who then instructs the workers to follow them. The company has supervisors who conduct regular inspections. Later, even the 'Chairman' personally went to sites to inspect, which is why you see many videos on Douyin of bosses going to sites to point out problems. So how do we control profits? This involves the 'full-renovation' model, which I won't detail here. Simply put, it's a price per square meter that includes certain items. The foreman can only do work within the 'standard' scope, and we pay the foreman based on that standard. Anything beyond the 'standard' requires a client add-on. The client pays the company, the company takes a cut, and then the foreman does the work. Therefore, a small number of clients pay the foreman directly for add-ons privately, bypassing the company. The company isn't foolish; they send inspectors. The client thinks it's for quality control, which it is, but more importantly, it's to check if any unauthorized extra work was done. However, much of it goes 'undetected.' As the saying goes, 'water that is too clear has no fish.' It's all human-driven. Furthermore, 'where there's a policy, there's a countermeasure,' especially in renovation, where human factors are decisive. The site inspectors aren't necessarily experts; they often only know the basics. If they were real experts, wouldn't they be doing the renovation themselves? There's a large full-renovation company here that only targeted the mid-to-high-end market. Later, their performance declined because the overall market consumption wasn't high. So, they adjusted their products, creating a renovation package for mid-to-low-end clients, and their performance doubled. Many clients who started projects had no workers for a long time, forcing the company to publicly recruit foremen and workers. Later, relevant leaders personally went to Henan to recruit workers. After a large number of workers came in, the quality of work inevitably became uneven, and some clients complained. The company then started recruiting 'reserve management personnel' and 'general management personnel.' The Chairman personally went to sites to pick problems and 'scold people,' filming videos for dissemination. This served two purposes: to show the boss's seriousness and to make management pay attention. Is the foreman necessarily part of the company? Accurately, it's still called cooperation, and usually, no labor contract is signed. Title: Can Teacher Rotation Solve the "Hot" School District Housing Problem? Latest Response from Education Department Content: On August 25th, Beijing officially released the implementation rules for the exchange and rotation of outstanding principals and teachers under the "Double Reduction" policy. What other questions remain unanswered regarding this pilot implementation in Beijing? "News 1+1" invited Li Yi, Deputy Secretary of the Beijing Municipal Education Working Committee and spokesperson for the Municipal Education Commission, to clarify——Authoritative Response Q: Are teachers willing to participate in the rotation in Beijing? Li Yi, Deputy Secretary of the Beijing Municipal Education Working Committee and spokesperson for the Municipal Education Commission: Actually, during the rotation process, we fully consider the teachers' feelings, their professional growth, the school's service quality, and the relationship with students' actual gains. So why did we propose rotation within districts this time? Especially carrying out cadre and teacher rotation within already mature school groups and school districts is about balancing their development needs regarding teachers' living space and job mobility. Of course, a key point is that our performance assessment and honor recognition for teachers are also important guidance and leverage. Q: Are parents willing to accept teacher rotation in Beijing? Li Yi: We particularly understand that parents might have such speculations and feelings. Although parents don't directly face this teacher exchange, actually, four or five years ago, following the overall deployment from the central government and the Ministry of Education, Beijing's school district management and group-based schooling had basically achieved full coverage. That is, every individual school is within a school district or education group. So parents can feel that while they send their child to one school, the educational resources the child actually receives, including courses and teacher services, might be supplied by a district or group. This is what we specifically discuss today: in the process of changing from supply by a single school to supply by a district or group, educational balance and flow naturally occur. Then our children's actual gains change from receiving resources from one single school to receiving more resources, which should be better. Q: How will high-quality resource teachers from Beijing's top schools flow? Li Yi: This is a crucial question, actually not just an operational issue but also a perceptual one. We do not artificially divide schools into high-quality and non-high-quality, but in the public's mind, there are indeed differences between schools. Over the past period, during the reform of school districtization and group-based schooling, school principals have already reached a consensus in thinking: no school's resources and teachers are exclusively possessed by one school; they all serve to provide educational resources for a broader student population and education. So in the transformation from individual schools to districts and groups, the thinking and stance of these teachers and principals have shifted from focusing on being所谓的 high-quality or top-notch within a single school to entering a broader space. Now we can carry out such rotation precisely based on this reformed understanding, allowing smooth progress. Q: Can large-scale promotion of teacher rotation solve the "hot" school district housing problem? Li Yi: Actually, education has a significant impact, connected to millions of households. But in promoting this work, we particularly note that the central and Beijing's "Double Reduction" documents do not directly mention cadre and teacher mobility. However, we observe that reforms like homework reform and after-school service reform are all driven by people, necessitating the promotion of personnel mobility and the overall improvement of quality services. In this promotion process, parents' understanding of the reform in the educational supply-side structure will definitely affect their school choices and recognition of school district housing, etc. I believe it certainly has a mitigating effect. But promoting teacher rotation focuses more on building a high-quality education system and better serving children, which will naturally bring corresponding changes to the surrounding environment and resources. Q: Can cross-district rotation for Beijing teachers be achieved in the future? Li Yi: This has always been a difficult problem for us. Indeed, in Beijing's exploration and practice, we once rotated teachers from Haidian and Dongcheng to distant suburban counties like Yanqing or Miyun, for one year or three years, but the actual results were not very successful. On one hand, it affected the teachers' overall quality of life and work; on the other hand, the match between students and teachers might not achieve ideal results. So currently, for cross-regional long-distance cadre and teacher mobility, we mainly use the online "Dual-Teacher Classroom" format. Relying on local teachers, while transferring the service attributes of urban high-quality educational resources through informatization means, guiding local teachers to continuously improve school running levels, thereby enhancing the entire education service level. We feel this might be an effective method in building a high-quality education system in the new era. Viewpoint Link: Students might not feel much change in the new semester, but the impact on rotating teachers is significant. Li Yi: Experienced parents and students will notice some teacher adjustments after the semester starts, as this includes teachers from graduating grades being reassigned to starting grades after seeing their students off. In this process, children might notice that some teachers are not from their original school. Actually, the impact on teachers participating in rotation is relatively greater, after all, teachers have to cross campuses or schools to another school, accepting certain challenges. Includes both backbone/special-grade teachers and teachers suitable for after-school services, etc. Li Yi: Through years of exploration and piloting, in the process of teacher and cadre mobility, we don't just rotate based on teacher rank or honors, but according to the needs of the rotation position. For example, under the "Double Reduction" policy background, we focus more on how to leverage effectiveness at the subject group and grade group levels. So in the selection process for personnel rotation, there are both backbone teachers and special-grade teachers, as well as teachers suitable for different positions like after-school services, homework research, and exam evaluation research. Therefore, the proportion of transfers is decided based on the post and the need. Source: Comprehensive CCTV News Client, Modern Education News, Jiangsu Education Channel, etc. Scan the QR code to follow the Parent Circle video account for more Yangzhou campus videos, hot news, etc.

Although 360 loan has a good background and complies with regulations in all aspects, users still need to understand clearly before applying for a loan with 360 loan to avoid applying for a loan with unreasonable fees. If there are any unreasonable charges, users can directly report to the CBRC to protect their legitimate rights and interests. The three loan products under 360 Finance have different focuses. 360 IOU mainly provides users with credit loans, similar to Baidu Qianhua, Alipay's Ant Credit Pay (借呗), etc. Users can apply for a credit loan of up to 300,000 RMB based on their credit situation with 360 IOU. The loan interest rate is charged daily, generally around 0.05%. 360 Micro Loan is a loan product provided by 360 Finance for small and micro enterprises, generally mainly providing loans to corporate legal persons. E-commerce sellers can also apply for 360 Micro Loan, with a maximum loan amount of 200,000 RMB. Users can apply without providing mortgage guarantees when taking the loan. 360 Installments is a consumer installment product launched by 360 Finance. Users can directly shop in installments on the 360 Installments app, or enter the 360 Mall within the 360 IOU app for installment shopping. That's all for the introduction to loans under 360.

Title: What to do if problems are found with the house after the completion of a second-hand house transaction? Content: What to do if problems are found with the house after the completion of a second-hand house transaction? 1. Solutions if problems are found with the house after the completion of a second-hand house transaction are as follows: (1) Determine the specific situation of the house quality, you can first go to a housing quality appraisal institution for an appraisal; (2) Determine whether the problem falls within the warranty scope. If it does, you can claim the warranty within the warranty period; conversely, if the problem is not covered by the warranty, or is due to human damage, the second-hand owner has corresponding legal responsibilities and can be required to undertake the repair obligations; (3) If the second-hand house has major quality problems in its structure, affecting the buyer's normal living and use, the buyer can terminate the sales contract with the owner, and request the owner to return the purchase price and compensate for corresponding bank interest losses. 2. Legal basis: Article 610 of the 'Civil Code of the People's Republic of China': If the subject matter does not meet the quality requirements, making it impossible to achieve the purpose of the contract, the buyer may refuse to accept the subject matter or terminate the contract. If the buyer refuses to accept the subject matter or terminates the contract, the risk of damage or loss of the subject matter shall be borne by the seller. Article 611: If the risk of damage or loss of the subject matter is borne by the buyer, it shall not affect the buyer's right to demand that the seller bear liability for breach of contract due to the seller's failure to perform its obligations as agreed.

Title: Confucius Institute at the University of Seychelles Holds Teaching Work Exchange Meeting Content: On February 16th, all teachers of the Confucius Institute at the University of Seychelles conducted a teaching exchange activity with the theme of 'Sharing, Exchanging, Improving'. The activity aimed to share teaching experiences for the next step of the institute's teaching work and to improve the teaching quality of the institute's different Chinese language classes in Seychelles. Teachers analyzed, explored, and reflected on teaching based on their current teaching work, organized and participated cultural activities, student learning status, and teaching cases, aiming to summarize teaching experience, identify existing teaching problems, and improve teaching quality through mutual exchange and learning. Teachers expressed their opinions freely and conducted relatively comprehensive exchanges and sharing. Teaching Exchange 1 Volunteer Teacher Yuan Meng Volunteer Yuan Meng spoke from four aspects: personal growth, teaching reflection, future planning, and personal suggestions. She believed that she had gained a lot from teaching at the Confucius Institute this year, and her teaching level had greatly improved. With the help of the Confucius Institute teachers, she quickly integrated into Seychelles and the Confucius Institute at the University of Seychelles. In actual teaching, she also discovered the difference between theory and practice. For example, classroom management at the Tourism School was a major challenge. Through her own exploration, she found that visually marking students' classroom behavior and providing timely feedback for students to adjust their behavior was a good method. At the same time, she emphasized the importance of persistently writing teaching reflection notes and having a comprehensive grasp of teaching materials. She suggested increasing fun in primary and secondary school teaching, incorporating suitable classroom games, and printing and distributing teaching materials to students to facilitate review and mastery. In her work at the Confucius Institute, she also gained a lot from participating in the short video production competition, learning video editing, PS image editing, and public account editing, gradually progressing from unfamiliarity to proficiency, and significantly improving her comprehensive abilities. In terms of cultural activities, everyone worked together to host many large-scale events, enhancing team spirit and gaining experience through work. 2 Volunteer Teacher Zhang Chenhui Volunteer Teacher Zhang Chenhui shared teaching experiences from the different teaching classes she had taught, analyzed teaching problems, and proposed solutions. On one hand, as a volunteer, the process from first stepping onto the podium to growth is a gradual adaptation process and also a process of mutual learning between teaching and learning. Familiarity with the teaching model and delivering a complete Chinese language lesson require comprehensive qualities. On the other hand, it involves helping students solve problems through communication and磨合. For example, in tutoring students for HSK5, she tried her best to help students solve practical learning problems and provide the materials they needed, identified students' strengths and weaknesses in exam preparation and some common language errors, and provided targeted help and tutoring. It was gratifying that all students who received tutoring passed the exam. Third, she shared her experiences teaching in different primary and secondary school interest classes and overseas Chinese children's classes. Through teaching these primary and secondary school classes, her teaching level and ability began to improve. She implemented different classroom activities to enhance students' learning enthusiasm, used different teaching methods for students of different ages, simplified the teaching model for younger students, adjusted teaching content promptly based on student feedback in class, and focused on sparking students' interest in learning Chinese. There are still shortcomings in the selection and design of teaching content for primary and secondary school Chinese interest classes. Fourth, regarding her experience teaching social classes, her teaching level grew the fastest in social class Chinese teaching, and the teaching results were relatively good. On one hand, her familiarity with the teaching materials improved, and she could sense during class whether students had truly learned the content. On the other hand, she established good interactive relationships with students. 3 Dispatched Teacher Luo Na Dispatched Teacher Luo Na shared her work regarding the teaching of newly added primary and secondary school interest classes and the promotional work of the Confucius Institute. In the big family of the Confucius Institute, sharing teaching experiences with peers and improving together is a very happy thing. She herself has continuously deepened her understanding and familiarity with international Chinese language teaching through teaching various classes and repeated lessons. She believes that a reward mechanism should exist in primary and secondary school teaching, but it is not the only method to maintain students' interest in interest classes. Students need to understand the meaning and purpose of the reward mechanism. The teacher's teaching method is very important, and it is necessary to continuously study and try teaching methods suitable for students. In the promotional work of the Confucius Institute, to enhance the institute's influence and meet the needs of activity promotion, everyone consciously strengthening the accumulation of various abilities will benefit the overall work of the institute. Through continuous efforts, her video and image editing skills have improved significantly, and she has become more proficient in doing the design and editing required for the Confucius Institute's promotional work. 4 Dispatched Teacher Yang Junguang Dispatched Teacher Yang Junguang shared from both teaching and activity aspects. In terms of teaching, Teacher Yang shared his experiences before, during, and after teaching. Before teaching, teachers should familiarize themselves with the teaching materials, prepare the teaching calendar, and prepare the lesson课件. The课件 should be concise and to the point, while balancing knowledge and fun. It is best to have a contingency plan for emergencies before teaching. During teaching, teaching design should be done in advance, teaching links should be designed, homework should be assigned and tracked for检查. After teaching, teaching reflection should be conducted, and teaching archives should be sorted and filed. What runs through the entire teaching process is actually 'details' – 'the spirit is revealed in the subtleties'. In terms of cultural activities, Teacher Yang proposed to plan ahead, design in advance, assign tasks to students early, and not to cram at the last minute. It is necessary to discover students' strengths and have incentive measures, maintain communication, and provide help随时. Colleagues should pool their wisdom and work together. After activities, activity reflection should be conducted to identify and fill gaps, striving for excellence. Finally, Teacher Yang shared four sentences with everyone for mutual encouragement: Nothing is difficult if you put your heart into it; The world fears nothing but seriousness; Forever young, forever on the road, forever moved to tears; Love and tolerance. 5 Chinese Director Wang Dongxia After listening to everyone's speeches, Director Wang Dongxia summarized: Teaching离不开 four aspects: teachers, teaching materials, teaching environment, and students. For Confucius Institute teachers, it is first necessary to have the basic teaching literacy, quality, and ability of an international Chinese language teacher. Teachers should also have a loving heart for students, have a basic understanding of the students they teach, and achieve 'teaching without discrimination, teaching according to aptitude'. Teachers should continuously learn and improve during the teaching process. The selection of teaching materials should also be adjusted according to the characteristics of the students and the specific situation of the class, choosing content suitable for student learning. During the class, teachers should choose appropriate teaching methods, formulate and implement teaching content according to the教学大纲, and also modify and adjust according to the actual teaching environment. The ability to organize teaching should be reflected upon, accumulated, and improved through continuous teaching. The current Chinese teaching at the Confucius Institute at the University of Seychelles has achieved significant results, but there are still many problems. As teaching materials, teachers, and students are constantly changing, how to achieve a better upward trend in the institute's continuous development and teaching quality requires us to continuously strive for progress, do a good job in team mentorship, master new teaching skills, and keep up with the times. We believe that with the unremitting efforts of the people at the Confucius Institute at the University of Seychelles, the teaching quality and recognition of our Confucius Institute, as well as Seychellois students' interest in learning Chinese, will continue to increase. This teaching activity sharing served as a one-year summary of Confucius Institute teaching experience for volunteers about to end their term, while also accumulating strength for the institute's teaching development in the new year, marking a new beginning for the Confucius Institute at the University of Seychelles. Through unremitting efforts, all teachers of the Confucius Institute at the University of Seychelles have enhanced the institute's visibility and recognition in Seychelles, and the number of people learning Chinese continues to increase. Facing new challenges, we must more carefully assess the situation, overcome difficulties, unite as one, and continuously contribute our strength to the development of the Confucius Institute. Research with certainty, action with fervor; learning is endless, teaching is endless, research is endless. This teaching work experience exchange meeting provided teachers with a platform for mutual learning, achieving the purpose of exchanging and sharing, and mutually promoting progress. We believe that in future teaching and research activities, teachers will have more碰撞 of ideas and ignite more sparks of wisdom! Title: How is cyberspace security? Is it easy to find a job? Content: When choosing an industry, you should look at the talent demand in that industry, but this is not the most important factor. The most important thing for finding a job easily in the industry you choose is to look at the supply-demand ratio. Everyone knows the market rules: when supply exceeds demand and when demand exceeds supply, the price of goods is different. In terms of the talent demand in the IT industry, the demand for programmer positions is undoubtedly the highest, but have you considered how oversaturated the programmer field is? A talent demand of 30 million corresponds to 60 million job seekers, so the employment situation is可想而知 not good. Although the talent demand for cybersecurity may not match that for development, the cybersecurity talent gap is large, and there is a supply shortage. Cybersecurity might only have a talent gap of 3 million, but it corresponds to only 300,000 job seekers. The employment situation is一目了然 very clear! (The above data are unofficial.) Furthermore, the current relationship of demand exceeding supply is continuously intensifying. In the future, our country will certainly move towards 'digitalization.' To achieve digitalization, we must rely on networks, and wherever there are networks, there must be cybersecurity engineers to safeguard them. Moreover, a 'digitalized' society will have more data, and this data also needs protection! Specifically, where are cybersecurity engineers needed for protection? From the daily lives of ordinary people (clothing, food, housing, transportation) to modern warfare, cybersecurity will be involved. Online shopping, scanning codes to order meals, scanning codes for travel, and mobile navigation are things almost every one of us does daily, and the data behind these actions are actually very sensitive! For example, if you use navigation to drive to work in the morning and use it again to go home after work, this data, when aggregated, can reveal when and where people are more concentrated. If this data is obtained by other countries, they could launch precise strikes during wartime... the consequences are unthinkable. As for modern warfare, it's even more terrifying. Let's imagine: a ship or submarine, believing itself safe and hidden, sends its real-time location to the enemy leader; a missile that should have been launched at the enemy at a critical moment inexplicably malfunctions; a group of robot dogs, just released, suddenly turn around and attack their own side... Seemingly virtual and intangible cyber attacks could really determine the outcome of a real war. Before a real war begins, cyber warfare largely involves preparation work: finding vulnerabilities, implanting malware, creating backdoors. We can certainly discover and remove some, but we cannot guarantee cleaning them all up. Once a real war breaks out, no one can say for sure which weapons have already been infiltrated by the enemy. However, it is comforting that the enemy also doesn't know if we have invaded their systems. The above mainly describes current or potential future cyber warfare. In the more distant future, especially when humanity enters an era of ubiquitous robots and intelligence, cyber warfare will be endowed with even more specific meanings. Therefore, the cybersecurity issue cannot be ignored now or in the future! The demand for talent will also continue to grow! Choosing to learn cybersecurity technology now and entering the cybersecurity industry is definitely the best choice! But the prerequisite must be that you are interested in cybersecurity and have sufficiently strong motivation!

Title: 【Public Interest Litigation】Learning Exchange, Promoting Development Together—Dong'an District Court Public Interest Litigation Department Visits Ning'an City People's Procuratorate for Exchange and Learning on Public Interest Litigation Procuratorial Work Content: To further enhance the professional level of our court's public interest litigation procuratorial work, learn advanced experience, and complement each other's strengths, on the morning of August 17, a delegation of three people from our court's Public Interest Litigation Department, led by Director Zhang Weiguang, went to Ning'an City People's Procuratorate to exchange and learn about the experience and practices of procuratorial organs in public interest litigation work. Upon arrival, a special symposium on public interest litigation work exchange was first held in the conference room of Ning'an City People's Procuratorate. At the meeting, Director Xie Xuewen, head of the Public Interest Litigation Department of Ning'an City People's Procuratorate, provided a detailed introduction on how to expand case sources, communicate with administrative agencies, collect evidence, and enhance the effectiveness of case supervision in their work. He particularly emphasized the "Grid Leader + Public Interest Litigation" working mechanism of the procuratorate and gave an in-depth and detailed explanation of the significance, purpose, role, and the intended social and legal effects of this work. The officers from both procuratorates engaged in thorough and extensive discussions on difficult and common issues encountered in their work. After the meeting, the delegation conducted a field inspection of the ancient villages and sites involved in the special tourism public interest litigation case currently being handled by Ning'an City People's Procuratorate. During the inspection, Director Xie Xuewen provided a detailed explanation on the discovery of case clues, the circumstances of public interest damage involved in the case, and the specific case handling process. This exchange and learning activity strengthened the friendship between the Dong'an and Ning'an procuratorates and enhanced communication and connection between them. The exchange served as an opportunity to broaden horizons and a means to learn from each other and progress together. Our court will take this exchange as an opportunity to further deepen mutual learning, achieve resource sharing, platform sharing, and outcome sharing, laying a solid foundation for realizing the "catching up and surpassing" goal of Dong'an's public interest litigation procuratorial work.

Title: Typical Food Safety Cases in Xishan District Content: Case 1 Details: On December 16, 2015, law enforcement officers from the Xishan District Market Supervision Bureau conducted an inspection of a certain supermarket in our district. On-site, they found that one bag of "Thai Fragrant Rice" sold by the party involved had insect infestation, suspected of violating Article 34 of the "Food Safety Law of the People's Republic of China": "The following foods are prohibited from production and operation: ... (6) Foods that are spoiled, rancid, moldy, infested with insects, unclean, mixed with foreign objects, adulterated, or have abnormal sensory properties..." After a thorough investigation, the bureau's law enforcement officers, in accordance with Article 124, Paragraph 1, Item (4) of the "Food Safety Law of the People's Republic of China", imposed an administrative penalty on the party involved: confiscation of one bag of insect-infested "Thai Fragrant Rice"; a fine of 57,500 yuan, to be turned over to the state treasury. Case 2 Details: On December 23, 2015, following an on-site consumer report alleging that a supermarket located on Dongting Street was selling expired "Master Kong Soup Vermicelli" food, law enforcement officers from the Xishan District Market Supervision Bureau immediately conducted an on-site inspection of the party's business premises. On-site, they found: in the clearance area on the 3rd floor of the supermarket, in a slanted cage, there was one box of food labeled as "Master Kong Soup Vermicelli". The food's outer packaging indicated a production date of April 24, 2015, and a shelf life of 6 months. The outer packaging also had a label from the supermarket attached, marked with "Clearance date December 21, 2015, original price: 4 yuan, clearance price: 1 yuan" and other wording. The party involved was suspected of selling expired food, violating Article 34 of the "Food Safety Law of the People's Republic of China": "The following foods, food additives, and food-related products are prohibited from production and operation: ... (10) Foods and food additives labeled with false production dates, shelf life, or that exceed the shelf life." After a thorough investigation, the bureau's law enforcement officers, in accordance with Article 124, Paragraph 1, Item (5) of the "Food Safety Law of the People's Republic of China", imposed an administrative penalty on the party involved: confiscation of one box of expired "Master Kong Soup Vermicelli" food; a fine of 50,500 yuan, to be turned over to the state treasury. Analysis: Food production and operation enterprises are the responsible entities for food safety. Providing the market with safe, abundant, reliable, and high-quality food to safeguard people's health is an unshirkable responsibility of food production and operation enterprises. Article 4 of the new "Food Safety Law" states: "Food producers and operators are responsible for the safety of the food they produce and operate." This is a general requirement for food producers and operators. How food production and operation enterprises can fulfill this responsibility effectively hinges on implementing the primary responsibility of the enterprise's main responsible person. In ensuring food safety within food production and operation enterprises, the main responsible person holds a central position and plays a decisive role. Only when they take the lead in earnestly implementing the enterprise's food safety management system and engage in production and operation activities in accordance with laws, regulations, and food safety standards can the enterprise's food safety be guaranteed. (Provided by the Xishan District Market Supervision Bureau)

Title: What to do if there is no local connection and only a 1394 connection? Content: The network card driver is not installed properly. Go to Device Manager and check if the network card is disabled. Open Device Manager by right-clicking on My Computer, selecting Manage, then finding Device Manager, and then look at Network Adapters. Check if the network card has a red '×' or an exclamation mark. If it does, enable it. If not, check if there are any other devices with exclamation marks. 1. In the console == system, check if the network card hardware shows a yellow question mark? If so, it means the driver was not installed successfully. 2. If the network card installation appears normal in the console == system, use ping 127.0.0.1 to check for network card hardware failure. If there is a reply with ts=255 or 64, it means it's OK. 3. If it's an integrated network card, check in the BIOS if it is disabled. Try reinstalling the network card driver. Your network card driver might not be installed correctly. Uninstall the local network adapter and then reinstall the driver to see if that works. Right-click on My Computer on the desktop! Then left-click on Manage -> Device Manager. A window with your computer's devices will pop up. Right-click anywhere and select 'Scan for hardware changes'. This will make your network card hardware appear. If you still don't understand, send me a message. The website driver is not installed properly.

Title: Terrifying! Thousands of Listed Companies 'Looted'; Xiaomi Suddenly 'Halts' CDR Listing Content: Wanlian Introduction On June 19, Xiaomi Corporation officially announced that after repeated and careful study, the company decided to implement its listing plans in Hong Kong and mainland China in steps. That is, it will list in Hong Kong first, and then choose an appropriate time to list domestically by issuing CDRs. 1 On June 19, Xiaomi Corporation officially announced that after repeated and careful study, the company decided to implement its listing plans in Hong Kong and mainland China in steps. That is, it will list in Hong Kong first, and then choose an appropriate time to list domestically by issuing CDRs. To this end, the company will apply to the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) to postpone the meeting of the issuance review committee to review the company's CDR issuance application. Subsequently, the CSRC website issued an announcement stating that it respects Xiaomi Group's choice. 2 Upon closer examination, why did Xiaomi, which was about to list domestically, proactively apply for a postponement? Intermediaries close to Xiaomi's IPO revealed that after multiple rounds of communication, the CSRC and Xiaomi reached a consensus. As an innovative measure, CDRs inherently face challenges in refining policy details and the market's digestion and understanding of the CDR innovation. Considering the recent overall market conditions, the review is temporarily suspended to ensure a higher-quality pilot CDR issuance, with plans to restart at an opportune time later. The recent market environment can be described as 'falling incessantly.' Today, the secondary market witnessed another phenomenon of 'thousands of stocks hitting the daily down limit,' with thousands of listed companies being 'looted' again. Xiaomi, which has always sought a higher market valuation, is clearly also concerned whether such a capital market is the best time for its 'return,' and pressed the 'brake' button just before the review. As the first company to submit a CDR application, Xiaomi's move indicates, to some extent, that the capital market is calling for a more calm and rational value judgment regarding future 'unicorns.' 3 Compared to Xiaomi's postponed listing, the impending spin-off of Xiaomi's financial business has attracted even more market attention. Spinning off financial businesses seems to have become a trend in the internet industry. Whether it's Ant Financial and JD Finance, which were spun off early on, or Baidu Finance, which announced its spin-off in April this year, or the soon-to-be-independent Xiaomi Finance, internet giants all want a piece of the pie in the fintech industry, which has not yet been fully divided. Spinning off the financial business from the main entity for listing, or separating it directly after it becomes large and strong, seems to have become a common strategy for many companies. Is Lei Jun's current spin-off of the financial business from the main entity following the trend of the times or does he have his own plans? According to a study by the School of Economics at Peking University, the growth rate of supply chain finance is 10%-30% in developed countries and 20%-25% in emerging economies like China and India. The '2017 Internet+ Supply Chain Finance Analysis Report' published by Wangku Research Institute predicts that by 2020, China's supply chain finance market size will reach 18 trillion RMB, making the industry a blue ocean. And what lies before Xiaomi is precisely this vast blue ocean. How could Lei Jun not be tempted? 4 As early as June 2015, from casting a wide net until now, Xiaomi Finance's business has covered multiple internet finance areas including payments, lending, credit reporting, and wealth management. Its products include key products on the Xiaomi ecosystem chain like the wallet and wristband. Furthermore, Xiaomi's foundational advantages in C-end users, B-end supply chains, as well as channels and technology, have laid a solid foundation for its future independent development. On the other hand, the ecosystem of upstream and downstream industries built by Xiaomi provides natural customers for Xiaomi's supply chain finance. As a top-three mobile phone vendor in China by shipment volume and a top-five vendor globally, Xiaomi has gathered numerous suppliers and customers upstream and downstream. This is a very large market with capital demands. Additionally, Xiaomi has established an ecosystem comprising over 210 companies. With its extensive layout across the ecosystem chain, Xiaomi has also built the world's largest IOT consumer platform. Finally, looking ahead, Lei Jun stated that he aims to open 1000 Mi Homes within three years. The small, medium, and micro enterprises in Xiaomi's upstream and downstream form a huge ecosystem. They can rely on the natural advantages of Xiaomi's supply chain finance for financing, which represents a huge market in the future. 5 From the comprehensive layout of Xiaomi Finance, it can be seen that Lei Jun, founder of Xiaomi Group, had already planned the move into supply chain finance. Supply chain finance is already in a stage of rapid development. Competition is becoming increasingly fierce. Compared to the financial businesses of BAT, Xiaomi Finance still has a long way to go. Can Xiaomi Finance become the next Ant Financial? Only time will tell. Suddenly reminded of a quote by Charles Li, 'No matter what happens in the future, it will definitely be very interesting, and it will certainly be pushing society forward.' Title: PICC Life Chuxiong Central Sub-branch Conveys the Spirit of the Provincial Company's Half-Year Work Conference Content: On July 25, PICC Life Chuxiong Central Sub-branch held a meeting for all internal staff across the prefecture. A total of 51 people attended, including all staff from the central sub-branch headquarters and cadres and employees from various county sub-branches. The meeting was chaired by Luo Kaiqiang, Deputy General Manager and Deputy Party Committee Secretary (Acting). Based on the spirit of the half-year work conference conveyed by Deng Huaming, Deputy General Manager and Deputy Party Committee Secretary (Acting) of the Provincial Company, and combined with the actual situation of the Chuxiong Central Sub-branch, the spirit was communicated to all cadres and employees across the prefecture from five key aspects. First, review operations and assess performance results. From overall business conditions, institutional performance, financial indicators, short-term insurance performance, consumer protection assessments, and institutional strengthening, the pain points in the current operations of PICC Life Central Sub-branch were pointed out. It was emphasized that all employees must implement cost reduction and efficiency improvement effectively, and only by doing well in short-term insurance can revenue be generated to reverse the situation of expense deficits. Second, focus on quality recruitment and cultivation, and strengthen the construction of the "Large Individual Insurance" team. This includes aspects such as the manpower overview of large individual insurance institutions, monthly average effective manpower, IWP team construction, and the performance of high-achievers in large individual insurance. Third, innovate mechanisms and systems to enhance operational efficiency. All employees, especially Party members and cadres, must strengthen political construction, deeply advance strict Party governance, and possess the "Three Political Capabilities"; they must also enhance their judgment regarding the strategy, direction, and measures of the "Xiangjiang Breakthrough." Fourth, conduct in-depth analysis to identify problems accurately. Internal staff must improve their service attitude and work style. As the saying goes, "A kind word warms in winter, but a harsh word wounds in June." Serving the "three types of customers" (external partners, fourth-level institutions, and real customers) is the focus of back-office employees. Fifth, strengthen market-oriented assessments and cultivate the cadre team. Cadres are required to diligently study the Huawei spirit, as serving customers is also the reason for the existence of the financial insurance industry. In conveying the spirit of this work conference, Luo Kaiqiang focused on professional leadership, innovation, and transformation, accelerating the breakthrough, analyzed the current situation and problems of PICC Life Chuxiong Central Sub-branch, and pointed out what each department, channel, institution, and employee should do under the "Xiangjiang Breakthrough" strategy, and what pragmatic work style should be upheld to strive towards common goals. Title: Don't Give Up on Cerebral Infarction! With Good Daily Care, a Normal Life Is Not a Problem! Content: Cerebral infarction is a cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease that middle-aged and elderly people are prone to. Daily care after the onset is particularly important, and correct practices can help patients live a normal life. I. Life Care 1. Strengthen Skin Care: If the cerebral infarction condition is severe and the patient needs to be bedridden for a long time, family members should regularly turn the patient, wipe the body, and keep the skin dry and hygienic to prevent bedsores. 2. Regular Life: After getting sick, it is essential to maintain a regular lifestyle, go to bed early and wake up early, ensure adequate sleep time; rest moderately, and balance work and rest. 3. Quit Smoking and Alcohol: Smoking and drinking increase the brittleness of blood vessels and may cause the cerebral infarction condition to worsen or recur, so once diagnosed with cerebral infarction, one should quit smoking and alcohol. II. Dietary Regulation 1. Supplement Vitamins: When suffering from cerebral infarction, you can appropriately eat more fruits and vegetables because they are rich in vitamin C, potassium, magnesium, etc., which can regulate cholesterol metabolism, soften blood vessels, and benefit the improvement of the condition. 2. Eat Less Animal Fat: Foods like lard, cream, fatty meat, and animal organs are rich in fat and cholesterol. Frequently eating these foods can worsen the condition. Therefore, after getting sick, eat less or avoid such foods. It is best to choose vegetable oil for cooking. 3. Light Diet, Not Overfull: After getting sick, the diet should be light-based, avoid high-salt foods to prevent increased blood pressure and worsening of the cerebral infarction condition. Food intake should also be appropriate, about 70% full per meal, otherwise it will increase the burden on the heart and induce worsening of the cerebral infarction condition. 4. The brands and products come from dozens of countries worldwide, with huge differences in bottle design, taste, mineral content, and even color. It truly lives up to its name as a water museum. Besides water, they also sell alcoholic beverages, but only one type: single malt whiskey, and they focus solely on perfecting this one variety. Most customers who come here to drink are people who have high requirements and a particular taste for whiskey. Address: Hezuo Road Jie Lifang Creative Space

Title: A Brief Discussion on the Wealth Management Market Content: From 2007 to the present, the wealth management industry has experienced a journey from explosive growth to today's bleak and cautious state; from lax regulation to today's strict oversight; from irregular practices to standardization; from constant explosions of scandals to today's delayed responses. It's really hard to describe in a few words. It started with the P2P scandals and runaway platforms in 2015, then private equity began having problems from 2017-2019, trusts broke rigid redemption in 2020, and public funds plummeted in 2022. Investors have gradually lost confidence in wealth management and the industry. Look at the increase in M2 this year and the rise in bank demand deposits - these funds need to be lent out for banks to generate profits. This also indirectly shows that investors have lost confidence in wealth management and are keeping their money in banks. Of course, there's nothing wrong with doing this. Considering the three characteristics of funds: safety, liquidity, and profitability, safety comes first. Personally, I also believe the principal is most important in wealth management. As long as the principal remains, there's still a chance to recover; if the principal is gone, there's no possibility of making a comeback. However, if you want your funds to appreciate and combat inflation (6% annually), and have your own ideas, you still need to find reliable financial tools. Personally, I think: For fixed-income-like products, 1) you can learn about standardized urban investment bonds, which have had zero defaults in 30 years. 2) Government credit trusts. For equity products (public or private), you still need to look at the underlying investments - it's best if the underlying assets invest in some standard bonds, government bonds, corporate bonds. The overall return might be slightly lower, but the advantage is stability. If you want higher returns, you can look at index-enhanced funds. For primary equity products, you need to examine the investment track and past successful cases of the investment institution, but I don't really recommend inexperienced investors venture into equity investments, firstly because of the high investment threshold and secondly because of the high risks. Title: Yangtian Village, Miping Town, Xixia County: Setting Out Again After the "War on Epidemic", Conducting In-Depth Surveys to Alleviate People's Worries
Content: At the beginning of 2020, a novel coronavirus pneumonia epidemic swept across the country. To win this war without smoke, party organizations at all levels deployed their best forces. The resident work team stationed in Yangtian Village, Miping Town, Xixia County by the Xixia County Tax Bureau quickly transformed their roles, becoming the village's epidemic prevention propagandists, checkpoint duty personnel, and shoppers for isolated individuals. As the epidemic prevention and control situation evolved, General Secretary Xi emphasized at the symposium on securing a decisive victory in poverty alleviation the need to overcome the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, unite with concentration to win the battle against poverty, ensure the completion of poverty alleviation targets and tasks on schedule, and ensure the comprehensive establishment of a moderately prosperous society. Consequently, the resident work team returned to the main focus of poverty alleviation, visiting poor households' homes to conduct detailed surveys of their production and living conditions during the epidemic. Entering Zhong Yaotang's home, the attentive responsibility team leader Yang Chun noticed that Mr. Zhong's home lacked space for clothes and was missing a wardrobe. He applied to the town to provide him with a multi-functional combination wardrobe. Upon receiving the wardrobe, Zhong Yaotang warmly grasped the hand of the poverty alleviation team member, insisting on having the team stay for a meal. The resident work team delivered a multi-functional combination wardrobe to Zhong Yaotang. Photo provided by Wang Ziming. Arriving at poor household Bai Yanyun's home, she was intently attending online classes. Upon inquiry, it was learned that during this period when school hadn't started, she had been taking online classes at home, but without an internet connection, she could only use mobile data to watch videos. The poverty alleviation team immediately coordinated with China Unicom upon learning this, and China Unicom promptly agreed to provide Bai Yanyun with a special mobile phone card, waiving call and data fees during the epidemic. Bai Yanyun studying online at home. Photo provided by Wang Ziming. Visiting poor household Chen Xiaopo's home, it was discovered that the sheep he raised last year using industrial award subsidy funds had already been sold. When asked if he would continue developing industries this year, he seemed somewhat confused, unwilling to continue but unsure what else to do. At that time, Muyuan Company happened to be recruiting in the town, so the work team persuaded him to try applying. The timid Chen Xiaopo, under everyone's strong persuasion, finally decided to give it a try. Responsibility team leader Yang Chun found the cleanest clothes in his wardrobe and specifically took him for a haircut and a bath, giving him a completely refreshed appearance. The next day, Chen Xiaopo called, happily informing everyone that he had been hired and was just waiting for a text message notification to start work.

Title: How much do you know about DRG healthcare reform? Content: 1. What exactly is DRG? Simply put, for each type of illness treated in a hospital, medical insurance will use big data to package and categorize it based on symptoms, severity, and other factors. Then, a fixed corresponding standard treatment cost is set for each classified disease, essentially putting a price tag on it. 2. What negative impacts might the DRG reform bring? (1) It might lead to a shift of inpatient costs to outpatient or external costs; (2) It might reduce medical institutions' willingness to adopt new technologies, limiting patients' choices; (3) Hospitals might select patients and cases from the perspective of reducing costs, and those hospitals originally willing to care for inpatients might need to adjust bed numbers for cost savings. 3. How should we respond to the healthcare reform? The implementation of DRG is an inevitable path for the reform of the medical insurance system. No matter how the external environment changes, adequate health insurance can allow customers to enjoy truly multi-layered medical security. (1) Million-yuan medical/high-end medical insurance becomes a standard supplement beyond basic medical insurance. Having only basic medical insurance is far from sufficient. DRG reminds us that out-of-pocket medical expenses will increasingly become more common. Million-yuan medical/high-end medical insurance will become a standard supplement, offering more choices when necessary, such as reimbursement for self-paid drugs or advanced treatments in private hospitals; (2) Allocate adequate critical illness insurance. Critical illness insurance is an independent compensation system unrelated to basic medical insurance and provides lifelong coverage. Its importance is self-evident. Only by resolving these worries can we better experience and enjoy life. #MedicalInsurance #HealthcareReformAffectsEveryone #InsuranceAwareness #MedicalInsurance #HealthcareReformAffectsEveryone #InsuranceAwareness

Title: What are the precautions for painless childbirth? 1. Not suitable for a minority of people The most important precaution is that painless childbirth is not suitable for everyone. Women with coagulation problems, pregnancy complications, allergies to anesthetic drugs, or those who have suffered lower back injuries are not suitable, as there are significant risks. For example: coagulation dysfunction can easily cause bleeding reactions. Therefore, prenatal consultation with a doctor and relevant examinations are necessary. 2. Slight discomfort during anesthesia Of course, if there is slight discomfort during anesthesia, there is no need to be nervous; it is a normal phenomenon. 3. Be careful with movement Painless childbirth usually involves attaching a soft tube to the back, connecting the epidural space to the analgesic pump, which can continuously administer pain relief until the end of childbirth. Therefore, if you vigorously rub your back or pull on the catheter, it may cause the catheter to dislodge, preventing the analgesic drugs from being delivered properly and leading to failure of pain relief. So, during painless childbirth, you must be careful with movement and try to avoid pulling the catheter. 4. The mother still needs to continue efforts Another very important point to clarify is that painless childbirth does not mean the mother can completely relax. She still needs to continue exerting effort to accelerate the delivery of the baby. Anesthesia only blocks the pain sensation and does not affect the motor nerves, because childbirth mainly relies on the mother's conscious efforts, with medical staff only providing guidance and assistance. #Women's Health# #Painless Childbirth#

Title: Will overdue Huabei payments result in debt collectors visiting family members? Content: Credit card overdue payment is a serious breach of contract that can bring many adverse consequences. Based on my search results, the main consequences of credit card overdue payments include the following aspects: Interest and penalties: After a credit card payment becomes overdue, the bank will charge you interest and penalties according to the agreed interest rate and penalty rate, which will increase your repayment burden and total debt. Credit record: After a credit card payment becomes overdue, the bank will report your overdue situation to the People's Bank of China Credit Reference Center and record it in your personal credit report. This will affect your personal credit score and credit rating, thereby impacting the approval rate and conditions for future applications for loans, renting, visas, and other services. Debt collection and litigation: After a credit card payment becomes overdue, the bank will pursue debt collection through phone calls, text messages, emails, etc., and may entrust third-party agencies or law firms to conduct collection activities. If you refuse to repay for an extended period or cannot be contacted, the bank has the right to file a lawsuit in court according to relevant laws and regulations such as the "Contract Law of the People's Republic of China," demanding that you fulfill your repayment obligations and bear litigation costs and other losses. Doorstep debt collection: After a credit card payment becomes overdue, the bank or a third-party agency might potentially conduct doorstep collection, but this situation is not common and is not a legal method. According to relevant regulations like the "Basic System for Protecting Financial Consumer Rights and Interests," debt collectors must not use violence, threats, insults, harassment, or other methods for collection, nor may they arbitrarily enter a consumer's residence or workplace for collection activities. If you encounter such a situation, you can refuse to accept it and complain to the relevant departments or call the police. If you want to 'get back on shore,' meaning escape the debt predicament, you need to take effective measures as soon as possible to resolve the issue. I suggest you refer to the following aspects: Stop using credit cards and reduce unnecessary expenses. You need to clearly understand your financial situation, including income, expenses, assets, liabilities, etc., and create a reasonable budget plan. Try to increase income or reduce expenses to have more cash flow for repayment. Communicate and negotiate with the bank. You can explain your repayment difficulties and sincerity to the bank and request some grace period or preferential terms like reduced interest. If possible, you can try to consolidate multiple credit cards into one and apply for installment payments or balance transfer repayment.

Title: Use Some Cheap "Sterilization King" for Flower Growing, Spray It in the Flowerpot, Sterilize and Remove Dust Content: When growing flowers and plants at home, the biggest fear is them getting sick. If the plants get infested with insects, spending some time picking them off one by one can improve the situation. But if they get sick, germs cannot be "picked" off; you can only use medication. Using medication for outdoor flower growing is not a big problem, but it's not ideal for indoor flower growing. In areas where the weather is relatively cold in winter, the activity of pests and diseases decreases, and plants are less likely to get infested or sick. However, plants grown in warmer temperatures or in heated rooms can still get infested or sick, affecting their growth. When plants are likely to get sick, using some cheap "Sterilization King" and spraying it in the flowerpot can sterilize and remove dust, eliminating the disease. The Cheap "Sterilization King" Baking Soda Baking soda is a cheap "Sterilization King". If used properly, it is beneficial for plant growth. Baking soda itself does not have a sterilizing effect, but its solution is alkaline, has strong permeability, can neutralize acidic substances, and remove stains. Various miscellaneous bacteria that affect plant growth, some prefer acidic environments, and some hide in stains on branches and leaves. Spraying a little baking soda solution on the flowerpot and plants can sterilize, remove dust, and drive away diseases. In daily life, people use baking soda to wash pots, pans, bowls, or clothes with heavy oil stains for the same reason. Besides cleaning very thoroughly (baking soda is alkaline and can neutralize the acidity of oil stains), it also has the effect of sterilizing and removing dust (bacteria hide in stains, and when the stains are gone, the bacteria naturally decrease). Therefore, baking soda is one of the essential household items, cheap and very useful. The Correct Method of Using Baking Soda for Flower Growing Cleaning Leaves When the stains on plant leaves are heavy and difficult to clean, spray the leaves with a 300-fold diluted baking soda solution, then gently wipe with a towel to remove the stains. For plants with small, numerous leaves, after spraying with a 300-fold baking soda solution, wait a minute or two, then rinse with clean water; most stains can be washed away. For plants with larger leaves, you can also directly wipe them with a towel dipped in a 300-fold or more diluted baking soda solution. After wiping, the leaves will be shiny and exceptionally clean. Cleaning plant leaves makes them look better and enhances their ornamental value. On the other hand, various miscellaneous bacteria have no place to hide and cannot multiply in large numbers, so the plants are less likely to get sick. Especially for plants with larger leaves, such as Monstera deliciosa, Fiddle-leaf Fig, Rubber Plant, etc., when the leaves are dusty, cleaning with baking soda water works best. Pest Prevention and Control Regularly cleaning plant leaves with baking soda water can also prevent pest infestations. Some pests prefer acidic environments and will stay away when encountering alkaline baking soda water. Even if plants are already infested, spraying baking soda water can help prevent and eliminate pests. For example, when aphids come into contact with baking soda water, the alkaline solution quickly penetrates their protective membrane. Once the aphids' tender bodies lose their protective membrane and are exposed to the air, they easily die. Cleaning Miscellaneous Bacteria, Sterilization During seasons when diseases are likely to occur, regularly spraying the leaves, branches, and pot surfaces of plants with low-concentration baking soda water can clean miscellaneous bacteria, sterilize, and reduce the likelihood of plants getting sick. Even if plants are already sick, proper use of baking soda water can slow down the spread of pathogens. For plants grown in enclosed environments, there is a significant difference in the probability of getting sick between those frequently using baking soda water and those not using it at all. In winter, when it's cold, and windows and doors are opened less frequently, if you have many plants at home and the temperature is relatively high, you might try using baking soda water for sterilization. Points to Note When Using Baking Soda for Flower Growing 1. Do not use baking soda water for root drenching When using baking soda water for plants, whether for cleaning dust, pest prevention, or sterilization, only spray it on the leaves, stems, and pot surface. Do not use it for root drenching. Baking soda water is alkaline, and most plants grown at home prefer acidic soil. After watering with baking soda water, the pot soil quickly changes from acidic to neutral or alkaline, which plants cannot adapt to, leading to yellowing leaves, leaf drop, or even the entire plant dying. 2. Control the concentration of baking soda water Although baking soda water has the effects of sterilization, dust removal, and pest prevention, the concentration must be carefully controlled when using it. If the concentration is too high, it can cause side effects in plants. Generally, a dilution of 300-fold or more is safer. If the concentration is too high, after spraying on plant leaves, white crystals may remain, affecting plant growth and appearance. 3. Do not use baking soda water too frequently When using baking soda water for plants, space out the applications. For example, if only cleaning dust from leaves, use it once every one or two months. During seasons with frequent diseases, use it once every ten days or half a month. Using it too frequently can affect plant growth, making the leaves look rough and not smooth. 4. Use medication for seriously sick plants Although baking soda water can sterilize, it is not a professional sterilizing agent and has limited effects. If plants have minor diseases, using baking soda water, increasing ventilation, and providing more sunlight might slowly cure them. But if your plants are already seriously diseased, do not rely solely on baking soda for sterilization, as it will be basically ineffective. Instead, use specialized fungicides, such as Carbendazim, Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, etc. Use some cheap "Sterilization King" for flower growing, spray it in the flowerpot, sterilize and remove dust, and the diseases will be gone.
