Title: Frequent rainfall, yet apple spider mites still occur? Understand 3 reasons and implement 4 measures to reduce losses. Content: Frequent rainfall surprisingly has little impact on the growth and development of spider mites. In some severely affected orchards, a single leaf can host more than 7 harmful mites, so we remind everyone to pay attention and prevent apple spider mites promptly. Apple spider mites mainly infest the upper surface of leaves, and tender buds, leaves, and young fruits can all be harmed. After leaf damage, small chlorotic spots initially appear, which gradually merge into large patches. In severe cases, leaves turn yellow-green, become brittle and hard, and eventually the entire leaf appears gray-white from a distance, severely affecting normal photosynthesis. However, under light infestation, leaves generally do not fall. When buds are severely damaged, they gradually wither and die. This significantly impacts apple yield and quality, often causing substantial economic losses. In fact, spider mite outbreaks have shown an increasing trend in recent years, capable of causing damage from June to September. The optimal control period is before and after flowering. The current outbreaks among these fruit growers indicate inadequate previous prevention and control efforts, leading to significant leaf damage. Orchards with severely damaged leaves suffer from poor ventilation and light penetration. Based on our observations, orchards affected by spider mites, especially severely affected ones, share a common issue: poor ventilation leads to heavier infestation. Issues include excessive planting density, overcrowded trees with overlapping branches and leaves blocking light, lack of timely thinning, resulting in poor field ventilation and light penetration; excessive retained branches without pruning, leading to overly dense foliage; failure to thin fruits, with too many bagged fruits, creating a densely packed appearance. Poor ventilation not only affects orchard air circulation and light but also provides favorable habitats for pests, complicating pesticide application. The inner canopy and tree trunks are hard to spray thoroughly, reducing overall pesticide coverage and greatly diminishing control effectiveness. This is why many fruit growers complain that spider mites are hard to control, recurring shortly after pesticide application. Poor prevention awareness. Spider mite infestations develop gradually, starting from points and spreading to areas, or from one tree to a group. If fruit growers miss the critical control period and only start applying pesticides during peak infestation, it's already too late, resulting in poor control effectiveness. Additionally, some growers focus only on killing adult mites but neglect mite eggs. While adults may be temporarily eliminated, hatched eggs continue the cycle. Without targeting eggs, control efforts are largely ineffective. Once an outbreak occurs with high pest density, it becomes uncontrollable and inevitably spreads. Issues with pesticide use for bud spider mites. Some growers, to save costs, use cheap, inferior pesticides that are ineffective against mites, delaying control and worsening the infestation. Furthermore, continuous use of the same pesticide year after year, often at arbitrarily increased concentrations and application frequency to achieve quick results, leads to mite resistance and shortens the pesticide's effective lifespan. Beyond these issues, problems in spraying techniques are also prominent, such as failing to target affected areas or achieving incomplete coverage. Both the upper and lower leaf surfaces can be infested by spider mites. Although the upper surface is more commonly affected, the lower surface should not be overlooked during spraying. Only uniform coverage on both sides ensures effective control. 1. Chemical control pesticide方案: Based on the infestation situation, promptly spray with 45% bifenazate-etoxazole suspension concentrate at 2000-2500x dilution, or 43% bifenazate at 2000-3000x dilution, or 24 g/L spiromesifen suspension concentrate at 2000x dilution, or 5% fenpyroximate suspension concentrate at 2000x dilution, or 36% pyridaben-spiromesifen suspension concentrate at 2000-2500x dilution mixed with Fino at 2000-3000x dilution for control. Apply pesticides promptly and pay attention to alternating pesticides. Notes: The types of pesticides used and the duration of use vary by region, leading to differing levels of pesticide resistance in spider mites. Not all pesticides are equally effective in every region. Specific effective pesticides should be selected based on local control practices. To overcome and reduce resistance development, rotate pesticides and avoid long-term use of a single product. Do not use any single pesticide more than twice, and avoid repeated, long-term use even if a pesticide shows good initial effectiveness. Additionally, during spraying, ensure uniform and comprehensive coverage. Spray thoroughly on trees, ground vegetation, inner canopy, and tree trunks. Both leaf surfaces should be evenly coated to avoid misses and ensure control effectiveness. 2. Agricultural control through pruning and shaping. For overly dense plantings, transplant trees in batches to reduce density. Maintain reasonable tree structure, avoiding excessively high or shaded canopies that hinder later spraying and reduce control effectiveness. Increase reshaping efforts to control canopy size reasonably, keeping it compact. Remove all branches detrimental to tree growth or useless, improving ventilation and light penetration, and facilitating spraying. Orchard cleanup and pest elimination. After apple harvest, thoroughly remove coarse and loose bark from trunks, scrub off overwintering eggs on trees, sweep up fallen leaves and diseased leaves from the ground, and prune pest-infested branches, then burn them collectively. Before budding, spray the entire orchard with lime sulfur once to further eliminate overwintering populations. Cover the ground under trees with a layer of clean soil from outside the orchard to reduce and prevent pests from emerging and climbing trees. Alternatively, tie grass around trunks to attract mites, remove and burn it before thawing in spring. These measures can reduce spider mite numbers the following year.

Title: Fuzhou Regional Development Concept: Integrating Taijiang into Gulou, Transforming Minhou County into a City, Expanding and Upgrading Pingtan Content: Against the backdrop of globalization, urban development and regional integration have increasingly become focal points for national and local governments. As a historically rich city, Fuzhou's regional adjustments not only impact its own development but also represent a significant reshaping of the broader regional economic landscape. This article explores the macroeconomic implications and potential impacts of integrating Fuzhou's Taijiang District into Gulou District, transforming Minhou County into a city, and expanding and upgrading Pingtan. I. Strategic Significance of Integrating Taijiang into Gulou The merger of Taijiang District and Gulou District signifies a redefinition of the administrative boundaries within Fuzhou's city center. This move holds considerable importance for optimizing administrative management and resource allocation. Firstly, the consolidation of administrative resources will enhance government service efficiency and reduce management costs. For instance, post-merger, urban planning, traffic management, and educational resources can be coordinated and utilized more effectively. Secondly, the integrated development of commerce, culture, and tourism will introduce new growth drivers for Fuzhou's central area. Using specific data and case studies, we can examine how this integration enhances the overall competitiveness of Fuzhou's city center. II. Economic Effects of Transforming Minhou County into a City As a key satellite city of Fuzhou, elevating Minhou to city status, thereby increasing its economic autonomy and administrative authority, will have profound effects on the regional economy. This change will enable Minhou to more flexibly promote industrial upgrades, attract domestic and foreign investment, and accelerate economic growth. Simultaneously, Minhou's development will support the urban area of Fuzhou by alleviating issues like urban overcrowding and providing more job opportunities and living space. Utilizing relevant data and examples, this article analyzes the potential economic impacts of Minhou's city status transformation on Fuzhou and surrounding areas. III. Regional Impact of Expanding and Upgrading Pingtan As China's only cross-strait economic zone, the expansion and upgrade of Pingtan carry unique strategic significance. This initiative will not only strengthen Pingtan's own economic development but also enhance economic and trade ties between Fuzhou and Taiwan, promoting cross-strait economic and cultural exchanges. This article examines how Pingtan's expansion and upgrade serve as a bridgehead for regional economic integration, fostering the development of cross-strait relations, while exploring its effects on Fuzhou and the broader regional economy. These three regional adjustments represent not only an optimization of Fuzhou's administrative management but also a crucial realignment of its economic development strategy. Through in-depth analysis of the potential economic effects of these changes, we can better understand and predict Fuzhou's development trends in the new era.

Title: Why is ZhiLiu Sewage Lift Pump's "Reverse Cleaning" Technology More Suitable for Kitchen Scenarios? Content: When building a kitchen on the basement level of a villa, the reliability of the drainage system is indeed a core challenge, especially the risk of blockages caused by oil and grease. Improper handling can directly affect the user experience. Based on your needs, here are some additional targeted details and suggestions to help make the drainage system more stable: 1. Why is ZhiLiu Sewage Lift Pump's "Reverse Cleaning" technology more suitable for kitchen scenarios? The particularity of kitchen wastewater lies in oil and grease (especially animal fats that solidify easily when cold, and frying residues) and fine food particles. Once these substances adhere to the pump body, impeller, or tank inner wall, long-term accumulation will inevitably lead to blockages. 2. ZhiLiu's automatic reverse cleaning function specifically addresses this pain point: Proactive Prevention Rather Than Passive Cleaning: It doesn't wait for grease to solidify before laboriously removing it. Instead, it uses scheduled (customizable based on daily cooking frequency, peak hours) high-pressure clean water flushing to disperse and discharge the grease with the wastewater before it completely hardens, reducing adhesion at the source. 360° Dead Spot Coverage: The rotating cleaning head design covers corners of the tank, impeller gaps, and other easily soiled "blind spots," avoiding incomplete cleaning caused by obstructed views and cramped spaces during manual cleaning. No Additional Operation Required: Compared to manual cleaning (which requires opening the tank and contacting dirty water) or oil-water separators (which require regular disposal of waste oil), this "automatic operation" mode adds almost no daily maintenance cost, making it more worry-free for villa users. 3. Beyond the equipment itself, some habits in daily use can also help reduce oil and grease: Install a Pre-filter: Add a fine mesh filter at the kitchen sink drain outlet to intercept large debris like vegetable leaves and bones in advance, reducing impurities entering the lift pump. Control Water Temperature and Discharge Timing: For high-temperature oil and grease generated after cooking (like frying pan wastewater), let it cool or add a small amount of cold water to dilute it first. Avoid allowing high-temperature grease to enter the pump directly (although the ZhiLiu tank has strong temperature resistance, grease solidifies more easily at lower temperatures; pre-treatment can reduce the equipment's burden). Regular "Hot Water Flushing" Assistance: Manually flush the sink pipes weekly with 40-50°C warm water (not too high to avoid accelerating rubber part aging). Use the water temperature to soften small amounts of residual grease, complementing the equipment's automatic cleaning for dual protection. Overall, ZhiLiu Sewage Lift Pump's automatic reverse cleaning technology fundamentally solves the core problem of kitchen grease blockages. Combined with simple daily habit optimizations, it can ensure the long-term stable operation of the basement kitchen's drainage system, being both practical and maintenance-free.

Content Details: Car enthusiasts. For example, dash cams, window tinting, seat covers, etc. Car enthusiasts. In the eyes of car owners, this seems like nothing. Actually, many things are very superfluous and may endanger safety. Pay attention when choosing installations. The first is not to hang red cloth strips on your new car. Everyone buys a new car and hangs red cloth strips to pray for peace and good luck. Actually, these red cloth strips fluttering around can directly affect our field of vision. And the most serious is hanging them on the four tires. These red cloth strips are very likely to get tangled in the brake discs. Car enthusiasts. This is very unsafe for our parking. So it's best not to put flashy things on a new car. The second is not to hang decorations on the rearview mirror. These decorations, more or less, will block our view. Previously, there was a car owner who hung a small pendant on their new car. As a result, not long after driving the new car, during an emergency brake, the pendant directly smashed the front windshield. The third rather superfluous thing is installing seat covers on the car. Car enthusiasts. Many people think installing them can protect our seats. Car enthusiasts. However, some high-end leather seats come with functions like ventilation, heating, and massage. If we buy a new car and directly put a seat cover on it, we cannot directly experience these functions. So it's superfluous. And we buy leather seats to enjoy their comfort. After putting on a roughly made seat cover, the leather seat becomes just for show. What do you think are other things for a new car, car enthusiasts, that are unnecessary to install? Content Title: Pet Store Employee Responds to Store Fire Where No Pets Survived Publication Date: 2025-10-23 04:10:04 Content Status: Review Completed Content Type: Multimedia Industry: Digital Government Affairs_Government Media_Government Media Author Name: Qilu Evening News Guoran Video Owner Name: Qilu Evening News Guoran Video Content Account Type: Enterprise Content Details: A fire broke out in a pet shop, and no pets survived. Employee: Rushed into the store twice immediately upon arrival. But the store was filled with black smoke, and nothing could be seen. The owners were all very understanding and did not make things difficult, but I feel very sorry and guilty. Electric scooter. On October 20, a sudden fire occurred in a pet store in Guangdong, and the pets inside unfortunately died. On the 21st, the involved pet store posted a message. Electric scooter. Apologized to the pet owners and stated that they would 'fully cooperate with all subsequent matters and bear all responsibilities that should be undertaken.' Title: 77-year-old man suddenly falls ill, traffic police clear the way to hospital Content: A 77-year-old man suddenly fell ill, experiencing incontinence and gradually losing consciousness. In a panic, his family hurriedly drove him to the hospital. However, the journey was quite long, so the driver quickly called the police for help. Upon understanding the situation, the traffic police immediately drove a police car to meet them and got the patient to the hospital in less than 10 minutes. At 19:40 on the 10th, officers from the High-Speed Rail Squadron of the Daizhou District Traffic Police Brigade were on a mission when they suddenly received an emergency call. It reported that a minivan was traveling from Xiazhang Town along Taidong Road towards the city center, carrying a critically ill patient whose condition was rapidly deteriorating. Time was life. The officers who received the call immediately drove their police car along Taidong Road to locate the minivan. They finally found the speeding van near Woniushi on Taidong Road. The patient onboard was a 77-year-old man who had suddenly become incontinent that evening and was semi-comatose during the journey. After meeting the driver, the police car immediately turned on its siren and lights to lead the way, running several red lights along the route. They delivered the patient to the Affiliated Hospital of Taishan Medical College in under 10 minutes—a journey of about 10 kilometers that would normally take around 20 minutes. Upon arrival, emergency department doctors immediately began treating the elderly man. The family repeatedly expressed their gratitude to the officers who cleared the way. After ensuring the patient was properly settled, the officers who escorted them drove their police car away into the night, returning to their posts to continue their duties.

Title: Behind the Reduction of Logistics Costs Lies the "Blood and Tears" Bill of Truck Drivers Content: Behind the Reduction of Logistics Costs Lies the "Blood and Tears" Bill of Truck Drivers In 2024, the ratio of total social logistics costs to GDP dropped to a record low, taking a big step towards the 2027 target of 13.5%. Behind these seemingly positive numbers, there is a group of people whose smiles are gradually fading; they are the truck drivers traveling all over the country. These drivers support the arteries of logistics with their sweat, yet their income has become the "sacrifice" for reducing logistics costs. The contradiction between this reduction and shrinkage becomes increasingly prominent. Recently, a set of logistics industry data has attracted widespread attention. In 2024, the ratio of China's total social logistics costs to GDP dropped to 14.1%, setting the lowest record since statistics began in 2006. The National Development and Reform Commission has also set a future goal: planning to further reduce this ratio to around 13.5% by 2027. From a macro perspective, reducing logistics costs is of great significance to China's economic development. Lower logistics costs mean lower operating costs for enterprises, which can directly enhance their competitiveness and promote national economic development. For every percentage point reduction, enterprises can save significant funds to invest in key areas such as R&D and production, aiding industrial upgrading. In the manufacturing industry, lower logistics costs allow companies to flexibly adjust production strategies, accelerate product updates, and enhance market competitiveness. From an industrial development perspective, reducing logistics costs helps optimize industrial structure upgrading. When logistics costs are reduced, enterprises can allocate resources more rationally, investing more resources into core businesses and improving production efficiency. From a livelihood perspective, consumers also benefit from lower logistics costs. Commodity prices are expected to decrease due to lower logistics costs, allowing consumers to purchase desired goods at lower prices and improving their quality of life. For example, when shopping online, reduced logistics costs might lead to lower delivery fees or more affordable product prices. However, behind this prosperity, truck drivers have unspeakable hardships. Many truck drivers have spoken out, pointing out that the reduction in logistics costs largely comes at the expense of their freight rates. In the logistics industry, truck drivers are a crucial link, traveling day and night on roads across the country, providing solid support for cargo transportation. But in recent years, they have faced the dilemma of continuously decreasing freight rates, leading to a significant reduction in income and a sudden increase in living pressure. Some truck drivers helplessly said: "In the past, a long-distance trip yielded a decent income. Now, freight rates keep dropping. After deducting fuel costs, tolls, and vehicle wear and tear, the remaining money is less and less, sometimes making it hard to cover basic living expenses." Such sentiments reflect the difficult situation of many truck drivers and force us to examine the cost behind the reduction in logistics expenses. A Multi-faceted Analysis of Logistics Cost Reduction Positive Factors for Cost Reduction The reduction in China's logistics costs is not accidental but the result of multiple positive factors working together. The optimization and upgrading of the industrial structure is an important driving force for reducing logistics costs. With China's economic development, the industrial structure is shifting from traditional labor-intensive industries to high-tech industries and services. High-tech industry products have high added value, small size, and light weight, resulting in relatively lower logistics demand, which reduces logistics costs. For example, the rapid development of the electronic information industry has led to a gradual decline in the proportion of logistics costs for electronic products in the total logistics costs. Furthermore, industrial structure upgrading promotes the diversification and premiumization of logistics demand, driving logistics companies towards specialization and refinement, improving logistics service efficiency and quality, and further reducing logistics costs. The continuous improvement of the logistics operation system provides strong support for reducing logistics costs. In recent years, China has increased investment in logistics infrastructure, building a number of modern logistics parks, ports, railways, highways, and other facilities, forming a relatively complete logistics network. The development of multimodal transport achieves seamless connection between different transportation modes, improves transport efficiency, and reduces transport costs. For example, the promotion of rail-water combined transport, where goods are transported jointly by rail and water, reduces intermediate links and lowers transportation costs. The development of logistics informatization improves the transparency and controllability of logistics operations, reduces waste and delays in logistics links, and lowers logistics costs. Through logistics information platforms, enterprises can grasp the transportation status of goods and inventory situation in real-time, arrange transportation and storage reasonably, and improve the utilization efficiency of logistics resources. Advanced technologies such as big data, artificial intelligence, and the Internet of Things are widely used in the logistics field, achieving intelligent management and operation of logistics. Automated sorting equipment improves sorting efficiency and reduces labor costs. Intelligent warehousing systems can automatically optimize storage locations based on the frequency of goods movement and inventory status, improving warehouse space utilization. Logistics companies can also use big data to analyze customer needs and behaviors, optimize logistics distribution routes, improve distribution efficiency, and reduce distribution costs. Policy support and guidance have created a favorable environment for reducing logistics costs. The state has introduced a series of policies to support logistics development, such as reducing the tax burden on logistics enterprises, increasing investment in logistics infrastructure construction, and promoting logistics standardization. The implementation of these policies has lowered the operating costs of logistics enterprises, improved the overall competitiveness of the logistics industry, and promoted the reduction of logistics costs. Controversy: The Link Between Cost Reduction and Workers' Wages Regarding the view that logistics cost reduction comes at the expense of workers' wages, a deeper analysis is needed. From the perspective of transportation structure adjustment, policies like "shift from road to rail" and "shift from road to water" have squeezed the market share of road transport to some extent. The reduced business volume for road transport practitioners naturally affects their income. In the past, road transport accounted for a large proportion in logistics, and truck drivers could obtain relatively stable income through frequent transport business. However, with the development of railway and waterway transport, some goods originally handled by road transport have shifted to rail or water transport, leading to reduced cargo sources and lower freight rates for truck drivers. From the perspective of enterprise operation, in a highly competitive market environment, some logistics companies may take measures to compress labor costs in order to reduce costs. Labor cost is an important part of logistics companies' expenses. Companies might reduce operating costs by lowering drivers' wages and reducing benefits. Although this approach can reduce costs in the short term, in the long run, it may affect drivers' work enthusiasm and service quality, thereby impacting the entire logistics industry's development. The informatization and intelligent development of the logistics industry also affect truck drivers' income to some extent. With the rise of logistics information platforms and the application of intelligent transport equipment, logistics transport efficiency has improved, but drivers' work has become more transparent. In this situation, drivers' bargaining power is relatively weakened, making it difficult to increase freight rates. Intelligent dispatch systems automatically arrange transport tasks based on cargo transport demand and vehicle location. Drivers cannot freely choose tasks as they did before, affecting their income. The Living Situation of Truck Drivers Wages and Working Environment Against the backdrop of the logistics industry's development, the living situation of truck drivers is concerning. In terms of wages, although the logistics industry is booming, the income growth of truck drivers is slow. According to the "Truck Driver Employment Status Survey Report" by the China Federation of Logistics & Purchasing, the average monthly net income of truck drivers is concentrated between 5,000 - 8,000 yuan, accounting for 28.13%; those with a net income between 8,000 - 10,000 yuan account for 23.05%, totaling about 51.18%. Truck drivers with an average monthly net income above 10,000 yuan account for 21.42%. Those with an average monthly net income below 5,000 yuan account for 27.4%, close to thirty percent. In terms of working environment, truck drivers face many difficulties. Long hours of driving put tremendous physical pressure on them, with an average daily driving time exceeding 10 hours, sometimes even up to 15 hours. Long-term sitting and bumpy rides make them highly susceptible to occupational diseases, such as lumbar disc herniation and cervical spondylosis. Old Zhang, a driver with 10 years of experience, said helplessly: "Sitting in the driver's seat every day for over ten hours at a time, when I get off the car, my back can't straighten up, and my neck is stiff and uncomfortable." Irregular meals and rest are also major problems. To deliver goods on time, they often cannot eat on time and have to make do at service areas or roadside stops. Rest time is hard to guarantee; sometimes, to complete transport tasks, they have to drive continuously, severely compressing rest time. Such a working environment not only affects their physical health but also puts great psychological pressure on them. The Dilemma of Empty Return Trips Holidays like May Day are a time for family reunions for many, but for truck drivers, it can be a "money-burning" journey. On the day before the May Day holiday, return traffic on the highway was heavy, but the cargo holds of some truck drivers were empty. At 3 a.m., Old Zhang held the steering wheel, sighing as he looked at the empty cargo hold in the rearview mirror. This trip from Guangzhou to Zhengzhou was fully loaded with e-commerce packages on the outbound leg, with a freight charge of 8,000 yuan; but for the return trip, he couldn't find any cargo and had to return empty. After calculating fuel costs, tolls, and vehicle depreciation, this trip resulted in a net loss of over 5,000 yuan. When resting at a service area, Old Zhang communicated with peers, and everyone complained about the difficulty of finding return cargo, with freight rates so low they operated at a loss. Data shows that the empty load rate of China's road freight transport is as high as 40%, especially during holidays when factories shut down and logistics demand decreases, making it even harder for drivers to find return cargo. Some freight platforms have introduced a "bidding mode," where shippers push down prices, and drivers have no choice but to accept the orders reluctantly, otherwise they wouldn't even earn enough for fuel. To reduce losses, many drivers take risks. Some, knowing that overloading is illegal, still choose to overload to avoid a completely empty run. For instance, Old Li was fined 3,000 yuan last year for overloading, but compared to an empty run, it at least meant a smaller loss. More dangerous is fatigued driving; to rush to the next job, many drivers drive continuously for over ten hours, chewing betel nut or drinking Red Bull to stay awake when tired. At 10 p.m., Old Zhang arrived home. His wife was still awake, with food kept warm on the table. His wife cautiously asked how much he earned this trip. Old Zhang lowered his head, eating quickly, not daring to look his wife in the eye, because he didn't earn anything and even lost money, while next month's child tutoring fees, mortgage, and car loan are all waiting for this money. Where is the Way Out? In recent years, some emerging freight platforms have tried to use intelligent matching to reduce the empty load rate, but with limited effect. Drivers hope for policy support, such as reducing highway tolls and regulating恶性 competition in the freight market. They are not afraid of hard work, but they fear losing money on a trip. Reducing logistics costs is an inevitable trend. How to protect the rights and interests of truck drivers while reducing costs is an urgent problem to be solved. This requires the joint efforts of the government, enterprises, and all sectors of society. While pursuing the efficient development of the logistics industry, attention must be paid to the living conditions of every practitioner, finding a balance between logistics cost reduction and the protection of drivers' rights, making the development of the logistics industry healthier and more sustainable.

Title: Beijing's Most Famous Pastry Shop, Over 100 Years of History, More Than 100 Flavors, These 6 Flavors Should Not Be Missed Content: Hello, hello, everyone! The New Year is just a few days away. I really enjoy reading about New Year traditions from different places, so today I'll also talk about the taste of the New Year on the tip of the tongue - Beijing's New Year flavor: the pastry box. The following content might seem a bit like an advertisement, but it really isn't; it's purely to share the taste of Beijing's New Year with everyone. In recent years, another Daoxiangcun (Suzhou Daoxiangcun) has appeared. To be honest, I'd never heard of this Suzhou Daoxiangcun growing up. I see many friends online get confused, so all I can say is, in Beijing, people eat the pastries from the Sanhe Beijing Daoxiangcun. If you want to experience the taste of Beijing or local Beijing life, you really should go to the Sanhe Beijing Daoxiangcun. (No praise or criticism towards Suzhou Daoxiangcun, never tried it). During festivals, the Beijing Daoxiangcun shops get so crowded that long queues form. In my family, if we don't buy some Daoxiangcun pastries for the New Year, it feels like something is missing. When I was little and our family situation wasn't as good, my parents wouldn't buy a whole pre-selected box. They would buy separately packaged pastries and put them in a mooncake tin. Now that I'm older, I also buy a whole pastry box for my parents during the New Year as a token of affection. Daoxiangcun (referring here specifically to the Sanhe Beijing Daoxiangcun, will just call it Daoxiangcun below) seems to have over 100 varieties; I haven't tried them all yet. So I specifically bought several of the most recommended ones, hoping to give everyone a reference. Also, for those living in Beijing or visiting, I suggest going to the store to buy loose, weighed pastries. I bought just one piece of some varieties to taste, and overall, it's more economical than buying boxed sets. The picture below shows part of my purchase; some are duplicates, just bought 2-3 extra pieces. In total, I spent 35 yuan – isn't that a great deal? This is what the loose pastries look like. This is the Daoxiangcun that Beijing locals go to buy~ Now, let's talk specifically about which ones I recommend the most – these are my favorites since childhood, and also the most recommended by friends around me. First is this Zao Hua Su (Jujube Flower Pastry). Everyone should be familiar with it by now. Solid jujube paste filling and crispy, fragrant outer layer – you really can't stop eating it. If you like jujube paste, you really must try it. When you break it open, it's filled solidly with jujube paste. The sweetness is just right; if 10 is the sweetest, this Zao Hua Su is about a 5. I don't know if the cream in time-honored brand pastries from other places is also like this – it's that kind of white, relatively solid hard cream. People who love cream adore it, while those who don't might find it a bit greasy. The cream in this cake is the same hard cream. As someone who超级 loves cream, I think it's absolutely delicious. Even if you don't usually like cream, I suggest buying one piece to try this unique texture and flavor characteristic of time-honored brands. The chocolate cake base is somewhat dense, sweetness around level 3, and has a chewy texture when you bite into it. The cross-section shows layers of cream – really super delicious. Haha. A must-try for pork floss lovers. They have several pork floss varieties; two more later are also highly recommended by me. This pork floss cake has a very crispy, crumbly skin with a sesame fragrance. The filling is a solid, thick layer of savory pork floss – very tasty. Even after eating so many pork floss rolls, the first bite still makes me exclaim, 'This is so delicious!' The cake is very soft and tender, with that transparent white salad dressing inside (seems unique to time-honored brands). The pork floss on the two ends tastes different from the pork floss cake above; this one has a slightly stringy texture and a sweet-salty flavor. There's no pork floss rolled inside, just a layer of transparent salad dressing, which is a little sweet and a little creamy – delicious. This is a relatively dense cake, can be a breakfast, and is quite large. The top layer has a hardness and texture somewhere between a biscuit and pastry. Inside, it's layers of cake and cream stacked together, but the cream isn't thick. A very milky-flavored one. I really超级 like this one; it's also very popular. Its outer skin feels like a biscuit but with a slight韧性 (chewiness). The jujube paste filling inside contains a bit of nuts. Sweetness is around level 5. Very solid. This is probably the one I've eaten the most, by far. Since I was little, my mom would buy it frequently (along with Daoxiangcun's char siu pork). The inside has a spiced salt, sweet-salty flavor (not sure if it actually contains spiced salt, just using the term to describe the taste). The outer skin is made of thin, flaky layers, so crispy it crumbles – a texture that's crispy outside and chewy inside. These two are the same variety, just different flavors. They are not very big, quite solid, and the texture is on the harder side. If buying for elderly people, I wouldn't recommend this one. But if giving to friends or classmates, I believe many would like it. The matcha flavor in the Matcha Su is quite strong. The filling's texture is like lotus seed paste, but with a matcha flavor. For the Taro Su, I don't think it has a very distinct taro flavor, but it's delicious. It's slightly sweeter than the Matcha Su, around level 6 sweetness. This one is a relatively pure red bean paste flavor pastry, without too many other mixed flavors. Sweetness is moderate, level 5. The outer skin is similar to the Zao Hua Su, resembling a biscuit but not as dry. Friends who love red bean paste should definitely take this home. The red bean paste filling inside is also full and substantial. This is a corner of the box I bought for my parents last year. Haven't bought this year's yet; will update everyone after I do~ Okay, that's all for today's share. Hope this article can give those who see it some reference. Title: Zhou Li from Weihai Central Hospital: Twenty Years of Dedication to Epilepsy Diagnosis and Treatment, Using Professionalism and Compassion to Dispel Prejudice
Content: In the consultation room of Zhou Li, Deputy Director of the First Ward of the Department of Neurology and Chief Physician at Weihai Central Hospital, there is always a sense of reassurance that makes people shed their anxiety. Facing patients and their families who are filled with apprehension and hope, she conducts inquiries, examinations, and explains the condition. Her speech is not fast, but carries a certainty that can soothe people. This certainty stems from the accumulation of over twenty years of clinical experience.
In 2000, Zhou Li began her medical career. The field of neurology is vast and profound. After solidifying her foundation in cerebrovascular diseases, she turned her attention to the more challenging specialty of epilepsy. To pursue more advanced medical knowledge, she went to Beijing twice for further training at Peking Union Medical College Hospital, focusing on cerebrovascular diseases and epilepsy respectively. The training experience not only enhanced her diagnostic and treatment skills but also shaped her rigorous and practical clinical thinking. "At Union Hospital, you see the most complex cases in the country. It teaches you to always broaden your thinking and not overlook any clues."
The training experience played a key role in her later handling of complex conditions. Zhou Li told reporters about one morning in 2017 when an elderly patient nearly 80 years old was admitted with a first episode of consciousness disorder. The condition seemed stable but suddenly deteriorated in the early morning, with severe convulsions and respiratory failure, leaving the patient's life hanging by a thread. Zhou Li quickly reviewed the patient's head MRI images and discovered a subtle abnormal signal. "Considering the critical condition, I highly suspected it was a type of autoimmune encephalitis that was considered 'rare' at the time." The standard treatment for this disease involves high-dose hormones and expensive immunoglobulin. Relying on the confidence gained from similar cases she had seen at Peking Union Medical College Hospital, Zhou Li organized rescue efforts while communicating deeply with the family, ultimately securing the treatment opportunity. Simultaneously, she urgently activated the hospital's remote consultation platform to connect with experts from Peking Union Medical College Hospital, receiving full affirmation of the treatment plan. The next day, the patient's condition turned around. "The sense of achievement from pulling a patient back from the brink of death is indescribable." This successful case further solidified her determination to root advanced diagnosis and treatment concepts locally in Weihai.
In 2016, Zhou Li, as a visiting scholar selected by the Shandong Provincial Health Department, went to Germany for academic exchange. The overseas trip opened her international perspective. After returning, she took the lead in establishing a specialized epilepsy outpatient clinic in the Weihai area. "The original intention was simple: I felt the diagnosis and treatment of this disease needed to be more standardized, and there were too many misconceptions among the public." The establishment of the outpatient clinic was like sowing a seed. In 2020, this seed grew into a more professional platform – the First Ward of the Department of Neurology, with epilepsy and dizziness as its sub-specialty features, was officially re-established.
"Epilepsy is the second most common disease in neurology after cerebrovascular diseases, but it is very special," Zhou Li said. Many people's impression of epilepsy still remains at the scenes from movies and TV dramas: 'suddenly collapsing, foaming at the mouth, and convulsing limbs.' But in her view, the 'face' of epilepsy is ever-changing. "Some people walk on the road and only come to their senses after crossing the traffic light; some students suddenly space out in class, and the teacher thinks they are daydreaming, but it might actually be an epileptic seizure." The complexity and diversity of this disease are precisely why it is easily misdiagnosed or missed.
In Zhou Li's view, epilepsy is by no means an isolated 'convulsion' symptom; behind it may lie various causes such as structural, infectious, immune, metabolic, genetic factors, like an iceberg. "Our work is not only to control the superficial 'seizures' but also to dive underwater to explore the entire iceberg and find the root cause." This also means her work extends far beyond the outpatient clinic and wards; consultation requests from various departments throughout the hospital often come unexpectedly. "Refractory status epilepticus in the ICU, seizures in postoperative patients in the oncology department, epilepsy during pregnancy encountered in obstetrics, even patients suddenly convulsing in the dialysis room... What we need is teamwork." She metaphorically compared neurologists to 'detectives,' who need to rely on professional knowledge and experience to find the truth for patients among various clues.
Besides the complexity of the causes, what worries Zhou Li the most is the heavy social pressure borne by epilepsy patients and their families. "The biggest enemy of this disease is sometimes not the disease itself, but misunderstanding, discrimination, and low self-esteem." Therefore, her consultation room is also a classroom for transmitting confidence and science. She pays special attention to two special groups: women of childbearing age and students.
"For young women, our treatment must have long-term planning, considering the effects of medication on the fetus, and guiding them to plan pregnancies and breastfeed safely." Zhou Li often works side by side with obstetrics colleagues. When former patients specially come to share the good news of holding a healthy baby, or even happily discuss plans for a 'second child,' those are the moments she feels most gratified. "At such times, you feel all the effort is worth it."
For student patients, she invests even more effort. "Epilepsy comorbidities, such as anxiety, depression, and cognitive impairment, need particular attention in children. Our goal is not only to control seizures but also to protect their brain function, maintain their mental health, and give them the courage and opportunity to study, advance in school, and find employment normally." Zhou Li once spent nearly two years carefully guiding a teenager with medication and providing continuous encouragement. Eventually, the child successfully gained admission to their ideal university. The child's father, when calling Zhou Li to report the good news, could not hide his choked voice due to excitement: "We never thought our child could still have a day of entering university. We always thought this disease would ruin his life..." Zhou Li responded: "What we need to do is to make society and parents believe that epilepsy patients can also have a bright future."
This philosophy of 'treating the person as well as the illness' also runs through her teaching work. She has served as the Teaching Director of the Neurology Resident Training Base for many years, shouldering the important task of cultivating a new generation of doctors. She generously imparts her rich clinical experience and rigorous thinking模式. In 2017, she won the second prize in the Qingdao University Medical Department Teaching Ward Round Competition, which is a vivid reflection of her teaching and learning mutually and striving for excellence.
Now, she holds multiple positions such as Council Member of the Shandong Anti-Epilepsy Association, Member of the Epilepsy Group of the Neurology Branch of the Shandong Medical Association, and Member of the Professional Committee on Epilepsy and Paroxysmal Diseases of the Shandong Medical Doctor Association, working on broader platforms to improve the level of regional epilepsy diagnosis and treatment.
Zhou Li深知 that the power of the medical team alone is limited. Every year on "June 28 International Epilepsy Care Day," she consistently organizes or participates in public welfare free clinics and popular science lectures. Going to the countryside, entering communities, and holding lectures, she face-to-face educates the public about epilepsy first aid knowledge, calls for the elimination of discrimination, and emphasizes the importance of standardized diagnosis and treatment. "This is a work of 'clarifying the source,' with profound significance. More understanding from society means more space for patients."
Looking to the future, Zhou Li has an ideal vision in mind – building an epilepsy diagnosis and treatment center integrating multiple disciplines such as neurology, electrophysiology, neurosurgery, and pediatrics. "Currently, about 30% of patients still have drug-resistant epilepsy. They need more comprehensive treatment plans like surgery. This is the direction our team is striving for. Although there are many difficulties, we must fight for it."
"Epilepsy, on one hand, requires emergency rescue, and on the other hand, needs chronic disease management, just like hypertension and diabetes, requiring scientific treatment. Patients need confidence, family members need attentiveness, and the public needs more understanding and tolerance." This might be the best footnote for all her efforts – using professional pursuit to dispel the fog of disease and using warm care to illuminate the path forward for patients. In the coastal city of Weihai, Zhou Li and the team she leads are quietly lighting lamps of hope for countless epilepsy patients and families. (Correspondent Wang Qian)

Title: Causes of Migraine and Acupuncture Treatment Methods. Content: Headache is a common disease clinically. Migraine accounts for a considerable number in acupuncture outpatient clinics. During severe attacks, it can seriously affect patients' work and study. Therefore, in acupuncture outpatient clinics, how to improve the therapeutic effect of this disease has important clinical significance. Now combining literature, I will share my personal experience, attempting to clarify from a clinical perspective the causes and classification of migraine, as well as the rules of acupuncture treatment. Theoretical Discussion: Classical literature has made concise and comprehensive records on the causes and treatment of this condition. The Ling Shu Jue Bing Pian states: For half-cold headache of the head, first take Hand Shaoyang and Yangming, then take Foot Shaoyang and Yangming. Through rich clinical practice, physicians of successive generations have gained more specific understanding of this condition. Through clinical observation combined with literature records, we believe that migraine, in addition to having the common nature of general headaches, has many characteristics in terms of etiology, pathology, and treatment. (1) Etiology: The occurrence of this disease has significant internal causes. Since the head is the meeting place of all yang, where essence rises and descends, externally protected by hair, flesh, tendons, and bones, and internally warmed by clear yang, if the exterior is solid and the interior is full, various evils cannot invade upward. It must wait until the exterior defense fails or clear yang is blocked before various evils can invade. Specifically, there are those where wind evil takes advantage of deficiency to lodge in Shaoyang, mostly belonging to wind-cold; those where yang qi is blocked and Shaoyang meridians are不通, mostly belonging to spleen deficiency with damp excess; and those where liver-gallbladder wind-heat with phlegm rebels upward, mostly belonging to phlegm-fire. In reality, it is wind, phlegm, and fire combining to cause disease. In terms of external causes, wind-cold among the six excesses is most commonly seen, but clinically, wind-cold is the external cause and the condition. The basis for disease onset remains the internal cause. Just as the Su Wen Sheng Qi Tong Tian Lun states... when the flesh and interstices are closed and solid, even strong winds and severe toxins cannot cause harm. This appropriately reflects the objective role of internal and external causes in the occurrence and development of this disease. (2) Classification: We have classified this disease based on clinical syndrome differentiation. (1) External Wind Type: External wind is an important factor in the occurrence of this disease. According to the Su Wen Feng Lun Pian records: Wind is good at moving and changes frequently... therefore wind is the leader of all diseases. Its evil enters through the shu points, travels along the meridians upward, or merges into the Shaoyang meridian, causing meridian stagnation on one side of the head, resulting in migraine. Therefore, in medical history, being exposed to wind while sleeping at night or sweating in the wind are important bases for classifying this type. In terms of symptoms, there is persistent distending pain on one side of the head, worsening with wind-cold exposure, more severe pain and tension at the Fengchi acupoint, or accompanied by cough, stiff neck with aversion to cold, and pain in all joints, with a floating and wiry pulse. In terms of pathology, it is wind evil lodging in the collaterals and meridian blockage; in treatment, use the method of dispersing wind and unblocking meridians. (2) Excess Heat Type: Liver-gallbladder stagnation heat is the basic cause of this disease onset. The liver belongs to wind-wood, stores the soul, its emotion is anger, and it governs free flow. If emotions are unfulfilled, liver qi stagnates, and over time transforms into fire generating wind. In terms of symptoms, there is throbbing pain in the side of the head, pain like splitting, red face and eyes, irritable temperament, red tongue with greasy coating, and a wiry and forceful pulse. In terms of pathology, it is liver-gallbladder blazing heat rebelling upward to the head and eyes, and in severe cases liver-gallbladder fire blazing generating wind. Treatment mostly uses the method of calming the liver and draining fire. The prognosis is worse than the previous type, with a longer treatment process. Those with concurrent external wind have good short-term effects but are also prone to relapse. (3) Damp-Phlegm Type: Spleen-stomach weakness is the basic cause of this disease onset. Liver-wood overwhelming earth with phlegm rebelling upward is an important condition for this disease onset. In terms of symptoms, there is dull pain in the side of the head, distention and oppression like being wrapped, often accompanied by chest and epigastric fullness and oppression, aversion to odors and reduced food intake, thick greasy tongue coating, and a wiry-slippery or slow-slippery pulse. In terms of pathology, it is spleen-stomach weakness, with central qi unable to transform and transport water and grains, damp-phlegm obstructing the middle burner, liver-wood overwhelming earth, carrying phlegm upward along the Shaoyang meridian, or even carrying triple burner deficient fire floating upward to cause migraine. Treatment should simultaneously strengthen the spleen and transform phlegm, and calm the liver and descend rebellion. In terms of prognosis, the selection and coordination of methods to strengthen the spleen and calm the liver have important significance for the treatment course and effect of this disease. When used appropriately, complete recovery can be achieved. But this type of migraine is relatively complex and difficult to achieve rapid results. (3) General Treatment Description: On the basis of following general treatment principles, fully according to the condition, flexible syndrome differentiation and treatment were carried out. Below is a discussion from three aspects: treatment acupoints, the use of bloodletting, and acupuncture techniques. (1) Point Selection and Formulation: We take unblocking meridians and activating collaterals, and dispersing wind and relieving pain as the basic formulation for treating all types. Select Sizhukong penetrating to Shuaigu, Hegu, Lieque, and Zulinqi, supplemented with Fengchi, Quchi, and Juegu as one group. The points in this group have the effect of unblocking the Foot Shaoyang meridian and dispersing wind to relieve pain. In terms of formulation meaning, Sizhukong is where the Foot Shaoyang meridian qi emanates and is also the terminal point of the Hand Shaoyang meridian. The point itself can treat migraine; penetrating along the skin to Shuaigu further strengthens the unblocking of the Hand and Foot Shaoyang meridians. This is because Shuaigu is not only a point of the Foot Shaoyang meridian, treating migraine, but it is also the meeting point of the Foot Shaoyang and Foot Taiyang meridians, having the effect of dispersing Shaoyang wind-heat and allowing it to reach the exterior through the Taiyang meridian. Therefore, Sizhukong penetrating to Shuaigu is the main point for dispersing wind-heat in the Shaoyang meridian and is an effective acupoint for treating all migraines. In all our cases, over 90% of cases have used this point, and all have achieved quite good results. Hegu and Lieque: Hegu is the yuan point of Hand Yangming, with extensive therapeutic effects and sedative and pain-relieving properties. Lieque is the luo point of Hand Taiyin. According to the Ma Danyang Heavenly Star Twelve Points Treating Miscellaneous Diseases Song: Lieque is good at treating偏头患. Paired with Hegu, it has the significance of yuan-luo point pairing. Zulinqi is the shu point of the Foot Shaoyang gallbladder meridian, where the gallbladder meridian pours into. According to five-shu theory, it is a shu-wood point nature. It has a good effect on draining Shaoyang wind-heat. Because it is far from the disease site, it has the effect of guiding heat downward. The Lei Jing Tu Yi states: When wood is in excess, it is appropriate to drain here, making fire deficient so wood naturally calms, which also confirms the importance of this point in draining fire. The above formulation is not only suitable for external wind-type migraine but is also the basic formula for damp-phlegm type and excess heat type. The latter only needs appropriate supplementation with points to strengthen the spleen and transform phlegm and calm the liver and drain fire to achieve better therapeutic effects. For damp-phlegm type migraine, supplement with Xuanlu, Hanyan, Zhongwan, Zusanli or Fenglong, and Qihai (needle and moxibustion). Xuanlu and Hanyan are both located in the temporal region around the ear. In addition to their outstanding effects on migraine through meridian circulation, they are also meeting points of the Foot Shaoyang and Yangming meridians, having the dual effect of dredging the stomach and invigorating central yang. As for Zhongwan, it is the meeting point of the six fu organs, especially effective for warming and transforming damp-phlegm in the middle burner and descending upward-rushing stomach qi. Paired with Zusanli or Fenglong, the power to strengthen the spleen and transform phlegm becomes even more obvious. Qihai treats true qi insufficiency and heals all deficiencies and damages; strengthening lower burner qi transformation naturally supplements the middle earth.

Title: The Joke About a Girlfriend Having a 40°C Fever Content: The joke about a girlfriend having a 40°C fever. A woman in Hangzhou had an unexplained fever for over a week. She took various medicines but didn't get better, with the highest fever reaching 40.6°C. She even experienced loss of consciousness. Infectious disease doctors investigated various causes and finally found a clue from a 'mark' on her body. Ms. Tang, nearly 50 years old, lives in a suburban county of Hangzhou. More than half a month ago, she inexplicably developed a high fever. Thinking it was an ordinary cold or something similar, she planned to take some medicine herself. Recently, she has been unwell, experiencing chills and high fever. She originally thought it was due to catching a chill from the sudden temperature drop. Aunt Xu took cold medicine at home for a few days, but the effect was mediocre. She had recurrent fever for three consecutive days; when the fever was high, it once reached 40 degrees Celsius. She even experienced nausea and vomiting, and her condition felt increasingly wrong. My girlfriend caught a cold and had a fever. I said I would buy her antipyretic medicine, but she refused to take it. I said, then let's get a fever-reducing injection, but she refused that too. Having no other ideas, I said, then I'll get you an ice pack and alcohol for physical cooling. She suddenly got furious: 'Get lost! I've been hoping for a long time to have a fever to burn some fat, and you insist on reducing my fever. What kind of mentality is that? How can you not wish well for others?! 1. Hahaha, you understand the principle of reducing fever! 2. Just say it, dare you still have a fever like this? 3. Be careful, if the fever goes down, he won't let you sleep holding him anymore because he won't be afraid of the cold. 4. Having you is simply your boyfriend's blessing! 5. Harbin has this function too? Do the people of Harbin know about it themselves? 6. How can you bear to hurt the loving heart of someone who is rushing towards you with a passionate 40 degrees? 7. I clearly remember the night my fever reached 40 degrees, my consciousness gradually blurred. So, what exactly does a person experience in the 30 seconds before death? According to accounts from over 150 near-death experiencers, 'out-of-body experiences' are the first thing they felt when near death. Many truly felt their consciousness float out of their bodies, looking down at their own bodies from the ceiling. They also gained extrasensory perception while losing their sense of time.'

Title: Will high-rise residential communities turn into slums? Content: It depends. I live in an old community in Beijing's North Fourth Ring Road, but it's managed by our unit's internal property service. In 2021, the old community renovation replaced everything that could be replaced: elevators, windows, community roads, landscaping, external insulation, indoor water supply and drainage, electrical circuits, heating, and gas. They even renovated kitchens and bathrooms for some elderly residents whose homes hadn't been refurbished in years, retiling, replacing toilets, and gas stoves - essentially a full renovation. The key point is that all this didn't cost a penny. Aside from frequent work stoppages during the pandemic, the long duration, and some inconvenience to daily life, it was really cost-effective. The renovated community actually looks newer than before. On the flip side: My father-in-law lives in a community built around 2010 in a county town in Hunan province. It was considered quite good locally at the time, but a few years ago, because they couldn't collect enough property fees, the property management company abandoned their duties. You can see it deteriorating. Fortunately, it's not a high-rise, so it's still livable, but if you wanted to sell, it would be hard to find a buyer now.

Title: Which is better, hourly work or contract work? Content: Hourly work and contract work each have their advantages, and which one is better depends on the specific situation. I. Advantages of hourly work Hourly work is usually billed based on the actual workload, making the measurement of work and compensation more direct. This method is more beneficial for skilled workers because they can complete tasks quickly based on their individual skill levels. At the same time, hourly work offers higher flexibility on projects, allowing workers to adjust their work plans and progress at any time. Additionally, with hourly work, employers can flexibly increase or decrease personnel based on project progress to control costs. II. Advantages of contract work Contract work focuses more on the completion of the entire project. The contractor is typically responsible for the organization and management of the whole project, including aspects such as personnel allocation and material procurement. This method is more suitable for large projects or work requiring complex coordination. Contract work can make things easier for the employer because all matters are handled by the contractor, and the employer only needs to focus on the final outcome of the project. Meanwhile, contractors usually have some bargaining power and can secure better prices for the employer in areas like material procurement. III. Factors to consider when choosing which method to use 1. Project scale: Small projects or simple tasks may be more suitable for hourly work, while large, complex projects require the comprehensive management of contract work. 2. Skill requirements: If the task requires specific skills or proficiency, hourly work might better reflect individual value. 3. Cost control: For employers, contract work may help control overall costs better, while hourly work is more flexible, allowing adjustments to manpower and expenses based on progress and needs. 4. Risk and uncertainty: In some situations, such as unstable material supply or frequent changes in project requirements, the hourly work method might be more稳妥 (prudent/secure). IV. Summary Hourly work and contract work each have their applicable scenarios and advantages. The choice depends on factors like the specific needs of the project, individual skills, and resources. In practice, adjustments can be made flexibly based on project progress and needs. Regardless of the chosen method, it is essential to ensure that the contract is clear and the rights and interests of both parties are protected.

Title: The largest-scale sandstorm in the north 'rages', affecting 15 provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities. Why have sandstorm weather conditions been so frequent in the north this year? Content: The following is personal understanding and does not represent the actual situation. I first became aware of Bai Jin in 2008, and the spring of 2009 was my first encounter with a sandstorm. When I stepped out of the building, the cars on the roadside were completely covered in yellow sand and soil. Walking on the road, I could clearly feel the sand and dust flying into my mouth, and I've remembered it ever since. Roughly between 2015 and 2019, sandstorm days significantly decreased. For several years, there weren't even severe sandstorm days after winter. Where did the sand go? They said protective forests were strengthened in the west and north, blocking it all outside. Along with the story of sandstorm control, there was also smog. When the wind didn't blow in winter, smog came. During this period, opening an APP to check air quality, showing 200+ was normal, and 500 was within reach. Why 500? Because 500 was the upper limit; anything higher wasn't displayed. For example, today it's 500. During the three years of the pandemic, everyone's focus wasn't on blue skies and white clouds, but on whether we could go out. In April 2020, we were staying at home; in April 2021, staying at home; in April 2022, coincidentally, still staying at home. This year is the first year that everyone has truly returned to normal order. Paying attention to the weather is the best proof that we have returned to normal life.

Title: External hard drive beeps when plugged into computer, device not displayed. Content: This is caused by the currently USB-connected device not functioning properly. Here are the specific troubleshooting solutions: 1. First, locate the "Computer" icon on the desktop, right-click on the Computer icon. 2. In the context menu that appears, select the "Manage" menu item to open the Computer Management page. 3. After opening the Computer Management page, double-click the "Device Manager" option on the left side of the page to open the Device Manager page. 4. In the list of devices that appears, find the "Universal Serial Bus controllers" option, double-click to expand the list, and select the "USB Root Hub" menu. 5. Next, in the context menu that appears, select the "Uninstall device" option. 6. Then, in the dialog box that appears, click the "Uninstall" menu button to uninstall the device currently connected to the USB port. 7. Move the mouse pointer to the top, right-click or press the right-click menu key on the keyboard, and select the "Scan for hardware changes" option from the expanded menu. 8. Next, Windows will rescan the devices connected to the USB ports and recognize them, while relevant device information will be displayed in the lower right corner of the desktop. 9. At this point, you can reinsert the external hard drive into the computer's USB port. You should now see the "USB Mass Storage Device" module in the Device Manager list. 10. Finally, wait for the Windows system to automatically install the driver for the hard drive device. Once the driver installation is complete, the external hard drive device will be recognized normally and can be accessed using Windows Explorer.

Title: Spending over 20,000 yuan to buy a 'fourth-hand car' at Nanchang 'YouChuang', he suspects it was in a major accident. Content: Spending over 20,000 yuan to buy a 'fourth-hand car' at Nanchang 'YouChuang', he suspects it was in a major accident. Source｜Urban Scene Original. Unauthorized reproduction prohibited. In March of this year, Mr. Fu purchased a used Buick at the 'YouChuang Used Car' store on Chenghu Middle Road, Nanchang County, Nanchang City, Jiangxi Province. Not long ago, he decided to sell the car. However, during the vehicle inspection, he discovered many problems with the car. The red Buick in the picture above is the one Mr. Fu bought for 24,900 yuan. He said that the shop owner told him at the time that the car had no major issues. Consumer Mr. Fu: I planned to sell it, but when it went for evaluation and inspection, they found the car had been cut, the doors were replaced, it definitely had an accident, including the engine being removed, the hood replaced, all with non-original parts. If you had told me, it would have been fine, a willing buyer and a willing seller. Mr. Fu said this Buick was first registered on April 23, 2009, and had traveled a total of 130,000 kilometers. It had undergone three previous ownership transfers, meaning Mr. Fu was the fourth owner. During this time, whether the car had been in a major traffic accident was unknown to Mr. Fu. Consumer Mr. Fu: I came to the store on the 6th, and he admitted it was an accident car. I asked why he didn't tell me when I bought it. He said he didn't know and hadn't inspected the car carefully. You have an obligation to tell me these things; it's the最基本 (most basic) thing you as a car dealer should do. He also said that's how they sell cars everywhere in Nanchang. I really don't understand. If it didn't affect my ability to sell it normally, I wouldn't have come to him. To verify the situation, on the morning of August 7th, a reporter went to 'YouChuang Used Car' on Chenghu Middle Road, Nanchang County. Regarding the car condition described by Mr. Fu, the shop owner, Mr. Li, stated that it cannot prove the car was in a major accident. YouChuang Used Car Owner Mr. Li: When I sold the car, I told him the car had no major accident, significant accident, fire, or flood damage. There might be some scratches and dings, it's a 13-year-old car after all. He said the sill was cut, is that a frame? Replacing a door, is that a major accident? Isn't that normal? Mr. Li also said the current used car market is not good, and加上 (plus) this car has obvious flaws, so if traded again, the price would definitely be heavily discounted. However, he is willing to help Mr. Fu sell the car for free, regardless of the price, without charging an中介费 (agency fee). YouChuang Used Car Owner Mr. Li: He initially asked me to buy it back. I told him if a customer comes, I'll connect you, you sit here and watch him transfer the money, we won't take a penny. He said no, he must have 20,000 yuan to buy it back. How is buying it back different from selling it here for us? We have no money, what do we use to buy it back? I'm already deep in debt. Consumer Mr. Fu: Then tell me, is it an accident car or not? YouChuang Used Car Owner Mr. Li: I said it's not an accident car, not a major accident car. If you get an appraisal saying it's a major accident, I'll take the car back.

Title: Is it important to rely on connections when looking for a job? Title: Yulin Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau Content: Yulin Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau October 06, 2024 Yulin Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau Yulin Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau# Administrative Penalty Decision (Changqing Oilfield Branch Company Third Oil Production Plant) Release Time: 2016-09-29 00:00 Source: Supervision Detachment Views: 2456 Administrative Penalty Decision of Yulin Municipal Environmental Protection Bureau Yu Huan Fa Zi [2016] No. 130 Changqing Oilfield Branch Company Third Oil Production Plant: Business License Registration Number: Legal Representative (Responsible Person): Shen Fuxiao Address: Jingbian County, Changqing Third Oil Production Plant I. Investigation Situation and Discovered Environmental Violation Facts, Evidence, and Statement/Defense (Hearing) and Adoption Situation This authority conducted an investigation of your unit on May 24, 2016, and found that your unit had implemented the following environmental violation: On-site inspection of your plant's affiliated Pan 28-46 expansion well, which was undergoing drilling operations, revealed a mud pit was constructed. The mud pit body was not constructed with brick-concrete and geomembrane for anti-seepage, but only used black plastic sheeting for anti-seepage. Some joints were damaged, and some mud leakage occurred. The above facts are supported by evidence such as on-site photos and on-site inspection records. Your unit's above action violated the provisions of Article 33, Paragraph 3 of the "Shaanxi Province Coal, Petroleum, and Natural Gas Development Environmental Protection Regulations". This authority informed your unit of the right to state your case and defend yourself via the "Administrative Penalty Prior Notice" (Yu Huan Fa Gao Zi [2016] No. 130) on August 25, 2016. II. Basis for Administrative Penalty, Type, Method of Performance, and Deadline According to the provisions of Article 45, Item 2 of the "Shaanxi Province Coal, Petroleum, and Natural Gas Development Environmental Protection Regulations", this authority decides to impose the following administrative penalties on your unit: 1. Order your plant to immediately correct the illegal acts; 2. Impose a fine of Twenty Thousand Yuan only. The fine must be paid to the designated bank and account within fifteen days from the date of receiving this penalty decision. If the fine is not paid by the deadline, this authority will, according to Article 51 of the "Administrative Penalty Law of the People's Republic of China", impose an additional fine of 3% of the fine amount per day. Receiving Bank: Chang'an Bank Yulin Branch Business Department Account Name: Shaanxi Province Non-Tax Revenue Pending Disbursement Account Account Number: 10180 60500 01224 10599 800136 III.途径和期限 for Applying for Administrative Reconsideration or Filing an Administrative Lawsuit If you disagree with this penalty decision, you may apply for reconsideration to the Shaanxi Provincial Department of Environmental Protection or the Yulin Municipal People's Government within sixty days from the date of receiving this penalty decision, or directly file a lawsuit with the Yuyang District People's Court within six months. Title: 2020 Qingdao Intermediate People's Court Judicial Recommendation (IV) Content: 2020 Qingdao Intermediate People's Court Judicial Recommendation (IV) July 22, 2020 Author: Lü Jiao Print Share to: Qingdao Intermediate People's Court Judicial Recommendation Letter China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission Qingdao Supervision Bureau: The difficulty in serving judicial documents is a significant factor restricting the improvement of financial trial efficiency. After reporting to and obtaining instructions from the Provincial High Court, our court recognizes the validity of 'the delivery address explicitly agreed upon by the parties in the financial loan contract' in financial loan contract cases. We have already recommended to banks and other financial institutions that when signing loan guarantee contracts with customers, they should also sign a separate 'Address Confirmation for Service of Process' with the customer. This requires the customer to provide a definite delivery address and explicitly inform them of the legal significance of the agreed address, the requirements for changing the delivery address, and the corresponding legal consequences. From the financial cases concluded by Qingdao courts in 2019, it can be seen that most financial cases, due to the explicit agreement on judicial delivery addresses in the contracts, have resolved the issue of 'extended trial periods caused by service by public announcement due to the defendant's whereabouts being unknown,' significantly improving trial efficiency. However, during trials, it was also discovered that in some cases, due to unclear content agreed upon in the 'Address Confirmation for Service of Process' or untrue address information, the agreed address could not be applied in judicial trials, leading to low success rates in serving the parties. To effectively improve service efficiency, after study, we specifically put forward the following three judicial recommendations: I. Improve the Authenticity and Effectiveness of Delivery Address Information The delivery address information agreed upon in the 'Address Confirmation for Service of Process' generally includes the party's mailing address, contact person, contact method, etc. When agreeing on the mailing address, financial institutions should verify whether the address written by the party is their actual place of business or an address indeed in use. The contact person should preferably be agreed as the party's responsible person or legal representative to avoid difficulties in service caused by the mobility of ordinary employees. The contact method should preferably be the contact person's mobile phone number; office phone numbers can serve as supplementary contact methods, avoiding reliance solely on office phones. By reviewing the delivery address information provided by the parties, the success rate of service can be effectively improved, ensuring the appearance rate of the parties in court. II. Clarify the Judicial Effect of the Delivery Address When informing the parties of the legal consequences of the agreed delivery address in the 'Address Confirmation for Service of Process,' use unambiguous language to explicitly state that the effect of this delivery address applies to the first instance, second instance, retrial, and enforcement procedures arising from litigation related to this contract dispute. Avoid using vague language to prevent textual ambiguity. III. Recommend Adding an Electronic Delivery Address Currently, courts at all levels in Qingdao have basically opened electronic service platforms. To improve service efficiency, when banks sign the 'Address Confirmation for Service of Process' with customers, in addition to agreeing on a postal delivery address, they can specify that the party agrees to use electronic service for delivering legal documents during litigation. Electronic service is deemed effective when the sender's device shows a successful send, and explicitly agree on the email address, fax number, mobile phone number, etc., that the party will use to receive litigation documents. Please study the above recommendations and inform our court of the processing results within thirty days by letter.
