Title: About Beidou Navigation Terminal Issues Content: 1. Beidou satellite navigation terminals are also divided into military and civilian use. Military terminals can capture and calculate more precise codes, thereby obtaining high-precision navigation and positioning services. May I ask, should this military signal be encrypted? Do military terminals need to contain a decryption program? Who produces them? Do manufacturers producing terminals need to know the key to produce chip modules and the like? If so, wouldn't this leak military secrets? Even if central state-owned military enterprises produce them, shouldn't this decryption algorithm be top secret? Once everyone knows this algorithm, what's the point of military use? Am I misunderstanding something? 2. According to information, measurement-type Beidou terminal receivers can be used for measurement activities. When a vehicle passes over a bridge, it causes deformation of the bridge. Beidou terminals can detect even millimeter-level deformations, providing measurement data for relevant personnel. - What is the principle behind this? Since it can detect such small changes with such high precision, why is the published navigation and positioning accuracy only within 10 meters? Aren't they the same? 1. Military products can never be completely separated from civilian products 100%. There are no walls that don't leak; any secret will eventually be revealed, it's just a matter of a longer保密期. Radio navigation signals are difficult to crack and utilize, but they are particularly easy to干扰. In modern warfare,争夺电磁权 is the first priority, followed by air superiority. GPS was developed and used by the US military. Now GPS navigators are being sold even at street stalls, hasn't that affected the US military's use? 2. I don't know where you read that information, but it seems very unscientific. When a vehicle passes over a bridge, it确实产生变形, but there are also errors caused by factors like earth rotation\seismic activity\ground noise\vehicle suspension systems\wind, etc. For fixed-point surveying, achieving centimeter-level accuracy is already impressive. I think it sounds more like exaggerated宣传. Sharing a personal opinion, Beidou navigation terminals have different guiding standards for military and civilian applications in different fields. The algorithms and secrets involved in different standards are not the same. Therefore, not just anyone can make a Beidou terminal; you first need to obtain the production standard, and during the acquisition process, relevant departments conduct audits. Public Beidou standards are available for everyone to apply for, while some special-purpose ones require certain conditions. Secondly, the core reason millimeter-level deformation monitoring of bridges can be achieved is due to the installation of ground-based augmentation equipment at fixed locations. All parameters at a fixed point are unique, and this is combined with the Beidou system to achieve the monitoring. Navigation, however, generally occurs in a moving state where parameters are constantly changing, so achieving millimeter-level navigation is technically very difficult. However, technological breakthroughs have now enabled centimeter-level accuracy. If you want to learn more, you can follow Wuhan Excan Beidou Space-Time Technology Co., Ltd., which has seventeen years of experience in Beidou + intelligent location services.

Title: Does it really happen in hospitals that "a grandson unplugs his grandmother's ventilator to charge his phone"? Content: It does happen. After all, a ventilator also uses a standard 10A three-pin plug, compatible with any ordinary power strip. There's no unified shape standard across manufacturers, so they come in all sorts of shapes, just like everyday three-pin plugs - overall quite ordinary and nothing special. Even doctors unplugging the wrong one is a daily occurrence. I often struggle to figure out which plug in a row is for the bed, which for the pump, and which for the ventilator... The fool-proofing for ventilators is mainly in the machine itself. If you unplug the ventilator's power cord, the device has a backup power supply and a power failure alarm. The ventilator's shrill alarm after a power cut can summon doctors from the neighboring ward... The key point is, even as an experienced ICU doctor who has seen many older models, I find it very difficult to stop the ventilator's power failure alarm immediately...

Title: China Net Education: [Toddler Drowns for Over 20 Seconds in Swimming Lesson, Safety Coach Less Than 3 Meters Away Fails to Notice, Kindergarten Denies Responsibility] Recently, in Zhongxiang, Hubei. During a swimming lesson at a kindergarten, a toddler allegedly overturned their life ring and drowned for over 20 seconds before the safety coach was alerted and noticed. Surveillance video shows the toddler's life ring flipped over, causing them to fall into the water headfirst. The safety coach was looking in the toddler's direction but failed to detect any abnormality. It wasn't until a woman alerted the safety coach that the toddler was hurriedly lifted out of the water. Approximately 23 seconds passed from falling in to being rescued. The toddler's father stated that after the incident, when reviewing the surveillance footage at the school, they discovered this scene. The kindergarten's conclusion was that the man in the video was temporarily hired and had no teaching qualifications. Currently, the school has not provided any further explanation.

Title: The Four Most Unreliable Majors in University, 80% of Students Admitted Through Adjustment, Graduates Either Face Unemployment or Change Careers
Content: When filling out college applications, the most difficult part is choosing a major. If you don't choose a major well, you basically fall into a pit. Some majors are very deceptive, and often candidates get tricked. Today, I will introduce the four most unreliable majors in university. 80% of the students are admitted through major adjustment, and upon graduation, they either face unemployment or change careers.
The first major is Hotel Management. This major is a complete pit. The content learned is very vague. It's called studying hotel management, but hotels rarely hire graduates from this major. You could say it's a case of 'a hero with no place to display his prowess'. Currently, not many universities offer this major, and even so, many universities are phasing it out, which shows how problematic this major is.
The second major is Tourism Management. The对口工作 for this major after graduation is being a tour guide. However, being a tour guide is a profession with a very low entry barrier; it requires eloquence, not necessarily a degree. So, studying Tourism Management doesn't guarantee you can be a tour guide. In fact, many students who study this major end up changing careers, rendering their studies almost useless.
The third major is E-commerce. This is a major that universities started offering one after another after seeing the rise of e-commerce, with the goal of cultivating e-commerce talents. But if you look carefully at those around you who are engaged in e-commerce, how many of them graduated from this major? Very few, you could say. Then look at those e-commerce companies, how many students from this major do they hire every year? Also very few. The things learned in this major are very miscellaneous; it's a jack-of-all-trades major. After graduation, you have no particular advantage in e-commerce, and it's not a对口专业 for other jobs either. It can be said to be very awkward.
The fourth major is History. For the History major, students are basically admitted through adjustment. The things learned are very useful and interesting, but the employment situation is hard to describe. Think carefully, which units need history majors? Museums? History research institutes? These are very hard to get into. Taking the civil service exam? The positions available for History majors are few and far between. It can be said that for the History major, most students have to change careers after graduation. Those unwilling to change careers basically end up staying at home.
Final words: The above four majors are rarely actively applied for by candidates. In a class, basically over 80% of the students are admitted through adjustment. These students choose these majors out of helplessness, and in the end, these majors end up disappointing these students. For this year's college entrance exam candidates and their parents, unless absolutely necessary, do not actively apply for these majors. If you are unfortunately adjusted into one of these majors, you can actively seek to change your major within the university. If that's not possible, you can prepare for postgraduate entrance exams to change your field. What are your thoughts on these majors?

Title: How to avoid eating cooking oil transported by coal trucks? Content: 1. Don't buy oil in large plastic buckets. 2. Don't buy packaged foods with vegetable oil in the ingredient list or unpackaged foods from wet markets. 3. When eating noodles, hot pot, etc., don't be tempted to add chili, sauces, or Lao Gan Ma. 4. Try to avoid eating out, especially oily foods (pre-made dishes are the most dangerous). 5. Try to eat out less often and eat fewer processed foods; cook at home instead. 6. Raise your own pigs and render lard to eat.

Title: After joining a university, our salary was arbitrarily reduced to 1900. Can I file for labor arbitration? Content: Although your description says a lot, the overall impression it gives is that several basic issues are confusing and unclear. First, your previous take-home pay after deducting the five social insurances and two housing funds was 2400 yuan, so your basic salary was definitely not 2400 yuan. What was it exactly? You didn't say. Second, you say the university arbitrarily reduced your basic salary to 1900 yuan, and you actually received 1900 yuan. Does that mean the university is no longer paying the five social insurances and two housing funds for you? Clearly, the basic salary and your take-home pay after deductions are two different concepts. Third, how long has the salary reduction been in effect? If you did not raise an objection in the first month of the reduction, and it has continued for several months, this is equivalent to you having effectively accepted the university's change to the contractually agreed basic salary. You can protect your rights in the following ways: First, resign under duress on the grounds that the university illegally reduced your salary. You can claim certain economic compensation. Second, you can claim last year's overtime pay, but objectively speaking, it will be difficult for you to provide complete evidence of overtime work. It is recommended that you do not resign voluntarily, because if you resign voluntarily: First, you will not be eligible for corresponding severance compensation. Second, if you cannot find a job immediately, you will also lose your eligibility for unemployment insurance benefits.

Title: Same Road Section, Same Time Period, Same Reason: Man Gets Caught Twice by the Same Traffic Policeman! Content: Two years ago, the man was caught for drunk driving by Jimei traffic police and had his driver's license revoked. Now, without a license, he was caught again for drunk driving on the same road section. Recently, Jimei traffic police encountered such a driver during a night check, and he will face legal punishment. Around 21:00 on the 14th, Huang Haiyong, a police officer from the Houxi Squadron of the Jimei Public Security Bureau Traffic Police Brigade, was conducting a drunk driving enforcement operation on Section Suying of National Highway 324 in his jurisdiction. During a routine check of the rider of the ordinary two-wheeled motorcycle with license plate Min DTL*, Huang Haiyong noticed the smell of alcohol on the rider. Using a breathalyzer, an on-site alcohol test was conducted, revealing an alcohol content of 90mg/100ml in his body, constituting the traffic violation of driving a motor vehicle while intoxicated. Huang Haiyong asked him to produce his driver's license, but the rider could not provide it. After questioning, the rider, surnamed Lian, confessed that he had been caught for drunk driving once before in 2021, and his license was revoked at that time. At this point, Huang Haiyong also found the driver somewhat familiar. Upon checking, it was discovered that this driver had been caught driving the same vehicle, during the same time period, on the same road section. Since his last drunk driving incident where his license was revoked, Lian's driver's license status remained revoked. Huang Haiyong conducted on-site safety education for Lian, explaining the dangers of drunk driving and the legal consequences of a second offense. Lian admitted to his violation. Currently, the case is under further investigation. Once a drunk driving offense is recorded, it remains permanently in the traffic police information system. If a driver's license is reinstated after re-education, any subsequent drunk driving offense, regardless of when or where it occurs, even after one or two years or longer, will be considered a 'second offense'. (Xiamen Daily reporter Xue Yao, correspondent Fu Bangshu)

Title: If you can't accomplish these 5 things in land expropriation and demolition, how can you get high compensation? Content: Is land expropriation and demolition legal? The first thing to check is whether there is a legal basis. Many affected parties see documents like the 'Notice of House Demolition,' 'A Letter to the Affected Residents,' or 'Meeting Minutes Issued by the Local Government' and assume the expropriation is lawful, but that's not necessarily true. Legal land expropriation and demolition must follow strict legal procedures. After determining the legality of the demolition, we must also know our corresponding rights at each stage. 01. Verify the Approval Content Land expropriation and demolition first require local government application, followed by approval from the State Council or provincial government. Legal Provision: Article 45 of the Land Administration Law: Expropriation of the following land requires State Council approval: (1) Basic farmland; (2) Cultivated land exceeding 35 hectares, excluding basic farmland; (3) Other land exceeding 70 hectares. Expropriation of land not covered above requires approval from the provincial, autonomous region, or municipal government, and must be filed with the State Council. Typical Case: In practice, we often encounter situations where the demolishing party, to simplify procedures, save costs, lower approval thresholds, or for other reasons, applies to the provincial government to expropriate 100 mu of land, but ends up using the approval for 100 mu to occupy 1000 mu of farmers' land. If affected persons do not investigate and verify, they won't know about these issues, ultimately leading to failure to exercise their rights, loss of land, and inadequate compensation. Lawyer's Advice: Government land expropriation must have an application before approval. The expropriation approval document should be public. Accurately understand the expropriation information, verify the purpose of the expropriation (is it for public projects?), check if the applied project matches the actual construction project, and if the applied area matches the actual expropriation scope. If the reality differs from the approved materials, the government might be illegally expropriating more land than approved. 02. Confirm the Survey Results Legal Provision: 'Guiding Opinions on Improving the Land Expropriation Compensation and Resettlement System': Before legal approval of expropriation, the local land and resources department must inform the affected rural collective economic organizations and households in writing about the intended land use, location, compensation standards, and resettlement methods. The local land and resources department should survey the land ownership, type, area, and the ownership, type, and quantity of above-ground attachments. The survey results must be confirmed jointly by the affected rural collective economic organizations, households, and owners of the attachments. Typical Case: In practice, affected persons might have seen government staff who came to their homes for surveys, measured the house and land, but did not have them sign for confirmation. Only when the compensation details or assessment report arrive do they find the measured area is much smaller than actual, leading to significantly low compensation. Lawyer's Opinion: This material requires joint confirmation and signature by the local government and the affected residents. After the expropriation notice, any attachments or crops planted, built, or added抢栽,抢种,抢建 on the land after the notice will not be compensated during expropriation. 03. Understand the Expropriation Announcement Legal Provision: Article 5 of the 'Measures for Announcement of Land Expropriation': The land expropriation announcement should include: (1) The approving authority, approval number, approval time, and approved purpose; (2) Ownership, location, type, and area of the expropriated land; (3) Compensation standards and resettlement methods for affected agricultural personnel; (4) Deadline and location for compensation registration. Typical Case: In practice, the local government often does not post the announcement. When affected residents inquire at the land and resources bureau, they are often told: 'There is an announcement, but it's a state secret and cannot be shown to you!' Lawyer's Advice: The land expropriation announcement must be posted. Don't be intimidated by claims of 'state secret.' We have the right to know the content of the announcement and confirm its completeness. 04. Value the Compensation and Resettlement Plan Legal Provision: Article 8 of the 'Measures for Announcement of Land Expropriation': The compensation and resettlement plan announcement should include: (1) Location, type, area of the expropriated land of the collective economic organization, types and quantities of attachments and crops, number of agricultural personnel needing resettlement; (2) Standard, amount, recipient, and payment method of land compensation fees; (3) Standard, amount, recipient, and payment method of resettlement subsidies; (4) Compensation standards and payment methods for attachments and crops; (5) Specific resettlement methods for agricultural personnel; (6) Other specific measures related to compensation and resettlement. Typical Case: During expropriation, to save costs, the demolishing party often creates unreasonable compensation plans with compensation明显低于法定标准. They may use threats, intimidation, or small favors to trick uninformed villagers into giving up land and signing agreements, aiming to profit themselves. Lawyer's Advice: The compensation and resettlement plan must be clearly communicated in writing; all elements are essential. Villagers who haven't seen the expropriation announcement or the compensation plan have the right to refuse compensation registration. They can demand the village committee provide a payment list of the land compensation funds within a certain period and require the committee to publicize the income and expenditure details for villagers to query and supervise. 05. Legally Request a Hearing Before legal approval of expropriation, the local land and resources department should inform the affected rural collective economic organizations and households of their right to apply for a hearing regarding the proposed compensation standards and resettlement methods. If a party applies for a hearing, it should be organized according to the procedures and requirements of the 'Land and Resources Hearing Regulations.' Legal Provision: Article 9 of the 'Measures for Announcement of Land Expropriation': If the affected rural collective economic organization, villagers, or other right-holders have objections to the compensation and resettlement plan or request a hearing, they must submit their request to the relevant city/county land administration department within 10 working days of the plan's announcement. Typical Case: In practice, affected farmers often find their signatures or fingerprints forged, or village committee leaders' relatives/friends sign as 'representatives' agreeing to the expropriation and waiving the hearing right. Many village committees directly stamp documents proving hearing waiver. Affected villagers are unaware of these behind-the-scenes actions, which require investigation and evidence collection; otherwise, their rights are infringed without their knowledge. Lawyer's Advice: Affected persons should clearly state their demands. If dissatisfied with the compensation plan and believe it cannot maintain their current living standard, they can request a hearing. The local land and resources department should hold the hearing. If modifications are needed, they should be made according to the legally approved expropriation plan.

Title: Chengguan Police Station: Timely Prevention of a Telecom Fraud Case Content: Chengguan Police Station: Timely Prevention of a Telecom Fraud Case Release Time: April 24, 2020, 08:42 Source: Author: [Font Size: Large Medium Small] Recently, Chengguan Police Station received a "request for help" from a citizen. Officers on site used the case to explain the law, timely preventing a telecom fraud case and avoiding financial loss for the citizen. On April 17, a citizen came to the duty room of Chengguan Police Station seeking help from the officers, stating that they had applied for a loan of 11,000 yuan on an online platform. The loan was shown as successful, and they had already provided their bank card number to the platform. However, the platform's customer service repeatedly called to notify them that the bank card number was incorrect, and they requested the officers' help to verify and re-enter their bank card number. Based on the situation reported by the citizen, the officers' investigation confirmed that the citizen was highly likely to be a victim of telecom network fraud. The duty officer immediately used practical cases to explain to the "seeking help" citizen the possible subsequent situations they might encounter, advising them not to be deceived. After clarifying the套路 (trick) of telecom fraud to the citizen, the officer helped them uninstall the online platform suspected of telecom fraud from their phone on the spot and had the citizen promptly change their bank card password. At the same time, they reminded the citizen not to answer calls from the other party's "customer service" again. If there is a genuine need for a loan, they can go to a local bank to apply.

Title: Now everyone can buy a house with peace of mind, stop thinking about price drops, the Two Sessions support reasonable housing demand! Improvement has already taken the lead, rigid demand no longer needs to wait and see, act quickly when it's suitable! Content: Preface In 2022, the government work report proposed to continue ensuring the housing needs of the masses. Adhere to the positioning that housing is for living, not for speculation. Persist in promoting both rental and purchase, accelerate the development of the long-term rental market, advance the construction of affordable housing, and support the construction of commercial housing to better meet the reasonable housing needs of buyers. Stabilize land prices, housing prices, and expectations, implement city-specific policies, and promote a virtuous cycle and healthy development of the industry. So, what is the specific direction going forward? 01 Re-mentioning "city-specific policies," room for adjustment in real estate market policies increases! The wave of relaxation may become more fierce! At the Two Sessions in 2021, although adhering to the principle that housing is for living, not for speculation, city-specific policies were not mentioned. But this year, city-specific policies were mentioned again. This means that the central government will have room to adjust real estate policies for different regions in the future. Regulation will not be widespread but will become more targeted. This can be seen from the fact that since the beginning of 2022, over 40 cities have relaxed policies to varying degrees. This year, many places including Qingdao and Zhengzhou have introduced new real estate policies, comprehensively easing restrictions on sales and purchases, with unprecedented intensity and scale. In the future, targeted and personalized regulation for more different cities is already on the way! 02 Multiple "first mentions," indicating a significant shift in the central government's attitude towards real estate! Additionally, the 2022 Two Sessions emphasized "promoting both rental and purchase," "a virtuous cycle and healthy development of the real estate industry," and "meeting the reasonable housing needs of buyers." These descriptions have appeared for the first time in the Two Sessions' tone-setting for the real estate market in the past three years, signaling great importance!! Now is the small spring of the real estate market, should you buy? For ordinary people, the most important thing before buying a house is to weigh their capabilities clearly and understand their own strength. For those with rigid demand, housing prices and monthly payments are the primary considerations. Whether to buy a house or not does not depend on the level of housing prices but on what you want. For those who need to buy a house, everyone has a time底线. Therefore, when you need to buy a house, you still have to buy it, because once you cross this time底线, the house will no longer have meaning for you. For investment, it is really not recommended, because the best era has passed, and speculation is even more impossible, as it directly contradicts the national policy of "housing is for living, not for speculation."

Title: Litigation Services Upgraded, Judicial Services for the People Heart to Heart Content: One day in mid-July, nearing the end of the morning work hours, an elderly woman anxiously entered the case filing hall of the Liuzhou Railway Transport Court. Upon inquiry, the court staff learned that the elderly woman had applied for government information disclosure, undergone administrative reconsideration, and had only one day left before exceeding the deadline for filing an administrative lawsuit. She did not know how to write a complaint, felt dizzy from奔波ing between multiple departments, and seeing so many people waiting in line to file cases, she was worried that her turn wouldn't come before closing time, hence her great anxiety. The staff immediately comforted the elderly woman. After attending to other parties, they quickly understood her situation and demands, guided her in writing the administrative lawsuit petition, organizing and photocopying evidence materials, etc., providing her with fast and convenient one-stop litigation services. When the elderly woman received the case acceptance notice on the spot, she excitedly thanked the staff, gave high praise for their patient and enthusiastic litigation services, and apologized for delaying their lunch break. This is a snapshot of the Liuzhou Railway Transport Court's promotion of the "Demonstration Court for Serving the People" creation activity. Since the beginning of this year, taking the "Demonstration Court for Serving the People" creation activity as an opportunity, the Liuzhou Railway Transport Court has focused on creating "one-stop" judicial services, striving to provide more convenient and efficient litigation services for the people... Implementing "Convenience-oriented" Window Services: Improving various measures beneficial to the people, refining work processes, routinely setting up guidance desks to direct parties in quickly handling various litigation matters, establishing model Communist Party member posts and offline litigation service windows for the elderly, providing offline guidance and services for middle-aged and elderly people unfamiliar with the internet or unable to smoothly operate online litigation service procedures, offering tangible convenience to the people, and showcasing the good image of the court's service windows. Promoting "Digital" Litigation Services: The litigation service center fully promotes the use of platforms such as "People's Court Online Services," "Lawyer Service Platform," and "Guangxi Electronic Court," carrying out online case filing and cross-regional case filing, fully leveraging the advantages of "Internet+" to provide lawyers and legal workers with services like "Security Check One Code Pass" channels, fast online review via the lawyer service platform, paperless rapid filing, online payment, and other filing services, striving to achieve the goal of "letting data travel more, so the people travel less." Simultaneously, upgrading the 12368 litigation service hotline, assigning specialists to handle hotline calls and answer public inquiries. Since 2021, a total of 73 online case filing applications have been received, 55 approved, and 18 returned for supplementary materials; assisted with 10 cross-regional case filings, and as the jurisdictional court, accepted 2 cross-regional case filings. The 12368 litigation service hotline handled 28 instances of public inquiries regarding case filing, case queries, contacting judges, and other one-stop services. Strengthening "Multi-angle" Legal Publicity: Making full use of various media such as LED screens, the internet, and public accounts to increase publicity on the convenience and benefits of litigation services, diversified dispute resolution, and judicial transparency. The litigation service center specially produced ten types of promotional materials, including "People's Court Online Services Operation Manual," "Guidance on Querying Case Trial Process Information and Electronic Service Platform," "People's Court Online Preservation System Operation Guide," "People's Court Entrusted Appraisal System Operation Guide," and "Lawyer Service Platform Operation Guide," to publicize to parties,代理 lawyers, and the general public. Using internet technology and信息化手段 to provide online litigation services to the people, guiding parties and诉讼代理人 to conduct online case filing, online payment, online applications for preservation and appraisal through the Mobile Micro Court and Lawyer Service Platform. Since the beginning of this year, parties have applied for 3 preservations online and 2 appraisals online. Source: Nanning Railway Transport Intermediate Court, Liuzhou Railway Transport Court Author: Qin Jing, Mo Jifeng

Title: Always endlessly obsessing over my body shape day and night, what should I do? Content: Thanks for the invitation. First, I want to vent a bit: you probably aren't anxious enough, otherwise how could you not control it? I'll roughly share some useful little methods with you. 1. Maintain an exercise habit. It doesn't mean you have to work out five or six times a week. You can exercise more when you have time, and less or even skip it when you're busy. When you exercise more, you can reward yourself by eating more. When you don't exercise, control your intake appropriately, cut out sugar, and eat cleaner. 2. Ensure sufficient sleep. Aim for 7-8 hours of sleep per day, especially when work pressure is high or you're feeling anxious. Adequate sleep can effectively help lower your cortisol levels and reduce fat accumulation. 3. Keep yourself in a happy mood. Find things in life that bring you joy and happiness, whether it's reading books, hiking, watching movies, binge-watching shows, or karaoke. Or if you have other hobbies, regularly spend some time on them to maintain a good mood often. 4. Actually, not many people in life pay that much attention to you. Focus more on how you perceive yourself rather than comparing yourself to others. Take me as an example: I've been handsome, ugly, skinny, and also fat. Every time I reach a breaking point where I can't accept my current state, I take action to make a change. I never use anyone else as a goal.

Title: Should 'Home Hostels' Be Allowed in Residential Communities? -(Image)- Sohu News Content: Home hostels display 'single room rental' banners to attract guests. 'Hostels operating in residential buildings, how is the safety of homeowners guaranteed?' Homeowners in Poly Champagne Garden have expressed great dissatisfaction with the consecutive emergence of home hostels within the community. This phenomenon of converting residential units into home hostels exists in many communities. Yesterday, reporters visited several home hostels that are currently operating or preparing to operate and consulted relevant departments on the matter. 'There are several hostels here, which one are you looking for?' When a reporter entered Poly Champagne Garden and asked a cleaner about home hostels, she responded by listing the locations of three operating hostels. 'Recently, people come here every day looking for hostels.' 'The residential area has turned into a commercial area,' said homeowner Mr. Liu, who was walking nearby and overheard the conversation, angrily. Mr. Liu lives in Building 10, Area B, and there is a hostel below his home with good business, often having strangers staying. 'Running a hostel in the community brings complex traffic of people, and we residents are terrified.' Following the address provided by Mr. Liu, the reporter visited several home hostels in the community posing as a guest. In the home hostels at 4-1 and 7-1, Unit 4, Building 2, Area B, the reporter saw the units divided into several small rooms, categorized as single rooms and standard rooms, with prices ranging from 60 to 80 yuan. Each room was furnished like a regular hostel, with beds covered in white sheets, etc. Ms. Xu, a staff member at the hostel, explained that it opened last October, and almost all customers are from out of town 'because the train station is nearby.' 'Aren't there security guards at the main gate? How can I get in if I want to stay?' Xu said not to worry, 'When you come in, call us, and we'll send someone to pick you up.' She claimed that as long as you tell the security guard you are a friend or relative, they won't stop you. 'After all, we are residents here.' 'Do you have a business license?' When the reporter asked to see the business license, Xu became警惕: 'Why ask that? Are you staying or not?' While speaking, she pushed the reporter toward the door. When the reporter revealed their identity, Xu said, 'We bought the apartment with our money, we can do whatever we want, what does it have to do with others?' and then refused the interview, citing 'the boss is not here.' Meanwhile, at 2-1, Unit 1, Building 2, Area A, a unit is being renovated into a home hostel. The room is converted into a duplex structure, split into two levels and divided into small rooms. The renovators explained that the hostel owner is surnamed Cai, and the hostel will open in mid-July. 'Boss Cai bought this apartment specifically to open a home hostel; he has a good business mind.' There are several other home hostels in the community, either operating or preparing to open, all displaying banners outside their windows with 'Single Room for Rent' or 'Apartment for Rent' to attract guests. Mr. Pu, manager of the business department of a decoration company, has renovated several home hostels in this community and is familiar with them. 'There are five or six hostels in this community, none have business licenses. The owners bought apartments to open hostels because of the advantage of being near the train station.' What is the property management's attitude towards home hostels? When the reporter contacted the property management, staff member Li Lianchuan explained: There are no relevant documents that clearly specify whether home hostels can be established within the community. When asked about the impact of the home hostel business model on other homeowners' lives, Li expressed helplessness: 'The home hostel owners are also homeowners. They claim the guests are their friends or relatives, so we cannot阻止 them from entering.' He also said that property management only provides services to homeowners and has no law enforcement power. 'Homeowners have repeatedly raised this issue, and we can only report it to higher authorities.' Homeowners in the community have been posting on the community's online forum, planning to jointly seek answers from the property management and relevant departments on the 26th of this month. Chattering: Luoxia Gu Lu: Home hostels pose significant safety hazards. Strangers coming and going don't make it feel like a residential area; it's become a marketplace! What is the property management doing? How can they allow this? yjj_16: Perhaps some people are using home hostels for illicit activities. We cannot tolerate this continuing. We must unite and report to the relevant administrative departments, even call 110 to report suspicious people in the community. If relevant departments keep sending people to inspect, they won't be able to operate. Tanhua Yixian: If this continues, we might as well all use our homes for business—open hostels, foot massage parlors.大不了 we don't live there ourselves! Shenye Shangwang De Nvren: For the sake of having a peaceful home, we must坚决抵制 the emergence of home-style hostels. (Excerpted from various community websites in the city) Reporter Zhang Shuihong, Photo Report

Title: Reasons for the Medium-to-Long-Term Performance Difference Between Chinese and US Active Funds Content: I rarely visit a certain website now. Today I logged in and saw an article by a senior macro researcher from a well-known fund company. The article argues that the fundamental reason for the medium-to-long-term performance difference between Chinese and US active and passive funds lies in the different stages of economic development. It suggests the difference is caused by the disparities in economic and industrial development between China and the US. I don't know much about macro research, but I might have some macro-level understanding and feelings (not necessarily correct), and I'm thinking about this issue from another angle. The difference in returns between Chinese and US active funds. 1) From my memory, most US active funds underperform their benchmark indices over the medium-to-long term, to the extent that even Warren Buffett advises gamblers to be content with the status quo and buy ETF funds. Given this, why do US active funds still exist? I don't understand. 2) As of the end of 2021, the average annualized return of Chinese active equity funds over the past ten years was 13.6% (data from China Securities Index Co., Ltd.). The average annualized return on equity (ROE) of listed companies over the past ten years was around 12% (based on feeling, may have significant deviation). This means Chinese active funds can earn their deserved returns over the medium-to-long term, even more than they should. Whereas US active funds cannot. This is the difference in returns between Chinese and US active funds. Why is China's benchmark ROE? I don't understand, just based on feeling. Why doesn't China use an index benchmark? Looking at the index compilation methodology, I don't understand other aspects. With inflated initial public offerings, is the index benchmark meaningful? Differences in the composition of market participants between China and the US. I did a quick online search. According to 2018 interim reports, individual investors held 40.5% of the market capitalization in A-shares, while the figures for the US, France, the UK, and Japan were only 4.1%, 2.0%, 2.7%, and 4.6% respectively. Institutional investors held 31.5% and 93.2% of the market capitalization in A-shares and US stocks respectively (fund data). In 2021, the trading volume share of individual investors fell below 70% for the first time (official data). The chart below shows Haitong data. Around 12% ROE. 13.6% return. Does the excess return come from China's economic transformation and upgrading? Industrial cycles last at least a few years, three to five years. Looking at corporate reports, it's common for fund quarterly holdings to change by ±50%, even more volatile than the stock price fluctuations. Industrial cycle = holding cycle? Is it beta return? Is the fundamental reason for the performance difference between Chinese and US active funds due to different stages of economic development? Or different stages of securities market development? Title: Is it really cost-effective for fresh graduates to take the postgraduate entrance exam? Content: If you pass the exam, that's great and the future looks bright 🌸. But if you don't pass 💔, you will miss out on the valuable internship opportunities in your junior year. Because in many universities, the course load starts to decrease in the junior year. Some students choose to do internships to gain experience, while others start preparing for the postgraduate or civil service exams. The lack of internship experience will affect your chances of getting an offer through the autumn or spring recruitment cycles. If you make it to the复试 (second round) of the postgraduate exam but unfortunately fail, then having 🈚️/little internship experience ➕ a late start to the spring recruitment ➕ no connections 🟰 a high probability of difficulty finding a job. At the same time, you also lose the opportunity to participate in the Selected Graduates Transfer Program (选调) and the National Civil Service Exam (国考) as a fresh graduate (most candidates cannot handle preparing for both the postgraduate and civil service exams simultaneously). However, candidates who did not pursue the postgraduate exam from the start and focused solely on the civil service exam, even if they fail the Selected Transfer, National, and Provincial exams, can still take exams for public institutions (事业单位), non-staff positions (编外), social workers (社工), etc., relying on their previous preparation foundation, because the question types are similar, and the questions are only easier than the civil service exam. Their chances of success are far greater than those who start preparing only after failing the postgraduate exam. In contrast, the knowledge for the postgraduate exam seems only useful for the exam itself (for most majors). So, is taking the postgraduate exam as a fresh graduate really a good choice? Title: Dingcheng District Teacher Training School and Taoyuan County Teacher Training School Conduct Teacher Training Exchange Activity Content: Recently, a delegation from the Dingcheng District Teacher Training School in Changde City visited the Taoyuan County Teacher Training School for an in-depth educational exchange activity. The theme of this exchange focused on the management and implementation of teacher training programs, as well as how to enhance training effectiveness, among other aspects. Through this exchange, both parties shared their respective experiences and explored new ideas for educational reform and teacher professional growth. In the management practice of the project responsibility system, the Taoyuan County Teacher Training School demonstrated its innovative management model. By clearly defining the responsibilities and authority of the project leader, the school achieved efficient operation of training programs. The leader is not only responsible for the overall planning and implementation of the project but also bears ultimate responsibility for the training outcomes. This model enhances the professionalism and specificity of management, ensuring the quality and effectiveness of training programs. Cultivating potential teacher trainers was another focus of the discussion. The Taoyuan County Teacher Training School adopts diversified cultivation methods, including systematic training, mentorship by experienced teachers, practical exercises, and multi-role assignments for individuals. By establishing incentive mechanisms, the school has stimulated teachers' enthusiasm for participating in training work. At the same time, constraint mechanisms are implemented to ensure the professional conduct and teaching quality of the trainers. Furthermore, the two schools conducted in-depth discussions on workshop-based training, post-training evaluation and follow-up, and guiding schools in conducting school-based training. Through this exchange, the two schools deepened their mutual understanding and laid a solid foundation for cooperation in the field of teacher training. Source: Zhijian News Author: Liao Zhen Editor: Qiu Qi

Title: Why Are Multiple Institutions Lowering Fees Related to Wealth Management Products? Content: Recently, several banks and their wealth management subsidiaries have reduced fees related to wealth management products to varying degrees. The types of fees reduced mainly include fixed management fees and sales service fees, but also involve custody fees and redemption fees, with some fees even adjusted to zero. Industry insiders interviewed by the Economic Reference News stated that against the backdrop of slowing product issuance and poor returns, multiple institutions lowering fees for wealth management products aim to attract customers as a competitive strategy. At the same time, reducing product fees is also a way to cut costs and benefit customers, better reflecting the direction of inclusive finance. Experts also mentioned that when investing in wealth management products, one should comprehensively consider the overall situation of the product and personal actual needs, and it is not recommended to use the level of fees as a key factor in selection. The wealth management fee war begins. Reporters have found that recently, several banks and their wealth management subsidiaries have reduced fees related to wealth management products, with the main reductions being fixed management fees and sales service fees. The financial institutions reducing fees include various types such as large state-owned banks, joint-stock banks and their wealth management subsidiaries, and city commercial banks. Regarding fixed management fees, Nanjing Bank's subsidiary, Nanyin Wealth Management, announced that since 2022, it has offered discounts on fees for some wealth management products. For example, for the 'Nanyin Wealth Management Zhulianbihe Zhiyuan Balanced ESG Theme (minimum holding period 364 days)', from February 7 to June 30, the fixed management fee was reduced from 0.8% per annum to 0.4% per annum. For sales service fees, Bank of China Wealth Management announced that from March 2, 2022, to March 28, 2023, it would offer a fee discount on the 'Bank of China Wealth Management 'Wenfu' Fixed Income Enhanced (Closed) 2022 Issue 009' product. The sales service fee for Class A shares was reduced from 0.30% (annualized) to 0.15% (annualized); the sales service fee for Class C shares was reduced from 0.40% (annualized) to 0.10% (annualized). In addition to fixed management fees and sales service fees, product fee reductions also involve redemption fees. China Everbright Bank's subsidiary, Everbright Wealth Management, conducted a redemption fee promotion for the Sunshine Gold No. 2 (EB1888) wealth management product from February 14 (inclusive) to December 20 (inclusive). During non-promotion periods, if the holding period is less than 360 days, the redemption fee rate is 0.50%; during the promotion period, if the holding period is less than 360 days, the redemption fee rate is halved to 0.25%. It is worth noting that some product fees have been adjusted to zero. China Merchants Bank recently announced a reduction in fees for some products of bank wealth management subsidiaries it distributes, involving fixed management fees, sales service fees, and custody fees for more than ten products from several companies including CMB Wealth Management, Industrial Wealth Management, and Everbright Wealth Management. Some fixed management fees were reduced to zero. Huaxia Bank announced that starting January 25, it would adjust the sales fee rates for Class A and B shares of Huaxia Wealth Management Cash Management Product No. 3, reducing the sales fee for Class A shares and Class B shares from the previous 0.3% per annum to zero. Rizhao Bank also announced that it plans to offer phased discounts on sales fees and management fees for three designated wealth management products in the second investment cycle, with the discounted sales fee rate and management fee rate both being 0%. Reducing fees to benefit customers and seize the market. What are the reasons behind the widespread reduction of various fees for bank wealth management products? Dong Ximiao, Chief Researcher of Zhaolian Finance, stated that there are multiple reasons for the recent fee adjustments of bank wealth management products. Last year, the bank wealth management market had a balance of 29 trillion yuan, with a growth rate of about 12%. The scale is relatively large, profitability has increased, and nearly one trillion yuan in returns were created for investors, providing a basis for reducing fees. 'In the context of increasing support for the real economy and reducing fees to benefit customers, lowering product fees is also a way to reduce costs and benefit customers. Compared to the stock market, the bank wealth management market is relatively stable and is an important choice for ordinary people's investment and wealth management. After fee reductions, it better reflects the direction of inclusive finance.' Su Xiaorui, Senior Analyst of the Financial Industry at Analysys, also said that with the successive establishment of bank wealth management subsidiaries and the deepening impact of the new asset management regulations, competition on the supply side of the wealth management market is intensifying. At the product issuance level, with the transformation of wealth management products to net value-based products, the issuance volume and outstanding scale of net value products continue to rise, and economies of scale will also drive fee rates down to a certain extent. Industry insiders also believe that banks reducing fees is one of the methods of competition among institutions. Huang Shihui, researcher at Puyi Standards, stated that since January this year, the A-share market has continued to fluctuate, and the yields of major interbank interest rate bonds have generally declined slightly, affecting the returns of some bank wealth management products. Due to the slowdown in product issuance and poor returns, several wealth management companies have reduced management fees and sales fees for wealth management products. The reduction of related fees is a competitive means among institutions. Dong Ximiao said that from the perspective of banks and wealth management companies, reducing fees can attract more customers, increase sales volume with small profits, and further expand the scale of bank wealth management. It is expected that the scale of wealth management products will exceed 30 trillion yuan in 2022, and the number of investors is expected to exceed 100 million. If fee reductions lead to an increase in investors and an expansion of business scale, wealth management business income may not decrease but increase. Investors should rationally plan their investments. What will be the long-term trend of wealth management product fees? Huang Shihui stated that it is normal for wealth management companies to adjust fees to attract or retain investors and seize market share. It is expected that this phenomenon will continue to expand in the short term, but under normal circumstances, low-fee products will not persist for a long time. Su Xiaorui also believes that fee reduction is currently a short-term trend. In the long run, with the stabilization of the macroeconomic environment and the gradual formation of the net value product market structure, fees are expected to stabilize. Dong Ximiao believes that for some time, fees for products such as public funds have been reduced to varying degrees. It is expected that there is still room for further adjustment of fees related to bank wealth management products to enhance their attractiveness to investors. However, different banks, wealth management companies, and wealth management products will adopt different charging strategies, and differentiation in charging methods and fee rates will become more apparent. Huang Shihui said that for investors, short- to medium-term fee adjustments are beneficial for reducing investment costs, but investors also need to rationally plan their investments. Dong Ximiao reminded investors that bank wealth management products have many types of charges. In addition to management fees, there are subscription fees, purchase fees, redemption fees, etc. It is important to recognize that a reduction in a single fee does not mean no fees; some bank wealth management product fee adjustments come with certain preconditions, such as holding periods. Moreover, when investing in wealth management products, one should comprehensively consider the overall situation of the product and personal actual needs, and it is not recommended to use the level of fees as a key factor in selection. (Reporter Zhang Mo, Intern Wang Mengzhen)

Title: Has Freight Forwarding 'Completely Cooled Down'? Shipping Companies Are Building Customer Databases to Bypass Agents → Content: Freight forwarders in Australia have recently expressed concerns that major shipping companies (including Hapag-Lloyd and Maersk subsidiary Hamburg Süd) are planning to build a customer database to deal directly with shippers, completely cutting out agents. According to overseas media reports, one freight forwarder claimed that some carriers are refusing to accept cargo unless the freight forwarder agrees to book domestic inland trucking with the carrier, which precisely requires the agent to provide the shipper's detailed information. However, with space currently hard to find, freight forwarders have no choice but to agree to these terms in order to secure available space. A spokesperson for Hapag-Lloyd denied any coercion: "Inland transportation is indeed part of the service we offer in Australia, but we absolutely do not insist in any form that customers use this service to secure bookings for our services or space." Hamburg Süd also refuted the claim that freight forwarders are forced to disclose customer data, stating, "Our available space is tight globally. In the intra-Oceania trade, due to operational disruptions across Oceania, we are facing severe capacity constraints. Due to limited capacity, we are currently unable to accommodate additional long-term business. We regret that not all booking requests can be fulfilled, and we are doing everything we can to bring sea freight logistics back to normal levels. Our Hamburg Süd Instant product (which Maersk calls Spot) is still available for any customer to book without using Hamburg Süd trucking. Therefore, we do not see the problem you mentioned." Nevertheless, freight forwarders claim that, so far, this carrier strategy is limited to the Australia-New Zealand trade. As vessels have been redeployed to more profitable trade routes in the Northern Hemisphere, vessel space is now very precious. Freight forwarders claim, "What we are worried about is that in 6 to 12 months, when the market returns to normal, carriers will use the database to contact our customers directly for quotes. At that point, who will still use freight forwarders?" The freight forwarder stated that the carriers' actions are "predatory" and violate Australian competition law. Australian freight forwarders have contacted their representatives in the Freight & Trade Alliance (FTA) to make a submission to the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC). Paul Zalai, Director and Co-Founder of the FTA, a member of the Australian Peak Shippers Association secretariat, and Director of the Global Shippers' Forum (GSF), believes the threat from carriers is real. He explained, "Clearly, everyone in the Australian supply chain is facing a threat. The trend of vertical integration among shipping companies, stevedores, etc., is increasing. While disruptions in international trade logistics are inevitable, we will pay more attention to ensuring all activities comply with Australian law." An ACCC spokesperson said the Commission cannot comment on specific businesses or industries, but it is responsible for investigating the competition provisions of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010. Businesses generally have the right to set the terms on which they supply goods or services, including as part of a bundled arrangement. However, in limited circumstances, this may breach competition law, particularly if the arrangement is done by a company with substantial market power and the conduct substantially lessens competition. The FTA will escalate the issue by calling for "an independent federal government review of international shipping practices and the introduction of a maritime regulator to oversee reforms," which will coincide with the FTA's submission to the Productivity Commission's inquiry into vulnerable supply chains. Furthermore, they stated that Australia has world-class manufacturers and producers, supported by skilled customs brokers and freight forwarders, and is ready to capitalize on opportunities created by free trade agreements and economies recovering from Covid-19. A level playing field is needed to ensure all members of the supply chain can compete and continue to serve Australian trade effectively. James Hookham, Senior Executive of the European GSF, pointed out that a similar situation occurred in Europe in the 1990s, which was deemed anti-competitive under EU law and led to the end of the carrier conference system. This latest move by carriers will allow them to understand shippers' movements, and there are no privacy protections for data owners in the competition rules. It will allow carriers to cut out the middleman, and under the block exemption rules allowing lines to form alliances, they can share this data. This is very sensitive commercial information. If carriers know how much cargo is expected, they can manage trade capacity and increase freight rates. There is a real and urgent need for a data protection bill for the shipping industry. In fact, this problem is not unique to Australia; it is a global supply chain issue. Freight forwarders everywhere in the world will face this problem. Once it happens, shippers will become more reliant on carriers, and freight rate manipulation will become more apparent! Please share to inform and remind friends around you~ This article is reproduced from Mike Foreign Trade Talk news

Title: Can excessive masturbation cause erectile dysfunction and premature ejaculation? Content: Actually, this question shouldn't require too much explanation. On the other hand, frequent masturbation may make the body accustomed to specific stimulation methods and intensity, which might lead to sexual dysfunction during normal intercourse, such as being unable to achieve or maintain a sufficient erection for satisfactory intercourse. Furthermore, excessive masturbation may cause damage to the nerves and tissues of the penile corpus cavernosum, increasing sensitivity, which could potentially lead to erectile dysfunction. Of course, it's important to note that not everyone who masturbates frequently will experience these problems. Individual differences, psychological state, living environment, and other factors all influence the extent to which masturbation affects sexual function. If you are concerned that masturbation might be affecting your sexual function, it is advisable to adjust the frequency of masturbation and cultivate healthy lifestyle habits and a positive mindset. Since we're on this topic, here is some advice for male compatriots who are already experiencing troubles in this area; if you don't have these issues, take it as encouragement to stay vigilant. In spring and summer, sleep late and rise early; in autumn and winter, sleep early and rise late. Avoid bad habits: Quit smoking, quit alcohol, quit spicy foods, quit staying up late, and avoid excessive sexual activity. Adjust sexual behavior methods: Try changing the methods and frequency of sexual behavior to find what works for the individual. This may include prolonging foreplay, using condoms to reduce stimulation, etc. It is important to maintain an open mind and communicate with your partner. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) adjustments: TCM believes that erectile dysfunction and premature ejaculation are related to kidney deficiency and can be improved through TCM herbal adjustments. Specific TCM prescriptions need to be selected and used based on individual circumstances.
