Title: Where to Repair a OnePlus Phone Content: If your OnePlus phone is broken, you can apply for after-sales service on the OnePlus official website and then mail the phone for repair. If you don't want to go through this hassle, you can simply go to the nearest phone repair shop. OnePlus (OnePlus) is a smartphone brand under Shenzhen Wanplus Technology Co., Ltd., which made its debut on January 13, 2014. The brand's phones are sold online, and the first-generation phone was officially launched on May 28, 2014. On January 13, 2014, at the Ullens Center for Contemporary Art in Beijing's 798 Art District, the OnePlus (OnePlus) brand was officially launched for the first time, announcing the product philosophy of "Never Settle." At the launch event, OnePlus CEO Pete Lau stated that the core approach of OnePlus phones is that "OnePlus" is responsible for hardware development, while the software aspect is optimized by CM (CyanogenMod, the world's largest third-party Android ROM team), and they plan to enter the global market simultaneously in the future. Unfortunately, if your OnePlus phone screen has issues such as cracking, leakage, detachment, or burn-in, to restore the product to normal use as soon as possible, it is recommended that you bring the purchase invoice, warranty card, and the phone to the local OPPO authorized service experience center, where professional engineers will inspect and repair it. OPPO official service centers are authorized by OPPO to provide offline service points for OPPO and OnePlus product consultations, system upgrades, product repairs, inspections, and exchanges. If you have any questions about your purchased OPPO or OnePlus products or if the product malfunctions, you can go to the nearest OPPO official service center for assistance: 1. Visit the OPPO official website, select "Service > Self-Service > Store Locator and Appointment" to search, or go directly to https://support.oppo.com/cn/service-center/ to check. 2. Open the "My OnePlus" app, on the "My" page, select "E-Warranty Card > Service Centers" to find a service center in your location. 3. Search for and open the "OPPO Service" mini-program on WeChat, click "Store Locator and Appointment"; 4. If you cannot visit an OPPO official service center or there is none nearby, we offer a two-way free mail-in repair service to handle product issues. Visit the OPPO official website, select "Service > Self-Service > Mail-in Repair," or search for and open the "OPPO Service" mini-program on WeChat to apply for mail-in repair. Friendly reminder: Before visiting an OPPO official service center, it is recommended to call ahead to check parts inventory, etc., to avoid unnecessary trips and to plan your journey safely. Due to group strategy adjustments, OnePlus after-sales services are fully authorized to OPPO service centers. OPPO customer service centers can provide you with product repairs, system upgrades, inspections, exchanges, and product consultations. Services cover: phones, watches, earphones, and other accessories. You can find the address, business hours, and phone number of OPPO customer service centers using the following methods: 1. Visit the OnePlus official website, select "Service > Common Services > Service Center Search" to search and make an appointment. 2. If you cannot visit a customer service center or there is none nearby, visit the OnePlus official website, select "Service > Mail-in Repair," and we offer a two-way free mail-in repair service to handle product issues. Friendly reminder: Before visiting a customer service center, it is recommended to call ahead to check parts inventory, etc., to avoid wasted trips. If the phone is not answered, it might be due to high call volume; try calling again later. OnePlus phones are mainly sold online, so repairs are also done via official website mail-in, primarily using SF Express for service, and customers are usually asked to choose cash on delivery. This is done quite well. When SF Express cannot meet requirements, EMS is generally chosen. There are many online phone repair services on Taobao; it's best to choose ones in Shenzhen! That is the national manufacturing base for phones, and any issue can be fixed there. The repair cost is within 100 RMB. Just courier the phone to them.

Title: Divorce Also Entails Joint Liability for Pre-Marital VAM Failure Repurchase
Content: On August 4, 2017, Zhuhai Hengqin Leri Enterprise signed the "Stock Subscription Agreement" with Wuxi Vivame Company. On the same day, Xiangfu Company and Han signed a "Supplementary Agreement" with Zhuhai Hengqin Leri Enterprise. The agreement stipulated: Whereas the investor intends to sign the "Stock Subscription Agreement" with the target company, agreeing that the investor subscribes to 2,131,287 shares of the target company for a total consideration of RMB 49,999,993.02. 2. To further safeguard the investor's rights after investing in the target company, all parties hereby agree to enter into this agreement. Article 1 Investment Arrangements: 1.2 Repurchase Right: Party A agrees that if the target company encounters any of the following circumstances, the investor has the right to require one or more parties of Party A ("Repurchase Entities") to repurchase part or all of the shares held by the investor, limited to the value of the target company's equity directly or indirectly held by them, at an annualized return rate of 9%: (1) The target company fails to submit a qualified initial public offering application to the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) for listing on the Shanghai or Shenzhen Stock Exchange by December 31, 2018; (2) The target company fails to complete listing on the Shanghai or Shenzhen Stock Exchange within 36 months after this investment; (3) The target company fails to complete a backdoor listing within 36 months after this investment; (4) The target company's IPO application submitted to the CSRC is withdrawn, returned, revoked, or not approved by the CSRC for any reason; (5) The target company's performance involves fraud, or the company's management or actual controller has major integrity issues; (6) Any major adverse change in the legal environment preventing the target company from achieving a qualified listing on the Shanghai or Shenzhen Stock Exchange; (7) Any material breach by the company or its major shareholders; (8) Before the company's IPO, the major shareholder or actual controller sells shares without the investor's written consent, resulting in loss of major shareholder status or control; (9) All matters described in clause 1.3(10) of this Supplementary Agreement are not completed by December 31, 2017. The target company's repurchase entities shall complete the repurchase transaction and pay the repurchase price within 20 working days after the investor's written repurchase request. The repurchase amount calculation formula is: P = M(1 + 9% * T) + dividends the investor should have received but did not from the target company, where: P is the repurchase price, M is the investment amount paid by the investor for this capital increase, T is the number of calendar days from the date the investor paid the share subscription price (inclusive) to the date the investor exercises the repurchase right and the repurchase payment is fully paid (exclusive) divided by 365. 1.3(10) VIE Matters: The company shareholder Xijin Venture Capital Company shall, after this investment, actively seek investors to transfer part of the company's shares to old shareholders at a price not exceeding 90% of this investment price. The transfer proceeds shall be specifically used to acquire the equity held by Wuxi Vivame Company in Hongrong Xinyuan Company, and such acquisition price shall not be lower than Wuxi Vivame Company's initial investment amount in Hongrong Xinyuan Company (i.e., RMB 42 million) plus interest calculated based on the同期中国人民银行贷款基准利率 from the actual payment date to the date of receipt. After Wuxi Vivame Company receives the aforementioned acquisition price, Han's affiliate shall transfer its equity in Hongrong Xinyuan to a third party as soon as possible to ensure Hongrong Xinyuan no longer constitutes an affiliate of the company, and complete the industrial and commercial registration change for the equity transfer by December 31, 2017. Additionally, it shall促尽快注销 Directlink Business Limited, Zhong Capital Fund, L.P., and Han's foreign exchange registration for overseas investment by domestic residents, and complete this by December 31, 2017. Article 6 Default Liability and Remedies: 6.1 If any party ("Defaulting Party") breaches its representations, warranties, commitments, or obligations under this agreement, or if such representations or warranties are untrue, inaccurate, or contain material omissions, the other party ("Non-defaulting Party") has the right to notify the Defaulting Party to rectify within the specified period and shall compensate the Non-defaulting Party for actual losses suffered. 6.2 If Party A breaches the repurchase obligation under this agreement, Party B has the right to require Party A to continue performance and pay an additional penalty: Penalty = Amount of unpaid repurchase price × 0.05% × days overdue. On August 9, 2017, Zhuhai Hengqin Leri Enterprise's investment funds were received by Wuxi Vivame Company. On March 5, 2019, Zhuhai Hengqin Leri Enterprise demanded that Han and Xiangfu Company perform the repurchase obligation. On June 13, 2019, Guo and Han, who were originally married, divorced. On December 30, 2020, the Beijing Third Intermediate People's Court conducted the first instance. The court held: The "Stock Subscription Agreement" signed between Zhuhai Hengqin Leri Enterprise and Wuxi Vivame Company reflects the true intent of both parties and does not violate mandatory laws and regulations, thus is valid. I. Whether the "Supplementary Agreement" signed between Zhuhai Hengqin Leri Enterprise, Xiangfu Company, and Han is valid. According to Article 52 of the "Contract Law of the People's Republic of China", contracts violating mandatory laws and regulations are invalid. The mandatory provisions herein refer to效力性强制性规定. In this case, Xiangfu Company, Han, and Guo argued that the "Supplementary Agreement" violated Articles 20 and 30 of the "Measures for the Supervision of Non-listed Public Companies", Articles 67 and 70 of the "Securities Law of the People's Republic of China", and Article 20 of the "Company Law of the People's Republic of China", and should be invalid. The court held that the "Measures for the Supervision of Non-listed Public Companies" is a measure formulated by the CSRC to regulate stock transfers and issuance of non-listed public companies, protect investor rights, and maintain public interest, based on relevant laws and regulations, and does not fall under the category of laws or administrative regulations. Articles 67 (interim reporting) and 70 (information disclosure methods) of the "Securities Law" and Article 20 (shareholder abuse of rights liability) of the "Company Law" are not效力性强制性规定. Therefore, the arguments for invalidity by Xiangfu Company, Han, and Guo are unfounded and rejected. The "Supplementary Agreement" reflects the true intent of the parties, does not violate mandatory laws and regulations, is valid, and all parties should perform their obligations accordingly. In this case, the repurchase conditions were based on whether Vivame Company could submit an IPO application by December 31, 2018. Xiangfu Company and Han argued that changes in IPO conditions for internet culture companies constitute reasonable business risks, and there is no evidence proving IPO review policies became stricter. Therefore, the court rejected their "change of circumstances" defense. II. Whether the repurchase conditions were triggered, and whether Xiangfu Company and Han should pay the repurchase price and penalty to Zhuhai Hengqin Leri Enterprise. After the agreements were signed, Zhuhai Hengqin Leri Enterprise remitted funds to Vivame Company as agreed, fulfilling its payment obligation and acquiring 2,131,287 shares. According to clause 1.2 of the "Supplementary Agreement", if Wuxi Vivame Company encounters any stipulated circumstance, the investor can require repurchase. This includes failing to submit an IPO application by December 31, 2018, or failing to complete VIE matters by December 31, 2017. As Wuxi Vivame Company failed to meet both deadlines, Zhuhai Hengqin Leri Enterprise has the right to require Xiangfu Company and Han to repurchase the shares. Repurchase should be completed within 20 working days after the written request. Evidence shows the investment was paid on August 9, 2017, and the repurchase demand letter was delivered on March 7, 2019. Thus, Xiangfu Company and Han should have paid by April 4, 2019. The repurchase price is calculated at an annualized 9% return: P = M(1 + 9% * T) + unpaid dividends. Therefore, Xiangfu Company and Han should pay the principal RMB 49,999,993.02 plus profit (calculated from August 9, 2017, until actual payment, at 9% annual rate based on 365 days). According to clause 6.2, if Party A breaches the repurchase obligation, Party B can require continued performance and an additional penalty. As Xiangfu Company and Han failed to perform, Zhuhai Hengqin Leri Enterprise has the right to demand a penalty from April 5, 2019. The penalty calculation is: unpaid repurchase amount × 0.05% × days overdue. The court held that penalties primarily compensate losses and punish default. Since the agreement already includes a 9% annual return, which partly covers the fund occupation loss, calculating both return and penalty as per the agreement would be excessive. Although Xiangfu Company and Han did not formally apply to adjust the penalty, their defense arguing against repurchase can be seen as a request for adjustment. Based on fairness, the court adjusted the penalty to: based on the unpaid amount (including profit) as of April 5, 2019, calculated at 0.03% daily until actual payment. As of April 5, 2019, the repurchase amount was RMB 49,999,993.02 + RMB 49,999,993.02 × 9% / 365 days × 605 days = RMB 57,458,902.98. III. Whether Guo should bear joint liability for Han's repurchase and penalty obligations. According to the "Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases Involving Marital Debt Disputes" Article 3, debts incurred by one spouse during marriage exceeding daily household needs are not supported as joint marital debts unless the creditor proves the debt was for common life, joint production/operation, or based on mutual consent. Thus, Zhuhai Hengqin Leri Enterprise must prove: (1) the debt occurred during marriage; (2) it exceeded daily household needs; (3) it was for common life/joint operation or based on mutual consent. Evidence shows the agreement and debt occurred during marriage and were for Vivame Company's operation, exceeding daily needs. The key issue is whether Guo jointly operated Vivame Company. First, business registration information shows Guo directly or indirectly held equity/partnership shares in four of Vivame's top ten shareholders (Xijin Venture, Xiyuan Growth, Jiangtong Xijin Center, Xijin Growth No.1), serving as legal representative/executive director. These four shareholders held 43.51%, 34.53%, 33.46% of Vivame's shares from 2016 to 2018. Meanwhile, Han's controlled Xiangfu Company held 32.36%, 29.73%, 28.81%, totaling about 70% jointly,足以 influencing major decisions. Second, Vivame's "2018 First Interim Shareholders' Meeting Resolution" appointed Guo as head of the audit committee. WeChat records, witness statements, etc., show Guo had decision-making power over important appointments (finance, legal, directors, supervisors). Third, after the repurchase trigger, Guo communicated with the plaintiff multiple times, proposed repurchase plans, and chaired post-investment management meetings. Additionally, Guo jointly applied for bank credit guarantees with Han for Vivame's needs, represented Vivame in external negotiations, arranged financing, and held positions in Vivame's affiliated companies. Based on this, the court reasonably concluded that Guo actually participated in Vivame's management, knew about and agreed to the financing and repurchase obligations. The debt was for joint production/operation during marriage, thus constituting a joint marital debt. Guo should bear joint repayment liability. Guo's defense that her communications were post-investment management or goodwill assistance as a fund manager is inconsistent with common sense and rejected. In summary, the agreements are valid, repurchase conditions were triggered, Xiangfu Company and Han are liable for repurchase price and penalty. Han's debt is a joint marital debt, Guo bears joint repayment liability. Judgment: I. Xiangfu Company and Han shall pay the plaintiff Zhuhai Hengqin Leri Equity M&A Investment Fund Partnership (Limited Partnership) the repurchase amount within ten days of this judgment taking effect, including principal RMB 49,999,993.02 and profit (calculated from August 9, 2017, until actual payment, at 9% annual rate); II. Xiangfu Company and Han shall pay the plaintiff a penalty within ten days (based on RMB 57,458,902.98, from April 5, 2019, until actual payment, at 0.03% daily); III. Defendant Guo shall bear joint liability for Han's debts in items I and II. Reference: Case No.: (2019) Jing 03 Min Chu 395

Title: Court Ruling: Injuries sustained in a hotel bathroom fall during rest periods while attending an off-site meeting can be recognized as a work-related injury. Content: Basic Case Details: On April 1, 2019, Zhang checked into a hotel as required by the company to attend a meeting. That evening, while taking a shower in the guest room, Zhang slipped and fell due to a malfunctioning non-slip mat in the bathroom. Zhang was taken to the hospital for treatment the next day. The diagnosis concluded: injury to the medial meniscus of the right knee, fracture of the right tibial plateau, avulsion of the medial collateral ligament of the right knee, and osteochondral injury of the medial malleolus of the right femur. Zhang believed the injury was work-related and applied for recognition as a work-related injury. After investigation and verification, the Human Resources and Social Security Bureau recognized Zhang's injury as a work-related injury. The employer disagreed and filed a lawsuit with the People's Court. Case Proceedings: Both the first-instance and second-instance People's Courts upheld the specific administrative act of the Human Resources and Social Security Bureau recognizing the injury as work-related. The employer still disagreed and filed an application for retrial with the local Supreme People's Court. After hearing the case, the retrial court held that Zhang was an employee of the company's office and had checked into the hotel on April 1, 2019, at the company's request to attend a meeting. The fall occurred that evening while showering in the guest room, diagnosed as an avulsion of the medial collateral ligament of the right knee and an osteochondral injury of the medial condyle of the right femur. According to Item (5) of Article 14 of the Work-Related Injury Insurance Regulations, the period when an employee engages in job-related activities outside the workplace due to work reasons should be recognized as a period of business travel. Zhang checked into the hotel to attend a meeting as arranged by the company, which falls within the period of business travel. Accident injuries sustained during activities organized or arranged by the employer that are related to work can be considered as arising from work reasons. Zhang's injury from falling in the shower in the company-arranged room was therefore due to work reasons. This complies with the provisions of Article 5 of the "Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Work-Related Injury Insurance Administrative Cases": "If the social insurance administration department recognizes the following situations as 'during the period of business travel,' the People's Court shall support it: (1) the period when an employee is assigned by the employer or needs to engage in job-related activities outside the workplace due to work requirements; (2) the period when an employee is assigned by the employer to study or attend meetings outside; (3) the period of other outside activities required by work. If an employee is injured during personal activities unrelated to work or to being assigned by the employer to study or attend meetings during the business travel period, and the social insurance administration department does not recognize it as a work-related injury, the People's Court shall support it." Ultimately, the court rejected the employer's retrial request.

Title: Brokerage IPO Subscription Software Should Allow Investors to Subscribe with Clear Understanding Content: With the implementation of the full registration-based system, and in response to market calls and regulatory intervention, the 'one-click IPO subscription' function in brokerage app IPO subscription systems has finally been abolished. Now, when investors log into a brokerage app's IPO subscription system to apply for new shares, they can only subscribe to each new stock one by one when multiple new stocks are issued; 'one-click IPO subscription' has officially become history. This modification to the brokerage app IPO subscription system is very necessary. After all, 'one-click IPO subscription' was a product of the historical period when new stocks were issued at a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 23 times. At that time, the P/E ratios of new stock issuances were controlled below 23 times, which reserved some upside potential for the new stocks upon listing. Therefore, new stock listings were basically 'guaranteed not to fail'; investors could essentially earn a risk-free 'IPO subscription' profit as long as they were allocated shares. Thus, whenever new stocks were issued, investors could subscribe without risk. It was precisely in this market environment that the 'one-click IPO subscription' function in brokerage apps emerged. After all, at that time, IPO subscription was a benefit, and 'one-click IPO subscription' conveniently met investors' needs. However, the implementation of the full registration-based system has ended the risk-free era of IPO subscription, instead filling it with risks. Under the full registration-based system, new stock issuances are no longer subject to the 23-times P/E ratio limit; issuance P/E ratios can reach dozens or even hundreds of times. New stocks can fall below their issue price on the first day of listing, or even open below the issue price. The era of 'new stocks never failing' is over. Consequently, investors must consider the risks involved and subscribe selectively, rather than subscribing to every new issue. Therefore, 'one-click IPO subscription' no longer meets the needs of investors under the full registration-based system, making modifications to brokerage app IPO subscription systems inevitable. However, judging from the changes made to some brokerage app IPO subscription systems, although the 'one-click' mode is gone, what remains for investors is still a confusing situation. Investors are essentially subscribing in a daze, finding it difficult to make clear, informed decisions. The reason for this is that the brokerage app IPO subscription systems do not provide investors with the basis for making correct choices; entering the subscription system puts investors into a 'confusion mode'. For example, when entering some brokerage app IPO subscription systems, investors are greeted with the brokerage's 'Friendly Reminders'. These remind investors that new stocks may fall below the issue price after listing, urge investors to fully understand all risk factors of the issuer and participate prudently in IPO subscriptions, remind investors to fulfill fund settlement obligations based on the allocation results, ensuring sufficient funds in their accounts before the close of the allocation payment day (shortfalls are considered as abandoned subscriptions), and inform investors that if they fail to make full payment after being allocated shares three times cumulatively within 12 months, they will be barred from participating in new stock subscriptions for 6 months. Such 'Friendly Reminders' are certainly necessary for investors. However, providing only these reminders is clearly insufficient. Since the brokerages' 'Friendly Reminders' advise investors to fully understand the issuer's risk factors, the brokerage app IPO subscription system should provide relevant information to enable investors to do so, facilitating informed investment decisions on whether to subscribe or not. Unfortunately, some current brokerage app IPO subscription systems lack this service, making it difficult for investors to understand the potential investment risks of the issuer through the app. Therefore, to allow investors to subscribe with clear understanding and truly enable them to fully grasp the issuer's risk factors, brokerage app IPO subscription systems need further improvement. For instance, by clicking on the issuer's stock name or code, the system could display the issuer's relevant materials or links to such materials, allowing investors to make correct decisions by reading them. This would transform IPO subscription from a懵懵懂懂 (muddled) process to an明明白白 (clear and understood) one. This should be a mandatory feature for brokerage app IPO subscription systems. The relevant issuer materials that should be displayed by the brokerage app IPO subscription system should at least include the following aspects: the P/E ratio of the new stock issuance and the average P/E ratio of listed companies in the same industry; the issuer's performance over the past three years; the issuer's position within the industry and its core competitiveness; the issuer's development plans for the coming years; and various investment risks disclosed in the prospectus. Through such relevant information, investors can have a clear understanding of the issuer's investment risks and decide whether to participate in the subscription. Unlike the current situation with some brokerage app IPO subscription systems, where relevant materials are essentially unavailable, leaving investors subscribing completely 'in the dark' – a situation that clearly cannot continue.

Title: Excuse me, I don't agree with your statement that villas have poor investment value. I believe villas are definitely the next investment hotspot and will start to boom within three years at most. Reasons are as follows: 1. Villas come with land, while other flat-type apartments do not have the land attribute. Even in third-tier cities, land costs at least 5,000 RMB per square meter. 200 square meters of land is worth 1 million RMB. In Beijing, it will only be higher; outside the Fifth Ring Road, it's at least 30,000 RMB per square meter. 2. Referring to the United States, villas are the standard for middle-class families, and this is the same in all cities. If China's economy develops, it will inevitably progress from basic subsistence to a quality life. Civilization progresses step by step upwards. 3. Don't criticize housing prices with an attitude of 'I'm poor so I don't believe it'. Your lack of money doesn't mean others lack it. You can't afford a villa, but many people can. Although I am not wealthy either, a villa is my ultimate dream and also the goal for everyone to settle down and live happily. Given Beijing's income level, more and more people will be able to afford villas in the future. 4. As the population decreases, people will no longer pursue education and basic urban amenities, but instead seek green and environmentally friendly options in the suburbs. This is the advanced goal of humanity. 5. Currently, the state restricts the number of villas, which will further push up villa prices. Scarcity increases value. The scarcer a commodity is, the more it stimulates people's investment desire. This is like refrigerators and color TVs 40 years ago, which were very expensive, but more people wanted to buy them, and they eventually became standard for middle-class families. Content: 1. Let's go through this point by point. All properties have a land attribute, including apartments and commercial shops, as well as various flat-type ordinary residences. Villas simply have an independent plot. But this isn't very useful in China because even rural homesteads aren't allowed to be built freely, let alone commercial housing. So the land is just a formality; it doesn't have a separate function and thus no special value. Let's compare prices. For example, in the Central Villa Area, there are plenty of single-family villas costing tens of thousands per square meter, while flat-type apartments aren't much cheaper. So where is the land value reflected? Why would it appreciate separately in the future? 2. Because there are too many homeless people and 'zero-dollar shopping' (looting) in the urban areas of large American cities, leading to poor safety and environment. Title: In South Korea, going to the cinema to watch a movie has become a "luxury consumption"? Content: Source: Global Times [Global Times Comprehensive Report] Recently, famous South Korean actor Choi Min-sik suggested lowering movie ticket prices on the MBC talk show "Son Seok-hee's Question," sparking widespread discussion in society about movie ticket prices. The Asian Daily reported on the 16th that whether the reason for the decrease in cinema audiences is solely due to ticket prices is worth exploring. The current weekend 2D screening ticket prices at major South Korean cinema chains such as CJ CGV, Lotte Cinema, and Megabox are 15,000 won (approximately 80 yuan), which is an increase compared to the pre-pandemic price of 12,000 won. However, according to the "Film Industry Settlement" report, the average spending per cinema-goer in South Korea in the first half of this year was 9,768 won. Compared to pre-pandemic levels, the average increase in spending per viewer is only 15.7%. File photo: On May 1, 2024, local time, in Seoul, South Korea, movie fans enter a cinema to watch "The Roundup 4." (Visual China) The Kyunghyang Shinmun reported that Kim, an office worker in his 20s, used to go to the cinema once or twice a month before the pandemic, but in the past year, the number of times he has been to the cinema can be counted on one hand. He said, "I rarely go to the cinema recently. The price of watching one movie is more expensive than a month's subscription fee for an OTT (Internet TV platform)." The report also stated that the number of people going to cinemas is significantly decreasing. According to the Filmmakers Association, composed of 16 groups including the Korean Independent Film Association, as of August 25th, the number of theater audiences this year reached 84.5 million, only 56% of the same period in 2019. The Filmmakers Association stated that the three price increases by major South Korean cinema chains from 2020 to 2022 are the main reason for the downturn in the film industry. In June this year, organizations including the Korean Film Workers Union reported to the Korea Fair Trade Commission, suspecting that the three multiplex cinema chains CJ CGV, Lotte Cinema, and Megabox colluded on movie ticket prices. They argued, "During the three years of the pandemic, the three multiplex chains raised the standard weekend ticket price from 12,000 won to 15,000 won. Now that the pandemic is over and the cinemas are profitable again, they should revert to the previous price." According to reports, investigations show that South Korea's movie ticket prices are higher than those in other major countries. According to the global price statistics website numbeo, the average movie ticket price in South Korea is $11.17, ranking 27th among 96 countries and regions worldwide. It ranks 9th among the G20 major economies, placing it at an average level. However, the ratio of ticket price to per capita GDP is 0.033%, which is higher than that of the United States (0.016%), Germany (0.025%), and the United Kingdom (0.027%). This is why consumers perceive movie ticket prices as relatively high. According to the "Consumer Behavior Survey Results" published last year by the Korean Film Council, the largest proportion of respondents (38.9%) considered an appropriate movie ticket price to be "8,000-10,000 won." Some South Korean media even claimed that watching movies in South Korea has become a "luxury consumption." Although some netizens complain that ticket prices are too high, there are also views suggesting that actual ticket prices have not significantly increased due to discount offers. The logic behind cinemas insisting on providing ticket discounts lies in pursuing economies of scale. However, whether lowering prices can effectively attract audiences back remains unknown. Audiences have become accustomed to diverse entertainment options, and the challenges facing cinemas may extend beyond just price issues. (Han Jing)

Title: Intangible Cultural Heritage: Visiting the Danba Cultural Business Card Exhibition Hall Content: In the summer, Danba is shaded by green trees and scorched by the blazing sun. In the afternoon, while strolling through the streets, the reporter was attracted by a uniquely Jiarong-style antique building in the center of the county town. Logs served as pillars, and stone slabs built the walls. The variety of colors, the quaint charm, the Jiarong beauty leaning against the wall, and the unique appearance suggested that the interior must be "a hidden gem." Upon closer inspection, the reporter learned that this building is Danba County's newly popular tourist destination—the Intangible Cultural Heritage Exhibition Hall. Passing through the ancient-style gate and entering the hall, what greeted the eyes was an ancient folk textile craft. An elderly Tibetan woman sat intently before an antique-like loom, concentrating on weaving cloth. She smiled in response to tourists but did not stop her work. Yong Tianxiu, over 60 years old, has been learning weaving since her teens and has never stopped. As looms gradually became obsolete, Yong Tianxiu has become a "living fossil" inheriting this ancient craft. When the Intangible Cultural Heritage Exhibition Hall opened, Yong Tianxiu voluntarily offered to demonstrate Danba textile techniques to tourists for free. "I love Danba embroidery and textile crafts; I usually do them at home too. Now my eyes aren't very good, so I can't do embroidery anymore. Tourists enjoy watching me weave here, and I explain everything when they have questions." The ancient Jiarong textile techniques, through Yong Tianxiu's hands, are gradually becoming known to people, and countless photos of tourists with her have been shared online. Thanks to her live demonstrations, the sales of pure handmade cloth, valued at 600 yuan per bolt, have been steadily rising. Yong Tianxiu's handiwork, honed over many years, has finally found its "purpose" in the exhibition hall. Folk customs, labor scenes, religious practices, and daily life—almost every aspect of Jiarong Tibetan culture can be traced within the exhibition hall. The reporter learned that the hall houses one national-level, four provincial-level, and several prefectural-level intangible cultural heritage projects. Since its completion and opening in October 2014, it has received nearly 40,000 visitors in less than a year. Currently, the exhibition hall does not charge an entrance fee; the main收费 items are the café in the leisure area and specialty products. Speaking about the creation of the exhibition hall, Luo Bujiata, Director of the Danba County Culture, Tourism, Radio, Television, and Sports Bureau, expressed deep feelings: "We pondered a lot about the question, 'What exactly is intangible cultural heritage?' Intangible cultural heritage is not just about protection; more importantly, it should be about display and inheritance. Therefore, the Intangible Cultural Heritage Exhibition Hall we created, especially the key 'Jiarong Artisan Workshop,' bears the responsibility of reshaping the soul of Danba's intangible cultural heritage. The exhibition hall is a window for promoting Danba's intangible cultural heritage and even more so a window for displaying folk culture." As Luo Bujiata said, every part of the Danba Intangible Cultural Heritage Exhibition Hall showcases the local folk customs. The distinctive ethnic window carvings incorporating Gesang flowers and Duodeng Meiduo, the reconstructed walls of Danba watchtowers, and even the "fire alarm"—a pig's bladder—used on ancient stoves decades ago are reproduced in the hall. Undoubtedly, the Danba County Intangible Cultural Heritage Exhibition Hall plays a pivotal role in exhibiting, displaying, recording, preserving, and managing Danba's intangible culture. Amid these ancient artifacts and vivid live displays, a sense of Danba's historical and cultural atmosphere envelops visitors.

Title: Does dysmenorrhea have any adverse effects? Content: Hello: Dysmenorrhea can be divided into two types: primary and secondary. Primary dysmenorrhea is mostly caused by uterine hypoplasia, narrow cervical os, excessive uterine flexion, or membranous menstruation, i.e., the expulsion of large pieces of thickened endometrium or endometrial casts causing intense uterine contractions. Secondary dysmenorrhea is mostly caused by reproductive organ lesions such as pelvic inflammation, endometriosis, tumors, etc. It is recommended that you go to the hospital for a detailed examination to identify the cause and receive targeted treatment! Wishing you good health! You can also check out the introduction of related symptoms at Quanzhou Dongfang Gynecology Hospital's website.

Title: The Five Major Pitfalls of Resumes Content: 1. Being older and unmarried - don't emphasize it, many companies will silently filter out your resume. 2. The best approach is not to mention it unless the interviewer asks. 3. Don't include entrepreneurial experience - few companies like people who have started businesses; they are seen as too ambitious and unlikely to settle into the job. 4. Avoid frequent job-hopping; no matter how many years you've worked, keep your work history to no more than 5 positions, otherwise you'll eliminate yourself. 5. Being an older junior employee - having worked 10 or 8 years and still doing miscellaneous tasks offers poor cost-effectiveness. How many of these apply to you?

Title: News Update丨Party Secretary Liu Xiaotao Holds Expert Symposium on Ancient City Renewal, Dean Wu Yongfa Attends Content: Recently, Suzhou Municipal Party Committee Secretary Liu Xiaotao presided over an expert symposium on the protection and renewal of the ancient city, listening to opinions and suggestions face-to-face and discussing plans for protection and development. Dean Wu Yongfa of our institute was invited to attend and speak, sharing insights and work suggestions on topics such as improving the ancient city protection plan and enhancing the urban living environment. At the meeting, Wu Yongfa proposed three views on the ancient city protection and renewal work. First, a multi-scale, gradual, and micro-renewal protection method under systematic thinking is an important foundation for ancient city protection. It is necessary to adjust and optimize the functional structure of the ancient city, propose solutions from multiple dimensions such as the city, blocks, and buildings, and lead the comprehensive improvement of ancient city protection through demonstration cases. Second, the distinctive features of the ancient city's water system and spatial texture are important aspects of ancient city protection. The integrity of the ancient city's water system characteristics and spatial texture should be maintained, preserving the urban spatial characteristics that have continued for thousands of years and inheriting the wisdom of traditional Chinese human settlement creation. Third, scientific decision-making led by overall coordination is an effective means for ancient city protection. As one of the first batch of urban renewal pilot cities designated by the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, Suzhou continuously implements new policies and measures for ancient city protection, strengthening a multi-party consultation and co-construction governance approach to urban renewal. Relying on national-level professional platforms to enhance the systematic nature of ancient city protection has become an effective means to ensure scientific decision-making in ancient city protection. The China-Portugal Joint Laboratory for Cultural Heritage Protection Science under the Belt and Road Initiative, as a national-level innovation technology platform, plays a significant supporting role in Suzhou's scientific coordination of ancient city protection, urban renewal, and livelihood improvement, and should take on this responsibility to provide innovative momentum for Suzhou's urban development and cultural heritage. Liu Xiaotao listened carefully and responded to the experts' speeches. He emphasized that ancient city protection efforts should focus on three aspects: "continuation, multiplicity, and innovation." "Continuation" emphasizes inheriting traditions, preserving the Jiangnan water town气质 and the unique lifestyle of the ancient city, while also focusing on sustainable development, upholding correctness and fostering innovation. "Multiplicity" involves multi-objective coordination, multi-element development, multi-stakeholder participation, and multi-method implementation to enhance the ancient city's distinctiveness and promote characteristic development. "Innovation" requires strengthening policy innovation, mechanism innovation, technological innovation, and format innovation, developing through protection and protecting through development, revitalizing the ancient city with innovation and entrepreneurial vitality. Meanwhile, he emphasized that when facing complex issues in ancient city protection, the professional role of universities and laboratories in technological innovation should be fully utilized. Source丨Suzhou Daily, China-Portugal Joint Laboratory for Cultural Heritage Protection Science

Title: BTV Overseas Student Chen Hua: How to Choose a Major for Studying Abroad as a Junior Translation Student at Sichuan International Studies University? Content: Student Background: Student Li: Junior in Translation at Sichuan International Studies University, Second Foreign Language: French, Average Score: 84.76, IELTS: 6. Goals: Master's in accounting, business, or education-related majors in Canada or Australia. BTV Overseas Student Teacher Chen Hua's View: First, analyzing from a country perspective, you currently lean towards Australia or Canada. Australia and Canada share some common characteristics: first, they are both Commonwealth countries; second, they have very rich tourism resources. So, from the perspective of your major and interests, these two countries meet your needs. If we compare further, Canada, being closer to North America, might offer more opportunities in terms of tourism or employment if you seek broader prospects in the future. From a macro market perspective, North America has advantages in tourism patterns, industry formats, and resource strengths. Therefore, between these two countries, I might lean towards Canada, as it could offer you more diversity. Regarding majors, first, I must advise against choosing accounting. In all my student consultations, the first thing I do is help students clarify their personal attributes and the attributes of the major they want to study. Personal attributes and major attributes must match; only then can you study well, progress far, and sustain long-term. If they don't match, you will inevitably encounter obstacles and might have to give up eventually. Accounting requires a strong sense of rules; it doesn't allow you to deviate, as everything must follow accounting principles. However, what you've shown us is that you desire to go out, travel, seek change, and value freedom. I think your personal attributes are extremely incompatible with accounting, so I suggest excluding that option first. If you want to balance a career with your interest in travel and hobbies, there are three broad major directions you can consider. First is media. Personally, I suggest avoiding news, communication, theory, culture, religion, etc. You could lean towards digital media. If you want to do live streaming, what you lack is technical skills. Digital media can provide you with a skill set—what skills you should have in editing, clipping, and effects presentation—and directly support your interests. The second broad direction is tourism management, hotel management, resort management, etc., because working in this industry allows you to engage with new tourism formats, sales methods, people's vacation styles, and overall planning. Another broad direction is marketing, where you need to meet different people, perceive different business formats, and think about how to sell various products. If you acquire these skills and find a solution that supports your career financially, you'll be closer to achieving your dream of traveling more and farther. So, broadly speaking, you can choose among these three majors. Title: Drunk Driving Through Checkpoint Causes 1 Death, Criminal Detention! | Frontline Microscopy Content: Around 19:50 on the evening of April 8th, in Rugao City, Jiangsu Province. Feng, driving under the influence of alcohol, encountered a traffic police check. To avoid punishment, he first slowed down pretending to cooperate, then suddenly slammed the accelerator and rushed through the checkpoint. During his escape, he hit a pedestrian and a car, causing the pedestrian to die on the spot. Feng did not stop there but continued to accelerate and flee, ultimately crashing into another parked car by the roadside before abandoning his vehicle and fleeing the scene. Around 00:50 on the morning of the 9th, under strong pursuit pressure from the police, the suspect Feng turned himself in at the traffic police brigade accompanied by relatives and friends. A blood test revealed his blood alcohol content was 83.2mg/100ml, constituting drunk driving. Ultimately, Feng was criminally detained for the crime of causing a traffic accident and fleeing the scene. In the detention center, he finally expressed regret: "I am sorry to the victim's family, I know the pain of losing a loved one, I am truly sorry!" Currently, for drunk driving through a checkpoint, fleeing, and continuing to drive causing consecutive accidents resulting in one death and damage to multiple vehicles, Feng has been placed under investigation on suspicion of endangering public safety by dangerous means. If convicted, he faces over ten years in prison. Information source: Traffic Management Bureau of the Ministry of Public Security

Title: Is Starbucks Hazelnut Chocolate Waffle Cake Delicious? Content: As we all know, Starbucks is a very popular coffee beverage shop that launches many new products with different flavors every year, including various flavored dessert cakes. The Hazelnut Chocolate Waffle Cake is a new product that was just recently released. So, is Starbucks Hazelnut Chocolate Waffle Cake delicious? Let's take a closer look below! How much does a Starbucks Hazelnut Chocolate Waffle Cake cost? Price: 39 RMB. When I saw the picture, I thought it would be super large, but when I got it, it was okay, just the size of their regular cakes. It's a banana chocolate-flavored cake in the shape of a waffle. The surface has chocolate crisps, crushed nuts, mango and strawberry bits, and a few small marshmallows, topped with a chocolate drizzle. The filling is hazelnut paste paired with chocolate mousse. The texture is delicate and smooth, with a rich chocolate flavor. The waffle cake is fluffy and soft. With one bite, you get multiple textures and flavors – delicious and satisfying! The surface has crushed nuts, dried fruits, crispy chocolate chips, and marshmallows. The waffle overall is on the moist and soft side. There is chocolate spread between the layers, but the chocolate flavor is very subtle. When I tried it first thing in the morning with a bland palate, I almost couldn't taste it and even detected a hint of banana flavor! In terms of sweetness, it's definitely a bit milder than the mousse varieties. The layer of syrup on the surface is slightly sweet. Overall, it's okay, but it doesn't quite live up to the hazelnut-chocolate theme of its name~ Is Starbucks Hazelnut Chocolate Waffle Cake delicious? This is a banana chocolate cake in the shape of a waffle. Top layer: Decorated with chocolate crisps, crushed nuts, mango bits, strawberry bits, and marshmallow bits, with a chocolate-flavored drizzle. Filling: Uses hazelnut paste combined with chocolate-flavored mousse. This cake is banana chocolate flavored. The very top is a layer of crispy chocolate chips, decorated with some nuts, marshmallows, etc. The filling is hazelnut paste and chocolate mousse. The overall texture of the waffle is quite soft. Even though it's chocolate flavored, this cake really isn't cloying! It's not an extremely rich chocolate cake but has a slight banana flavor. (However, eating it gives a feeling like a Holichewy pie, haha). With the first bite, the chocolate sauce melts in your mouth bringing a wave of sweetness, then the banana flavor slowly emerges. Chewing carefully reveals a rich texture from the various ingredients, reminiscent of breakfast cereals. The overall texture has hints of early brownies, but the waffle body is softer and the sweetness is relatively high, making it suitable to pair with an oat latte. This cake is actually quite substantial; one person might get full eating it! Pairing it with cold brew or pour-over coffee while eating is also very good~ How does the Starbucks Hazelnut Chocolate Waffle Cake taste? The Hazelnut Chocolate Waffle Cake leans towards being very sweet because the ingredients are particularly rich, the cake volume is large, and it's quite dense. If you already find Starbucks' classic cakes very sweet and cloying, then you might want to skip this one. The flavor is chocolate banana. I'm not sure if the banana is mixed into the paste or into the waffle itself, but the banana component is 100% present. You can tell from the pictures the heavy, layer upon layer of ingredients; this 39 RMB is still good value for money. The texture of the waffle is moist and dense. Eaten with the filling paste, it's not dry at all, just sweet. All in all, I personally quite like this new product; it just depends on individual taste. Trying it for the novelty is fine, but it still can't surpass the New York Cheesecake.

Title: Guangxi Youjiang: Illuminating the Better Lives of Individuals with Mental Health Conditions through Skillful Hands Content: Under the promotion of the Baise Civil Affairs Bureau, the Guangxi Jiahe Social Work Service Center has been innovatively carrying out community rehabilitation services for mental disorders since July 2024, using the "Laoxiang Jiayuan" resettlement community in Youjiang District as a community rehabilitation site. By introducing diversified intervention methods such as handicraft activities and community participation, they have built a bridge for individuals with mental health conditions to integrate into society, empowering them to actively participate. Xiao Li (pseudonym), an individual with a mental health condition who relocated to Laoxiang Jiayuan, always felt unfamiliar with her surroundings and was affected by her illness and medication side effects, leaving her trapped in a monotonous cycle of housework and television, falling into the predicament of "blunted thinking and social isolation." Xiao Li once confided in a social worker: "Staying at home for long periods makes me feel my thinking is getting slower and slower." During the service process, "rebuilding social function and integrating into community life" were the main rehabilitation goals. The social workers empowered Xiao Li and aided her recovery using a "three-step" service strategy. First, emotional connection: guiding Xiao Li to participate in community activities as a volunteer, gradually building interpersonal trust and a sense of community belonging through interaction with residents. Second, skill development: the social worker led Xiao Li in trying to make handmade flowers, stimulating her manual dexterity and creativity through repeated training, allowing her to master a skill and possess a pair of skillful hands. Third, value realization: the social worker accompanied Xiao Li in starting a handmade craft business, helping her gain economic income and self-identity. Today, Xiao Li has transformed from "I don't know what I can do" to "I can create value," achieving a leap from passive care recipient to active social participant. She exclaimed emotionally: "I really earned money, I'm so happy! Doing this (handicrafts) not only gives me income but also makes my life less monotonous." Compared to disease treatment, the reconstruction of social function and the development of potential are the longer-term goals of community rehabilitation for mental disorders. Individuals with mental health conditions ultimately need to integrate into society and continue living. Using handicrafts as a platform for service, enabling more individuals like Xiao Li to participate, break out of their daily closed environments, receive professional rehabilitation training, and regain self-esteem and confidence for a better life, is what the social work team has been consistently doing. The picture above shows the social worker leading Xiao Li in learning to make handmade flowers. In the future, Jiahe Social Workers will continue to uphold the service tenet of "demand-oriented, people-centered," deeply explore the needs of the mental health population, innovate service delivery models, use precise individual rehabilitation and diversified group services to weave a social support network, and use systematic and comprehensive professional services to stimulate the potential of individuals with mental health conditions, drive the pace of social integration, and assist them in achieving stable recovery and regaining a wonderful life! Contribution: Guangxi Jiahe Social Work Service Center Baise City Mental Disorder Community Rehabilitation Service Project (Youjiang District)

Title: Buying Pets Online Also Requires Caution Content: Nowadays, more and more people enjoy keeping pets. Buying pets online is favored by many due to its price advantage. However, there are currently few formal platforms for pet transactions, making it a 'gambling-like' consumption for buyers. They may face situations such as being blocked after payment or receiving pets without any guarantees. 1. On January 2, 2021, Mr. Cao from Kunshan reported to the police that he bought a cat on WeChat. After agreeing on a price, he paid the other party 5400 yuan by binding his mobile phone to the WeChat account. The other party then kept making excuses not to ship the cat. When Mr. Cao requested a refund, the other party refused. Mr. Cao later realized he had been scammed. 2. On January 4, 2021, Mr. Wang from the Industrial Park reported to the police that he saw information about a 'Pet Home Center' in a Weibo comment regarding free pet adoption. He paid a total of 5418 yuan for shipping and taxes via a link provided by the other party. The other party then continued to ask Mr. Wang for more money. Mr. Wang realized it was a scam and reported it. 3. On January 25, 2021, Mr. Zhou from Suzhou bought a pet dog online and transferred 400 yuan to the seller via WeChat. He later found that he could no longer contact the seller and realized he had been scammed. Police reminder: Most people lack a reasonable understanding of pets and decide to buy them based solely on an online picture. Besides using formal online trading platforms, regardless of what you are buying, citizens should never pay in advance. Choosing cash on delivery or using third-party institutions like Alipay is safer.

Title: Eczema keeps recurring, how can it be cured? Content: At 3 a.m., have you ever been tormented by an unbearable itch that prevents you from sleeping? The moment you scratch your skin raw, a burning pain and an uncontrollable urge to scratch pull you back and forth. Finally, when the itching subsides, you find the affected area even more red, swollen, and oozing the next day, so painful that even clothes brushing against it make you grimace. This might be eczema "acting up". Today, let's talk about what to do if you get eczema! Clinical Manifestations Atopic dermatitis, also known as eczema, is characterized by dry skin and intense itching, but its clinical manifestations vary greatly. Acute eczema is characterized by intensely itchy red papules and blisters, accompanied by exudation and crusting; subacute or chronic lesions present as dry, scaly, or exfoliative red papules. Skin thickening (lichenification) and fissures caused by long-term scratching may gradually appear. Many patients may have lesions at different stages simultaneously. Severe cases can affect any part of the body in all age groups, but it is less common in the armpits, buttocks, or groin areas. If lesions appear in these areas, other diagnoses such as psoriasis, allergic contact dermatitis, or seborrheic dermatitis should be considered. Additionally, eczema has regional variants including: atopic hand eczema, eyelid eczema, and atopic cheilitis. Based on the impact on quality of life and psychosocial health, it is classified into three levels of severity: mild, moderate, and severe. Impact on Life: ● Mild: Localized dry skin, infrequent itching (with or without small areas of redness); minimal impact on daily activities, sleep, and psychosocial health. ● Moderate: Localized dry skin, frequent itching, redness (with or without skin breakdown from scratching and localized skin thickening); moderate impact on daily activities and psychosocial health, often affecting sleep. ● Severe: Widespread dry skin, persistent itching, redness (with or without skin breakdown from scratching, widespread skin thickening, bleeding, oozing, fissures, and pigment changes); severe limitations in daily activities and psychosocial function, significant nighttime sleep loss. General Management Approaches: Eliminating Aggravating Factors — Some factors can damage the already abnormal epidermal barrier in patients with atopic dermatitis, including excessive bathing without subsequent moisturizing, dry environments, stress, xerosis (dry skin), skin overheating (e.g., sun exposure, saunas, hot baths), and exposure to solvents and detergents. Avoiding these situations helps prevent acute flares and is beneficial for long-term management. Although there is debate about whether environmental or food allergies are aggravating factors for atopic dermatitis, if you know you are allergic or intolerant to a certain food, it's best to avoid it. (Avoid direct contact with irritants) Contact Allergens — Atopic individuals are more prone to allergic contact dermatitis from nickel and many topical treatment ingredients (e.g., fragrances, preservatives, neomycin). Allergic contact dermatitis should be suspected when a patient does not respond to appropriate topical treatment or when the affected area spreads beyond common flexural areas. Skin Moisturization: Emollients and Moisturizers — Skin moisturization is key to the overall treatment of patients with atopic dermatitis. To maintain skin hydration, emollients should be used at least twice daily, immediately after bathing or washing hands. Thick creams with low water content or water-free ointments (e.g., petroleum jelly) are generally preferred as they better prevent dryness. If patients find ointments or thick creams too greasy, lotions can be chosen. It is best to apply emollients immediately after bathing when the skin's water content is high. (Skin moisturization is key to the overall treatment of patients with atopic dermatitis.) Bathing: Bathing Frequency — Warm water soaking baths or showers using mild or soap-free cleansers should be part of the routine skin care for patients with atopic dermatitis. Whether showering or bathing, it is important to apply emollients and/or topical prescription preparations immediately afterwards. The use of bath additives for treating atopic dermatitis is not recommended. Controlling Itching: Non-pharmacological Interventions — The foundation of treating atopic itch is optimal skin hydration and topical anti-inflammatory therapy. Warm water soaking baths to hydrate and cool the skin, followed by emollient application, can help relieve itching. For more severe cases, wet wrap therapy (wet dressings) can help soothe the skin, reduce itching, and interrupt the itch-scratch cycle by limiting skin access. Apply an emollient to the skin first, then wrap the affected area with a damp cotton cloth, covered by a dry layer. The damp cloth should not be allowed to dry out completely. These dressings can be used overnight if tolerated, or changed every few hours during the day. Some moisturizers contain anti-itch ingredients such as phenol, menthol, and camphor. Patients with Mild to Moderate Atopic Dermatitis: • Initial Treatment – For patients with mild to moderate atopic dermatitis, initial treatment with topical corticosteroids and emollients is recommended. Mild: Low-potency corticosteroid cream or ointment: 0.05% desonide or 2.5% hydrocortisone. Moderate: Medium to high-potency corticosteroids: 0.025% fluocinolone acetonide, 0.1% triamcinolone acetonide, or 0.05% betamethasone dipropionate. For acute flares, ultra-high or high-potency topical corticosteroids can be used for no more than 2 weeks (e.g., 0.05% clobetasol propionate, 0.25% dexamethasone, 0.005% fluticasone propionate), then switched to a lower potency preparation until the lesions resolve. If a patient with atopic dermatitis has lesions in areas at high risk for atrophy from corticosteroid use (e.g., face and skin folds), treatment with topical calcineurin inhibitors is recommended (tacrolimus ointment and pimecrolimus cream). Long-term, widespread use of topical corticosteroids (especially high or ultra-high potency formulations) on the body can lead to adrenal suppression. Other adverse effects include skin thinning, telangiectasia, folliculitis, and contact dermatitis. Here, Class 5-8 has compiled a short rhyme to help everyone remember. Second-line Therapy – Second-line therapies for mild to moderate atopic dermatitis include crisaborole (for adults and children) and topical ruxolitinib (for adults and children over 12 years old). Proactive Treatment – For adolescents and adults with mild to moderate atopic dermatitis that responds to ongoing topical treatment, proactive treatment with topical corticosteroids or topical calcineurin inhibitors is recommended to prevent recurrence. Apply topical corticosteroids or topical calcineurin inhibitors once daily, for two consecutive days per week, for up to 16 weeks. Patients with Moderate to Severe Atopic Dermatitis: For adults and children with moderate to severe atopic dermatitis that does not respond to topical treatment alone, dupilumab is recommended as first-line therapy, rather than non-targeted immunosuppressants. Tralokinumab, abrocitinib, and upadacitinib are newly approved drugs that can be used as alternatives for adult patients who have an inadequate response to dupilumab. When conditions permit and the patient accepts it, narrowband ultraviolet B (NB-UVB) phototherapy can also be chosen as a first-line therapy for adults and adolescents with moderate to severe atopic dermatitis. Phototherapy is usually administered in a hospital setting, 2-3 times per week. During phototherapy, topical corticosteroids and emollients can be continued as needed.
