Title: Don't always think about taking advantage when buying wine, beware of being scammed! Content: I've heard countless friends say the phrase "the wine industry is very murky." To be honest, which industry isn't murky? But there are indeed some unfair competitive practices that easily mislead consumers. We have summarized the major tricks in the wine industry, hoping everyone will understand them and beware of being deceived! Fake Wine Counterfeiting is the most stubborn chronic disease in the wine industry. Common fake wines in China mainly take the following two forms: 01. Genuine bottle, correct label and vintage, but the wine has been refilled. The market for top-tier wine bottles is particularly active. It was once reported that an empty Château Lafite Rothschild bottle could sell for over a thousand yuan. This is because counterfeiters, after buying the genuine bottle, can refill it with other wine and sell it at a high price. This is particularly difficult to authenticate. You can try to identify it by checking if the capsule, cork, or label have been re-glued to secure them. 02. Fake bottle, fake label, fake cork, and fake capsule. This type of fake wine is very common and cheap in China, so its counterfeit traces are also easily spotted. For example, incorrect label information, label paper lacking texture and three-dimensional feel, poorly made capsules, etc. Taking Penfolds 407 as an example, there are many fakes on the market now, with lots of poorly made ones; the raised logos on many counterfeits are not three-dimensional or smooth enough. In November 2017, Hongkou District, Shanghai cracked a major case of producing and selling counterfeit brand red wine, seizing over 14,000 bottles of counterfeit "Penfolds" brand red wine, with a case value exceeding RMB 10 million. In March 2018, Zhengzhou dismantled a criminal gang producing and selling fake Penfolds wine, seizing over 8,000 cases of fake wine, with a case value as high as RMB 18 million. Brother reminds everyone to always choose reliable channels and brands when buying wine, and never be greedy for small bargains. If you come across Lafite or Latour for a few hundred yuan, Romanée-Conti for a few hundred, or Penfolds for tens of yuan, don't even think about it – they are definitely fake. Knockoff Goods Knockoff wines mainly involve riding on the coattails of famous châteaux and brands. The most common example in China is Château Lafite Rothschild, a Bordeaux First Growth that is always imitated but never successfully copied. For instance, the famous '82 Lafite might occasionally appear as "82年拉飞" (82 La Fei). This is a rather crude knockoff. Let's look at some slightly more clever ones: Doesn't this label look very similar to Bordeaux's "King of Wines," Petrus? But why does Chairman Mao appear... and the English name is "PATUSI." This wine also looks very familiar. Isn't that tower the symbol of the Bordeaux First Growth Château Latour? Look closer, the label says "LA TURE". Brother truly admires this knockoff. Château Latour also has a Clos du Marquis wine with a yellow label, which they imitated as well. Uninformed consumers might really think this is a third wine from Latour. There was also the sensational "Lafei" case. It is said that a company used the name "Lafei" years ago. Château Lafite Rothschild complained and sued them, but the court ruled in favor of the legality of "Lafei". Brother laughed again; the Rothschild family probably never encountered counterfeit power like that in our great China. The most impressive part is that the label pattern looks almost identical to real Lafite, and it even bears the slogan "China's Only Legal Lafei." Knockoff manufacturers' tricks are endless. The secret to identifying knockoffs is passed around like a folk rhyme: Maotai plus a 'Zhen' (town), be cautious when buying. Luzhou without 'Laojiao', turn back immediately. Fen Jiu plus 'Jituan' (Group), basically finished. Xifeng without 'Jiu' (wine), must avoid. Wuliangye without 'Ye', buying it is a sin. Yanghe, Haitian, Meng, don't touch the others. Gujing without 'Gong' (Tribute), drink it and bump into things. Jiannanchun without 'Chun' (Spring), don't ask if it's real. ... Bulk Imported Wine, Domestically Bottled Long ago, because of low shipping costs and less aging pressure, many quality wineries would transport their wine in bulk (Bulk Wine) to their distributors, who would then bottle and sell it themselves. Later, wineries found that more and more distributors started blending the wine, selling blended, bottled wine under the wineries' names, passing off inferior products as good. Actually, Bulk Wine is very profitable. For example, bulk wine juice from countries like Spain, Southern France, South Australia, Chile, etc., is sold by the ton, generally ranging from a few thousand to tens of thousands RMB per ton. After purchase, one ton can yield over a thousand 750ml bottles of red wine. These wines are sold in supermarkets for tens to hundreds of RMB per bottle. But unfortunately, blending became the trick for distributors to make money. There are some conscienceless merchants in China who import grape juice from abroad, blend and process it on fishing boats on the high seas, bottle it into bottles with original import labels, and then smuggle it into China as imported wine, passing customs inspection, paying duties, and selling it to their kind and lovely compatriots. Here, the bottled wine becomes the raw material for wine counterfeiting. The scariest part is that their procedures might be complete. You have to open the bottle, taste the garbage quality, and then realize the wine you bought doesn't match the label. Excessive Packaging, All Show No Substance Heavy bottle,浮雕 (relief) design, deep凹 (concave) bottom. Wooden cork, wax seal, metal label. Horizontal wooden case,硫酸纸 (parchment paper), leather box, wine tools must be included. "Packaging upgrade" has become an industry standard. Whether it's bottling plants without their own brands or wineries also doing OEM business, to meet the demands of importers, they more or less accept clients' custom packaging requirements. Importers seize on consumers' lack of expertise and虚荣 (vanity)心态 (mentality) for豪华 (luxurious) packaging, equipping some average-quality wines with super luxurious bottles, labels, and outer boxes, then transforming them to sell for a good price. Ironically, the whole world is talking about environmental protection and consumption downgrading, especially European countries hoping to use lighter bottles and screw caps. It can be said that only Asia, especially Chinese consumers, particularly like heavy-duty packaging: wide-shoulder bottles, deep punt, cork plus wax seal... Reserve, Special Reserve - Misleading Names Importers go to great lengths when naming their products to make them stand out among competitors or add a little weight to some essentially mediocre wines. For example: "Selected," "Special Selection," "Reserve," "Cuvée," "Grand Cuvée," "Grand Cru," "Family Reserve"... It's like dazzling flowers, which one is the synonym for good wine? Actually, except for Spain, which has clear minimum aging requirements for the three levels "Crianza," "Reserva," and "Gran Reserva," other countries have no clear definitions for similar terms above. But we find that wines from almost all countries use these terms on their labels to indicate the wine's grade. This hurts the wineries that work hard to make good wine and label it as Reserve or Family Reserve, because some wineries can use the cheapest wine and still label it as Reserve or Special Reserve... Grey Market Goods, Parallel Imports Speaking of "genuine goods," they also have three identities: Authorized Imports (行货), Grey Market (水货), and Parallel Imports (平行货). Authorized Imports are legitimately cleared through customs, genuine wine with genuine identity. Grey Market goods are smuggled in from Hong Kong, Macau, or other places, genuine wine but without proper identity. Parallel Imports are similar to cross-regional goods. For example, an Australian wine originally meant for South America is shipped to the Chinese market via South America, priced lower than what the Chinese agent offers. Grey market wine refers to wine that has not gone through Chinese customs clearance, tax payment, or commodity inspection, and therefore lacks a series of complex formal import procedures like the Chinese back label. It enters China through unclear channels and is sold illegally. The benefit of grey market goods, for the importing merchants, is naturally saving time, effort, and taxes. For consumers, the price is cheaper. But there are also many drawbacks. Wine coming through irregular channels, who knows if it's real? Who guarantees hygiene and safety? If there's a problem, who do you go to for a refund, exchange, or compensation? Probably only God can solve that. QR Code Hype, Inflated Prices For a long time, imported red wine, like luxury goods, has been a symbol of status, so inflated prices are, to some extent, a result of consumer acquiescence. But some distributors are insatiably greedy. Taking advantage of imperfect market supervision systems and consumers' lack of expertise, they take wine costing only tens of RMB, add luxurious packaging, and price it at hundreds or thousands. Most consumers cannot distinguish good from bad wine when buying in physical stores and can only follow the salesperson's advice. Salespeople recommend products with high commissions, and consumers can only suffer in silence. Besides, WeChat scan prices have become a hot business. Importers only need to spend a few hundred yuan to have a product's barcode scan display a price, which is often set by themselves. Some of the lowest-quality table wines can show a retail price of 1999 upon scanning. Then the retailer gives the consumer a discount, and some uninformed consumers fall for this trick. In short, when buying wine, don't always think about getting a cheap deal. Learn some practical wine knowledge, and you won't be easily tricked. Wine Think Tank WeChat public account: wineku. Wine Think Tank helps you drink better. This account is a signed account of NetEase News · NetEase Hao "Each Has Its Own Attitude".

Title: Why Treat the Mother When the Baby is Sick? Content: Papular eczema Zhong, a six-month-old male infant, was brought to the clinic by his mother on June 10, 2023. According to the mother's account, large areas of red papules had appeared on the baby's face and legs over the past three months, and he cried incessantly whenever he scratched them. They had sought medical help multiple times before, but the treatment results were unsatisfactory. A dermatology department at a hospital diagnosed it as eczema and prescribed an eczema ointment for topical application, yet the condition kept recurring and was difficult to cure completely. Subsequently, they tried Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) treatment, using herbs like Sophora flavescens, Cnidium monnieri, and Adina rubella for external washing, along with internal decoctions containing Phellodendron chinense, Honeysuckle, Atractylodes, Cicada molting, Dandelion, Viola, Red Peony, Poria, Forsythia, and Licorice. However, the condition still showed no significant improvement. They then decided to seek the author's help. The author carefully examined the infant and found eczema covering his face and inner thighs with significant discharge. The tongue was red with a slightly yellow, greasy coating. The stool had a foul smell, urine was yellow, the infant was restless and cried continuously, and the pulse was slightly rapid. After deep thought, the author considered that the previous TCM prescription was theoretically appropriate for the syndrome, so why was there no improvement? This led to contemplation. Recalling the ancient medical maxim, 'To treat a disease, one must seek its root cause,' for this six-month-old infant, the 'root' of the illness undoubtedly originated from the mother. The author inquired in detail about the mother's daily habits and learned that since giving birth, fearing inadequate nourishment and insufficient breast milk, she had been consuming homemade glutinous rice sweet wine with boiled eggs daily, and lunch and dinner invariably included pig trotter and papaya soup. Furthermore, following the advice of an elderly neighbor who claimed vegetables and fruits were cold and damp and would pass to the baby through breast milk, she had avoided all fruits and vegetables for the entire six months postpartum. Observing the infant's tongue, which was red with a thick, yellow, greasy coating, obvious halitosis, and a slightly slippery pulse, these were typical signs of the mother's preference for rich, sweet, pungent, and heating foods, passing damp-heat toxins to the infant through her milk. Therefore, the author decided to treat the mother. The author explained to the mother that the infant's condition was due to her dietary bias towards rich, heating foods and avoidance of vegetables. A prescription was given to the mother, including Rehmannia, Honeysuckle, Smilax glabra, Forsythia, Kudzu flower, Hovenia dulcis seed, Dandelion, Viola, Atractylodes, Phellodendron chinense, and Licorice. These herbs aimed to clear heat, resolve dampness, detoxify, and drain pus, intending for their effects to be transferred to the infant via the breast milk. Simultaneously, the mother was instructed to stop consuming the egg sweet wine and papaya trotter soup and instead eat a small amount of lean meat stir-fried with green vegetables daily. For the infant itself, only a small amount of a topical powder composed of Rhubarb, Phellodendron chinense, Talc, and Borneol was applied to the affected areas. After three doses of the mother's medicine, even though the infant did not take medicine directly, the eczema symptoms significantly reduced. After ten days, the eczema completely resolved, and the infant's skin returned to health. Thereafter, with the mother paying attention to her diet, the infant's eczema never recurred. This case again proves the importance of 'treating the disease by seeking its root cause'; only by finding the etiology can the disease be cured completely. Malnutrition Zhang, a mere four-month-old male infant, was brought to the clinic by his mother on October 7, 2023. According to the mother, although Zhang was a full-term vaginal delivery, his growth and development had been unsatisfactory since two months old, gradually showing signs of emaciation. At a hospital's pediatrics department, he was diagnosed with first-degree malnutrition and treated with vitamins, but the effect was not obvious. Later, they tried TCM treatment, approaching it as Gan accumulation (malnutrition), yet the results were still poor. In the clinic, Zhang's complexion was sallow and withered, with obvious emaciation of the cheeks and limbs. Although he had no fever, his cry was weak. Bowel movements and urination were normal. The tongue was pale, and the pulse was deficient. These were typical signs of deficiency of both Qi and Blood. As the old saying goes, 'When treating an infant, one must not fail to observe the mother.' While observing Zhang, the doctor also noticed his mother's complexion was similarly sallow. Upon inquiry, it was learned that for the past two months, the mother had frequent diarrhea, poor appetite, low spirits, fatigue, abdominal distension after eating, and belching. Although she still produced breast milk for the infant, it was thin and clear like water. Her tongue was pale with a white, slightly thick coating, and her pulse was deficient, slow, and weak. These were symptoms of Spleen and Stomach deficiency. Considering Zhang's symptoms were closely related to his mother's condition, the doctor decided to treat her with a modified formula of Buzhong Yiqi Tang (Tonifying the Middle and Augmenting the Qi Decoction) combined with Xiangsha Liujun Tang (Six Gentlemen Decoction with Aucklandia and Amomum). The prescription included Codonopsis (Dangshen), Astragalus (Beigi), Atractylodes (Baizhu), Poria (Fuling) to tonify the middle and benefit Qi, strengthen the Spleen and harmonize the Stomach; Chinese Angelica (Danggui, Guishen) to nourish and invigorate Blood; Bupleurum (Chaihu) and Cimicifuga (Shengma) to raise Yang; Tangerine peel (Chenpi), Chinese Yam (Huai Shan), charred Three Immortals (Jiao Sanxian, i.e., Hawthorn, Medicated Leaven, and Barley Sprout), Cyperus (Xiangfu), and Amomum (Sharen) to move Qi, promote digestion, strengthen the Spleen, and stimulate appetite; and prepared Licorice (Zhigancao) to harmonize the formula. After one dose, the mother's diarrhea stopped, her appetite improved, abdominal distension disappeared, and her spirits significantly improved. After three doses, her breast milk became whiter and thicker. Seeing the medicine had taken effect, the doctor was confident about Zhang's recovery. A week later, Zhang's complexion gradually became rosier, and his spirits improved. A month later, his skin became plump, and the signs of malnutrition were gone. This successful case not only highlights the charm of TCM but also reflects the doctor's superb skill and meticulous care for the patients. When treating infant ailments, we must pay close attention to the mother's condition and daily habits. The mother's health status and dietary habits are often directly related to the infant's health. Let's explore two specific cases to understand this better. First, in case one, the infant's symptoms were directly linked to the mother's preference for rich, sweet, pungent, and heating foods. The mother's diet directly affects the composition and quality of her breast milk. When the mother excessively consumes such foods, the damp-heat pathogens can be transmitted to the infant through the milk, leading to the accumulation of damp-heat in the infant's body and causing a series of health issues. Therefore, when treating such infant ailments, we need to focus on the mother's dietary habits, guide her to adjust her diet, avoid excessive intake of rich, heating foods, improve the quality of her milk, and thereby help the infant recover. Second, in case two, the infant suffered from malnutrition because the mother had Spleen and Stomach deficiency, leading to impaired intake and thus poor quality breast milk. In such cases, infants often show signs of malnutrition after breastfeeding. Therefore, treatment should focus on regulating the mother's Spleen and Stomach deficiency, enhancing her digestive function and nutrient absorption to improve milk quality. When the mother's Spleen and Stomach deficiency improves, the infant's nutritional status naturally improves. In summary, when treating infant ailments, we should not only focus on the infant's symptoms but also deeply understand the mother's condition and lifestyle. By adjusting the mother's diet and addressing issues like Spleen and Stomach deficiency, we can fundamentally improve the infant's health. This approach of treating both mother and child reflects the holistic concept of TCM and comprehensive concern for the infant's well-being.

Title: 【Eliminating Hidden Dangers, Forging Peace】 Officer Instantly Sees Through Loan "Verification Fee" Scam Content: Recently, the Zhujing Police Station of the Jinshan Branch of the Shanghai Municipal Public Security Bureau received a request for help from Mr. Gu, who claimed to have encountered a loan scam. Officer Huang Xiaochuan immediately reviewed his chat history with the online "customer service." As soon as he saw the words "verification fee," the officer determined that Mr. Gu had encountered a scammer. The scammer claimed that because Mr. Gu had entered the wrong bank account number, the loan funds being disbursed were intercepted and frozen by the credit center's system. The scammer also sent a document purportedly from the National Banking Regulatory Commission, demanding a verification fee equal to 30% of the loan amount (6,000 yuan) for the loan to be released normally. They informed Mr. Gu that he had already signed an electronic contract and could not cancel midway, and that police would later visit to collect evidence and submit materials to the Supreme People's Court. After patient explanation by the police auxiliary officers about the scammer's tricks – everything was fake, fake, fake (important things said three times!!!) – Mr. Gu was finally reassured and avoided financial loss in time. The case is currently under further investigation. Meanwhile, the officer helped Mr. Gu uninstall the loan app and download the National Anti-Fraud Center App, guiding him on how to view relevant real anti-fraud cases. Please do not轻易 believe various online loan advertisements on phones, text messages, apps, and social media. For loans, please go to正规 financial institutions. If you are unfortunately scammed, please保存好 relevant evidence and promptly call 110 to report it.

Title: Yesterday I posted a Weitoutiao complaining about the inconvenience of not having a car for transportation in Shanghai. It got nearly 30,000 views and many comments, which made me realize a few things. [Fist bump][Fist bump] First, the difference between Shanghai's urban area and suburbs. Living in the urban area is indeed very convenient; the subway doesn't get stuck in traffic, travel time is predictable, transfers are easy, and driving is so congested that it's better to take the subway. Living in the suburbs, however, some buses genuinely don't have real-time tracking available, and living far away often means making two transfers is common. The Outer Ring Road separates the urban area from the suburbs, something urban residents might not fully understand, but it's okay, they don't know any better. No wonder my friend told me before that she really likes Shanghai because it's convenient – of course, she lives in Huangpu. [Heart][Heart] Second, Shanghai's user traffic is indeed huge. Many citizens were very enthusiastic in sharing with me how to check bus locations, how to save money by carpooling, the difficulty of finding parking spots and the high cost of parking if driving, or suggesting buying an electric bike. For me, new to Shanghai, this was undoubtedly a warm gesture... [Thumbs up][Thumbs up] Third, a few netizens gave me encouragement, telling me to stop complaining as it harms my health. They said they went through the same thing initially, but through their own efforts, their living conditions have improved a lot now; they advised me to change my mindset, saying only people adapt to the city. They really understood the lowest point I was feeling inside. To be honest, in this first week here, I really felt a sense of落差 (disparity). No one willingly gives up a comfortable life to experience a difficult one; it's all for the next generation or for a better life in the future. It's just the growing pains of starting a new life. Last night when I got back, I really couldn't hold back my tears. The living conditions aren't great, the commute is long, and I can't bring myself to spend money on taxis. These past few days I've been constantly trying to figure out the best route. Suddenly I realized I'm too fragile. Luckily, my husband can understand and give me some comfort, and with the concern and encouragement from friends, I feel much better. Instead of complaining, it's better to think carefully about how to optimize my commute route and save some time. Shanghai is indeed a diverse, inclusive, and growing city. There are still many good aspects worth exploring. The biggest feeling I have is that people are really quite warm-hearted and have shown me great kindness. Perhaps it's because every outsider can empathize with the hardships of striving in Shanghai. As the saying goes, 'Those who have been rained on are more likely to hold an umbrella for others.' The road ahead will still be hard, but with all this kindness, it always feels warmer. The advantages I haven't physically experienced yet have quietly been bestowed upon my spirit. I hope I can be someone who holds an umbrella for myself and also for others. Finally, let me encourage myself again with Uncle Cat's words: 'Making yourself better is the key to solving all problems.' Go for it 💪

Title: Poverty Alleviation Workshops Deliver Wealth to Doorsteps – Jiaxiang County Human Resources and Social Security Bureau in Shandong Province Explores Local Employment Models for Poor Households Content: Poverty Alleviation Workshops Deliver Wealth to Doorsteps – Jiaxiang County Human Resources and Social Security Bureau in Shandong Province Explores Local Employment Models for Poor Households 2018.10.15 In recent years, the Jiaxiang County Human Resources and Social Security Bureau in Shandong Province, leveraging local industrial advantages, has actively explored and established employment and entrepreneurship poverty alleviation workshops. They bring projects to villages, jobs to households, skills to individuals, and policies to homes, providing nearby employment opportunities for poor households unable to work away from home. This explores a model for local employment of poor households, achieving a "four-win" situation for the masses, the collective, enterprises, and industry. Leveraging Local Traditional Industry Advantages to Rapidly Establish Poverty Alleviation Workshops Jiaxiang County effectively combines poverty alleviation with the development of characteristic industries. Relying on labor-intensive processing such as gloves and garment processing, and through policy guidance and market-oriented operations, it guides and supports local leading enterprises with good economic benefits and strong demonstration effects. It establishes employment and entrepreneurship bases in enterprises and sets up poverty alleviation workshops in poor villages using idle village houses. Li Xianqing, General Manager of Jining Tianjiu Industrial and Trading Co., Ltd., actively carried out employment poverty alleviation. He invested 38 million yuan in the Jiaxiang Glove Industrial Park to build a barrier-free multi-story industrial plant covering 15,000 square meters, establishing the first local employment and entrepreneurship base for people with disabilities. In 2016, the Jiaxiang County Human Resources and Social Security Bureau signed a employment agreement for poor households with Tianjiu Industrial and Trading Co., guiding the company to prioritize hiring poor people with disabilities who have the ability to work, providing them with suitable positions, allowing them to enjoy the happiness of self-reliance. Simultaneously, it guided Tianjiu Industrial and Trading Co. to provide a monthly living subsidy of 300 yuan to each poor disabled employee on top of their original salary. To encourage employees to learn from and surpass each other, the company offers an additional 200 yuan reward to poor employees with a monthly salary exceeding 1,000 yuan, and so on, with a 100 yuan reward for every 500 yuan increase in monthly salary. Currently, the company has cumulatively absorbed and employed over 140 people, including 17 from poor households. Additionally, it set up glove processing workshops in enterprises in surrounding towns and streets, using the company's workshops and home-based processing to drive employment for over 50 people in difficulty, with each poor household earning 30-60 yuan per day. Up to now, Jiaxiang County has established and developed several employment poverty alleviation workshops, including those with Dishang Huarun Group, Jinxia Garments, Chao'ao Footwear, Jinchong Gloves, etc. Among them, eight workshops, including Jining Tianjiu Industrial and Trading Co., Ltd., have been recognized as provincial-level demonstration employment poverty alleviation workshops, enabling 156 poor people to achieve local employment. Based on the actual number of working-age registered poor people absorbed by the poverty alleviation workshops, a one-time subsidy of 58,000 yuan for employment poverty alleviation workshops was implemented. Implementing Employment and Entrepreneurship Support Policies to Achieve Local Poverty Alleviation through Employment Jiaxiang County fully leverages the advantages of characteristic industry villages and the "one village, one product" initiative, introducing projects with low technical requirements, long project cycles, and suitable for decentralized processing, such as paper flower and accessory processing. It fosters "small-scale processing," setting up small workshops in village committees and farmers' homes for incense making, sesame oil production, broom processing, willow weaving, garlic and chili processing, and vermicelli processing, absorbing poor households for self-reliance and poverty alleviation through manual labor. It actively handles the recycling and sales of small processing products to ensure poor households obtain stable, long-term income. Simultaneously, it actively implements employment and entrepreneurship support policies, bringing employment skills training classes to towns, streets, and villages, promoting training and employment for poverty alleviation; develops public welfare positions and enterprise poverty alleviation positions to help poverty alleviation targets achieve local transfer employment; adopts the "poverty alleviation base + poverty alleviation workshop" operation model, building poverty alleviation workshops in villages (communities), allowing the masses to work without leaving their villages (communities), thus achieving local poverty alleviation through employment for poor people. Considering the dilemma faced by left-behind rural women and the elderly of "cannot earn money while caring for the family, and cannot care for the family while earning money," the county's Human Resources and Social Security Bureau learned that Jiaxiang Wanxing Craft Processing Factory is committed to providing poverty alleviation paths for left-behind women and the elderly, and actively provided it with various employment preferential support policies such as entrepreneurial guaranteed loans. Supported by strong employment benefit policies, the rapidly developing Wanxing Craft Processing Factory lived up to expectations, teaching paper flower and other craft-making skills entirely to rural women and the elderly. They can work at home or come to the Wanxing workshop, entirely based on personal convenience. "When I have more free time, I come to the workshop, work while chatting with the sisters, earning money while talking and laughing; during times like taking children to school or cooking for them, I work at home while doing housework, so taking care of children and earning money don't conflict..." said Sister Cao, a villager from Liangbaosi Town, with a smile on her face when talking about this satisfactory job. Today, over 200 villagers like Sister Cao work at Wanxing, including over 90 poor individuals. Relying on their skillful hands, they process over 2 million various paper flowers annually, with an output value of 50 million yuan, and the products are exported to many countries including Europe and America. Furthermore, Jiaxiang County also established the Jiaxiang Qingzhu Broom Processing Cooperative in Qiandu Village, Mengguji Town, setting up a targeted employment poverty alleviation training workshop, changing the traditional scattered family workshop production model. The cooperative implements unified raw material purchasing, unified process standards, unified processing production, and unified export sales. The production and processing model divides the previously family-completed processing steps into an assembly line workflow, with different members specializing in specific steps, greatly improving craft maturity and production efficiency. It has currently absorbed 2,000 employees, including 33 poor households from the village and 14 surrounding villages. (Sun Aifang)

Title: Chinese Tourist in Phuket Captures Starfish and Sea Urchins Exposed by Local Media and Criticized, Chinese Consulate Reminds. Content: A Chinese tourist was strolling on the beach in Phuket, with warm sunshine and a gentle breeze brushing against his face. His footprints marked the soft sand, as if softly conversing with the sea. Not far away, a crystal-clear starfish shimmered in the seawater, catching his eye. He bent down to pick up the starfish, feeling an inexplicable joy in his heart, as if he had uncovered the secrets of the entire ocean. However, just as he placed the starfish into a bucket, a voice suddenly called out, 'Hey! Stop!' He looked up and saw two local staff members hurriedly approaching with serious expressions. 'What are you doing?' one staff member asked sternly. 'I... I just wanted to take a look at this starfish,' the tourist explained somewhat awkwardly. 'I meant no harm.' 'Do you know this is illegal?' the other staff member said coldly. 'According to our laws, capturing starfish and sea urchins is strictly prohibited.' Upon hearing this, the tourist realized his actions might have caused negative consequences. He quickly withdrew his hand from the bucket and looked at the staff apologetically. 'I'm sorry, I didn't know,' he apologized sincerely. 'I just wanted to get closer to nature.' 'If you don't know, don't act recklessly,' the staff warned. 'Please remember, respecting local laws and customs is every tourist's responsibility.' Hearing these words, the tourist felt somewhat guilty and gained a deeper understanding of the local culture and laws. He decided to be more cautious in future travels, respecting local customs and laws, and avoiding violations. Just then, a gentle breeze blew, carrying the fresh scent of the sea. The tourist looked out at the vast ocean, filled with awe and reflection. In this expansive sea, every creature has its unique significance, and every part of the ocean holds boundless beauty and wonders. He vowed to become a guardian of marine life, using actions to demonstrate reverence and care for nature. As he turned to leave, a starfish remained behind, gently swaying in the seawater, as if cheering for the tourist's decision. On this beautiful beach, everything seemed so harmonious and wonderful. #BeachSceneryAsBeautifulAsAPainting #ChineseTourist #PhuketIsland

Title: Jilin University Second Hospital's Medical Team Supporting Tonghua Returns Safely - Jinri Toutiao Content: Jilin University Second Hospital's Medical Team Supporting Tonghua Returns Safely. Over 60 days of fighting day and night, 189 people giving their all in treatment, carrying the heavy responsibility for the lives of 2.3 million people... On the 23rd, amidst the warm sunshine and gentle spring breeze, Jilin University Second Hospital's medical team supporting Tonghua returned triumphantly. Facing the challenges of elderly patients and difficult treatments, the team undertook the most arduous tasks in all wards of the designated hospital, taking charge of the most critically ill and complex patients. All team members raced against time and contended with death, fulfilling their mission with their lives. As the 'backbone' of this pandemic treatment effort, they achieved outstanding results with zero medical accidents and zero infections among medical staff. 'After the testing team arrived in Tonghua, they began testing work within 24 hours. The team members fought continuously for 14 days and nights, accumulating 13,000 samples tested, with daily testing volume reaching the ideal design limit of the testing vehicle,' recalled Xu Li, leader of the nucleic acid testing medical team, reviewing the work of the 17 testing team members. In this battle against the pandemic, Jilin University Second Hospital dispatched 189 people in 5 batches to support Tonghua, bringing along high-precision life support equipment worth tens of millions of yuan with the medical team, providing 'relocation-style' support, forming the largest, best-equipped, and most powerful medical team supporting Tonghua in Jilin Province. In this young team with an average age of 34, most members had experience supporting Hubei and treating severe cases, with over two-thirds of the doctors specializing in critical care medicine and respiratory diseases. The average age of the critically ill patients treated was 74 years, with the youngest child patient being only 1 year old. During their support in Tonghua, the medical team successfully completed the treatment task for COVID-19 patients and received high praise from the Tonghua municipal government and its people.

Title: The traffic difficulty problem at the Kaiyuan Bridge culvert in Zhumadian urban area will be resolved in May
Content: The traffic difficulty problem at the Kaiyuan Bridge culvert in Zhumadian urban area will be resolved in May

Zhumadian Radio and Television Media News: On April 2, Zhumadian Guangshi Network published a report titled 'Severe Water Accumulation at Kaiyuan Bridge Culvert in Zhumadian Urban Area Makes Pedestrian Passage Difficult'. Recently, reporters followed staff from the Municipal Smart City Management Center to revisit the site for a follow-up on the traffic difficulty problem at the Kaiyuan Bridge culvert.
The ground of the Kaiyuan Bridge culvert is uneven and has severe perennial water accumulation. In recent years, this has not only caused inconvenience for nearby residents but also posed safety hazards. On that day, staff from the Municipal Smart City Management Center contacted the relevant responsible unit, the Development Zone Urban Management Law Enforcement Bureau, to come to the site and address the issue on the spot. According to staff from the Development Zone Urban Management Law Enforcement Bureau, there are three construction projects ongoing around the Kaiyuan Bridge culvert, and the high volume of passing vehicles is the main reason for the severe damage to the culvert's road surface. Currently, the repair project for the Kaiyuan Bridge culvert has been incorporated into the Kaiyuan Avenue Underpass Railway Project section from Fuqiang Road to Qianjin Road. With the orderly progress of the project, the traffic difficulty problem at the Kaiyuan Bridge culvert is expected to be resolved around May Day this year.
Liu Qian, the project manager for the Kaiyuan Avenue Underpass Railway Project section from Fuqiang Road to Qianjin Road, stated that as the Kaiyuan Road underpass project is gradually completed, the construction party will address the Kaiyuan Bridge culvert. According to the municipal government's requirements, the Kaiyuan Avenue Underpass Railway Project is scheduled to be basically completed around May Day, and the culvert water accumulation problem will be resolved by then.

Content Title: Marriott Hotel Exposes Five-Star Hotel Slippers Are All Recycled for Reuse Release Date: 2025-09-24 08:55:47 Content Status: Review Completed Content Type: Multimedia Industry: Digital Government Affairs_Government Media_Government Media Author Name: in Jiashan Owner Name: in Jiashan Content Account Type: Enterprise Content Details: Marriott Hotel exposes that five-star hotel slippers are all recycled for reuse. Some netizens found that the slippers were noticeably pilled and contained hair inside. Hotel: Never labeled as disposable items. They are recycled and used 2 to 3 times. Online material. A Marriott hotel in Changzhou, Jiangsu was exposed for hygiene issues. A guest claimed the hotel slippers were pilled and had residual hair, questioning if the slippers were recycled and reused. 'Regarding our slippers, it's like this...? Never labeled as disposable items.' Hotel: 'They are indeed not disposable.' Hotel: Never labeled as disposable items. MARRIOTT. 'But, they are recycled.' The hotel responded that for environmental reasons, hotel slippers are not disposable items. After professional cleaning and disinfection, they are recycled and used 2-3 times. 'Housekeeping department error.' But admitted that residual hair belongs to... But admitted that residual hair belongs to a 'Housekeeping department error. And then maybe only about two times.' Online material. The hotel did not proactively declare the slippers' recyclable nature. Guests assumed they were disposable by default. This sparked widespread consumer concern about hygiene risks and lack of informed consent. 'During the cleaning process of cotton textiles, some [pilling] might occur.' Currently, the Changzhou Municipal Health Inspection Institute has intervened in the investigation. The key determination is the nature of the slippers: if they are disposable items, reuse is strictly prohibited; if they are recyclable items, the disinfection process must be ensured to be compliant. 'A small amount of pilling. But all our slippers are changed for each guest and disinfected.' Title: How to view those who buy a car but not a parking space? Content: My family didn't buy a parking space, nor did we rent one. At first, very few people had moved into the residential area, so we could just find a spot anywhere nearby to park, and no one cared. Gradually, as the area became livelier, parking spaces became harder to find. We also looked into the price of the residential garage spaces; they started at 68,000 each and are now 58,000 each, but very few people have bought them. Currently, renting a space costs 250-300 yuan per month, including management fees, and many neighbors who bought spaces regret it deeply. Six years on, only half of the underground garage is being used. As long as the price of parking spaces doesn't drop, we won't buy one. After all, except for the few days when the school opposite starts or ends its term and there are more cars, we can park freely in the empty spaces around the area. At worst, we just have to walk a bit more.

Title: Is Marine Engineering a Popular Field for Postgraduates? Content: Marine engineering professionals are highly sought after in the current job market, primarily because there are relatively few institutions offering this major, leading to high demand and low supply of talent in related fields. Graduates have broad employment prospects and can enter various sectors such as ship and marine engineering design and research units, maritime bureaus, domestic and international classification societies, shipping companies, shipyards, offshore oil units, higher education institutions, ship transportation management, ship trading and operations, customs, marine insurance, and maritime arbitration. In these fields, they can engage in the design, research, manufacturing, inspection, use, and management of ships and marine structures. Additionally, they can find employment opportunities in related industries and information technology sectors.

Title: Can't benefit from the purchase tax reduction? Audi takes the initiative to let you get the advantage with Q7 price adjustment to reward users. Content: The detailed rules for the purchase tax reduction policy have been implemented, making consumers planning to buy cars overjoyed. However, limited by the condition of "passenger cars with a single vehicle price (excluding VAT) not exceeding 300,000 yuan and a displacement of 2.0 liters or below", many consumers wanting to buy luxury cars face difficulties, as they cannot enjoy this wave of benefits. But for those who are business owners, workplace elites, etc., the demand for business connections and improving quality of life remains. From the perspective of price adjustment, this wave of profit-sharing is even more beneficial than the purchase tax reduction, especially since this profit-sharing move is made against the backdrop of frequent price increases by many brands in the domestic and international car markets due to cost considerations. Price increases by car brands under the pressure of the pandemic are a helpless move, as logistics, materials, chips, and other costs have significantly increased during the pandemic. Under the series of blows brought by the pandemic, shrinking profits for business owners and reduced income for workplace elites are common, but demands such as business connections and improving quality of life are enduring. Audi Q7's price adjustment not only responds to the trend of promoting car consumption but is also an act of rewarding users based on their needs. Against the backdrop of rising fuel car prices, it can be called the most beautiful contrarian in the car market. This concept of "thinking what users think, doing what users need" is deeply embedded in Audi's brand DNA. Title: How to clean up when the C drive of the computer is full? Content: If possible, try to reinstall the system. Then allocate more than 1TB of space to the C drive. Windows and various domestic software will continuously consume the space of the C drive. On one hand, it's due to the design of the software itself, and on the other hand, it's due to the unreasonable design of disk space by Windows itself. For example, in Linux, the user's /home is usually allocated a separate partition for storing user documents and data generated by programs for the user. However, in Windows, it is forcibly allocated to the C drive. As a result, by default, programs have to store a large number of cache files and temporary files on the C drive. Moreover, these files are mixed with the user's "My Documents," "Videos," and "Pictures" files. After long-term use, users will find that the D: drive and E: drive are empty, while the C drive is full. In contrast, Linux users and MacOS users rarely encounter such situations. Therefore, Windows users should consider allocating a large proportion of space to the C: drive. Then use some backup software to regularly back up the data from the C: drive to the D: and E: drives. Windows comes with a built-in backup tool. Just set it up, and it will automatically run backups in the background every day.

Title: Physical Examination, Health Check-up Content: A while ago, the company organized a physical examination, and one of the items was taking body temperature. I was quite puzzled. Usually, taking a temperature is done in just a moment, but this time, it took forever. The person in charge of taking temperatures was a young nurse who seemed quite sharp. When it was the guy in front of my turn, the nurse placed the thermometer under his armpit and then started writing something with her head down. After a while, the nurse came to retrieve the thermometer, looked at the reading, and her expression changed. She said, "Sir, why is your temperature so high? Are you feeling unwell?" The guy was also stunned and said, "I don't feel unwell." The nurse looked at the thermometer more carefully and muttered, "Could the thermometer be broken?" Then she took a new thermometer and measured his temperature again. Watching from the side, I was thinking to myself, what could possibly go wrong with a thermometer? Finally, it was my turn. The nurse handled the thermometer like it was fragile, gently placing it under my armpit and specifically reminding me to hold it tight. When the time was up, the nurse came to take the thermometer, glanced at it, frowned, and said, "Strange, why is your temperature also so odd?" I panicked immediately. I'm full of energy every day, how could my temperature be odd? The nurse thought for a moment and asked me, "Did you just exercise?" I shook my head and said no. She checked the thermometer again and still found it odd. Just then, an older doctor passed by, and the nurse quickly explained the situation to him. The doctor took the thermometer, looked at it, asked about the previous few people's situations, and then laughed. He said, "Oh, you silly girl, you didn't shake down the thermometer!" The nurse then realized that she had forgotten to shake down the thermometer at the beginning, which caused the inaccurate readings. I finally breathed a sigh of relief. So, it was just a silly mistake. What a fuss over such a simple task like taking a temperature, making everyone anxious. Everyone, have you ever encountered such jokes caused by carelessness in daily life? #PhysicalExamination# #HealthCheckup#

Title: How is transferring from Materials Science to Clinical Medicine (5-year program) at Nankai University? Is it recommended to transfer? Content: It's very difficult for graduates of the 5-year clinical program to secure a position at a decent institution. To become a doctor, further education is necessary, so if you want to work at a top-tier hospital, you must pursue a doctorate, residency training, and specialized training. This means you need to first get into an academic master's program, totaling about 13 years. At Nankai, roughly one-quarter of the 5-year clinical students are recommended for exemption to academic master's programs, and another quarter enter professional master's programs (which integrate four certifications). However, those in the integrated program basically cannot pursue a doctorate, meaning they won't be able to work at top-tier hospitals and will have to settle for less desirable institutions, which limits future development. The remaining students have to take the postgraduate entrance exam themselves, and the clinical medicine exam is quite difficult. As for the previously mentioned residency training, it lasts 2-3 years (one year less for PhD holders). During this period, women are worked like men, and men are worked like beasts, with shift work and high labor intensity. If you can't endure the hardships of studying medicine and residency training, it's better not to try your luck. Of course, if you can persevere through all these hardships and eventually secure a position in a lucrative department, things will get better as you gain seniority. Hmm... wait, considering your background in 'biochemistry, materials, environment' (notoriously tough fields), it seems you don't have much of a fallback option anyway.

Title: Summer Ground High Temperatures - Tire Maintenance Importance Ranks First, Calling All Car Owners. June 1st, summer has arrived. Driving in Guangzhou, the high temperature of the road surface can even cook an egg. In this situation, vehicles are most prone to tire blowout accidents. Many car owners have this question: What methods can effectively prevent tire blowouts and other failures? Summer tire maintenance has once again become the focus for all car owners. 5 Situations Prone to 'Blowouts' - Be Careful. If you have never... Content: Summer Ground High Temperatures - Tire Maintenance Importance Ranks First, Calling All Car Owners. June 1st, summer has arrived. Driving in Guangzhou, the high temperature of the road surface can even cook an egg. In this situation, vehicles are most prone to tire blowout accidents. Many car owners have this question: What methods can effectively prevent tire blowouts and other failures? Summer tire maintenance has once again become the focus for all car owners. 5 Situations Prone to Blowouts - Be Careful. If you have never checked your tires, then with summer here, you should quickly drive your beloved car into the shop for an inspection. If you usually encounter the following situations while using your car, then you need to be careful about the occurrence of blowouts. 1. High temperatures. Once the road surface temperature rises, the friction between the tire and the road causes the tire surface temperature to become very hot. Due to thermal expansion and contraction, the tire body expands and becomes thinner, and then—a blowout occurs. 2. Vehicle overload. If the tire pressure is high, overloading is more likely to induce a blowout. 3. Poor tire condition. Needless to say, if your tire is excessively worn, has aged, has cracks, or external damage, etc., it is very prone to blowouts. 4. Speeding. Can speeding also cause blowouts? Of course. The speed limit of a tire is strictly calculated and determined by the manufacturer. Prolonged excessive speeding rapidly increases tire temperature, accelerates rubber aging, and makes the tire extremely prone to bursting. 5. Poor road conditions. Uneven road surfaces or roads with a lot of gravel cause significant damage to tires. It is also common for vehicles traveling at high speed to experience air leakage and subsequent blowouts due to friction or impact with sharp stones or objects on the road. Short Self-Rescue Time Once a Blowout Occurs. Most blowouts are caused by tire pressure. Experts point out that a so-called blowout refers to a situation where a tire loses air suddenly due to rupture in a very short time (generally less than 0.1 second). A blowout can happen at any time. For a vehicle, what is more terrifying about a blowout is that it can lead to more serious accidents. Because after a blowout occurs, the time available for the driver and passengers to take self-rescue measures is very short. At this point, the vehicle has lost control, which can lead to rollovers, collisions, or even friction-induced combustion and explosions, resulting in the tragic scene of instant vehicle destruction and death. Foreign research shows that when a tire blowout accident occurs while a car is traveling at speeds above 160 km/h, the mortality rate of the occupants is close to 100%. Preventing Blowouts: Start with Daily Maintenance. It's best to have a simple tire pressure gauge on hand; they are generally quite simple to operate. When driving in high-temperature conditions, pay attention to the temperature and pressure of the tires. The owner's manual provides detailed specifications. Before each long-distance drive, ensure the tire pressure meets the specified standard. If you find the tire pressure is insufficient, replenish it promptly. Absolutely do not make do and drive for a long time, as this will actually accelerate tire wear. Generally, the service life of a tire specified by the manufacturer is between 80,000 and 100,000 kilometers (or about 5 years). Usually, develop the habit of frequently checking the wear condition of your tires. After driving for a long time on high-temperature roads, take a break periodically. Park the car in a shady spot, allow the tire temperature to decrease, and then continue driving. Do not use the method of splashing cold water to reduce tire temperature, as this can cause cracks due to uneven contraction of different parts of the tread and sidewall rubber layers.

Title: What to do with a PDF file that cannot be edited? Try these methods. Content: When encountering a PDF file whose content cannot be edited, you can try the following methods: Use professional PDF editing software: Choose a professional PDF editing software, such as Adobe Acrobat or 迅捷PDF编辑器, etc. These software usually provide more powerful editing functions, including text editing, image editing, form editing, etc. ✅ 迅捷PDF编辑器 迅捷PDF编辑器 is a powerful PDF editing tool. It not only supports basic text editing, image processing, and page management but also has advanced features such as form creation and editing, batch operations, and advanced security settings. Using this software, users can easily add, modify, or draw annotations on PDF files, thus solving the problem of PDF files being difficult to edit. Operation method: Open the PDF editing software, select the 'Open' or 'Import' function, find and import the PDF file that cannot be edited. In the software interface, find and click on the content that needs to be edited. For text content, you can modify it directly; for image content, you can crop, replace, or add it. After the editing work is completed, press the [Ctrl+S] shortcut key to save the changes made to the PDF file. It is worth mentioning that 迅捷PDF编辑器 can accurately preserve the original layout style of the file during the editing process, ensuring the copy is neat and error-free, with a unified format, greatly saving users time on repeated typesetting and editing. Use OCR technology: If the text in the PDF file exists in image form (such as a scanned copy), you can use OCR technology to convert the text in the image into editable text. Choose an OCR tool, open the PDF file, and perform OCR recognition. After the recognition is completed, you will be able to edit the recognized text content. After editing, save the modified PDF file. Title: How to prevent and control rice stem borer? Content: Tyrosine hydroxylase plays a crucial role in the formation of the larval cuticle and larval-pupal melanization in the rice stem borer. The rice stem borer is a notorious pest that infests rice and has developed high resistance to many commonly used insecticides. In this study, we analyzed whether tyrosine hydroxylase (TH), which is required for larval development and cuticle melanization in many insects, could be a potential target for controlling the rice stem borer. The full-length cDNA of the rice stem borer TH (CsTH) was identified and characterized. The complete open reading frame of CsTH (MW690914) is 1683 bp long, encoding a protein of 560 amino acids. Figure 1. CsTH gene expression: In the first to sixth instar larvae, CsTH levels were higher on the first day after molting and lower in the following days. From the wandering stage to the adult stage, CsTH levels began to rise and peaked during the pupal stage. These patterns suggest that this gene plays a role in larval development and larval-pupal cuticle melanization. Figure 2. CsTH gene expression levels: When we injected dsCsTH or 3-iodotyrosine (3-IT) as a TH inhibitor, or fed larvae a diet supplemented with 3-IT, larval development and larval-pupal cuticle melanization were significantly affected. Adult eclosion was severely impaired, and most adults died (Figure 3). Figure 3. RNAi inhibition phenotypes: These results indicate that CsTH may play a key role in the larval development, larval-pupal melanization, and immunity of the rice stem borer, and this gene could form a potential new target for pest control. Title: How can enterprises protect customer information security? Content: Protecting customer information security is crucial for enterprises, especially in today's increasingly rampant cyber attacks. If customers' personal privacy and sensitive data are leaked, it not only harms the interests of customers but also severely impacts the enterprise's reputation and operations. Therefore, enterprises need to adopt a series of effective measures to ensure the security of customer information. The following are some key strategies and best practices: 1. Data Encryption Encryption is one of the most effective means to protect customer information. Through encryption technology, even if data is stolen by hackers, its content cannot be read. Enterprises should encrypt all sensitive data, including customers' personal information, payment information, and communication records. File Encryption: Use high-strength encryption algorithms (such as AES-256) to encrypt sensitive data. Transmission Encryption: Use SSL/TLS protocols to protect data security during transmission, ensuring network communication is not stolen. Full Disk Encryption: Perform full disk encryption on data stored internally by the enterprise, ensuring that even if the device is lost or stolen, the data will not be leaked. Recommended Tools: Such as GoTrust software, which can provide enterprises with comprehensive file encryption and communication encryption solutions. 2. Access Control and Identity Authentication Enterprises need to ensure that only authorized personnel can access sensitive customer data. This means implementing strong access control and identity verification measures. Role Permission Management: Restrict employees' access to different data based on their positions and roles. For example, only senior management or designated employees can access customers' financial information. Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA): Enhance account security through dual authentication methods such as password + fingerprint, password + SMS verification code, to avoid data leakage caused by password theft. Principle of Least Privilege: Grant employees only the minimum access permissions necessary to complete their tasks, reducing unnecessary risks. 3. Data Backup and Disaster Recovery In the event of data loss or leakage, enterprises must have backup and recovery mechanisms. Regularly back up critical data and ensure backup data is stored in a secure location. It is best to choose encrypted backups to prevent the backup data itself from becoming a target of attack. Cloud Backup: Choose cloud backup services that support encryption to ensure the security of backup files. Local Backup: In addition to cloud backup, enterprises should also establish secure local backup systems and ensure the security of backup data. 4. Employee Security Training and Awareness Employees are a crucial link in the information security chain. Regularly conducting information security training for employees and enhancing their security awareness can effectively reduce human errors and internal/external threats. Preventing Social Engineering Attacks: Such as phishing emails, malicious links, spoofed calls, etc. Security Operation Standards: Teach employees how to create strong passwords, avoid accessing company information in insecure network environments, avoid using personal devices to handle company data, etc. By educating employees to identify potential security threats, enterprises can significantly reduce the risk of information leakage caused by employee negligence. 5. Network Security Protection Enterprises should strengthen network security protection to ensure their IT infrastructure is protected from hacker attacks. Adopt a series of technical means, such as firewalls, Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), Intrusion Prevention Systems (IPS), etc., to monitor network traffic in real-time, detect anomalies, and intercept them. Firewalls and Intrusion Detection Systems: Used to block insecure network traffic and detect potential attacks. Virtual Private Network (VPN): Provide encrypted connections for remote employees to protect data transmission security. Regular Security Assessments: Conduct penetration testing and vulnerability scanning to promptly identify and fix security vulnerabilities in the network. 6. Data Storage and Processing Compliance Enterprises must comply with local and international data privacy protection regulations, such as the EU's GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation), the US's CCPA (California Consumer Privacy Act), etc. These regulations require enterprises to adopt strict data protection measures and specify the storage, processing, and usage methods of customer privacy information. Data Minimization: Collect and store as little customer data as possible, only retaining necessary information. Data Deletion and Destruction: When data is no longer needed, customer information should be completely deleted through secure destruction measures to prevent its recovery and misuse. 7. Security Auditing and Log Management Regularly conducting security audits and log analysis can help promptly identify potential security vulnerabilities or abnormal behaviors. Enterprises should record and analyze key data such as access logs and operation logs to ensure they can trace the source of any information leakage or malicious attack. Log Monitoring: Continuously monitor and analyze log records of employee and customer information access to promptly detect suspicious activities. Auditing and Compliance Checks: Regularly conduct compliance audits to ensure all customer information protection measures meet regulatory requirements. 8. Using Efficient Encryption Tools When protecting customer data, enterprises can utilize some efficient encryption software to ensure data security. For example, tools like GoTrust software not only provide strong file encryption and communication encryption functions but also support comprehensive identity authentication and access control, helping enterprises enhance data security protection.

Title: 2020 Fastest Charging Phones Ranking, Is Your Phone on the List? Content: 2020 Fastest Charging Phones Ranking, Is Your Phone on the List?

It's already 2020. Sometimes when you're watching TV shows, movies, or playing games on your phone, you suddenly get a low battery warning. At that point, you definitely think about charging your phone. How annoying if the charging is too slow! Today, I'll introduce a few phones with the fastest charging speeds.

The speed of our phone's charging is closely related to the charger head and the data cable. The charger head has voltage and current data. For example, if my current phone is 5V/2A, that's 10W charging. If I switch to a 5V/0.5A or 1A charger, the charging speed slows down. The standard now is 9V/2A, which is 18W. This year, many flagship models have charging power that has already broken through 40W.

Furthermore, the longer the data cable, the slower the charging speed; the shorter the cable, the faster. Additionally, it depends on the transmission current; the higher the value, the faster.

First Place: Lenovo Legion Gaming Phone (Not yet released for sale)

The Lenovo Legion Gaming Phone has announced again that it will be the first to feature 90W fast charging. There will definitely be surprises in charging speed. I believe many people are looking forward to it. The battery capacity of the Lenovo Legion Gaming Phone seems to be 4000mAh, and it can be fully charged in 15 minutes.

Second Place: OPPO Find X2 Pro (65W Super Wired Fast Charging)
The OPPO Find X2 Pro has a battery capacity of 4260mAh and supports up to 65W SuperVOOC fast charging. The official standard charger is rated at 5V/2A and 10V/6.5A. It can fully charge the phone in just 39 minutes.

Third Place: Realme X2 Pro (50W Wired Fast Charging)
Realme X2 Pro is a sub-brand under OPPO. The Realme X2 Pro has a battery capacity of 4000mAh. The fast charging technology has been directly upgraded to 50W, and the price is below 2000 yuan. It's the cheapest fast-charging phone.

Fourth Place: iQOO Pro (44W Wired Flash Charging)

iQOO is a very popular sub-brand under vivo.
The iQOO Pro is equipped with 44W dual-turbo engine flash charging. With a 4000mAh battery, it can charge 50% in 15 minutes, 85% in 30 minutes, and 100% in 45 minutes.

Fifth Place: Huawei P40 Pro (40W Wired Fast Charging)

The Huawei P40 Pro series has a built-in 4200mAh battery and supports 40W SuperCharge fast charging. The real-world performance of the Huawei P40 Pro series has been exposed by foreign media. Foreign media outlet PhoneArena tested the 40W fast charging of the Huawei P40 Pro. The test results showed that the 40W fast charging achieved 30% charge in 10 minutes, 50% in 25 minutes, 80% in 40 minutes, and 100% in 59 minutes.
It also supports 40W wireless fast charging and reverse wireless charging. The Huawei P40 Pro is Huawei's first phone to support commercial 40W wireless fast charging.

Summary

Title: From 2017 to 2019, Xuancheng Procuratorial Organs Prosecuted 283 People Involved in Cybercrime Content: Cybercrime Preface With society developing into the information age, the Internet has been gradually widely applied in people's work and life. While providing convenience to the public, it also leaves space for criminals to exploit. To cope with the increasing trend of cybercrime, the Xuancheng People's Procuratorate strives to advance the punishment of cybercrime and focuses on maintaining cybersecurity. From 2017 to 2019, the entire Xuancheng city accepted 95 first-instance public prosecution cases involving cybercrime, involving 343 people; prosecuted 84 cases involving 283 people; and courts rendered effective guilty verdicts in 82 cases involving 249 people. Typical Case [Keywords] Crime of Operating a Gambling Den, Online Gambling, WeChat Group [Gist] Defendants Yang Moumou, Jin Moumou, and Kai Moumou, for the purpose of profit, used mobile WeChat to create groups for crowd gambling, profiting from taking a cut, with serious circumstances. Their actions have violated the provisions of Paragraph 2, Article 303 of the "Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China" and should be investigated for criminal responsibility as the crime of operating a gambling den. [Basic Case Facts] In mid-February 2018, after discussion, defendants Yang Moumou, Jin Moumou, and Kai Moumou each contributed 10,000 yuan to purchase mobile phones and WeChat accounts. They used mobile WeChat to establish the "New Perfect" red envelope "Bull Bull" gambling group. Defendant Yang Moumou was responsible for daily management within the group, defendant Jin Moumou was responsible for adding/subtracting points and Alipay settlements, and defendant Kai Moumou was responsible for operating the mobile robot software. They invited players to gamble by grabbing red envelopes and comparing Bull Bull points. By early April 2018, they had accumulated a cut of 210,000 yuan, and the three defendants shared the illicit proceeds equally. After the case was discovered, defendants Yang Moumou and Kai Moumou each returned 70,000 yuan in illicit proceeds, and defendant Jin Moumou returned 20,000 yuan in illicit proceeds. [Case Handling Process and Result] This case was prosecuted by the Ningguo People's Procuratorate on May 29, 2019, against defendants Yang Moumou, Jin Moumou, and Kai Moumou for the suspected crime of operating a gambling den to the Ningguo People's Court. After trial, the Ningguo People's Court sentenced defendant Yang Moumou to three years imprisonment and a fine of 30,000 yuan for the crime of operating a gambling den; sentenced defendant Jin Moumou to three years imprisonment and a fine of 30,000 yuan; and sentenced defendant Kai Moumou to three years imprisonment and a fine of 30,000 yuan. [Typical Significance] Gambling is a social毒瘤 (cancer). With the rapid development of modern network technology, gambling has gradually penetrated the Internet. Online gambling is not constrained by time or environment, can spread rapidly and widely through the network, has low crime costs, relatively concealed methods, a large radiation range, and is difficult to supervise, already seriously endangering social harmony and stability. In this case, the three defendants, for the purpose of profit, solicited gamblers by inviting people to join WeChat groups, and conducted gambling by grabbing red envelopes in the WeChat groups and comparing "Bull Bull" points. They continuously organized online gambling activities for a certain period, accumulating a cut profit of 210,000 yuan. The Ningguo People's Procuratorate accurately characterized the nature, determining that the above behavior conformed to the provisions of Paragraph 2, Article 303 of the Criminal Law, constituting the crime of operating a gambling den and falling under "serious circumstances." They promptly prosecuted the three defendants, demonstrating the procuratorial organ's determination to severely punish online gambling criminal activities and effectively maintaining social stability and the safety of people's property. Typical Case [Keywords] Fraud, Conditional Non-Prosecution, Social Investigation [Basic Case Facts] Yue Moumou, male, born in 1999, Han ethnicity, was a student at a school in Xuancheng city at the time of the crime. In July 2017, suspect Yue Moumou posted information on the "Idle Fish" online platform about selling his "Zotac PGF GTX1070 Home Use" computer graphics card. During transactions with buyers, Yue Moumou repeatedly used fabricated facts and concealed the truth to defraud Yin Moumou and Ma Moumou of property, totaling 37,700 yuan. On July 24, 2017, police from the Jing County Public Security Bureau, through clues from higher-level public security organs about a suspected fraudulent package, apprehended suspect Yue Moumou at his home in Jing County on the spot and found a快递包裹 (express package) containing a sound card at the scene. After the case was discovered, suspect Yue Moumou and his legal representative Wu Moumou successively returned the full losses to the two victims and obtained their forgiveness. [Case Handling Process] On October 31, 2017, the Jing County Public Security Bureau transferred Yue Moumou's case for suspected fraud to the Jing County People's Procuratorate for review and prosecution. After review, the Jing County Procuratorate believed that suspect Yue Moumou, for the purpose of illegal possession, used fabricated facts and concealed the truth to defraud others of money, a relatively large amount, and his actions had violated criminal law, constituting the crime of fraud. Considering statutory and discretionary mitigating circumstances, the minor Yue Moumou might be sentenced to less than one year of imprisonment. The case met the conditions for prosecution. Simultaneously, during the review process, the procuratorial organ found that Yue Moumou indeed showed signs of confessing and repenting, and actively returned all illegal gains and obtained the victims' forgiveness. Following the provisions of the "Guidelines for Juvenile Criminal Procuratorial Work (Trial)", after listening to the opinions of Yue Moumou himself, his legal representative, defender, the two victims, and the public security organ, they conducted a social investigation on Yue Moumou, and submitted to the prosecutors' joint meeting and the procuratorial committee for collective research on whether conditional non-prosecution could be applied to Yue Moumou. Finally, on December 8, 2017, the Jing County Procuratorate decided to impose conditional non-prosecution on Yue Moumou and set a 10-month probation period for him. During the probation period, the conditionally non-prosecuted person Yue Moumou worked at a computer company in Jing County, responsible for the maintenance of monitoring equipment. He performed well, worked actively, complied with laws and regulations, and obeyed supervision. He submitted a "Probation Period Report" monthly as required by the procuratorial organ, and submitted bank account statements and Alipay, WeChat transfer records and other materials to the procuratorial organ every three months, reporting his activities. On October 8, 2018, after the probation period ended, the Jing County People's Procuratorate, considering Yue Moumou's performance during the probation period, finally decided not to prosecute Yue Moumou. [Typical Significance] Juvenile delinquency is largely related to their living conditions. Social investigations can fully understand the life situation, usual performance, criminal motives, etc., of juvenile suspects, thereby enabling more targeted assistance and education efforts to save juvenile offenders. In this case, to better provide assistance and education to Yue Moumou, the handling prosecutor learned through social investigation that during his school years, Yue Moumou had average grades, was quite interested in computer network technology, got along well with classmates, but usually spent money lavishly, which was also the main reason for his fraud crime. After understanding the relevant situation, during two interrogations, the handling prosecutor explained the law and the harm of crime to Yue Moumou to avoid him going astray again. At the same time, they explained the basic content of conditional non-prosecution to the juvenile suspect and his legal representative, including the legal basis, applicable procedures, relief procedures, investigation procedures, additional obligations, and legal consequences. After announcing the conditional non-prosecution decision, the procuratorial organ formulated a specific plan for the supervision and inspection环节 (link), and innovatively used a "quantitative assessment" method to evaluate Yue Moumou's performance during the probation period, avoiding mere formality in supervision and inspection. Furthermore, preventing and reducing juvenile delinquency cannot be separated from school support. The procuratorial organ found that Yue Moumou's school had insufficient legal education and publicity, so it issued a procuratorial suggestion to the school, recommending that the school strengthen legal publicity regarding common property crimes and crimes infringing on personal rights, and improve students' awareness of the illegality and harmfulness of using computer networks for crime. Simultaneously, it aimed to enhance the self-protection awareness of minors in school. Reviewed by Song Congwen, Chen Jian Text by First Procuratorial Department Edited by Zha Dan
