Title: Nearly a thousand students each paid a 365 yuan registration fee, braved the scorching heat in Ningbo to take the Olympic Math competition—why is the违规 "Hope Cup" still being held? Is it worth participating in? Content: For a long time, our media and the Ministry of Education have been promoting the idea that "Olympic Math" or other "subject competitions" are acts of "pulling up seedlings to help them grow" or even "distorted and crazy" behavior. This bizarre approach is truly astonishing: "Olympic Math"... violates educational principles; the distorted and crazy Olympic Math harms students' physical and mental health, intensifies social conflicts, and has drawn strong public reaction. On the eve of the spring semester, the Ministry of Education showed its determination to crack down heavily on "Olympic Math," with strong resolve, clear direction, and practical measures, reflecting the courage and determination of the education authorities to respond to public concerns and address deep-seated educational contradictions and problems. We applaud this, and the public has high expectations. ...We believe that, following the Ministry of Education's deployment and requirements, by firmly grasping key enrollment links, strengthening supervision of training institutions and guidance for parents, strictly supervising, and punishing according to the law, the current overheated "Olympic Math fever" can be alleviated. The governance of "Olympic Math" has been discussed for years, but it has repeatedly resurfaced, becoming a stubborn problem. The key issue is that some regions and schools have insufficient understanding and inadequate implementation, causing good policies and measures to become distorted during execution. Therefore, the key to the effectiveness of this new "Olympic Math" governance policy lies in its execution and implementation. Education administrative departments and schools at all levels should treat the governance of Olympic Math as a battlefield to test their work style and a stage to showcase the image of education. They should understand the issue from the perspective of running education that satisfies the people and promoting social fairness, addressing both symptoms and root causes with comprehensive measures to ensure that good policies are not distorted and that the public can benefit. Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China, 2013-02-22, "Real Measures Yield Real Results," link: Look at the wording used! "Show its determination to crack down heavily," "governance"—what a resolute attitude! A similar attitude, on the Ministry of Education's official website, seems to be reserved only for illegal and criminal activities, anti-pornography and anti-piracy campaigns, and reducing student burdens, alongside Olympic Math. It must be said that for our Ministry of Education bureaucrats, Olympic Math (and even extracurricular education) is like a flood beast, endangering the youth of the Republic! Similarly: Recently, media like CCTV reported on the "crazy Olympic Math" phenomenon, attracting widespread social attention. On August 21, the Beijing Municipal Education Commission held a press briefing, stating that it would take four measures to intensify governance, resolutely severing the link between Olympic Math results and升学, while welcoming widespread media participation in supervision to jointly create a good social environment for the healthy growth of primary and secondary school students. How "crazy" is Olympic Math? According to reports, some parents go into debt to enroll their children in Olympic Math classes, and children are forced into these classes. The most exaggerated example was on July 21 this year, when the heaviest rainfall in 60 years in Beijing still couldn't stop students from attending Olympic Math classes. In the pouring rain, the teacher expected most students to be late or absent, but upon arriving in class, found that not one of the more than 20 students was late; the parents accompanying the children were drenched like "drowned rats" but had no complaints. Similarly, in the Ministry of Education's description of students' holiday lives, we see: The winter vacation is half over, and vast numbers of primary and secondary school students, accompanied by their parents, are exercising, cultivating interests, respecting the elderly and showing filial piety, and engaging in labor practices, gaining a meaningful holiday. But it has also been found that some are taking advantage of the winter vacation to illegally hold competition activities. For example, a WeChat group spread消息 about holding an online "Hope Math"违规 competition on the sixth day of the Lunar New Year. Regarding this, the Ministry of Education, together with relevant departments, conducted serious investigations, and the relevant institutions have issued statements denying involvement in organizing违规 competitions. It seems that during holidays, anything can be done except studying! Then I would like to ask further, are publications like "Happy Winter/Summer Vacation" printed for profit, or to poison children's minds and bodies, making primary and secondary school students' lives meaningless? (Although, indeed, the significance of these trash publications being printed is minimal.) Overall, the lords of the Ministry of Education and the media seem to superficially hold a strange idea: "Since Olympic Math is only suitable for 5% of students, then to prevent the remaining 95% from wasting time and money, we decide to ban Olympic Math—so that no one learns it." Every year, new policies are introduced, "cracking down heavily" with a one-size-fits-all approach to ban extracurricular tutoring, Olympic Math, competitions, and all knowledge. I wonder if the official lords have ever studied in Cambodia at some point—why do I always see shadows of certain past figures? Actually, the answer is obvious. For the broad youth population, Olympic Math and subject education are completely unimportant to the official lords—they themselves have long passed the age of learning this content, and their descendants can always enjoy the best public school treatment—if they wish, the best private education is just a trivial matter for them. What is truly important is to give the outside world the impression that "the Ministry of Education and the media are cracking down heavily on educational inequality." Similarly, it is often said that the college entrance exam (Gaokao) is the fairest exam. While this is not false, it is only one side: for those who advance through the Gaokao, it is of course almost fair, but there are always some who can bypass it. Subject competitions are one way, and the Ministry of Education and media use them as targets to gain inexplicable public trust; when it comes to topics like the annually hyped high-level athletes, "transshipped crabs" from Guinea-Bissau, 4+4 programs, Wang Chuqin's public enrollment into Peking University, etc., they either play dead or敷衍. I think online反感 towards these power and升学 channels should far exceed that towards Olympic Math and competitions—why not crack down heavily on them? We say again, actually the answer is obvious: because they need these channels.

Title: 2013 Yiliang "Tourism Culture Flower Street Festival" Concluded on the 18th_Investment Trends_Kunming Municipal People's Government Portal Content: Dragon boat racing on the Nanpan River. The 8-day Yiliang 2013 "Tourism Culture Flower Street Festival" concluded on June 18th. "A festive season meets a prosperous era, harmony promotes development." This year's "Flower Street Festival," centered around the theme "City of Flowers and Water, Livable Yiliang," continuously enriched the festival's content by integrating elements such as flower exhibitions and sales, flower selection competitions, commodity sales, dragon boat races, the "68 Bends" bicycle race, cultural performances, the launch ceremony of the Yiliang Literature Series, intangible cultural heritage exhibitions, the Beautiful Yiliang Photography Exhibition, and the 2013 Investment Promotion Signing Ceremony. It truly embodied the concept of innovation, excellence, celebration, and harmony, keeping the traditional Yiliang Flower Street Festival fresh, distinctive, and full of charm. "This year's Tourism Culture Flower Street Festival was jointly organized by the County Culture, Tourism, Radio, Television, and Sports Bureau and the Tiancheng Group. The County Bureau promptly invited media friends and extensively invited stakeholders from the tourism industry, especially well-established travel agencies, to visit Yiliang for inspections and reconnaissance. The County Development and Reform Bureau and the Economic and Trade Bureau, adhering to the concept of making friends through the festival, invited important business guests to Yiliang for business trips, to strengthen connections, discuss major projects, laying the foundation for economic and trade negotiations in the second half of the year," said Yiliang County Mayor He Jiansheng. During the Flower Street Festival, Yiliang leveraged its resource advantages to carefully launch high-quality tourism and cultural activities, striving to make the Flower Street Festival a spectacular event full of highlights. This created a wave of promoting tourism and showcasing culture, allowing the activities to fully display the charm of Yiliang's "City of Flowers and Water" and amplify the effects of tourism culture. Extremely Lively 660,000 People "Pack" the Flower Street On the opening day, 70,000 tourists from all over flocked to Yiliang. The second day of the Flower Street Festival coincided with the annual Dragon Boat Festival, and the number of tourists reached 90,000 at one point. The small county town was packed, with crowds everywhere, pushing the entire Flower Street Festival to its climax. Throughout the festival, long queues formed every morning at 9 a.m. at the Yiliang toll station entrance, with cars from various regions entering the county town in an orderly manner. Noon was the busiest and most congested time on Xiangyahu Avenue. Men, women, and children jostled shoulder to shoulder; under the scorching sun, there wasn't even room to open an umbrella. "It's too crowded, how can there be so many people!" Complaints were heard incessantly. "The Yiliang Flower Street is the liveliest. Coupled with the local custom of visiting the flower street and buying flowers during the Dragon Boat Festival, the flower street is overcrowded every day," said local resident Qin Hua, while squeezing into the endless "sea of people" on the flower street. "Every day, from 10 a.m. until 1 a.m. the next morning is the peak period for pedestrian flow in the main venue area," introduced Yiliang County Deputy Party Secretary Lu Chunlin. According to statistics, this "Flower Street Festival" attracted 660,000 visitor trips to Yiliang for viewing, admiring, purchasing flowers, and shopping. Flower sales reached over 2 million RMB, and comprehensive revenue from tourism, commerce, and other aspects exceeded 46 million RMB. At the Flower Street Festival site, many locals and visitors were busy viewing, admiring, and buying flowers. "This year's Flower Street Festival is much livelier than previous years and on a larger scale," introduced a relevant responsible person from Yiliang County. Superior natural, geographical, transportation conditions, and a profound cultural foundation have contributed to the unique advantages of Yiliang County's flower production. As of the end of last month, the total area for seedlings and flowers in Yiliang reached 55,252 mu, with an annual total output value exceeding 800 million RMB. This includes 7,000 mu for fresh cut flowers, with an annual output of 420 million stems and an output value of 70 million RMB; and 48,252 mu for landscaping seedlings and potted flowers/penjing, with an output of 250 million pots/plants and an output value of 730 million RMB. The county has successively introduced 21 enterprises for seedling base construction, attracting investment of 199 million RMB. There are 16 enterprises engaged in landscaping seedlings and potted flowers/penjing, among which 5 have areas over 1,000 mu, 3 over 500 mu, and 10 have areas over 300 mu with annual business revenue exceeding 5 million RMB. There are over 2,000 individual散户 growers. The county employs over 40,000 people in the landscaping seedling industry, with more than 500 varieties of seedlings planted. During the 8-day festival, tourists enjoyed the beautiful scenery of Yiliang's blooming flowers, saw Yiliang's top-tier tourist attractions, and tasted Yiliang's unique local snacks. They came with excitement and left satisfied, becoming fascinated with and falling in love with Yiliang, which transformed into the passion and action for starting businesses, investing, and building in Yiliang. Intangible cultural heritage display activity - making giant incense for the Ancient Town Giant Incense Festival. Colorful and Diverse Activities Adorn the Festival This year's Flower Street Festival featured numerous activities covering a wide range. There were traditional exhibitions and sales themed around flowers, including the Top Ten Bougainvillea Selection, as well as events highlighting regional culture like the Beautiful Yiliang Photography Exhibition, the launch ceremony of the Yiliang Literature Series, and the Intangible Cultural Heritage Exhibition. Additionally, there were exciting sports events like the Dragon Boat Race and the Jing'anshao "68 Bends" Bicycle Challenge, fully reflecting a festive atmosphere of public participation and joyful harmony. The 2013 Tourism Culture Flower Street Festival placed greater emphasis on the harmonious factors of the county's natural, cultural, and ecological landscape; it emphasized government leadership, market operation, and enterprise organization. This year's festival was meticulously crafted with an investment of 5 million RMB from Kunming Tiancheng Real Estate Co., Ltd.; actively creating the beautiful floral environment of "A Pleasant Flower City Built by All, Bougainvillea Blooms Everywhere" to welcome guests from all directions. To better promote the "flower attire" and strengthen the traditional industry of the county flower—bougainvillea, Yiliang utilized the platform of the Tourism Culture Flower Street Festival to conduct the "Top Ten Bougainvillea" selection activity county-wide. Ten potted bougainvillea were selected in the penjing category, and ten sites were selected in the landscape greening category, with total rewards exceeding ten thousand RMB, aiming to advocate and encourage the public to plant bougainvillea, build Yiliang into the "Flower Capital" for bougainvillea, and thereby enrich the connotation of "City of Flowers and Water." The 2013 "Jiuxiang Cup" First Yiliang "68 Bends" Mountain Bike Climb Challenge was one of the series of events of the Flower Street Festival. 268 cyclists from 13 provinces and cities gathered at the famous Yiliang Jing'anshao "68 Bends" to compete for the title of "King of the Climb." At 9 a.m., the 268 cyclists and enthusiasts, fully equipped, were ready. With the sound of the starting gun, the 205 male participants quickly mounted their bikes and headed towards the mountaintop via the "68 Bends." Subsequently, the 63 female participants also embarked on their journey. Riding on the "68 Bends," where steep S-shaped bends appear approximately every hundred meters, posed a great test to the riders' speed and endurance. Ultimately, He Chong from Hangzhou and Hu Tiantian from Hainan won the men's and women's group championships respectively. As part of the Flower Street Festival activities, Yiliang held the launch ceremony for the "Yiliang Literature Series." The series, totaling over a million words, collects works from 15 writers, adding a significant touch to Yiliang's cultural development. The "Yiliang Literature Series" includes works by 15 writers, such as local writer Tang Siliang's "Green Ode" and Zhang Weilin's "Turtle Insect Chronicle." The entire series exceeds a million words and includes novels, prose, poetry, and reportage, featuring the efforts of writers from old, middle-aged, and young generations, as well as works by emerging writers. While developing its economy, Yiliang highly prioritizes revitalizing the county through science and education, creating a new "one-dragon" pattern for tourism culture with Jiuxiang cave culture as the "dragon head," the Nanpan River tourism cultural landscape corridor as the "dragon body," and Zhushan ecological culture as the "dragon tail." Delving into these tourism resources provides more fresh material for Yiliang's literary creation. Prominent Benefits: 46 Million RMB Earned in 8 Days This Flower Street Festival was a win-win event that gathered wealth and popularity. Both economic and social benefits were fully highlighted. People tirelessly enjoyed strolling the flower street and buying flowers. During the Tourism Culture Flower Street Festival, 242 flower farmers set up 439 exhibition booths, organizing over 800 varieties and more than 200,000 pots of flowers for the flower exhibition and sale; 300 merchants organized over 400 varieties for the commodity exhibition and sale. According to the organizing committee statistics, this year's Flower Street Festival generated comprehensive revenue from tourism, commerce, and other aspects exceeding 46 million RMB, indeed a substantial profit. It is worth mentioning that during the Flower Street Festival, Yiliang timely held an investment promotion presentation and signing ceremony, both achieving significant results. Investment intentions for 6 projects were reached, with agreed investment amounting to 823 million RMB. The "Tourism Culture Flower Street Festival," as an important form of "culture building the stage, economy singing the opera," has been successfully held for 8 sessions since 2005. It has become a festival brand integrating flowers, tourism, culture, economy, trade, and exhibitions. The communication platform of "using flowers as a medium, making friends through flowers" has become a major feature and highlight in Yiliang County's investment promotion work. "Holding the signing ceremony on such a day is precisely hoping to use flowers as a medium, make friends through flowers, and use the Flower Street Festival as a platform, bridge, and link, allowing entrepreneurs to experience the flower street culture and Yiliang's harmonious development, thereby further promoting economic and cultural exchanges and cooperation," promoted He Jiansheng. The Yiliang County Tourism Culture Flower Street Festival, as an important form of "culture building the stage, economy singing the opera," has, since 2005, become an increasingly broad platform radiating across regions and an important bridge for enhancing foreign economic and trade exchanges. There were 6 projects signed this time, including both internally cultivated and externally introduced projects, with a total agreed investment of 800 million RMB. The projects involve liquor production, minerals, building materials, new energy development, commercial city construction, and amusement park construction. These include: a project by Kunming Yiliang Saffron Wine Co., Ltd. for an annual production line of 1,200 tons of saffron health series products, with agreed investment of 58 million RMB; a project by Kunming Yaoming Resource Comprehensive Utilization Co., Ltd. for an annual 400,000-ton coal blending center, with agreed investment of 100 million RMB; a project by Yiliang Red Lion Cement Co., Ltd. for an annual production line of 800,000 square meters of commercial concrete, with agreed investment of 100 million RMB; the Kunming Yiliang Baishen Commercial Center construction project with investment of 100 million RMB; the Yiliang County Shuanglong Wind Farm construction project with investment of 450 million RMB; and the Yiliang Xiangyahu Amusement Park project with investment of 15 million RMB. The successful hosting of the 2013 Yiliang County Tourism Culture Flower Street Festival fully demonstrates Yiliang's determination and confidence in building the largest "City of Flowers and Water" in Kunming and the most pleasant and livable "New Living Room" in eastern Kunming. It further激发了 the broad masses of people in the county with a sense of responsibility and mission to love and build their hometown. Centered around the goals, Yiliang will persevere, strive hard, with加倍 high morale and加倍 pragmatic style, create new highlights for the "Tourist Resort, Gourmet Kingdom, Leisure Paradise," comprehensively open up a new局面 for economic and social development, and make the Yiliang Tourism Culture Flower Street Festival a never-ending event! (Kunming Daily Reporter Yang Xuehuang, Intern Ge Jie, Correspondent Zhao Ping)

Title: Should China implement free universal healthcare? Does everyone support it? Content: Public policies inevitably benefit some while disadvantaging others. For example, I live in Australia, which has universal healthcare. All permanent residents or citizens (and their temporary spouses) can obtain a Medicare card. However, the cost structure is relatively complex. The most direct way to see the cost is on the annual tax return from your salary – it shows how much you paid for the Medicare levy. This amount is solely based on your income, meaning you pay it even if you never see a doctor. So, essentially, young people who have started working are contributing. Of course, those who pay little or no tax contribute less to this fee but benefit more. Hence, I say public policies inevitably create winners and losers. But I know that I am a master of this country; I have the right to know and ways to participate in the discussion. Furthermore, I will age, and if health issues arise in the future, this healthcare system can relieve me of many worries. Coincidentally, today I received a letter about voting for the district councilor this Saturday. Both competing parties have made promises regarding medical services. The Labor Party even sent a bilingual campaign letter to my home: Labor Party campaign letter Liberal Party campaign letter. I mention Australia's situation just for your reference. The specifics of China's free healthcare are far too complex. Based on what I know, even analyzing it might risk getting my account banned. Moreover, whether I or anyone here supports it or not, what difference does it really make?

Title: Contributing Ideas for the Water Environment Management of Rivers in Putuo District Content: A beautiful river and lake ecological environment is the foundation for ensuring healthy public life and green development. Topics such as river ecosystem restoration, the impact of pump station discharges during rainy weather, waterfront space greening, landscape quality improvement, the planning and construction of recreational waterfront platforms, and the handling of issues like river release, fishing, and wild swimming are all hot topics close to citizens' lives. Recently, the "Suhe Discussion Hall (Second Session)" – a major discussion activity focusing on the "One River, One Policy" for key rivers – was held at the Putuo District Party-Mass Service Center. Nearly 200 participants, including district people's congress representatives, district CPPCC members, community residents, community cadres, property managers, enterprise representatives, students, functional departments from the municipal, district, and sub-district levels, professionals, and media observers, actively participated. The event also invited some enthusiastic residents who had raised related issues through the People's Suggestions mailbox and the 12345 citizen hotline. Meanwhile, the organizers also launched a special collection of people's suggestions titled "I Contribute an Idea for the Water Environment Management of Rivers in Putuo District" on the Suishenban app, welcoming citizens to actively provide suggestions through online channels. Participants engaged in lively discussions based on their life and work practices, covering topics such as how to better manage pollution from pump station discharges after rain, how to standardize the management of river fishing and swimming, and how to protect the river water ecology. PART.1: What to do if water quality deteriorates and odors appear after pump station discharge? After discharge from the Taopu River pump station, the water quality is polluted, producing a pungent smell, causing nearby residents to hesitate to open their windows. They hope the government departments will provide feedback on relevant management standards and measures. After rain, the Xiqiu River has floating debris and garbage; residents hope the management departments will clean it promptly and improve related facilities. On-site, residents reported water pollution issues caused by pump station discharges after rain, with situations at Taopu River and Xiqiu River being particularly prominent. "Taopu River is cleaned in nine sections. Upon receiving the discharge notification via text message, river cleaning and maintenance personnel arrive at the discharge outlet within half an hour, clean the discharged pollutants within an hour, and use cleaning boats for mechanical cleaning," said Zhen Tile, head of the Putuo District river maintenance team. Wang Huiqing from the Water Affairs Section of the Putuo District Municipal Water Affairs Management Center responded, "To ensure urban flood control and drainage safety, rainwater pump stations along rivers like Taopu River and Xiqiu River discharge rainwater into the rivers when the operating water level is reached. Due to pollutants like road dust, leaves, and garbage being washed into the pipes, and the fermentation of accumulated rainwater and sludge in the pipes, the discharged water quality is poor. We arrange for cleaning personnel to prepare in advance at each discharge outlet, remove garbage, and collect and treat it at designated points." PART.2: Should riverside fishing be managed or not? Xia Peizhen, a Changfeng river protection volunteer, mentioned, "The Changfeng river protection volunteer team actively patrols along the Suzhou River bank, promptly identifying and reporting issues like garbage and floating debris, and pays special attention to fishing activities along the Suzhou River, suggesting standardized fishing spots and times." Pan Linyi, a resident of Changshou Road Sub-district, had a different opinion: "Fishing along the Suzhou River damages the greenery along the walkway and leads to uncivilized behaviors like climbing over railings. Fishing should be managed through registration, fees, etc." Wu Fang, secretary of the Zhiyinyuan Residential Committee, said, "Many residents report that fishing at the bends offers the best experience, but it indeed causes damage to greenery and safety hazards. Therefore, sub-district offices, urban management departments, etc., have dissuaded such activities. It is suggested to reasonably set up fishing spots through a combination of疏导 and control." In response to the above issues, Dong Rui, Deputy Director of the Putuo District Water Affairs Bureau, stated, "Shanghai has issued the 'Shanghai Huangpu River Suzhou River Waterfront Public Space Regulations,' and Putuo District issued the 'Putuo District Suzhou River Shoreline Management Measures (Trial)' last year, specifying fishing as a restricted activity. Putuo District has set up fishing points according to the management measures, prioritizing management safety by selecting points with railings, open views, and easy observation. However, these points do not fully match the actual needs of anglers. We will optimize and adjust the points based on the suggestions received." PART.3: Should citizens be allowed to swim in the rivers? Xu Huiping, a resident of Changzheng Town, proposed, "Many residents swim in the Caijiabang River near Yunling West Road because the river water is clear and the scenery pleasant, making it suitable for cooling off in summer. We hope some rivers can be opened for open-air swimming." The District Water Affairs Bureau responded, "Swimming in rivers is not recommended or encouraged, for two main reasons: health concerns, as river management does not regulate indicators like E. coli; and safety concerns, as the safety facilities along rivers are not equipped to swimming pool standards. Meanwhile, the District Water Affairs Bureau will take this discussion activity as an opportunity to actively explore and research topics related to river swimming." Ju Yunpeng, a reporter from People's Daily, said, "With the Paris Olympics in full swing recently, we hope Shanghai can benchmark internationally and set higher goals for water environment management." Tang Xiaotian, a resident of Yichuan Road Sub-district, suggested, "For issues like fishing and swimming, the government should engage in consultations with all sectors of society, adhering to asking the people for their needs and ideas, to solve problems in the most reasonable and efficient way." PART.4: How to solve the problem of golden apple snail infestation in rivers during summer? With summer arriving, the problem of golden apple snail infestation in rivers was also a focus of discussion. Yang Qingze, a student and community 'little river chief' from Jinding Huayuan, raised his hand and said, "I hope we can introduce species that control golden apple snails, increase publicity about their hazards, and use channels like the Young Pioneers broadcast station and primary and secondary school life science classes for educational promotion." What measures are currently available in the industry to control the growth of golden apple snail populations? She Xinzheng, head of the Putuo District river water ecological maintenance unit, explained, "The golden apple snail is an invasive species with no natural predators in China. It damages aquatic plants in rivers, affecting water quality. Currently, the industry mainly employs two measures: one is using chemicals, but this is generally avoided as it affects fish and shrimp; the second method is controlling egg production by manually removing eggs to control population growth. We hope citizens can inform us via the River Chief publicity signs when they see golden apple snails or their eggs, so we can handle them promptly." Additionally, Zhou Qiong, a representative of the Putuo District People's Congress, Ma Xueyan, an Algerian international student from Shanghai University, Xie Yixuan, a graduate student from East China Normal University, and others offered suggestions and opinions on controlling pollution sources like industrial wastewater and restaurant discharges into rivers, channels for citizen participation in water environment management, and setting up storage facilities to reduce pollution. Negotiation expert Pan Li said, "To address the information gap between government communication and public reception, first, standards must be clear and public; second, rights and responsibilities must be balanced." Pan Yun, a professor at Shanghai University, suggested, "Government departments should create more platforms and channels to listen to citizens' opinions and suggestions, making policy formulation and work advancement more aligned with public needs." Xu Xiaodong, Deputy Director of the River Chief Office of the Municipal Water Affairs Bureau, responded regarding the city's water affairs management work and how to improve the water environment from three aspects: source pollution reduction, process control, and end-of-pipe potential tapping. Since the beginning of this year, Putuo District has held two sessions of the "Suhe Discussion Hall" activity, innovating participation models and opening up expression of opinions. Using a series of "Golden Idea" discussion halls as a bridge, the district aims to gather people's wisdom and strength through joint consultation, co-construction, co-governance, and sharing. The valuable ideas proposed during this activity will be carefully studied by the Municipal Water Affairs Bureau, the Municipal People's Suggestions Collection Office, and relevant departments of Putuo District, who will actively promote the implementation of related policies and measures. Title: Former Director of Land and Resources Bureau in Luliang County, Yunnan Sentenced for Bribery. Content: Gao Shijiu, former director of the Land and Resources Management Bureau in Luliang County, Yunnan, was sentenced to 10 years in prison yesterday by the Luliang County People's Court for accepting bribes totaling 320,000 RMB. Additionally, all illicit money he 'spit out' was confiscated. According to the investigation, from June 2003 to July 2004, Yuan, while developing a residential area in Luliang County, gave 60,000 RMB to Gao Shijiu to facilitate land supply procedures. In September 2003, Miao offered 50,000 RMB to Gao to secure a plot of land south of Zhongshu Primary School in the county development zone, and succeeded. From April 2003 to July 2004, Dong, who contracted the renovation of the Luliang County Land Transaction Hall, gave Gao 90,000 RMB in four installments, leading to the project starting on schedule and passing inspection smoothly. From January to April 2004, a deputy manager of a Hunan-based clothing branch company offered a 40,000 RMB kickback to secure an order for uniforms for Luliang Land and Resources Bureau employees. On April 16 this year, the procuratorate, armed with solid evidence, prosecuted Gao Shijiu for suspected bribery. Considering that Gao voluntarily 'spit out' the 320,000 RMB bribe after being apprehended and confessed to other bribery facts not yet known to the procuratorate, the Luliang County Court rendered the above judgment in accordance with relevant legal provisions. After the first-instance verdict was announced, the 50-year-old defendant Gao Shijiu deemed the sentence too harsh and expressed his intention to appeal. (According to Xinhua News Agency)

Title: What are the reasons for water leakage from the small hole at the bottom of a baby bottle? Content: There may be multiple reasons for water leakage from the small hole at the bottom of a baby bottle. First, there might be foreign objects blocking the area around the small hole, leading to poor sealing and thus leakage. For example, milk residue or dust entering the hole can affect its normal drainage function. Second, if the rubber or plastic components around the small hole at the bottom of the bottle age or become damaged, the seal deteriorates, which can also easily cause leakage. Furthermore, the baby bottle might be subjected to external forces such as impacts or compression during use, causing the connection between the small hole and surrounding components to loosen, thereby triggering leakage. Additionally, improper installation could be another reason, such as the small hole not being aligned correctly with the drainage channel, or related components not being installed properly. Another possibility is quality issues with the bottle itself, where there are inherent design or manufacturing defects leading to poor sealing performance of the small hole. 1. Regarding foreign object blockage, milk residue is a common occurrence. If the bottle is not cleaned promptly after the baby finishes drinking, milk residue can easily adhere around the small hole. Over time, the residue will gradually dry and harden, blocking the hole. Dust might also enter through the bottle's opening, especially if the bottle is placed in a less clean environment. The presence of these foreign objects hinders the normal drainage of the hole. When there is liquid inside the bottle, it will seep out from the blocked area, causing leakage. 2. Component aging and damage: As usage time increases, the rubber or plastic components around the small hole will gradually wear out and age. Rubber parts may lose elasticity and fail to fit tightly around the hole, resulting in a poor seal. Plastic parts might develop cracks or deform, similarly affecting the sealing effect. This type of aging and damage is more common in bottles that have been used for a long time. Once it occurs, leakage problems will follow. 3. External forces: The baby bottle might accidentally be subjected to impacts during daily use. For example, the baby might knock against the bottle while playing, or it might experience jolts during transport. Compression can also occur, such as when the bottle is placed in a cramped space and gets squeezed. These external forces can alter the connection between the small hole and the surrounding components, making the originally tight structure loose and thus causing leakage. 4. Improper installation: When installing the relevant components of the bottle, if the small hole is not accurately aligned with the drainage channel, liquid cannot flow smoothly through the hole and will instead seep out from other gaps. Alternatively, if the related components are not fully installed, the seal around the small hole remains incomplete, which can also easily lead to leakage issues. 5. Quality issues: If the bottle itself has design or manufacturing defects, such as an unreasonable hole size or insufficient precision in the fit with surrounding components, it may result in poor sealing performance of the small hole. Even under normal use conditions, leakage can easily occur. Such quality issues might have been present when the bottle was purchased but only discovered after some time of use.

Title: Dongying Women's Federation News Content: Time: 2020-02-13 Source: Publisher: Hekou District Liuhe Street Clicks: [Font: Large Medium Small] During the critical period of prevention and control work for the pneumonia epidemic caused by the novel coronavirus, He'an Community established the "Seven-color Flower Epidemic Prevention and Control" Party Member Volunteer Service Team to assist the community and residential property companies in duty assignments at important roads and traffic nodes, as well as in the management and persuasion of relevant personnel to return. Yuan Jinlan, a retired Party member from the Qiufeng Party Branch, took the initiative to volunteer, overcoming the difficulty of needing to care for her elderly parents at home. She stood duty with other Party members at the Qiufengyuan East Gate Party Member Responsibility Post, assisting community and property security personnel in epidemic prevention and control work. Having previously served as Deputy Director of the Justice Bureau, she is now a full-time member of the District Care Committee and Deputy Director of the District Government Agencies Care Committee. After retirement, she has consistently served the healthy growth of young people, acting as a volunteer for protecting the rights of women and children in Dongying City and as a "Five Olds" volunteer. She also uses her legal expertise to provide free legal consultations for residents, draft legal documents, guide residents in emotional management, correctly seek dispute resolution channels, and promote harmonious coexistence. Additionally, she enthusiastically takes photos for community group activities to promote positive energy. She said: Because we are Party members, we must have a sense of responsibility and courage to take on duties. In the face of the epidemic, we march forward against the tide, fully committed to epidemic prevention and control work, and safeguarding the safety of community residents. Marching alongside her against the tide is her son, Shi Liang, a retired soldier who has repeatedly donated to comrades-in-arms with family difficulties, and a volunteer of the Hekou District Volunteer Association. He is usually enthusiastic about public welfare and offers suggestions for community management. A few days ago, learning that there was a shortage of personnel for epidemic prevention, he immediately gave up his rest. Together with other volunteers from the Emergency Epidemic Prevention Volunteer Service Team, he put on masks, gloves, and professional protective suits, disregarding the pungent smell of disinfectant. He carefully sprayed disinfectant at important entrances and exits of 12 communities including He'an, Yuyuan, Caiyuan, Hekang, Hehui, and Huaou Shopping Mall. Sweat and disinfectant mixed together, drenching his clothes, which became discolored and "blotchy" from the chemicals. He said: I have worked as a veterinarian, so I understand too well the importance of timely epidemic prevention. Now that the country is facing difficulties, each of us must shoulder our own responsibility. Generate as much heat as we can, emit as much light as we can, unite our efforts, overcome difficulties, help others to help themselves, and selflessly contribute.

Title: How to view the situation where Zhanjiang City's economy became the only city with negative growth in Guangdong Province in 2024? Content: Zhanjiang can actually fully position itself as a high-end manufacturing base for South China and even the Western Pacific region. This is not empty talk but a conclusion based on existing foundations. Let's first look at Zhanjiang's existing elements: 1. A high-quality port that can reach all regions globally, including bulk cargo, crude oil, and container terminals. 2. An established comprehensive transportation network where railways and highways can meet the logistics needs of high-end manufacturing. If possible, strive to transfer Zhanjiang from Liuzhou Railway to Guangzhou Railway, but it's fine if not achievable. 3. Sufficient labor population; the greater Zhanjiang area has seven million people and has potential attraction for labor from eastern Guangxi, Hainan, and northern Vietnam. 4. Upstream foundations needed for a high-end manufacturing base: world-class refineries (Zhongke Refining and Chemical), world-class steel plants (Baosteel), world-class chemical plants (BASF), world-class glass factories (Saint-Gobain). 5. Abundant land; Zhanjiang possesses the entire Leizhou Peninsula, with terrain mainly plains, minimizing costs for land leveling, development, and factory construction. 6. A livable subtropical marine environment attractive to global high-value labor and management groups. 7. Two universities sufficient for continuously cultivating advanced labor. 8. Proximity to the Yangjiang Nuclear Power Plant, ensuring adequate energy and power supply (this element should rank first but I'm too lazy to revise the layout). Based on the above elements, the Zhanjiang government can focus on attracting the following high-end manufacturing industries to establish factories and manufacturing centers: 1. Automotive manufacturing. Attract new energy vehicle enterprises to establish manufacturing centers targeting western China and Southeast Asia, such as European car companies like Volkswagen and Stellantis that are willing to undergo energy transformation and self-revolution. It would be even better to attract leading companies like BYD and Huawei. 2. Aircraft manufacturing. The primary goal is to attract Airbus or even C919 to establish component or even whole aircraft production plants in Zhanjiang. It's also acceptable if American helicopter companies like Bell and Sikorsky are willing to set up factories; strive to attract European and Chinese helicopter companies as much as possible. 3. Rail transit manufacturing. Strive for CRRC and Bombardier Siemens to set up factories here, especially the latter. Foreign capitals, facing the imminent S3 outbreak, are likely to transfer more production capacity from Europe to China to maintain output. 4. Shipbuilding industry manufacturing. Zhanjiang itself has high-quality naval shipyards and Nanhai Oil's drilling platform production bases with good human resources. It is possible to further attract domestic shipbuilding enterprises to establish production capacity here, especially as they also face the S3 gray rhino, and the demand for naval shipbuilding 'dumpling production' will persist. 5. Spacecraft manufacturing. Zhanjiang can fully become the material production and logistics center for the Wenchang Space Launch Site. Various spacecraft and their required components can be built in Zhanjiang and then transported to Wenchang at the lowest cost and fastest speed via sea transport or a potential future Qiongzhou Strait tunnel. With the support of the provincial party committee and government (if more proactive, even connect resources with relevant State Council ministries, especially the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, with the provincial government's help), the Zhanjiang government can establish a high-end manufacturing investment promotion office, concentrating talent and various resources to attract the aforementioned European industrial companies. Prioritize France (historical connection) and Germany (BASF as a case study), and if resources allow, expand to Italy, Spain, and the UK. Establish offices in these five countries, go all out to attract their attention, and undertake the transfer of Europe's high-end manufacturing industry. Europe's future prospects are quite bleak, coupled with the rhythm of the S3 outbreak. European large enterprises indeed have a demand to transfer to China or the US (no other countries can ensure their asset safety and manufacturing stability besides these two). Zhanjiang can fully connect with this demand in advance. The most crucial thing for doing business and pulling in clients is a successful case to persuade them. Title: How to treat a 1-year-old baby with papular urticaria? Remember these 3 points. Content: Papular urticaria is an allergic disease that often occurs in infants and young children and is prone to recurrence. When papular urticaria appears, it generally produces some red, hive-like bumps accompanied by itching symptoms. Severe scratching can easily lead to skin purulent infection. How to treat a 1-year-old baby with papular urticaria? 1. Papular urticaria is most often caused by insect bites. If the symptoms are relatively mild, just like small mosquito bites, some anti-itch and anti-inflammatory medications can be used for treatment. 2. If it is caused by other allergic factors, or if the symptoms of papular urticaria are severe, it is recommended that parents promptly take the baby to the hospital for examination. After the doctor helps identify the allergen, corresponding anti-allergy treatment should be administered. 3. If the problem is due to the baby's own immune system issues or other influencing factors, it is recommended that parents handle it under the guidance of a doctor. Do not use medication blindly to avoid adverse effects of related drugs on the baby. How to prevent papular urticaria in a 1-year-old baby? 1. Parents can take the baby to the hospital for relevant tests to determine if the baby has an allergic constitution or which substances the baby is prone to allergic reactions to. After identifying the allergens, take protective measures in daily life and try to avoid having the allergen substances around the baby. 2. Maintain good family environmental hygiene and the baby's personal hygiene. Items that the baby frequently comes into contact with, such as toys and bedding, need to be washed and changed frequently, regularly disinfected, and can also be sun-dried. 3. Families with babies should try not to keep pets to avoid parasites carried on pet fur or bodies affecting the baby's health. If you must keep a pet, it is recommended to minimize its contact with the baby and clean the pet regularly. 4. Avoid taking the baby to places with deep grass and many insects, and also try to avoid crowded places. For a one-year-old baby, who has almost no self-care ability, after developing papular urticaria, they are prone to scratching with their hands. Their skin is relatively tender and easily damaged. Therefore, parents should promptly seek medical treatment and usually take the above preventive measures to reduce the likelihood of the baby developing papular urticaria. #医联媒体超能团# #清风计划#

Title: Can Hyperthyroidism in Men Also Affect the Next Generation? Content: Can hyperthyroidism in men also affect the next generation?\n\nMany people want to ask, can hyperthyroidism be left untreated? What are the consequences of not treating it? As a doctor, I really don't understand how these people think. How can hyperthyroidism not be treated? This is a disease that concerns one's own health. Perhaps some people are dismissive, even patients in the early stages of hyperthyroidism question our judgment. This is understandable, after all, these people don't have a deep understanding of hyperthyroidism and don't know its severity. What is hyperthyroidism? The scientific name for hyperthyroidism is hyperthyroidism, which is caused by the thyroid gland synthesizing and releasing too much thyroid hormone, leading to increased body metabolism and sympathetic nerve excitement, causing symptoms such as palpitations, sweating, increased eating and bowel movements, and weight loss. Although early symptoms are not very strong, only making people feel somewhat restless and have a fast metabolism. But once past the early stage, hyperthyroidism can have a severe impact on people. Have you seen people whose eyeballs seem about to pop out? Have you seen people with swollen necks like a ball is stuffed inside? Have you seen those with haggard faces like they've stayed up for a week? These are the symptoms of hyperthyroidism patients. Therefore, hyperthyroidism must be treated, and it's urgent. Another point about hyperthyroidism is that this disease can be hereditary. Not only can women pass it to the next generation, but men also have a chance of passing hyperthyroidism to their children. Below, I will tell you about a case of a patient I once treated. He was an air conditioning installation technician, very young, about twenty-seven or twenty-eight, just married. When he first came to my clinic, I could see his neck was already very noticeable, and his eyeballs were protruding. He told me he had had hyperthyroidism for several years. His family had consulted many doctors, both Western and traditional Chinese medicine, which had improved his condition. But later, due to family reasons, he stopped medication before he was fully recovered, causing his condition to relapse. Then he told me he had started medication again but found that even with consistent use, there was no improvement. I told him this was because the Western medicine he was taking suppresses thyroid hormone, and his body had adapted to this external suppression, making his own suppression ability weaker. Once this external suppression is removed, his body's own suppression capacity can't keep up, leading to a more severe rebound of hyperthyroidism. Based on his condition, I prescribed some traditional Chinese medicine formulas for him to take along with Western medicine. To cure his condition, I even considered surgical treatment. But he refused. He said his job involved physical labor, and surgery would affect his work. Also, he was getting married soon and didn't want a scar on his body at the wedding. Knowing his situation, I advised him not to have children until his hyperthyroidism was completely cured. Although the genetic probability for men is relatively low, hyperthyroidism can still cause significant trouble for offspring, even leading to serious conditions at birth. He agreed casually, but from his expression, I knew he didn't take it seriously. Later, about two years later, this man came back to my clinic. This time, he wasn't alone; with him were a woman and a child about one year old. When they entered, I didn't immediately recognize him, as too much time had passed, and I see many patients daily, making it hard to remember everyone. But the man remembered me and tearfully explained his story. It turned out that after getting the prescription I gave him and combining it with Western medicine, it had worked very well. However, hyperthyroidism treatment often takes a long time to completely cure. After he got married, his family didn't think about waiting and started constantly urging the couple to have a child. He actually didn't want a child yet, as he was still young and his condition wasn't fully recovered. But his family kept saying he wasn't young anymore, and they were getting old, wanting to see grandchildren. After a long period of urging, the couple eventually decided to have a child before his hyperthyroidism was cured. Although risky, they heard the genetic probability for men was low, so they took a gamble. The child was fine at birth, very active, loved eating and sleeping, but cried a lot. However, the elders said a crying child is good and will be smart when grown up. But not long ago, he noticed a lump on the child's neck, and the child looked unhealthy. So he took the child to a children's hospital for a check-up, and it was found that their child had hyperthyroidism. The couple was very shocked. After learning the child had hyperthyroidism, the family elders blamed them, saying they disregarded the child's health by having a child before the hyperthyroidism was cured. Although angry, the couple had no time to argue and could only take the child everywhere for treatment. Later, the man thought of me, and the couple brought the child to see me. I asked them to bring the child for me to examine. By then, the child already had obvious hyperthyroidism symptoms and needed prompt treatment. But for such a young child, any treatment would cause harm. However, for his health, I had to take a risk. To this end, I contacted some excellent doctors in hyperthyroidism treatment and discussed how to treat this child. After discussions with dozens of Chinese and Western doctors nationwide, we finally devised a treatment plan. Although it would be hard for the child to accept, for his health, we asked his parents to proceed with the treatment. After some time, the child began to improve, and his parents' tense expressions eased. However, even for a child, hyperthyroidism requires a long treatment period to be effective. Although the child eventually recovered, this case shows us that the harm of hyperthyroidism can even affect the next generation. For the healthy life of the next generation, please do not let your illness threaten your children's health. Hyperthyroidism can be cured, and it requires patients to cooperate with doctors for treatment.

Title: 【Online Rumor Debunker】Can a person be infected with COVID-19 at most 8 times? Experts respond. Content: "No matter how healthy or strong a person is, they can only be infected with COVID-19 at most 8 times. The 9th time will be fatal." This claim has recently sparked discussion. Multiple experts told a reporter from People's Daily Health Client that this statement has no scientific basis. Li Yongtao, Deputy Chief Physician of the National Center for Infectious Diseases at the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University School of Medicine, told the reporter that currently, for normal people without underlying diseases, the claim of "can only be infected at most 8 times" is completely unscientific. Furthermore, reinfections generally result in milder symptoms, so there is no need for excessive worry. Zhao Wei, Director of the Biosafety Research Center at the School of Public Health, Southern Medical University, told the reporter that while there is no definitive conclusion on how many times one can be infected, the possibility of repeated COVID-19 infections indeed exists. Current observational studies indicate that symptoms become progressively milder with each reinfection. One reason is that the body develops immunity to the pathogen after the first infection. "Even if our specific immunity against this pathogen gradually declines over time, upon reinfection, the body can quickly boost this immunity through an anamnestic response to eliminate the pathogen. Therefore, symptoms do not become more severe after repeated infections." "On the other hand, pathogens, during the process of spreading and circulating, often mutate towards gradually weaker pathogenicity and stronger infectivity," Zhao Wei said. Zhao Wei suggested that if people are truly concerned about repeated infections, those over 60 years old and individuals with underlying diseases can get vaccinated and receive booster shots. Secondly, when going to crowded places, especially hospitals, try to wear a mask throughout the visit and wash hands promptly upon returning home. - END - Source: People's Daily Health Client

Title: Why are many migrant workers afraid to go to labor arbitration and choose to endure it themselves? Content: A few years ago, when the Advertising Law was introduced, many people printed tens of thousands of complaint letters, used bots to pull business license information, and filed complaints against all online stores. Local industry and commerce offices received the complaint letters and called in the local online store owners for verification. The store owners had to print several pages of materials, and the industry and commerce offices had to print over ten pages of materials just to withdraw the complaint. If the store owners were too busy or too lazy to deal with it, they would pay the complainant 500 yuan to settle the matter, but the industry and commerce offices still had to print over ten pages of materials. Later, the industry and commerce offices prepared a standard format. Upon receiving a complaint, they would send a reply acknowledging receipt and firmly oppose the store owners paying money, because once money is paid, the standard format becomes useless, and materials have to be prepared separately. Thus, the Advertising Law was effectively rendered useless. Similarly, there are those who target expired food for fraud, intentionally hiding food in a corner of the supermarket, waiting for it to expire, then buying it and demanding compensation. When such things happen frequently, the channels for safeguarding rights get blocked. Lawyers on Zhihu might tell you various ways to claim wages or seek compensation, but essentially, they are just eyeing your few thousand yuan in legal fees. This path is already blocked; otherwise, they would have done it themselves. At the very least, lawyers' social security payments are basically not covered by the law firm.

Title: Why are intermediary agencies needed for publishing papers in journals? Content: This is a very good question. It should be a doubt in many people's minds. As a journal blogger, I think it is very necessary to answer this question. Generally speaking, when we mention intermediaries, most of us have the stereotype that they are a bit... you know, with heavy marketing traces and prone to exaggeration. For example, the more common ones in life are those real estate agents. To be honest, I particularly dislike the real estate agents who keep calling me. First of all, is there a possibility that I simply can't afford it? Have you found the right target customer group? You just keep calling me blindly, it's really speechless. Similarly, there are also intermediaries in the journal industry. First of all, I hope you don't look at journal intermediaries with the same disdain as you do for real estate agents. Of course, I don't exclude or deny that there are also those who engage in crazy marketing among journal intermediaries. But please take a careful look at the practical information I've written before, and you will know that I am definitely not that style. It's not an exaggeration to say that I am the most laid-back journal blogger on Zhihu. Let's first quote a principle from philosophy: existence is rational. You have to believe that the appearance of everything is not meaningless, nor is it born for no reason. Since it exists, there must be a reason for its existence. You can question it, which is very reasonable. If you want to publish a paper in a journal and you say you want to submit it yourself, do you know how difficult it is to submit on your own? I want to remind you that you must start preparing one or two years in advance. The cycle is waaaaay too long. Very few authors get accepted on their first try. Submitting on your own is inherently difficult. Unless your paper writing level is particularly high and the quality is very good, it is generally difficult for anyone to get accepted on the first try, let alone the fact that most people's submissions often sink without a trace... Does everyone know why a manuscript you have submitted cannot be used again? This is because you cannot submit the same manuscript to multiple places. Before you receive any response from the journal you submitted to, you cannot submit the same article a second time. This is like an unwritten rule in the journal industry. If you have a long time before you need to use the paper, then you can definitely try submitting on your own. If you are in a hurry, don't even think about it! It's not that I'm being absolute, but after all, I've encountered this situation more than once or twice. When the time to use the paper is approaching, the articles submitted before have simply vanished without a trace. You get anxious, but there's nothing you can do. Therefore, the emergence of intermediary agencies is to help everyone successfully submit their manuscripts as soon as possible, get published early, and then use the paper. That's all. I really dislike some of the ridiculous comments online sometimes, talking about academic fraud. May I ask? The journal is printed and published by the magazine office. The acceptance notice is also issued by the magazine office after reviewing the article and confirming that the quality meets the requirements. There is no falsification in any step. The acceptance notices issued by the magazine office are unique. No non-official entity of the magazine office has the qualification to issue them. If those official seals could be used randomly, it would be a disaster! They would have been sued into bankruptcy by the magazine office long ago! I sometimes find it really hard to understand some people's thought processes. You can't get accepted by submitting on your own, and then you go and slander the rationality of the existence of intermediary agencies? The magazine office's behavior is also within a reasonable range. The magazine office is not a public institution; it is not a non-profit organization. Making a profit is completely normal, okay? The only difference between the two is that one costs no money or very little money, while the other charges different publication fees based on the journal's value, with specific costs depending on the journal. The above is my answer to this question. I suggest that everyone choose between submitting on your own or finding an agency based on your actual situation. If you have any questions, feel free to leave a message anytime. I will be happy to answer when I see them.

Title: Day 51 of lockdown in a Shanghai residential community due to the pandemic. Today, I saw on my social media feed that an APP can be used to check the community's three-zone status, so I couldn't wait to try it. My community has two lane numbers. One lane number is marked as a "Precautionary Zone," while in the other lane number, several buildings are "Lockdown Zones," and the rest are "Control Zones." Because they belong to the same community and share a main gate, even residents in the Precautionary Zone are affected and cannot enjoy the privilege of leaving the community for a walk. Last night, a video circulated in the group chat, showing community committee staff discarding food residents had group-purchased. The person filming gave no explanation of the context, just repeatedly emphasized these were "unofficial group purchases" and that such activities should not be tolerated. This morning, news came out explaining the specific situation. It turns out the community had a long-standing rule against group purchasing non-essential items. For this purchase, the group leader had reported it as vegetables, but it was actually prepared food. The first delivery was refused. The second time, it was disguised as a regular parcel and accepted. When community volunteers were preparing to deliver it, they discovered it was prepared food that had been sitting for quite some time. Fearing it could cause food poisoning, they discussed the matter with the group leader along with a community police officer. Eventually, the group leader agreed to let the community committee staff handle the disposal. It was originally a simple matter, but due to the inappropriate way the person filming expressed themselves on-site, it led to misunderstandings. Title: Cancer is not an incurable disease. How to break the stereotypical perception of cancer? What good mental attitudes should be established to fight cancer? Content: A good mental attitude can improve immunity and reduce cancer recurrence. Director Zhao said: 'Don't think that you can't do anything once you get cancer. To a large extent, cancer also bullies the weak and fears the strong.' Professor Yuan Fenglan from the Cancer Prevention Department of the Cancer Hospital of the Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences also agrees with this view. She said that about 10% of early-stage cancer patients do not survive more than 5 years, mainly due to mindset issues. The better the mindset, the less likely the cancer is to recur. In summary, it is indeed impossible to experimentally see the effect of a good mindset on fighting cancer, but subjectively, a good mindset does have certain positive effects for cancer patients. Therefore, it is recommended that everyone... Additionally, maintaining a good mindset has the following benefits: 1. Enhances intelligence: Research indicates that children with positive and optimistic emotions have significantly higher intelligence levels than children with pessimistic and melancholic emotions. Intelligence levels are not only reflected in IQ but also in daily thinking, memory, creativity, and imagination. Maintaining a positive mindset is also very helpful for achieving good results. 2. Improves physical function: Maintaining positive emotions over the long term can have a significant impact on health status, effectively improving physical function and promoting the body's metabolism. Negative emotions, on the other hand, can reduce a person's physical strength and energy, making them easily feel tired and fatigued during activities, which is not conducive to the normal conduct of activities. 3. Avoids depressive emotions: It also has a great impact on one's outlook on life. Nowadays, many people suffer from depression. A negative mindset can directly lead to an inability to adjust oneself in the face of pressure and negative emotions, causing one to sink deeper. People with good emotions are not like this; they face life with a positive attitude, do not get discouraged after failure, and even in high-pressure environments, they adjust themselves in a timely manner.

Title: When did you realize that online loans should not be touched? Content: When you want to apply for a low-interest loan from a bank, you will understand that online loans are a big pitfall. Institutions like the five major banks have relatively stricter loan review requirements compared to other small and medium-sized commercial banks because they do not lack customers, let alone high-quality customers. Generally, the loan interest rates of the five major banks are relatively low because their cost of obtaining funds from the central bank is low, so the interest on such loans is relatively lower. Major banks need to pay interest to the central bank when they obtain funds from it. If the interest rate for obtaining funds from the central bank is high, then the interest rate passed on to individual borrowers will be even higher, and this interest is borne by the borrower. Once, a foreign bank called Standard Chartered rejected my application during the risk control review simply because I had an outstanding online loan from Du Xiaoman on my credit report. The credit manager told me it was primarily because of this online loan, especially since the repayment method was 'interest first, principal later.' He said if it weren't for this loan, the application would have been approved. Later, I applied for a large credit card installment product from a commercial bank, and the interest rate was quite low. Afterward, I paid off all my online loans, canceled the accounts, and my credit report gradually became clean. As long as you don't touch online loans again and stop robbing Peter to pay Paul, your big data will become relatively cleaner. Then, I successfully obtained a product from Bank of China with an annualized rate of 3.55%. The interest rates for many bank products fluctuate based on individual qualifications. The worse your qualifications, the higher the loan interest rate; conversely, the better your qualifications, the lower the rate. However, for this Bank of China product, I asked the credit manager, and he said the loan interest rate is basically fixed. As long as you can get approved, the rate is the same for everyone. If you participate in their bank's activities, the rate might even drop by one percentage point. So, if you can avoid online loans, don't touch them. If you need money, I suggest going to a bank. Banks now offer many products with relatively low interest rates. Online loans are varied, with unstable and fluctuating interest rates. In the end, if you go to a bank, they might look down on you. However, having a bank loan does not prevent you from applying for another loan.

Title: Which stranded tourists from Suqian in Hainan can return? - Suqian Local Bao Content: Which stranded tourists from Suqian in Hainan can return? Title: Should You Use a Phone Case? Many People Are Doing It Wrong, Insiders Reveal These 3 Major Drawbacks Content: With the rapid development of the mobile phone industry, phone cases have become a huge market. Initially, many people used phone cases simply to protect their phones from being damaged if dropped. However, as the industry has evolved, the design variety of phone cases has become increasingly rich. Nowadays, people use phone cases not only for protection but also for aesthetics. Furthermore, a phone case only costs a few dozen yuan, and many people change their cases every few months. So, should you use a phone case? Many people are doing it wrong, and insiders reveal these 3 major drawbacks. 1. Affects Heat Dissipation: During use, phones generate heat, especially when running large applications like games. However, after putting on a case, the heat from the back of the phone cannot dissipate effectively, which can affect the lifespan of the components on the back and accelerate the phone's aging. Moreover, some phone cases are made from cheap silicone materials that can release harmful substances when heated, which is very bad for your health. 2. Affects Phone Signal: Everyone knows that when we enter enclosed spaces like elevators, the phone signal weakens. Putting a case on the phone essentially encloses it, which can affect the signal. Especially with very thick and heavy cases, the phone signal can become very poor. 3. Affects Feel/Grip: Nowadays, phone screens are getting larger. To fit our phones and allow us to hold them comfortably, manufacturers are researching how to make phones thinner and lighter. However, putting on a case can worsen the phone's feel/grip. For people with smaller hands, holding the phone can become more strenuous. Of course, phone cases do provide good protection for the phone. Therefore, when deciding to use a case, everyone should also consider these 3 issues. Don't just pursue aesthetics blindly; consider practicality more and avoid choosing overly cheap, low-quality phone cases. Do you usually put a case on your phone?

Sentenced to one year and 8 months in the first trial. News on September 5th. Video footage. Unrelated to the event. A post-90s police officer, Li Mou A, from Fujian, exploited his work position to query citizens' personal information and sold it at 80 yuan per piece.
