Title: Why are special-purpose technical vehicles so expensive? How is the level of China's special-purpose vehicles? Content: Recently, Zhongmu County in Henan Province spent 11.6 million yuan to buy 6 sanitation vehicles, which made the news and sparked interest in China's special-purpose vehicle market. Due to relatively small market demand, many large automobile manufacturers generally overlook this market. Many special vehicles, such as fire trucks and engineering rescue vehicles, are imported. Only companies with strong professional backgrounds are involved in this field. For example, the 6 sanitation vehicles purchased this time were developed and produced by Henan Hualu Co., Ltd. This company is a subsidiary of North China Road and Bridge Construction Group and is a high-tech enterprise with qualifications for producing specialized vehicles. It currently has 120 employees, including 7 with senior professional titles and 21 other technical personnel. Although the company is not large in scale, it has considerable technical expertise. So, how do they manage to produce high-tech sanitation vehicles with such a small team? This is thanks to China's robust new energy vehicle industry chain. Six of the world's top ten power battery companies are from China, and suppliers can be found in areas like motors and electronic controls. As long as a company masters the specialized technology for special vehicles, it can produce valuable special-purpose vehicles. Taking the purchased sanitation vehicles as an example, according to the company's负责人, they possess two core technologies: first, the use of pure electric drive to avoid secondary pollution to the atmosphere caused by fuel vehicles; second, excellent filtration effectiveness, with atmospheric particulate matter PM2.5 levels below 75, and dust removal efficiency exceeding current national standards. How is this achieved? It is due to their proprietary patents: the "Dual Pulse Reverse Blowing Dust Removal Device" and the "Water Mist Membrane Filter Cloth and Its Coating Method." During vehicle operation, these technologies efficiently capture PM2.5 fine particles, ensuring that the amount released back into the atmosphere is <75 μg/m³. Thus, these sanitation vehicles are indeed worth their price—technology makes a difference. In the field of special vehicles, China started relatively late, and many still rely on imports. For instance, many fire trucks we commonly see are imported and even more expensive. China spends over 700 million yuan annually on importing fire trucks, with the most expensive one costing 24 million yuan. Why is a single vehicle so expensive? And why purchase them despite the high cost? This is somewhat unavoidable. Many large cities in China have numerous skyscrapers, which are extremely difficult to rescue if they catch fire. This type of ladder fire truck is a 101-meter-level, world's tallest aerial ladder fire truck. The ladder on this fire truck can extend to a height of 101 meters, equivalent to over 30 stories, and it can be deployed in just 9 minutes. It is suitable for firefighting and rescue operations in buildings ranging from 69 to 101 meters in height. To support such heights, the reliability of the chassis and hydraulic system is crucial. In this aspect, Chinese companies still have some distance to go to reach world-leading levels. With the rise of China's automotive industry, the country is also accelerating development in special-purpose technical vehicles, and the future looks promising.

Title: Seeking advice from experts, 2024 college entrance exam, Hebei candidate, male student in Physics, Chemistry, and Geography track, score roughly between 540-580, what majors are better to choose? Title: How to turn off Apple payments Content: There are three ways to turn off Apple payments, which can be selected according to the usage scenario: Option 1: Turn off subscriptions through Apple device settings Open the phone "Settings", click on the top Apple ID (which shows your name). Select "Subscriptions" to view all automatic payment items. Click on the service you need to turn off, select "Cancel Subscription" and confirm. Applicable scenario: Directly managing App Store subscriptions (such as video memberships, iCloud storage, etc.). Option 2: Turn off payment authorization through WeChat Open WeChat "Me" → "Services" → "Wallet", click on "Payment Settings" at the bottom. Select "Apple Service Payments" or "Password-Free Payment", enter the signed list. Find the corresponding item, click "Stop Payment" to unbind. Applicable scenario: Apple payment services opened through WeChat Pay. Option 3: Turn off password-free payment through Alipay Open Alipay "My" → "Settings" in the upper right corner → "Payment Settings". Select "Password-Free Payment/Auto-Debit", find the authorization related to "Apple Services". Click "Turn Off Service" and confirm the cancellation. Note: If the account has arrears or subscriptions have not been cancelled, payment may be automatically deducted during cancellation. It is recommended to cancel the subscription first. In addition, there are some precautions: After canceling the subscription, the service can be used until the end of the current cycle and will not terminate immediately; If "Family Sharing" is enabled, the main account needs to operate to close related subscriptions; After turning it off, it is recommended to check your email to confirm the successful cancellation email sent by Apple.

Title: Company Falsely Issues 200 Million Yuan in VAT Invoices for Profit, Police Block Over 35 Million Yuan in Tax Evasion Content: A trading company in Suining falsely issued over 200 million yuan in value-added tax (VAT) invoices, then used the same method to obtain input VAT invoices, intending to evade taxes through tax credit claims. Just as the company was about to proceed with the credit claims, it was intercepted by economic investigation police from the Economic Development Zone Branch of the Suining Public Security Bureau, promptly blocking over 35 million yuan in evaded taxes. Currently, the company's legal representative, Mr. Li, has been transferred to the local court for prosecution. Trading Company Falsely Issues 200 Million Yuan in VAT Invoices for Profit, Investigation Reveals In early September 2015, the Suining Municipal State Taxation Bureau and the Suining Branch of the People's Bank of China reported to the public security authorities that Suining Yuxiong Trading Co., Ltd. in Chuanshan District was suspected of forging and falsely issuing special VAT invoices, profiting hugely from it, with an exceptionally large amount involved. "Through investigation and meticulous checks, we quickly verified evidence of the trading company's tax evasion," an economic investigation officer from the Suining Public Security Bureau's Economic Development Zone Branch told reporters. On September 10, 2015, they established a task force to investigate the case of falsely issuing VAT invoices. That same day, officers raided Yuxiong Trading, intercepting its legal representative, Mr. Li, in the office. They seized 960 special VAT invoices, 29 company seals, over 50 purchase and sales contracts, and a large number of tools used in the crime, including scanners, invoice printers, and desktop computers. According to the economic investigation police, their investigation into Yuxiong Trading revealed that the company had no actual business operations. It first obtained VAT invoices in the name of a jewelry company and forged input special VAT invoices itself. Subsequently, the company altered the product names and falsely issued output special VAT invoices externally. Over more than a month, the public security authorities and tax departments traveled to Hebei, Tianjin, Beijing, Chongqing, and other locations, conducting in-depth investigations and visits to over twenty enterprises, gathering evidence of the company's crimes. Police verification showed that Yuxiong Trading had issued special VAT invoices totaling 203,353,500 yuan, with input tax amounting to 34,570,100 yuan; the falsely issued special VAT invoices externally amounted to 207,748,700 yuan, with output tax totaling 35,317,300 yuan. Shell Company with No Business Operations, 969 Invoices Forged The economic investigation officer stated that during police interrogation, Mr. Li confessed that after he and his accomplices registered and established Suining Yuxiong Trading Co., Ltd., they did not conduct any actual business. Instead, they extensively obtained falsely issued input special VAT invoices, certified them for tax credit through the tax system, then illegally obtained forged input special VAT invoices with altered goods names, which they handed over to accountants for bookkeeping, creating a false appearance of actual purchases of the goods listed on the forged invoices, thus covering up the company's illegal activities of falsely issuing output special VAT invoices externally. During interrogation, Mr. Li also admitted that based on the content of the forged input special VAT invoices, the company correspondingly issued a large number of falsely issued output special VAT invoices externally, charging downstream enterprises a 7.3% handling fee, illegally profiting from it. Appraisal by the Suining Municipal State Taxation Bureau and the Printing and Minting Science and Technology Research Institute of the People's Bank of China confirmed that all 969 input special VAT invoices used by the company for accounting were forged. Blocked 35.31 Million Yuan in Evaded Taxes, Case with the Largest Economic Loss Recovery in the Province "We blocked these VAT funds before they could flow out," the police officer told reporters. When they seized these falsely issued VAT invoices, Mr. Li and others had not yet had time to verify and claim credits for them. It was reported that this successfully solved major case of falsely issuing special VAT invoices involving gold transactions took over a month during the investigation phase, recovering economic losses of 35,317,300 yuan. "This case is also the one with the largest economic loss recovery among cases of falsely issuing special VAT invoices involving gold transactions in the province." Currently, the investigation of the case has concluded, and it has been transferred to the Chuanshan District People's Procuratorate for prosecution. Mr. Li and others await severe punishment by law. Wang Yi Long, Huaxi Metropolis Daily Client Reporter Zhou Hongpan (Images provided by the police)

Title: Over 1,000 Telecom Fraud Cases Occurred in Hebei in the First Three Months, Gang Members Mostly Relatives and Friends Content: The Hebei Provincial Public Security Department held a press conference today to report on the province's efforts to combat and prevent telecom fraud crimes: According to statistics, in 2014, Hebei province had a total of 5,970 telecom fraud cases, involving an amount of 330 million yuan. The public security organs arrested 1,715 criminal suspects, dismantled 134 criminal gangs, and shut down 123 telecom fraud platforms. From January to March this year, Hebei has already reported 1,037 telecom fraud crime cases, with defrauded amounts exceeding 50 million yuan. "Such cases are numerous, widespread, and involve long chains; the vast majority of cases are cross-provincial or even cross-border and transnational operations, and the不法分子 have evolved from solely mainland personnel to collaborations between domestic and overseas actors," said Wang Xingliang, head of the Criminal Investigation Bureau of the Hebei Provincial Public Security Department, adding that investigating and obtaining evidence for telecom fraud crimes is very difficult, and the cost of solving cases is high. Prominent Regional Characteristics In October 2014, the Julu County Public Security Bureau in Xingtai City dismantled a telecom fraud gang, arresting three criminal suspects. Since January 2014, this gang, posing as staff of the armed forces department under the pretext of purchasing military tents, defrauded over 30 people in Hebei, Henan, Gansu, and other places, committing over 30 offenses involving more than 500,000 yuan. In December 2014, the Xingtai City Public Security Bureau dismantled a gang that impersonated QQ acquaintances to commit fraud, arresting eight gang members in the Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region; this case involved a sum as high as 1.16 million yuan. It is understood that the main perpetrators of telecom fraud crimes fall into two categories: one is overseas personnel, and the other is mainland-based regional professional fraud groups. The occurrence of such cases often centers around the location of the fraud gang, with multiple cases happening across regions or even cross-border in a radial pattern within a similar timeframe. "The operational scope of telecom fraud crimes is gradually expanding, and the harm is escalating," Wang Xingliang introduced, noting that the regional characteristics of telecom fraud crimes are very prominent. In some cases, suspects often gather in groups based on village, community, or family ties, with clear division of labor and individual responsibilities. Moreover, the core members of most fraud gangs are relatively fixed; they form a core force bound by blood, clan, or friendship ties, often colluding to engage in fraud using specific methods. Constantly Evolving Methods On April 18 this year, Zhao, a resident of Shijiazhuang City, received a call from a number displayed as 95559. The caller claimed to be from the Bank of Communications credit card center and offered to help increase his credit limit. After verifying Zhao's name, work unit address, ID number, and credit card number, Zhao received a verification code. After inputting the code, Zhao's credit card was used for a transaction of 20,000 yuan on Alipay. According to Hebei police, the level of sophistication in telecom fraud crimes is increasing. The equipment used by fraud gangs has evolved from using mass SMS senders for fraud, to bundling phones with any number, and now to using "arbitrary number display software" and internet telephony for fraud. Especially in recent years, fraud gangs have adopted methods like multiple mobile phone call transfers, using VOIP technology to set arbitrary virtual numbers, setting up virtual computers to simulate voice prompts, and other fraudulent techniques, making them more deceptive and enhancing their anti-investigation capabilities. Furthermore,不法分子 constantly change their tactics by exploiting common psychological weaknesses, with new tricks and forms emerging endlessly. On April 24, 2015, Liu received a call from an unknown man asking if Liu's brother was disabled, stating that if so, he could enjoy national disability subsidies, and instructing Liu to operate at an ATM. Liu went to an ATM and followed the prompts, only to discover that 40,456 yuan in cash had been transferred from his card. "These kinds of 'pie in the sky' good deals always blind the victims. Once some victims receive such information, they can't resist the temptation to try and ultimately fall into the陷阱 carefully set by the骗子," Wang Xingliang said. It is reported that within telecom fraud crimes, those that utilize the victim's personal information are the most deceptive. The perpetrators first obtain the victim's personal identity details and related information through various channels. Then, during the fraud process, several individuals play different roles, providing the victim's real identity and other relevant information, and imitating voice prompt calls from entities like government, financial, or tax departments to deceive the victim and make them深信不疑. Losses Difficult to Recover On June 24, 2014, the Cangzhou City Public Security Bureau cracked the case of "Zhong Sheng An Tai" company涉嫌 network investment fraud, arresting 75 individuals involved, raiding 5 criminal dens, and freezing funds exceeding 86 million yuan. The company registered a trading website on the internet, attached it to a legitimate third-party payment platform, lured victims to invest under the guise of bulk commodity spot trading, had traders manipulate the backend程序 to control trading activities, profit from client losses, and defraud victims of their money. "The professional characteristics of telecom fraud crimes are more evident, showing organization," Wang Xingliang introduced. Telecom fraud gangs operate with company-like management, clear division of labor, commit crimes分散ly, and their methods and anti-investigation tricks are more professional, with their scale continuously expanding. Unlike traditional fraud crimes which have fixed times, locations, and face-to-face contact between perpetrator and victim, telecom fraud crimes have a larger spatial scope. The perpetrator, the fraud target, the person transferring money, and the person withdrawing money are often in different places, posing great difficulties for investigation. "Telecom fraud is like an invisible net always open; one不小心 can fall into it," Wang Xingliang stated. Curbing the high incidence of telecom fraud crimes,打击 is just one method. To prevent such cases from the source, it requires the general public to improve their awareness of fraud prevention and their ability to recognize fraud; this is the fundamental way to curb telecom fraud crimes. Intern reporter Zhou Xiaopeng

Title: How to Deal with Low-Price and Chaotic Pricing in E-commerce (Solutions) Content: Hello everyone, this is Xinyang. Recently, many brand owners have been consulting me about e-commerce shopping, which, with its simplicity, speed, and price advantages, has gradually become the preferred shopping method for modern consumers. However, for brand owners, the phenomenon of low-price and chaotic pricing sales on e-commerce platforms has become a thorny issue. Low-price sales not only damage the brand image but may also affect normal market order. So, how can brand owners effectively control the low-price sales of their products on e-commerce platforms? I. Three Possible Reasons for Low-Price Sales: Loose Channel Control: On e-commerce platforms, some merchants may obtain products through unofficial channels and sell them at low prices. These merchants often do not comply with the brand's pricing strategy, attracting consumers with low prices to gain market share. Loose channel control is one of the important reasons for low-price sales. Malicious Competition and Price Wars: Some merchants deliberately lower prices to attract customers in order to quickly capture the market. This malicious competition not only disrupts the market price system but also harms the interests of other merchants who follow the rules. Once a price war starts, it often leads to the collapse of the entire market price system, causing serious damage to the brand image and market order. Promotional Activities and Discounts: E-commerce platforms frequently hold various promotional events, such as "Double Eleven" and "618," during which merchants offer large discounts and promotions. While these activities help boost sales, they can also lead to chaotic product pricing, especially when prices fail to return to normal levels promptly after the events end. II. Difficulties in Price Control on E-commerce Platforms: High Difficulty in Platform Supervision: There are numerous merchants and a wide variety of products on e-commerce platforms, making it extremely difficult for platforms to monitor the prices of each product and merchant in real time. Additionally, some merchants may use hidden methods for low-price sales, further increasing the difficulty of platform supervision. Legal and Regulatory Limitations: Although China has relevant laws and regulations to standardize market prices, in practice, there are still some ambiguities in defining and penalizing low-price sales behavior. This provides opportunities for some merchants to exploit legal loopholes and engage in low-price sales. Fierce Market Competition: In a highly competitive market environment, merchants often adopt low-price strategies to seize market share. While this strategy may boost sales in the short term, the long-term harm to brand image and market order cannot be ignored. III. Price Control Methods for Brand Owners: Establish Strict Channel Management Systems: Brand owners should establish a comprehensive channel management system, clearly defining the rights, responsibilities, and benefits of each channel level to ensure effective control of every step from source to end-user. Simultaneously, strengthen training and supervision of channel partners to prevent them from engaging in low-price sales. Develop Reasonable Pricing Strategies: Brand owners should formulate reasonable pricing strategies based on market conditions and product positioning, ensuring strict compliance by all channel partners. Merchants who violate the pricing strategy should be penalized accordingly to maintain the stability of the market price system. Use Technological Means for Price Monitoring: Brand owners can leverage big data and artificial intelligence technologies to monitor product prices on e-commerce platforms in real time. Once low-price sales are detected, immediate measures should be taken to intervene and ensure market price stability. In summary, brand owners need to take measures to protect their rights online based on their actual situation, thereby effectively safeguarding their interests and brand image.

Title: A Man Detained for Illegally Withdrawing Money with Someone Else's Bank Card He Found - Xiangyin County Government Website
Content: A man was criminally detained for illegally withdrawing money after finding someone else's bank card.
Source: Xiangyin County Government 2018-03-13 11:49
Page views: 1 | | | |
Recently, Ms. Xu, who lives in Wenxing Town, left her card near an ATM after withdrawing money. Someone else obtained her password and withdrew all the money from the account. On January 28, Ms. Xu went to the ATM at the Xiangyin Branch of China Postal Savings Bank on Beizheng Street in the urban area to conduct business. After withdrawing money with her first card, Ms. Xu directly placed the card on the ATM machine, then used her second card to withdraw money. After finishing, she left directly, completely forgetting that one card was still on the ATM machine. Surveillance footage shows that in the early hours of January 30, a suspicious man, covering his head with clothing to deliberately avoid bank surveillance, went directly to the ATM. He withdrew all the more than 19,000 yuan from the card in eight separate transactions before leaving the scene; the entire process took nearly ten minutes. After extensive investigation and visits, police from the Chengguan Police Station successfully identified the suspect, Mr. Zhang, through relevant technical means and arrested him on February 27. What puzzled the police was how Zhang, who was a complete stranger to Ms. Xu, knew her bank card password. Zhang said he simply guessed it. It turned out that Ms. Xu had set her password too simply for easy memorization, which led to the theft of funds from her card. After interrogation, the suspect Zhang confessed to the criminal facts: on the evening of January 28, 2018, he found the victim Ms. Xu's social security card in the urban area, obtained the password, and withdrew the more than 19,000 yuan from the card in eight transactions. Currently, Zhang has been criminally detained according to law, and the case is under further investigation.

Title: Which small country language is better to learn? Content: If the original poster plans to work in areas like Guangxi and Yunnan, they can choose Southeast Asian languages, such as Thai, Vietnamese, Burmese, or Korean, which are currently quite popular. Especially the job prospects for Vietnamese language talents are showing an increasingly positive trend.

Broadly speaking, I think French is good; it's used in many places in China as well.

The easiest to learn is Korean, with simple pronunciation, but I don't really advocate learning Korean. After all, they are actively learning Chinese now, so we don't have much need to learn their language.

As for Arabic, it depends on where the original poster wants to develop in the future. If they are willing to go abroad, undoubtedly Arabic is the best choice. Because it's basically useless domestically, but there's a high demand abroad. Since Arabic-speaking regions are generally underdeveloped and plagued by frequent conflicts (except for wealthier Gulf countries like the UAE and Saudi Arabia), not many people are willing to go. Another important point is that Arabic is very difficult to learn. There's a basic sound that is a trill, and the grammar is complex and hard to understand. Compared to other languages, Arabic even lacks reasonable textbook setups; the textbooks we use were compiled in the 70s and 80s. It's almost impossible to buy a genuine Arabic-Chinese dictionary. I suggest the original poster not learn it.

Actually, as mentioned above, the main thing is to see if you like it. Only if you're interested can you learn it well. As for the job prospects we analyze, it's really "plans can't keep up with changes." After all, learning a language isn't an overnight thing, and no one can fully predict market changes several years later.

Since prospects can't be predicted, my advice to the original poster is: learn what you like, so you have the motivation to study. Even if what you learn might not be useful in the future (like in my case), at least you've put in the effort and can be proud of having learned that subject.

Another very important point I forgot to mention: learning a language must be done at a正规学校正规 school; don't think you can learn it just from books and tapes—that's impossible. ### Omg~~ Arabic is the most difficult language in the world. I suggest you still don't learn it because even if you learn it, you might not learn it well; even if you learn it well, you might not master it; if you don't master it, finding a job will be hard. After all, your major serves your work. There are very few jobs in China that require Arabic. Personally, I think Spanish is very good; German is also okay. Interest is very important in learning a language; see which language you like yourself. Only after liking it can you fully devote yourself to master it. Any major, as long as you master it to a level ordinary people can't reach, you win. ### Arabic, even the US is cultivating talents in this language now, but you need to be prepared—it's very difficult! ### Small countries in terms of geography~~ easy to say~

Spanish is not bad, but its pronunciation is a bit difficult. ### If you want to get into gaming, choose Korean, but they say French is the most beautiful language in the world.

Title: After laying off agents, now laying off back-office staff?! Insurance companies are all conducting layoffs in the name of optimization... Content: From large insurance companies to small and medium-sized ones, layoff actions are being carried out under the name of optimization. 1 The wave of layoffs in the US insurance industry continues to surge. According to statistics, since 2024, 362 companies in North America have conducted layoffs, involving a total of 107,000 people, including large enterprises in the finance and technology industries. Although this number includes multiple industries, the insurance industry, as part of the financial sector, has clearly been significantly affected. According to the latest data, the layoff situation in the US insurance industry in 2024 remains severe. In March this year, the number of layoffs announced by US employers reached 90,309, including 28,715 layoffs in the financial industry, ranking third among all industries, although this represents a 6% decrease compared to the same period last year. This wave of layoffs in the US insurance industry has been surging since last year. In the first 10 months of last year, more than 13 insurance companies in the US had announced layoffs, with the publicly disclosed number of layoffs nearing 8,000, including health insurance giants like Centene, UnitedHealth, CVS Health, as well as GEICO, the auto insurance company owned by Berkshire Hathaway. For example, Centene laid off about 2,000 employees, Farmers Insurance announced an 11% layoff, approximately 2,400 employees, and CVS Health also issued layoff notices to its subsidiary Aetna. These layoff actions reflect that the insurance industry is undergoing cost structure adjustments and business restructuring under macroeconomic challenges, particularly the pressure of inflation and interest rate hikes. Many US insurance companies have cited reasons such as "inflation," "macroeconomic conditions," and "reducing costs and expenses" in their explanations. These trends indicate that the US insurance industry in 2024 is using layoffs to cope with macroeconomic challenges and changes in the market environment. Furthermore, according to data from Trading Economics, the number of layoffs and discharges in the US in June 2024 was 1,498 thousand, showing a decrease compared to previous data. This might suggest that the layoff situation is easing as economic conditions gradually improve. 2 A wave of back-office layoffs sweeps through China's insurance industry. As part of the global financial industry, China's insurance sector, affected by the broader environment and its own transformation, is also deeply embroiled in a vortex of back-office layoffs—from large insurers to small and medium-sized ones, all are conducting layoff actions in the name of optimization. Overall, the wave of back-office layoffs in China's insurance industry stems from the following six factors: First, pressure to reduce costs and increase efficiency: insurers are taking measures to optimize their back-office personnel structure to control costs and improve profits. As the number of field agents decreases, insurers need to correspondingly reduce back-office staffing to adapt to the new business scale and structure. Second, the irrationality of the agency system: for a long time, the mass-tactics of insurance companies required back-office staff to provide multi-dimensional support to field agents; with the significant reduction in field personnel, insurance companies have closed many branch companies and marketing service departments, especially large insurance companies, which directly leads to the reduction of back-office staff. Third, the impact of regulatory policies: for example, the implementation of the "Filing and Operation Integration" policy affects the premium income of life insurance companies, which in turn may affect the demand for back-office personnel. Fourth, capital market fluctuations and the low-interest-rate environment: this increases the pressure on insurers' asset allocation, leading to pressure on investment returns, thereby affecting the profitability of insurance companies and their personnel needs. Fifth, the implementation of the Solvency Regulatory Rules (Rule II): imposes higher requirements on the capital measurement of insurance companies, prompting them to focus more on risk management and capital efficiency, which may trigger adjustments to the personnel structure. Sixth, business structure transformation: as the overall business structure of the insurance industry optimizes, especially the transformation of the business structure of life insurance companies, the demand for back-office personnel will also change.

Title: Treatment Methods for Pica Content: Pica is a very complex syndrome of multiple diseases caused by metabolic dysfunction, abnormal taste, etc. In the past, it was believed that pica was mainly caused by a deficiency of trace elements such as zinc and iron. Currently, more and more doctors believe that pica is mainly caused by psychological factors. There is no particularly effective treatment method, but you can try supplementing the following substances: (1) Minerals: such as sodium, copper, cobalt, manganese, calcium, sulfur, zinc, etc. (2) Vitamin B complex. Additionally, appropriate psychological counseling is needed.

Title: Wuyi Overseas Compatriots Unite in Fighting the "Epidemic" - 68 Overseas Organizations and 35 Individuals Receive Commendation Content: Yesterday morning (October 15), at the 2020 Jiangmen "Online World Youth Conference" event, our city announced the list of outstanding overseas organizations and individuals in Jiangmen's fight against the COVID-19 pandemic, commending 68 overseas organizations including the Federation of Venezuelan Chinese Associations and 35 individuals such as Ma Guanshi. This year, the sudden COVID-19 pandemic touched the hearts of overseas compatriots and compatriots from Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan. They immediately took action, rushing to aid their hometown through various means such as donations and material collection, especially during the early stages of pandemic prevention. Batch after batch of urgently needed supplies like masks, medical protective clothing, medical gloves, and goggles were continuously sent back to the hometown and the front lines of the epidemic fight, solving the urgent needs of our city's hospitals, enterprises, and citizens, allowing us to feel the profound bond between overseas compatriots and those from Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan. As of now, our city has received donations from overseas compatriots and compatriots from Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan totaling approximately 13.395 million RMB in cash and materials worth approximately 13.928 million RMB, summing up to 27.323 million RMB. The event expressed high respect and sincere gratitude to all compatriots at home and abroad who cared about and supported the fight against the epidemic in the motherland and hometown. It hoped that the commended overseas organizations and individuals would continue to promote the fine tradition of loving the country and hometown, unite Wuyi compatriots overseas to continue fighting the pandemic, and further strengthen exchanges and cooperation with our city in various fields. It also hoped that all sectors of society would follow the example of overseas Chinese models and make new and greater contributions to combating and overcoming the COVID-19 pandemic. (By Tang Da, Huang Zhiyao) Voice: Zheng Anting, President of the Macau Jiangmen Youth Association: Promoting Business and Trade Exchanges through the World Youth Conference World Jiangmen Youth Gather "Online". Zheng Anting, President of the Macau Jiangmen Youth Association who has attended the World Youth Conference multiple times, believes that the "Online World Youth Conference" continues the "warmth" and "breadth" of the conference, maintaining communication among Jiangmen youth worldwide amid the pandemic and bringing them closer. Utilizing new technologies like the internet also aligns better with young people's communication habits, allowing them to participate anytime, anywhere. The potential for Jiangmen-Macau cooperation is limitless. Zheng Anting stated that in economic, trade, and cultural exchanges between Jiangmen and Macau, Macau can further leverage its role as a cooperation platform connecting Portuguese-speaking countries, facilitating overseas youth's entry into markets like Jiangmen in the Greater Bay Area and helping Jiangmen products "go global". Meanwhile, the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macau Greater Bay Area has given Jiangmen new positioning and missions, aiming to build an important platform for cultural exchange and cooperation among overseas Chinese. Through the World Youth Conference, Jiangmen can extend its influence to more cities within the Greater Bay Area and beyond, rallying young talents worldwide to promote business exchanges and jointly advance the development of the Greater Bay Area. Li Guozhong, President of the Venezuelan Jiangmen Wuyi Youth Federation: Making Exchanges Among Compatriots More Convenient Li Guozhong, President of the Venezuelan Jiangmen Wuyi Youth Federation, resides abroad year-round and returns to Jiangmen roughly every six months. Regarding Jiangmen, Li Guozhong has endless emotions: "Jiangmen is my hometown, where my roots are." This year's pandemic has left many countries worldwide still struggling, but China's significant achievements in fighting the epidemic particularly moved Li Guozhong: "Under the leadership of the Communist Party of China, the strong and effective prevention measures implemented early in the pandemic quickly restored people's lives and the economy to normalcy, showing the world a different China." His heart is filled with pride and honor. "This year's 'Online World Youth Conference' is a great innovation, making exchanges among compatriots more convenient," Li Guozhong said. For the future, he hopes the conference can organize more offline or online business exhibitions to better facilitate trade and cooperation among compatriots and promote the World Youth Conference brand in various aspects. Zhao Zheng, Honorary President of the Los Angeles Jiangmen Wuyi Youth Association: Timely, Forward-Thinking, and Innovative in Form "Affected by the COVID-19 pandemic this year, overseas compatriots worldwide found it difficult to gather and communicate. The successful hosting of this 'Online World Youth Conference' built a bridge for emotional exchange and business trade, characterized by its timeliness, forward-thinking意识, and innovative form," commented Zhao Zheng, Honorary President of the Los Angeles Jiangmen Wuyi Youth Association, who has attended the conference multiple times. Zhao Zheng recalled that in the past, communication between overseas compatriots, their homeland, and other compatriots mainly relied on overseas Chinese associations. After the establishment of the World Youth Conference platform, compatriots worldwide gained a bridge for hometown ties, cultural exchange, and business cooperation. He hopes the "Online World Youth Conference" will continue to improve and play a greater role in promoting business exchanges and socio-economic development. (By Tang Da, Huang Zhiyao)

Title: Water Parks Have Six Major Risk Points, Experts Remind: Drowning Has Nothing to Do with Water Depth Content: (People's Daily Health Client Reporter Zhang Bingyu) On August 10th, the topic "6-year-old girl drowns in play pool with water depth below knee level" trended online. The accident occurred at 6:00 PM on July 18th at a hotel in Jinghong City, Xishuangbanna Dai Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province. While playing in the water children's park, the girl Yueyue had her leg sucked into the pool's return water pipe and could not pull it out. Despite rescue efforts, she unfortunately drowned. The diameter of the return pipe was 27 cm, the water depth in the pool was below Yueyue's knees, and Yueyue was sturdier than her peers and had decent swimming ability. Why did this tragedy still occur? Can similar water children's parks be played in safely? On August 12th, a People's Daily Health Client reporter interviewed Li Zhenhua, Senior Trainer of the Education and Training Branch of the Beijing Emergency Volunteer Service Corps, and Qi Xinglong from the News and Publicity Department of the Tongzhou District Fire and Rescue Bureau in Beijing. The two experts stated that the accident might be related to the following risk points. The children's water playground where the 6-year-old girl drowned. China News Weekly image Risk point 1: Lack of protection at the pipe opening. Judging from the report's pictures, the pool's return pipe lacked a proper protective grate (mesh) above it, leading to the child accidentally stepping into it. Risk point 2: The powerful suction of the water pump. There is a water pump operating below the pipe opening, creating a very strong water flow. Once stepped into, it can create a vacuum effect, sucking and trapping the body. Risk point 3: Lack of signage indicating the return pipe location. When the safety protection of the return pipe is inadequate, the lack of corresponding warning signs doubles the probability of an accident. Risk point 4: Overlooking the dangers of shallow water. Safety is not related to water depth. Once a person falls in the water, out of fear and nervousness, they will try to support themselves on the bottom with their arms. However, if the water depth exceeds the arm's length, the head and face cannot surface, easily leading to loss of balance, continuous tumbling in the water, and resulting in drowning. This risk is greater for children, whose arms are shorter. Risk point 5: Lack of lifeguards. According to "GB 19079.1-2013 Conditions for Opening Sports Venues and Technical Requirements Part 1: Swimming Places," a swimming pool with a water surface area of 250 square meters or less should have at least 3 lifeguards; for pools larger than 250 square meters, one additional lifeguard should be added for every additional 250 square meters or part thereof. However, according to the report, there were no corresponding staff on duty at the scene at the time of the incident. Risk point 6: Lack of an emergency stop device for instant water cut-off. The report indicated that the staff were not proficient in operating the pump valve controls, and there was no emergency plan for draining the pool, suggesting significant deficiencies in hotel supervision and an inadequate emergency response mechanism. In response, Li Zhenhua called for parents to improve their awareness, understand the potential risks of shallow water areas, and teach children to identify drain outlets; he called for the industry to reduce the diameter of return pipes, especially in children's pools, where pipes should be smaller in diameter and greater in number; he also called for operators to standardize the placement of return pipe warning signs and arrange for lifeguards to reduce tragedies. In addition, Qi Xinglong emphasized that while the operator's responsibility in such accidents is undeniable, parents, as the primary guardians of their children's safety, should also fulfill their supervisory duties and not be negligent just because the water is shallow. He suggested that if a child experiences a similar drowning incident, a long rubber tube can be extended to the child's mouth for them to bite on, ensuring normal breathing and buying time for rescue.

Content Title: What is the so-called "universal mandatory social security" all about? Six Questions and Answers on the New Social Security Regulations Release Date: 2025-08-20 21:04:43 Content Status: Review Completed Content Type: Multimedia Industry: Digital Public Service_Ministerial_Ministerial Group 1 Author Name: People's Media Convergence Owner Name: People's Media Convergence Content Account Type: Enterprise Content Details: Six Questions and Answers on the New Social Security Regulations! What is the so-called "universal mandatory social security" all about? Six Questions and Answers on the New Social Security Regulations! Core Points: · Interpretation (II) did not create a new legal system. What is the functional purpose of the social insurance system? Social insurance is a social security system established by the state in the form of insurance, where eligible participants pay insurance premiums in advance into a fund. When participants face old age, illness, work-related injuries, unemployment, childbirth, etc., relevant expenses are paid from the fund. While providing economic security for participants, the social insurance system also functions to ease labor-management conflicts, redistribute income, maintain social stability, and promote social fairness. Phenomenon of "Insurance Discontinuation"? Why does the phenomenon of "Missing Insurance" and "Insurance Discontinuation" exist in society? Reason 1: The life and occupational risks that social insurance protects against have a low probability of occurrence in the short term (e.g., aging risks often occur many years later). Both employees and employers may exhibit opportunistic and short-sighted behavior, choosing not to participate in insurance to obtain higher take-home pay. Method: Employers hold the initiative for enrollment and premium payment. To secure employment opportunities, workers are often reluctant to raise social security demands with the employer. How does Interpretation (II) define the legal validity of "Voluntary Social Security Waiver Agreements"? "Agreement" is absolutely invalid: The employer... Rather, it strengthens the rigidity of the existing system? Why does the new regulation not create new obligations but strengthen the rigidity of the existing system? What is the so-called "universal mandatory social security" all about? What is the so-called "universal mandatory social security" all about? Buffer mechanisms for enterprises facing diversified operational difficulties? If an enterprise is indeed facing severe operational difficulties and cannot pay social insurance contributions fully and on time: It can apply to the relevant departments for a deferral, and make up the payments after its operational situation improves. It can negotiate with employees to temporarily reduce the social security contribution base or rate. During specific periods, the state may introduce relevant policies to phase out or reduce the social security contribution obligations of enterprises (e.g., during the pandemic, reductions for enterprise pension, unemployment, and work-related injury insurance). Some localities may introduce local policies. Content Understanding Tags: Government and Livelihood - Five Social Insurances and One Housing Fund - Policy Release - Social Security

Title: Chengde Medical University Clinical College Conducts Summer Research on Visiting Enterprises and Expanding Internship Bases at Teaching Hospitals Content: Source: [Future Net] From August 8th to 12th, a delegation of five people from the Clinical College of Chengde Medical University, including Party Secretary Wang Ruiting and Dean Zhao Lianzhi, visited Cangzhou People's Hospital, Cangzhou Hospital of Integrated Traditional Chinese and Western Medicine, Baoding First Central Hospital, Baoding Second Central Hospital, Baoding First Hospital, Baoding Second Hospital, Bethune International Peace Hospital, 252 Hospital, Baoding Maternal and Child Health Care Hospital, and Beijing Children's Hospital Baoding Branch. They conducted discussions and inspections regarding undergraduate theoretical teaching,见习实习 (probation/internships), revision of talent training plans, graduate surveys, postgraduate (Master's) student training, student employment, and student living and learning environments. Strengthening university-hospital cooperation to improve the quality of undergraduate and postgraduate training. The leaders of each hospital attached great importance to undergraduate clinical teaching and postgraduate training, introducing the hospital's history, current development status, undergraduate teaching, and postgraduate training work. Wang Ruiting introduced the university's recent developments in undergraduate program construction and discipline construction, emphasizing the promotion of medical-education collaboration, strengthening the integration of basic sciences and clinical practice, cultivating students' clinical thinking and problem-solving abilities, and offered suggestions on alleviating the conflict between students preparing for postgraduate entrance exams and completing their internships. Discussions were held with supervising teachers to understand students' learning situations, and both sides exchanged views on how to further improve the quality of undergraduate and postgraduate training. Visiting enterprises to expand internships and broaden employment resources. This visit investigated the work performance of the university's graduates. Each hospital fully affirmed the solid theoretical foundation and diligent, down-to-earth work style of the university's graduates, stating that they have become key personnel in clinical work and management positions at the hospitals. By understanding the hospitals' talent needs in terms of educational background, specialty, and ability, and combining these with the needs of society and employers, the direction for talent training and employment guidance was clarified, creating a favorable employment atmosphere and providing strong support for better graduate employment. Through the visits, the hospitals indicated they would give priority consideration to employing graduates from Chengde Medical University. In-depth discussions with students to answer questions and resolve doubts. The Clinical College held student forums to understand the effectiveness of theoretical teaching,见习 (probation), and internships. Addressing the conflict between internship and postgraduate exam preparation raised by students, and considering the requirements of postgraduate exam content and medical-education collaboration on medical students' clinical thinking and practical problem-solving abilities, it was emphasized that internships and postgraduate preparation are complementary, not contradictory. In-depth guidance and Q&A were provided on aspects like applying for postgraduate programs. Visiting student living and learning areas to assess hardware support. The Clinical College focused on inspecting student dormitories, classrooms, and clinical skills training centers at four hospitals responsible for the theoretical teaching of senior undergraduate students. Overall, each hospital provided students with safe, clean, and comfortable accommodation. Teaching classrooms and self-study rooms were well-equipped, and opening hours were extended as much as possible for students preparing for postgraduate exams. The clinical skills training centers had complete facilities, with models and equipment suitable for student internships and见习 (probation). Student management had its own characteristics at each site, ensuring the students' living and learning needs were met. Expanding hospital resources in preparation for building teaching bases for new programs. As the university's program construction continues to achieve new breakthroughs, there is a need to further expand hospital resources and plan ahead for subsequent programs. In addition to visiting the university's existing non-affiliated affiliated hospitals and teaching hospitals, visits were also made to 252 Hospital, Baoding Maternal and Child Health Care Hospital, and Beijing Children's Hospital Baoding Branch to understand their basic situation and strengths. Investigations were conducted regarding the construction of internship bases for new programs such as Stomatology, Pediatrics, and Medical Laboratory Technology, assessing the base's teaching faculty, department setup, and teaching conditions. It is reported that this summer research provided an in-depth understanding of employer talent needs, further deepened university-hospital cooperation, broadened employment channels for undergraduates and postgraduates, and will help further enhance the quality of student training and employment. (Correspondent: Chengde Medical University Yu Miao) This article is from [Future Net] and represents only the author's views. Title: University Gates, Should They Be Opened? Content: Recently, the news that Zhengzhou University has canceled public entry restrictions has attracted attention. Through the visitor appointment system, applying for campus entry in one's personal name only requires a few simple steps to complete the registration application. In fact, since July this year, many universities in Hubei such as Wuhan University, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, and China University of Geosciences (Wuhan) have also successively opened their gates, restoring the campus visit appointment channel for the first time in nearly four years. More and more university gates are 'opening.' While everyone sighs with emotion that 'the campus gates have finally returned to normal,' some netizens have also reported that 'the entry of outsiders has made places like teaching buildings noisy' and 'affected the study and life of students on campus.' University opening must be orderly. The differing attitudes of netizens towards the opening of campus gates precisely indicate that opening will inevitably bring some problems, but these problems are not 'problems brought by opening' but 'problems brought by poor management.' This tests the daily management ability of the school to achieve 'orderly opening.' The prerequisite for university opening is that the university has made full preparations and contingency plans, able to guarantee the normal teaching order of the school and the stable study and life of students, especially safety guarantees. In fact, real-name appointment itself is a process of screening management. Through this review and traceability, universities can easily achieve effective management. The friendliness between the university and the public is crucial. Campus opening is not only a matter for the university but also something the public must strive for. Show friendliness towards the university campus: respect the university as a quiet teaching unit, maintain its research order, and not interfere with commercialized and entertainment consumption of the university campus. This is a holy place for students to seek knowledge, not a tourist attraction, not a check-in spot to satisfy 'visiting a prestigious school and posting a video as proof,' not a prestigious 'background' to show off on social media, not a 'hot topic label' for social media. A university is a high ground of academia and thought in society. Approach quietly, pass by quietly, gaze quietly, attend lectures quietly, with awe for knowledge, manage your steps well. Under this public friendliness, university campuses will also show greater openness. More open universities are the general trend and should become common practice. Whether a university is suitable for opening and the pros and cons after opening are not only the university's own business but also related to the city where it is located. Issues such as public security, civilized literacy, resource sharing and crowding all require coordination and resolution by the city management departments where the university is located, as well as the support and cooperation of citizens. But in any case, more open universities are the general trend and should become common practice. Some universities that have not yet truly opened their gates should not remain in the comfort zone of closed management. This is essentially a mindset of 'if you don't do it, you won't make mistakes.' For better universities and better education, we look forward to more universities returning to 'my door is always open.' Do you think university gates should be open to the public? Title: Analysis of the Efficacy of Hydrogen in Treating COVID-19 Infection and Its Sequelae Content: During the process of COVID-19 infection, so-called 'asymptomatic' is nominally asymptomatic, not truly asymptomatic. The experience for most people far exceeds that of a severe flu they have had before, lasts longer, and recovery is slower. Professor Sun Xuejun (a leader in China's gas medicine field, particularly hydrogen medicine) pointed out in his article 'What Can Hydrogen Do in COVID-19 Infection?' that the combined use of hydrogen has a certain effect in alleviating various discomforts caused by viral infection. To deal with such a fierce viral attack, a multi-pronged approach should be adopted: inhaling hydrogen, drinking hydrogen water, and hydrogen baths. The effects might be more pronounced. In the article, Professor Sun Xuejun listed the effects of hydrogen therapy: for example, for muscle soreness, hydrogen can relieve pain. For poor sleep, inhaling hydrogen improves sleep. For gastrointestinal symptoms, hydrogen water can protect the gastrointestinal mucosa. Some studies have found that the virus might damage the retina, and hydrogen can also protect the retina. In short, for those problems that have no specific treatment but cause us great discomfort, hydrogen can provide possible help. Research Progress In December 2022, the renowned medical journal 'Medical Research Archives' published a study by an expert team from the University of the West of England (the university's history can be traced back to 1595, over 400 years ago) on the efficacy of hydrogen for COVID-19 and its sequelae. Research on common COVID-19 sequelae indicates that some people recovering from COVID-19 experience a long and protracted recovery period, including dyspnea (27%), fatigue (58%), difficulty concentrating (27%), and persistent cough (43%). Common Symptoms and Treatment Methods for COVID-19 and Post-COVID Conditions Analysis of Hydrogen's Efficacy on COVID-19 Symptoms One of the primary clinical functions of hydrogen is as an antioxidant. In COVID-19 patients with moderate to severe symptoms, reduced blood oxygen saturation (SpO2) levels can lead to hypoxemia and tissue hypoxia, driving the disease towards Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) and causing Multiple Organ Dysfunction Syndrome (MODS), which is life-threatening. Current medical interventions mainly include high-flow oxygen therapy, invasive mechanical ventilation, and medications (including anti-inflammatory drugs, antivirals, and immunomodulators) to increase oxygen levels. However, the efficacy of these methods remains to be seen. In previous studies, hydrogen has been proven to have effects such as reducing levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines, decreasing M1 activation, reducing neutrophil infiltration (neutrophil infiltration is usually a sign of inflammation in the body), and mitigating DNA damage caused by oxidative stress. Therefore, hydrogen is an ideal effective treatment for intracellular dysfunction. In clinical studies, hydrogen-oxygen inhalation therapy (66% hydrogen, 34% oxygen, for 7-8 hours per day), delivered via nasal cannula at a rate of 6L/min, has been shown to alleviate chest pain and severe dyspnea, improving outcomes for hospitalized COVID-19 patients. The study found that neutrophilia was suppressed in patients, while C-reactive protein (CRP) levels decreased, indicating that hydrogen-oxygen therapy prevents hypoxia-induced tissue damage by suppressing abnormal immune responses. Analysis of Hydrogen's Efficacy on Post-COVID Sequelae Statistics show that 63% of COVID-19 patients experience various sequelae. The most common symptoms are chronic fatigue (58%), dyspnea (36%), cognitive impairment (28%), and muscle pain (26.5%), among others. These symptoms have already affected patients' normal work and life. Research has found that elevated levels of ROS/RNS (ROS refers to Reactive Oxygen Species, RNS refers to Reactive Nitrogen Species) and long-term low-grade inflammation are the main causes of the aforementioned symptoms. Hydrogen is a very effective anti-inflammatory and antioxidant substance, which is significant for patient recovery. Studies show that hydrogen is as effective as commonly used nutritional supplements, such as Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide (NADH) and Coenzyme Q (CoQ), in treating Chronic Fatigue Syndrome. Moreover, hydrogen not only repairs damage caused by oxidative stress and excess reactive gases to the body but also reduces the gene expression and serum levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines (such as interleukins, tumor necrosis factor-alpha) and chemokines (such as interferon-gamma), which are capabilities that many nutritional supplements lack. Research Conclusion Professor Sun Xuejun pointed out: Facing the virus, hydrogen still holds value, which I have always maintained. As a non-toxic tool suitable for most people, with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, in the current context of the entire population being exposed to the virus, hydrogen should very likely play an irreplaceable role in helping people reduce suffering, alleviate symptoms, promote recovery, and reduce sequelae. Title: Conditions for Receiving Unemployment Insurance in Zhaoqing City Content: Conditions for Receiving Unemployment Insurance in Zhaoqing City Introduction How can one receive unemployment insurance in Zhaoqing City, and what conditions are required to receive unemployment insurance? Zhaoqing Local Treasure provides you with relevant information about Zhaoqing unemployment insurance, hoping to be helpful. 1. Have participated in unemployment insurance in accordance with regulations, and both the employer and the individual have fulfilled the payment obligation for at least 1 year. 2. Interruption of employment is not due to personal意愿, meaning the unemployed person is unwilling to中断 employment but is forced to中断 due to reasons beyond their control. The "Measures for Applying for and Issuing Unemployment Insurance Benefits" issued by the Ministry of Labor and Social Security specifies which situations are considered involuntary employment interruption, mainly including: termination of labor contracts, employees being解除 labor contracts by employers, employees being fired, expelled, or laid off by employers, and employees resigning due to employer violations of law or the labor contract. If unemployment results from the above situations, the employee has the right to apply for unemployment insurance benefits. 3. Have completed unemployment registration and have job-seeking requirements. Unemployment registration is conducted to grasp the basic situation of the unemployed and confirm their eligibility. Having job-seeking requirements is considered because an important function of unemployment insurance is to promote the reemployment of the unemployed. This is a prerequisite for享受 unemployment insurance benefits and also an obligation that the unemployed should fulfill. Other materials specified by provincial labor security administrative departments. Apply for benefits at the unemployment insurance business agency within 60 days from the date of labor contract termination (generally at the street or township employment service agency at the place of household registration). If the 60-day period is exceeded, the application will not be processed, so it must be done promptly. Unemployed persons who meet the following conditions simultaneously can enjoy unemployment insurance benefits: have participated in unemployment insurance in accordance with regulations, and both the employer and the individual have fulfilled the payment obligation for at least 1 year; employment interruption is not due to personal意愿; have completed unemployment registration and have job-seeking requirements.

Title: What is it like to have a monthly salary of 2000 yuan? Content: I live in Shanghai. It is now the end of November 2024, and my current salary is 2690 yuan, which is the minimum wage standard in Shanghai. I work in an outsourced position at a large state-owned bank. My job is to call bank customers and persuade them to add the relationship manager's corporate WeChat. This position requires successfully adding 650 WeChat contacts per month. After exceeding 650, I get a 2.5 yuan commission for each additional contact. I met this target in July and August, earning a few hundred yuan in commission, with total salaries around 3200 and 3500 yuan respectively. For the last two months, I haven't met the target, so my salary has returned to 2690 yuan. I usually have very little personal spending: no social life, no buying clothes, no spending on games, no participating in group meals, no pursuit of any holiday celebrations, and no participation in e-commerce shopping festivals like Double Eleven or Double Twelve. I also don't have a girlfriend. My salary is basically all spent on food and transportation. I eat at home, which doesn't cost me anything personally. I have lunch at the bank cafeteria; the food is good quality and cheap, costing about 10-20 yuan per day. On weekends, I occasionally eat out, about 1-2 times a week, spending around 100 yuan per meal. Now, I basically live paycheck to paycheck each month and find it very hard to save money. For entertainment, I borrow free books from the library, watch TV, or watch movies. I don't have any video streaming memberships; I just watch movies on TV.

Title: A Peaceful "Salary" New Year! Dongsheng District People's Court Recovers Overdue Wages for 11 Workers. Content: As the New Year approaches, Dongsheng District People's Court has opened a green channel for cases involving people's livelihoods, addressing the urgent needs and concerns of the public. Title: Summary of Reasons for Losing Points in Qingdao Junior High School Third-Year Sports Simulation Exam Content: A few days ago, various schools in Qingdao went to schools like Qingdao No.1 Middle School to conduct a simulated physical education high school entrance exam test. [1R] The test equipment, [2R] test procedures, and [3R] test standards were all consistent with the actual high school entrance exam, with a full score of 30 points. Last Saturday before class, I received a call from the parent of one of my students, who introduced a classmate to come for my lessons. Before class, I briefly communicated with the child: the child had taken the test in the morning, the test results were very poor, the mother was very anxious, immediately got my contact information and came for a lesson in the afternoon. As soon as we met, the child was very upset, and started crying as soon as I asked. After understanding the situation, the main issue was that the results from usual practice tests at school were much better than the simulation test results. On Sunday, I led a team to No.1 Middle School and observed for a while outside the test venue, indeed discovering many reasons for losing points. I have compiled them here. Pay attention to these details, and the score should be able to improve further. What are the reasons for losing points? 1. Unfamiliarity with equipment: The event where performance was most affected compared to usual practice was volleyball. The required height for the volleyball test is 2 meters 20 cm. Many children don't pay attention to the height requirement during practice. When they get to the test venue and stand inside the instrument, they find that no matter how they bump the ball, the instrument doesn't beep and the count doesn't increase, so they start to panic and blindly add force, wanting to increase the height of the ball. After adding force, the height is sufficient, but the ball becomes uncontrollable. The crying child mentioned earlier was like this; originally capable of bumping 50-60 times, but in the test venue, the effective score was only five. For the volleyball event, as long as you master the standard bumping posture and judge the ball's landing point well, it's easy to get a full score. If your child's score is not yet full, their movements are not standard, they don't know how to exert force, and the ball's height is insufficient, and there is still one month until the exam, you must find someone knowledgeable to guide them. 2. Unfamiliarity with rules: Basketball: Wherever the ball goes out of bounds, continue from there. Never pick up the ball and give up. The core of basketball is running, the person chasing the ball. Those who score less than 8 points generally don't understand what 'person chasing the ball' means. Simply put, don't treat the basketball test as a basketball test; treat it as a sprint, and the results will be completely different. Due to space limitations, we will look at the 1000m/800m run, standing long jump, 50m dash, sit-and-reach, and sit-ups tomorrow (the last two are major areas for fouls. Leading a team of 600 participants in the test, 241 chose these two events, and 53 people fouled). If you found this article helpful, please follow, like, and bookmark. If you need help improving your child's high school entrance physical education score, please feel free to private message me.

Title: When the maximum battery capacity of an iPhone falls below 80%, will the battery drain slower after replacement? Content: After replacing the battery, the battery life will increase but not be the same as when the phone was new. Battery life = total battery capacity ÷ real-time power consumption. Power consumption varies with usage time and scenarios, there is no fixed power consumption, and battery drain cannot be precisely evaluated, so the final battery life cannot be directly determined. It's generally an estimate, so don't set your expectations too high. Usually, it's sufficient to sustain most people's light to moderate usage for a day.

Title: Dr. Liu Yi Talks About Lung Diseases (5306) - Is there any conflict between taking blood pressure and blood sugar medication and anti-inflammatory drugs for lung nodules? Content: Some lung nodules are considered to have inflammatory factors after discovery. After a period of anti-inflammatory treatment, a follow-up examination can be done to observe changes in the lung nodules. Each doctor has different experience with anti-inflammatory treatment for lung nodules, and the morphology of each lung nodule is also different. Some patients may be arranged for intravenous anti-inflammatory infusion, while others may be prescribed oral anti-inflammatory medication to take at home. A daughter of a patient who discovered lung nodules contacted me through an online consultation platform, planning to take oral anti-inflammatory medication for a period and then re-examine the changes in the lung nodules. She asked me if there is any conflict between the anti-inflammatory drugs and the blood pressure and blood sugar medications her mother is currently taking. Taking the currently most popular Moxifloxacin as an example, there can be some conflicts with certain hypoglycemic drugs and heart medications, so it is better to take them at intervals. I have listed Moxifloxacin and some conflicting medications below for your reference. If you are taking medications that should not be taken simultaneously, it is best not to take them and consider switching to other oral anti-inflammatory drugs. For medications that require cautious combined use, they should be taken orally only if the physical condition allows, with a minimum interval of two hours.
