Title: Netizens reported that Jiang Mou Lian's request for donations was suspected of fraud. The official announcement stated that 'fraud is inconsistent with the facts, and no tax-related issues were found.' What details are worth paying attention to? Content: In response to netizens' reports that Jiang Mou Lian's request for donations was suspected of fraud and involved village cadre Wang Mou Jie and other related issues, the Jimo District previously established a joint investigation team to conduct an in-depth investigation in accordance with laws and regulations. The investigation findings are now announced as follows: I. Regarding whether Jiang Mou Lian's request for donations is suspected of fraud: According to the investigation, on November 3, 2016, Jiang Mou Lian's daughter Jiang Mou was murdered in Japan. Jiang Mou Lian made multiple trips to Japan to participate in the lawsuit. On March 3, 2017, Jiang Mou Lian, claiming to need funds for the lawsuit in Japan, publicly posted her bank card number, Alipay, and WeChat accounts on the Weibo platform to seek help and also launched a fundraising campaign on "Qingsong Chou" (which closed on March 13, 2017, after reaching the set goal of 300,000 yuan). On November 15, 2017, while participating in the lawsuit in Japan, Jiang Mou Lian issued a statement on the Weibo platform stating that she would no longer accept donations. On December 20, 2017, the Jiang Mou murder case was adjudicated in the Tokyo District Court of Japan. The investigation found that from March 3 to November 15, 2017, Jiang Mou Lian received a total of 34,815 "donation" transactions amounting to 3.5478 million RMB through the aforementioned four channels. From November 16, 2017, to the present, her bank card, Alipay, and WeChat accounts received a total of 5,363 "donation" transactions amounting to 570,500 RMB. Since March 2017, Jiang Mou Lian has spent over 1.22 million RMB on trips to Japan for the lawsuit and handling her daughter's aftermath, 1.5364 million RMB on legal service fees, and donated 897,300 RMB to society. Based on the verification, Jiang Mou Lian made multiple trips to Japan to participate in the lawsuit after her daughter's murder. From March 3 to November 15, 2017, she sought donations online for the purpose of covering lawsuit expenses in Japan and did not fabricate information or conceal the truth. The funds received after her November 15, 2017, statement declaring she would no longer accept donations are considered gifts. In summary, the claim that Jiang Mou Lian's request for donations involved fraud is inconsistent with the facts. II. Regarding Jiang Mou Lian's associated enterprises and tax-related issues: The investigation found that Jiang Mou Lian has two market entities, one of which was deregistered on December 16, 2024. Since their tax registration, both entities have filed quarterly declarations, and no tax-related issues were identified. III. Regarding Jiang Mou Lian's use of a POS machine for cash advances: In October 2014, Jiang Mou Lian operated a supermarket in a residential community. In May 2016, she transferred the supermarket to another person but did not complete the industrial and commercial transfer procedures. In June of the same year, the actual operator applied for a POS machine in the supermarket's name for business operations. Jiang Mou Lian did not use this POS machine for cash advances. IV. Regarding Jiang Mou Lian's acquisition of resettlement housing in Wangjiaguanzhuang Village: The investigation found that in 1997, Wangjiaguanzhuang Village, due to owing construction fees to contractor Wang Mou Jin, used a piece of construction land in the village as compensation. Wang Mou Jin subsequently sold portions of the land to others. In 2000, Jiang Mou Lian purchased one of these plots and built a single-story house for personal use in 2006. In 2010, when Wangjiaguanzhuang Village underwent old village renovation, Jiang Mou Lian received two resettlement apartments according to policy—one for personal use and the other compensated with over 470,000 RMB. During the investigation, it was discovered that during the land transfer process, the then Party branch secretary of Wangjiaguanzhuang Village, Wang Mou Zhi, village committee member Wang Mou Jie, and village committee staff Wang Mou Hui, among others, failed to perform their duties adequately. They will be dealt with according to regulations and laws. V. Regarding Jiang Mou Lian's alleged occupation of the homestead and above-ground attachments of "Five Guarantees" household Huang Mou Xian, and the concealment of having another son: The investigation found that Huang Mou Xian was a resident of Dalongzui Village, Aoshanwei Street, Jimo District, and was not a Five Guarantees household. Around 1997, Huang Mou Xian, being single and childless, recognized his neighbor Wang Mou Qin as his godson and verbally agreed that Wang Mou Qin would provide for him in old age and handle his funeral arrangements, after which the house would belong to Wang Mou Qin. As Huang Mou Xian lived away for a long time, he entrusted the house to Wang Mou Qin for management. In October 2007, Huang Mou Xian passed away due to illness, and Wang Mou Qin arranged his burial. In 2018, Wang Mou Qin renovated and rebuilt the house and has lived there since. The claim that the homestead and above-ground attachments of "Five Guarantees" household Huang Mou Xian were occupied is untrue. The investigation also found that in 2007, the then village committee director of Wangjiaguanzhuang Village, Huanxiu Street, Wang Mou Jie, and his wife Zhang Mou Yun violated the family planning policy at the time. Zhang Mou Yun used Jiang Mou Lian's ID card for hospitalization to give birth to a son, who was registered under Jiang Mou Lian's name but has always lived with Wang Mou Jie and Zhang Mou Yun. The netizens' claim that Jiang Mou Lian had another son is inconsistent with the facts. During the investigation, it was discovered that Wang Mou Jie had disciplinary violations. He has been suspended from his duties, and a disciplinary review has been initiated. Personnel from the former family planning department of the street and the District People's Hospital were found to have inadequately performed their duties and will be dealt with according to regulations and laws. Zhang Mou Yun's use of Jiang Mou Lian's ID card for childbirth will be investigated and handled according to the law. VI. Regarding the claim that Wang Mou Jie is a professional lender: The investigation found that an image circulating online containing the phrase "Wang Mou Jie is a professional lender" was part of the plaintiff Gao Mou's appeal statement in a civil judgment document from the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court and does not represent a fact confirmed by the court. Due to a dispute over unjust enrichment between Gao Mou and Wang Mou Jie, Gao Mou previously filed a lawsuit in the Jimo District People's Court. In October 2020, the Jimo District People's Court dismissed Gao Mou's claim. Gao Mou then appealed to the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court, which rejected the appeal and upheld the original judgment. https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/3wf4VQB3Ex3rIcYnyFGamQ?version=4.1.30.99529&platform=mac&nwr_flag=1#wechat_redirect

Title: For Mutton, Choose This Black Pearl Restaurant by the Sea Content: Yang Ruitang, this Black Pearl restaurant from Xi'an, has opened two restaurants at Xiamen's Peace Wharf. One is the Xi'an Snack Market focusing on night market barbecue and Xi'an snacks, and the other is the Dajia Roasted Lamb Village specializing in roasted lamb. This time, we came to try this particular branch - Yang Ruitang Xi'an Snack Market, which features iron pot stewed young lamb and Xi'an snacks. Located on the first floor of Peace Wharf, it has an impressive entrance, fashionable interior decor, and outdoor seating with views of Gulangyu Island, making it perfect for young people to check in. Iron Pot Stewed Young Lamb is one of their signature dishes. With 30 years of professional experience cooking lamb, they focus on perfecting this one pot. The lamb soup is rich and flavorful, the meat tender and delicate. A bowl warms you up comfortably. Roasted Lamb Spine (Yang Xiezi) is different from the usual hot pot style where you mostly chew on bone. Theirs is roasted. The spine is roasted until incredibly fragrant, crispy on the outside and tender inside, yielding mostly meat with every bite, leaving a lasting aroma. Xi'an Oil-Splashed Old Tofu is quite an interesting dish. The old tofu is soft, tender, and full of bean flavor, infused with chili, surprisingly delicious. Roasted Lamb Skewers, ranked No.1 in Xi'an, feature well-proportioned fatty and lean meat, seasoned with chili powder and cumin, cooked to perfection. Old Xi Handmade Liangpi is authentic Xi'an-style cold skin noodles. Mixed with vegetables and sesame sauce, the liangpi has a chewy, bouncy texture and the sesame sauce is rich and flavorful - you can taste it right here in Xiamen. Roasted Lamb Leg is a meat lover's favorite. As soon as it's served, it grabs everyone's attention. The owner deftly carves it, allowing you to eat big chunks of meat. The skin is roasted until crispy and aromatic, offering immense satisfaction. Get Rich Ice Jelly (Bao Fu Bing Fen) is perfect after a hearty meat meal. A sweet milk tea ice jelly helps cut the grease and cools you down. It looks small but contains a surprise inside - barley, ice jelly, raisins, etc. This May Day holiday, quickly bring your family and friends to Yang Ruitang to enjoy authentic Xi'an snacks!

Title: Three Children Lost in Longyao, Traffic Police Help Them Return Home Safely Content: ↑Click the blue font above, follow to stay on track Click the image above to enjoy low-cost express delivery↑↑↑ I do practical things for the masses On August 13, 2024, a local resident presented a banner inscribed with 'Thank you, good traffic police of the people, helping others is a new trend' to the Traffic Police Brigade of the Longyao County Public Security Bureau, expressing gratitude to the traffic police who helped find their lost child. Recently, while police officers from the Urban Area Squadron of the Traffic Police Brigade were on duty on Yaoshan Street, three children approached the on-duty traffic police for help, saying they couldn't find their way home. The on-duty traffic police comforted the three children, telling them not to worry, and patiently communicated with them. Upon inquiry, it was learned that the oldest of the three children was 9 years old and the youngest was 6. They had secretly ridden an electric bike from home to the county town in the morning and got lost on their way back. Fortunately, one child remembered their grandfather's mobile phone number. The on-duty traffic police immediately called the number and got in touch with the grandfather. The grandfather and other parents were anxiously searching for them, and their worried hearts were put at ease upon learning the children were with the traffic police. Subsequently, the children's parents arrived in the county town. The police officers criticized and educated the parents, and explained traffic regulations to both the parents and the child who rode the electric bike, such as the requirement to be at least 16 years old to ride an electric bike on the road. Longyao Traffic Police hereby warmly reminds all parents: fulfill supervisory responsibilities, children must be at least 12 years old to ride a bicycle on the road, and at least 16 years old to ride an electric bicycle on the road. Integrate traffic safety into family education to jointly protect children's safe and happy growth.

Title: The County Youth League Committee and the County People's Hospital Jointly Held the "'On the Epidemic Frontline, I Am Here' and 'Youth Gives Their All'" Outstanding Volunteer Commendation Conference
Content: (Source: Reunion Qinyuan Communist Youth League Qinyuan County Committee) To commend the advanced, set an example, further inspire and encourage the county's youth to base themselves in the new era, shoulder new missions, demonstrate new achievements, and vigorously promote the volunteer service spirit of "dedication, friendship, mutual assistance, and progress," on the afternoon of February 14th, the County Youth League Committee and the County People's Hospital jointly held the "'On the Epidemic Frontline, I Am Here' and 'Youth Gives Their All'" Outstanding Volunteer Commendation Conference. Huang Xiangdong, Party Secretary of the County Medical Group and Director of the People's Hospital, Yao Jie, Deputy Secretary of the County Youth League Committee, Zhang Wei, Secretary of the Youth League General Branch of the County People's Hospital, Zhang Yifan, Part-time Deputy Secretary of the County Youth League Committee, Chen Yulu, Head of the County University Student Union, and young volunteers attended the meeting. The meeting was presided over by Zhang Wei, Secretary of the Youth League General Branch of the County People's Hospital.
Interim Youth League Branch Secretary Zhang Haipeng reported on the epidemic prevention and control volunteer service situation. Zhang Yifan, Part-time Deputy Secretary of the County Youth League Committee, read out the "Decision of the Communist Youth League Qinyuan County Committee and Qinyuan County People's Hospital on Commending 21 Epidemic Prevention and Control Volunteers including Zhang Haipeng."
Awards were presented to outstanding volunteers.
Outstanding volunteer representatives shared their experiences.
Yao Jie, Deputy Secretary of the County Youth League Committee, on behalf of the County Youth League Committee, expressed sincere thanks and high respect to the volunteers who participated in the epidemic prevention and control volunteer service, extended warm congratulations to the commended outstanding volunteers, and offered advice to the young volunteers: First, understand the local situation and be good image ambassadors for their hometown. Closely integrate personal development with the development of their hometown. Qinyuan is the home of Qinyuan people, and all Qinyuan people should love Qinyuan. This is not just a slogan but something that students away from home should always remember. Second, be reasonable and be pioneers in internships and practice. During holidays, return to their hometown and actively participate in volunteer services such as cultural creation, changing customs, poverty alleviation, etc., and utilize their expertise. Third, plan for the future and be leaders in building their hometown. Many young volunteers are medical students; they should diligently study professional knowledge, seize opportunities, and inject fresh vitality into the development of the county's health sector.
Huang Xiangdong, Party Secretary of the Medical Group and Director of the People's Hospital, on behalf of the County Medical Group and the County People's Hospital, expressed high respect to the young volunteers who gave up rest, braved risks, overcame difficulties, selflessly dedicated, and assisted the County People's Hospital in epidemic prevention and control. He also raised three hopes for the volunteers: First, he hopes that the students will take the lead in actively cooperating with epidemic prevention and control work and play a exemplary role as youth in their future lives. Second, he hopes that everyone will return to school with the feelings from this practice, integrate the practical experience of this volunteer service into their studies, be down-to-earth, serious in their work, brave in taking responsibility, and become useful talents for social construction and pillars for national rejuvenation. Third, he hopes that everyone will continue to promote the volunteer service spirit of "dedication, friendship, mutual assistance, and progress," treat volunteer service as a life value and pursuit, care about the development of their hometown, and through continuous efforts, return after completing their studies to give back to their hometown, contribute to the construction of their hometown, and realize their life value.

Title: Why does the left thumb hurt when playing guitar? What is the reason? Content: When pressing chords, if you don't keep the left thumb flat and let it stick up for a long time, it can easily injure the bone, causing pain. \nInitially, the left thumb should press against the middle of the fingerboard, providing a support point for the left hand to press the strings. It helps coordinate the four fingers and stabilize the guitar. This also allows more of the left fingers to appear above the fingerboard. The left wrist should be bent as much as possible, forming a 90-degree angle with the arm, serving the same purpose of facilitating string pressing. The right hand should lightly support the guitar at the back half of the fingerboard because this allows the other fingers of the left hand to move more steadily while playing. The most fundamental requirement is to keep the left hand relaxed. ### Playing guitar is inherently tough on the hands. If your hands are too tender, you might not be able to learn. You probably didn't pay attention! Try to use your thumb less during practice, and only use it when playing for your teacher or during a performance! It won't hurt as much then! ### Don't be afraid of the pain. Try playing a classical etude of grade seven or above ten times in a row. You won't feel any pain because your hand will be broken. Learning an instrument requires persistence; the pain will go away in a few days. ### Just let the left thumb rest lightly unless you're using a full barre or partial barre chord. Otherwise, take a break from practicing for a while; don't practice continuously. ### You must not be keeping your left thumb flat when pressing chords; you're definitely holding it up for too long, which can easily injure the bone.

Title: What should I do if my 4-year-old child is nearsighted? Content: As a mother of a child, I fully understand the anxiety of the questioner. Nearsightedness of several hundred degrees in a 4-year-old does indeed look frightening. However, after reading other answers, many respondents believe that computer optometry can only be used as a reference, possibly because the child was too nervous, so the questioner doesn't need to be overly anxious. The most important thing is to quickly take the child to a regular eye hospital or optometry center for more scientific and rigorous eye development examinations. Even if the child is truly nearsighted, there's no need to panic excessively, as many children are nearsighted nowadays, and products like orthokeratology lenses and defocusing lenses can help control the further progression of myopia. For example, my child was diagnosed with 100 and 125 degrees of myopia at age 7. I was very worried at first, but after being fitted with Zeiss MyoCare, and using it for almost a year, the prescription has remained stable, which has put my mind at ease a lot. Zeiss MyoCare uses the Concentric Annular Ring Emmetropization (C.A.R.E.) technology. It utilizes annular ring lenses distributed concentrically to provide dynamic light signals to the eyes, introducing high-order aberrations within the retinal field of view, continuously stimulating the retina, thereby slowing the growth rate of the axial length and achieving the goal of delaying myopia progression. Experimental results show that the MyoCare H and S versions have relative effectiveness rates of 68% and 71%, respectively, in slowing axial elongation compared to emmetropic eyes. That is to say, experiments have proven that Zeiss MyoCare can effectively slow the progression of myopia in children. ￼ Additionally, a reminder: if you purchase Zeiss lenses, remember to activate the electronic warranty card when you pick up the glasses. This not only allows you to verify the authenticity of the lenses but also includes a one-year coating warranty service. Furthermore, for adolescents, Zeiss MyoCare offers a care service: if a MyoCare wearer's prescription increases by 50 degrees or more within six months, they are eligible for a free lens replacement. Specific service details can be viewed on the Zeiss Vision Selection mini-program. Besides Zeiss MyoCare, we also looked into some other myopia control lenses at the time, such as Stellest and MiyoSmart, which also have experimental proof of slowing myopia progression. However, their trials were conducted earlier, and whether they are suitable for today's children who use electronic devices frequently still needs verification. It's important to note that the recommended age range for these glasses is 6 to 18 years old, so whether a 4-year-old can use them must be determined after consulting a professional optometrist. Finally, I hope the questioner's child's eyes will be fine.

Title: Work Report of the Beijing Higher People’s Court for 2020 Content: Delivered on January 25, 2021 at the Fourth Session of the Fifteenth Beijing Municipal People’s Congress by Kou Fang, President of the Beijing Higher People’s Court Dear Deputies: On behalf of the Beijing Higher People’s Court, I now report on the work of the court for your deliberation, and I also invite comments from members of the Beijing Municipal Committee of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference. Main Work in 2020 Since the Third Session of the Fifteenth Beijing Municipal People’s Congress, under the strong leadership of the Beijing Municipal Party Committee, the effective supervision of the Municipal People’s Congress and its Standing Committee, and the correct guidance of the Supreme People’s Court, courts across the city have adhered to the guidance of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, thoroughly studied and implemented Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law, administered justice for the people, upheld judicial fairness, served the overall situation, and strived to ensure that the people feel fairness and justice in every judicial case. Courts across the city newly accepted 839,175 cases and concluded 836,514 cases. I. Putting the people’s life safety and health first and providing strong judicial support for epidemic prevention and control In the face of the sudden outbreak of the epidemic, courts across the city responded immediately and proactively, ensuring that adjudication and enforcement work did not come to a halt and achieving dual safety for litigants and court personnel alike. Under severe tests, court work made new breakthroughs and new progress. The Beijing Higher People’s Court promptly formulated 28 documents, including measures on providing judicial services and guarantees for resolutely winning the battle against epidemic prevention and control, clarified judicial countermeasures related to epidemic prevention and control in a timely manner, and submitted more than 90 articles of legal countermeasure suggestions concerning epidemic-related disputes to Party committees and governments, thereby promoting source prevention and proper handling of such disputes. The courts lawfully, strictly, and swiftly concluded 90 criminal cases involving resistance to epidemic prevention and control, violent attacks on medical personnel, price gouging, and the like. In the Sun Wenbin case of murdering a doctor, the defendant was lawfully sentenced to death, firmly safeguarding the personal safety of medical workers and public health security. Adhering to consultation as the primary approach and mediation as the priority, the courts guided parties to overcome difficulties through settlement and properly handled 1,623 civil and commercial disputes arising from the epidemic in accordance with the law. Six cases were designated by the Supreme People’s Court as typical cases for serving and safeguarding epidemic prevention and control. The courts innovated contactless litigation services, built the Beijing Cloud Court, formulated and improved new rules for online litigation, and achieved breakthrough progress in online trials. Throughout the year, 359,000 hearings were conducted online, accounting for 40 percent of all online hearings nationwide and ranking first in the country. II. Centering on the overall national and municipal priorities and creating a fair and efficient rule-of-law environment for strengthening the functions of the Four Centers and improving the level of the Four Services Deepening the special campaign against organized crime and local criminal gangs. The courts resolutely assumed the political responsibility of consolidating the Party’s governing foundation and safeguarding the fundamental interests of the people, and completed the tasks of the special campaign against organized crime on schedule. Over three years, 165 first-instance cases involving organized crime and criminal gangs were concluded, and 745 criminals were sentenced. The lawful adjudication of major cases involving Chen Haitao, Lin Guobin, Gao Fuxin, He Bo, and others delivered heavy blows to criminal gangs and created a strong deterrent effect. The courts adhered to coordinated action against organized crime and corruption, and lawfully concluded 69 cases involving 92 persons related to corruption and protective umbrellas connected to organized crime. Efforts to strike at assets and cut off financial lifelines were continuously intensified, with RMB 2.7 billion in property ordered to be recovered, confiscated, or returned as compensation, completely destroying the economic foundations of criminal organizations. Strict standards were applied to evidence, procedure, and application of law, and 18 alleged cases of gang-related crimes were not recognized as such according to law, ensuring that no person was wrongly convicted and no criminal escaped punishment, and that every case could withstand the test of law and history. Adhering to both symptomatic and root-cause treatment, the courts implemented the principle of one case, one recommendation in response to social governance issues, thereby effectively helping to eradicate the breeding ground of criminal gangs. Resolutely safeguarding the security and stability of the capital. Fully recognizing the special importance of the capital’s security and stability, the courts lawfully and severely punished crimes endangering national security and serious violent crimes such as homicide and robbery, and severely punished crimes such as illegal fundraising, online fraud, and offenses endangering food and drug safety. A total of 18,703 criminal cases were concluded during the year. Crimes infringing on minors were lawfully and severely punished, and work on social observation and protection and psychological counseling was further advanced to safeguard the healthy growth of minors. Actively serving innovation-driven development. Giving full play to the leading and safeguarding role of intellectual property adjudication in encouraging innovation and promoting high-quality development, the courts concluded 68,327 intellectual property cases. Judicial protection was strengthened by formulating adjudication guidelines for damages in intellectual property infringement cases and improving the judicial determination mechanism for infringement damages, thereby lawfully raising compensation standards. In the series of electronic map copyright infringement cases involving NavInfo and companies such as Baidu and Qihoo, damages awarded reached RMB 75 million. The courts also gave full play to their role in creating rules, explored new standards for the protection of new types of intellectual property rights in the digital economy, and through the adjudication of new-type cases such as artificial intelligence copyright and Douyin short video cases, created a sound rule-of-law environment for the development of new technologies and new business forms. Innovation in the judicial protection mechanism for intellectual property was deepened. The Beijing Internet Court built a world-leading internet litigation platform, and the coordinated governance platform linking Copyright Chain and Tianping Chain was described by the industry as a transformative innovation that empowers industry through justice and technology. Continuously optimizing the law-based business environment. Implementing the Beijing Regulations on Optimizing the Business Environment, the courts solicited opinions and suggestions from enterprises and industry associations 107 times, introduced 32 reform measures regarding online case filing, postponed hearings, online judicial auctions, and other matters, and concluded 443,751 civil and commercial cases. Focusing on safeguarding financial security and promoting risk prevention and control, the courts launched the nation’s first integrated diversified dispute resolution platform for financial cases, realizing the full online handling of blockchain evidence preservation, pre-litigation mediation, and judicial confirmation, thereby effectively promoting efficient, convenient, and low-cost resolution of financial disputes. In service of supply-side structural reform, the courts vigorously improved the convenience of bankruptcy handling, improved the government-court coordination mechanism, and jointly introduced 25 institutional measures with relevant municipal government departments to solve issues such as bankruptcy expenses. As a result, the average handling time under the fast-track procedure of the Beijing Bankruptcy Court was reduced to 99 days. In service of high-level opening up, a one-stop diversified dispute resolution center integrating litigation, mediation, and arbitration for foreign-related commercial disputes was established at the Fourth Intermediate People’s Court, actively building a high ground for international commercial dispute resolution. Making efforts to safeguard the coordinated development of the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region. The courts lawfully and properly resolved disputes relating to key tasks such as decongestion, rectification, and upgrading, construction of the sub-center, and the application for World Heritage status of the central axis, concluding 1,115 related cases. Twenty typical cases serving and safeguarding decongestion, rectification, and upgrading, as well as the Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games, were selected to provide standards and guidance for dispute resolution. The courts also lawfully served and safeguarded special governance in the planning and natural resources field and the rectification of illegal villas, promptly submitted legal suggestions to Party committees and governments, conducted one-case-one-assessment reviews for 1,318 disputes, made every effort to resolve contradictions, and lawfully adjudicated and enforced cases to ensure the smooth advancement of rectification work. The courts supervised and supported administrative organs in exercising administration according to law and concluded 19,520 administrative cases. Effectively strengthening judicial protection of people’s livelihood. Implementing the requirements of stabilizing employment, finance, foreign trade, foreign investment, domestic investment, and expectations, and ensuring jobs, basic livelihood, market entities, food and energy security, stable industrial and supply chains, and smooth functioning at the grassroots level, the courts established green channels for filing, mediation, trial, and enforcement for disputes arising from production and operation difficulties during the epidemic, thereby serving and safeguarding the recovery and sustainable development of small, medium, and micro enterprises. Pilot work was carried out to unify compensation standards for personal injury among urban and rural residents, changing the traditional practice of determining personal injury compensation standards based on distinctions between urban and rural household registration, thereby promoting fairness of rights and fairness of rules. The courts lawfully heard marriage and family disputes and other cases and protected the lawful rights and interests of women, children, the elderly, and persons with disabilities. The trial work for military-related cases was strengthened to lawfully safeguard national defense interests and the lawful rights and interests of service members and their families. State compensation and judicial aid work was earnestly carried out, with 1,674 such cases concluded. Accurate law popularization was continuously advanced, in-depth publicity and educational activities on the Civil Code were carried out, and small cases such as road rage and throwing coffee illustrated major principles of the rule of law. Through forms such as the Beijing Court Circuit Lecture Hall and Jing Xiaochui micro-animation, legal publicity and education were carried out on epidemic prevention and control, staying away from drugs, and preventing telecom fraud. In the Central Political and Legal Affairs Commission’s selection of outstanding political and legal new media under the Four Hundreds program, the Beijing Higher People’s Court was the only court in the country to win all awards. Promoting effective resolution of difficulties in enforcement. Adhering to goodwill-based and civilized enforcement, the courts carried out special enforcement actions to serve and safeguard the goals of stability and security, and while intensifying enforcement efforts, adopted judicial measures that had the least impact on enterprise production and operations, thereby helping maintain the stability of industrial and supply chains. The enforcement coordination mechanism was improved, integrated systems for inquiry, control, and seizure were advanced, and new online seizure systems for real estate and Beijing-registered vehicles were established. The mechanism of one case, dual review for the handling of enforcement cases and misconduct issues in enforcement was implemented, strengthening supervision over enforcement work. Throughout the year, 267,846 cases were enforced and RMB 108.32 billion was recovered or implemented. III. Administering justice for the people and upholding judicial fairness, deepening judicial reform, and improving trial quality and efficiency Strengthening trial supervision and guarding the lifeline of fairness and justice. The courts strengthened the role of collegial panels as statutory adjudicatory bodies, gave full play to the substantive participation of people’s assessors, and ensured lawful and standardized deliberation. Measures for retrieving similar cases were formulated, and a mandatory similar-case retrieval system was implemented to regulate the exercise of judicial discretion and promote consistency in adjudication standards. Systems concerning supervision and administration by court presidents and division chiefs, case handling by court presidents and division chiefs, judges’ meetings, and judicial committees were strictly implemented. Special inspections were carried out regarding the performance of duties by court presidents and division chiefs. Court presidents and division chiefs handled 277,968 cases, accounting for 33.2 percent of all concluded cases. Problems existing in commutation, parole, and temporary service of sentence outside prison were deeply examined and actively corrected. Detailed rules and management systems were formulated for commutation, parole, and temporary service of sentence outside prison, the applicable conditions were strictly controlled, and substantive and standardized adjudication was promoted. Prosecutorial supervision was lawfully accepted. The courts concluded 165 protest cases filed by procuratorial organs, of which 63 were revised or remanded for retrial. Judicial openness was continuously advanced. The online publication rate of judgments and rulings that should have been disclosed reached 99.9 percent, and the rate of live-streamed court hearings reached 36.1 percent, an increase of 16.2 percentage points over the previous year. Strengthening trial management and continuously improving quality and efficiency. Activities such as case quality evaluations and judgment document competitions were carried out in depth. The Beijing Higher People’s Court reviewed 6,419 cases, promoting continuous improvement in trial quality, and the rate of acceptance of judgments and cessation of petitions in effective cases reached 97.4 percent. To shorten service periods, a system for confirming service addresses of market entities was established, and the electronic service rate in civil and commercial cases increased to 58.3 percent. To shorten the cycle for appraisal and evaluation, measures on assessment, evaluation, and dynamic management of professional appraisal and evaluation institutions were formulated, reducing the average time for appraisal and evaluation from 40 working days to 24 working days. Pilot reform on the diversion of civil procedures between simple and complex cases was promoted, and six supporting documents were formulated on the application of sole-judge trials, electronic litigation, and other matters. The average time required for small-claims procedures and summary procedures was shortened by more than half compared with the statutory trial limits. Strengthening the building of a one-stop diversified dispute resolution and litigation service system and providing the public with menu-based choices for resolving disputes. Adhering to the principle of placing non-litigation dispute resolution mechanisms at the forefront, the courts concluded 324,395 cases through the diversified mediation plus speedy adjudication mechanism. This working mechanism has been promoted nationwide and has provided Beijing experience for building a layered and progressively resolving litigation mechanism for contradictions and disputes. In connection with the Party-building-led reform under which street-level and township-level authorities sound the whistle and departments respond, the courts built a unified citywide platform for source governance of litigation, providing source governance services to primary-level organizations 15,000 times. As a result of this work, the number of newly accepted cases in courts across the city declined for the first time in many years, by 14.7 percent, while property service disputes and private lending disputes that are prone to mass filing fell by 65.2 percent and 31.5 percent respectively. Focusing on issues strongly reflected by the public, the courts continuously deepened the convenient service mechanism of answering immediately upon receipt of a complaint and handling immediately upon receipt of an assignment. The 12368 hotline answered 737,000 calls, and the rate of successfully contacting judges reached 100 percent. Deepening the building of smart courts and promoting the modernization of the trial system and trial capacity. The Beijing Higher People’s Court established an electronic case file generation center to promote simultaneous generation and in-depth application of electronic case files along with case processing, driving citywide courts toward full-process online case handling and whole-node supervision and management. Relying on the Beijing intelligent management system for political and legal case handling, 31 business processes for criminal judicial case handling were launched online. Nearly 100 process nodes for civil, commercial, and administrative cases were embedded into the adjudication system, making automatic warnings, real-time reminders, and risk blocking possible. IV. Adhering to the direction of revolutionization, regularization, professionalization, and specialization and building a trial team that the Party and the people can trust, rely on, and feel assured about Giving top priority to political development. The courts continuously carried out large-scale study, discussion, and training on Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, thoroughly studied and implemented Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law, and conducted special education on upholding the Party’s absolute leadership over judicial work and adhering to the socialist rule of law path with Chinese characteristics. A total of 104 political training sessions were held to effectively strengthen consciousness of the need to maintain political integrity, think in big-picture terms, follow the leadership core, and keep in alignment, strengthen confidence in the path, theory, system, and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and achieve the Two Upholds. The two systems of primary-level Party building were implemented, and activities to create Party-building brands were carried out, further enhancing the cohesion and combat effectiveness of the ranks. Judges concluded an average of 332 cases per person. A total of 4,497 Party-member court officers went down to communities to participate in epidemic prevention and control. Four Party-building cases from courts across the city were selected as innovative Party-building cases of courts nationwide, ranking first in the country by number selected. Over the past year, 50 collectives and 103 individuals from courts across the city received commendations at or above the provincial-ministerial level. Cultivating strong judicial capabilities. Focusing on laws and judicial interpretations such as the Civil Code, the courts comprehensively carried out professional training and established the Jingfa Online Classroom, with 45,000 participant attendances. The courts solidly advanced the building of four high grounds in trial business, trial research, reform and innovation, and talent concentration, organized the Bai’an Yunting professional skills competition, and conducted selections of experts in adjudicatory practice and adjudicatory research. Specialized talent high grounds for criminal, intellectual property, and administrative adjudication were挂牌 established in three courts respectively. In national selections of outstanding court judgments, outstanding case analyses, and academic research papers, Beijing courts ranked first nationwide in all categories. Judicial reform micro-innovation activities were carried out in depth to promote great changes across all work, and Beijing courts ranked first nationwide in the number of typical judicial reform cases selected by the Supreme People’s Court. Tempering fine discipline and work style. Special rectification regarding the three provisions on preventing interference in justice was carried out in depth, and concrete operating procedures were formulated to ensure full-process recording of case inquiries, reporting on a case-by-case basis of inquiries into cases, and serious accountability for improper interference. The system of recusal from appointment was strictly implemented to effectively prevent conflicts of interest and promote the prevention and control of integrity risks. Judicial inspections and supervision of court affairs were carried out in depth, including video inspections of discipline and work style in courtrooms and reception windows, and judicial corruption was punished with a zero-tolerance attitude. Eighteen court employees received Party or administrative disciplinary sanctions, and eight were held criminally liable. Over the past year, courts across the city consciously accepted the supervision of the Municipal People’s Congress and its Standing Committee, carefully implemented the opinions and suggestions put forward during deliberation of the court work report at the Third Session of the Fifteenth Municipal People’s Congress, submitted special reports to the Standing Committee of the Municipal People’s Congress on optimizing the rule-of-law business environment and intellectual property adjudication, and accepted special inquiries. The courts also consciously accepted democratic supervision by the CPPCC and actively cooperated with investigations, consultations, and other activities carried out by the CPPCC. Suggestions and proposals submitted by deputies and committee members were carefully handled, and all 62 suggestions and proposals were completed. New mechanisms for communication and liaison with deputies and committee members under epidemic prevention and control conditions were innovated, and 374 online and offline liaison activities were carried out, with 2,044 deputy and committee member participations. The achievements in the work of the past year were the result of the strong leadership of the Municipal Party Committee, the effective supervision of the Municipal People’s Congress, and the care and support of the government, the CPPCC, and all sectors of society. The supervision and support of deputies to the People’s Congress and members of the CPPCC strongly promoted new development in court work. Here, on behalf of courts across the city, I express sincere respect and heartfelt thanks. We are also clearly aware that there are still some problems in the work of courts across the city. These mainly include the need to strengthen trial supervision and management, insufficient implementation of supervision and management systems, the need to improve trial quality and efficiency, continued public concern over issues such as long case-handling cycles and inconsistent adjudication standards, the need to improve the quality and capabilities of some adjudicatory personnel, insufficient reserves of high-level talent, insufficient transmission of pressure in comprehensively and strictly governing the Party, and the continued occurrence of disciplinary and legal violations by court personnel. In response, courts across the city will adopt effective measures and resolutely and forcefully make improvements. Tasks for 2021 In 2021, the overall thinking for the work of courts across the city is as follows: adhere to the guidance of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, thoroughly study and implement Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law and the important instructions of General Secretary Xi Jinping on political and legal work, conscientiously implement the guiding principles of the 19th National Congress of the Communist Party of China and the Second, Third, Fourth, and Fifth Plenary Sessions of the 19th CPC Central Committee, as well as the Central Conference on Comprehensively Governing the Country According to Law, the Central Economic Work Conference, the Central Political and Legal Work Conference, and the National Meeting of Presidents of Higher People’s Courts, earnestly implement all decisions and arrangements of the Municipal Party Committee, attach greater importance to systems thinking, rule-of-law thinking, and a foundation-strengthening orientation, highlight political development, highlight services and safeguards for the capital’s high-quality development, highlight trial supervision and checks and constraints, highlight source governance of litigation, deeply advance judicial reform, effectively strengthen the building of a high-quality adjudicatory team, promote the high-quality development of adjudicatory work, and provide strong judicial guarantees for making a good start to the Fourteenth Five-Year Plan. Firmly grasping the correct political direction and unswervingly following the socialist rule of law path with Chinese characteristics. The courts will thoroughly study Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and conscientiously implement Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law. Centering on the celebration of the 100th anniversary of the founding of the Party, the courts will comprehensively carry out political training, continue Party-building brand creation activities, further strengthen the Four Consciousnesses, the Four Self-confidences, and the Two Upholds, and implement the Party’s leadership throughout the whole process and in all aspects of court work. Closely centering on the capital’s central tasks and fully performing adjudicatory functions. The courts will make every effort to safeguard the capital’s security and stability, lawfully and severely punish serious criminal offenses, and build a long-term mechanism for combating organized crime and local criminal gangs. They will make every effort to serve the building of an international science and technology innovation center and a benchmark city for the global digital economy, increase judicial protection of intellectual property in key fields, and implement the punitive damages system for intellectual property. They will make every effort to safeguard the coordinated development of the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region and continue to lawfully and prudently hear cases concerning decongestion, rectification, and upgrading, construction of the sub-center, and the Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games. They will make every effort to serve the building of a new development pattern, construct the Beijing Financial Court to high standards and from a high starting point, formulate concrete measures for providing judicial services to the two zones construction, and further optimize the law-based business environment. They will make every effort to serve and safeguard supply-side structural reform and the building of an international consumption center city, strengthen judicial protection of property rights, and enhance adjudication in anti-monopoly and anti-unfair competition cases. They will make every effort to elevate the level of judicial protection of people’s livelihood and conscientiously implement the Civil Code. They will also make every effort to carry out epidemic prevention and control and provide strong judicial support for normalized epidemic prevention and control. Continuously deepening reform and innovation and effectively improving trial quality, efficiency, and judicial credibility. The courts will conscientiously implement the Plan for Building a Law-based China and serve and safeguard the building of the demonstration leading area of a law-based China in the capital. They will improve the judicial supervision and checks-and-constraints mechanism, advance the reform of the criminal procedure system centered on trial, give full play to the supervisory function of trial levels, and further strengthen internal supervision. They will deepen diversified mediation plus speedy adjudication and source governance of litigation to form a governance system that is comprehensive in coverage, coordinated from top to bottom, and collaborative among all parties. They will deepen measures for justice for the people and comprehensively build a modern litigation service system that is intensive and efficient, diversified in dispute resolution, smart and precise, and integrated and shared. Always adhering to comprehensive and strict Party governance and striving to forge a high-quality adjudicatory team. Taking the education and rectification of the ranks as the focal point, the courts will build the soul of loyalty, firmly investigate and rectify problems, strictly enforce discipline and work style, and carry forward the spirit of heroic models. They will continue to advance the building of the four high grounds, enhance professional capabilities, and cultivate and reserve a group of high-quality specialized personnel so as to ensure that the Beijing court team always remains at the forefront nationwide. Dear Deputies, under the strong leadership of the Municipal Party Committee and the effective supervision of the Municipal People’s Congress and its Standing Committee, courts across the city will conscientiously implement the resolution of this session, forge ahead with determination, work hard and diligently, strive to serve and safeguard taking the lead in basically realizing socialist modernization, and celebrate the 100th anniversary of the founding of the Party with outstanding achievements.

Title: Talking about Win11's HDR: Does the monitor turn gray when HDR is turned on? This is not your problem. Content: Starting from Windows 10, Microsoft has set up an HDR mode in the operating system. If the user's monitor supports HDR, then turning on the HDR switch in the system will put the entire Windows 11 in an HDR picture state. However, almost everyone has found that no matter how high the brightness of the HDR monitor is, after turning on HDR mode, the entire picture will appear gray, and the brightness seems to be lower. Monitors with low brightness and poor color gamut will be more obvious, but even LG's OLED monitors will have similar problems, but the situation will be slightly better. There has been a long-standing debate among netizens about this issue, and various methods have been tried for debugging, but no good results have been obtained. So how did this problem arise? Is there any way to make the monitor display normal colors in Windows' HDR mode? Today we will discuss this matter, and by the way, we can also talk about how to correctly use HDR mode in the Windows system. Because this problem involves too much, and almost all current monitors are unsolvable, many people hope that no matter what the reason is, Microsoft had better come up with a good solution. And on Microsoft's official page, there are indeed statements related to HDR. In fact, it is nothing more than two aspects. One is that the picture brightness decreases after turning on HDR, and the other is that the color display is inaccurate after turning on HDR. These two problems together are what we often call the picture turning gray. Regarding the brightness change, Microsoft also has its own statement. Microsoft said that if all SDR content and applications appear too bright or too dark on an HDR-supported monitor, you can drag the slider under "HDR/SDR brightness balance" in the HDR options to get the correct brightness balance between HDR and SDR content. This method is indeed effective and can adjust the brightness of the desktop, but it will obviously make the entire picture overexposed or underexposed, and in fact, the problem of the overall gray and dim color of the desktop has not been solved, but it can visually improve the viewing experience to some extent. Generally, the default slider is at 50%, which is the state of balanced brightness between SDR and HDR, but this is obviously not enough. If the user feels that the desktop is too gray after turning on HDR, then we recommend adjusting it to about 80%. Whether the monitor is HDR400 or HDR1000, it should be set this way. This will make the desktop look brighter. Although it cannot completely solve the problem of the gray and dark picture, it will definitely be much better than not adjusting it. Of course, we still have to say that no matter how you set it, the picture of the Windows desktop under HDR is definitely not as good as SDR. In the color part, Microsoft also explained separately what to do if the color cannot be displayed correctly on an external monitor that supports HDR. Of course, what Microsoft said is nonsense. Microsoft said that HDR-supported monitors support a wider range than sRGB, so after turning on "Use HDR", the HDR monitor should correctly reproduce the sRGB colors used in desktop applications. If some HDR-supported monitors do not correctly reproduce these colors, then users should consider buying a monitor certified by VESA Display HDR... But this is obviously not correct, because we also encounter inaccurate colors when using VESA-certified HDR monitors. The dim color cannot be solved even by adjusting the brightness. This is the case whether it is an HDR400 or HDR1000 monitor, LCD, MiniLED, or OLED. We have tried all types of monitors, and all of them cannot display accurate colors in Windows' HDR mode, especially the color brightness will significantly decrease, and this has little to do with the actual brightness of the monitor. That is to say, Microsoft actually knows about such problems and has provided some mitigation solutions, but this cannot solve the phenomenon of the overall picture color turning gray after the HDR monitor turns on Windows' HDR mode. So how to solve this problem? First, we use screen shots to illustrate the difference between Win11's SDR and HDR pictures. I believe many users' monitors are like this: under SDR, the picture is normal, the color is accurate, and the brightness looks higher; after turning on the system's HDR, the entire picture color becomes dim, and the picture feels like it is covered with a layer of gray. It should be noted that the brightness under HDR is higher than under SDR, which can be confirmed by color calibration hardware. So why does the picture look so bad? Microsoft actually does not have a clear statement on its official website, and there are many discussions online. But the relatively accurate statement is that Microsoft did not consider the current situation of monitors in the color gamut conversion part, so such a problem occurred. Microsoft's interface actually uses sRGB, but after turning on HDR, the monitor's color gamut is converted to BT2020, so Microsoft will also use the Lut conversion method to convert the original sRGB color gamut to BT2020 to meet the display needs of the monitor. Otherwise, the entire picture will show extremely bad colors. But after Microsoft converts the color gamut, it defaults to 100% of the BT2020 color space. That is to say, the higher the monitor's BT2020 color gamut coverage value, the more accurate the color will be in Windows' HDR mode. So the question is, what is the current monitor's BT2020 color gamut? The answer is that most are no more than 70%. This is why most monitors cannot achieve ideal results in Windows' HDR mode no matter how they are adjusted. Whether it is a monitor or a TV, although they are currently boasting about their wide color gamut, and of course they are not wrong, we can see 100% sRGB color gamut coverage, which is no problem in Windows' SDR mode, and even 100% AdobeRGB color gamut coverage, over 95% NTSC color gamut coverage, and close to 100% DCI-P3 color gamut coverage. But in terms of BT2020, that is, Rec2020 color gamut coverage, there are currently almost no products that exceed 80% color gamut coverage. Taking monitors as an example, achieving 75% BT2020 color gamut coverage is very excellent. Like LG's OLED TVs, which have such high ratings, but usually the BT2020 color gamut coverage is only about 71%. If the display device can achieve 100% BT2020 color gamut coverage, then the color will naturally be accurate in Windows' HDR mode, but unfortunately, there are currently no such consumer display products; whether it is a TV or a monitor, exceeding 70% BT2020 color gamut coverage is considered excellent. In this case, in Windows' HDR mode, the color shift will naturally be more obvious, the original high dynamic color content is lost, and naturally it looks gray. Of course, another part of the reason is that under Windows' HDR mode, the Gamma value has also changed, no longer the standard Gamma 2.2 under SDR, which will also have some visual impact. But in general, the reason why everyone sees their monitor's color deteriorate under Windows HDR mode is still because their display device is not good enough! Of course, Microsoft should take the blame for this part. This color gamut conversion mode is too rough and simple, and does not consider the actual situation of users. So how to solve it? The answer is unsolvable... Because there are currently no monitors or TVs that can cover 100% of the BT2020 color gamut, and those exceeding 80% are very rare. So everyone facing the gray desktop under HDR mode cannot completely solve it. Currently, we can only wait for display devices with wider color gamuts to be launched in the future. It is said that Samsung's QD-OLED panel can cover more than 85% of the BT2020 color gamut. If monitors using this panel are used, it is estimated that they can achieve better results in Windows' HDR mode than now, but of course the price is not cheap. After understanding the above content, everyone will understand: since this problem cannot be solved at present, then normally, just run Windows in SDR for a long time. Here we need to talk about several situations. After all, many applications themselves have HDR. If the monitor is always in SDR mode, it would be too wasteful. If the monitor is connected to non-PC external devices, such as PS5, Xbox Series X, or other products, if the monitor can automatically identify HDR content, then the user does not need to worry. These devices can automatically switch between SDR and HDR, and will not be as perverted as the Microsoft system, which requires 100% BT2020 color gamut coverage to display correctly. Everyone's HDR mapping is very normal. We mainly talk about the correct HDR application mode under Windows. In fact, software applications under Windows also have two types of HDR modes. One does not require Windows to switch to HDR mode. As long as the monitor supports HDR mode, it can be automatically set to HDR mode. Some games and applications are like this, such as the "Resident Evil" series, such as DVDFab Player, etc. The desktop continues to use SDR mode. After entering the game or video, the user can turn on the HDR option in the game. At this time, the monitor automatically switches to HDR mode. After exiting the game or video, it automatically returns to SDR mode. This is the simplest and most worry-free method. But there are still some game applications that require Windows to be set in HDR mode before they have related HDR options, such as Microsoft's full series of PC games "Forza", "Gears 5", "Halo", etc. Games from other game manufacturers may also have this situation; in addition, some web video applications, such as YouTube, Netflix, etc., also require Windows to be set in HDR mode to provide HDR content. So when playing these games or watching videos at this time, you must set Windows in HDR mode. Anyway, the HDR content of games and videos will not be as gray as the desktop. The effect in full-screen mode is very good, mainly because the manufacturer's SDR-HDR mapping is done well. So the method is actually very simple. Usually, users can set Windows in SDR mode, that is, do not turn on HDR mode. Then when watching videos or playing games, if the application must have Windows in HDR mode to appear HDR options, then turn on the system's HDR at this time. The purpose of writing this article is that both myself and other users have encountered this problem, and no matter how we set and adjust it, we cannot completely solve the situation where the picture color is not as good as SDR. This problem is indeed not the user's fault. Microsoft certainly has some responsibility, but Microsoft's approach seems to be the simplest and most feasible solution. Because if the color gamut of display devices continues to improve in the future and can cover a higher BT2020 color gamut, this problem will be gradually solved. As for now, either set the system in SDR or let the eyes endure more. In addition, some monitor manufacturers themselves understand the situation better and will make some adjustments to the display devices to better adapt to Windows' HDR mode. Therefore, we often see that the effects of some brand products may be better than other brands, but the improvement is limited, at least it cannot completely solve this troublesome matter. In addition, if you must set Windows in HDR mode, not to mention higher color gamut, monitors with higher brightness usually have better effects, so high-brightness monitors still seem to be necessary at present. Return to Sohu, view more

Title: Xiaonan: Joint Efforts to Tackle Key Issues and Support City Creation Content: Xiaonan: Joint Efforts to Tackle Key Issues and Support City Creation In recent days, the Xiaonan District Urban Management Comprehensive Law Enforcement Brigade, in collaboration with the Comprehensive Law Enforcement Bureau of the Xiaonan Economic Development Zone Management Committee, has carried out a city appearance improvement campaign to comprehensively enhance the business environment. Law enforcement officers from the Nanda Squadron and the Mobile Squadron, adhering to the "721" work method, focused on concentrated rectification of issues such as merchants operating beyond their shops, mobile vendors occupying roads, and randomly hung advertising banners in demonstration areas including Minbang Market, Dongzha Road, and Huangxiang Road. They promoted relevant urban management laws and regulations, proactively assisted merchants in moving items displayed outside back into their shops, and guided mobile vendors occupying roads to operate in farmers' markets and temporary convenience疏导点. These efforts continuously promote the standardization, normalization, and long-term effectiveness of urban appearance management and further advance the "Five Cities Co-creation" initiative. Title: People's Court Case Database Case: If one party gives birth to a child within six months after divorce, can the other party claim divorce damages? Content: Editor's Note: A couple divorces by agreement. After the divorce, the wife learns that the conception time of the child born from the man's subsequent marriage occurred during their marital relationship. The wife then sues in court, requesting the court to order the man to pay compensation for damages. Will the court support her claim? 1. Key Points of the Judgment If one spouse violates the duty of fidelity, engages in an improper relationship with a third party during the marriage, remarries just three days after the divorce, and gives birth to a child within less than six months, seriously harming the marital relationship and leading to the breakdown of the marriage, this should be recognized as falling under the "other major faults" circumstance stipulated in Article 1091 of the Civil Code. 2. Basic Facts of the Case Hu and Liu registered their marriage in 2011 and had a daughter, Liu Nv, during the marriage. They later divorced by agreement at the Civil Affairs Bureau in October 2019. The divorce agreement stipulated: After the divorce, Liu Nv would be raised by the wife, Hu. Regarding property division: To the man: 50% ownership of a property in a certain residential area in Chaoyang District. To the woman: Personal belongings. To the daughter Liu Nv: 50% ownership of the property in a certain residential area in Chaoyang District; one car, to be shared equally by the man and the woman. Regarding claims and debts: There were no claims or debts after the marriage. In October 2019, Liu remarried someone else and gave birth to a son, Liu Nan, in April 2020. Hu claimed: Due to Liu's infidelity, they divorced by agreement in 2019. After the divorce, Liu remarried and had a child with his new spouse. In 2022, Hu accidentally learned that the conception time of the child from Liu's remarriage was during Hu and Liu's marital relationship. Liu's above actions caused Hu significant psychological trauma. Additionally, Hu requested the court to order Liu to pay her 200,000 RMB in compensation for damages. 3. Court Judgment The disputed issue in this case was whether Liu should pay divorce damages to Hu. Hu argued that Liu's act of marital infidelity and having a child with another person was continuous. From the perspective of protecting civil subjects' rights and promoting socialist core values, the provisions of the Civil Code should apply, and the claim for divorce damages should be supported. Liu argued that they divorced before the implementation of the Civil Code, and the relevant provisions of the Marriage Law and its judicial interpretations should apply. Hu's lawsuit for divorce damages was filed more than one year after the divorce by agreement and should not be supported. Regarding this issue, the dispute mainly involved the identification of major faults in the divorce damages system and the time requirements for claiming divorce damages. The following three sub-issues needed clarification. First, regarding the identification of fault behavior for divorce damages. The Marriage Law revised in 2001 first established the divorce damages system, reflected in Article 46: If one of the following circumstances leads to divorce, the no-fault party has the right to claim damages: (1) bigamy; (2) cohabitation with a third party while married; (3) domestic violence; (4) maltreatment or abandonment of a family member. This provision was the first legislative establishment of the divorce damages system in China, aiming to compensate the injured spouse and provide consolation through financial compensation and spiritual comfort. However, in practice, facing complex and changing social life, the restrictive enumeration method in Article 46 of the Marriage Law could not be expansively interpreted to cover other fault situations, making it difficult to fully realize the system's function of sanctioning the fault party causing the divorce. Article 1091 of the Civil Code adopts a legislative approach combining enumeration and general provisions, further improving the divorce damages system based on Article 46 of the Marriage Law. It adds a catch-all provision of "other major faults" besides the original four statutory faults, thus solving the problem of the system's overly narrow application scope. In this case, Hu and Liu divorced by agreement in October 2019. Liu remarried just three days after the divorce and gave birth to a son in April 2020. Based on the timeline of Liu's remarriage and childbirth and the facts acknowledged by both parties during the trial, the degree of his fault behavior has met the conditions of the catch-all clause "other major faults" stipulated in Article 1091 of the Civil Code. Second, the time requirement for claiming divorce damages after a divorce by agreement. The Marriage Law did not specify a time limit for claiming damages after completing divorce registration procedures. However, Judicial Interpretation (II) of the Marriage Law, Article 27, set a time limit: the claim must be made within one year after completing the divorce registration procedures at the marriage registration authority; claims made after this period will not be supported. This "one-year" rule aimed to urge the right holder to exercise their rights promptly and maintain the stability of social relations. However, it had two main issues: First, the Marriage Law has always treated protecting the interests of the no-fault party as a principle in the division of marital property upon divorce. As one of the three major divorce relief systems, divorce damages should fully reflect this concept. If the no-fault party only learns of the other party's fault more than a year after the divorce, limiting the lawsuit period to one year is detrimental to the exercise of the no-fault party's rights and deviates from the purpose of protecting the legitimate rights and interests of the no-fault party in divorce damages proceedings. Second, from the nature of the right to claim divorce damages, the one-year period stipulated in Judicial Interpretation (II) of the Marriage Law excludes parties who divorced by agreement from exercising their right to claim damages after one year. As a provision that significantly impacts parties' rights, it lacks a clear basis in China's civil law system. Considering the above factors, the "Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Marriage and Family Part of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (I)" [hereinafter referred to as Interpretation of the Marriage and Family Part (I)], effective January 1, 2021, Article 89 stipulates that if a party, after completing divorce registration procedures at the marriage registration authority, files a damages claim with the people's court based on Article 1091 of the Civil Code, the people's court shall accept the case. However, if the party has clearly waived this claim during the divorce agreement, the people's court will not support it. This article removed the provision in Judicial Interpretation (II) of the Marriage Law that "claims made one year after completing divorce registration procedures will not be supported." Since the Marriage and Family Part is located in Part Five of the Civil Code system, based on the method of systematic interpretation, the exercise of the right to claim divorce damages should also apply the principle of the statute of limitations in the Civil Code. The statute of limitations for the no-fault party to file a lawsuit claiming divorce damages should be three years, calculated from the date the party knew or should have known of the ex-spouse's major fault. In this case, Hu claimed divorce damages more than one year after their divorce by agreement in 2019. According to Article 27 of Judicial Interpretation (II) of the Marriage Law, Hu's lawsuit was filed beyond the one-year limit and should not be supported. The first-instance court dismissed Hu's claim based on this reasoning. Therefore, the key issue in this case is whether the time for the no-fault party to claim divorce damages can be governed by the relevant provisions of the Civil Code and its judicial interpretations,不受协议离婚后一年内的限制。 Third, this case should apply the relevant provisions of the Civil Code and Interpretation of the Marriage and Family Part (I). Article 2 of the "Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Time Effect of the Application of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China" (hereinafter referred to as the Provisions on the Time Effect of the Civil Code) states that for civil dispute cases caused by legal facts before the implementation of the Civil Code, if the laws and judicial interpretations at that time had provisions, the laws and judicial interpretations at that time shall apply, unless applying the provisions of the Civil Code is more conducive to protecting the legitimate rights and interests of civil subjects, maintaining social and economic order, and promoting socialist core values. This clause primarily addresses how to apply the law when the old law has provisions but the new law changes them, including the principle of "no retroactivity of law" and the rule of favorable retroactivity. Regarding the standard for favorable retroactivity, the "three more conducives" – more conducive to protecting the legitimate rights and interests of civil subjects, more conducive to maintaining social and economic order, and more conducive to promoting socialist core values – are used as the criteria for judging favorable retroactivity. The benchmark for reasonable expectations is compliance with the requirements of good faith, public order and good customs, and the rules of daily life experience, thereby ensuring the stability of the legal order. Autonomy of will, as a basic principle of the Civil Code, is particularly important in the marriage and family领域 involving private affairs. The best manifestation of autonomy of will is civil subjects disposing of their rights according to their own will. The right to claim divorce damages, explicitly granted to the no-fault spouse in Article 1091 of the Civil Code, if still judged based on the four fault situations under the Marriage Law, or if the no-fault party's claim is dismissed solely because it exceeds the "one year" after the divorce by agreement, clearly does not align with the purpose pursued by the principle of protecting the interests of the no-fault party in the Marriage and Family Part of the Civil Code. Based on the above analysis, the catch-all provision for statutory circumstances of divorce damages in the Civil Code and the provision regarding claiming divorce damages after a divorce by agreement in Interpretation of the Marriage and Family Part (I) meet the "three more conducives" standard for favorable retroactivity under Article 2 of the Provisions on the Time Effect of the Civil Code. Applying the provisions of the Civil Code and Interpretation of the Marriage and Family Part (I) in this case is more consistent with public order and good customs and conducive to promoting socialist core values. In summary, Liu's behavior constitutes "other major faults" as defined by the Civil Code. Hu, as the no-fault party, has the right to receive corresponding compensation and relief through the divorce damages system. Although Hu made the claim more than one year after the divorce registration, and the divorce occurred before the implementation of the Civil Code, she did not explicitly waive this claim in the divorce agreement. Applying the provisions of the Civil Code and relevant judicial interpretations in this case is more conducive to protecting the legitimate rights and interests of civil subjects. The first-instance court's dismissal of the claim solely based on it exceeding one year after the divorce by agreement was improper, and this court corrects it. The specific amount of compensation will be determined by this court based on the actual circumstances of the case, considering the property division处理情况 in the divorce agreement. Title: Traffic Police Wake Up Driver in Service Area to Issue Ticket, Latest Response Content: This article is reposted from [Jiupai News]; Recently, a netizen posted a video claiming that at the Gao'andong Service Area in Yichun, Jiangxi, a truck driver resting and sleeping in the service area was woken up by traffic police to check for fatigued driving and issued a ticket. In the video, two uniformed staff stand by a police car checking driving documents, etc. The videographer stated: "Traffic police woke up the sleeping car (driver), woke him up to fine him, checking for fatigued driving." The original video has now been deleted. On December 6th, staff from the Eighth Brigade of the First Detachment of Jiangxi Provincial High-Speed Traffic Police, to which the Gao'andong Service Area belongs, stated that they are investigating the matter and will release the investigation results later. "If there is indeed a case of fatigued driving, traffic police can investigate and deal with it; this seems unrelated to what you are doing in the service area," the staff member said. "Some drivers are sleeping, some are eating, some are in the restroom; it's hard to say." He explained that the traffic police detachment has a police office and stationed police in the service area. When asked whether punishment could wait until the driver has rested properly if there is indeed a violation, he said, "That suggestion is quite good." Traffic police are checking whether the driver was fatigued driving. Figure/Video screenshot Fu Jian, a well-known criminal defense lawyer and director of Henan Zejin Law Firm, believes that according to the relevant provisions of the "Road Traffic Safety Law of the People's Republic of China," fatigued driving is a clear illegal act. As long as there is continuous driving for more than 4 hours without stopping to rest or the rest stop time is less than 20 minutes, it constitutes a violation, and traffic police can punish the driver according to the law. However, the driver actively entering the service area to rest indicates an awareness of avoiding fatigued driving and taking active measures to eliminate safety hazards. Traffic police can pay more attention to the rationality and humanization of law enforcement without affecting the effectiveness of enforcement. Reporter: Wang Jiaqing
