Title: How to Determine the Defense Strategy for Illegal Business Operations? Content: Illegal business operation is a catch-all charge, used wherever needed. For the crime of illegal business operation, determining the defense strategy is crucial. First, it is essential to determine guilt or innocence, and if guilty, whether the offense is minor or serious. For example, in the past, operating beyond the scope of a tobacco license—such as having a license for District A but operating in District B—was treated as the crime of illegal business operation. However, with subsequent national economic development, such behavior is no longer considered a crime. For this situation, whether your retail qualifications match, whether they fall within the relevant scope, and whether relevant qualifications need to be recognized directly determine the constitution of the crime of illegal business operation. This is the first key point: determining guilt or innocence. Second, it is about determining the specific charge. For instance, the same act might constitute the crime of illegal business operation or the crime of selling counterfeit and shoddy products, or the crime of selling goods with counterfeit registered trademarks. Which charge it constitutes will directly affect the sentencing. Third, the determination of the amount involved in illegal business operations is also critical. Generally, the amount of illegal business operations is determined based on sales revenue or appraisal results. This appraised amount can be recognized based on cost, sales revenue, or market value. For the same appraised amount of 550,000, if the appraisal is inappropriate, applying for a reappraisal might reduce it to below 500,000, and the sentence could be reduced from the original 5-10 years to less than 5 years. Third, the determination of illegal gains: in judicial practice, there are two methods. The first is when the investigative authorities have clear evidence of the amount of illegal gains. If there is no evidence, it depends on the defendant's own confession regarding the illegal gains. Fourth, there are conventional defense strategies, such as whether there was an attempted crime, discontinuation of the crime, whether the defendant is a principal or an accomplice, and whether there are circumstances like voluntary surrender or confession. Title: Causes of Gas Explosion Accidents Content: The main causes of gas explosion accidents are as follows: Equipment and Facilities Title: Damage, Aging, Severe Corrosion: Gas equipment and facilities may become damaged, aged, or corroded due to prolonged use or lack of maintenance, leading to gas leaks. Failure of Safety Protection Devices: If safety protection devices on equipment, such as valves and pressure gauges, malfunction or fail, they can also cause gas leaks. Improper Human Operation: Violation of Operating Procedures: If enterprise operators or household users violate operating procedures while using gas, such as improper operation or negligence, it may lead to gas leaks and explosions. Unattended Use or Flame Extinguishment: When using gas for cooking, if the gas is turned on and left unattended, or if the flame is extinguished due to reasons like boiling liquid overflow, it can cause continuous gas leakage, increasing the risk of explosion. To prevent gas explosion accidents, it is recommended to: Regularly inspect and maintain gas pipelines and equipment to ensure there is no damage, aging, or corrosion. Stay vigilant when using gas, avoid leaving it unattended or allowing the flame to go out. If a gas leak is detected, immediately close the main gas valve, ventilate the area to reduce indoor gas concentration, evacuate quickly, and call emergency services.

Title: Is it better to exercise in the morning or in the evening? Scientists suggest: women in the morning, men in the evening. Content: Before reading this article, please click on the blue font "Dr. Hou" above, then click "Follow", so you can continue to receive articles for free. Shared daily, completely free subscription, please feel free to follow. Source: Internet, contact for infringement and deletion. The benefits of exercise for physical health and longevity are not unfounded. In today's society, many office workers spend at least 8 hours a day sitting in front of a computer handling work, neglecting exercise. This has also led to a decline in physical resistance among many young people, making them prone to colds and hiding the risk of chronic diseases. Therefore, exercise is a very necessary thing, and it also has many unexpected benefits. However, to achieve the ideal exercise effect, it is necessary to grasp the correct exercise time. Scientists in the United States point out that exercise helps reduce the risk of heart disease and can also control blood pressure, but the best exercise time for men and women is quite different. What exactly is going on? Exercise by time: Women in the morning, men in the evening. The authoritative American medical journal "Frontiers in Physiology" has published new research, which was jointly published by scientists from California State University and Skidmore College in the United States. This study also included 56 volunteers, with 26 men and 30 women respectively. After 12 weeks of continuous exercise, the volunteers' physical fitness was significantly improved. Surprisingly, exercising at different times had different effects on the cardiovascular health of men and women. 1. Morning exercise is better for women. Women who exercised in the morning consumed about 7% more abdominal fat than those who exercised in the evening, and their blood pressure decreased by 7%. Women who exercised in the evening had stronger muscle strength, up to 29% higher than those who exercised in the morning. Therefore, if women want to lose weight and lower blood pressure, exercise time should be arranged in the morning; if the goal is to increase muscle, exercise time should be arranged in the evening. 2. Evening exercise is better for men. There was no significant change for men whether they exercised in the morning or evening. However, if the goal is to lower blood pressure and relieve fatigue, then exercise should be arranged in the evening. The reason for the significant difference in women may be related to overnight fasting, which can increase fat utilization during aerobic exercise and also increase resistance exercise, promoting fat tissue loss. 3 recognized longevity exercises that can be practiced more after the age of 40. Harvard University once conducted a follow-up study with up to 650,000 middle-aged volunteers. They persisted in 30 minutes of exercise every day. Title: Citi predicts the impact of tariffs on consumer prices will be slower and more persistent than expected. How will this affect future inflation trends? Content: Wall Street News Citi stated that the impact of tariffs on consumer prices is slower and more persistent than the market expected, and August-September will be a critical window period to verify this trend. Investors need to focus on: tariffs may lead to moderate but sustained increases in commodity prices; core PCE inflation is expected to rise to 3.1-3.2% by year-end; a weak demand environment may suppress significant price hikes, forcing companies to absorb tariff costs for a longer period. Citi's latest inflation weekly report shows that the impact of tariffs on consumer prices is not absent, but appears in a slower and more persistent form than the market expected. According to Zhui Feng Trading Desk news, Citi stated in its latest research report that the worst-case 'inflation blitzkrieg' (i.e., rapid, comprehensive price surges) has been temporarily avoided, but this may indicate a more sticky inflationary pressure is forming, which will gradually erode corporate profits and eventually pass through to consumers. The next few months (August to October) will be a critical window period to verify this trend. Investors need to closely monitor price movements in categories such as apparel, automobiles, and electronic products, as seasonal factors and cost transmission chains suggest prices in these areas may show 'unusually strong' increases. Citi predicts that, affected by this, the core Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index may reach 3.2% in the fourth quarter of 2025, indicating the inflation alarm is far from over. Tariff Transmission Surprisingly Slow, but 'Worst Case' Avoided Despite multiple rounds of tariff increases implemented in the US since spring, their direct push effect on consumer goods prices in the inflation data of the past 4-5 months has been much smaller than expected. Although July's inflation data showed some strength (core CPI monthly growth of 0.3%, meeting expectations), its main driver came from services, not goods. Citi expects core PCE to grow 0.27% month-on-month in July, with the annual rate rising to 2.9%. The report clearly states that the 'worst-case' scenario feared by the market – a situation of rapid, large-scale, and widespread price increases for goods due to expected cost rises – has been avoided. The core reason lies in weak end-demand. Against the backdrop of sluggish demand, companies are forced to absorb tariff costs themselves for longer periods to avoid losing customers through significant price hikes. Although this strategy temporarily suppresses CPI data, the cost is squeezed corporate profits, which may in turn further drag down future aggregate demand. Therefore, the impact of tariffs is not gone, but the timeline has been stretched. Key Window Period in the Coming Months: Focus on Apparel, Automobiles, and Electronics Citi emphasizes that inflation data from August to October will be the 'biggest test' for tariff transmission dynamics. The bank's framework indicates that the risk of goods price increases during this period is significantly higher, mainly based on the following points: Although Citi slightly lowered its forecast for future goods prices due to slow transmission in previous months, its model still shows core goods prices will be 'unusually strong' in the coming months. The report, by analyzing import price data, found that the phase where exporters 'paid' for tariffs seems to be over. Data shows that from March to May, import prices for goods like apparel and home furnishings declined, indicating some exporters absorbed tariff costs initially. However, recent data shows import prices for home furnishings have stabilized, while import prices for apparel have risen again. This suggests exporters, after a brief 'grace period,' are no longer continuing to digest tariff costs. As importers bear higher tariffs on shipments starting from June and July, this cost pressure is highly likely to be passed on to final consumers in the autumn, setting the stage for inflation data at that time. Services Inflation: Seemingly Strong, Actually Driven by a Few Items The strong performance of services prices in July easily raises market concerns about broad-based inflation heating up. But after in-depth analysis, Citi believes this is not a widespread price pressure. Specifically, the rise in CPI services prices was mainly driven by two 'one-off' factors: a significant 2.6% increase in dental services prices and a seasonal rebound in airfare prices. Similarly, the high 0.7% increase in PPI core services prices was mainly due to a significant 5.8% rebound in portfolio management fees linked to asset prices. Citi believes these specific item surges are not sustainable and do not represent a broad return of services inflation pressure. The University of Michigan's preliminary August survey showed inflation expectations rising again (1-year rose to 4.9%, 5-10 year rose to 3.9%). But Citi is cautious about this, believing that data volatility has increased after the survey methodology change, and its reference weight should be reduced. However, one detail in the survey alerted Citi: the proportion of respondents who think 'it's not a good time to buy large home furnishings due to high prices' Citi: Tariff Transmission Inflation Slower and More Persistent Than Expected, Next Few Months Will Be Key Verification Period

Title: Housing prices keep falling. What if the mortgage interest rate drops to 2.5%, and then to 2%? Content: Yesterday, my friend Xiao Li said he wanted to buy a house, but he felt housing prices would keep falling. I said if the mortgage rate drops to 2.5%, many properties now have an annual rental yield of around 2.5%. Would you buy a house then? He said 90% yes. Firstly, his child needs to go to school. Secondly, renting costs about the same amount. Thirdly, owning a house is definitely much better than renting - no need to deal with agents, pay agency fees, or constantly move. I asked, if the mortgage rate drops to 2% and the rental yield is 2.5%, would you buy? He said he would buy immediately. When housing prices were soaring, we blindly followed the trend, caught up in the frenzy, unable to be dissuaded from buying. When prices plummet, we also tend to believe they will keep crashing, overestimating the decline. In reality, in many places, the transaction prices for second-hand homes have fallen by more than half compared to their peaks. Even some good properties have seen price drops of 30% to 40% from their highest transaction prices. But there must be a price bottom. It's not just falling or rising. This round of US financial interest rate hikes is nearing its end, and the US is worried about problems caused by its own rate increases. On August 15th and 16th, the China-US Financial Working Group met in Shanghai, achieving two new outcomes. The People's Bank of China and the US Treasury Department, under the framework of the China-US Financial Working Group, signed an exchange of letters to strengthen financial stability cooperation, exchanged lists of financial stability contacts, aiming to maintain timely and smooth communication channels between the financial authorities of both sides during financial stress events and operational risks of financial institutions, reducing uncertainty. For the US, it must cut rates, but rate cuts could cause the US dollar to suddenly outflow rapidly, and it fears problems in the US stock market. Just a few days ago, the Japanese stock market crashed massively, with the Nikkei index plunging 13% in a single day, after several consecutive days of significant declines beforehand. China is worried about its mortgage problems because if housing prices fall further, many people may be unwilling to repay their loans. For buyers who put down 20% or 30%, if prices fall 30%, those with rigid demand might grit their teeth and keep repaying due to concerns about their credit history. But for those who put down 20%, if prices fall 40% or more, even buyers with rigid demand or those seeking upgrades might abandon their mortgage repayments en masse. Because if the house is now worth 1.5 million but they still owe the bank 2.8 million, coupled with decreased wages, they see no hope of recovering in their lifetime, so they'd rather keep the money. So, from an individual perspective, many people actually don't want housing prices to fall. From a national perspective, it's best for the economy if most housing prices remain stable, with good properties appreciating slightly. This way, bank loans can also be issued effectively. Yesterday, I mentioned that some bank loan interest rates are as low as 2.9% because banks are struggling to lend money; even consumer loans can be obtained at 2.9%. From a local government perspective, revenue from land sales is crucial and cannot be significantly reduced. From the perspective of housing interests, if mortgage rates drop further or rents rise, making the annual rental yield equal to the mortgage rate, a large number of people will inevitably start buying houses. We are not far from that point now. If the market remains lukewarm even when the rental yield equals the mortgage rate, a short-term influx of capital could create a mini-bull market. Coupled with a slight reduction in mortgage rates and media hype about the划算 of buying, prices might rise. At that point, some people will definitely enter the market, and since it's inherently划算, there will be sustained demand. Wishing everyone abundant wealth. Title: What to do if it's too loose after childbirth, how to restore tightness? Content: Vaginal relaxation is a common problem for women after childbirth, mostly caused by the fetus passing through the birth canal, expanding the local mucosa, fascia, and muscle tissues, resulting in relaxation of the vaginal wall, levator ani muscle, and related structures of the urogenital diaphragm. In severe cases, it can lead to a decline in sexual life quality and reduced sexual sensation. When the degree of relaxation in the female private parts already affects the quality of marital life, it actually causes significant physical harm to the woman and requires early treatment. What causes vaginal laxity after childbirth? Increasing age and declining estrogen levels: the vaginal fascia, ligaments, and related support structures undergo inevitable degenerative changes, reduced elasticity, thinning fascia, and simultaneous atrophy of the vaginal mucosa, which worsens vaginal relaxation. Another reason is that normal women in the mid to late stages of pregnancy experience significant relaxation of vaginal ligaments and smooth muscles. This is a natural physiological evolution. During natural childbirth, when the baby passes through the vagina, the vagina expands significantly, and elasticity inevitably decreases. The more children born, the greater the degree of relaxation. Even if a cesarean section is chosen, the vagina will be looser than before pregnancy. What other obvious symptoms does vaginal relaxation have? 1. Frequent vulvar itching: Vaginal relaxation can easily allow harmful bacteria to invade, causing intense vaginal itching that is hard to bear, making it difficult to sit still, and affecting work and life. 2. Vaginal dryness and discomfort: Vaginal dryness is a symptom of vaginal relaxation. No matter how much foreplay is done before marital life, the vagina remains extremely dry, causing suffering for both parties. 3. Vaginal gas or noise: Vaginal gas, also known as 'vaginal flatulence,' means the vagina makes sounds, which can be very embarrassing. What to do about vaginal relaxation? If vaginal relaxation occurs, it can be improved through physical therapy OR surgical treatment. Physical therapy: includes independent Kegel exercises combined with biofeedback, electrical stimulation therapy, and laser therapy for the pelvic floor muscles. This is recommended for women whose relaxation is not severe. When vaginal relaxation is severe, surgical treatment is recommended for more obvious results.

Title: Is it necessary to conduct nucleic acid testing for the entire population? Expert from the State Council's Joint Prevention and Control Mechanism: Not needed. Content: Is it necessary to conduct nucleic acid testing for the entire population? Expert from the State Council's Joint Prevention and Control Mechanism: Not needed. Recently, Wuhan launched a city-wide nucleic acid screening "Ten-Day Campaign" for the novel coronavirus. On the evening of the 14th, Feng Zijian, Deputy Director of the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention and expert from the liaison group of the State Council's Joint Prevention and Control Mechanism, appeared on the "News 1+1" program to discuss the situation regarding Wuhan's mass nucleic acid testing and respond to hot topics about cluster outbreaks. 1. What is the liaison group's assessment of Wuhan conducting mass nucleic acid testing? Feng Zijian: After Wuhan reported zero new confirmed cases on March 8, medical institutions have been continuously expanding the scope of nucleic acid testing. During this period, positive cases have been detected daily, who are asymptomatic infections. Recently, another cluster outbreak occurred in Wuhan, indicating that the previous virus transmission in Wuhan had not been completely blocked. Wuhan's measure of conducting mass nucleic acid testing is a proactive action, involving significant social mobilization. 2. Can mass nucleic acid testing identify all potential patients? Feng Zijian: Expanding testing will certainly discover more asymptomatic infections. It must be understood that virus transmission is a dynamic process, while testing is completed at a single point in time. Therefore, it is difficult to completely identify all infected individuals or sources of infection through a one-time, single-point test. 3. According to reports, the cost of Wuhan's mass nucleic acid testing is about 2 billion yuan. If promoted nationwide, the cost would be about 280 billion yuan. Some analyses suggest that compared to the huge losses from the epidemic, the 280 billion yuan testing cost is bearable. Can mass testing be promoted nationwide? Will mass testing bring safety for all? Feng Zijian: First, nationwide mass testing is not necessary. Currently, China has deployed relevant arrangements with a very broad coverage, which can play a significant role in discovering potential sources of infection and infected individuals. Second, while expanding testing helps find potential sources of infection, besides considering economic and efficiency factors, our testing capacity must also be taken into account. Even if nationwide mass testing were conducted, it would not be possible to completely identify all sources of infection or infected individuals. 4. Are there more optimized plans for expanding the scope of nucleic acid testing? Feng Zijian: Currently, we are focusing the testing scope more precisely and targeting priority groups for testing. Old urban areas, communities densely populated by migrant tenants, urban-rural fringes, and residential areas around large markets can be prioritized for testing; in areas where positive cases or asymptomatic infections are found, the testing scope has also been expanded, which helps improve testing efficiency. Since the 9th, 6 local cases have appeared in Dongxihu District, Wuhan, Hubei Province, all in the same residential complex. The first patient was 89 years old, with a history of hypertension, cerebral infarction, and hepatic cysts, and had not left the complex since the Spring Festival. He experienced fever symptoms in March and self-medicated to recovery, but tested positive in the nucleic acid test in May. Subsequently, 5 close contacts were infected. 5. Was the 89-year-old patient in the Wuhan cluster outbreak the source of infection? Feng Zijian: In this cluster outbreak, there are 6 confirmed cases and 7 asymptomatic infections. Based on current analysis, this 89-year-old patient is the index case. His symptoms in March might not have been related to COVID-19, and he was likely infected in April. Through investigation, the first case was an asymptomatic infection discovered on April 25. He was a tenant living in a bungalow within the complex, a migrant worker in Wuhan, but the source of his infection remains undetermined. Analysis suggests that the first asymptomatic introducer brought the virus into the bungalow area, first infecting the wife of the 89-year-old patient. The elderly couple had frequent and active contact with this tenant, leading to the subsequent outbreak. 6. Recently, 6 new local cases were reported in Dongxihu District, Wuhan, and about 70,000 related individuals were scheduled for testing. What are the results? Feng Zijian: So far, 13 confirmed patients and positive cases have been identified, mainly concentrated in an old community in Dongxihu District. There is a bungalow in this community where migrant workers live as tenants; 10 of these positive cases are tenants from this bungalow. Additionally, 3 asymptomatic infections were found in two residential buildings adjacent to the bungalow, showing a focal distribution of cases. The risk of further spread from this outbreak is very low, and there is no need for overinterpretation or excessive worry. It's important to understand that expanding the testing scope is a process. In the early stage of this Wuhan cluster outbreak, testing primarily targeted close contacts of the confirmed cases or asymptomatic infections, as well as residents living very nearby. Based on this, the testing scope was then expanded to the residential complex where the affected bungalow is located and related personnel in the surrounding area, including a very large building materials market. Overall, the total number of tests is very large, approximately 60,000 to 70,000 people, and 20,000 to 30,000 tests have been completed so far. Currently, all test results are negative, and no new asymptomatic infections or positive cases have been detected.

Title: Besides electrocardiogram examination, what other methods can diagnose heart problems? Content: A Chinese friend living in Sweden is not in good health. Coincidentally, her husband had an opportunity to work in Shanghai, so she accompanied him back to Shanghai. Before going to Shanghai, she first returned to Chengdu because her parents are there. Due to her poor mental state, she went to see a traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) practitioner in Chengdu to check for issues. After taking her pulse, the TCM practitioner said she had a heart problem. She couldn't believe it, and her doubtful expression was probably too obvious. The TCM practitioner noticed but still confidently told her that her heart indeed had a problem, and if she didn't believe it, he suggested she go to a Western medicine doctor for an examination. After arriving in Shanghai, she quickly went to what is considered the most advanced hospital in Shanghai for a check-up. Initially, the standard heart problem examination didn't detect anything. But she and her husband were still worried, so they underwent further examination, reportedly a color Doppler ultrasound. Finally, the heart problem was discovered: it turned out she had a small hole in her heart. Western medicine treatment had too many side effects, and she couldn't stand the bitter herbal decoctions of TCM treatment. Now she is resting at home and has no major issues, but she cannot overexert herself.

Title: Stepping Hard on the Gas vs. Driving Slowly – Which Driving Habit Is More Damaging to the Car? Content: Many people believe that stepping hard on the gas is more damaging to the car, especially to the engine, while gently pressing the accelerator is friendlier to the engine. In reality, engines are not as fragile as one might think. Everything you can imagine, car manufacturers have already considered in advance. During the R&D phase, manufacturers design engine usage based on the most extreme conditions. It is commonly thought that stepping hard on the gas is unfriendly to the engine, as it causes the engine RPM to spike instantly, increasing wear on the piston, connecting rod, and crankshaft. However, these are just subjective perceptions. My first job was in engine design at an OEM. Regarding whether stepping hard on the gas damages the engine, let me explain how we conduct durability tests. The engine is placed on a test bench, ignited, and the RPM is adjusted to 5000-6000. It then runs continuously for 800 hours without stopping. This is the engine's durability test. 800 hours, converted into mileage, far exceeds 240,000 kilometers. After the test, the engine is disassembled, and each component is analyzed and inspected for any issues. If problems are found, we trace back to the design to check for flaws. If design changes are needed, we modify the design and continue testing the components. If it's not a design issue, we check for matching problems. In short, every component must be rigorously analyzed to identify and resolve issues. Taking the engine as an example, how many ordinary consumers who buy a fuel-powered car can actually rev the engine beyond 5000 RPM? Most cars today are automatic transmissions, which usually shift gears around 2500 RPM. Unless it's a manual transmission, where you can rev it to the redline. For ordinary family cars, engine RPM exceeding 4000 is considered high. As for the wear on piston rods from stepping hard on the gas, there's no need to worry. Engines are lubricated; the engine oil we regularly change is the lubricant. (Image from the internet, can be deleted if infringing) There is an oil pump in the oil pan that pumps oil from the pan into the main oil passage, flowing to the camshaft, valves, and timing pulley in the cylinder head, lubricating them. The piston, connecting rod, and crankshaft are all lubricated. Any mechanical moving part in the engine is lubricated. The oil pump is usually driven by the crankshaft or balance shaft, mostly connected by gears. This means that as long as the engine is running, the oil pump is also operating. When the engine RPM increases, the oil pump speed also increases, raising the oil pressure. When the engine RPM decreases, the oil pump speed slows down. (Image from the internet, can be deleted if infringing) Therefore, even if you step hard on the gas, the oil pump responds accordingly, providing timely lubrication to the engine's moving parts. So, there's no need to worry about engine wear from stepping hard on the gas. What actually accelerates engine wear is failing to change the oil promptly. Additionally, some fuel vehicles have tachometers that show a maximum of 8000 RPM, while others show 9000 RPM. However, many engines cannot reach the maximum RPM displayed on the tachometer. Why? Because engine calibration restricts it, preventing the engine from reaching the tachometer's maximum value. Any RPM that your engine can reach is safe. If there were issues, calibration would restrict it. If it's not restricted, it means there's no problem. Personally, I believe stepping hard on the gas does not damage the engine. As for transmissions, I think manual and AT transmissions are fine. However, for CVT transmissions, there are reports of owners breaking the steel belt inside by stepping hard on the gas. The only potential damage I can think of is accelerated tire wear. Also, stepping hard on the gas is often followed by hard braking, which accelerates brake pad wear. But tires and brake pads are aftermarket parts that require regular replacement. This isn't considered damaging the car—it's just accelerated wear. (Image from the internet, can be deleted if infringing) Moreover, as long as the car is regularly maintained and aftermarket parts are replaced on schedule, it won't break down. During R&D, we consider extreme conditions. Things like stepping hard on the gas or brakes are trivial. Engine technology has been developing for over 100 years and is very mature. By the way, if you drive too slowly, the engine is prone to carbon buildup, which is not good. It can lead to higher fuel consumption and reduced power.

Title: What kind of job is considered a good job in Xi'an? Content: Working within the system, I was resting at home this week after testing positive for COVID, and I've been thinking about this question. When I took the exam for this unit, the competition was fierce. Ultimately, two of us succeeded, both with master's degrees from very good universities. After joining the unit, I found that my colleagues also graduated from good schools, with several from Peking University. However, the salary is just average and very transparent. The older colleagues had the benefit of housing allocation several times in the past, and now they have high pensions. We, on the other hand, missed out on all those benefits. Some of my classmates pursued PhDs and are under great pressure; others joined big tech companies – I'm quite envious of their high salaries, but they have to work on Saturdays as well. Since I started working, I've been doing investment and financial management in my spare time. I've been lucky these past few years, earning more from investments than my salary, but it's unstable. Sometimes I make a few thousand in a day, sometimes I lose a few thousand. It's hard to predict future market trends. Anyway, perhaps my ability level isn't high enough, but so far I haven't seen any job that is perfect with only advantages...

Title: Wenzhou Municipal People's Congress Representatives Investigate the Construction of Wenzhou Buddhist College (Women's Section) in Lucheng District Content: Wenzhou Municipal People's Congress Representatives Investigate the Construction of Wenzhou Buddhist College (Women's Section) in Lucheng District Time: 2015-01-19 0:00:00 Source: Wenzhou Municipal Ethnic and Religious Affairs Bureau View Count: 23 Font Size: [Large, Medium, Small] On January 15th, a delegation of Wenzhou Municipal People's Congress representatives went to Lucheng District to investigate the construction progress of the Wenzhou Buddhist College (Women's Section). They also carried out a special promotional campaign titled 'Working Together in Unity, Building Harmony.' Wu Haiyan, Director of the Lucheng District People's Congress Standing Committee, and District Chief Zhu Chongmin, among others, accompanied the delegation. The investigation team carefully listened to the work report on the construction of the Wenzhou Buddhist College (Women's Section), inquired in detail about the difficulties and problems encountered by Taiping Temple during the construction process, and conducted an on-site inspection of Taiping Temple's construction status. The investigation team fully affirmed the achievements made by Taiping Temple in the past year. They also proposed three 'Xin' (Hearts/Minds): First,要有 'Heng Xin' (Perseverance). The construction of Wenzhou Buddhist College is a significant project with far-reaching impact, crucial for promoting the new development of Wenzhou's culture and economy. Everyone must be prepared for a long-term effort and steadily advance the work of the Buddhist College. Second,要有 'Jue Xin' (Determination). With the determination to perfectly complete the construction of Wenzhou Buddhist College (Women's Section), plans should be formulated and meticulously organized. Using the special activity 'Working Together in Unity, Building Harmony' as a focus, resources should be integrated, and the strength of religious believers should be consolidated, uniting everyone into one force, working together with one heart to overcome difficulties and resolutely complete the construction of Wenzhou Buddhist College as early as possible. Third,要有 'Xin Xin' (Confidence). Building on the existing work foundation, summarize the work and identify problems. Particularly regarding the site selection for the Buddhist College (Women's Section), high importance must be attached, ensuring meticulous attention at every step and implementation at every level. Confidence should be established,敢于直面困难 (daring to face difficulties directly), solve key problems, and ensure the smooth completion of the Wenzhou Buddhist College (Women's Section).

Title: Untitled Content: For the Spring Festival travel season, distance needs to be considered. If the distance is moderate, the current range of electric vehicles can basically meet the requirements, and whether charging or battery swapping, neither has much impact on the driving experience. For long-distance travel, the coverage of battery swap stations currently cannot compare to that of charging piles. Considering NIO's current profitability, it is foreseeable that it still won't be able to compare to charging piles in the future. Even if it becomes profitable, charging piles are implemented by multiple companies, while there are only one or two companies operating battery swap stations, so it still can't compare. If extended-range and fuel vehicles are included, then it has even less advantage.

Title: Luobo Kuaipao Explodes with Orders, Where Should Ride-Hailing Go? Content: First, the promotion of Luobo Kuaipao won't happen that quickly. Currently in Wuhan there are only a few hundred vehicles, accounting for only a small portion of ride-hailing and taxis. Now that public opinion is争议, the pace may slow down further. So, the question of where 10 million ride-hailing and taxi drivers should go does not exist; this is a very slow process, not like the sudden unemployment of tens of millions of state-owned enterprise workers or internet education and training大厂裁员. Second and more importantly, autonomous driving will create a large number of new jobs, such as safety officers, or traffic order maintenance personnel mentioned by other respondents. It is imaginable that as Luobo Kuaipao becomes more普及, demand in this area will increase. Young veteran drivers with strong learning abilities may also find转行 a good choice. Those who can drive taxis or ride-hailing cars but are too old to adapt to new technology can be inferred to have been in this line for quite a while, and their economic pressure does not seem that great (those with disappointing children are not within the scope of discussion). Combining the above two points, this is inevitably a slow replacement process of良性进步 and will not be a very serious socio-economic problem. Current public opinion is clearly over-interpreting. Nevertheless, this is not the main point; many people's views are simply wrong. In terms of ethics and morality, Luobo Kuaipao is definitely social progress, and whether from the perspective of the poor or the rich, it should be supported with both hands. Ride-hailing and taxi driver is not a good profession; if technology can replace it, it is a great step forward for human progress. In fact, driving for more than ten hours a day is very tiring, and many drivers have occupational diseases. Using technology to gradually eliminate drivers, this mechanized labor工种, will definitely increase overall social welfare. As for those who cannot become safety officers or adapt to new occupations, they can change careers, or the government can levy a special transformation cost tax on such autonomous driving companies to compensate these people; this is a matter of government distribution. More importantly, in an economic sense, if Luobo Kuaipao can promote the advancement of autonomous driving technology and free up driving time, using commute time multiplied by the number of commuters, this will be a huge social liberation. Furthermore, if the普及 of autonomous driving makes commuting less painful, and with auxiliary transportation systems greatly improving the efficiency of the entire transportation system, from the perspective of commuting, people won't have to crowd into the city center, and one-way commutes of over 50km will no longer be an obstacle. Our urban form will therefore undergo tremendous changes. Other main doubts also don't hold water: Why do internet giants always come to steal poor people's business? This seems reasonable at first glance, but actual analysis shows it is a朴素认知 that doesn't make sense. From a market perspective, if technological progress leads to reduced income or even unemployment for ride-hailing drivers, these former practitioners should learn new career tracks. The simplest example is becoming a safety officer for autonomous vehicles, rather than calling for blocking technological progress (although this is cruel, if individuals don't work hard, society won't progress; no one has a reason to eat for free). If they can't find work locally, they can go to big cities or even abroad; market price signals will play a corresponding role. For those who are old, weak, sick, or disabled and cannot keep up with social progress, this should be the scope where social security plays a role, not simply restricting the application of enterprise technology; these are two different levels of issues. The direction of technological progress itself is difficult to plan. It is hard to say which areas technological progress should serve and which it should not. For example, games have caused many teenagers to waste their studies, but who would have thought they promoted the development of AI technology? Autonomous driving is one of the most mature application fields of AI; if China doesn't do it, other countries will try. To take a step back, driving for more than ten hours a day is very tiring, and many drivers have occupational diseases. Using technology to gradually eliminate drivers, this mechanized labor工种, will definitely increase overall social welfare. Many drivers should consider changing careers or having social security provide a safety net. What does autonomous taxi have to do with ordinary people? In the long run, technological progress will definitely be able to improve social production efficiency, thereby enhancing the welfare of底层人民. After all, today many people enjoy a high quality of life that even emperors and nobles of the past could not enjoy. Today the average life expectancy is over 70, which was unimaginable in ancient times. After the普及 of autonomous driving, the time drivers free up from driving can be used for more meaningful things, such as meditation, daydreaming, or even reading and watching movies. For most people, any of these would be more meaningful than driving. For passengers, taking a taxi is cheaper, and the money saved can be used to buy good food or nice clothes; this is definitely an improvement in welfare. Economics focuses on efficiency; politics is the business of politicians. They should be distinguished (although in reality they cannot be separated). The primary stage of socialism should still first consider making the cake bigger. Is Baidu now grabbing the market with low prices, and will it charge passengers high prices after monopolizing the market in the future? The best reference for this is shared bicycles. Previously there were so many shared bicycle companies, and in the end only two or three remained. Are they now charging high prices to割韭菜? I believe most people can still feel that even though shared bicycle prices have risen somewhat, they are still very helpful for our travel. Not to mention that new entrants and the competition from ride-hailing and taxis will always exist, constraining the power of any single company.

Title: DHL Express Customs Clearance How to handle DHL international shipments stuck in customs clearance status_Baidu Knows Content: If a DHL international shipment remains in customs clearance status, the first step is to confirm the specific customs clearance situation with the recipient. If there is a customs clearance delay, the local DHL will notify the recipient of the relevant issues. It is recommended to contact the recipient to confirm if they have received a notice from DHL and to assist in resolving the customs clearance problem. Due to time differences and customer service allocation issues, responses from the local DHL might be slow, so contacting the recipient directly is more efficient. Secondly, if the recipient's information is incorrect or they cannot be contacted for other reasons, accurate recipient information needs to be provided again. Ensure the recipient can be contacted promptly; the DHL company will send the information to the local DHL to arrange for customs clearance. At the same time, notify the recipient to contact the local DHL directly, as this can confirm the information more quickly. Additionally, factors such as incorrect recipient details or holidays can cause customs clearance delays. If this happens, it is advised that the recipient provides correct contact information and replies to DHL as soon as possible to facilitate timely handling of the customs clearance issue. If the recipient cannot reply promptly, accurate contact information should be provided quickly to avoid further delays. In summary, when dealing with DHL international express customs clearance issues, you should first communicate with the recipient to confirm information, provide accurate recipient details, and maintain smooth communication to speed up customs clearance. Meanwhile, the DHL company will also fully assist in tracking the shipment's status to ensure smooth customs clearance.

Title: Should Special Forces-Style Family Trips Be Promoted? What Are the Pros and Cons? Content: Should special forces-style family trips be promoted? What are the pros and cons? Recently, more and more people have begun to advocate for special forces-style family trips. This type of travel not only emphasizes physical exercise and building perseverance but also brings family members closer together. However, is this method suitable for all families? What are its advantages and disadvantages? Pros: Exercise Body and Willpower Individuals with a special forces background typically possess high physical fitness and strong willpower, along with rich experience in dealing with and arranging for difficult situations. Family trips can exercise the body, enhance cooperation among family members, and train the family's psychological resilience when facing difficulties. Cons: High Safety Risks However, special forces-style family trips also carry significant safety risks that cannot be ignored. Accidents are hard to avoid during outdoor travel. Once an accident occurs, the consequences could be irreversible. Pros: Strengthen Family Bonds Special forces-style family trips can also bring family members closer together. When sharing the hardships and dangers of the journey, family bonds are more easily deepened, and the默契 (tacit understanding) and trust among family members become more apparent when facing challenges. Cons: High Time Cost Special forces-style family trips usually require more time and extensive preparation. Not only does it take more time to plan the itinerary and train physically, but it also necessitates purchasing more professional equipment and medicines, thereby increasing both the time and financial costs of the trip. In summary, special forces-style family trips have both advantages and disadvantages. Families should weigh the pros and cons based on their own circumstances and travel purposes to decide whether to adopt this approach. Adequate preparation must be made before the trip, and safety during the journey must be ensured.

Title: Barber shop owner stops urban management officer from tearing down advertisement at shop entrance, gets finger bitten during conflict; Party involved: Other shops have posted advertisements, why only tear down mine? Lanzhou police response. Content: "I don't understand, other shops are posting them, why target me?" said Mr. Zhang from Lanzhou, Gansu, puzzled. He hopes the urban management officers will apologize for the law enforcement error of "biting the finger." On September 28, Huashang Bao Dafeng News learned from the local police station that the urban management law enforcement officers were not wearing body cameras and mistakenly believed the merchant's obstruction was an assault, thus triggering the conflict. Online Video – Physical altercation between urban management officers and street-side shop. On September 25, a video about a conflict between urban management officers and a street-side merchant spread online, attracting attention. In the video, personnel wearing urban management law enforcement uniforms push a red-haired man into a corner, with a woman nearby seemingly trying to mediate. Then, another uniformed person comes up the steps, and pushing and shoving ensues between the two sides. During this, a man in yellow nearby grabs the red-haired man's hair and pulls. Pushed by the two uniformed personnel, the red-haired man loses his balance and falls. The man kicks repeatedly, after which the uniformed personnel disperse. Many onlookers are present at the scene. After being separated by people around, the red-haired man squats on the ground, and one uniformed person holds his forehead. At this point, the red-haired man suddenly picks up a brick nearby, which is seemingly taken away by someone around. Subsequently, the red-haired man rushes forward and punches a uniformed person. People around mediate and separate the two sides again. The video poster claimed the incident occurred in Lanzhou, Gansu, and the merchant complained that he was bitten on the finger by an urban management law enforcement officer. Account from the Party Involved – Conflict with multiple urban management officers after refusing to tear down advertisement; "One person bit the little finger of my right hand." On September 28, Huashang Bao Dafeng News contacted Mr. Zhang, the red-haired man in the video. He said he is the owner of a barbershop in Lanzhou. Around October 2024, after opening his shop here, urban management officers often came demanding the removal of advertisements. "Before it was poster stands, which were frequently confiscated, so later I posted them on the shop's glass and walls." "I posted advertisements mainly because many shops around have placed poster stands at their entrances and posted advertisements near their doors. Secondly, the customer flow in my shop is low, I'm anxious, and I think posting a price list or similar is quite normal," Mr. Zhang explained. The conflict occurred around 1:33 PM on September 24. Mr. Zhang said several urban management officers came along the street at that time, some in uniform, some not. When they reached his shop door, they told him to tear down the advertisement at the entrance. "I retorted, so many shops around have posted them, and there are stalls on the street, why target me?" Subsequently, four people came forward one after another, trying to tear down the advertisement, but he stopped them, leading to a conflict between the two sides. "During the whole process, I was bitten on the little finger of my right hand by a heavier-set law enforcement officer," Mr. Zhang said. After being sent to the hospital, he was diagnosed with an "open hand injury." "Eighty percent of my nail is broken, but fortunately, the check-up showed no infection." Surveillance Video – After pushing and shoving, two law enforcement officers fall down the stairs. "After he let go of my finger, he fell down the steps while stepping back." According to the surveillance footage Mr. Zhang obtained from a nearby shop, at 1:34 PM, two uniformed personnel arrived at Mr. Zhang's shop entrance. A man in yellow seemingly raised his phone to record. About 14 seconds later, Mr. Zhang came out of the shop. After about 50 seconds of argument, the heavier-set man went up the steps to continue the dispute. At 1:35:30 PM, two uniformed men stepped forward, seemingly to remove the advertisement at Mr. Zhang's shop. Presumably because Mr. Zhang tried to stop them, the man in yellow also went up the steps, and the three surrounded Mr. Zhang. At 1:36 PM, another man approached. At 36 minutes and 08 seconds, seemingly after being pulled, Mr. Zhang made a throwing motion with his hand, and pushing and shoving started. The heavier-set uniformed person fell to the ground from the steps, and a uniformed person behind him, seemingly unable to avoid in time, also fell. After the physical altercation, the two sides were separated by people around. About 10 seconds later, Mr. Zhang rushed down the steps and got into a physical altercation with the other side, and was again separated by people around. Mr. Zhang explained that after a group of people surrounded him, someone held his arm. "I don't understand why the heavier-set law enforcement officer bit my finger." "I cursed at him for biting, he let go and stepped back, rolling down the steps. The result is that they claim I pushed him down." Demand for Apology – "Other shops have posted advertisements, why only tear down mine?" "Right hand injury affects business, hope urban management apologizes." According to the hospital medical record, the physical examination showed soft tissue injuries throughout the body, accompanied by skin abrasions. Skin breaks were visible on the dorsal and ventral sides of the right little finger, deep to the muscle layer, covered with scabs. Outpatient diagnosis: Open hand injury. Photos provided by Mr. Zhang of the barbershop entrance show the damaged advertisement posted on the wall outside the shop, with a price list and words like "New Customer Experience Price" posted next to the door. Simultaneously, Mr. Zhang provided photos of advertisements and poster stands posted at the entrances of several nearby shops. He believes he was targeted by the urban management law enforcement officers. "These were taken after the incident. Why not tear down other shops', only mine?" Mr. Zhang said on September 28, he went to the hospital again. The doctor said more than twenty percent of his nail root was broken, but since there was no infection, it暂时 didn't need to be removed. "I cut hair for customers mainly with my right hand. Now injured, my business is definitely affected." He stated that despite his injury, the business must continue. "The shop is run by me and my wife. Our child is just over 1 year old, so we will still open for business." "I hope the urban management department enforces the law equally and apologizes to me for improper law enforcement such as biting the finger." Response from Related Parties – Urban management denies targeted enforcement, says both sides were hospitalized. Police: Urban management had no body cameras, case accepted and handled. On September 28, Huashang Bao Dafeng News contacted the Gaolan Road Urban Management Law Enforcement Squadron. A staff member said the police had already filed a case to investigate the matter, and surveillance videos etc. had been handed over to the police. Regarding the law enforcement officer "biting the finger," she said it was because Mr. Zhang did not cooperate with law enforcement and threw the first punch. "The police station will provide results later." Was it confirmed via body camera that Mr. Zhang struck first? The staff member did not directly reply, "I'm not clear if body cameras were worn. The leader is out on inspection now." Regarding Mr. Zhang's belief that the urban management officers targeted him, the staff member said they enforce according to work procedures. "We manage advertisements outside shops, banners, etc., not just his shop. Some comply when told, some don't cooperate, and sometimes disputes occur." On September 28, the responsible person at the local police station said the urban management officers were not wearing body cameras during law enforcement; they only took a few photos, no video recording. Based on analysis of surveillance video and other materials, when the urban management officers were tearing down the advertisement, Mr. Zhang made obstructing movements, which were mistaken by the other side as assault, hence the conflict occurred. "That's basically the process." "Obstructing law enforcement is inappropriate, but it doesn't involve urban management law enforcement officers assaulting the merchant," the responsible person explained. They have accepted the case but have not yet formally filed it. Subsequently, they will handle it according to law based on Mr. Zhang's injury condition. "Legal responsibility of the involved law enforcement personnel will be pursued based on the injury." Source: Dafeng News

Title: Wuwei's First Special Education School Opens
Content: Recently, Wuwei County's first special education school successfully completed the enrollment of first-grade freshmen and officially began classes. The Wuwei County Special Education School was officially established in May this year, located at the intersection of Kaifan Road and Changjiang Road in the southern new town of Wucheng, covering an area of 16 acres with a construction area of 3,500 square meters. Principal Wu Zhibin told reporters: 'Currently, the school has 2 administrative staff; 5 teachers teaching Chinese, mathematics, physical education, and art respectively; and 8 students, all children with intellectual disabilities, the youngest being only 7 years old and the oldest just 13, all enrolled in first grade.' According to reports, the purpose of establishing the special education school is to provide a school for all school-age children in the county with moderate to severe intellectual disabilities. Each classroom is equipped with an LCD TV all-in-one machine for teaching, allowing students to intuitively understand the knowledge taught by the teachers. The school has six functional and rehabilitation rooms for rhythm, sensory integration, Montessori, games, arts and crafts, and labor skills, providing strong support for the learning and rehabilitation of children with intellectual disabilities. Zhang Man, the homeroom teacher for these new students, said: 'In the first week, we did not teach textbook knowledge but focused on helping the new students adapt. We mainly emphasized getting along with the students, understanding each student's situation, and teaching them basic issues such as classroom discipline, safety education, behavioral habits, and learning habits. For example, they need to pay attention to safety when going up and down stairs, and they must never touch the plug and socket of the classroom cabinet air conditioner. We have to repeat these most basic things over and over again for them to possibly remember.' Zhang Man told reporters that the classes are now gradually getting on track. Although not very lively, the students are already able to pay attention to the teacher, unlike the beginning when only the teacher was performing a monologue. The knowledge taught focuses more on daily life, such as teaching children to recognize money in math class and teaching children to write their own names in Chinese class. 'They will eventually live together with normal people; what we need to teach them are mainly basic life skills.'

Title: Taohuajiang Town: Vegetable Farmer Couple Delivers 300 Jin of Vegetables for Free to Relocation Site for Poverty Alleviation Content: Dayiyang Client News (Correspondent Gao Chao) 'Attention, fellow villagers, stay at your respective doorsteps, fresh vegetables will be delivered to each household for free.' Early in the morning of February 2nd, a small truck loaded with various vegetables drove into the relocation site for poverty alleviation in Banjiazhou Community, Taohuajiang Town. Hearing that free vegetables were available, residents who had been 'holed up' at home to prevent the epidemic looked out from their windows. 'Staying home every day and unable to go out, we were almost out of vegetables. Thank you so much,' said Lan Jiahao, who had been in home isolation after returning from Wuhan, expressing continuous thanks after receiving the vegetables. However, the community cadres delivering the vegetables repeatedly waved their hands, saying that the real thanks should go to a couple. 'The two spent the whole day yesterday picking vegetables in the field, over 300 jin in total.' Under the introduction of Community Party Secretary Wu Yunhua, everyone learned that this full truck of vegetables was donated for free to the residents by Yao Guoliang, a member of the community's Party branch. Yao Guoliang and his wife make a living by growing and selling vegetables. Since the outbreak of the epidemic, residents have been staying indoors, and many outside shops have closed. Seeing that many impoverished households who had just moved in at the end of last year were already financially strained and unfamiliar with the area, he decided to give them the vegetables he originally intended to sell. 'How scarce vegetables are now! Yao Guoliang is giving them away instead of selling them. Truly remarkable!' Residents who learned the truth gave him a thumbs-up. 'As a Party member, I am just fulfilling my responsibility.' After loading the vegetables onto the truck with the community cadres, Yao Guoliang hurried back to the residential group to busy himself with promoting epidemic prevention and control. Title: 【The Party Flag Flies Red on the Epidemic Prevention Frontline】All for the Health and Safety of the Masses—A Record of the Epidemic Prevention and Control Work of the Fifth Traffic Police Brigade Content: Learn More News Information NEWS In the warm spring of March, the usual tranquility of our beautiful island was broken by the epidemic! Facing this severe test, the entire Fifth Traffic Police Brigade was mobilized, united as one,坚守岗位 (held their posts firmly), and "疫"无反顾 (advanced unhesitatingly against the epidemic), building a "copper wall and iron bastion" for epidemic prevention and control in the Beidaihe District. As the epidemic struck, the Party General Branch of the Fifth Traffic Police Brigade quickly activated emergency work mechanisms, concentrating all forces into a frontline "array." All officers and auxiliary police投入疫情防控斗争 (threw themselves into the epidemic prevention and control struggle) with the fastest speed, shortest time, and strongest resolve. They worked with health departments on joint prevention, control,排查检查 (screening and inspections),坚守岗位 24 hours a day, providing strong support to win the battle against the epidemic. Shouldering the heavy responsibility of epidemic prevention and control, the Fifth Traffic Police Brigade deployed personnel scientifically and rationally, clarified work tasks, and strictly implemented a "fixed personnel, fixed post, fixed responsibility" work mechanism. Starting from March 23rd, they organized 60 elite police officers to be dispatched to 10 epidemic prevention checkpoints around the Beidaihe District, maintaining 24-hour uninterrupted duty, interpreting the iron-like loyalty and responsibility of traffic police in the new era with their unwavering steps. The leadership team of the Fifth Traffic Police Brigade performed their respective duties responsibly, commuting daily between the unit and the checkpoints. Officer Wang Zhijian, who has been in poor health, developed shingles during the anti-epidemic effort but始终坚持在工作岗位 (persisted in staying at his post), only going to the hospital for IV treatment during shift changes. Comrades urged him to take leave, but he said, "I am a Party member, I must be here at this time!" Four female auxiliary police officers, worried that lockdowns in their residential compounds would prevent them from working, resolutely left their young children in the care of their parents and lived and ate at the brigade just like their male counterparts. Veteran officer Zhang Haibin, who is due to retire next year,依然坚守在疫情防控卡口 (still坚守 (held fast) at the epidemic prevention checkpoint), using practical actions to stand his final watch. Initial heart is like a rock, mission is like steel! The epidemic is an order, prevention and control is a responsibility! Title: Some questions about Panasonic cameras. Content: I asked a friend to bring me a Panasonic FX77 from Japan, which is the FX78 in China. But because I can't understand the manual, I don't know how to charge the camera battery. Does it need to be charged for 8 to 12 hours the first time you use it, like a mobile phone battery? I would appreciate it if someone knowledgeable about this could give me an answer. Thank you! This is not necessary. Panasonic camera rechargeable batteries will automatically cut off when fully charged! You can't even charge it if you want to! And today's batteries are not like the old ones! I also use a Japanese Panasonic machine! There is a charger inside. I put the battery in, and when the battery is full, it automatically cuts off the power! The use and maintenance of the battery are exactly the same as those of a mobile phone battery. The camera battery is just a general lithium battery, the same as a mobile phone battery. However, since your camera was bought from Japan, there are some points that require special attention. Japan's circuit voltage is 110 volts, while China's is 220 volts. You need to buy a voltage converter. A small transformer, you can go to a computer mall or camera mall to ask. Never connect it to the circuit rashly, it will burn out. If it's hard to find, check on Taobao. Also, is your machine the Japanese version? Bought in Japan doesn't necessarily mean it's the Japanese version. You can check the information on the battery. If it says 110v, it means you need to buy a transformer.
