Title: Can IVF choose twins? Content: The probability of having twins through IVF is higher because in some cases, to increase the success rate, doctors will implant two embryos. However, whether the mother can carry twins also depends on her physical condition. Twin pregnancies carry certain risks. The uterus is like an egg; originally, the space and nutrients inside are only enough for one chick. Squeezing might support two at most. Any more, and either the eggshell will burst, or the chicks will suffocate before growing up. Similarly, for IVF patients, the uterine blood supply and volume are just right for a single fetus. In multiple pregnancies, embryos may suffer from insufficient nutrients and poor development in the early stages; miscarriages and abortions are more likely in the mid-term; and in the late stages, fetal demise and uterine rupture are more common. Single or double embryo transfer? Do I have the final say? - MOON FLOWER's article - Zhihu

Title: Urgent Reminder! Some People Have Already Fallen Victim Content: While working hard, you suddenly receive a call from the "Social Security Bureau" claiming you are "involved in insurance fraud," and the "Public Security Bureau" will pursue your criminal responsibility. What would you do? Don't hesitate, hang up immediately—it's a scam call! A Hefei citizen received a call saying "I'm from the Social Security Bureau." On October 10, Ms. Yang, who lives in Yaohai District, received a call from an unknown number. The caller claimed to be from the Shanghai Social Security Bureau and asked if Ms. Yang had applied for a social security card on February 17. (The criminals are very familiar with the victim's personal information or delivery details, gaining trust by verifying information.) After Ms. Yang denied it, the caller said they would check for her and then transferred the call to another person. This person claimed to be from the Shanghai Public Security Bureau, stating that Ms. Yang was suspected of using fake medical records to commit insurance fraud. They even sent Ms. Yang an enforcement order with her photo attached, claiming that her social security card had been frozen and all her bank cards would be frozen soon. They demanded that Ms. Yang transfer her funds into her soon-to-be-frozen bank account for supervision. (By impersonating police officers, they pressure the victim, causing anxiety.) However, the "officer" then told Ms. Yang that if it wasn't her doing, they could help her contact a "bank section chief" to apply for a quick unfreezing with the court. (First, they threaten to arrest the victim, then offer a way to clear suspicion, making the victim rely on the scammer's instructions.) To prevent Ms. Yang from making mistakes, the caller "considerately" asked her to download a screen-sharing app and send her personal information, bank card number, and password to the bank's official customer service number. This way, the "bank section chief" could check her bank transactions. (Asking the victim to send bank card information to the official number lowers their guard, but sending the message is just a pretext—the real goal is to obtain payment details via the screen-sharing app.) After following the instructions, Ms. Yang found her funds stolen and reported it to the police. Common Social Security Scam Tactics: Tactic 1: "Your social security card has been suspended due to abnormal activity." Scammers send fraudulent messages posing as social security or medical insurance staff, claiming the card will be terminated, needs upgrading, or that electronic card approval failed, asking for personal information or directing victims to transfer money to specified accounts. Tactic 2: "Your social security/medical insurance card has been fraudulently used elsewhere." Scammers send messages stating the card was misused in another location, the case has been transferred to authorities due to large amounts involved, and request fund transfers to "secure" accounts. Tactic 3: Using fake documents or "preferential policies" as bait. Scammers forge documents or pose as social security staff offering "discounted" enrollment policies, luring victims via phone or text to apply for cards and transfer money under false pretenses. Police Reminders: 1. Police do not handle cases via phone or online. 2. Handle social/medical insurance card applications or cancellations through official channels; do not trust calls from unknown numbers. 3. There is no "safe account" in police investigations, and they will never ask for transfers to specified accounts. 4. If someone calls claiming you violated laws, do not believe them; verify at a local police station if in doubt. 5. If scammed, preserve evidence and call 110 immediately. Title: What are the causes of cyanobacterial blooms, and what is the best way to handle them? Content: From an environmental perspective, the cause of cyanobacterial blooms is a pollution phenomenon resulting from increased nutrients like N and P in water bodies due to human activities, leading to excessive algal growth and disruption of the entire aquatic ecological balance. Cyanobacteria are prokaryotes, also known as blue-green bacteria, and are the simplest and most primitive type of algal organism. They are single-celled organisms without a nucleus, belonging to prokaryotes. Cyanobacteria become easily visible when they appear in cell colonies, which is what we commonly refer to as 'water blooms.' In China, the main species of cyanobacterial water blooms are Microcystis aeruginosa, visible to the naked eye as olive green or dark green, with cell diameters of 3-7um, possessing pseudovacuoles that allow them to float and sink freely in water. Cyanobacteria control technology targets water bodies with large-scale cyanobacterial growth by using micro-ecosystem restoration techniques to transfer, transform, and degrade pollutants in the water, thereby purifying the water and creating an environment suitable for the survival and reproduction of various organisms, rebuilding and restoring the aquatic ecosystem. By regulating the water's micro-ecosystem, it stimulates and accelerates the rapid reproduction of indigenous microorganisms, activates their activity, and controls the biodiversity and ecological community structure of the water body, providing human intervention and guidance to the micro-ecosystem within the water. This fundamentally restores the aquatic ecosystem and the water's self-purification capacity. The main technical approach is divided into the following three steps: 1. Source Control and Interception: Based on the specific conditions of different rivers, lakes, and reservoirs, propose professional interception solutions. For sewage not connected to the municipal管网, which cannot be intercepted in the short term and can only be discharged into the river, use specialized integrated sewage treatment equipment to address the issue. For situations where interception is incomplete, such as sewage leakage, use specialized sewage outlet processors to resolve the problem. 2. Internal Source Management: Depending on the sediment conditions of different rivers, lakes, and reservoirs, the main methods for sediment removal are physical dredging and ecological dredging. Physical dredging primarily involves using environmental dredgers and other physical equipment to remove sediment. Ecological dredging focuses on in-situ treatment, using biological agents to reduce the organic matter content and moisture content in the sediment. 3. Ecological Restoration: Mainly through comprehensive management techniques such as micro-ecosystem restoration technology, aquatic plants and animals (pollution-absorbing ecological floating islands, submerged vegetation, constructed wetlands, etc.), and aeration oxygenation to reduce the pollution load of the water body, restore a healthy aquatic ecosystem, and the water's self-purification capacity. After establishing a complete aquatic ecosystem, conduct后期运营维护 to achieve long-term clarity and cleanliness.

Title: Today, Huilai Reports 3 Close Contacts! Content: Notification on the Activity Trajectories of 3 Close Contacts in Huilai County. Title: Octogenarian Climbs onto Shed Roof to Rescue Cat, Suffers Serious Injuries Content: Recently, an 82-year-old elderly person in Suzhou risked climbing onto a simple shed roof to catch a cat, but fell from it, resulting in a very dangerous situation. At noon, the elderly person was urgently carried into the emergency room, with multiple wounds on the head and body that were still bleeding, making the situation quite critical. The elderly person's spouse explained that the injured person is surnamed Jiang and is already 82 years old. The spouse said that Mrs. Jiang likes to take in stray cats, so there are often many stray cats at home. At that time, for a cat that had climbed onto the shed roof, the elderly person risked climbing onto the simple shed, leading to the dangerous incident. Neighbors who saw it were terrified and quickly went to find community staff. More than ten community staff soon arrived at the scene, helped carry the elderly person out, and called an ambulance to take her to the hospital. It is understood that Mrs. Jiang has a daughter who was also recently hospitalized due to a car accident. Now, the spouse has to care for two injured persons, which is already very difficult. The community will try to assist in handling the multiple cats taken in by Mrs. Jiang. The fire department reminds that if you encounter cats or dogs going to dangerous places, you can seek help, but never try to catch them yourself, especially for elderly individuals.

Title: Why was the company suddenly listed as abnormal in industry and commerce? How to remove it? Content: Four common situations of industry and commerce abnormalities. Accidentally discovered that my company is showing as abnormal in industry and commerce. May I ask what the situation is? How to resolve it? For a normally operating company that suddenly becomes "abnormal in industry and commerce," there are generally four situations: 1. Address Abnormality: This occurs when the company cannot be contacted through its registered address or business premises, leading to its inclusion in the list of abnormal business operations. The industry and commerce department periodically sends letters or calls the contact information on the registration address during its duties. If no one receives the company's mail or answers calls, and it is confirmed that the company is not at that address, it will be deemed abnormal. The department may also send staff for on-site verification. If the address number doesn't exist or the company isn't there, it will be directly listed as abnormal. 2. Annual Report Abnormality: Failure to submit the annual report on time will cause abnormality. According to regulations, all enterprises established before December 31 of the previous year must submit their annual report between January 1 and June 30 of the current year, regardless of whether they have started operations or use independent accounting. 3. Failure to Publicize as Required: The industry and commerce department requires companies to publicize information such as shareholders' subscribed and paid-in capital, contribution times and methods, equity changes, administrative permits, intellectual property pledges, and administrative penalties. If a company fails to publicize within the stipulated period, it may be deemed as not fulfilling its obligation to disclose instant information and marked as abnormal. (Usually done during the annual industry and commerce report.) 4. False Publicized Information: If a company intentionally conceals its true situation or uses the company for fraud, and is discovered by the industry and commerce department, it will be listed as abnormal. If a company unintentionally becomes abnormal, it can generally be resolved by explaining the situation to the relevant department, providing clarification, and submitting relevant materials, without affecting the company. Risks of Abnormal Status to the Company: If the abnormal status is not addressed, what harms can it cause? 1. Affects Company Credit and Personal Credit: Once listed as abnormal, the company's status is visible to the public. Not only will partners question the company's credit, but the legal representative, shareholders, and supervisors will also be blacklisted, facing restrictions like high consumption limits, inability to get loans for housing or immigration, banned from flights and high-speed trains, and even unable to receive pensions. 2. Restricted Normal Loans: Information from the abnormal operations list is used by banks and financial institutions as a reference for loans, guarantees, insurance, etc. Companies on the list may be denied bank account openings or loans, hindering development. 3. Unable to Make Changes or Cancel: When a company is on the abnormal list, it cannot process changes or cancellations with the industry and commerce department, delaying progress. The owner must identify the cause of the abnormality, as different causes require different solutions. 4. Unable to Participate in Government Projects: Listed companies are affected by credit constraints, unable to participate in government procurement, project bidding, state-owned land use rights, or apply for honors. They may be restricted or banned. 5. Restricted Tax Matters: Cannot process tax changes, upgrade to general taxpayer, approve invoice types, set VAT limits, issue anti-counterfeiting tax controls, or receive invoices. 6. Abnormal Record: Even after removal, the abnormal record remains public on the Market Supervision Administration website and third-party query sites, affecting the company's image. 7. Revocation of Business License: If ignored, the worst outcome is revocation of the business license. Since abnormality causes so many problems, how to remove it? Read on. How to Remove Industry and Commerce Abnormality? For the situations listed above, how to remove the abnormality and what materials are needed? 1. Address Abnormality: If marked abnormal due to inability to contact via registered address, apply for a change of address or prove contact can be re-established. Submit relevant materials to the local industry and commerce department, which will decide within 5 days of verification. Materials required if address has changed: (1) Application for removal from abnormal list, (2) Proof of company representative or agent, (3) Original business license and stamped copy; ID of legal representative or agent, (4) Notice of approval for change of registration (address), (5) Others (as required by the department). If contact can be re-established: (1) Application, (2) Proof of representative, (3) License and ID, (4) Relevant proofs (lease contract, property certificate, etc.), (5) Others. 2. Annual Report Abnormality: If marked abnormal for late annual report, submit the missing report and publicize it. Then apply for removal with materials. Decision within 5 working days. Materials: (1) Application, (2) Proof of representative, (3) License and ID, (4) Explanation of report submission (with screenshot/stamped copy), (5) Others. 3. Failure to Publicize as Required: If marked abnormal for not disclosing instant information, fulfill the obligation first. The department will decide within 5 working days after publicity. Materials: (1) Application, (2) Proof of representative, (3) License and ID, (4) Relevant proofs (corrected information and commitment), (5) Others. 4. False Publicized Information: If marked abnormal for false information, correct the information and apply for removal. Decision within 5 working days of verification. Materials: (1) Application, (2) Proof of representative, (3) License and ID, (4) Application for annual report data correction, (5) Relevant proofs (corrected information and commitment; may require capital verification report, audit report, etc.), (6) Others. Title: Major Event! Are 400 Million Home Slaves "Destroying" China's Economy? Some Experts Bluntly State: China's Consumption is Worse Than India's Content: How high are housing prices now? Let's refer to a set of housing price data released by Anjuke. As of 2021, the average housing price in 4 domestic cities has exceeded 50,000 yuan. These four cities are Beijing, 59,123 yuan/㎡; Shenzhen, 56,612 yuan/㎡; Shanghai, 53,541 yuan/㎡; and Xiamen, 50,017 yuan/㎡. Currently, the housing prices in the vast majority of cities have entered the "ten-thousand yuan" era. It is worth mentioning that even in many of China's county towns, housing prices are "advancing rapidly." In May 2021, Xinhua News Agency "criticized" the current high housing prices in Chinese county towns. According to relevant statistics, there are a total of 103 county towns nationwide where housing prices exceed 10,000 yuan, and the one leading the county town housing prices is Lingshui County in Hainan. According to data from Hainan Province, as of the first quarter of 2021, the average commodity housing price in Lingshui, Hainan was 29,343 yuan/㎡. In contrast, the average sales price in Haikou City, the provincial capital of Hainan, from January to May was 17,211 yuan/㎡. The high housing prices make the "dream of buying a home" unattainable for many families. It's important to know that the general salary level in China is still not very high, especially when faced with high housing prices, it seems somewhat "insufficient." According to data from the National Bureau of Statistics, as of the first quarter of 2021, the median disposable income of urban residents was 11,090 yuan; however, this per capita disposable income is hardly enough to buy even one square meter, so taking out a bank loan has become the only way for most working-class families to buy a home. Are the 400 million people burdened with mortgages destroying China's economy? So how many people in the country are "burdened" with mortgages? According to incomplete statistics, approximately 400 million people in China are "burdened" with mortgages, accounting for about 30% of the total population. In order to buy a house of their own, many people are willing to exhaust their family's savings and even repay mortgages for up to 20 years. According to the outstanding real estate loan data released by the central bank, in the first quarter of 2021, the national outstanding real estate loans were 50.03 trillion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 10.9%; among these, the outstanding personal loans were 35.67 trillion yuan. Financial experts stated that the current household leverage ratio is as high as 72%. Since 2020, the debt ratio of Chinese families has further climbed. The International Monetary Fund stated that when the household sector leverage ratio exceeds 65%, it is highly likely to affect economic stability. In response, the Advanced Institute of Economics at Shanghai University of Finance and Economics released a report stating that as of February 2021, Chinese families had accumulated 15.5 trillion yuan in short-term loans and 49.1 trillion yuan in medium- and long-term loans, respectively. At a time when the global economy has not fully recovered to pre-pandemic levels, households burdened with large amounts of debt will not only weaken their liquid cash but also constrain consumer demand. So what is China's current household consumption rate? Economist Chen Yanbin stated that China's current consumption rate is only 39%, even lower than India's. It is important to note that India's GDP in 2020 was 2.62 trillion US dollars, while China's GDP was 14.73 trillion US dollars. However, India's household consumption rate is nearly double that of China, reaching 66%. Low household consumption rate? Mortgages are the "chief culprit." As mentioned above, because most of the cash in ordinary people's hands is used for loan repayment, coupled with the rising prices due to current inflation, the household consumption rate has decreased instead of increased. The well-known entrepreneur Cao Dewang said that even though China has a population of 1.4 billion, the number of people with spending power does not exceed 200 million. Furthermore, as more and more people "scrimp and save" to buy a house, the funds flowing into other industries will inevitably decrease significantly, which is actually detrimental to the development of the national finance. Thus, the "drawbacks" brought by high housing prices have gradually become apparent in society. In response, the state has been implementing relevant policies in recent years. For example, in 2016, the policy of "housing is for living, not for speculation" was responded to in major property markets, explicitly prohibiting the behavior of "property speculators." At the same time, to intensify efforts to curb the rising trend of housing prices, the "Three Red Lines" policy was fully implemented, and the state's regulatory efforts on real estate continued to tighten. In 2020, the fundraising amount of 50 mainstream real estate enterprises nationwide decreased by 64%. After financing tightened, the debt ratio of real estate enterprises decreased. According to the "Three Red Lines Status of Top 100 Real Estate Enterprises in 2020," the industry's net debt ratio dropped from 96% to 86%. Of course, besides the "Three Red Lines," the state also introduced the "Five Tiers of Mortgages" and "Concentrated Land Supply." With the "constraints" of these policies, the financing in the real estate industry gradually slowed down in the first quarter of 2021. According to data from the Shell Research Institute, in the first quarter, the financing of national real estate enterprises decreased by 23% year-on-year, with a total financing amount of 304 billion yuan. Now, housing prices are no longer "galloping." Under the "full swing" of multiple policies, houses will return to their residential attribute in the future. Once the real estate market begins to stabilize, it is believed that the funds in the hands of ordinary people will flow into more industries, on one hand increasing the household consumption rate, and on the other hand stabilizing the development of the national economy. What do you think about buying a house with a loan? Would you choose to buy a house with a loan? Welcome to share your thoughts. Title: What is zero down payment car purchase all about? Content: These things are taxed based on the invoice, and in reality, you'll end up paying more than what you spent when buying the car. There are two main types of cars on the market. One involves over-invoicing. If you buy a car worth 100,000 and apply for a loan of 10% of the invoice amount, I will increase the amount when issuing the invoice, so that 70% of the invoice amount is exactly your car's 100,000. It seems fine, and we seem to have made a lot of money, but when paying the purchase tax and insurance, you'll find the cost is higher because these are paid based on the invoice amount. If you can't even afford the down payment, it's recommended not to buy a car. Isn't that just putting on a brave face? Furthermore, there are many things to pay attention to when taking out a normal car loan: Be wary of secondary mortgages. Although this problem is rare, a preventive mindset is essential. Car owners should be vigilant that their car is not mortgaged twice by the dealer, leading to loan fraud. Don't be blinded by monthly payments that are too low. When car financial institutions advertise, they often don't state the interest rate directly but talk about monthly and daily payments to attract car buyers. It might not seem like much per day, but only by calculating the loan interest rate clearly will you know if your loan is worth it. Dealers will charge a handling fee. When buying a car, if you often get a loan through a dealer, they must charge a handling fee, which they keep for themselves. Fourth, negotiate the cancellation agreement before mortgaging. During the car mortgage loan process, the buyer might encounter situations where the loan approval is unsuccessful or relatively slow. At this point, the deposit has already been paid. If you want to cancel the order, in some cases, the dealer refuses to refund the deposit. Therefore, the buyer and seller should negotiate in advance. Timely loan repayment is very important. Be sure to pay attention to the monthly repayment date; don't think it's okay to be a day late. If the financial institution doesn't deduct the money, they will call the car owner to collect the loan within 3 days. Each call incurs a fee of 2300 yuan, plus interest, which unknowingly increases the loan cost. So, it's better to understand clearly before trying. For consumers, 'zero down payment' is never truly realized; it just converts the down payment into installments. According to the "Automobile Loan Management Measures," the amount of a loan for a personal vehicle issued by a lender cannot exceed 80% of the car's price, meaning the minimum down payment for a consumer car loan cannot be less than 20%. 'Zero down payment' is, in principle, impossible. This method involves the car finance company or dealership cooperating with the bank again, merely shifting the payment method. Car buying precautions: 1. Choose a reasonably priced model based on your family income. Select the model according to your family's needs, such as the car's purpose and the number of family members. 2. The car brand you purchase should preferably have high safety ratings and good value for money; appearance and personal preference come second. 3. Test drive the car at a 4S店 to assess its performance, price, and maintenance-related matters. After comparing several models, choose the one with the best value for money. 4. When picking up the car, you need to check the car's purchase invoice, vehicle certificate, triple guarantee service card, etc. For zero down payment car purchases, it is not recommended because the interest is particularly high, and there are many tricks involved, such as registering under a company name or lease-to-own schemes, which are common pitfalls. Buying a car online with a low down payment is acceptable, but choose options that register under a personal name. 蛋蛋-订车-A-P-P is good. It focuses on 0.5-1成 down payments and registers under a personal name, which is good. When buying a new car online, the down payment is generally 1成, meaning a low down payment of 10%. The down payment method varies depending on the car model. Zero down payment will have other fees; there's no such thing as a free lunch. It's better to use a legitimate platform for a low down payment.

Title: Smokers Use This to Brush Their Teeth! Dissolves 10 Years of Tartar, Eliminates Years of Bad Breath, Cleaner Than Dental Cleaning! Content: So embarrassing! You have no idea how much trouble smokers have - opening their mouth releases a sewer-like smell, smiling reveals a row of shiny yellow teeth. Sitting next to a beautiful woman or across from a boss, the other person subtly moves away. The situation is extremely awkward. They probably think you never brush your teeth! That's so unfair! Whether in daily life or the workplace, people often judge by appearance, or even "by teeth." Yellow teeth and bad breath can make people look down on you, even affecting work and life! At work, everyone prefers colleagues who are well-groomed and dressed appropriately. Similarly, white teeth are a symbol of positivity, conveying an upward work attitude. But a set of yellow teeth can ruin everything, instantly dropping your personal score to failing. Take blind dates, for example. No matter how excellent your personal conditions are, smelly yellow teeth are a key reason for rejection. Dental health is just that important. However, yellow teeth and bad breath caused by smoking are super hard to remove. Even brushing diligently every day doesn't work. Why is that? Is it the toothpaste or the toothbrush? Most people think teeth are smooth and flawless, but the truth might shock you. Look at the image above - doesn't it look like craters on the moon? Title: What would you do if you found a foreign object in your food at a restaurant? Content: It's best not to swallow a foreign object. If you have already swallowed it, some foreign objects can be passed out of the body with feces. However, if the object is metal, plastic, etc., you need to go to the hospital promptly to have it removed under the guidance of a professional doctor. If you accidentally swallow a foreign object like a date pit, you can eat vegetables rich in cellulose, such as spinach or celery. The ingested fiber can wrap around the foreign object, helping to reduce damage from sharp edges to the digestive tract. Usually, the foreign object can be passed with feces within 1-2 days. If the foreign object is plastic, it will not be digested or absorbed by the digestive tract and may be passed with feces after a few days, generally requiring no special treatment. If you swallow a foreign object like metal or heavy metal, you need to visit the ENT or gastroenterology department to determine the object's location in the digestive tract. If it is in the esophagus, stomach, or upper duodenum, it can be removed via endoscopy or laryngoscopy. If the object pierces the intestine, surgical intervention is needed to remove it via surgery. In daily life, do not swallow foreign objects casually, especially children must avoid putting various foreign objects in their mouths. Guardians should pay attention to strengthening supervision. When eating, we should not talk or play around to avoid swallowing unchewed food directly. If you accidentally swallow a foreign object and experience symptoms like difficulty swallowing or pain, you must go to the hospital for examination as soon as possible and let a professional doctor handle it.

Title: Are there any type restrictions on vaccination for adolescents? What should adolescents pay attention to after vaccination? - Taiyuan Local Treasure Content: > Q&A > Are there any type restrictions on vaccination for adolescents? Currently, COVID-19 vaccines are divided into three types: single-dose, double-dose, and triple-dose. Are there any type restrictions on vaccination for adolescents? Currently, the inactivated vaccine approved by the state for emergency use in people aged 3~17 requires 2 doses, with an interval of 3~8 weeks. Before adolescents are vaccinated, parents should further understand and grasp their children's health status and psychological state. During the vaccination process, according to the current needs of pandemic prevention and control and relevant local regulations, personal protection and that of accompanying personnel should be ensured. In addition, truthfully inform the vaccination doctor about the child's current health status and psychological tension, sign the informed consent form, and let the doctor judge whether vaccination is possible based on specific contraindication requirements. After the child is vaccinated, they should be observed for 30 minutes. If there is any discomfort, report it to the vaccination unit and seek medical attention if necessary. How to obtain a proof of contraindication for COVID-19 vaccination in Taiyuan? Persons applying for a proof of contraindication for COVID-19 vaccination need to submit their ID card and medical diagnosis materials issued by a secondary or above medical institution (including outpatient medical records, inpatient medical records, relevant examination and test reports, disease certificates, etc.). The evaluating doctor, after comprehensive judgment, will issue a proof of contraindication for COVID-19 vaccination for those who are indeed contraindicated; for those who are not contraindicated, no proof is needed, and vaccination is recommended. Issuing the proof of contraindication for COVID-19 vaccination is free of charge; if there is no relevant disease proof material, registration is required and relevant examinations will be conducted at one's own expense.

Title: Why is the leucorrhea like water, and is it harmful to the body? Content: Click the blue text to follow me. Women's physiological conditions are relatively special. For example, some female white-collar workers spend the whole day at work, and their bodies will eventually break down if this continues. Therefore, it is very common to experience some physiological problems. Recently, some women have asked why leucorrhea flows like water. This issue deserves attention. Normally, leucorrhea is a white, sticky substance. If leucorrhea flows out like water, it is medically called "watery leucorrhea." If it is obviously odorless, it is usually an early stage of gynecological inflammation. If it has a strange odor, it is seen in patients with advanced cervical cancer, vaginal cancer, or submucosal fibroids with infection. Q: Why does leucorrhea flow like water? A: Leucorrhea flowing out like water is usually a sign of gynecological inflammation. You should go to the hospital promptly to check which bacteria is causing it. The doctor will analyze the specific problem based on the examination results. ● Causes of abnormal leucorrhea ● 1. Heavy use of cleaning solutions: If women frequently douche the vagina, especially with cleaning solutions, lactobacilli will decrease, which disrupts the vaginal microecological balance and causes flora imbalance. 2. Long-term use of sanitary pads: Long-term use of sanitary pads is not breathable. Due to the high volume of leucorrhea secretions, the vulva is often in a moist state, which can irritate the local skin. This disrupts the vaginal balance and makes infection easy. 3. Poor hygiene, not changing underwear frequently: Women should change their underwear once a day, pay attention to personal cleanliness, and it is best to dry the washed underwear in the sun. Increased leucorrhea: If abnormal leucorrhea is not treated in time and not eradicated, serious sequelae can occur, such as gynecological inflammations like pelvic inflammatory disease and endometritis. In severe cases, terminal illnesses like vaginal cancer, uterine cancer, and cervical cancer can appear. Many middle-aged women who get cancer are due to not paying attention to abnormal leucorrhea when they were young. Furthermore, long-term insufficient leucorrhea weakens the vagina's self-defense function, making women susceptible to vaginitis. "Why does leucorrhea flow like water?" The above content is believed to provide an answer. Frequent use of cleaning solutions to wash the lower body and improper use of sanitary pads can easily lead to abnormal leucorrhea. If leucorrhea flows like water, you need to be even more vigilant. This is indeed quite serious. The most correct choice is to seek hospital treatment promptly. Title: Laptop mouse not working, touchpad can be used, restarting the mouse returns to normal. What's going on? Is it a mouse problem or a system problem? Content: After system restart, the mouse works fine without being replaced, so it must be a system issue. The touchpad and mouse are different; the mouse is an external device, while the touchpad is internally integrated. It might be an issue with the interface driver causing the mouse to malfunction. After restarting, the interface program returns to normal, and the mouse works again. It's like when the system freezes, and your computer becomes unusable, but after restarting, it's fine. It should be a system problem.

Title: How to Build a Park City - Citizens' Ideas Welcome Content: Recently, the Municipal Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau organized a media opinion communication meeting for the design plans of the Green Ecological Belt Construction Project on both sides of Jing Lake, and the Ecological Restoration and Functional Improvement Projects of Donghu Mountain and the Cultural Entertainment City, to report on the project's relevant situation. From May 7th to 11th, after the "Four Consultations with the People" study tour group in the city's construction field visited Chengdu, Yibin, Chongqing, and Nanchong for observation and learning, they actively provided suggestions and ideas. At the meeting, the Municipal Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau reported 36 sorted opinions and suggestions, including 22 for the Green Ecological Belt Construction Project on both sides of Jing Lake, 4 related to the Ecological Restoration and Functional Improvement Projects of Donghu Mountain and the Cultural Entertainment City, and 10 involving both Jing Lake areas, Donghu Mountain, and the Cultural Entertainment City. These opinions mainly suggested preserving the original facilities and landscapes without damage, adding new content on this basis, creating unique landscape attractions with Deyang characteristics, making these spots leisure destinations for citizens and check-in places for tourists, and meeting citizens' aspirations for a better life. The project responsible party and design party stated that 90% of the 36 opinions and suggestions proposed by the study tour members have been reflected in the preliminary design plan. They will try to incorporate these good suggestions into the design plan and welcome more and better opinions and suggestions from the public. The relevant person in charge of the Municipal Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau said that if citizens have suggestions or opinions, they can submit them by following the Deyang Housing and Urban-Rural Development WeChat public account, or from now until May 21st, they can provide them on-site to staff at 10 promotional locations including Wenmiao Square, Zhonggulou Square, the entrance of the Golden Coast residential area, and the square at the west end of Qingyijiang Road Bridge. Title: Can you still adhere to value investing when the market plummets? Content: During a market crash, value investors may face significant psychological pressure as their portfolio values are also affected by the market decline. However, if one is a true value investor, they should be able to stick to their investment philosophy. The core idea of value investing is to buy undervalued stocks and hold them until their value is correctly reflected by the market. Therefore, when the market falls, value investors see more opportunities because they can discover more undervalued stocks. In such situations, value investors should work harder to analyze stocks, seek out true value, and make appropriate investment decisions. At the same time, adhering to the investment plan and discipline is very important. Value investors should not be influenced by market sentiment and media, but should firmly follow their own investment plan and avoid impulsive trading. If they can remain calm and stick to their value investing strategy during a market crash, they have the potential to achieve long-term gains.

Title: Who is liable for compensation when a wall collapse during demolition injures a worker? Content: During renovation and construction, if a property owner hires unqualified personnel to carry out wall demolition work and an accident occurs resulting in worker injury, what legal liability will the owner face? Recently, the Qinbei District People's Court in Qinzhou City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region concluded a case regarding a dispute over compensation for harm to a service provider. The court legally ruled that the property owner bears 20% of the liability, while the unqualified worker bears 80% of the liability themselves. (Image source: internet, infringement deleted) In January 2024, Jiang contracted the work of building walls in the basement of a villa from the property owner, Wu, with Yi responsible for organizing the construction team. Yi then hired workers including Yue and He to carry out the wall-building work. During construction, the property owner Wu found that the layout of some existing walls was unreasonable and discussed demolition work with Yue, He, and others. Ultimately, both parties agreed that Yue, He, and others would be responsible for demolishing the walls and removing the construction waste, with Wu paying a remuneration of 5,000 yuan. On January 22nd, while He was performing the wall demolition work alone, he improperly used a method of demolishing from the bottom of the wall upwards, causing the wall to collapse. He, who was standing on scaffolding, was struck and fell to the ground, suffering multiple fractures including to his lumbar vertebrae and ribs. After the accident, He was hospitalized for 17 days and rested in bed for 3 months as prescribed by the doctor, incurring economic losses totaling over 68,000 yuan for medical expenses, lost wages, nursing costs, etc. A dispute arose over compensation, and He sued Jiang, Yi, Yue, and the property owner Wu, demanding that the four defendants jointly compensate for the losses. After hearing the case, the court held that Jiang contracted the wall-building work from Wu and arranged for Yi to hire Yue, He, and others for the construction work. Yue, He, and others did not directly contract the demolition work from Wu through Jiang or Yi. He was injured while performing demolition work, which was not directly related to the wall-building work contracted by Jiang and Yi. Therefore, Jiang and Yi were not at fault for He's personal injury and did not need to bear compensation liability. Regarding the demolition work, a contracting relationship was formed between the property owner Wu and Yue, He, and others, with Wu as the client and Yue and He as joint contractors. Yue was not at fault for the personal injury suffered by He and did not need to bear compensation liability. Wu, without verifying information such as the contractors' qualifications, entrusted the highly dangerous demolition work to He and others, who lacked safe production conditions and professional skills, failing in his duty of care and demonstrating clear fault in selection, and thus should bear corresponding compensation liability. He, fully aware that wall demolition involved certain dangers and that he himself lacked safe production conditions and professional skills, neglected his own safety, violated operating procedures, leading to the wall collapse and his injury, demonstrating clear fault and should bear the primary responsibility. Considering the respective degrees of fault and the causative contribution to the harm, the court determined that Wu should bear 20% of the liability and He should bear 80% of the liability himself, meaning Wu should compensate He over 13,000 yuan. Judge's Explanation: The Civil Code of the People's Republic of China stipulates that a contract for work is a contract whereby the contractor completes the work according to the client's requirements, delivers the work results, and the client pays the remuneration. Yue, He, and others completed the demolition work using their own equipment, technology, and labor, and Wu paid them remuneration, which conforms to the legal characteristics of a contracting relationship. In a contracting relationship, the client is generally not liable, and only bears several liability if there is fault in the commissioning, instruction, or selection. In this case, Wu was at fault in selecting He and others, who lacked safe production conditions and professional skills, for the highly dangerous demolition work; He, as a person with full capacity for civil conduct, improperly performed the bottom-up demolition work and failed to exercise due diligence, demonstrating clear fault. Therefore, both should bear corresponding responsibility. This case serves as a warning to property owners undertaking renovations and construction personnel. Owners should fulfill their duty of care during renovations, must hire qualified workers who meet physical and age conditions, and should not hire unqualified workers for the sake of convenience or cost savings to avoid unnecessary legal liability. Construction personnel also need to fulfill their duty of diligence during work, strictly adhere to safety operating procedures, be the primary responsible person for their own life and property safety, and avoid accidents. ▼For more information, long press|scan the QR code to follow © Shandong High People's Court Author: Wu Qi, Pang Ping Source: People's Court News Editor: Shi Hui Interviews with Chief Justices|Shandong High Court President Huo Min: Firmly Shouldering the Judicial Responsibility of 'Leading the Way and Carrying the Load', Supporting and Serving the Practice of Chinese Modernization in Shandong with High-Quality Development of Court Work. Title: Should jaywalking in Shenzhen affect personal credit loans and home purchases? What's your view? Content: A large-scale campaign targeting jaywalking by pedestrians and non-motorized vehicles is underway in Shenzhen. Recently, a relevant official from the Shenzhen Traffic Police Bureau revealed to the media that the bureau is collaborating with multiple credit agencies to establish a credit system for Shenzhen's traffic participants. The aim is to link traffic violations with personal credit loans, home purchases, and other aspects, thereby curbing traffic offenses like jaywalking. Title: Two Injured as Car Hits Tree on Maogang Road, Huangpu District After Collision Content: ■ A flatbed truck's front end pressed down on the car, with relevant personnel conducting an on-site investigation. Photo by Zhang Liang / Xinkuaibao News (Reporter Zhang Liang) Yesterday morning at 7:20, on Maogang Road in Huangpu District, a car was hit hard by a flatbed truck. It then broke a roadside fire hydrant and knocked down a large tree. A man and a woman in the car sustained serious injuries. The cause of the accident is under investigation. Around 9 a.m. yesterday, when the reporter arrived at the scene, they saw a flatbed truck stopped in the middle of the road with a dented front end. A tree about 40 cm in diameter was lying by the roadside, and a car was severely deformed, with the cabin stained with blood. Traffic police had cordoned off the scene, and traffic on nearby roads was moving slowly. An employee from a nearby store told the reporter: 'The car was preparing to make a U-turn when it was hit hard by the flatbed truck going straight. It was pushed onto the sidewalk, broke a fire hydrant, and then hit a large tree before stopping.' Eyewitness Mr. Zhang told the reporter: 'The female driver broke her leg, climbed out of the car by herself, and then collapsed on the ground. A man in the passenger seat was trapped in the car, unconscious. Firefighters arrived later and rescued him.' According to Huangpu District Hospital, both injured individuals are in serious condition. The police are further investigating the cause of the accident. (Informant: Mr. Zhang Reward: 50 yuan)

Title: Laid-off Worker Accused of Multiple Crimes After Raising Funds to Develop Land Enters Third Second-Instance Trial After Two Remands for Retrial Content: Zhu Guizhi, a laid-off worker from Yongcheng City, Shangqiu, Henan Province, was drawn into the vortex of a criminal case because of her involvement in a land development project. In September 2010, Zhu Guizhi invested money intending to cooperate with others to develop a public welfare project. She later joined with others to raise funds and lawfully acquired the relevant land-use rights. Over the course of the project, after changes in the nature of the land, shifts in the project itself, and various disputes large and small, a mixed residential and commercial community was gradually built after more than ten years of twists and turns. The current condition of the residential complex involved in the case. All images in this article were provided by interviewees. However, in September 2021, Zhu Guizhi was prosecuted by the procuratorate on five charges: embezzlement by taking advantage of position, fraud, bribery of non-state personnel, illegal transfer and resale of land-use rights, and forced transaction. The first-instance court later found Zhu guilty of three crimes and sentenced her to 20 years in prison. Zhu appealed, and the Shangqiu Intermediate People’s Court remanded the case for retrial and designated a different court for trial on the grounds that the facts were unclear and the evidence insufficient. After retrial at first instance, her sentence was reduced to 13 years. Zhu appealed again, and the intermediate court remanded the case a second time on the ground of procedural violations. In April 2024, the first-instance court again sentenced Zhu Guizhi to 13 years. After three years of proceedings, two of the original five charges against Zhu had been dropped, but she has consistently maintained her innocence. During this period, shadowy extraneous factors surrounding the case attracted widespread attention. Recently, after the third first-instance judgment, Zhu appealed again, and the case entered its third second-instance trial. Today, residential buildings stand on the land involved in the case, located in a busy area of the county seat. Since 2023, the local government has set up a special task force to actively coordinate self-rescue by property owners through pooled funds, but the project has still not reached the conditions for full delivery. Zhu Guizhi, as one of the investors, is still defending herself against the criminal charges. The self-rescue action regarding the residential complex involved in the case. Approval documents and development: from an elderly rehabilitation center to residential-commercial buildings The case originated from a cooperative land development project 14 years ago. According to the judgment, Zhu Guizhi, born in 1969, was a laid-off worker from the Gaozhuang Grain Management Office in Yongcheng, Shangqiu. That year, she obtained information about a land development opportunity and, through an introduction, came to know Chen, the legal representative of Henan Lihong Enterprise Management Consulting Co., Ltd., hereinafter referred to as Lihong Company. At the time, Chen possessed a report submitted by the Yongcheng Civil Affairs Bureau to the city government on May 10, 2010, applying for approval for Lihong Company to invest in and construct an elderly rehabilitation center in Yongcheng’s new urban area, requiring 80 mu of land. After being laid off, Zhu Guizhi had been raising money everywhere to do business. As an entrepreneur starting on her own, she saw this as an opportunity to build a career. On September 17, 2010, Zhu Guizhi and Chen signed a Land Cooperative Development Agreement, stipulating that the project would be filed in the name of Lihong Company, that Zhu Guizhi would be the actual investor, contributing 10 million yuan and taking full responsibility for investment in and operation of the relevant land, and that Lihong Company would assist in handling the relevant procedures. In the agreement, the parcel, which at that stage existed only in government documents, was set as being on the west side of the northern section of Mangshan Road in Yongcheng East Urban District, directly opposite the Municipal Real Estate Administration Bureau, with an area of 50 mu. After signing the cooperation agreement, Zhu Guizhi first paid 10 million yuan as investment for the 50-mu project, and later paid another 25 million yuan to obtain from Chen the use rights to an additional 25.459 mu of land. Zhu Guizhi lacked sufficient funds, and so she found others to jointly raise money in the name of buying land. This conduct was later charged by the procuratorate as constituting the crime of illegal transfer and resale of land-use rights. According to the court judgment, around 2012, Zhu Guizhi successively sold 54 mu of the land to nine people including Cui Moufeng, referred to in the judgment as landowner households, and collected 32.36 million yuan in land payments, from which Zhu Guizhi was found to have made illegal profits. However, multiple letters of authorization issued by those landowner households between September 2010 and May 2012 show that Cui Moufeng and others all entrusted Zhu Guizhi to hand over the more than 30 million yuan in land payments to Chen or to Lihong Company. Another notice letter explicitly states that the land was purchased from Chen and that Zhu Guizhi was only the intermediary handler. On October 31, 2012, Chen also issued proof that payment for the 75.36 mu elderly rehabilitation center land had been made in full. Proof issued by Chen that payment for the elderly rehabilitation center land had been fully made. Zhu Guizhi has repeatedly stated that she made no profit and was only raising money for development in the name of selling land. One fact not disputed by either the prosecution or the defense during the various trials is that Zhu Guizhi and the other landowner households successively paid Chen personally a total of 40 to 50 million yuan, and even promised him an additional unpaid amount of 22 million yuan. The nature of the land involved in the case also changed repeatedly, making implementation of the elderly rehabilitation center project impossible. Relevant documents show that on January 17, 2011, the Yongcheng Development and Reform Commission issued a Notice of Approval for the Construction Project of Yongcheng Elderly Rehabilitation Center to the Yongcheng Civil Affairs Bureau, making clear that all project investment would be self-financed. In December 2012, the Yongcheng Municipal People’s Government approved changing the nature of the land parcel from planned allocated land to actual granted land. On December 31, 2012, Lihong Company signed a Contract for the Grant of the Right to Use State-Owned Construction Land with the Yongcheng Bureau of Land and Resources. More than ten landowner households raised funds from various sources and, in the name of Lihong Company, paid 29.8189 million yuan in land grant fees to the government on January 14, 2013. Two days later, Lihong Company obtained the land-use rights certificate. Just three months later, the land underwent another change in nature: the city government decided to change the parcel from public welfare use to residential-commercial use, and Lihong Company was required to make supplementary payment of land grant fees after assessment. During this period, on August 13, 2013, Lihong Company and Cui Moufeng signed an equity transfer agreement stipulating that Lihong Company would transfer the project land to Cui Moufeng for 77 million yuan, that after deduction of the 45 million yuan already paid, 32 million yuan remained outstanding, and that after a payment of 10 million yuan, Chen would unconditionally transfer all of Lihong Company’s legal person status and equity to Cui Moufeng. Zhu Guizhi, Cui Moufeng, and the other investors then scraped together another 10 million yuan and paid it to Chen, leaving 22 million yuan unpaid. On January 30, 2014, the legal representative of Lihong Company was changed from Chen Li to Cui Chengfeng. At the same time, the landowner households, in accordance with the new land use, sought a real estate development partner. On January 12, 2015, Lihong Company and Shangqiu Baiyi Real Estate Co., Ltd. signed a Cooperative Development Contract, deciding to develop the Zhuangyuan Fudi residential complex on the acquired land. On February 29, 2016, Lihong Company made a supplementary payment of 49.4893 million yuan in land grant fees to the government. At that point, a cooperative land development project had completed a complex process, from a simple approval document to allocated land, then to granted land, then to conversion into residential-commercial land, and from an elderly rehabilitation center into a residential-commercial community. Zhu Guizhi also went from being an initial investor in the elderly rehabilitation center to one of more than ten landowner households. According to the agreement, those landowner households could obtain ownership of certain residential units and shops after completion of the complex. The street-level commercial units of the development involved in the case remain unused to this day. From civil dispute to criminal case: from one charge to five charges China Real Estate News once reported on the Zhuangyuan Fudi project and described it as an atypical real estate development case in which all sides had fallen into disputes for various reasons. During the process of changes in legal representative status and joint fundraising and development by the landowner households, Chen was successively convicted in other criminal cases of trading in state organ certificates and bribery and was sentenced to a total of five years in prison. After Chen was released from prison in 2019, he demanded the outstanding 22 million yuan from Zhu Guizhi and the other landowner households, and disputes resumed. The landowner households reported Chen to the public security bureau for suspected fraud and extortion, while Chen reported Zhu Guizhi and others for suspected embezzlement by taking advantage of position. Chen alleged that while he was serving his sentence, his 1.33 percent shareholding in Henan Guangshen Real Estate Co., Ltd., into which Lihong Company had been renamed, was transferred into another person’s name. In 2018, Chen filed a lawsuit to recover the shares and won judicial support. After industrial and commercial registration changes, the 1.33 percent shareholding was returned to Chen’s name. Just when it seemed that the equity dispute had been resolved, Zhu Guizhi was arrested on June 30, 2020 on suspicion of embezzlement by taking advantage of position. After that, one charge turned into five. On September 16, 2021, the Xiayi County Procuratorate prosecuted her on charges of embezzlement by taking advantage of position, fraud, bribery of non-state personnel, illegal transfer and resale of land-use rights, and forced transaction. The indictment of the Xiayi County Procuratorate shows that, apart from the embezzlement charge involving the above-mentioned equity dispute with Chen, the other four charges also mainly revolved around the development of the land involved in the case. For example, Zhu Guizhi’s fundraising from the landowner households in the name of buying land around 2012 was charged as the crime of illegal transfer and resale of land-use rights; in 2014, after a dispute arose between Baiyi Company, the developer of the Zhuangyuan Fudi residential complex, whose legal representative was Yang Baiwei, and the contractor, the contractor Ji sought Zhu Guizhi’s help in coordinating relations with Yang Baiwei, and the prosecution charged Zhu Guizhi with defrauding Ji of 700,000 yuan in the name of coordination; in 2016, Ji sought Zhu Guizhi’s help again in order to proceed smoothly with the construction of the Zhuangyuan Fudi project, and Zhu suggested that he give Yang Baiwei 200,000 yuan, on which basis the prosecution charged Zhu with bribery of non-state personnel; in 2019, Yang Baiwei, without authorization or consent from the landowner households, renovated shops on the first and second floors belonging to the landowner households, and Zhu Guizhi’s support for the renovation led to her being charged with forced transaction. Zhu Guizhi denied all five charges. After trial, the Xiayi County Court held that as to the embezzlement charge, what Zhu Guizhi and others allegedly infringed upon was Chen’s equity interests, but Chen had already protected his lawful rights and interests through civil litigation, and the case did not meet the constituent elements of the crime of embezzlement by taking advantage of position, so Zhu did not constitute that offense. As to the charge of bribery of non-state personnel, since it involved offsetting project funds, the evidence also did not support conviction. On November 7, 2021, the Xiayi County Court found Zhu Guizhi guilty at first instance of fraud, illegal transfer and resale of land-use rights, and forced transaction, and sentenced her to 20 years in prison and a fine of 3.2 million yuan. Zhu Guizhi maintained that she was innocent and appealed. The Paper noted that on June 30, 2020, Yang Baiwei, the developer of the Zhuangyuan Fudi project, was arrested on suspicion of picking quarrels and provoking trouble, and was later sentenced to ten years in prison for the three crimes of picking quarrels and provoking trouble, forced transaction, and fraud. However, among the accusations against Yang Baiwei for forced transaction was not included the fact at issue in Zhu Guizhi’s case, namely the forced renovation of the first and second floor commercial units of the Zhuangyuan Fudi project. Cheng Guangxin, Zhu Guizhi’s defense lawyer in the first second-instance trial, stated that the judgment in Zhu Guizhi’s case identified Yang Baiwei as the perpetrator of the forced transaction conduct, while Zhu Guizhi herself was one of the many victims, namely the landowner households, who were subjected to forced transaction. He argued that finding a victim guilty of forced transaction when the perpetrator was not found guilty clearly violated common sense and ordinary reasoning. Repeated twists: designated out-of-area trial and prosecutor accused of not saying a single word After the first-instance judgment, an audio recording caused the first-instance court in Zhu Guizhi’s case to fall under suspicion. According to China Real Estate News, after Zhu appealed, an audio recording attracted widespread attention. In the recording, the presiding judge at first instance stated that the case had a background, that witness testimony was contradictory before and after, and that if he did not decide it this way, he feared offending the higher-ups. The reporter sought confirmation from the presiding judge surnamed Jiang in the Xiayi County case by phone and text message but received no response. On March 3, 2022, the Shangqiu Intermediate People’s Court ruled to revoke the first-instance judgment in Zhu Guizhi’s case and remanded it for retrial on the grounds that some facts were unclear and the evidence insufficient. It then designated the Liangyuan District People’s Court to hear the case in another locality. On March 28, 2023, the retrial at first instance opened in the Liangyuan District Court, and another problem arose during the hearing. Defense lawyers discovered that the indictment read aloud in court by the prosecutor did not match the indictment in the lawyers’ hands: the prosecution had issued two indictments with exactly the same document number and date, but with different contents. The Liangyuan District Court immediately adjourned the hearing and postponed the trial. On August 22, 2023, the Liangyuan District Court rendered its retrial first-instance judgment, again finding Zhu Guizhi guilty of fraud, illegal transfer and resale of land-use rights, and forced transaction, but reducing her sentence to 13 years in prison. Among the charges, the prosecution alleged that Zhu had defrauded contractor Ji of 700,000 yuan while coordinating relations between the developer and the contractor, but the evidence was found insufficient. The court held that in fact there was only Ji’s solitary and false testimony, which was completely inconsistent before and after, and that it could not be credited, much less serve as a basis for conviction. Zhu Guizhi’s sentence for fraud was reduced from 12 years in the original first-instance trial to 3 years and 6 months. But Zhu continued to insist that she was completely innocent and again appealed. Illegalities that arose during the second trial in the Liangyuan District Court became an important reason for this appeal. Zhu Guizhi argued on appeal that, at the hearing in the Liangyuan District Court, because the original prosecutor had retired, Prosecutor Zhao, who appeared in court to support the public prosecution, did not say a single word throughout the court proceedings and expressed no opinion whatsoever related to the hearing of the case, while all the work that should have been done by Prosecutor Zhao was instead done by the prosecutor’s assistant. She argued that the prosecutor’s silence in court violated the Supreme People’s Procuratorate’s procedural rules on prosecutors appearing in court and affected the fair trial of the case. Because the prosecutor’s total silence in court led to procedural illegality, the case was again remanded for retrial. On November 23, 2023, the Shangqiu Intermediate People’s Court ruled that there had been procedural illegality in the original trial and remanded the case for retrial a second time. On April 12, 2024, the Liangyuan District Court issued a third first-instance judgment in the case, again sentencing Zhu Guizhi to 13 years in prison for the above three crimes. Zhu appealed once more, and the case entered its third second-instance trial. Dispute over the crime of resale of land-use rights: the land-use rights remained in the company’s name throughout The criminal case involving Zhu Guizhi originated from the land, and the core charge against her, illegal transfer and resale of land-use rights, has been highly controversial. In its retrial first-instance judgment, the Liangyuan District Court held that the right to use construction land may lawfully be transferred, and therefore cooperative development conduct after June 6, 2014, when the Yongcheng Urban and Rural Planning Service Center changed the nature of the land parcel to residential-commercial use, did not constitute a crime, but that conduct before the land was changed to residential-commercial use did constitute the crime of illegal transfer and resale of land-use rights. The Working Rules for Filing and Investigating Natural Resources Violations, Trial Version, clearly provide with respect to the investigation of major land violations that illegal transfer of land cannot be determined solely on the basis of signing a transfer contract or agreement or paying a transfer price, and that it must also be confirmed whether the transferee actually received, possessed, and controlled the land. In the view of Zhang Liang, a lawyer at Beijing Zhongwen Law Firm, before January 16, 2013, when the Yongcheng government issued the land-use rights certificate to Lihong Company, the land involved in the case was still only at the project approval and examination stage, and no company or individual possessed any land-use rights that could be transferred. In fact, objective evidence shows that the land-use rights involved in the case remained from beginning to end in the name of Lihong Company, later renamed Henan Guangshen Real Estate Co., Ltd., and that there was never any change or transfer of the land-use rights. The landowner households, including Zhu Guizhi, raised funds through equity transfers for Lihong Company to pay land grant fees. In essence, this was a partnership for development and house construction. After the residential complex was completed, the landowner households obtained ownership of the buildings constructed on the land, rather than the land or land-use rights themselves. A search by The Paper found that in a series of official interpretations of the Working Rules for Investigating and Handling Land and Resources Violations organized and compiled under the leadership of Yue Xiaowu, former deputy director of the Law Enforcement and Supervision Bureau of the Ministry of Land and Resources, it is clearly stated with respect to the determination and handling of illegal transfer of land-use rights that where a holder of allocated state-owned land-use rights transfers the allocated land-use rights to a transferee without approval from a people’s government with approval authority, this shall be deemed an illegal transfer of allocated land-use rights. However, if before filing and investigation the transfer is approved by the people’s government with approval authority and land grant procedures are handled, or if the people’s government with approval authority agrees to the transfer and the transferee handles land grant procedures, then it shall not be investigated and handled as an illegal transfer of land-use rights. Zhu Guizhi’s family said they could not understand how conduct for which even administrative punishment by the land authorities would not apply could nevertheless give rise to criminal liability for illegal transfer and resale of land-use rights.

Title: How to work in Japan or get permanent residency directly? Content: I think you have some misunderstandings. First of all, your major is not easy to find a matching job. I've heard that the art and painting industry in Japan is even more exploitative. Regarding the timeline, I doubt it's feasible. It's not easy to master either IT skills or English in just six months. If you go there with half-baked skills, you'll face double pressure during technical communication due to lagging in both language and technology. You should assess your own stress tolerance. Secondly, after deducting food and drink expenses (6-8k RMB), that converts to about 140,000 yen. Bro, in areas with IT jobs, even a conservative estimate for rent is 50,000 yen. I guess you're not the type to skimp on food, so 40,000-50,000 yen is reasonable, and Japanese utilities aren't cheap. To take home 300,000 yen, calculate how much you need before tax. I don't understand how you dare to aim for this income abroad when you didn't even achieve it in China. If you want a relaxed life with relatively high income, I seriously suggest considering factory work - I'm not joking. As for costs, I think your 10,000+ RMB savings might just cover the first month's rent and basic setup in Japan. Prepare around 40,000-50,000 RMB for agency fees and airfare.

Title: Trump Signs Bill to Address COVID-19 Pandemic Content: Trump Signs Bill to Address COVID-19 Pandemic Xinhua News Agency, Washington, March 18 (Reporter Xiong Maoling) - US President Trump signed a bill on the 18th to address the COVID-19 pandemic, which includes measures such as paid leave, enhanced unemployment insurance, and free virus testing. Earlier that day, the US Senate passed the bill with 90 votes in favor and 8 against. The Democrat-controlled House of Representatives passed multiple measures to combat the pandemic in the early hours of the 14th, including ensuring that businesses with fewer than 500 employees provide two weeks of paid sick leave, up to three months of paid family leave and paid hospitalization sick leave, and offering free testing to all who need COVID-19 testing, including those without health insurance. The version passed by the Senate made minor adjustments based on the House version. US Treasury Secretary Mnuchin stated on the 17th that in response to the pandemic's impact, the White House is discussing a major economic stimulus plan with Congress, focusing on assisting small businesses, the aviation industry, the hotel industry, and possibly providing direct cash support to the public. According to US media reports, this fiscal stimulus measure could amount to one trillion US dollars. (End)

Content Title: When driving normally, suddenly encountering an obstacle ahead, never do this wrong again, remember! Release Date: 2025-04-12 00:20:08 Content Status: Review Completed Content Type: Multimedia Industry: Digital Government Affairs_Government Media_Government Media Author Name: Haiyue Talks Cars Owner Name: Haiyue Talks Cars Content Account Type: Enterprise Content Details: While driving, suddenly an obstacle falls onto your front windshield, completely blocking your view. What exactly should you do in this situation? Or, while driving, if you suddenly encounter traffic cones like this ahead, how should you handle it correctly? I think maybe 90% of drivers don't know how to avoid such emergencies. 90%. If handled improperly, the consequences are really unimaginable. So today, Siling will share with you how to correctly handle the above two emergency situations. It is recommended to like, save, and share with your friends who have cars. Because it can really save your life at a critical moment. First, while driving, if you suddenly encounter such an obstacle falling onto our front windshield, when encountering this situation, you must not panic. Avoid emergency braking. If you brake hard, if there is a vehicle behind, it is very easy to rear-end our car. Remember not to steer randomly. When the vehicle speed is relatively high, if you steer randomly, our car is very prone to losing control, or rolling over/skidding. "You should immediately turn on our hazard warning lights. Because when we are driving, our forward visibility is blocked. We must use the car's center rearview mirror to observe the distance to the vehicle behind. Slow down gradually. At the same time, observe our right-side mirror to see if there is a car coming from the right rear. Then turn on our right turn signal. Under safe conditions, slowly drive our car onto the emergency lane. After stopping on the emergency lane, you can then deal with the obstacle on the front windshield. Second, what should you do if you suddenly encounter traffic cones like this?" Content Understanding Tags: Government and Livelihood-Public Security and Firefighting-Information-Traffic Management

Title: Asymmetric Hearing Loss, Should the Poor Ear Be Abandoned? Content: Asymmetric hearing loss (AHL)/single-sided deafness (SSD) is not uncommon among the hearing-impaired population, mostly caused by functional damage or structural variation of the inner ear. In complex acoustic environments, it directly affects the effective social ability of the hearing-impaired [1]. In daily life, many hearing-impaired individuals choose to be fitted with a hearing aid in only one ear, mainly for the following reasons: AHL/SSD, where normal hearing does not require intervention or the individual chooses not to intervene on the better-hearing side; consideration of cost leading to fitting only one aid; poor hearing aid effectiveness in the worse ear, refusal of cochlear implants and hearing aid fittings, etc. This group often experiences difficulty in the auditory center's normal integration of signals received by both ears in the time, frequency, and intensity domains due to the asymmetry of binaural hearing and auditory function [2]. From a scientific hearing intervention perspective, considering the impact of binaural hearing on the daily life, psychology, and personality of the hearing-impaired, it is recommended that individuals with hearing loss should not abandon the poorer ear but actively intervene. Intervention for asymmetric hearing loss varies depending on the situation: 1. If one ear has 20-65dB HL loss and the other <90dB HL, consider fitting hearing aids of different power in both ears; 2. If one ear has 20-65dB HL loss and the other ≥90dB HL without structural abnormality, consider fitting a hearing aid on the better ear and implanting a cochlear implant in the poorer ear; 3. If one ear has 20-65dB HL loss and the other ≥90dB HL with structural abnormality, choose a BICROS hearing aid [3]. If the better ear has conductive or mixed hearing loss, a bone conduction hearing aid can also be considered. Attached are intervention plans for different degrees and types of hearing loss. References: [1] Li N, Wang S, Dong R J, et al. Speech intelligibility under noise conditions in sensorineural hearing-impaired[J]. Chinese Archives of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery, 2018, 25(2): 86-88. [2] Liu J F, Dai J S, Wang N Y. Advances in effect of unilateral auditory deprivation on sound localization[J]. Chinese Journal of Otorhinolaryngology Head and Neck Surgery, 2017, 52(2): 136-142 [3] Hol M K S, Kunst S J W, Snik A F M, et al. Pilot study on the effectiveness of the conventional CROS, the transcranial CROS and the BAHA transcranial CROS in adults with unilateral inner ear deafness[J]. Eur Arch Otorhinolaryngol, 2010, 267(6): 889-896.

Title: How to Prevent Colds in Autumn and Winter? Content: Prevention is key. You can start from the following aspects: 1. Keep warm and adjust clothing appropriately: Especially protect the chest, back, and feet to avoid sudden chills. 2. Maintain indoor air circulation: Open windows for ventilation daily for 15-30 minutes each time. This is the most effective way to dilute the concentration of 🧊viruses indoors. 3. Strengthen personal hygiene · Wash hands frequently: Wash hands thoroughly with running water and soap (or hand sanitizer). This is key to preventing 🧊viruses from entering through the mouth. · Avoid touching the mouth, nose, and eyes with hands: 🧊Viruses mainly invade the human body through these mucous membrane areas. · Cover your mouth and nose with a tissue or your elbow when sneezing/coughing. 4. Wear a mask: Wearing a mask in crowded public places (such as subways, shopping malls, hospitals) or when in contact with cold patients can effectively block droplet transmission. 5. Healthy living to enhance immunity · Balanced diet: Eat more fresh vegetables and fruits to ensure nutritional intake. · Drink plenty of water: Keep the respiratory tract mucosa moist to enhance its defense capability. · Get enough sleep: Avoid staying up late.
