Title: Is eating more peanuts more beneficial or harmful? Content: Peanuts should not be eaten in excess, as overconsumption can easily lead to diarrhea, internal heat, and weight gain. Four types of people who are not suitable for consuming peanuts: 1. Because peanuts are very high in fat and protein, people with gastrointestinal diseases should not eat them, otherwise it will worsen diarrhea. 2. For people with hepatobiliary diseases, peanuts will increase the burden on the liver. 3. People with旺盛 skin oil secretion and prone to acne should also not eat excessive amounts of peanuts. 4. Since peanuts have a hemostatic effect, can promote blood coagulation, and facilitate thrombus formation, those with high blood viscosity or thrombosis should not consume them. Extended Information: Experts point out that peanuts have a sweet taste and neutral nature, are rich in nutrition, and have the effects of strengthening the spleen, harmonizing the stomach, nourishing blood and stopping bleeding, moistening the lungs and relieving cough, promoting diuresis, and stimulating lactation. They can lower cholesterol, prevent and treat atherosclerosis, hypertension, and coronary heart disease. Additionally, they can prevent and treat tumor-like diseases and are a good traditional Chinese medicine. 1. Control Appetite: Peanuts are "high-satiety" foods that make you feel fuller or full for a longer time. An article published in the journal "Nutrition and Metabolism" found that people who snack on peanuts eat less. Dr. Mattes, a professor in the Department of Nutritional Sciences at Purdue University, said: "The high satiety of peanuts is not only due to their fat, dietary fiber, and protein content, but the result of all factors working together." Kathy McManus, director of the nutrition department at Brigham and Women's Hospital, said that if you eat peanuts or peanut butter for breakfast, you can reduce the amount of food you eat that day. 2. Help Reduce Salt: Salty snacks are usually high-salt foods. However, the salt content of salted peanuts is less than that of sliced bread or frozen waffles of the same weight. Therefore, salted peanuts can not only satisfy your craving for salty food but also are less likely to lead to excessive salt intake. 3. Stabilize Blood Sugar: Research has found that if people replace a portion of red meat in their diet with peanuts, the risk of diabetes is reduced by 21%. Peanuts slow down the absorption of carbohydrates. If you eat some peanuts in the morning, your blood sugar will not be too high for the rest of the day. Reference: Eating More Peanuts Benefits the Heart - People's Daily Network; 4. Excessive Peanut Consumption is Harmful and Not Beneficial - People's Daily Network

Title: 3·15 Exposes Home Appliance Repair Scammer "Woodpecker Home Repair" - Unnecessary Repairs, Exaggerating Minor Issues, How Deep Are Their Tricks? How Should Consumers Identify Them? Content: Multiple deceptive tactics run deep. Pricing traps with vague quotes: On the Woodpecker mini-program, consumers only see approximate price ranges for repair services, e.g., washing machine repair: simple repair 98 - 179 yuan, standard repair 136 - 616 yuan, medium repair 176 - 508 yuan. This vague pricing makes it hard for consumers to estimate costs upfront, giving repair technicians leeway to set arbitrary prices later. On-site inspection before quoting: When consumers inquire about fault repair costs, customer service uniformly replies that an on-site inspection is needed first to determine the repair method and specific fault before providing a quote. Even for "price-sensitive consumers," they promise "no charge if no repair is done" to secure the visit. However, the quote after inspection is often shocking, and consumers, having already invested time, feel pressured to accept the high price. Numerous bargaining tricks: If customers are unhappy with the quote, repair technicians have a series of tactics. First, they emphasize Woodpecker is a major platform, prices include technical fees, material costs, and come with a warranty to reassure the customer; then they offer a 10% discount using "new user, old user" schemes; if the customer still doesn't accept, they pretend to apply for higher approval, offering a 20-30% discount; finally, they use the "cost price" gimmick, claiming a limited number of 40% discount applications per month, though there's no real limit. After this process, many consumers succumb to the psychological pressure and accept the high price. Technicians can alter quotes: Usually, technicians must quote based on the pricing system, but during bargaining, they can modify the amount through "discount applications," giving them significant flexibility. This renders the seemingly standardized pricing system ineffective, allowing technicians to adjust prices arbitrarily for higher profits. Parts scams with inflated prices: When sourcing parts externally, technicians often inflate prices. For example, a faucet bought for 180 yuan might be quoted to the user as 300 yuan, earning a high margin, with the engineer also getting a substantial commission. Substituting inferior parts: To cut costs, technicians might use poor-quality parts. For instance, a technician bought a low-quality plastic washing machine motor online for 91 yuan but charged the customer 659 yuan for replacement, even taking away the original good-quality metal motor. Recycling and reuse: During repairs, technicians might remove original brand parts from the customer's home and replace them with cheap ones, planning to refurbish and reuse them later. For example, a customer had a loose toilet inlet valve causing a leak; the technician removed the original valve and installed a cheap replacement. Exaggerating minor issues: Technicians intentionally exaggerate fault severity, turning small problems into major ones. For instance, a customer's washing machine was leaking due to a damaged inlet hose, but the technician claimed the tripod was broken, quoting 719 yuan, and persuaded the customer to replace the tripod and bearing for a "cost price" of 500 yuan (the bearing cost was already included in the tripod price). Unnecessary repairs: In worse cases, even when the appliance has no fault, technicians invent problems to charge for repairs. For example, a customer's washing machine wouldn't fill because the faucet wasn't turned on, but the technician falsely claimed the inlet valve was faulty, charging over 100 yuan; another customer's gas stove wouldn't ignite after a battery change—actually, the battery cap wasn't removed—but the technician replaced the igniter, costing 20 yuan but charging over 250 yuan. Sharp-eyed identification methods: Research prices beforehand: Before choosing a repair service, research market prices for similar repairs through multiple channels. Consult other reputable repair shops or check online appliance repair forums and communities for shared price experiences to get a rough idea of costs, avoiding overpriced traps like Woodpecker's. Check credentials and reputation: Choose repair platforms or technicians with proper credentials and good reputations. Verify if the platform has relevant industry certifications and business licenses. Be cautious with platforms like Woodpecker that have numerous complaints. Also, search online for reviews of the platform or technician; if there are many negative evaluations, be wary. Demand clear quotes: Before the technician arrives, insist on detailed pricing for specific repair items. If they refuse or are vague, decline the visit. If the on-site quote differs significantly from your researched market price, question it immediately and demand a breakdown of costs. Supervise the repair process: During the repair, try to supervise, observing if the technician's operations are standard and if the parts used are new and quality-approved. If you notice suspicious actions, like intentionally damaging other components or replacing parts not originally in your appliance, stop them and keep evidence. Request repair documentation: After completion, always ask for formal repair documentation detailing the repair items, replaced parts, and cost breakdown. This helps protect your rights if issues arise later. Woodpecker Home Repair's various tricks severely harm consumer interests. Only by staying vigilant and learning identification methods can consumers avoid being "ripped off" when repairing appliances and protect their legal rights. Meanwhile, relevant authorities should strengthen supervision of such repair platforms, standardize market order, and ensure a fair consumer environment.

Title: The phone card is clearly 4G, but when I turn on mobile data, it shows 2G. What's going on? Content: If your phone cannot use the 4G network, it is recommended that you: 1. Check if the phone supports 4G networks. 2. Check if you are using a phone card with 4G service; it is recommended that you contact your network operator to activate 4G service. 3. Check if the 4G network mode is enabled: Settings - Connections - More networks - Mobile networks - Network mode - Select 4G/3G/2G (LTE/WCDMA/GSM) network mode (some phones/tablets do not support changing network bands). 4. Confirm that your location has 4G network coverage. 5. Try turning the phone off and on again. 6. Back up your data (such as contacts, messages, pictures, etc.) and perform a factory reset. If the problem still persists, it is recommended that you take your purchase invoice, warranty card, and the device to a local Samsung after-sales service center, where a professional engineer can help you diagnose the issue.

Title: Nanjing Announces 5 Typical Cases Content: As the May Day holiday approaches, to further standardize market price order during the holiday period, actively create a harmonious and orderly holiday atmosphere, and fully protect consumers' legitimate price rights and interests, Nanjing's market supervision departments continue to strengthen supervision over price behaviors in the tourism market. They are closely monitoring key areas such as hotels and homestays, restaurants, cultural and tourism streets, and scenic spots, increasing enforcement inspections, and strictly investigating and punishing various price violations such as failing to clearly mark prices as required and price fraud according to law. On April 26, the Nanjing Municipal Market Supervision Bureau announced a batch of typical cases. Case 1: A homestay near Nanjing Mochou Lake Scenic Area charged extra fees beyond the listed price. In March, the Jianye District Market Supervision Bureau conducted an on-site inspection of the party based on complaint clues. It was found that the party charged an additional fee upon check-in despite the consumer having pre-booked and paid for the hotel room. This behavior violated Article 13 of the Price Law of the People's Republic of China, constituting the price violation of selling goods at a price higher than the marked price. The Jianye District Market Supervision Bureau ordered corrective actions and imposed administrative penalties according to law. Case 2: Price fraud case at a hotel in Nanjing Xinjiekou. In April, the Qinhuai District Market Supervision Bureau conducted an on-site inspection of the party and found that the party could not provide genuine evidence for the compared strikethrough prices marked for its rooms. It was suspected of using false or misleading price means to deceive consumers into transactions. This behavior violated Article 14 of the Price Law of the People's Republic of China, constituting improper price behavior. The Qinhuai District Market Supervision Bureau ordered on-site corrections and initiated an investigation according to law. Case 3: A supermarket in Nanjing Gaochun Old Street Scenic Area charged extra fees beyond the listed price. In March, the Gaochun District Market Supervision Bureau conducted patrol inspections of shops in the Gaochun Old Street Scenic Area. It was found that the electronic scale in the party's store was set to automatically remove the decimal places of the total amount and round up the tenths place, resulting in consumers paying more than the marked price. This behavior violated Article 13 of the Price Law of the People's Republic of China, constituting the price violation of selling goods at a price higher than the marked price. The Gaochun District Market Supervision Bureau ordered on-site corrections and initiated an investigation according to law. Case 4: Price fraud case at a specialty store in Nanjing Confucius Temple. In April, the Qinhuai District Market Supervision Bureau conducted patrol inspections of shops in the Confucius Temple Historical and Cultural Block. It was found that the party's store was suspected of fabricating the original price for gift packages sold in the store, using false or misleading price means to deceive consumers into transactions. This behavior violated Article 14 of the Price Law of the People's Republic of China, constituting improper price behavior. The Qinhuai District Market Supervision Bureau ordered on-site corrections and initiated an investigation according to law. Case 5: A restaurant near Nanjing Yuejianglou Scenic Area failed to clearly mark prices as required. In March, the Gulou District Market Supervision Bureau conducted an on-site inspection of the party based on complaint clues. It was found that the party could not provide a price list for tea. This behavior violated Article 13 of the Price Law of the People's Republic of China, for failing to clearly mark prices as required. The Gulou District Bureau ordered on-site corrections and initiated an investigation according to law. The Municipal Market Supervision Bureau stated that it hopes all businesses will take warning, strictly abide by the law, operate with integrity, strengthen price self-discipline, earnestly fulfill social responsibilities, and must not use price means to infringe upon consumers' legitimate rights and interests or disrupt market price order. Market supervision departments will continue to increase enforcement inspections, strictly investigate and punish various price violations according to law, and effectively safeguard consumers' legitimate rights and interests. Fair交易，明码标价 (Fair交易，Clear Marking of Prices) Businesses should price fairly, legally, and reasonably, fully protect consumers' right to fair交易, strictly comply with relevant regulations such as the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests, the Price Law of the People's Republic of China, and the Anti-Monopoly Law of the People's Republic of China, strictly implement the regulations on clear price marking, ensure price publicity is truthful and accurate, corresponds to the goods and labels, and is clearly marked, must not charge any undisclosed fees, and must not use price means to infringe upon consumers' legitimate rights and interests or disrupt market price order. 诚信经营，杜绝欺诈 (Integrity in Operation, Eliminate Fraud) Integrity is the foundation of operation. Businesses should adhere to the principle of good faith, must not maliciously breach contracts or pass off inferior products as good ones, must not implement misleading price markings and price promotions; must not fail to fulfill or only partially fulfill price commitments, and must not intentionally delay or unreasonably refuse reasonable refund and compensation requests from consumers. Businesses should continuously improve service levels, strive to enhance tourist consumption experiences, and establish excellent brand images. 加强自律，品质服务 (Strengthen Self-Discipline, Quality Service) Businesses should firmly establish the bottom-line awareness of 'safety first,' starting from food safety, consumption safety, property safety, personal safety, etc., strictly guard the safety bottom line, earnestly fulfill primary responsibilities, practice service commitments such as 'no-reason returns and exchanges' and 'small-amount advance compensation,' and protect consumers' legitimate rights and interests. At the same time, with the main line of 'boosting consumption confidence,' treat guests with courtesy and sincerity, improve service levels, and demonstrate the potential city image and service quality of Nanjing as an international consumption center. Title: What to do when an ASUS desktop encounters startup failure Content: When an ASUS desktop encounters startup failure, you can troubleshoot and resolve it by following these steps: Hardware issue check Power supply: Check if the power outlet is loose and if the power cord is damaged. If loose, reconnect it; if damaged, replace it promptly. Additionally, the power supply unit itself might be faulty, consider further testing or replacement. Internal hardware: Open the main case, check if the memory module and graphics card are properly inserted, if loose, reinsert them firmly. At the same time, check if the CPU fan is operating normally, if there's a problem, replace it promptly. System fault troubleshooting If the hardware check reveals no issues, it might be an operating system problem. You can use the system disk's startup repair function for fault recovery; you can also choose to reinstall the system, but remember to back up important data beforehand, and before reinstalling, confirm whether the startup issue is caused by software conflicts or virus infections. BIOS settings issue Enter the BIOS setup interface, try resetting the BIOS to default settings. Check if the boot order in the BIOS settings is correct. If the optical drive is set to boot before the hard drive, it might prevent normal startup; adjust the boot order correctly. If there is a newer BIOS version, you can update to the latest version, but updating carries certain risks. Before operating, carefully read the relevant instructions to ensure correct operation. If necessary, seek professional help and back up important data in advance. Other special situations If the above steps cannot resolve the problem, it might be a motherboard issue. You can try removing the battery on the motherboard, wait a few minutes, then put it back to see if it resolves the issue. If the problem persists, it is recommended to contact ASUS official customer service or professional repair personnel. They will use professional tools and equipment for further inspection and repair.

Content Status: Review completed. Content Type: Multimedia. Industry: Digital Government_Other_Other. Author Name: Kanfa Video. Owner Name: Kanfa Video. Content Account Type: Enterprise. Content Details: Kanfa. Recently, a netizen in Nanjing reported being fined 50 yuan for riding a bicycle on the road without a license plate. The Nanjing Municipal Public Security Bureau Traffic Management Bureau immediately formed an investigation team to conduct an inquiry. Investigation found that at 17:46 on April 9, a police officer from the bureau, while on duty at the intersection of Zhongshan Road and Changjiang Road, discovered the involved party, Wang, riding a bicycle in the wrong direction. The officer issued a warning for the illegal act of riding against the traffic flow and imposed a 50 yuan fine for riding without a license plate. According to the "Jiangsu Province Road Traffic Safety Regulations" effective January 1, 2024, bicycles are no longer classified as non-motor vehicles requiring registration and do not need license plates for road use. Based on this, the bureau has revoked the penalty decision regarding riding the bicycle without a license plate and will hold the responsible officer accountable for the law enforcement error. Regarding the issues exposed by this enforcement action, the bureau will use this case as a cautionary example, learn from it comprehensively, further strengthen legal training and enforcement supervision, and continuously enhance law enforcement capacity building. Thanks to the netizens and media for their supervision and attention. Jiaohuidian News.

Title: A trainee developed rhabdomyolysis after 3 days of exercise, claiming over 100,000 yuan in compensation. How should the fitness institution respond? Content: A trainee developed rhabdomyolysis after 3 days of exercise, claiming over 100,000 yuan in compensation. How should the fitness institution respond? Lawyer's Notes: In the movie "Sheep Without a Shepherd," the male lead played by Xiao Yang has a classic line: 'When you've watched 1,000 movies, you'll find there's nothing strange in this world.' This also applies to lawyers; when you've handled 1,000 cases, you'll find there's no case that can't be resolved. At the beginning of this year, I handled a personal injury compensation dispute where the judgment outcome broke from the precedent of similar cases in the same region that I had researched. The defendant I represented was the owner and coach of a gym (a sole proprietorship). The plaintiff, a male trainee, was diagnosed with rhabdomyolysis after only 3 days of exercise following his contract with the gym. The plaintiff claimed that the defendant's arrangement of excessively intense training caused severe physical damage, demanding compensation for medical expenses, hospitalization meal subsidies, nutrition fees, nursing costs, lost wages, legal fees, etc., totaling over 100,000 yuan. Based on general reasonable understanding and the value judgments reflected in existing precedents, the fitness institution should bear at least 40% of the liability. However, in this case, the judge only held the defendant liable for 10% of the damages. The judge's diligence (the case went through three court sessions) and the rigor and detail in writing the judgment (14 pages) impressed me. There are no small cases; every case and every party deserves serious attention because behind each judgment lies value pursuit and interest balancing. Nowadays, more and more people are focusing on physical health and body shaping. Judging by the frequency of receiving fitness flyers on the streets or in malls, the popularity and demand for gyms in cities are increasing. Similarly, the concept of fitness and body beautification is gaining more recognition. Exercise is inherently good, but it's important to exercise reasonably, moderately, and scientifically. The plaintiff in this case, due to long-term lack of exercise and irregular作息 and diet, exercised at the defendant's gym for 3 consecutive days, one hour each day, after which he experienced physical abnormalities, including brown urine. He was diagnosed with rhabdomyolysis, spent 7 days in the ICU, narrowly escaping death, and incurred huge medical expenses. Returning to the topic, the legal relationship involved in this case is tort law - personality rights - right to life, body rights, and health rights. Liability for civil compensation arises only when the general elements of tort are met: subjective fault, unlawful act, damage fact, and a causal link between the unlawful act and the damage. Therefore, whether the fitness coach should bear compensation for the plaintiff's huge expenses due to rhabdomyolysis is analyzed based on the following three points: 1. Whether there is a causal link between the plaintiff's rhabdomyolysis and the exercise under the defendant's guidance. According to online searches, there are many causes of rhabdomyolysis, such as excessive exercise, medication, alcohol consumption, metabolic diseases, dietary disorders, etc. There are news reports that eating crayfish can also cause rhabdomyolysis and acute kidney injury. My view: Except for the plaintiff's own account, the medical records and other evidence provided by the plaintiff do not clearly state that the cause was exercise, let alone indicate that the training was excessively intense or overloaded. Existing evidence cannot prove a causal link. The plaintiff bears the burden of proof for causation but did not apply for judicial appraisal, so he should bear the adverse consequences of the undetermined cause. The court's view was humane. The court held: The plaintiff consistently stated in the medical records, admission notes, discharge summaries, etc., that the condition occurred after leg exercises, with bilateral lower limb muscle soreness, consistent with the radiological diagnostic report. The patient's account during treatment is crucial for diagnosis and treatment direction, and the possibility of providing a false account is small. No other evidence showed other causes for the plaintiff's rhabdomyolysis. Given his healthy young male physique, the possibility of other causes was small. The plaintiff's disease process basically fits the characteristics of exertional rhabdomyolysis. The plaintiff's claim had a high probability, which the court confirmed. 2. Whether the defendant was at fault in guiding the plaintiff's exercise and how liability should be determined? The defendant is a professional, experienced fitness coach with qualifications. Before the plaintiff purchased the course, the defendant conducted a physical assessment, understood his physical condition, and developed a suitable fitness plan and scientific diet. During training, the defendant arranged a low-intensity program suitable for a beginner, with proper stretching and rest periods. The court held: The defendant preliminarily understood the plaintiff's physical condition through health questionnaires and instrument tests, identified him as a beginner with weak physique, and formulated an intensity-appropriate training plan, objectively fulfilling a duty of care in good faith. However, during exercise, when the plaintiff showed painful expressions and inability to continue, the defendant should have focused on adaptation, progressing gradually based on the plaintiff's feedback. Thus, the defendant cannot be said to be entirely without fault. Everyone is primarily responsible for their own health, has the autonomy to exercise or not, and should bear the consequences. Individuals differ; the same intensity may benefit some but harm others. Arranging low-intensity training for an adult male like the plaintiff was not improper; normally, it wouldn't cause injury. The plaintiff's rhabdomyolysis is largely related to his own physique, especially muscle tolerance, which the defendant could not foresee. Thus, the defendant's fault was minor. 3. How are the scope and amount of personal injury compensation damages determined in judicial practice? The Tort Liability section of the Civil Code stipulates that causing personal injury to others requires compensation for reasonable expenses for treatment and rehabilitation, such as medical fees, nursing costs, transportation, nutrition, hospitalization meal subsidies, etc., as well as lost income due to missed work. Disability also requires compensation for assistive devices and disability compensation; death requires funeral and death compensation. Based on judicial interpretations like the Supreme Court's decision amending the 'Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Personal Injury Compensation Cases' and judicial practice, combined with the latest compensation standards in Shanghai, I have tabulated the main compensation categories and calculation standards. Note: According to the 'Shanghai High People's Court's Implementation Opinions on Pilot Work for Unifying Urban and Rural Personal Injury Compensation Standards,' from January 1, 2020, for all personal injury compensation cases accepted by courts citywide (including civil, criminal incidental civil, and maritime cases), disability and death compensation are calculated based on the previous year's Shanghai per capita disposable income published by government statistics. Dependent support is calculated based on the previous year's Shanghai per capita consumption expenditure and included in disability or death compensation. According to the '2020 Shanghai National Economic and Social Development Statistical Bulletin,' the annual per capita disposable income of Shanghai residents in 2020 was 72,232 yuan, and per capita consumption expenditure was 42,536 yuan.

Title: No profit, no fees? How attractive are bank wealth management fee discounts really? Content: Have you noticed that recently many bank wealth management product fees are being discounted? Just like the temperature during the dog days of summer, the heat of the "price war" for bank wealth management product fees continues to rise. Since June, at least 10 bank wealth management companies have issued announcements to reduce fees, including fixed management fees and product redemption fees. Some wealth management companies have even touted a "zero fee" slogan. Does this mean we can buy cheaper, more cost-effective wealth management products? Next, I'll have a good chat with everyone about it~ 1. Why are bank wealth management fees being discounted? First, we need to understand why bank wealth management companies are lowering fees. This is actually influenced by multiple factors. On one hand, fee reduction is a direction encouraged by regulators. According to the "Supervisory Measures for Commercial Bank Wealth Management Business," commercial banks should publicly disclose investment management service fees and other related service charges, and adjust them promptly based on market changes. Regulators hope to increase investor returns by reducing investment costs and promote fair market competition. On the other hand, fee reduction is also one of the measures wealth management companies are taking to cope with market competition and challenges. Last year's two rounds of "net value breakage waves" caused many investors to lose confidence in net-value wealth management products. Although the bond market bull run in the first half of this year led to a recovery in the wealth management market, investors' operational style remains relatively conservative, and demand for wealth management products is not strong. In this context, to stabilize and expand their scale, companies need to take measures to attract investors. Reducing fees is one such method. By lowering fees, wealth management companies can convey confidence in their own investment capabilities and market development, aiming to help investors achieve a better investment experience and encourage long-term holding. 2. What fees do wealth management products charge? Generally, fees for bank wealth management products can be divided into three categories: management fees, custody fees, and sales fees. Management Fee: The management fee is used by the wealth management company to cover operational costs. It is usually accrued at a fixed rate and charged regardless of whether the product is profitable or not. For example, for a product with a size of 1 billion yuan and a management fee of 1.5% per annum, it means approximately 15 million yuan in management fees are fixedly collected each year. Custody Fee: The custody fee is related to the custodian bank. To ensure the safety of investors' funds, regulators require wealth management companies to place raised investment funds with qualified third-party banks for custody. The custody fee is the fee paid to the custodian bank and is also calculated daily. The calculation method for this fee is as follows: Custody Fee = Holding Size * Custody Fee Rate / 365. Sales Fees: Sales fees are given to the sales channels and can be seen as promotion costs for the channels. Some products charge a one-time subscription fee or redemption fee; some products charge a sales service fee accrued daily. These fees are directly deducted from the subscription or redemption amount. 3. Which fees are being competitively discounted? Currently, many wealth management companies are adjusting their fees. Some wealth management products have even reduced their management fee rates to zero, and others have proposed the slogan "no profit, no fees." The number of products with reduced fees is not large, mainly consisting of cash and bond products, while equity products rarely see adjustments. These fee reductions have an impact on investors' returns, but not a significant one. This is because the yield and risk level of the wealth management product are the key factors determining the final return. Furthermore, these fee reductions have channel and time limitations. Some products only reduce fees on specific platforms or channels, or only during specific time periods or phases. If you want to enjoy the latest discounts, you might need to redeem your original product and then purchase a new one at a designated place, which could increase operational and time costs. 4. What should we do? So, should we consider fee-reduced products when investing? Professionals suggest: do not treat fees as the key factor in selecting wealth management products. Instead, conduct comprehensive asset allocation based on various factors such as your own risk preference, liquidity needs, and investable assets. In asset allocation, choosing a wealth management product that suits you is paramount; the level of fees is just one of many factors and not the key consideration. Of course, it would be even better if you could find a wealth management product that not only matches your investment goals and risk tolerance but also offers lower fees and higher yields. That's all for this edition of Wealth Management Q&A~ If you have questions related to wealth management, feel free to leave a comment below. Yours might be selected for the next edition's Q&A! See you next week. -END- Author | Han Ziyu Image Source | Beta Data Compiled and Edited | Beta Research Institute *Risk Warning: The market carries risks, investment requires caution. Title: Why was a 14-year-old girl swept underwater by a waterfall and drowned? Content: At 3:30 PM on July 18, at a waterfall section of Zhongdu Xiangshui River in Luzhai County, a 14-year girl jumped into the water from a high place to play but was swept underwater by the current and tragically drowned. According to eyewitnesses, this area is a relatively flat section of Xiangshui River, forming a large pool where people enjoy swimming to escape the heat. The pool is about the size of a basketball court, with an area of about 6 square meters at the 2-meter deep point. At the time, the girl, around 14 years old, jumped from a height and was pulled underwater by the churning currents under the waterfall. People noticed within less than a minute. Many people were swimming there at the time, and over ten individuals dived repeatedly to search for her, but after more than 10 minutes, they couldn't find her. "She was probably swept into a rock crevice," said a rescuer. The Zhongdu Xiangshui River often has sections where waterfalls and pools connect. Near the waterfall in the pool, the swirling currents created by the waterfall are very complex; even strong swimmers struggle to escape them, let alone a young girl. Over ten people were playing in the water there at the time. Unable to find the girl, they quickly called the police. After the accident, fire services, 120 ambulances, and relevant departments rushed to the scene and actively conducted rescue operations. Upon receiving the alert, police officers and auxiliary police from the Zhongdu Police Station quickly arrived and joined the rescue efforts with the public. The final rescue process was recorded by onlookers: three men found a long rope for protection, went below the waterfall, and one swimmer in trunks dove forcefully into the water. Shortly after, he surfaced holding the girl. The thin girl, wearing a swimsuit and sandals, had already turned pale. The crowd carried her out of the water and onto the bank for resuscitation. Unfortunately, having been trapped underwater for over 20 minutes, the girl could not be revived. It was learned that the girl, surnamed Huang, was 14 years old, from Zhaisa, with her father working in Guangdong. That day, she had gone to Xiangshui with her grandfather and cousin to play in the water. While her grandfather and cousin were swimming nearby, the girl went to jump from a high point near the waterfall, slipped into the deep water, and disappeared.

Title: What to do if the phone's positioning signal is interrupted? Content: What to do if the phone's positioning signal is interrupted? 1. Frequent area changes causing frequent network disconnections. If your phone only experiences frequent network disconnections during long-distance travel (such as trains, high-speed rails, long-distance buses, etc.), it is because such roads are generally built in areas far from cities, where the network coverage capability of operators is insufficient. The network is better near densely populated areas, but the network coverage quality may be poor in areas far from population centers, leading to repeated network connection and disconnection. 2. Poor network quality of an operator in a specific area. If your phone only experiences this phenomenon in the same area, it is recommended to observe the network status of other phones with the same operator's SIM card or check the network status in other areas to determine if other phones have the same issue. If the phone cannot be located, try moving to a more open area without obstructions or interfering devices, and it should return to normal. However, if it cannot be located regardless of the location, it is necessary to check if the gyroscope and internal components are damaged, which requires handling by after-sales service.

Title: Transitioning from the Design Industry to Journal Editor, Salary Doubled, from Working Overnight on Drawings to 8-Hour Office Work, Exclaiming It's Amazing! Content: After staying in the design industry for a long time, I felt numb as if I had been emotionally manipulated. When I switched careers and submitted resumes, there was no response. A while ago, I participated in an English interview at a company (), applying for the position of Assistant Journal Editor. As someone from the design industry, I thought a salary between 5-7k was normal or even generous. Unexpectedly, they offered quite a lot—just look at the image below! It shocked me! During the internship, the monthly take-home pay is over 8k, and after regularization, it's over 12k, with an 8-hour workday. After passing the interview, I needed to attend offline training (corporate culture, job content training and introduction, experience). After the training, there was an interview with the district manager (on the day I went for training, the interview ended at 6 PM. The company floor was empty except for the HR who guided me and the editor-in-chief who conducted the interview. The manager was abroad on business, so it was via online video). During the interview, I was asked if I could accept sitting in front of a computer for 8 hours a day!!!!!!!!!!!! Fortunately, I hate working overnight. Whether it was final design projects in school or other design tasks, I never stayed up late drawing—except for binge-watching dramas or having fun! No amount of exclamation marks can express the speechlessness of design industry practitioners—it’s truly suffocating! Just 8 hours! And no drawing required! There are two work schedules to choose from based on personal preference: one is working from 8 AM to 5 PM, with a lunch break included; the other is working from 9 AM to 6 PM, with a 1.5-hour lunch break. I calmly said, 'I can accept it. I really like this work mode. I prefer reading text and can sit still.' Inside, I was shocked! Do people outside the design industry really not know how exhausting design work is? Perhaps they don’t realize how exploitative it is—with such meager pay! I often wonder why I know so many software tools yet end up tired and underpaid... Maybe this is the so-called 'industry barrier'! I was inwardly delighted... but on the surface, I had to pretend the job was tough and that I could barely accept it, expressing my willingness... Acting isn’t easy! The image above shows comments from non-design industry people interviewing for this job: 'This job strains the eyes.' They’re not wrong. Staring at a computer is eye-straining, but an assistant editor’s job involves computer work... See, as someone from the design industry, I’m so resilient—my tolerance threshold is high, and I’ve been conditioned to even persuade others to accept it. Graduate students in STEM fields doing experiments (especially those required to clock in and out at the lab) share the same sentiment as design professionals—they think it’s not bad. One person’s poison is another’s nectar! So, breaking out of the design industry truly opens up a world of opportunities! Since this series is based on chat records: topics derived from conversations among friends (or submissions) that I want to discuss, let’s keep it casual. I hope you enjoy this format of sharing! Looking forward to more exchanges with everyone—everyone is welcome to join the conversation and explore various topics together! That’s all for today. Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments! —END— Likes and shares are the greatest support! Title: NICE900 Door Machine Encoder Tuning Fault and Troubleshooting Content: NICE900 Door Machine Encoder Tuning Fault and Troubleshooting

Technical Data Provider: Gao Tian
I. Fault Description
The door machine does not operate and does not open the door. However, there is an open door command on the car top board (the open door command light is on, indicating a normal state, but the door does not open). Checking the main control cabinet board shows fault code: E53. Sometimes, no fault is reported, but the elevator door does not open.
II. Troubleshooting
1. Restore the door machine FA01 to factory settings and rewrite all parameters in F9!
2. Set F002 to 1 (Manual)
3. Set F600 to 4
Motor magnetic pole tuning will begin, and the door will open to the 20 position! If the door machine does not report a fault afterwards, the magnetic pole tuning is successful.
III. Special Problem Troubleshooting
a. If E20 is reported, check if the wiring is correct;
b. If 19 is reported, check if the door machine encoder AB phase wires are swapped.

Title: Shaodong: Liuze Town People's Congress Deputies and CPPCC Members Conduct Special Research on the Operational Difficulties of Special Breeding Households Content: On the morning of April 28, Liuze Town organized municipal and town-level People's Congress deputies and CPPCC members to visit Zhongyi Village in Liuze Town. They conducted a field investigation of the Shaodong Wanshun Special Breeding Base to gain a detailed understanding of the farm's production situation. The deputies, members, and the farm owner discussed the current difficulties and potential solutions from different perspectives. Zhongyi Village is a provincial-level impoverished village, and the Shaodong Wanshun Special Breeding Base is a poverty alleviation project for the village. The project involved the transfer of over 50 acres of land, with all 34 impoverished households in the village signing equity participation agreements. Since June 2018, over 4.5 million yuan has been invested. The original plan was to breed bamboo rats and snakes. Currently, there are over 7,000 snakes, and the bamboo rat breeding facility has been completed. Mass breeding was originally planned, but investment stopped after the COVID-19 pandemic outbreak. Currently, wildlife has been blacklisted and banned from trade, leaving the farm depleting its resources and struggling to sustain itself. The farm owner hopes the government will introduce specific policies as soon as possible to provide direction and support for special breeding. The attending deputies and members unanimously agreed that the farm should continue to do a good job in wildlife protection and supervision, and accelerate the transformation pace by leveraging the existing site and facilities. Title: No More Bailouts for Real Estate Content: The US has escalated its technological suppression against China once again. The new executive order on restrictions on investment in China will further hinder China's development in cutting-edge fields such as semiconductors, quantum information, and artificial intelligence. The US has almost comprehensively upgraded its containment of China in the technological sphere, creating an atmosphere of impending storm. Bailing out real estate again will likely lead to becoming a second-rate country. However, facing the US technological suppression, there doesn't seem to be much discussion in the domestic public opinion arena; instead, the most discussed topic is how to bail out real estate. When choosing between bailing out technology and bailing out real estate, the latter is probably the choice. Does real estate need a bailout? In recent days, news has been circulating that the four major first-tier cities are about to relax purchase restrictions, and signs of a real estate revival are causing a stir in agent groups. It is certain that there will be new policies for adjusting the real estate market. But is strong stimulus really effective? Can it really boost real estate? This still needs to be observed. Over the past few decades, high housing prices have severely squeezed the Chinese economy, with 40% of loans going to individual housing mortgages. The negative problems brought by high housing prices are increasing. Everyone knows what's going on, so why still promote real estate? Bailing out real estate again will inevitably lead to further capital shifting from the real economy to the virtual economy. An ordinary person's manufacturing enterprise, built through a lifetime of hard work, is worth less than buying a small apartment in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, or Shenzhen. On the other hand, it raises the operating costs of the real economy. Many enterprises, including high-tech ones, have to increase salaries because rents are rising, housing prices are rising, and if salaries aren't increased, employees leave. High wages and high social security contributions place a greater burden on enterprises, adding insult to injury for technology companies already struggling to survive. In recent years, despite significant GDP growth, domestic residents' internal demand has not grown rapidly along with it; instead, the growth rate has slowed or even shrunk. In recent years, despite significant GDP growth, domestic residents' internal demand has not grown rapidly along with it; instead, the growth rate has slowed or even shrunk. The most correct approach to real estate is to respect market laws, let real estate clear naturally, and let it complete its historical mission in the tide of the market economy. If domestic high housing prices cannot return to rationality but are pushed even higher, it will not only be detrimental to China's economic development but could also destroy the Chinese economy, wipe out the achievements of decades of reform and opening up, and destroy the wealth foundation accumulated by the people over decades. For China, high housing prices are a very dangerous signal. This danger is also reflected in the nation's fate. The US's technological suppression is the best proof. Taking chips as an example, since Trump launched the trade war in 2018, the blockade in the chip sector has continuously intensified. Five years have passed, and so far, the domestic chip catch-up strategy has not been very effective. In fact, the situation of being constrained by others in chips has not changed. The recent anti-corruption storm in the chip sector has drawn more attention to the issues of the "National Integrated Circuit Industry Investment Fund Co., Ltd.", commonly known as the "Big Fund". Facts have proven that pouring money in without a good mechanism yields no results. After the "Chip Making" movement, the industry did not achieve breakthrough results. Domestically produced chips, in terms of quantity, only account for about 10% of the market share, with the rest relying on imports; in terms of quality, the困境 of 14-nanometer chips has not been broken through. If resources are poured into real estate again at this time, letting steel and cement drive the Chinese economy once more, then the situation of being technologically constrained by others will not change. Bailing out real estate again will ultimately relegate China to a second-rate country. Japan is the best example. Recently, there have also been rumors that purchase restrictions in first-tier cities will be completely lifted, meaning funds from across the country can flow into buying property in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Shenzhen. Regarding the attitude towards real estate, we can refer to neighboring Japan. Starting in 1990, Japan's Ministry of Finance took the lead in introducing a "Policy for Controlling the Total Volume of Real Estate Financing," requiring financial institutions to keep the growth rate of real estate loans from exceeding the growth rate of total loan balances. After this policy was introduced, the growth rate of Japan's real estate loan balance rapidly dropped from 15.3% in March 1990 to 0.3% in March 1991. This policy significantly reduced real estate financing activities in Japan. At the same time, after the Japanese real estate bubble burst, they did not bail out the property market but instead removed its last lifeline. Why didn't Japan bail out the property market at that time? They weren't foolish; they didn't want to ruin it. After the property market absorbed excessive funds, manufacturing and consumption were severely compressed. In the 1990s, Japan's household leverage ratio reached 69.5%, and the household debt-to-asset ratio reached 114.69%, meaning the entire population was in debt. The higher the household leverage ratio... Our bank data shows that in 2022, the debt ratio of urban households in China had already reached 56.5%. This means that nationwide debt is already very serious. At this point, bailing out real estate again – aren't we afraid of causing a greater crisis? Title: Scary! Ibuprofen Added to Commonly Consumed Beverages
Content: In hot summer weather, drinking herbal tea is a daily habit for many people. However, a question arises: if the herbal tea has other "additives"... can it still be considered herbal tea? On June 6th, the Second People's Court of Dongguan City, Guangdong Province, used three cases of producing and selling toxic and harmful food as examples to remind businesses to operate legally. It mentioned that a herbal tea shop owner was prosecuted for selling herbal tea with "additives."

Herbal Tea Shop Owner Sentenced for Selling "Laced" Herbal Tea
The defendant, Li Mou, was originally the operator of a certain herbal tea shop in Shatian, Dongguan City. In 2024, during his business operations, Li Mou arbitrarily added powder containing acetaminophen and ibuprofen into the herbal tea he sold. On March 11, 2024, the Shatian Branch of the Dongguan Market Supervision Administration conducted an inspection of the said herbal tea shop according to law, sampled six types of herbal tea being sold, and seized a packet of suspicious white powder from the scene. Tests revealed that some of the sampled herbal teas contained ingredients such as acetaminophen, chlorpheniramine, and ibuprofen. The powder seized from the scene contained acetaminophen and ibuprofen. On September 5, 2024, police officers arrested Li Mou.

The court, after hearing the case, held that the defendant Li Mou's actions constituted the crime of producing and selling toxic and harmful food and should be punished according to law. After being brought to justice, Li Mou confessed his crime, which could lead to a lighter punishment according to law. Considering that Li Mou's crime was relatively minor, he showed a good attitude of admitting guilt and repenting, there was no risk of reoffending, serving his sentence back in society would not cause adverse effects and was sufficient to achieve the purposes of punishment and education, he could be given a suspended sentence according to law. Ultimately, the Second People's Court of Dongguan City found Li Mou guilty of producing and selling toxic and harmful food, sentenced him to six months in prison, suspended for one year, and imposed a fine of 2,000 yuan.

Judge's Statement
Herbal tea is considered ordinary food. Substances like acetaminophen and ibuprofen are drugs explicitly prohibited from being added or used in food production and operation. Li Mou's actions could endanger consumers' health and disrupt the normal operating order of the herbal tea industry. This case reminds all businesses not to use gimmicks like "secret family recipe" or "100% natural" to cover up illegal additions. It also reminds consumers to strengthen their awareness of food safety identification and immediately report illegal business practices to the relevant authorities.

"Drinking Taboos" for Herbal Tea
First, never treat herbal tea as water or an ordinary beverage. Although it is a Chinese herbal medicine beverage, Chinese herbs are still medicine; beware of side effects.
Second, never drink too much. Even water can cause "water intoxication" if consumed excessively. Let alone a herbal plant-based beverage that might have nephrotoxicity; drinking too much can反而 increase the burden on the liver and kidneys.
Third, never assume that the more bitter the herbal tea or the darker its color, the more effective it is. The taste and color are related to the herbs used and are not directly linked to efficacy.
Fourth, never regard herbal tea as a "miracle cure." After all, herbal tea that works after one bowl is likely laced with Western medicine. If you trust Traditional Chinese Medicine more, it's better to go to a regular TCM clinic and have a doctor prescribe Chinese medicine when you are sick.
—Source: Southern Daily, Southern Metropolis Daily, Guangzhou Broadcasting Station, Shenzhen Big News

Title: Revealing the Lucrative Business of Catteries Content: In recent years, as people's standard of living has gradually improved, the demand for spiritual companionship has become increasingly evident. Pet-related businesses, whether online pet eating shows, the rise of various pet brands, or offline consumption venues like various types of cat cafes, dog cafes, have sprung up like mushrooms. This actually contains a lot of money-making opportunities, and of course, many gray and highly profitable projects have also emerged. Many people find that buying a cat from a formal cattery is almost like buying a luxury item; a random cat can cost four or five thousand, easily over ten thousand, and even tens of thousands is not uncommon. Some people wanting to buy a cat, after comparing the price of a purebred cat from a formal cattery with a "purebred" from backyard breeding, naturally feel: "Why are cattery cats so much more expensive? Is it robbery?" My colleague Tingting has two cats, both Persians, one male and one female. I visited her home once, and the two cats were very cute, looked noble, and were well-liked. Last May, Tingting noticed the female cat's soft belly starting to swell. One morning in August, she woke up to find five additional cats in the house overnight. Suddenly having five more cats, and not needing so many herself, she ended up giving two to colleagues. She had no choice but to try selling the three kittens herself on Xianyu. It was just an attempt, but surprisingly, all three were sold within about 10 days, for a total of about 7000 RMB, averaging 2300 RMB per cat, with the most expensive selling for 2800 RMB. The buyers were genuine; they had wanted a cat for a long time but found formal catteries too expensive, so they bought when they saw them on Xianyu. Furthermore, in July this year, Tingting found the female cat's belly swelling again. She didn't expect cats to be so fertile. She looked it up online and found they can conservatively have 2 litters of 10 kittens per year. The key is that the cost is actually very low, mainly just daily cat food and some other expenses. It seems breeding cats is a highly profitable business with minimal investment. Let's think about it, how much money can you roughly make by opening a cattery? Feeding is mainly daily cat food, occasionally supplemented with chicken breast, milk cake cans, fresh goat milk, etc., averaging about 400 RMB per cat per month. Additionally, two vaccines and one deworming cost 190 RMB. These are the main costs. The price of cats varies by location; generally, prices are higher in big cities like Shanghai. Cats of the same quality can sell for around 2000-3000 RMB in Henan, while higher quality cats can exceed 4000 RMB. I've roughly calculated the cost of raising cats. One male cat paired with three females; the cost of buying the cats is about 5000 RMB. You can't buy at this price from professional catteries (they are more expensive); buying privately on Xianyu is more cost-effective. The annual feeding cost per cat is 4000 RMB, so for one male and three females, it shouldn't exceed 15,000 RMB per year. If using cheaper domestic cat food brands, the cost might be around 10,000 RMB. Three healthy females can have 6 litters per year, averaging 5 kittens per litter, totaling 30 kittens. Calculating at an average price of 2500 RMB, the annual output value is roughly 70,000-80,000 RMB. Subtracting costs, the profit is at least 5 times, very stable. Few companies nowadays have a 5 times annual profit. I think cat breeding is quite suitable as a side business. It's almost impossible for kittens to be left unsold. As long as they are not hybrid breeds, the chance of them staying unsold is low. Some catteries specifically buy cats (some catteries focus on breeding, others on sales), albeit at below market prices, reducing profit compared to selling yourself, but still leaving at least a 3 times profit. Of course, besides the high profit, this process requires a significant amount of effort; it's not simply easy money. Life Aspect: Running a cattery requires a substantial investment of energy. Daily environmental cleaning, monitoring pregnant cats, checking on newborn kittens. You will lose a lot of free time. Work Aspect: Do you plan to run the cattery full-time or part-time? My personal suggestion for beginners is to start part-time. After all, you are new to the industry with limited knowledge and experience. Quitting a stable job for an unknown path carries higher risks. If you have diverse income sources and ample time, then full-time operation is more feasible. Financial Aspect: Besides the cats, you need to consider their living space. If you need to rent a place, consider the rental cost, which varies by city. Knowledge Aspect: There is a lot you need to learn. For example: ① How to choose breeding cats and avoid pitfalls. ② Feline nutrition knowledge – what to feed at each stage, what to avoid. ③ Daily cat care. ④ Feline genetics knowledge – learning how to breed excellent cats. ⑤ Handling common illnesses. Health Aspect: Health issues are inevitable in breeding; you will encounter problems. You need to learn how to handle common cat illnesses instead of rushing to the vet for every issue. It can be said that a breeder who cannot handle common illnesses can save 80% of medical costs by learning how to do so. Final Words: Running a cattery can indeed make money, with high profits. However, the effort required, like most industries, is not easy. If you have a short attention span and want to try just because you see others making money, I don't recommend this path, as it's not as smooth as you might think. If you have the confidence and determination, you can start part-time as a side business, beginning on a small scale.

Title: What to do after signing a house viewing agreement Content: 【Enter area, get free renovation quotes】 Many users, when buying a house, use agency companies to select properties, view houses, and make purchases. To protect their own interests, agencies will have users sign a house viewing agreement, which indirectly locks in that user. But what if a user, after signing the agreement, no longer wants to cooperate with that agency? What should you do after signing a house viewing agreement? What should you pay attention to when entrusting an agency to view houses? Let's find out with the editor below! \r\r\rWhat to do after signing a house viewing agreement \r\r\rFirst, carefully check the signed agreement to see if there are specific clauses indicating "full authorization" or "exclusive agency" by the agency; if not, you can try to have the landlord revoke the agency's qualification to sell the house. Once the qualification is revoked, the buyer can sign the contract directly with the landlord. \r\r\r\rWhat to pay attention to when entrusting an agency to view houses \r\r\r1. Choose a reputable agency \r\r\rAccording to experts from Qijia.com, when choosing an agency, you must carefully review its business qualifications, check its business license and other certificates, and understand its professional level and service quality. If you choose an agency with poor qualifications and bad attitude, it will not only be difficult to find an ideal property but also waste a lot of time and effort, and there is a risk of the agency disappearing. \r\r\r\r2. Understand the average housing price \r\r\rBefore viewing houses, you need to have a general understanding of the average housing price in the city area. If you are not familiar with the average price, you can easily be misled by the agent during the purchase process, leading to additional costs, and the agent can profit more from the price difference. \r\r\r\r3. Avoid full authorization \r\r\rWhether you are renting or buying, it is not recommended to grant full authorization when entrusting an agent. Title: Are You Suitable for Buying a House? Evaluate Your Purchasing Power and You'll Know. Content: Some people only realize after finding a house they like that they either don't have enough for the down payment or that the monthly mortgage exceeds their affordability. This ends up wasting their valuable time for nothing. The reason such awkward situations occur is essentially because you didn't properly evaluate your purchasing power before buying a house. Buying a house requires a detailed income and expenditure plan. Rather than being able to afford the house but not raise a child, it's better to assess your purchasing power first and then act according to your means. 1. Estimate Personal or Family Disposable Funds Given the current real estate market conditions, regardless of the type of property, the funds required for purchase are often substantial, typically involving the entire family's savings. This means buying a house is a matter for the whole family. Therefore, purchasing a house should be comprehensively considered based on your own or your family's payment capacity. For example, if you want to buy a house, how much savings does your family have? What are the amounts of liquid assets, financial investments, and the average monthly income and other income of the family, such as rental income, interest income, etc.? Determine exactly how much disposable funds are currently available. After calculating a relatively accurate amount, remember this: it is unwise to use all disposable funds for the house purchase. You should retain some funds to meet daily living needs and set aside funds for unexpected emergencies. 2. Purchasing Methods There are two main methods: applying for a mortgage or paying in full. If you have sufficient funds on hand, you can choose to pay for the house in one lump sum. This method avoids paying handling fees and bank loan interest, often comes with discounts, and has simpler procedures, but it also carries certain follow-up risks. Currently, most people choose to apply for a mortgage when buying a house. If opting for a loan, pay attention to two key points: Are the disposable funds sufficient for the down payment? Do you have the ability to repay the loan? The combination of down payment ability and repayment ability constitutes purchasing power. Furthermore, you should reasonably formulate a repayment plan based on your monthly income. When buying a house with a loan, don't forget the monthly mortgage payment. Therefore, it is often recommended that the monthly payment should be below 40%-50% of the total income for homebuyers aged 25-30, and below 30% of the total income for those aged 35 and above. It's best to set aside a year's worth of mortgage payments. 3. Ability to Maintain the House Purchasing power is important, but the ability to maintain the house is also necessary, and the costs of upkeep cannot be ignored. If buying with a loan, besides the monthly loan repayment, there are many fees to pay, such as various living expenses, property fees, water fees, electricity fees, heating fees, and gas fees, all of which the homebuyer must consider. The above is the full content of this article. Correctly evaluating your purchasing power can help minimize the life pressure on homebuyers after the purchase. Therefore, it is essential to conduct a purchasing power assessment before buying a house to avoid excessive pressure later. This is also why some people are largely unaffected after buying a house, while others feel immense pressure. Recommended Reading The house is registered under both spouses' names, but the wife gets nothing in the divorce. Why? Isn't it tiring for someone who hasn't even bought a house yet to constantly think about rising and falling prices? The bank helped you pay 70% of the house price and isn't worried about a market crash; you haven't even gathered your 30% yet but are worrying yourself sick. Title: What fault does Midea air conditioner display PP indicate? Content: If Midea embedded air conditioner displays PP: Compressor phase sequence reverse connection fault. PP drive protection: During compressor startup or operation, if the controller detects no feedback signal from the compressor, abnormal compressor load, or poor compressor startup, it will shut down the outdoor unit and display the protection code. (If startup is abnormal, it can be started 5 times consecutively. If startup is abnormal, abnormal protection can be re-initiated.) 1. If the compressor cannot start, check whether the three phases U, V, W of the compressor line are connected incorrectly or reversed. 2. If a fault is reported after the compressor runs, replace the module board. 3. When the compressor restarts shortly after shutdown, a fault alarm caused by pressure imbalance is a normal protection, and the compressor will restart after a long time. Midea air conditioner display content fault or protection. Extended information: Midea air conditioner display content fault or protection: E0 EEPROM parameter error. E1 Indoor and outdoor unit communication fault. E2 Zero-crossing detection error. E3 Fan speed out of control. E4 Temperature fuse open circuit protection. E5 Outdoor temperature sensor fault. E6 Indoor temperature sensor fault. P0 Module protection. P1 Overvoltage or undervoltage protection. P2 Compressor maximum temperature protection. 3.2 Outdoor main control panel LED display. When the Midea air conditioner displays a "PP" fault, it may be caused by the following reasons: 1. Power Title: Check if the air conditioner is powered normally. Ensure the power outlet is working correctly, and check if the power cord is plugged in properly, or if there is an open circuit or damage. 2. Air conditioner control board fault: The "PP" fault may be related to the air conditioner control board. Try restarting the air conditioner. If the problem persists, the control board may need to be repaired or replaced. 3. Sensor fault: The temperature sensor inside the air conditioner may be damaged or failed, causing the "PP" fault to display. In this case, it is recommended to contact a professional technician for inspection or sensor replacement. 4. Overload protection: If the air conditioner operates beyond its rated load, the system may trigger the overload protection mechanism, resulting in the "PP" fault display. In this situation, it is recommended to reduce the load on the air conditioner and ensure it operates within the rated power range. 5. Other faults: If the above methods fail to resolve the issue, there may be other faults, such as circuit faults or compressor problems. In this case, it is best to contact a professional air conditioner repair technician for diagnosis and repair. In summary, when a Midea air conditioner displays a "PP" fault, first check the power supply, control board, sensors, and load conditions. If the problem persists, it is recommended to seek professional air conditioner repair services to resolve the fault. Midea air conditioner displaying PP indicates a compressor phase sequence reverse connection fault. Possible reasons are as follows: The outdoor unit electrical control box is damaged. It is necessary to open the outdoor unit electrical control box and check if the wiring inside is aged. Poor compressor startup requires a professional to replace the motor wires in the modular air conditioner that are aged or broken. It is necessary to open the indoor unit and replace the motor wires. If none of the above reasons are correct, it is best to contact a professional repair company. They can provide you with professional technical support.

Title: Can online teaching replace classroom teaching, and what are the advantages and disadvantages of each? Content: Distance education conducted over the internet is a new educational model that has emerged with the development of technology. It undoubtedly has many advantages, but I do not agree with replacing traditional face-to-face in-school education with distance education as the primary method of higher education, because traditional face-to-face instruction plays an important role that online education cannot replace. Firstly, the function of a teacher, since ancient times, has not only been to impart knowledge and resolve doubts, but also to transmit the 'Dao' (the Way) – that is, not only teaching knowledge but also methods of scholarship and principles of conduct. The personal charisma of an excellent teacher can even influence a student's entire life. For example, Yang Changji influenced Mao Zedong's life. The transmission and influence of scholarly methods, principles of conduct, and personal charisma can obviously only be achieved through person-to-person, face-to-face interaction, which is something online education fundamentally cannot accomplish. Secondly, just as the competition mechanism is the internal driving force for the robust development of modern society, it is also a form that cannot be ignored in higher education. However, in online education, there is only one learning subject: the student themselves. The student faces a screen in a virtual world; they do not know who their academic competitors are, nor their respective strengths and weaknesses. Therefore, it is difficult to foster the kind of healthy, competitive learning atmosphere of mutual encouragement found in traditional face-to-face classrooms. The initiative and motivation of students might consequently be significantly reduced. Thirdly, university students are not only at a life stage of acquiring knowledge but also at a stage of forming their complete personality. The daily campus life where students live together, their multi-directional interactions, mutual help, care, and even love, have a significant impact on the formation of their sound personalities. Imagine if online education became the main form of higher education, and romantic campus life disappeared – this would have immeasurable negative consequences for the healthy and normal development of the younger generation! In summary, the internet can only transmit information. In this information-driven society, not everything can be informationalized. Personality, inspiration, taste, sincerity, etc., cannot be informationalized, and these are precisely the indispensable elements of our higher education.
