Title: Protected kraits and cobras are proliferating rampantly in rural areas. Who will protect the safety of rural people? Content: First, let me share a little piece of common knowledge. The krait is highly venomous. Its venom primarily contains neurotoxins, which can quickly affect the nervous system of prey or threats, leading to paralysis and even death. Therefore, extreme caution is required when encountering a krait. The krait has been included in the 'List of Terrestrial Wild Animals Protected by the State that are Beneficial or of Important Economic or Scientific Research Value' issued by the China National Forestry and Grassland Administration on June 30, 2023, and is classified as Vulnerable (VU) in the China Biodiversity Red List. The cobra genus (scientific name: Naja) is a genus of animals under the family Elapidae, order Squamata [2]. As of 2023, the Catalogue of Life (CoL) recognizes 33 species and 7 subspecies within this genus [7]. Cobras are also highly venomous. Their venom is a mixed toxin, containing both neurotoxins and hemotoxins, making it extremely potent. Many people die from cobra bites each year. Both of these highly venomous snake species are currently protected animals and cannot be casually killed. But when these protected, highly venomous animals are rapidly reproducing right where you live, posing a significant threat to your life, should humans still protect them? Is human life more important, or is their life more important? My home is in the hilly areas of Hunan. The warm and humid springs and summers create an environment perfectly suited for the reproduction of these two highly venomous snakes. When I was a child working in the fields, I often encountered water snakes and yellow-bellied snakes (commonly known as 'yellow belly'). Even though I knew these two types were non-venomous, my first reaction upon seeing any snake was to run, because I have an innate fear of snakes. One time, I was home alone and saw a snake slither through a crack in the door into my bedroom. I was so scared my hair stood on end. I ran out immediately to get help. By the time I brought an adult back, we searched the room for a long time but couldn't find the snake. I was too frightened to sleep in that room again. Another time, on a summer morning, I went to the field to pick water spinach. Walking along the ridge, I suddenly stepped on something soft. Looking down, I had stepped on a water snake. I was scared out of my wits, let out a scream, and ran like crazy for half a kilometer (absolutely no exaggeration). I believe I'm not the only one born with a fear of snakes. Most of the snakes I encountered as a child were non-venomous. Although I was very afraid, there were many young adults in the village back then. If you encountered a snake, an adult would come and chase it away. I rarely heard rumors of villagers dying from snakebites. One or two decades have passed. For some reason, the number of highly venomous snakes in rural areas has increased significantly now, and reports of farmers being bitten are becoming more frequent. A few years ago, a rural woman in her 60s went to the field to pick tobacco leaves a little after 3 a.m. She was bitten by a krait, was sent to the hospital, but could not be saved. There have also been cases of amputations following krait bites. In any case, the number of people bitten by venomous snakes has increased in recent years, and the amount of antivenom serum consumed by hospitals annually has also risen. Snakes prefer to live in dark, damp places. Nowadays, many old rural houses have collapsed and are left unattended. These collapsed old houses have become ideal breeding grounds for snakes. Just from March to June this year, I have seen kraits at least three times near my home, the largest being over a meter long, and these sightings were at night. To make a living, most young and middle-aged adults from rural areas work away from home, returning only during the Chinese New Year. At that time, both venomous and non-venomous snakes are hibernating, so many rural youth are unaware of the serious threat these venomous snakes now pose to their families, especially the elderly and children. Since most snakes are active at night, and rural road lighting is often poor, some elderly people with poor eyesight might not see a venomous snake clearly if they encounter one at night. Accidentally stepping on a snake could have unimaginable consequences. While kraits and cobras do not actively attack humans, if you step on one, see if it bites you or not. Children are curious. They don't know which snakes are venomous and which are not. If they encounter a venomous snake, they might even want to catch it to play with. For children over seven or eight years old, it's somewhat better, as children of that age know to run. But what can a two or three-year-old child do if they encounter a venomous snake? We all know that the first thing to do after a snakebite is to go to the hospital immediately and try to remember what kind of snake it was, so the correct antivenom can be administered at the hospital. However, many rural areas are quite far from county hospitals. The most remote village in our county takes three hours to reach the county town by car. If bitten by a krait or cobra, what would be the consequence of receiving antivenom only after three or four hours? Not every rural household owns a car, and not all elderly people staying behind in the villages know how to drive. If the person bitten cannot drive, they have to wait for the hospital ambulance to arrive. This delay can be fatal for the patient. Furthermore, in many places, medical insurance does not cover the costs of snakebite treatment. If medical help is received promptly, a few days in the hospital might lead to recovery. If treatment is delayed and amputation is required, the medical expenses are not cheap and could potentially exceed a rural family's annual income. I am not opposed to protecting these snakes. It's just that these snakes should stay away from human settlements. They should live in remote mountains, not around human habitation. They should not exist around your and my loved ones. TV programs and books often say that humans should coexist peacefully with animals. In my view, humans can only peacefully coexist with animals that do not harm human life. Animals that pose a threat to human life should either be protected in cages or kept far away from human living areas. Previously, there was talk of protecting wild boars. When wild boars come down from the mountains and destroy corn and sweet potatoes, it's the farmers who suffer the losses. Now, there is talk of protecting snakes, especially highly venomous ones. The snakes are indeed well-protected and can run rampant in every corner of the countryside. It's even possible that one might slither into a rural bed someday. Snakes are oviparous and have strong reproductive capabilities. In the wild, a 3-year-old female snake can lay 5-8 eggs per clutch. Female snakes aged 4-6 years can lay 12-18 eggs per clutch. At this rate of reproduction, in a few years, you might see snakes as soon as you step outside in rural areas. To use an perhaps inappropriate analogy: if I and my family lived in a densely populated urban residential area, and I saw snakes around, I could call the fire department to catch them. In that case, I would also support strongly protecting venomous snakes, because protecting them doesn't affect me, and a proliferation of venomous snakes wouldn't threaten my family's lives. One never feels the pain until the knife cuts one's own flesh. Perhaps we farmers lack knowledge and don't understand the macro-level goals of snake conservation. But I know that no animal, no matter how expensive or rare, is greater than or equal to human life. Here, I have a humble suggestion: Could the relevant authorities distribute some snake repellents or snake-catching medicines in rural areas? Could these highly venomous snakes be driven away from the vicinity of rural living areas? This way, they are protected, and the farmers are also protected.

Title: Tianjin City Focuses on Strengthening the Cultivation and Management of Social Emergency Forces Content: Conducting river patrols, water rescue training, waterlogging drainage drills, delivering drowning prevention lectures in summer childcare programs, cooperating in filming short dramas for drowning prevention awareness, providing medical emergency support for events like summer student basketball tournaments... Recently, social emergency forces in Tianjin have been active in multiple fields, playing their roles to the best of their abilities. In recent years, Tianjin has comprehensively strengthened the cultivation and management of social emergency forces. Through coordinated efforts across municipal and district-level departments, a "four-haves" on-site coordination mechanism has been established, featuring coordinating organizations, workplaces, support systems, and guarantee conditions. Nine core social emergency forces have been incorporated into this coordination mechanism for management. Standardized Guidance: Achieving Breakthroughs from Scratch Li Li, Deputy Director of the Rescue Planning Division of the Tianjin Municipal Emergency Management Bureau, introduced that in 2023, the bureau, together with relevant departments, formulated and issued the "Opinions on Further Promoting the Healthy Development of Social Emergency Forces in Tianjin," clarifying the direction for cultivating and managing these forces and shifting the management approach from encouragement and guidance to standardized guidance. According to the "Opinions," the emergency management department performs the duties of the business competent unit or industry management department, cooperates with civil affairs departments in registration review, and supports relevant social organizations in legally establishing social emergency forces. Departments such as emergency management leverage existing resources to promote the sharing of training resources between social emergency forces and professional rescue teams, and jointly conduct training, drills, and competitions. Zhen Yi, a staff member of the Disaster Rescue Coordination Section of the Jinghai District Emergency Management Bureau, said: "The 'Opinions' have resolved many issues, such as how to connect resources and support the development of social emergency forces, promoting their rapid development." Shortly after the issuance of the "Opinions," in March 2023, the Jinghai District Blue Sky Rescue Team was officially established. Jinghai is located in the lower reaches of the Haihe River Basin and is prone to flood disasters. Additionally, the district has a significant proportion of heavy industry, and the risk of production safety accidents cannot be ignored. The Jinghai District Blue Sky Rescue Team was established under the leadership of the Jinghai District Emergency Management Bureau. It possesses capabilities in water search and rescue, building collapse search and rescue, and can assist in grassroots public emergency rescue, publicity of self-rescue and mutual rescue knowledge, and initial response to disasters and accidents. During the team's preparation, under the guidance of the Tianjin Municipal Emergency Management Bureau, the Jinghai District Emergency Management Bureau mobilized local philanthropic enterprises to provide support and assistance to the rescue team; connected with the Jinghai District Red Cross Society and the Jinghai District Charity Association to mobilize some personnel from these organizations to join the rescue team; contacted experts from the Baodi District Red Cross Blue Sky Rescue Team to provide training and guidance for team members; and helped the team with publicity to facilitate public understanding and encourage more caring individuals to join. The Jinghai District Committee and District Government provided the rescue team with office space and training grounds. Similar to Jinghai District, in recent years, driven by the Tianjin Municipal Emergency Management Bureau, social emergency forces in districts like Hedong and Dongli have also achieved breakthroughs from scratch. By the end of 2023, there were 24 registered social emergency forces in the city, with over 4,800 personnel, covering rescue areas such as mountain, water, and building collapse. Establishing Rules and Systems: Reliance in Peacetime and Emergencies In late July and early August 2023, North China experienced heavy rainfall, and Zhuozhou City in Hebei Province was severely affected. The Tianjin Blue Sky Rescue Team dispatched 19 members, carrying rescue equipment such as assault boats and outboard motors, to rush to Zhuozhou for disaster relief and rescue operations. "The approval process was very smooth before departure," said Zhang Guangrui, Chairman of the Tianjin Blue Sky Rescue Team, recalling last year's cross-regional rescue. In March 2023, the Tianjin Municipal Emergency Management Bureau, the Municipal Civilization Office, and eight other departments jointly issued the "On-site Coordination Mechanism for Social Emergency Forces Participating in Major Disaster Relief Operations in Tianjin," providing support such as information consultation, highway passage, and logistical supply for social emergency forces involved in rescue operations. "We have incorporated nine social emergency forces with strong rescue capabilities, which are registered in the Ministry of Emergency Management's Social Emergency Force Rescue Coordination System, into the on-site coordination mechanism for disaster relief operations, for coordinated mobilization and coordination," said Ye Chunzi, a staff member of the Rescue Planning Division of the Tianjin Municipal Emergency Management Bureau. The Tianjin Blue Sky Rescue Team was established in June 2009 and is one of the city's nine core social emergency forces. Zhang Guangrui explained that in the past, during cross-regional rescues, the team had to obtain information themselves and then report to and apply for rescue with the local government of the disaster area. Now, the Tianjin Municipal Emergency Management Bureau provides information on rescue needs, and after applying through the system, the team can obtain a pass to enter the disaster area. "This shift from self-reporting to establishing an official reporting channel is a significant improvement," said Cui Wenjing, a director of the Tianjin Blue Sky Rescue Team. As one of the nine core social emergency forces, the Jinghai District Blue Sky Rescue Team participated in the cross-regional rescue following the 6.2-magnitude earthquake in Jishishan, Gansu. "On the way to the earthquake zone, the Municipal Emergency Management Bureau helped us arrange meals and accommodation," said Wang Nenghui, the team leader. "'How are the brothers doing? Have you eaten?' Throughout the journey, comrades from the municipal and district emergency management bureaus called us constantly, showing great concern, which deeply moved us." Tianjin adopts a hierarchical and territorial management model for social emergency forces across districts. During emergencies, the nine core social emergency forces are mobilized and coordinated by the Municipal Emergency Management Bureau to participate in rescues. During peacetime, all 24 teams are managed daily by their respective district emergency management bureaus. Municipal and district emergency management departments regularly organize training and drills for social emergency forces and encourage them to conduct safety publicity in enterprises, rural areas, communities, schools, and households. Social emergency forces submit monthly work reports to the district emergency management bureaus, reporting on personnel changes, pre-job training for new members, etc. The Municipal Emergency Management Bureau circulates selected information on publicity, training, and drills reported by the districts to facilitate exchange and learning among teams. Striving for Honors: Strengthening Incentives for Improvement "Today is International Volunteer Day, and we received the best gift. Thank you for your trust and support all along! We have finally fulfilled our mission and achieved our goal. Keep it up!" At the end of 2023, the Central Committee of the Communist Youth League and the China Young Volunteers Association awarded the Tianjin Blue Sky Rescue Team the "Outstanding Organization Award for Chinese Young Volunteers." Cui Wenjing reposted the news on her WeChat Moments that day, her excitement evident. "Our participation in this selection was jointly recommended by the Tianjin Municipal Emergency Management Bureau and the Tianjin Municipal Committee of the Communist Youth League. Over 100 units in the city participated in the selection, so it was not easy for us to stand out," said Cui Wenjing. Recognition incentives and resource sharing are two key measures the Tianjin Municipal Emergency Management Bureau uses to cultivate and support social emergency forces. The bureau has established a multi-departmental recognition and incentive platform. Through various forms such as the selection of Tianjin's Advanced Emergency Management Collectives and Individuals, the "Six Batches" Advanced Model Selection for Learning from Lei Feng Volunteer Service, and the "Most Beautiful Maritime Search and Rescuer" selection, it motivates social emergency forces and fosters a social atmosphere that cares about and supports their development. In 2024, the bureau leveraged the skills and instructor advantages of social emergency forces in areas like water, mountain, and building collapse rescue to organize the "Emergency Rescue Skills Training for Central Enterprises Stationed in Tianjin" volunteer activity. In mid-March and mid-June, catering to the different professional skill needs of the "National Team" and "Central Enterprise Team," the bureau organized the Tianjin Blue Sky Rescue Team to dispatch rescue technical experts to provide rescue skills training for the National Offshore Oil and Gas Emergency Rescue Tianjin Team and the China Construction Third Engineering Bureau North China Company Engineering Emergency Rescue Team, respectively. "The equipment of the National Offshore Oil and Gas Emergency Rescue Tianjin Team is quite advanced. Through mutual exchange, we also improved," said Zhang Guangrui. "Thanks to the coordination by the Municipal Emergency Management Bureau, we can use their facilities for training in the future, which somewhat solves our training ground issue." Wang Nenghui admitted that previously, social emergency forces operated independently. It was the emergency management department that united the various teams, bringing everyone together as one cohesive force.

Title: Self-healing discovery for stomach problems: Dry-wet separation is very important. Content: ————This is an eating method I personally practiced during my stomach nurturing period, which has been very effective for me. Since separating dry and wet foods, my stomach has become much more comfortable, gradually healed, and I have gained 3 pounds. I found on Xiaohongshu that some sisters also said that separating dry and wet foods made their stomachs much more comfortable, which resonated with me. .1. What is dry-wet separation? When eating, "wet" foods like water, soup, and porridge should be eaten separately from "dry" foods like steamed buns, vegetables, and meat, with an interval in between, not mixed together. Overall, it means controlling the moisture content in food to an appropriate level during meals. .2. Why does dry-wet separation make the stomach more comfortable? The dry-wet separation method properly controls the moisture content of food entering the stomach, avoiding simultaneous intake of food and large amounts of water, which dilutes gastric juice and increases digestive burden. Secondly, with this method, dry foods can be chewed more thoroughly and slowly in the mouth, allowing salivary enzymes to function. .Additionally, I personally feel that drinking large amounts of soup while eating causes a reflux sensation, making the stomach feel full and uncomfortable. Dry-wet separation also avoids this situation. .3. How to specifically practice dry-wet separation when eating? 👉 Drinking soup (or porridge) should be separated from eating: Drink soup more than half an hour before a meal, and wait more than an hour after eating before drinking again. Pre-meal drinking is more recommended. If I make soup, I drink it before eating and wait half an hour before having other food. .👉 Try not to drink soup during meals: If you really need to moisten your mouth, take small sips, just enough to moisten it. .👉 Be cautious with "dry-wet mixed" meals based on your condition: For example, noodle soup—though I really like it, when my stomach problem was severe, I didn't dare to drink the soup while eating the noodles. .👉 By analogy: Apply this principle to meals, snacks, and eating snacks. When consuming soups, porridges, or paste-like foods, separate them from other foods. .👉 Note: So-called "dry" foods should not be too dry, as this can also damage the gastric mucosa. Dry-wet separation means controlling the moisture content of food entering the stomach to a level that feels comfortable for you. Everyone can try dry-wet separation based on their own situation—I find it very useful! [Smirk R] @Health Potato

Title: Who Exactly Manages "Residential to Commercial" Conversion? Content: Who Exactly Manages "Residential to Commercial" Conversion? Qinghai News Network, September 19th – This newspaper reported on two street-facing residential buildings in the provincial capital's Beautiful Homeland community, where first-floor residents converted their homes into shops, causing dissatisfaction among other homeowners. Subsequently, reporters visited several residential communities and found the phenomenon of "residential to commercial" conversion to be quite severe. "Residential to Commercial" is Ubiquitous. With the continuous improvement of urban living environments, the growing and denser population has led to increasing demand for ancillary commercial services. Consequently, many residential communities have seen the emergence of shops converted from residences. Reporters found that almost every residential community has some degree of "residential to commercial" conversion. The ground floors of street-facing buildings, which were previously residential, have now largely been converted into shops. Some businesses have even set up shops inside the residential communities themselves. The types of "residential to commercial" conversions are becoming more diverse, ranging from trading companies in the past to beauty salons, private kitchens, mahjong parlors, massage parlors, etc. The trend of "residential to commercial" conversion is intensifying, and along with it, the social problems caused by such conversions are increasing, leading to numerous complaints from homeowners. The primary reasons for the prevalence of "residential to commercial" conversions are that residential properties not only have cheaper rent but also lower utility costs (like water and electricity) compared to commercial spaces. Additionally, being located near residential areas provides a large, fixed customer base. Most operators involved in "residential to commercial" conversions are small vendors and businesses with limited capital. Due to financial constraints, many cannot afford to operate in formal commercial streets. Renting a residential unit is not only cheaper but also allows for both business operations during the day and residence at night, making it economically advantageous. Numerous Drawbacks of "Residential to Commercial". Mr. Ma, a resident of Xining, stated that after the street-facing residential unit on the first floor of his building was converted into shops, private kitchens and mahjong parlors opened. Not only did the cooking fumes and noise bother the upstairs residents, but it also posed security risks to the community and potential safety hazards to the building's structure. Reporters summarized the main impacts of "residential to commercial" conversions on nearby residents: some first-floor homeowners break down walls to create storefronts, and some businesses, to meet operational needs,私自 alter the building's structure during renovation, damaging load-bearing walls, changing water and electrical pipelines, etc., which compromises the overall structural integrity of the residential building and affects its safety. Some "residential to commercial" businesses operating within residential communities, such as private kitchens, beauty salons, and mahjong parlors, bring in unfamiliar foot traffic, generating noise, fumes, and garbage that disrupt the community's normal order and the residents' peace and comfort. Furthermore, most "residential to commercial" businesses are hidden within residential communities, making supervision difficult for relevant authorities. Issues like unlicensed operations, tax evasion, and substandard food safety have become persistent problems in urban management. Who Exactly Manages "Residential to Commercial"? After visiting property management, construction, urban management, and industry and commerce departments, reporters learned that the first point of contact for residents opposing "residential to commercial" conversions is the property management company. However, a property management staff member said that regarding the issue of "residential to commercial" conversions, the property company is also helpless. The property belongs to the homeowners, and what they wish to do with it is beyond the property company's control. The property company lacks effective means of restraint and can only attempt mediation after problems arise, but the results of such mediation are often minimal. The construction department stated that if homeowners change the nature of the property's use, they can supervise during the renovation period, but only if the homeowner alters the building's structure. For instance, if load-bearing walls are damaged or key components are endangered during renovation, they can order a work stoppage and require the homeowner to restore the property to its original state. They can also impose penalties if the building's safety is affected. However, if the homeowner does not change the structure, the construction department has no authority to intervene. The urban management department stated that they only have the authority to act if "residential to commercial" conversion involves illegal structures, damage to public facilities, etc. Otherwise, they cannot manage it. The industry and commerce department stated that according to current regulations, as long as the operator provides the required materials meeting the standards for a business license, the department must issue the license. Whether the business location is a "residential to commercial" conversion is not within their review scope. Moreover, many businesses hidden within residential communities do not obtain business licenses as required. Without reports from the public, the industry and commerce department finds it difficult to supervise these unlicensed operators. Forming a Joint Force is Necessary to Manage "Residential to Commercial". "Regarding the supervision of 'residential to commercial' conversions, although each department has its own responsibilities, due to limitations in their authority, they cannot form a joint force. Therefore, the biggest challenge in regulating 'residential to commercial' conversions currently is the lack of a leading department and the failure of various departments to collaborate effectively," said Dr. Wei Renzhong, a sociology expert at the Qinghai Provincial Party School. Dr. Wei Renzhong believes that "residential to commercial" conversions bring convenience to residents to a certain extent and have a reason to exist. Therefore, they should not be outright banned but regulated. Although laws and regulations such as the "Property Rights Law" restrict the conversion of residential properties to commercial use, the lack of an effective supervision and management mechanism and a dedicated enforcement agency among various functional departments has resulted in the phenomenon not being effectively controlled. To regulate "residential to commercial" conversions, the "Property Rights Law" should first be taken as the guideline. The "Property Rights Law" stipulates that "residential to commercial" conversion must obtain the consent of the interested owners. Typically, 'interested owners' refer to all residents in the same building. If residents from other buildings can provide evidence that their interests are affected, their consent is also required. This procedure should be a prerequisite for any department handling "residential to commercial" conversion procedures. Simultaneously, the government should take the lead in organizing relevant functional departments to establish and improve coordination systems among them, based on the actual situation of "residential to commercial" conversions. Approval conditions should be detailed, and approval processes standardized, with relevant departments handling matters separately according to the regulations. Furthermore, government authorities in charge should strengthen the supervision of "residential to commercial" conversions. Homeowners considering "residential to commercial" conversion need to understand which industries are permissible within residential communities and which are not, and how to pursue the "residential to commercial" path legally and normatively.

Title: A woman in Guangyuan, Sichuan developed a fever exceeding 40°C 5 days after testing negative, pay attention to rest and don't be careless! Content: A 35-year-old woman in Guangyuan City, Sichuan Province improved after treatment for COVID-19 infection. An antigen test showed a negative result, so the woman happily returned to work. After all, everyone has a family to support, and going to work to earn money is the top priority. The images are unrelated to the content; infringement will result in removal. But unexpectedly, just 5 days later, the woman developed a fever again, reaching 40.7°C! Could she be so unlucky as to get infected again in such a short time? Didn't experts say that reinfection typically takes 3-6 months? The sudden high fever caused the woman great distress. According to her, this time was at least ten times more painful than the first. "Whole body pain, severe pain, headache, like being hit with a sledgehammer, constantly, temples bulging out with pain. Back pain, couldn't even turn over, lower body had no sensation except pain..." A second antigen test positive just 5 days apart. What surprised the woman was that the symptoms this time were much more severe than the first! Later, she reflected that she had let her guard down after testing negative, because she thought having been infected once, there shouldn't be a problem again so soon. Therefore, at work, she occasionally didn't wear a mask and didn't disinfect as frequently as before. Experts explain that so-called "re-positive" cases are of two types: one is nucleic acid "re-positivity", and another is called "antigen re-positivity". Ms. Zhang's situation likely falls under "antigen re-positivity". Antigen re-positivity means the first infection wasn't fully resolved; viral replication decreased, showing a "false negative", but the virus wasn't completely cleared from her body. She was misled by the false negative result. Generally, it takes 14 days after infection for the body to produce enough neutralizing antibodies for full protection. Ms. Zhang had only 10 days from the initial infection on the 9th to the 19th; the neutralizing antibody titer in her body wasn't high enough. In other words, her immunity against COVID-19 hadn't fully recovered. A key indicator of recovery is that it basically meets requirements only after at least 14 days. Frankly, since the reopening, many people have been misled by so-called experts. Some experts said it's just a bad cold, no need to worry too much, so some friends didn't stock up on necessary medicines, relying solely on their immunity and hot water. Some experts said 99.5% of people won't have symptoms, so some friends believed it 100%,准备ing to tough it out with bodies capable of hundreds of push-ups. Some friends believed experts who said recovery usually takes 7 days, so, like this woman, they went back to their normal routines as soon as they felt better. This is understandable – how many people aren't struggling right now? How many can afford not to earn money? But, like this woman, not resting properly led to a relapse, not only suffering a second time but potentially needing even longer to recover. I advise those experts without professional knowledge not to speak casually and consume the trust people place in you! Some online influencers have millions or tens of millions of followers; in daily life, their followers would rather believe what you say is the truth! So, without investigation or data support, speaking less is the greatest care for your followers, not speaking forcefully and misleading people. For us ordinary people, since the state has said we are the first person responsible for our own health, then if conditions allow, we might as well rest a few more days. Health is the foundation of revolution! Don't continue to neglect your health! Behind you, there are elderly parents, children, a family, and friends and relatives who love you!

Title: Newly purchased mechanical hard drive not detected after entering the system? Content: A newly purchased mechanical hard drive requires creating a new partition. Use DiskGenius software to create an NTFS partition on the mechanical hard drive, aligning to 2048 or 4096. If it is to be used as a system disk, it is recommended to set the partition table type to GUID (for Windows 10 and Windows 11 systems), set the number of partitions, rebuild the Master Boot Record (MBR), create a new ESP partition, create an MSR partition, and align to 2048 or 4096. If it is already partitioned, it might be that a drive letter has not been assigned. In DiskGenius software, go to Partition - Assign a new drive letter. Alternatively, go to My Computer - Right-click - Manage - Storage - Disk Management - Right-click the disk - Change drive letter and paths. If a drive letter already exists, it might be that the BIOS did not recognize it. Shut down - Turn on - Repeatedly press the Delete key to enter BIOS - Find the disk options - Select the disk boot order.

Title: What are your thoughts on loft beds with desks underneath? Content: The loft bed with desk underneath is a relatively common design in university dormitories. Because the user groups differ, the design naturally cannot be perfect and has its pros and cons. Advantages: First, better space utilization. The vertically layered design can effectively save space. The upper part is the sleeping area, and the lower part is the activity space, which usually includes a desk, wardrobe, and bookshelf. This can reduce the occupation of common areas and achieve a reasonable division between personal independent space and public areas. Second, clear functional zoning. This design separates the study and rest areas, which helps cultivate good habits of focusing on studying/working and focusing on resting, reducing external distractions. At the same time, the storage of personal items becomes more defined and centralized, avoiding area conflicts. Third, improved personal privacy. Compared to traditional bunk beds, it better avoids the exposure of personal privacy. Individuals can also add bed curtains to further enhance the sense of personal space and privacy. Fourth, improved personal rest quality. Traditional bunk beds are prone to causing mutual disturbance, especially during rest times. I have personal experience with both dormitory structures. With bunk beds, even turning over can be clearly felt by the other person, which is even more uncomfortable for light sleepers. Of course, where there are advantages, there are also disadvantages. First, the number of occupants is limited. With this structure, a dorm room can usually only accommodate 4 people. For the university, this requires more dormitory rooms, but for the students living there, it should be considered good news. Second, limited bed choice. With this structure, everyone can only choose the top bunk, which is naturally not very friendly for those who prefer to sleep on the bottom bunk. Third, safety hazards. With this structure, everyone needs to frequently climb the ladder to get in and out of bed, which carries a risk of slipping. It's also not very convenient for those who prefer level ground. Additionally, if the guardrail height on the top bunk is insufficient, it could lead to accidental falls, so safety standards need attention. Fourth, a sense of spatial confinement. The relatively independent space might reduce face-to-face communication with roommates, etc. In summary, the loft bed with desk underneath structure has both advantages and disadvantages. Personally, I quite like it. However, when getting in and out of bed for rest, one should still pay extra attention to safety precautions to avoid slipping or falling, because it really hurts – for example, getting in and out of bed slowly, raising the guardrail, or adding soft padding to the bed edge, etc.

Title: A Hospital in Zhengzhou Prescribes a 23,000 Yuan Herbal Prescription - What Should Be Questioned More Than the Exorbitant Price Is Medical Ethics Content: Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) has always been a controversial topic in China, with advocates and opponents almost irreconcilable. This phenomenon exists not only among the general public but also among doctors themselves. However, regardless of evaluation, as long as it can alleviate patients' suffering, efficacy is the ultimate criterion. On May 6th, Mr. Li, a resident of Zhengzhou, posted a herbal prescription online, which attracted public attention. This prescription, issued by a doctor from Zhengzhou Second Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, totaled 23,740.42 yuan for 30 doses, an exorbitant price that颠覆ed many people's perception of TCM. In the eyes of many, the price of a single dose of herbal medicine is generally几十to hundreds of yuan, but the price per dose in Mr. Li's prescription was as high as about 800 yuan. Due to doubts about the high price, the patient complained to the local 12315, but the response was that it was 'clearly marked' and there was no violation. A closer look at Mr. Li's prescription reveals that a single dose contains 37 herbs, with a total weight of 808 grams, including expensive ingredients such as saffron, agkistrodon, dragon's blood, gecko, scorpion, and Dendrobium officinale, which is the main reason for the overall high cost. As a local of Zhengzhou, based on personal experience, the price of herbal medicine in hospitals is slightly lower than in external chain pharmacies. Of course, the quality of the herbs may differ, but based on the unit prices listed on the hospital's settlement slip, they generally align with market prices. The爆料ed Zhengzhou Second Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine is a一级comprehensive public hospital. According to relevant regulations, public hospitals are not allowed to mark up Western medicine prices. TCM prices are also regulated, but in practice, due to the characteristics of TCM, price variations exist and loopholes can easily occur. In fact, compared to the high drug price, what should be questioned more is the medical skill and ethics of the hospital doctors. The posted prescription indicates the patient's clinical diagnosis was lung cancer. If these drugs are effective for the patient, even if they only alleviate symptoms or prolong the patient's survival, then despite the high cost, compared to Western medicine treatments costing millions per injection, a price of over 20,000 yuan might not be unacceptable. However, in today's materialistic world, whether such a prescription can withstand the拷问of conscience is a big question mark. The biggest problem with TCM is its individualized nature - it's difficult for the public to judge the effectiveness of a prescription. Even TCM professionals find it hard to assess the quality of these prescriptions, relying entirely on medical ethics to约束doctors, which似乎cannot guarantee against deviation. Regarding this specific prescription, a single dose amounts to 808 grams. How is the patient supposed to take such a large quantity? Prescribing 30 doses at once instead of starting with a one-week supply for辨证施治is puzzling. Only the doctor involved can explain the reasoning behind issuing such a prescription. Many hospitals view cancer patients as lucrative targets, exploiting their desperation to try anything and the families' willingness to pay without excessively high expectations for efficacy, making disputes less likely. Consequently, incidents of indiscriminate prescribing, expensive prescriptions, and overtreatment are层出不穷. The skepticism towards TCM from many people fundamentally lies not in whether TCM is scientific, but in the core issue of whether doctors can uphold the底线of medical ethics in the absence of standardization. If every TCM practitioner could act within their means, maintain reverence, and adhere to morality, TCM would naturally gain wider acceptance. Whether a 20,000-plus yuan herbal prescription delivers value for money tests both a doctor's ethics and a hospital's reputation. To prove their innocence, patient testimony would be needed. Treating patients as tools for profit and draining the pond to catch the fish only brings shame to medical ethics. A doctor without morality is no different from a murderer, but for problems that the law cannot solve, there will always be other forms of punishment. Heaven watches what people do; we hope this prescription can withstand the审判of morality.

Title: What equipment has improved your sports comfort and motivated you to exercise every time? Content: For many people, exercise is like the seasoning in food; it can make life more colorful. However, if the equipment is unsuitable during exercise, it's like trying to pick up garlic with chopsticks while eating—utterly unreasonable! Today, let's talk about those pieces of equipment that enhance sports comfort and how they make you more motivated every time you exercise! First, running shoes are the "pillar" of sports equipment. Many might think shoes are just something you wear—how important can they be? In fact, they greatly affect your comfort during exercise. According to statistics, wearing inappropriate shoes increases the probability of knee and ankle injuries while running by up to 60%! I have a pair of specialized running shoes that are lightweight and elastic; wearing them feels like stepping on clouds. Initially, I confidently planned to run 5 kilometers but almost couldn't stop; the comfort in my legs truly reminded me of "invisible happiness." Then there's sportswear, especially suitable functional athletic wear, which is like a "heartwarming little棉袄" (close companion). I used to wear cotton T-shirts, but when soaked with sweat during exercise, it felt like wearing a damp sandbag—so heavy while running. Later, I bought a set of breathable, quick-drying sportswear, and now when I go out to exercise daily, I feel like a gust of wind—so light it makes me want to fly! Also, the often-overlooked sports watch is a "faithful partner" that constantly motivates you. This small electronic device not only records your heart rate, steps, and calorie consumption each time you exercise but also sets goals and reminds you to stay motivated. I remember once seeing the numbers on the watch, which excited me more than the 8 kilometers I ran nearby, even astonishing the neighborhood cats! Furthermore, sports headphones are important equipment for enhancing exercise enjoyment. Data shows that listening to music can increase an exerciser's endurance by 15%. The wireless headphones I use have superb sound quality; running with rhythmic music makes me feel like I'm at a music festival, instantly feeling less tired. Once the headphones are on, it's like being enchanted—every movement becomes more graceful, and even the dogs on the street give me a thumbs-up. Finally, there's the sports water bottle; a good bottle not only hydrates you but also constantly reminds you to maintain fluid balance, ensuring good condition. Imagine not being troubled by thirst during intense workouts—your motivation to exercise naturally multiplies! Of course, improving comfort isn't solely dependent on equipment; it's also closely related to your persistence and condition. But it must be said, good sports equipment really can make every first step you take into exercise full of motivation. May everyone find their suitable sports partners and embark on a healthy, happy life path!

Title: University responds to requiring pants removal as proof for menstrual leave sick notes, stating the requirement "complies with relevant procedures". What issues exist with this requirement? Are there more reasonable solutions? Content: I looked at the comments, and they are almost universally criticizing the school. However, the essence of this matter, like many things in society, boils down to "a minority exploiting loopholes for gain, causing the majority to bear the consequences." Let me give a few examples: 1. A few women get pregnant as soon as they join a company, use up their marriage and maternity leave, and then resign, some even demanding compensation. This makes many companies extremely wary and defensive, making it harder for all women to find jobs. 2. Some people are greedy for small advantages, using various methods to get things for free online (especially with women's clothing), causing significant losses for merchants. To avoid losses, merchants can only raise prices and reduce quality and costs, meaning all consumers end up with expensive, poor-quality goods. 3. A company implements a humane management policy allowing employees to be up to 30 minutes late in the morning, with the original intention being that everyone might occasionally have an emergency. Then, a few individuals start being precisely 29 minutes late every day. Eventually, the company cancels the benefit, and no one is allowed to be a minute late. The essence of these situations is the same. When ordinary people who haven't gained any benefit are treated as "suspects," most feel it's unfair and vent their anger at the "inhumane" institutions. But is it really the fault of the companies "exploited by female employees who leave after using maternity benefits," the merchants "driven to losses by customers getting things for free," or the enterprises "where employees precisely work half an hour less every day"? Actually, it's that small minority exploiting loopholes that increases the operational costs for society. It's understandable that the girl felt humiliated and angry about being asked to remove her pants. Because, compared to the girls who exploit menstrual periods to take fake leave, she gained no benefit, did nothing wrong, but was still treated as a "suspect." Just like how more and more of us feel that female employment faces discrimination and online goods are becoming shoddier. However, when a minority starts exploiting loopholes for profit, more and more people will follow. If these loopholes aren't plugged, companies could be crippled by maternity leave abuse, merchants could be driven out of business by free-loading, and enterprise productivity will decline. In conclusion, I think the school's approach is not wrong. The blame should lie with that group of girls who first exploited the loopholes for gain; it is they who caused the later ones to suffer humiliation.

Content Title: High engine water temperature is not scary, what's scary is that the following operations may cause the engine to be scrapped
Publication Date: 2025-01-09 22:10:38

Author Name: Haiyue Talks Cars
Owner Name: Haiyue Talks Cars

Content Details: Incorrect operation directly scraps the engine! Hello friends. When we use our cars in summer, the biggest worry is high engine water temperature. Because high engine water temperature has a very significant impact on the lifespan of a car engine. If some friends drive carelessly and continue driving for a long time with high water temperature, it may directly cause the engine to be scrapped. There are also many friends who don't know what situation indicates high engine water temperature. Normally, on our engine's instrument panel, there is a water temperature gauge. 10. Normally, our water temperature should be right in the middle position. As long as while driving, this needle exceeds the middle position, it indicates abnormal engine water temperature. There is also a water temperature warning light, a red thermometer symbol. That is, as long as this red symbol lights up during normal driving, it indicates abnormal engine water temperature. If we discover high engine water temperature while driving, what should we do? What faults typically cause high engine water temperature? Today, I'll take you to understand with a real car. Friends, if we discover abnormal engine water temperature while driving, the best method is to pull over, find a safe place to park, and then immediately turn off the engine. Don't believe some advice online that says after the engine water temperature is high, you should let the engine run for a while to let the electric fan cool it down. Absolutely do not do this. Because at this point, you are not yet sure if your engine's electric fan is good or broken. We can also perform a simple check ourselves to determine what the problem with the car is. First, we need to find our coolant expansion tank. Look inside the coolant expansion tank to see if the coolant level is low. Normally, there are scale lines on it; the bottom one is the lower limit, and the top one is the upper limit. Generally, as long as there is a little water in the expansion tank, the main radiator is full, so it doesn't affect engine cooling. If the water in the expansion tank is completely gone, it proves that the main radiator is lacking water. At this time, we need to check around the engine for any water leakage spots, and also check the radiator. Because coolant doesn't just disappear that severely; it can only get that low if there is a leak. Also, don't unscrew the cap immediately because the engine water temperature is too high; wait at least 20 minutes before opening the cap. If it's lacking water, you can temporarily use something like mineral water or purified water instead; it's fine. Then, our next step is to check how the fan's cooling is. The electric fan is located right here. Actually, it's very easy to check. After we get in the car, turn on the air conditioning. The electric fan should start spinning on its own to cool down. If it doesn't spin when the AC is turned on, it proves there is a problem with the electric fan. Next, we can check the engine's coolant circulation. Title: Hearing via Video Conference Content: Recently, the Judicial Technology Service Center of Dongchangfu District People's Court in Liaocheng City organized an online judicial appraisal hearing for a medical dispute case using remote video conferencing, which received unanimous praise from both parties involved. In the case of medical damage liability dispute between plaintiff Liang and Zhang and Li, plaintiff Liang applied to the Dongchangfu District People's Court for an appraisal to determine whether there was fault and the degree of fault in the diagnosis and treatment process provided by Zhang and Li to Liang. The Dongchangfu District Court, following legal procedures, entrusted a judicial appraisal center to conduct the appraisal. After the appraisal materials were supplemented and completed twice, the appraisal institution notified the parties to hold a hearing. Considering the severe current pandemic prevention and control situation, which made it impossible for both parties to attend the hearing in person, and the fact that medical dispute appraisals currently face challenges such as a scarcity of appraisal institutions and long appraisal cycles, if this hearing could not proceed as scheduled, it might be postponed for several months. An excessively long appraisal cycle would not only affect the trial department's ability to conclude the case within the normal trial period but also cause the parties to wait too long. With the consent of both parties, the Judicial Technology Service Center of Dongchangfu District Court coordinated multiple times with the appraisal institution and decided to hold the hearing via video conference using Tencent Meeting. During the hearing, both parties fully stated their respective opinions, answered questions from the experts of the appraisal institution, and key evidence materials were verified one by one against the originals via video. The court participated and supervised the entire process. The hearing lasted one hour and achieved the expected results. Since 2020, the Technology Service Center of Dongchangfu District People's Court in Liaocheng City has organized multiple remote video hearings. This case-handling model allows for fully hearing opinions from all sides, protects the legitimate rights and interests of the parties, and reduces litigation burdens. Using the internet to conduct remote public hearings without direct contact not only aids in pandemic prevention and control but also ensures transparency and fairness in judicial case handling, shortens the appraisal cycle, improves the efficiency of judicial appraisal work, and effectively saves judicial resources. Text: Wang Li Editor: Li Mingyu Review: Li Guizhong, Qu Liming

Title: Psychological Counseling Volunteer Service Builds a Strong Psychological Defense Line Against the Epidemic Content: To ensure the mental health of individuals returning to Jinzhou from other places who are under centralized quarantine or home quarantine, and to prevent them from developing negative emotions such as panic, anxiety, and depression, recently, Wannian Community in Shiqiaozi Subdistrict, Linghe District, collaborated with the Jinzhou Red Cross Psychological Rescue Team to form a team of psychological counseling volunteers. Through face-to-face interactions, phone calls, and video chats, they provide psychological counseling to those under home quarantine and those who have been released from medical observation, addressing the root cause and building a strong defense line for the public's mental health. 'Fortunately, volunteer friends helped me alleviate my negative emotions; otherwise, I really wouldn't know how to get through the quarantine observation period,' said Mr. Zheng, a resident living in Wenxingli. At the end of December last year, Mr. Zheng returned to Jinzhou from a key controlled area in Dalian and underwent quarantine observation as required. During this time, Mr. Zheng became irritable. After learning of the situation, a grid member recommended a psychological counseling volunteer to him. The volunteer详细了解d Mr. Zheng's situation and suggested he listen to soothing music, focus on one thing, and relax his body and mind. Under the volunteer's guidance, Mr. Zheng's emotions gradually eased, and his mindset became calm and optimistic. Elderly people living alone in the community are an even greater focus for the community and volunteers. Aunt Zhang, who lives in Wenzhili, is an elderly person living alone. She returned to Jinzhou from a key controlled area in early January and, after 14 days of centralized observation, underwent 7 days of home observation. Considering her actual situation, to alleviate her anxiety, psychological counseling volunteers and community grid members often called her to chat, guiding her to maintain a positive mindset and promising to visit her after her home observation was lifted. When they finally met, the elderly lady warmly held the volunteer's hand, as if meeting an 'old acquaintance.' During the activities, volunteers always communicate with quarantined individuals in the most亲和 manner, understanding their issues related to life, psychology, and emotions, guiding them to maintain a positive, optimistic, rational, and calm mindset, properly adjust their psychology, and face the epidemic rationally. At the same time, community grid members, as frontline observers of the psychological counseling team, interact with home-quarantined individuals via WeChat. They monitor the living and psychological conditions of quarantined individuals in real-time, help address their daily needs, and provide targeted psychological counseling, offering warm services and caring support to help them escape 'emotional困境.' Seeing one person after another free themselves from the influence of negative emotions, staff members emotionally told reporters: 'No winter is insurmountable, and no spring fails to arrive. The epidemic tests our prevention and control capabilities, as well as our emotions and cognition. Shiqiaozi Subdistrict will further enhance psychological counseling for the public, strengthen humanistic care,凝聚 powerful spiritual strength for epidemic prevention and control efforts, and contribute to winning the battle against the epidemic.' (By Zhang Yang, Reporter Shen Xu)

Title: Cultural Relics Experts Conduct Field Investigation, Citizens Claim Mobile Phone Last Words Can Also Become Cultural Relics - Sohu News Content: Establishing an Earthquake Memorial Hall, Citizens Propose 6 Major Plans to Recreate Disaster Specimens. If possible or permitted, the most typical disaster scenes in the hardest-hit epicenter town (part) of Wenchuan County should not be altered or significantly changed, striving to preserve them in their original state as the core area of the Great Earthquake Site Park; Create a miniature panoramic view of the Wenchuan disaster; Build a "Memorial Wall" for the victims of the great earthquake. Chinese people can mourn, burn incense, light candles, offer flowers, and leave messages here to express their grief; Build an Earthquake Relief Memorial Hall. The memorial hall should include textual displays, data displays, physical object displays, image and video displays, and three-dimensional dynamic realistic art representations of the Wenchuan earthquake and relief efforts. There should also be a super-large statue (and oil painting) of the "Heroic Groups in Earthquake Relief," and a series of artistic sculptures reflecting the most touching scenes during the relief efforts; It is suggested that the park be funded and donated by Chinese real estate developers; Use tourism as continuous assistance. News Report (Reporter Huang Ye) The initiative launched by our newspaper's 966966 hotline yesterday to build a monument for the victims of the "5.12 Wenchuan Earthquake" (details in yesterday's page 29 of our newspaper) sparked heated discussions among people from all walks of life. Disaster area residents, government officials, scholars from various fields, students, ordinary employees... citizens have actively contributed ideas and suggestions for rebuilding the monument in the disaster area through phone calls and the internet. Setting up a memorial wall for the victims. Yesterday noon, Chongqing citizens Shu Mingwu, Cai Jianhua, and Zhou You, who enjoy creative planning, emailed our newspaper a 3,000-word proposal "Offering a Strategy for Wenchuan Post-Disaster Reconstruction," with core content covering six major aspects (see above). The leader Shu Mingwu stated that post-disaster reconstruction has now been put on the agenda, "Our plan mainly considers providing a strong self-hematopoietic function for the reconstruction of Wenchuan." Mobile phone last words can also become cultural relics. Over the 11 days since the Wenchuan特大earthquake, the news hotspots prominently reported by our newspaper have also become one of the most recommended memorials. At 2:28 PM on May 12, 2008, the hands of the four clock faces of the Hanwang Clock Tower in Mianzhu stopped at this sorrowful moment. Many citizens suggested turning the clock tower into a permanent earthquake memorial site. The reporter learned that Zhang Yangwu, the Party Secretary of Hanwang Town, also has such a plan, "to let people forever remember the moment the disaster occurred. This is a very good memorial." Additionally, some netizens said, "The ruins of Juyuan Middle School should be preserved as a memorial site; those dead and injured students were the future of our country!" Zhang Yuehui, Director of the Guanghan Cultural Relics Bureau and Deputy Director of the Sanxingdui Museum, offered suggestions from a professional perspective. He stated, "Media reports mentioned a victim's mother who left last words on a mobile phone; that mobile phone is a precious cultural relic"; furthermore, the remains and belongings of victims, such as "the schoolbag and shoes picked up by Premier Wen Jiabao from the ruins." Cultural relics experts begin field investigations. The reporter learned from "Huaxi Metropolis Daily" yesterday that Wang Qiong, Deputy Director of the Sichuan Provincial Cultural Relics Bureau, revealed that national cultural relics departments are already conducting investigations related to the museum. Currently, cultural relics departments across various regions are actively conducting scientific investigations and collecting physical materials. "We hope to establish museums on the damaged and disaster-affected sites for orderly protection. This, on one hand, allows people to remember the deceased, and on the other hand, can serve as a warning to future generations." Deputy Director Wang introduced that Sichuan Province has already actively launched comprehensive investigations, "We will invite a group of experts from Beijing to form an expert team with experts from Sichuan Province to conduct a special investigation of the disaster-affected areas in Sichuan Province, initially understanding the local damage situation. For example, the entire Beichuan county town was destroyed; can the original urban area be turned into a large site? Is it possible to build a museum in the epicenter, Wenchuan? All these are within the scope of investigation. During the Tangshan earthquake, three national-level cultural relics protection sites were established, but due to limitations of conditions at that time, most failed to achieve the initial ideas. So this time, we hope to do this more comprehensively and systematically." (Responsible Editor: Liu Xiaojing)

Title: What about Xintai Ruyizun (Tailai) Whole Life Insurance, an increasing life insurance policy where the cash value exceeds the premium in the 3rd year? Content: Currently in the market, how many types of single-premium, increasing whole life insurance policies have a cash value exceeding the paid premium by the 3rd year? I have only found 2 types, and Xintai Ruyizun (Tailai) Whole Life Insurance is one of them. Today, let's analyze this product in detail to see how it really is. First, an introduction to the insurer: Xintai Life Insurance Co., Ltd. was established on May 18, 2007, registered in Hangzhou, Zhejiang, with a registered capital of 10.2 billion yuan. It can operate various types of personal insurance businesses and has investment capabilities in multiple fields, with an annual scale premium platform of 50 billion yuan. By the end of 2023, the company's total assets exceeded 230 billion yuan, serving over 6.2 million customers. Shareholder details are shown in the figure below: Product details are shown in the figure below: 1. Application Rules Insured persons can be from 28 days old to 70 years old, with lifelong coverage. There are 4 payment term options. Single premium starts at 10,000 yuan; periodic premium starts at 5,000 yuan. Although the payment term options are limited, they basically meet the needs of many customers. 2. Effective Insurance Amount The effective insurance amount for the first policy year: equals the basic insurance amount. From the second policy year onwards, the effective insurance amount equals: the effective insurance amount of the previous policy year × (1 + 2.5%). 3. Death Benefit The death benefit is divided into 3 stages: (1) Before 18 years old: the greater of the paid premium or the cash value; (2) At 18 years old (inclusive) or older, death during the payment period: the greater of (paid premium × ratio) or the cash value; (3) At 18 years old (inclusive) or older, death after the payment period ends: the greatest of the annual insurance amount, (paid premium × ratio), or the cash value. Note: Payment ratio: Age 18 ≤ age < 40: 160%; Age 41 ≤ age < 60: 140%; Age 61 ≤ age: 120%. 4. Cash Value For single premium: By the 3rd policy year, the cash value exceeds the paid premium. For 3-year payment term: By the 4th policy year, the cash value exceeds the paid premium. For 5-year payment term: By the 5th policy year, the cash value exceeds the paid premium. For 10-year payment term: By the 8th policy year, the cash value exceeds the paid premium. Regardless of the payment method, the break-even speed is relatively fast. Once the cash value exceeds the paid premium, if you need money, you can withdraw it at any time. You might not need to use it, but this offers more flexibility. 5. Policy Reduction Rules After the contract has been in effect for 5 years and during the validity period of this contract, the cumulative reduction in the basic insurance amount in each policy year shall not exceed 20% of the basic insurance amount. This means you can withdraw 20% of the cash value in that year, which is the most lenient reduction method. It offers more flexibility if you need money. Case Demonstration: Insuring a 0-year-old boy with Xintai Ruyizun (Tailai) Whole Life Insurance, single premium of 1 million yuan. Detailed data is shown in the figure below: 1. For a single premium, the cash value in the 3rd year is 1.02 million, exceeding the total premium paid. The break-even speed is much faster than many products. 2. To prevent moral hazard, there is no death leverage before age 18. The death benefit is either the paid premium or the cash value for that year. For this product, starting from the 3rd year, the death benefit amount is consistent with the cash value. 3. At age 18, the cash value is 1.479 million. The annual cash value increase that year is 36,060 yuan. If you withdraw 36,000 yuan annually for living expenses during studies, the cash value will continue to grow. There is a trick to using the cash value of increasing life insurance. If the annual withdrawal amount exceeds the annual cash value increase, the future cash value will decrease. The more you exceed, the faster it decreases. If the withdrawal amount is less than the annual cash value increase, the future cash value will continue to grow. 4. At age 30, the cash value is 1.988 million. The annual cash value increase that year is 48,490 yuan. You can withdraw 48,000 yuan that year. If married with children, this money can be used for baby formula, and the cash value will still continue to grow. 5. At age 40, if no money was withdrawn previously, the cash value is as high as 2.545 million. The annual cash value increase that year is 62,080 yuan. We can withdraw 62,000 yuan annually as a supplement to our pension, and the cash value will still continue to grow. This is equivalent to funding your retirement while having access to a large sum of cash at any time, offering great flexibility. 6. At age 65, if no money was withdrawn previously, the cash value is as high as 4.719 million. This year's cash value exceeds that of some other products by over 100,000 yuan. The annual cash value increase that year is 115,090 yuan. The child can withdraw 115,000 yuan annually for retirement. 7. If the policy is not used earlier, when the child is 100 years old, the cash value is as high as 11.199 million. Title: Women Are More Prone to Thyroid Disease! How to Fix It? Content: According to authoritative statistics, nearly 50% of people in China have more or less thyroid problems, and women are 7 to 10 times more likely than men! - It has been said before that 90% of women's illnesses are caused by holding things in! Actually, it's not just gynecological issues; the relationship between the thyroid and emotions is also very significant. - Thyroid problems are generally caused by the following reasons: 1. Excessive or insufficient iodine intake 2. Trauma, body inflammation, immune reactions 3. Life stress, emotional influences. Women's roles in family and society are relatively complex, and emotions are more easily affected. Additionally, during the childbearing process, hormonal levels fluctuate greatly, leading to significant emotional swings. If postpartum recovery is not done well, physical depletion cannot be replenished, which can cause a series of health problems, such as sleep issues and decreased immunity, thereby affecting the thyroid. It becomes a vicious cycle: poor sleep leads to poor mood, and poor mood then brings on various gynecological diseases, causing the entire immune system to deteriorate! - How to solve it? In terms of daily diet, as mentioned, both excessive and insufficient iodine intake can cause thyroid problems. In modern society, it is mostly due to excess. The iodine in our daily diet mainly comes from salt or seaweed and seafood. The healthy standard for iodine is 150 micrograms per person per day. Each gram of salt contains about 25 micrograms of iodine, meaning we should not exceed 6 grams of salt per day to stay healthy! However, we also consume other iodine-containing foods, so 6 grams of salt would already exceed the limit! - For example: 1. Just seaweed alone! A small handful (about 150 micrograms of iodine) can meet a person's daily iodine requirement. If you eat that, you can only use non-iodized salt for the rest of the day! - 2. Kelp, be very, very careful! 50g of dried kelp (roughly a large handful) contains the iodine equivalent of 480 grams of salt. That's a whole bag of salt! Enough iodine for 80 days of healthy intake! If you eat a whole plate of kelp in one day, it is a serious overdose. - 3. Spinach: one plate (half a catty) contains 410 micrograms of iodine, enough for three days of healthy iodine intake. After eating a plate of spinach, you can only use non-iodized salt for the next three days, and you shouldn't even eat soy sauce. - 4. Persimmons: one persimmon contains iodine equivalent to nearly two days of healthy intake. After eating a persimmon, you can only use non-iodized salt for the rest of the day. - 5. Iodine content in other common foods: Dried shrimp: 265 micrograms per 100g Celery: 160 micrograms per 100g Yam: 140 micrograms per 100g Sea fish: 80 micrograms per 100g Cola: 68 micrograms per 100g Pistachios: 39 micrograms per 100g The human body only needs 150 micrograms of iodine per day. Excessive intake of the above foods can cause thyroid disease. - If you don't have non-iodized salt at home, here's a clever trick: when stir-frying, heat the oil first, then add the salt. The iodine in the salt will disappear instantly.

Title: What is the reduction rate for the "Six Taxes and Two Fees"? Who is eligible? 8 Q&As to clarify. Content: To facilitate taxpayers, fee payers, and grassroots tax authorities in consulting relevant policy response guidelines, the State Taxation Administration has comprehensively reviewed and confirmed the Q&As released externally by the State Taxation Administration from January 2019 to July 2024, and compiled the "Compilation of Q&As on Series of Tax and Fee Support Policies Since 2019". Today, we will learn about the Q&As related to the "Six Taxes and Two Fees" reduction and exemption policy. 【Question 1】What is the reduction rate for the "Six Taxes and Two Fees" preferential policy? Answer: According to Article 2 of the "Announcement of the Ministry of Finance and the State Taxation Administration on Further Supporting the Development of Small and Micro Enterprises and Individual Businesses with Relevant Tax and Fee Policies" (Ministry of Finance and State Taxation Administration Announcement No. 12 of 2023), from January 1, 2023, to December 31, 2027, resource tax (excluding water resource tax), urban maintenance and construction tax, property tax, urban land use tax, stamp tax (excluding securities transaction stamp tax), farmland occupation tax, education surcharge, and local education surcharge shall be halved for small-scale VAT taxpayers, small and low-profit enterprises, and individual businesses. 【Question 2】Which taxpayers can declare and enjoy the "Six Taxes and Two Fees" reduction and exemption preference? Answer: Small-scale VAT taxpayers, small and low-profit enterprises, and individual businesses can all declare and enjoy the "Six Taxes and Two Fees" reduction and exemption preference according to regulations. 【Question 3】My company is a sole proprietorship enterprise. Can it declare and enjoy the "Six Taxes and Two Fees" reduction and exemption preference? Answer: Sole proprietorship enterprises and partnership enterprises, if they are small-scale VAT taxpayers, can declare and enjoy the "Six Taxes and Two Fees" reduction and exemption preference. 【Question 4】How does my company determine whether it can declare and enjoy the "Six Taxes and Two Fees" reduction and exemption preference as a small and low-profit enterprise? Answer: The determination of a small and low-profit enterprise is based on the result of the annual corporate income tax final settlement. A newly established enterprise registered as a general VAT taxpayer, engaged in industries that are not restricted or prohibited by the state, and simultaneously meeting the two conditions of having no more than 300 employees and total assets not exceeding 50 million yuan at the end of the month before the declaration period, can declare and enjoy the "Six Taxes and Two Fees" reduction and exemption preference as a small and low-profit enterprise before completing the first final settlement; for those declaring on a per-transaction basis in the month of establishment, whether they can declare and enjoy the "Six Taxes and Two Fees" reduction and exemption preference as a small and low-profit enterprise is determined based on whether they simultaneously meet the two conditions of having no more than 300 employees and total assets not exceeding 50 million yuan at the time of establishment. 【Question 5】My company has already enjoyed other preferential policies according to regulations. Can it continue to enjoy the "Six Taxes and Two Fees" reduction and exemption preference? Answer: If small-scale VAT taxpayers, small and low-profit enterprises, and individual businesses have already legally enjoyed other preferential policies, they can additionally enjoy the "Six Taxes and Two Fees" reduction and exemption preference. In terms of the order of enjoying preferences, the "Six Taxes and Two Fees" reduction and exemption preference is enjoyed on top of other preferences. For those originally applicable to proportional reduction or fixed-amount reduction, the base for calculating the "Six Taxes and Two Fees" reduction amount is the tax payable after deducting the original reduction amount. 【Question 6】Can natural persons enjoy the "Six Taxes and Two Fees" reduction policy? Can taxpayers who issue invoices on behalf of others enjoy the "Six Taxes and Two Fees" reduction policy during the invoicing process? Answer: According to Article 29 of the "Detailed Rules for the Implementation of the Provisional Regulations on Value-Added Tax", Article 3 of the "Measures for the Implementation of Replacing Business Tax with Value-Added Tax" (issued by Cai Shui [2016] No. 36), Article 4 of the "Measures for the Registration of General VAT Taxpayers" (State Taxation Administration Order No. 43), and other regulations, natural persons (i.e., other individuals) do not register as general VAT taxpayers. Therefore, natural persons can enjoy the "Six Taxes and Two Fees" reduction policy as small-scale taxpayers. According to current regulations, general VAT taxpayers do not need to issue invoices on behalf of others. Various small-scale VAT taxpayers, including natural persons, can enjoy the "Six Taxes and Two Fees" reduction policy when issuing invoices on behalf of others. 【Question 7】How do cross-regional small-scale VAT taxpayers get refunds for local taxes and fees paid in other locations? Issues with cross-regional small-scale VAT taxpayers enjoying the "Six Taxes and Two Fees" preference: When a company reports and verifies at the business location and pre-pays and declares additional taxes without enjoying the reduction preference, but then returns to the registration location to declare, since the preference was not enjoyed at the verification location but should actually be enjoyed, a negative overpayment appears in the "Tax (Fee) Amount to be Supplemented (Refunded) This Period" field of the declaration form after normally filling in the data at the registration location. Should the refund for the overpaid tax be applied for at the registration location or the verification location? Answer: The refund should be applied for at the verification location. The principle is: where the tax was paid, there the refund should be applied for. 【Question 8】Can taxpayers with outbound verification and cross-district tax source registration enjoy the "Six Taxes and Two Fees" reduction policy? Answer: Various taxpayers, including those with outbound verification and cross-district tax source registration, should be comprehensively judged based on their tax registration information, general VAT taxpayer registration information, and corporate income tax final settlement information to determine whether they are small-scale VAT taxpayers, individual businesses, or small and low-profit enterprises. Those who meet the conditions can enjoy the "Six Taxes and Two Fees" reduction policy. Source: State Taxation Administration
