Title: How to Remove Ice from the Freezer Compartment Why Does the Refrigerator Tend to Ice Up in Summer? Content: When using the refrigerator in summer, it is often found that the refrigerator is particularly prone to icing up. Why is this? In summer, the weather is hot, and moisture in the air easily adheres to the refrigerator door. So, how to remove the ice from the freezer compartment? Let me introduce it to everyone below! 1. How to Remove Ice from the Freezer Compartment Refrigerator De-icing Methods: Method 1: Automatic De-icing The automatic de-icing method mainly involves disconnecting the refrigerator's power supply, taking out the food from the refrigerator and freezer compartments, and then placing a highly absorbent towel at the bottom of the refrigerator. Then, open the refrigerator door. Under room temperature conditions, the formed ice will naturally melt and fall off. After the ice in the refrigerator has completely fallen off, clear the fallen ice, and finally clean the water at the bottom of the refrigerator. This completes the de-icing process. Method 2: Blow-drying De-icing Using a hairdryer is also a good de-icing method. When de-icing the refrigerator, also disconnect the power supply and remove the food from the refrigerator or freezer compartment, then plug in the hairdryer. When using the hairdryer for de-icing, it is best to use a low setting, blowing while wiping with a towel. After a while, the ice in the refrigerator will be cleaned up. Blow-drying de-icing is much faster than automatic de-icing, but automatic de-icing requires no manual intervention. Method 3: Hot Water De-icing To use hot water for de-icing, first disconnect the refrigerator's power supply and remove the food from the refrigerator. Then, place several bowls of hot water in the refrigerator. After letting it sit for a few minutes, you will find that the ice layer in the refrigerator gradually begins to fall off. Once the ice layer has completely fallen off, remove the ice promptly and clean the water tray at the bottom of the refrigerator. Using this method for de-icing is fast and requires no manual cleaning, making it a very convenient method. 2. Handy Tips for Removing Ice from the Freezer Compartment 1. Before putting food into the freezer, apply a layer of plastic film to the freezer walls. The cold air in the freezer will make it adhere quickly. Then put the food in for freezing. When defrosting is needed, quickly move the frozen food to the refrigerator compartment for temporary storage. Just peel off the plastic film from the freezer, and the frost will be removed quickly. Then reapply the cleaned film, and you can continue freezing food. The whole process takes only one or two minutes, saving time, effort, and electricity. 2. After each defrosting, wipe the freezer dry with a towel, then apply a layer of vegetable oil to the aluminum walls. When frost forms next time, because it adheres to the oil-coated refrigerator walls, the adhesion between the frost and the walls is greatly reduced. So, everyone can easily peel off the ice chunks without much effort. 3. When defrosting is needed, first cut off the refrigerator's power supply, then use an electric fan or hairdryer directed at the freezer compartment at the highest setting. After blowing, the frost layer will melt very quickly, making it easier to remove. How to remove ice from the freezer compartment? I believe many people have experienced that the refrigerator easily ices up in summer. So why does the refrigerator tend to ice up in summer? Let's take a look. 3. Why Does the Refrigerator Tend to Ice Up in Summer? Experts explain that the phenomenon of icing in the refrigerator compartment is part of the frosting process. In summer, the ambient temperature is very high, while the temperature in the refrigerator compartment is very low. When people frequently open the refrigerator, there is a significant temperature difference between the inside and outside of the refrigerator. Water vapor in the environment suddenly encounters the cold in the freezer compartment and condenses into frost. If not handled promptly, it will eventually form a thick layer of ice. If the freezer compartment frequently ices up, it consumes a lot of electricity and takes up a large volume of the refrigerator compartment. To prevent icing in the refrigerator compartment, first melt the ice in the refrigerator compartment, then apply a layer of cooking oil to the inner walls. This will prevent the refrigerator from icing up.
